Title: Antiproteinuric Response to Finerenone in Diabetic Kidney Disease: Responder and Non-Responder Subgroup Analysis of the FINDKDLATAM Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Albuminuria is an early marker of kidney damage and an independent predictor of adverse outcomes, making its reduction a key therapeutic goal. Finerenone, a selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, has demonstrated renal and cardiovascular benefits in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD), although the magnitude of the antiproteinuric response may vary in clinical practice. This post hoc analysis aimed to characterize the six-month antiproteinuric response to finerenone and to descriptively explore baseline clinical and treatment characteristics across response categories in the FINDKDLATAM cohort. Methods: A subgroup analysis was performed on a real-world, multicenter, retrospective, observational study that included patients from the FINDKDLATAM study who had urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) measurements taken at baseline and six months. Patients were classified as absolute responders (≥50% reduction in UACR), partial responders (30-49% reduction), and non-responders (<30% reduction or no reduction in UACR) at six months of follow-up. Sociodemographic, clinical, biochemical, therapeutic, and safety variables were analyzed. Results: Of the 347 patients included in the original cohort, 334 had complete UACR data at six months and were included in the analysis. Of these, 80.2% (n = 268) were absolute responders, 11.7% (n = 39) partial responders, and 8.1% (n = 27) non-responders. Median UACR decreased from 350.7 to 67.0 mg/g among absolute responders and from 240.5 to 143.0 mg/g among partial responders (both p < 0.0001), whereas no significant change was observed among non-responders. No baseline clinical characteristic consistently distinguished responders from non-responders. Serum potassium increased during follow-up, particularly among non-responders. Conclusions: In this retrospective Latin American cohort, most patients experienced a reduction in UACR after six months of finerenone treatment. However, the uncontrolled observational design, concomitant therapies, UACR variability, and regression to the mean preclude attributing these changes exclusively to finerenone. These exploratory findings do not support selecting patients according to a particular responder phenotype but rather support prescribing finerenone according to currently approved clinical criteria. Prospective studies with adjusted analyses are needed to identify independent predictors of response.

Title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes in Acalabrutinib vs. Zanubrutinib in B-Cell Malignancies: A TriNetX Data Study.
Abstract: Next-generation Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis) such as acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib have improved treatment outcomes in B-cell malignancies, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), and Waldenström macroglobulinemia (WM), while reducing off-target toxicities compared to ibrutinib. However, their comparative cardiovascular safety profiles remain poorly characterized. This study evaluates real-world cardiovascular and clinical outcomes between zanubrutinib and acalabrutinib using a large multi-center database. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (October 2017-December 2024) including adult patients with CLL, MCL, WM, or small B-cell lymphoma treated with zanubrutinib or acalabrutinib. Patients with prior exposure to other BTKis were excluded. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 2887 patients were included in each cohort. We assessed one-year outcomes including new-onset atrial fibrillation/flutter, cerebral infarction, hypertension, and all-cause mortality using Cox proportional hazards modeling. The rate of AF/flutter events observed in the zanubrutinib group (4.05%) was numerically lower compared to the acalabrutinib group (5.25%). Time-to-event analysis did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in AF risk over time (HR 0.777, 95% CI 0.597-1.012; p = 0.06), which was similar in binary analysis (OR 0.761, 95% CI 0.581-0.997; p = 0.05). Cerebral infarction rates were similar between groups (1.09% vs. 1.12%), with no significant difference in time-to-event analysis (HR 0.984, 95% CI 0.596-1.626; p = 0.95) or binary analysis (p = 0.91). There was no significant difference in onset of hypertension in the zanubrutinib cohort (HR 1.199, 95% CI 0.957-1.501; p = 0.11) All-cause mortality was not statistically significant between the two groups (HR 0.865, 95% CI 0.740-1.012; p = 0.07). In this large, real-world analysis, fewer AF/flutter events were observed with zanubrutinib at one year; however, time-to-event analysis did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in AF risk over time. Notably, hypertension, cerebral infarction, and all-cause mortality occurred at similar rates. This suggests zanubrutinib and acalabrutinib share similar cardiovascular safety profiles overall. However these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before definitive conclusions about cardiovascular risk can be drawn.

Title: Cancer Cachexia and the Heart: A Review with Focus on China.
Abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic, multifactorial syndrome characterized by progressive depletion of skeletal muscle, disruption of metabolic homeostasis, and reduced survival. In experimental models, cachexia-associated mediators, including inflammatory cytokines, myostatin-related signaling, and proteolytic activation, have been implicated in driving cardiac atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and impaired myocardial function. Conversely, data from chronic heart failure suggest that reduced tissue perfusion, neurohormonal activation, and sustained inflammation secondary to cardiac dysfunction may further aggravate skeletal muscle wasting. These observations suggest a bidirectional relationship between cancer cachexia and cardiac dysfunction, which has not been tested in patients with cancer. Approximately 4.82 million new cancer cases occur in China annually, with a disease distribution predominated by gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, and thoracic malignancies, all of which carry high risks of cachexia. Among 710,170 Chinese patients with cancer, 5.0% had cardiovascular disease and 13.0% had at least one cardiovascular risk factor. These figures indicate a large population at risk, but they do not show that cardiac involvement in Chinese patients differs in frequency, phenotype, or clinical impact from that in other populations; to our knowledge, no prospective data on cancer-associated cardiac involvement have been reported for Chinese patients, and cachexia assessment does not include cardiac biomarkers or echocardiographic measures. This review summarizes cancer cachexia epidemiology in China, shows the evidence linking cachexia to cardiac wasting, and evaluates how cardiac dysfunction may in turn influence the cachectic trajectory. Accordingly, we outline the key clinical and mechanistic questions that remain unanswered in Chinese patients and propose a research agenda in which cardiac assessment is evaluated prospectively before it is considered for routine care.

Title: CBCT-Guided Online Adaptive Ultrahypofractionated Whole-Breast Radiotherapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer: Dosimetric Outcomes and Acute Toxicity.
Abstract: Ultrahypofractionated whole-breast radiotherapy reduces treatment burden but increases the importance of accurate dose delivery at each fraction. This retrospective single-center study evaluated cone-beam computed tomography-guided online adaptive radiotherapy in 55 patients with early-stage breast cancer treated with 26 or 27 Gy in five fractions. Dosimetric analysis was available for 52 patients and 259 paired scheduled and adapted fractions. Linear mixed-effects models with a patient-specific random intercept were used to account for repeated fractions within individual patients. The adapted plan was selected for 242 out of 260 delivered fractions (93.1%). Mean planning target volume V95% increased from 93.52 ± 2.94% with the scheduled plan to 98.13 ± 1.04% with adaptation (p < 0.001), with reduced interfraction variability. Ipsilateral lung V30% increased modestly from 13.94% to 14.96% (p < 0.001). In left-sided cases, no significant differences were observed for heart V25% (1.400% vs. 1.395%; p = 0.3825) or left anterior descending coronary artery D0.03 cm3 (1.771 vs. 1.873 Gy; p = 0.1390). Acute grade 1 toxicity occurred in five patients (9.1%), with no grade ≥ 2 events. Mean treatment-session duration was 28 min. Online adaptation significantly improved daily target coverage and was technically feasible within a five-fraction whole-breast workflow. Acute toxicity was limited in this cohort, while longer follow-up and cumulative dose analyses are needed to further define its impact on organ-at-risk exposure and clinical outcomes.

Title: Risk Stratification and Factors Associated with Heart Failure Hospitalization During Osimertinib Therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is the standard of care for epidermal growth factor receptor mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer, but heart failure hospitalization (HFH) remains a concern, and no practical tool exists to stratify HFH risk during therapy.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study using a Japanese claims database, 5802 patients newly initiating osimertinib were followed for HFH during treatment. Baseline predictors assessed before the index date were selected by 10-fold cross-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression and internally validated by bootstrapping (B = 500), repeating predictor selection in each resample. Cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event; cause-specific Cox models served as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: HFH occurred in 169 patients (2.9%) during a median on-treatment follow-up of 9.3 months, with 268 competing deaths. LASSO retained seven predictors. The apparent concordance index (C-index) was 0.731 (95% confidence interval, 0.691-0.771) and the optimism-corrected C-index 0.718. Observed incidence increased 10.2-fold across predicted-risk deciles (1.03-10.50%). Fine-Gray and Cox estimates closely matched the logistic model.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline cardiovascular vulnerability stratifies HFH risk during osimertinib therapy. The nomogram, not externally validated, is best used as a screening aid to identify patients who may benefit from intensified cardiovascular monitoring.

Title: Cardiotoxicity of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors with Anthracycline Chemotherapy in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
Abstract: Background/Aim: The addition of an immune-checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) to chemotherapy improves outcomes in both early-stage and metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, ICIs are associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs), such as cardiotoxicity, raising concerns for patients receiving both anthracyclines and ICIs. We sought to determine if combining anthracycline and ICI in TNBC is associated with greater cardiotoxicity than anthracycline alone. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a large academic center. Two cohorts were analyzed: anthracycline plus ICI and anthracycline alone. Demographics, comorbidities, medications, cardiac imaging, and outcomes were reviewed. Time to adverse cardiac events were compared. Results: A total of 382 patients were included: 297 received anthracyclines without ICI, and 85 received both. There were no major differences in baseline characteristics. The rate of acute cardiac events was 3.4% in the anthracycline-alone cohort and 3.5% in the anthracycline-plus-ICI cohort (p > 0.99) over a median of 1232 days of follow up (median of 1336 days in the anthracycline only group; median of 704 days in the ICI group). No significant differences in acute heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, myocarditis, or pericardial effusion were observed. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in cardiac event-free survival (p = 0.60). Furthermore, there was no significant difference in time to cardiac events between the two groups following competing risk analysis when accounting for both prior coronary artery disease (HR = 1.32, 95% CI: [0.42, 4.14], p = 0.64) and age (HR = 1.64, 95% CI: [0.52, 5.19], p = 0.40). Conclusions: This single-institution analysis did not identify a significant increase in cardiotoxicity with the addition of an ICI to anthracycline therapy in patients with TNBC. Active surveillance for cardiotoxicities should continue in patients receiving ICI in addition to anthracycline therapy.

Title: Analytical Characterization, Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Preliminary Immunogenicity of GNR-062, an Agalsidase Beta Biosimilar Candidate, in Healthy Male Volunteers.
Abstract: Fabry disease is a rare genetic multisystemic lysosomal disease characterized by progressive cellular accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (GL-3) in various organs with specific cutaneous (angiokeratoma), neurological (pain), renal (proteinuria, chronic kidney failure), cardiovascular (cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia), cochleovestibular and cerebrovascular manifestations (transient ischemic attacks, strokes). The phenotypic expression depends on the age of onset and, in females, on the level of X-inactivation. Enzyme replacement therapy is currently the standard therapy for the disease. JSC GENERIUM recently developed a potential biosimilar of Fabrazyme®, GNR-062, and investigated its physicochemical and biological properties, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity to assess its bioequivalence to Fabrazyme®. Direct evaluation of the N-glycosylation profile by HPLC revealed differences mainly related to the distribution of complex sialylated glycans. The overall sialylation level was comparable between the two products. The same conclusion follows from the results of direct analysis of the sialic acid content. Despite a small difference of a few percent in biphosphorylated glycan content, the overall measured M6P values were comparable. Thus, the internalization of agalsidase β into the inner space of lysosomes by binding to key receptors appear to be the same for both products. In a single-blind, randomized comparative study of the pharmacokinetics and safety of a single intravenous infusion of GNR-062 (JSC GENERIUM, Russia) and Fabrazyme® (Genzyme Europe B.V., The Netherlands) in a crossover design in healthy volunteers, the ratio of geometric means (90% CI) of AUCinf and Cmax for GNR-062 to agalsidase β was 0.9736 (0.9413-1.0070) and 0.9867 (0.9546-1.0199), respectively. These studies demonstrated pharmacokinetic bioequivalence of GNR-062 to agalsidase β. Immunogenicity findings are preliminary, as the study was not powered for formal immunogenicity equivalence, and the single-dose design in healthy volunteers does not reflect repeated long-term administration in patients with Fabry disease. In conclusion, GNR-062 demonstrated acceptable short-term tolerability in healthy volunteers and warrants further investigation as a potential therapeutic option for patients with Fabry disease.

Title: Deciphering the Benefits and Risks of Single-Inhaler Triple Therapy in COPD.
Abstract: Single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) combines an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS; for example, fluticasone furoate, budesonide, or beclometasone dipropionate), a long-acting β2-agonist (LABA; for example, vilanterol or formoterol fumarate), and a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA; for example, umeclidinium or glycopyrronium bromide) in one device. Triple pharmacological therapy reduces exacerbations in selected patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but its effects on mortality and cardiovascular outcomes remain uncertain. This structured narrative review summarizes randomized trials, observational comparative-effectiveness studies, target trial emulations, systematic reviews, and health technology assessments published between 2015 and 2026. We grouped the evidence by comparator: LABA/LAMA, ICS/LABA, multiple-inhaler triple therapy (MITT), and ICS continuation versus withdrawal, because each comparison addresses a different clinical question. Pivotal trials and evidence syntheses consistently showed fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations with triple therapy, with reported rate ratios of approximately 0.69-0.93. Mortality signals from IMPACT and ETHOS are clinically important, but previous ICS use and ICS withdrawal among participants assigned to ICS-free comparators make these findings difficult to interpret. Observational cardiovascular findings are also uncertain because residual confounding, treatment selection, exposure misclassification, outcome misclassification, and differences in baseline disease severity limit causal interpretation. Compared with MITT, the main advantages of SITT are simpler treatment and possible improvements in adherence and persistence, not greater pharmacological potency. Treatment decisions should consider exacerbation history, repeated blood eosinophil counts, pneumonia risk, cardiovascular disease, previous ICS exposure and response, inhaler technique, device suitability, and patient preference. Trials in patients with documented absence of previous ICS use and well-designed target trial emulations are needed to determine whether the observed mortality and cardiovascular associations are causal.

Title: Patterns of Falls and Fractures Among Older Adults Undergoing Rehabilitation After Fall-Related Fractures: A Retrospective Study in Croatia.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: The injury patterns of older patients who reach rehabilitation after a fall-related fracture are rarely described. We aimed to describe these patients and to examine how age, sex, recorded chronic conditions, osteoporosis and previous fractures relate to the mechanism of injury and the fracture site. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, the records of 255 patients aged 65 years and over who entered a rehabilitation programme at a Croatian rehabilitation hospital after a fall-related fracture between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2025 were extracted from the hospital information system and analysed using the chi-square test, the Mann-Whitney U test, the Kruskal-Wallis test and Spearman rank correlation. Results: Women accounted for 74.9% of the sample and hip fracture was the most frequent site (52.9%). Ground-level falls caused 78.8% of fractures overall, 95.2% of those in patients aged 85 years and over, and 86.7% of hip fractures; the mechanism of injury differed by sex, age group and fracture site (all p ≤ 0.005). Cardiovascular disease was recorded in 78.0% of patients but osteoporosis in only 19.2%. Both osteoporosis (p = 0.041) and having two or more recorded chronic conditions (p = 0.012) were associated with the mechanism of injury, but not with the fracture site. Conclusions: Hip fractures and ground-level falls predominated, particularly in the oldest patients. The findings support systematic nursing assessment of fall circumstances, chronic disease burden, bone health and fracture history after a fall.

Title: Relationship Between Social Isolation, Loneliness, and Systemic Inflammation: A Scoping Review of Biological Signatures and Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social isolation and loneliness are established social determinants of health, associated with 25-30% higher mortality risk, yet their relationship with systemic inflammation and broader biological and clinical outcomes has not been comprehensively synthesized across life stages.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched (2015-2025), supplemented by citation searching and a targeted supplementary search, for human studies linking social isolation, loneliness, or social connectedness to inflammatory biomarkers or biological/clinical outcomes. PRISMA-ScR guidance was followed; findings were synthesized narratively across five thematic axes as an evidence map.
RESULTS: Of 3351 records identified, 73 studies were included. Isolation was most often associated with CRP and fibrinogen, and loneliness with IL-6. Isolation predicted sarcopenia, venous thromboembolism, pancreatic cancer, and cardiovascular disease, with inflammatory or metabolic markers mediating a modest (≈5-19%) share. Proteomic (n = 42,062) and epigenetic analyses linked loneliness to inflammatory, antiviral, and complement-pathway proteins and to accelerated epigenetic ageing; Mendelian randomization supported causal involvement of several proteins. Social connectedness and relationship quality tracked with lower IL-6 and better functional indices. Evidence was strongest in midlife and older cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Social disconnection shows biologically plausible but heterogeneous associations with inflammatory and molecular signatures; harmonized measurement and prospective, hypothesis-free omics designs are needed to clarify causality and inform targeted screening.

Title: Real-World Pharmacological Patterns and Residual Cardiometabolic Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes in Romania.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has shifted from a glucose-centered approach toward integrated cardio-renal-metabolic protection. Although sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and intensive lipid-lowering therapies have demonstrated substantial cardiovascular and renal benefits, implementation in routine outpatient care and the burden of persistent residual risk remain insufficiently characterized in Romania.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate routine-care pharmacological treatment patterns, identify residual cardio-renal-metabolic risk despite ongoing therapy, determine independent correlates of persistent adverse outcomes, and explore potential therapeutic gaps in adults with T2DM.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included 232 unique adults with T2DM attending a specialized outpatient diabetes clinic in Romania between 1 October 2024 and 19 February 2026. One eligible outpatient record per participant was analyzed; when multiple records were available, the earliest eligible record in the exported dataset was used as the index visit. No a priori sample-size calculation was performed. Pharmacological therapies, cardiovascular and renal phenotypes, metabolic biomarkers, and clinical outcomes were extracted from routinely collected electronic medical records. Residual risk was evaluated using glycemic, lipid, renal, obesity, and blood-pressure targets. Multivariable logistic regression analyses identified independent correlates of persistent cardio-metabolic abnormalities. An exploratory cumulative residual-risk count was constructed by summing seven clinically relevant uncontrolled risk factors.
RESULTS: Biguanides were the most frequently prescribed glucose-lowering agents (53.0%), followed by SGLT2 inhibitors (44.8%), insulin (32.3% of the total cohort), GLP-1 receptor agonists (15.5%), and DPP-4 inhibitors (14.7%). Statins were prescribed to 48.7% of participants. SGLT2 inhibitor use did not differ significantly according to established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease phenotypes, whereas GLP-1 receptor agonists were prescribed more frequently in participants with obesity (22.0% vs. 7.6%, p = 0.003). Clinically important residual risk persisted across all treatment groups. Among SGLT2 inhibitor users, 57.3% had HbA1c ≥ 7%, while 27.9% remained albuminuric. Among insulin-treated participants, 84.0% had HbA1c ≥ 7%; reduced eGFR and albuminuria were also more frequent than among non-users. Despite statin therapy, 33.6% of treated participants continued to exhibit LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL. In multivariable logistic regression, insulin therapy was associated with higher odds of HbA1c ≥ 7% (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.50-15.65), while SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with lower odds of albuminuria (aOR 0.54, 95% CI 0.30-0.95). Absence of statin-containing therapy was associated with higher odds of LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL (aOR 6.01, 95% CI 3.38-10.66). Absence of statin-containing therapy was associated with higher odds of residual LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL (aOR 4.21, 95% CI 2.34-7.58). Seventy-two percent of participants presented at least three persistent cardio-renal-metabolic abnormalities, while 24.2% exhibited five or more. More than half of participants with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease were not receiving either an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant residual cardio-renal-metabolic risk persists in adults with T2DM despite use of contemporary pharmacological therapies. Disease severity markers and treatment exposure were associated with persistent adverse outcomes, but the cross-sectional design does not establish causality. The study identified potentially modifiable therapeutic gaps among patients with established cardiovascular and renal disease. Comprehensive and repeatedly reassessed cardio-renal-metabolic management, integrating pharmacological optimization with individualized risk stratification, may improve implementation of guideline-directed therapy and reduce long-term complications in routine clinical practice.

Title: Cognitive-Affective Dimension After Virological Cure of Hepatitis C Virus Infection: WBSI Dynamics, Liver Status, and the Role of Comorbidities.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Virological cure in chronic infection with hepatitis C virus (HCV) is followed by important clinical and biological benefits, including psychological ones. The White Bear Suppression Inventory (WBSI) assesses the tendency to suppress intrusive thoughts and was used in this study as a tool to provide a cognitive-affective assessment of patients with chronic HCV infection-both at the start of antiviral therapy and five years after achieving virological cure.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize patients with HCV infection who received antiviral therapy and completed the WBSI, to assess longitudinal changes in WBSI scores, and to identify clinical, biological, and comorbidity-related factors associated with these changes.
METHODS: The study employed an ambispective observational longitudinal cohort study design conducted on a sample of 386 patients, of whom 81 completed the WBSI both at baseline and at follow-up.
RESULTS: The WBSI subsample did not differ significantly from the remainder of the cohort in terms of age, cytolysis markers, bilirubin, albumin, platelet count, or major comorbidities. The WBSI score decreased significantly from baseline to follow-up, from 61.36 to 54.16, with a mean difference of 7.20 points (t = 6.32; p < 0.001). The correlation between the baseline and follow-up scores was very strong (r = 0.899; p < 0.001), indicating substantial interindividual stability. ΔWBSI was weakly but significantly correlated with the change in total bilirubin (r = 0.254; p = 0.022), with no significant correlations with the other biological markers. In the multivariable model, cardiovascular comorbidities (B = -8.469; p < 0.001) and metabolic comorbidities (B = -9.869; p = 0.002) were independent negative predictors of WBSI scoring, whereas fibrosis evolution, age, sex, and baseline total bilirubin had no significant influence.
CONCLUSIONS: Improvements in WBSI scores observed only in specific patient subgroups, one year after achieving HCV virological cure, underscore the need to integrate psychological assessment into long-term monitoring, particularly for patients with cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities.

Title: Role of Interleukin 17 in Severe Acute Pancreatitis: Human Retrospective Pilot Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Severe acute pancreatitis accounts for 20% of acute pancreatitis episodes and carries a substantial mortality risk. The systematic severity of the disease is driven by a massive cytokine release, with Interleukin-17 (IL-17) acting as a crucial modulator of the pro-inflammatory cascade. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of serum IL-17 at admission and correlate it with multi-organ dysfunctions and clinical-biological outcomes in patients with severe acute pancreatitis. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a cohort of 35 patients with severe acute pancreatitis. Demographic, etiological, and clinical-biological baseline characteristics were extracted. Serum IL-17 levels were determined at admission using the ELISA method, and data were statistically analyzed. Results: Significantly higher levels of IL-17 were observed in patients who developed multi-organ failure. Prognostic thresholds were identified via ROC analysis to predict organ dysfunctions: ≥19.77 pg/mL for neurological dysfunction (AUC = 0.814, p = 0.003) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (AUC = 0.756, p = 0.024); ≥18.45 pg/mL for respiratory (p = 0.004) and cardiovascular dysfunctions (AUC = 0.820, p = 0.002); and ≥19.81 pg/mL for renal dysfunction (AUC = 0.735, p = 0.020). Furthermore, univariate binary logistic regression identified elevated serum IL-17 as a significant prognostic factor for mortality among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (OR = 1.062, p = 0.048). Conclusions: Serum IL-17 at admission functions as a significant prognostic biomarker that reflects the severe systemic pro-inflammatory status in severe acute pancreatitis and mirrors the risk of subsequent organ dysfunctions and mortality. Incorporating IL-17 into initial risk stratification protocols may assist clinicians in timely therapeutic escalation.

Title: Temporal Dynamics of Emerging Cardiovascular Biomarkers in the Early Phase After Acute ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Prospective Single-Center Pilot Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Despite successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI), early myocardial injury and stress may contribute to left ventricular dysfunction. The optimal timing of biomarker assessment after STEMI remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the early kinetics of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2), galectin-3 (Gal-3), mid-regional pro-adrenomedullin (MR-proADM), and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) during the first 96 h after STEMI and identify potentially informative sampling time points for future prognostic assessment. Secondary, exploratory objectives were to evaluate differences in biomarker concentrations according to symptom duration, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and infarct-related artery.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center, exploratory pilot study, patients aged 18-75 years with first STEMI treated with pPCI within 6 h of symptom onset were enrolled between September 2024 and November 2025. Blood samples were collected at admission and 12 ± 4, 24 ± 4, 48 ± 8, and 96 ± 8 h after pPCI. Biomarkers were measured by ELISA, with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) as a reference marker of myocardial injury.
RESULTS: Of 46 enrolled patients, 16 were excluded, mostly due to early discharge, and 30 patients with complete samples at all five time points were included in the analysis (mean age 57.9 ± 11.1 years; 66.7% male). sST2, MR-proADM, and hs-cTnI showed significant temporal variation (all p < 0.001), with the highest measured concentrations of sST2 at 12 h and of MR-proADM at 24 h. No significant change over time was found for Gal-3 and GDF-15. In exploratory analyses, sST2 and MR-proADM concentrations were higher in patients with LVEF < 40%, and sST2 concentrations were higher in patients with left anterior descending artery (LAD) infarction. Symptom duration was not associated with biomarker concentrations.
CONCLUSIONS: sST2 and MR-proADM show distinct early post-STEMI kinetics, suggesting potentially informative sampling windows for future prognostic studies. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these kinetics and the exploratory differences according to left ventricular function and infarct location, and to evaluate the prognostic value of these sampling windows with echocardiographic and clinical follow-up.

Title: TMAO at the Crossroads of the Gut-Brain Axis: Emerging Mechanisms Linking Microbiota-Derived Metabolites to Neuroinflammation and Cognitive Dysfunction.
Abstract: Trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) is a gut microbiota-derived metabolite produced through the hepatic oxidation of trimethylamine. Although TMAO has been widely investigated as a therapeutic target in multiple cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, growing evidence suggests it may play a critical role in the neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction associated with the gut-brain axis. This narrative review summarizes the current literature to synthesize evidence on the mechanisms linking TMAO with neurological disorders; it discusses potential mechanisms contributing to this association, with particular focus on neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and activation of inflammatory pathways. Overall, this review also suggests the potential use of TMAO and its precursors as therapeutic targets for multiple neurodegenerative disorders. However, it emphasizes the need for conducting large, adequately powered randomized clinical studies to determine its therapeutic relevance.

Title: Medical emergency response related to MedicAtion InciDents (MERRMAID): a case series and lessons to improve medication safety.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence suggests that some medical emergencies in hospital are associated with preventable medication errors or adverse reactions.
AIM: The purpose of this case series was to investigate and describe the proportion of Medical Emergency Response Team (MERT) activations that are medication-related, the degree of preventability and underlying contributing factors.
METHOD: This retrospective case series included a review of MERT activations collected from an Australian tertiary hospital by two separate multidisciplinary teams. Initial review by the research team identified those that were potentially medication-related; these cases were then reviewed by an expert panel to determine the degree of causation and preventability and to identify errors within the medication management cycle and their underlying factors. The main outcome measures were the proportion of preventable medication-related MERT activations. The secondary outcome included descriptions of medications, medication errors in the context of the medication management cycle and consideration of factors underlying the errors including pharmacy review contributing to these activations.
RESULTS: Fifteen per cent (17/117) of MERT activations reviewed were medication-related, and 65% (11/17) of those were deemed preventable. The omission of medications due to errors in prescribing, administration, pharmacy review or supply stage was the main contributor to preventable medication-related MERT activations (7/11, 64%). Cardiovascular medications, predominantly metoprolol, were most implicated in preventable medication-related MERT activations.
CONCLUSIONS: Medication adverse events due to potentially error-prone steps in medication management processes are a common cause of inpatient MERT activations, presenting a considerable preventable burden to patients and healthcare resources.

Title: Sedation Versus General Anesthesia During Pediatric Electrophysiology Studies: A Paired Comparison.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anesthetic strategy may influence tachycardia inducibility during pediatric electrophysiology studies, but direct paired comparisons between sedation and general anesthesia remain limited.
METHODS: This prospective paired-comparison study included 51 pediatric patients aged 5-21 years with supraventricular tachycardia undergoing electrophysiology study under both procedural sedation and general anesthesia during the same session. Procedural sedation consisted of midazolam, fentanyl, and supplemental propofol boluses as needed. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and fentanyl and maintained with sevoflurane. Tachycardia inducibility and electrophysiological parameters were compared between anesthetic conditions using paired analyses.
RESULTS: Overall tachycardia inducibility was higher during sedation than during general anesthesia (40/51 [78.4%] vs. 29/51 [56.9%], p = 0.007). No significant differences were observed in atrial effective refractory period, ventricular effective refractory period, atrioventricular nodal Wenckebach point, jump, echo interval, or ventriculoatrial block duration. In patients with atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, inducibility decreased from 84.0% during sedation to 60.0% during general anesthesia (p = 0.109). In the Wolff-Parkinson-White/atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia subgroup, inducibility decreased from 73.1% to 53.8% (p = 0.063), and the accessory pathway effective refractory period, measured by extrastimulus pacing, was prolonged under general anesthesia (p = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: Procedural sedation was associated with greater overall tachycardia inducibility than general anesthesia during pediatric electrophysiology studies. The AVNRT and WPW/AVRT subgroups showed numerically lower inducibility under general anesthesia in the same direction as the overall finding, although these subgroup differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings support individualized anesthetic planning that considers the arrhythmia substrate, the need to preserve inducibility for mapping and post-ablation validation, and patient-specific requirements for procedural stability.

Title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Atrial Fibrillation in Brugada Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brugada syndrome (BrS) is an inherited arrhythmogenic disorder responsible for approximately 4% of sudden cardiac deaths. Atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexists and increases the risk of inappropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) therapies. Antiarrhythmic drugs are often limited by proarrhythmic effects, creating an unmet therapeutic need.
PURPOSE: We evaluated whether pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) reduces AF recurrence and provides effective rhythm control in patients with BrS and AF.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception until February 14, 2026. We included studies reporting outcomes of PVI in patients with BrS and AF. The primary endpoint was freedom from AF after ablation. Secondary endpoints included AF recurrence, changes in inappropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator shocks before versus after ablation, and procedural complications. Pooled proportions and risk differences were calculated using random-effects models.
RESULTS: A total of 2149 records were initially identified. After screening and eligibility assessment, Five studies comprising 214 participants overall, including 124 patients with BrS or Brugada-type ECG, were included in the final analysis. The mean age of participants ranged from 45.8 ± 15.5 to 57 ± 10 years, and the proportion of male patients ranged from 33.3% to 100% across studies. PVI significantly reduced inappropriate defibrillator shocks (pooled risk difference -0.35). Freedom from AF was achieved in 82% of patients. The pooled recurrence rate was 36%. A spontaneous type 1 electrocardiographic pattern was present in 10% of patients, and 32% had a family history of sudden cardiac death. Procedural complications were uncommon across studies.
CONCLUSION: PVI was associated with favorable rhythm-control outcomes and acceptable procedural safety in patients with BrS or Brugada-type ECG and AF. Inappropriate ICD shocks were less frequent after ablation, supporting PVI as a clinically relevant rhythm-control strategy in this challenging population. Larger prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

Title: Percutaneous mechanical aspiration versus medical management in tricuspid valve infective endocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous mechanical aspiration (PMA) has emerged as a treatment option for patients with tricuspid valve infective endocarditis (TVIE); however, comparative evidence on PMA versus medical management (MM) remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically review and meta-analyze clinical outcomes among patients with TVIE treated with PMA versus MM alone.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, MEDLINE Ultimate, and Web of Science were searched following the PRISMA guidelines through December 17, 2025. Studies comparing PMA versus MM alone in adult patients with TVIE were included. The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality. Secondary endpoints were in-hospital mortality, 1-year mortality, and hospital length of stay. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I V2 (Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions, version 2) tool. Random-effects models were used for quantitative syntheses.
RESULTS: Four nonrandomized studies of intervention were included in the systematic review, and 3 studies involving 252 patients were eligible for quantitative synthesis. Pooled analysis showed no significant benefit of PMA over MM alone for 30-day mortality (risk ratio, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.29-2.08; P = 0.62) or 1-year mortality (risk ratio, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.18-5.45; P = 0.99). There was no significant difference in hospital length of stay between the groups (mean difference, 2.40 days; 95% CI, -3.30 to 8.09; P = 0.41).
CONCLUSIONS: Current comparative evidence does not demonstrate a mortality benefit of PMA over MM in patients with TVIE; however, the available evidence is limited and of low to very low certainty. Prospective studies are warranted to establish the clinical indications and safety profile of PMA in patients with TVIE.

Title: Electrocardiographic screening for left atrial enlargement in dogs: derivation and validation of an algorithm combining lead II P-wave duration and the Morris index.
Journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Combining electrocardiographic measurements may improve identification of dogs requiring echocardiographic assessment. This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study derived a three-category algorithm in 150 dogs and evaluated it in 50 separate validation dogs. Three observers independently measured lead II P-wave duration and the V1 Morris index, with observer A providing the primary analysis. Left atrium-to-aorta ratio (LA/Ao) ≥ 1.6 was the primary outcome; normalized left ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN) ≥ 1.7 was evaluated independently as a secondary outcome. Thresholds from 114 reference dogs were 48 and 52 ms for P duration and 3.04 mV·ms for Morris. Positive triage comprised intermediate and high categories. Primary-outcome sensitivity and specificity were 90.6% and 50.0% in derivation and 100% and 85.7% in validation. Validation sensitivity had a 95% confidence interval of 88.1%-100%. The ordinal algorithm area under the curve was 0.961 in validation, compared with 0.868 for P and 0.844 for Morris; paired differences were not significant after Holm adjustment. Secondary-outcome validation sensitivity and specificity were 88.0% and 60.0%. The algorithm provided complementary detection of left atrial enlargement and reproducible measurements across observers, supporting further evaluation as an adjunct to echocardiographic triage.

Title: Underrepresentation of women in U.S. occupational cohort mortality studies.
Abstract: Reviews of the occupational epidemiology literature between the 1970s and 2010s found that men were more likely than women to be included in studies of occupational exposures and chronic disease. Our objective was to examine a contemporary sample of occupational cohort mortality studies to determine the extent to which women are underrepresented, how sex is used in analyses, and if the representation of women has improved over time. We searched PubMed for U.S. occupational cohort mortality studies published between 2000 and 2022 with cancer or cardiovascular disease mortality outcomes. We identified 176 U.S. cohort analyses meeting inclusion criteria. Among the cohort analyses that reported the sex of participants, 57% included men and women, 42% included men only, and 1% included women only. Sex was most commonly used in statistical analyses to adjust for confounding (69%) and to exclude women from the study population (26%). Between 2000-2004 and 2015-2022, the proportion of cohort analyses including women increased from 48% to 69%. Women remain poorly represented in occupational cohort mortality studies, although over time fewer studies excluded women. Achieving appropriate representation of women in occupational epidemiology research is essential for fully understanding relationships between occupational exposures and health.

Title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
Abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

Title: Workroom contact networks: implications for COVID-19 and other respiratory infections.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how physician workroom size affects healthcare professional contact networks and the risk of respiratory virus transmission.
DESIGN: Prospective observational study with agent-based simulations.
SETTING: Two physician workrooms of differing size (internal medicine, 208.7 sq ft; cardiology, 112.6 sq ft) in a large academic hospital.
METHODS: We deployed wireless sensor networks over 18 days in internal medicine and 14 days in cardiology workrooms. Physicians, residents, and medical students wore proximity-sensing badges during work shifts. Contacts were defined as two healthcare professionals within six feet, based on calibrated received signal strength indicators. Contact networks were generated in one-minute intervals. We simulated respiratory disease spread using a Susceptible-Infected (SI) model across varying transmission probabilities and estimated infection risk at different room densities.
RESULTS: Average occupancy was 2.7 persons in internal medicine and 2.3 in cardiology. Despite lower occupancy, the smaller cardiology room exhibited greater contact density: healthcare professionals in the smaller room had higher mean and median numbers of contacts. SI simulations showed consistently higher risk of secondary infections in the cardiology room, even at lower transmission probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: Workroom size significantly affects healthcare professional contact density and infection risk. Smaller rooms increased opportunities for transmission despite lower average occupancy. Designing larger workrooms, limiting occupancy, or reconfiguring shared spaces may reduce infection transmission in healthcare facilities.

Title: Automated Cerebrospinal Fluid Flow Quantification in Hydrocephalus Using Phase-Contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
Abstract: Quantitative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow analysis with phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging depends on segmentation and is affected by operator variability. This cohort method-comparison study evaluated whether a flow-aware deep learning (DL) model provides reproducible C2-C3 CSF segmentation and flow quantification compared with repeated manual segmentation. Ten hydrocephalus patients underwent 3-T phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging at C2-C3, with 32 magnitude and phase frames across the cardiac cycle. Three experts and one novice segmented each case twice using semi-automatic software, generating 80 manual annotations. A pretrained flow-aware 2D-UNet generated one fixed automatic segmentation per case. The inference pipeline was deterministic, meaning that repeated processing of the same input with fixed model weights and settings produced identical masks. A multi-expert reference was defined as the arithmetic mean of the expert measurements. Region of interest (ROI) surface area, peak flow amplitude, and stroke volume were compared using mean difference, Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Expert ICC(1,1) was 0.88-0.97 for surface area, 0.97-1.00 for peak flow amplitude, and 0.97-0.99 for stroke volume; novice values were 0.63, 0.95, and 0.92, respectively. Compared with the multi-expert reference, model mean differences were -0.42 mm2 for surface area, -0.00 mL/s for peak flow amplitude, and -0.01 mL for stroke volume, with CCC values of 0.50, 0.87, and 0.86. Bland-Altman limits of agreement were -69.12 to 68.27 mm2, -1.47 to 1.46 mL/s, and -0.34 to 0.31 mL. The model provided rapid, deterministic CSF segmentation with small cohort-level mean differences in peak flow amplitude and stroke volume; however, individual-level agreement with the flow-derived multi-expert reference was lower than for expert and novice segmentations obtained using the semi-automatic workflow.

Title: Cardiovascular outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors across the spectrum of myocardial infarction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) help in heart failure (HF), but their benefit after acute myocardial infarction is unclear. This meta-analysis assesses their impact on mortality and heart failure hospitalization post-acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and identifies which patients benefit most.
METHODS: Four databases were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and matched studies comparing SGLT2i with control post-AMI.
PRIMARY OUTCOMES: all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF); secondary: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Subgroups and meta-regression examined timing, diabetes, follow-up, design, SGLT2i type and baseline HF/diabetes.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies including 117 096 patients (58 613 SGLT2i vs. 58 483 control) were included. A total of 117 096 patients contributed to the all-cause mortality analysis (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.90), whereas 116 992 patients across 14 studies contributed to the HHF analysis (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.88). All-cause mortality was significantly lower in PSM observational studies (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.61-0.67), whereas the reduction did not reach statistical significance in RCTs (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.01), with a significant interaction by study design. HHF reduction occurred with both early and delayed initiation; dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were similarly effective. MACE was significantly lower with SGLT2i, but CV death, recurrent MI and stroke did not differ. Baseline HF or diabetes showed no association with primary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i reduced HHF after MI, but this benefit should be interpreted cautiously because of small-study effects and possible publication bias. The all-cause mortality benefit is driven by observational studies; RCTs show a favourable but nonsignificant trend.

Title: Development and Internal Validation of a Clinical Prediction Model for Coronary Slow Flow Phenomenon in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may exhibit coronary slow flow phenomenon (CSFP) despite the absence of obstructive epicardial coronary stenosis. Dedicated prediction tools remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a model for estimating the probability of TIMI frame count (TFC)-defined CSFP in patients with T2DM.
METHODS: Among 501 patients with T2DM undergoing coronary angiography at a single center in Xinjiang, China (2021-2025), 429 met eligibility criteria. CSFP was defined as maximum coronary stenosis <40% and TFC >27 frames in at least one major coronary artery. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 300) and validation (n = 129) cohorts. Predictors selected by penalized regression were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR), calibration, bootstrap-corrected concordance index, and decision curve analysis; additional analyses were complementary.
RESULTS: CSFP occurred in 44 patients (14.7%) in the training cohort and 16 (12.4%) in the validation cohort. The final model included smoking history, systolic blood pressure, hemoglobin A1c, lymphocyte count, and uric acid. ROC-AUC was 0.832 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.774-0.889) in the training cohort and 0.840 (95% CI: 0.733-0.946) in the validation cohort; AUC-PR was 0.467 and 0.542, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (Brier scores 0.101 and 0.084); bootstrap-corrected concordance indices were 0.827 and 0.846. Decision curve analysis suggested net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. Given the limited number of CSFP events in the validation cohort, validation estimates should be interpreted cautiously.
CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated a five-variable model for estimating the probability of TFC-defined CSFP in patients with T2DM. The model was translated into a nomogram and web-based calculator as a complementary tool for individualized risk characterization. External validation is required before broader clinical application.

Title: Holter-Detected Arrhythmias in Acute Exacerbations of COPD: NT-proBNP Correlates and Hypercapnia Associated with COPD-Related Readmission.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrhythmias are increasingly recognized during acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but their full spectrum and prognostic significance detected by continuous Holter monitoring remain insufficiently characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized for AECOPD between April 2022 and January 2025 who underwent continuous Holter monitoring. Arrhythmias were classified as atrial arrhythmias (AA), atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF/AFL), ventricular arrhythmias (VA), or coexistence of ≥2 arrhythmia types. Multivariable regression models were used to identify factors associated with arrhythmias and clinical outcomes. COPD-related readmission was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: Among 548 patients, 60.4% experienced at least one arrhythmia during hospitalization. AA (37.6%) was the most frequent subtype, followed by VA (31.0%) and AF/AFL (12.2%), while 21.5% exhibited multiple arrhythmia types. Older age, male sex, higher heart rate, elevated NT-proBNP, and larger left atrial diameter were independently associated with in-hospital arrhythmias. NT-proBNP was consistently associated with all arrhythmia phenotypes and demonstrated moderate discrimination for arrhythmia identification (AUC=0.730; cutoff, 131.5 pg/mL). AF/AFL was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (adjusted ratio=1.26, P=0.010). After accounting for the time-dependent effect of age, hypercapnia (PaCO2 ≥45 mmHg) remained associated with a higher risk of COPD-related readmission (adjusted HR=1.85, 95% CI 1.19-2.88; P=0.007).
CONCLUSION: In-hospital arrhythmias are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for AECOPD. NT-proBNP is consistently associated with multiple arrhythmia phenotypes and may aid arrhythmic risk stratification. Hypercapnia, but not arrhythmia status, remained independently associated with COPD-related readmission despite the limited sample and observational design.

Title: Long-Term Cardiovascular, Thromboembolic, and Malignancy Safety of Janus Kinase (JAK) Inhibitors in Dermatologic and Rheumatologic Populations: A Narrative Comparative Review.
Abstract: Janus kinase inhibitors are increasingly used in dermatology and rheumatology, but concerns about cardiovascular events, thromboembolism, and malignancy continue to influence long-term treatment decisions. This narrative comparative review examines evidence from randomized trials, integrated safety analyses, long-term extensions, selected observational studies, and regulatory sources, focusing on rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, atopic dermatitis, and alopecia areata. Topical agents and selective tyrosine kinase 2 inhibition are considered separately because of important differences in systemic exposure and pharmacology. The original, informally assembled evidence base was supplemented by a targeted literature update. ORAL Surveillance identified an important safety signal for tofacitinib compared with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and cardiovascular risk factors. Long-term dermatology studies have generally reported low absolute event rates, although younger study populations, restrictive eligibility criteria, limited long-term comparator data, and treatment discontinuation affect how these findings should be interpreted. Observational studies in dermatology have produced mixed results, including thromboembolic associations that warrant further investigation. Psoriatic arthritis provides additional evidence across the clinical boundaries of both specialties. Differences in patient populations, study design, outcome definitions, and statistical measures limit direct comparisons across studies. Treatment decisions should follow indication-specific prescribing requirements and consider cardiovascular disease, prior thrombosis, smoking, age, malignancy history, and available alternatives. Additional long-term comparative studies are needed to better distinguish patient-, disease-, and treatment-related risks.

Title: The Epidemiology and Associated Factors of Ectopic Pregnancy in Saudi Arabia: A Literature Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopic pregnancy (EP) is a serious maternal complication with a worldwide prevalence of about 2%. It is defined as the implantation of the product of conception outside the uterine cavity. Patients with EP may present with a wide range of clinical symptoms, including abdominal/pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, missed menstrual cycle, and an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound. After diagnosing EPs, medical and/or surgical treatment options are available based on the patient's hemodynamic status, ectopic location, fetal cardiac activity, size of the gestational sac, level of β-HCG, and patient profile.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative literature review aims to summarize published primary studies on the epidemiology and reported associated factors of EP in Saudi Arabia between 2000 and 2024.
RESULTS: A total of 1342 EP cases were reported across the included studies. Reported prevalence estimates ranged from 0.23% to 1.20%. The reviewed studies were from different regions of the Kingdom, including Abha, Khamis Mushait, Yanbu, Makkah, Madina, Jeddah, Khobar, and Majmaah. The prevalence of EPs fluctuated between 2000 and 2019 and had three peaks: 1.13% (2012), 1.14% (2013), and 1.2% (2019). Multiple associated factors linked to EP were reported in this review, including a history of pelvic surgery, C-sections, previous EP, abortions, intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) use, and pelvic inflammatory diseases (PIDs).
CONCLUSIONS: EP is a serious complication that causes significant maternal morbidity and mortality and has a substantial burden on the healthcare system. In this review, eleven studies were reviewed regarding the epidemiology of EPs in the Kingdom. No clear pattern or trend in prevalence was identified, although the majority of studies reported lower EP rates than the worldwide prevalence. Several associated factors were reported across the included studies; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because most studies were retrospective and descriptive in nature.

Title: Beyond the Threatened Limb: Acute Limb Ischemia as a Diagnostic Attractor.
Abstract: Acute limb ischemia is a time-sensitive vascular emergency, but in older patients with active cancer and multimorbidity, the threatened limb can become a diagnostic attractor: a correct specialized diagnosis that narrows attention before whole-patient physiology is integrated. We report an 81-year-old man with metastatic cecal adenocarcinoma receiving folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) who presented on day one with three days of progressive left lower limb claudication, coldness, discoloration, absent pulses, preserved motor and sensory function, and no rest pain. The presentation was clinically compatible with Rutherford I-IIa acute limb ischemia; bedside Doppler signals were not documented, precluding a definitive retrospective distinction between these categories. Concurrent findings included new atrial fibrillation, basal crackles, peripheral edema, markedly elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and troponin, bilateral pleural effusions, and radiological concern for low cardiac output. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed severe distal superficial femoral artery stenosis, long popliteal occlusion, slow distal flow, and limited runoff, favoring an acute-on-chronic ischemic process. On day two, a 6 mm x 60 mm covered stent was placed across the distal superficial femoral artery lesion. The treated lesion had a satisfactory technical result, but distal runoff remained severely compromised. Therapeutic anticoagulation initiated on day one was not maintained; discharge treatment on day three included prophylactic-dose enoxaparin and aspirin, with no rationale for the change documented in the available record. He returned on day five with recurrent coldness and toe necrosis despite normal lactate. No repeat vascular imaging was available to define the mechanism. Care became palliative on day 13, and he died on day 58. This case illustrates that a correct vascular diagnosis should not terminate integrative emergency reasoning. We propose that a vascular-plus-physiology cross-check may help preserve attention to systemic physiology and goals of care, but it is an educational framework rather than a validated clinical algorithm.

Title: Effects of Psycho-Cardiology Model-Based Psychological and Behavioural Management on Negative Emotions and Sleep Disorders in Patients With Resistant Hypertension Complicated by Anxiety and Depression.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To explore the effect of psychocardiology model-based psychological and behavioural management on top of routine cardiovascular treatment on negative emotions and sleep disorders in patients with resistant hypertension complicated by anxiety and depression.
METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed electronic medical records and follow-up data of patients treated in the Department of Cardiology of Tonglu Hospital, Hangzhou First People's Hospital Tonglu Campus between August 2022 and May 2025. A total of 126 patients diagnosed with resistant hypertension complicated with anxiety and depression who met the predefined inclusion criteria were enrolled. Based on whether the psycho-cardiology model-related assessment and psychological and behavioural management were systematically documented in their medical records, the patients were divided into a psycho-cardiology group (n = 63) and a regular group (n = 63). Changes in anxiety, depression, sleep quality, and blood pressure level were compared between the two groups during the follow-up period.
RESULTS: At the end of follow-up, the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, Hamilton Depression Rating Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores of the psychocardiology group were significantly lower than those of the regular group (p < 0.05); Reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure were greater in the psycho-cardiology group than in the regular group (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In the long-term management of patients with resistant hypertension and anxiety and depression, the psycho-cardiology model combined with psychological and behavioural management was associated with milder negative emotions, better sleep status, improved autonomic function and more stable blood pressure profiles in this retrospective cohort.

Title: Joint Association of Longitudinal Single-Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator Patterns and Hypertension Status with Incident Stroke Among Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages 0-3: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of longitudinal single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) patterns for stroke, particularly when considered in combination with hypertension (HTN), remains unclear among adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.
AIMS: This study aimed to examine the association of combined longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status with incident stroke among adults with CKM syndrome stages 0-3.
STUDY DESIGN: A nationwide prospective cohort study.
METHODS: We included adults aged ≥ 45 years with CKM stages 0-3 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. SPISE was calculated at Waves 1 and 3, and incident stroke was ascertained through Wave 5. K-means clustering was used to identify longitudinal SPISE patterns, which were dichotomized as persistently low or non-persistently low. Participants were then cross-classified according to longitudinal SPISE pattern and baseline HTN status. Cumulative SPISE exposure was calculated from repeated SPISE measurements. Cox models were used to examine associations with incident stroke. Dose-response, subgroup, sensitivity, and model-performance analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: Among 4,443 participants, 348 incident strokes occurred. A persistently low longitudinal SPISE pattern was associated with a higher risk of incident stroke than a persistently high pattern [hazard ratio (HR), 2.29; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.59-3.29]. Compared with the group with no HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern, stroke risk was higher in the group with no HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.12-1.95), the group with HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.10-2.23), and the group with HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.84-3.26). Higher cumulative SPISE exposure was inversely associated with incident stroke (HR per 1-unit increment, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93-0.97), with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. Incorporating the combined longitudinal SPISE pattern and HTN status increased the apparent C-index from 0.612 to 0.646. However, optimism-corrected discrimination was comparable between the combined model and the HTN-only model.
CONCLUSION: The combination of longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status identified a subgroup at the highest risk of incident stroke in this CKM population.

Title: Achieving Risk-Specific Absolute LDL-C Threshold with PCSK9 Inhibitors: A Real-World, Single-Center Analysis.
Journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors emerged as an effective treatment for hypercholesterolemia in clinical trials, however real-world evidence shows considerable heterogeneity. We aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of injectable PCSK9 inhibitors in real-world patients.
METHODS: Our retrospective analysis included 45 consecutive adults, 18 (40%) men, mean age 57.4 years, inadequately controlled on, or intolerant to, statins and/or ezetimibe, and newly initiated on alirocumab 75 mg or 150 mg, evolocumab 140 mg, or inclisiran 284 mg. Biochemical parameters and adverse events were recorded at baseline and when LDL-C reached the risk-specific absolute threshold or the lowest LDL-C closest to it after starting PCSK9 inhibitors (<55 mg/dL very high, <70 mg/dL high cardiovascular risk, per European Society of Cardiology). LDL-C was also assessed at standardized time points (3, 6, 12, 18, 24 months).
RESULTS: At 3 and 6 months, LDL-C decreased by a median of 54.4% and 59.2% (both p < 0.001), with 52.4% and 50.0% of patients below threshold. The best LDL-C reduction was 66.9% (from 145 mg/dL to 50 mg/dL; p < 0.001) at a median time to first documented threshold attainment of 5 months. In an exploratory analysis, no significant association was detected between LDL-C reduction and sex, diabetes, statin intensity or ezetimibe use. No clinically relevant hepatic or muscular toxicity was attributed to PCSK9 inhibitors.
CONCLUSION: In real-world patients aiming to achieve the absolute LDL-C threshold on PCSK9 inhibitors, treatment was associated with marked LDL-C reduction after a median of 5 months.

Title: Effectiveness of Digital Commitment Devices in Improving Lifestyle and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Adults with Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
AIM: Lifestyle modification is crucial for cardiovascular disease prevention but remains challenging due to complex behavioural factors such as the intention-behaviour gap. Digital commitment devices (DCD) could narrow this gap by leveraging behavioural economics, but its effectiveness remains unclear. Therefore, this review aims to evaluate the effects of DCDs on lifestyle and cardiometabolic outcomes in adults with elevated cardiometabolic risk.
METHODS: A systematic search of 12 electronic databases was conducted from database inception to August 2025. Study selection and methodological quality appraisal using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Where appropriate, effect sizes were pooled using random effects meta-analyses. The certainty of evidence for meta-analysed outcomes was assessed using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: A total of 7,378 articles were retrieved, of which 29 randomised controlled trials involving 7,534 participants were included. DCDs were found to significantly increase daily step count (WMD=664.87, 95% CI: 463.22 to 866.51, T=6.88, p<0.00001; I2=0%) and weight loss (WMD=-1.90kg, 95% CI: -2.59 to -1.21, p<0.0001; I2=70%), improve self-reported emotional (WMD=-1.34, 95% CI: -2.59 to -0.09, p=0.04; I2=0%) and uncontrolled eating (WMD=-1.74, 95% CI: -3.05 to -0.43, p=0.02; I2=0%) behaviours, body fat percentage, diet and medication adherence.
CONCLUSION: DCDs could improve lifestyle and cardiometabolic outcomes by improving physical activity and weight management, thus enhancing cardiometabolic disease prevention. Future research should prioritise long-term trials with extended follow-up periods beyond 12 months to observe physiological improvements and assess maintenance of effects.

Title: Longitudinal effects of CGRP-targeting migraine therapies on blood pressure and body mass index: A 12-month retrospective analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare blood pressure (BP) and body mass index (BMI) trajectories associated with individual calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeting migraine therapies versus matched CGRP-unexposed controls.
BACKGROUND: CGRP is a potent vasodilator with established roles in vascular homeostasis and metabolic regulation. Postmarketing surveillance identified BP elevations in erenumab-treated patients, prompting a U.S. Food and Drug Administration label update; however, comparative longitudinal data across CGRP monoclonal antibodies and gepants remain limited. Real-world evidence is needed to characterize medication-specific cardiovascular and metabolic effects in clinical practice.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using structured electronic health record data from the Jefferson Headache Center in Philadelphia, PA, USA (2018 to 2025). Adults initiating erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, atogepant, or preventive rimegepant were compared with propensity score-matched patients receiving migraine care without CGRP-targeting therapy. Twelve-month systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and BMI trajectories were evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 6361 patients were included (1892 controls; 4469 CGRP-treated; 80.4% female; mean age 45.6 ± 15.3 years). Controls demonstrated a positive within-group SBP trajectory (0.16 mmHg/month; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.06 to 0.27) and BMI trajectory (0.022 kg/m2/month; 95% CI 0.004 to 0.040) but not DBP trajectory (0.06 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.02 to 0.14). Among CGRP-treated groups, only erenumab showed a positive within-group SBP trajectory (0.11 mmHg/month; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.20); however, the difference in slope between erenumab and controls was not significant (-0.05 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.19 to 0.09). Compared with controls, atogepant (-0.38 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.61 to -0.15), fremanezumab (-0.27 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.42 to -0.11), and galcanezumab (-0.31 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.46 to -0.16) demonstrated more negative SBP trajectories. For DBP, only atogepant showed a more negative trajectory than controls (-0.18 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.32 to -0.04). For BMI, both atogepant (-0.113 kg/m2/month; 95% CI -0.159 to -0.067) and erenumab (-0.031 kg/m2/month; 95% CI -0.053 to -0.008) had more negative trajectories compared to controls.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center study, CGRP-targeting therapies were not associated with greater BP increases than matched controls. Cardiometabolic trajectories varied by medication, with generally small BP differences and a robust BMI reduction with atogepant. These findings do not support a uniform adverse cardiometabolic class effect, though prospective studies with systematic monitoring are needed to confirm long-term clinical significance.

Title: Four weeks of isometric handgrip training results in lower awake ambulatory blood pressure compared with control: a randomized clinical trial.
Abstract: We compared the effects of upper-limb (handgrip) and lower-limb (knee extension) isometric training on ambulatory blood pressure in individuals with controlled hypertension. In this randomized controlled trial, 67 adults receiving antihypertensive medication were allocated to a control group (CG, n = 22), small muscle mass isometric training (SMM, handgrip; n = 22), or large muscle mass isometric training (LMM, knee extension; n = 23). Participants completed 12 supervised sessions over 4 weeks, with the exercise protocols performed at 30% of upper-limb MVC or lower-limb maximal isometric load, respectively. Ambulatory blood pressure outcomes were compared using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for the corresponding baseline office blood pressure. Hourly 24-h profiles were analyzed using generalized estimating equations with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests. Significant between-group differences were observed only for awake ambulatory blood pressure. Compared with CG, SMM showed lower awake systolic blood pressure (121.8 ± 3.1 vs. 124.2 ± 2.6 mmHg; p = 0.017) and awake diastolic blood pressure (76.3 ± 3.6 vs. 80.8 ± 4.2 mmHg; p = 0.009). No significant differences were observed between LMM and CG, between the two exercise groups, or for 24-h and sleep blood pressure. These findings indicate that, after 4 weeks of supervised isometric training, modest between-group differences in awake ambulatory blood pressure were observed only for handgrip training compared with the control group. Greater muscle mass recruitment did not result in superior antihypertensive effects, suggesting that the chronic blood pressure response to isometric exercise is not determined solely by the amount of muscle mass involved. Trial registration: "ClinicalTrials.gov," "NCT07147595."
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Expanding Primary Care-Based Echocardiography Access in a Value-Based Care Network: Impact on Heart Failure Detection, Utilization, and Spending.
Abstract: This retrospective observational study assessed whether expanding primary care-based echocardiography access within a rural Pennsylvania value-based care network was associated with differences in heart failure (HF) diagnosis patterns, health care utilization, and spending compared with internal controls and a state-level benchmark. Eligibility, medical, and pharmacy claims were analyzed from 2 sources: third-party payers covering the primary care network and Merative's MarketScan Medicare data as a state-level reference. Members with HF-related risk factors were identified using diagnosis codes and followed for 12 months after index risk factor documentation, and the inverse probability of treatment weighting was used, incorporating age, sex, risk score, HF risk-factor category, and eligibility duration to address baseline demographic and clinical differences. Among members with HF risk factors, 21.0% of internal study members received an incident HF diagnosis compared with 13.7% of MarketScan members (P < 0.01). Internal cohort diagnoses were less likely to occur in inpatient (IP) settings than MarketScan diagnoses (0.53% vs. 10.2%; P < 0.01) and occurred after longer intervals from risk factor documentation (202 vs. 142 days; P < 0.01). Among diagnosed members, the internal cohort had lower HF-related IP admissions (21 vs. 28 per 1,000 member-years; P < 0.01), fewer HF-related emergency department visits (34 vs. 49 per 1000 member-years; P < 0.01), and lower average monthly spending ($1,937 vs. $2,826; P < 0.01).
