RESULTS: Screening increased discounted lifetime costs per person by €907 (95% CI €334-2 553) and QALYs by 0.14 (95% CI 0.07-0.31), yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €6 478/QALY. Screening increased life years by 0.30. Screening reduced acute kidney function decline (0.88 vs 0.90 events/person), heart-failure hospital days (6.47 vs 6.69 days/person), dialysis exposure (0.29 vs 0.32 patient-years/person) and transplant exposure (0.13 vs 0.14 patient-years/person).
CONCLUSIONS: In Finns aged 55 years, one-time CKD screening with eGFR/UACR followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment improves long-term outcomes and is likely cost-effective.

Title: Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy.
RESULTS: A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients <70 years (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470) (multiplicative interaction P = 0.054; relative excess risk due to interaction P = 0.016).
CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

Title: Minimally invasive anaortic quadruple and quintuple coronary artery bypass grafting: Feasibility and early outcomes of automated titanium suture fastener - a case series.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo describe the feasibility and early outcomes of automated terminal suture fastening and conventional hand tying during complex anaortic total-arterial minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG).MethodsThis retrospective, descriptive, single-center surgical case series included 12 patients who underwent elective anaortic off-pump MICS-CABG between January 2024 and May 2025. The first seven patients underwent conventional hand-tied terminal suture securing, whereas the subsequent five underwent automated terminal suture fastening, reflecting the chronological introduction of the device later in the surgeon's experience. Nine patients underwent quadruple and three underwent quintuple bypass grafting. Clinical follow-up was performed at 30 days and six months after surgery, with CT coronary angiography performed at six months.ResultsAll patients were male, with a mean age of 69.4 ± 7.5 years. Mean operating-room time was 373.0 ± 60.1 minutes overall, 384.3 ± 50.0 minutes in the hand-tied group, and 358.0 ± 75.6 minutes in the automated fastener group. No device-related technical failures, incomplete deployments, or device-related anastomotic revisions occurred. No deaths, perioperative myocardial infarctions, strokes, conversions to sternotomy or cardiopulmonary bypass, or repeat revascularizations occurred. Two patients developed pleural effusion, one developed atrial fibrillation, and one patient with pleural effusion required rehospitalization. At six-month CT angiography, all 30 arterial grafts were evaluable; 28 were classified as FitzGibbon grade A, one as grade B, and one as grade O. Both non-grade-A findings occurred in the hand-tied group, whereas all 13 grafts in the automated fastener group were grade A.ConclusionsIn this selected 12-patient, single-surgeon case series, automated terminal suture fastening using COR-KNOT® MICRO was technically achievable during complex anaortic total-arterial MICS-CABG without observed device-related failure. The small sample, chronological device introduction, operator learning curve, and short follow-up preclude conclusions regarding comparative operating-room time, safety, or graft outcomes. Larger prospective studies with anastomosis-specific timing and graft-level follow-up are required.

Title: A retrospective analysis of health care utilization and costs by body mass index category among adults with, or at risk of, cardiovascular disease.
Journal: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a need for more real-world evidence to better understand the long-term effect of excess weight on health care resource utilization (HCRU) and costs over time among people at risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) (primary prevention population) and those with established ASCVD (secondary prevention population).
OBJECTIVE: To describe all-cause HCRU and costs during a 5-year follow-up period, stratified by body mass index (BMI) category among commercially insured US adults at risk of or with known ASCVD in both primary and secondary prevention populations.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Optum administrative claims and electronic health record (EHR) data from January 1, 2007, to December 31, 2023 (study period). Included adult patients had at least 1 BMI measure in the identification period (January 1, 2008, through December 31, 2018), with the date of the first BMI measure being the index date. Patients had to have continuous health plan enrollment on a commercial insurance plan and EHR clinical activity for 12 months before index (baseline period) and 5 years after index (follow-up period). Patients were assigned to the primary prevention cohort if there was evidence of ASCVD risk factors, and patients with evidence of ASCVD conditions were assigned to the secondary prevention cohort. Cohort-specific results were reported by BMI category. The outcomes of interest were all-cause HCRU and costs. Descriptive results were reported, and adjusted cost ratios were calculated using multivariable modeling with repeated measures.
RESULTS: A total of 26,430 patients were included in the primary prevention cohort (37.9% female, 73.5% non-Hispanic White, and mean [SD] age = 53.9 [9.0] years), and 9,020 patients were included in the secondary prevention cohort (28.9% female, 73.9% non-Hispanic White, and mean [SD] age = 56.1 [9.8] years). Numerically, unadjusted total all-cause HCRU and costs increased with higher BMI classes; this was consistent across years of follow-up. In both the primary and secondary prevention cohorts, total costs among people with obesity ranged from 1.1-fold (class 1, ≥30 to <35 kg/m2) to 1.3-fold (class 3, ≥40 kg/m2) higher than those of people with normal weight after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study highlights the increasing economic impact of obesity in commercially insured people with or at risk of ASCVD. Future research is warranted to examine weight management strategies as an integral part of the primary and secondary prevention of ASCVD.

Title: Age, Gender, and Adherence in Low-density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Reduction with Statin Therapy: A Real-world Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend achieving ≥50% reduction in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in high-risk patients. Real-world data on response patterns, age and gender differences, and determinants of nonresponse remain limited. The aim of the study is to evaluate LDL-C reduction following statin therapy in routine clinical practice and to examine the influence of age, gender, and medication adherence on treatment response and cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: In this observational cohort study, adults initiated on statin therapy with documented baseline and follow-up lipid measurements were included. LDL-C levels were recorded at baseline and follow-up. The primary outcome was achievement of ≥50% LDL-C reduction.
RESULTS: In a total study population of 652 patients, statin therapy was associated with substantial early reductions in LDL-C that were largely maintained at 1 year. More than half of the patients achieved a ≥50% reduction, and nearly one-third achieved LDL-C levels <55 mg/dL. Patients >45 years demonstrated greater sustained LDL-C reduction compared with younger individuals. Numerical differences in LDL-C response were observed between men and women, although these were not statistically significant. Failure to achieve ≥50% LDL-C reduction appeared to be more closely associated with lower medication adherence rather than treatment intensity within this uniformly treated cohort. Greater proportional LDL-C reduction was associated with lower cardiovascular event rates during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In routine practice, approximately half of patients achieved ≥50% LDL-C reduction with high-intensity statin therapy. Adherence emerges as an important determinant of response. Age was associated with sustained response, whereas gender differences were not statistically significant. Nonresponse is primarily associated with modifiable treatment-related factors.

Title: Statin Utilization in High-risk Hypertensive Nigerians.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Individuals with high cardiovascular (CV) risk face major adverse CV events without statin use. However, the study of statin use among these populations in Nigeria remains limited. We examined statin use in high-risk hypertensives.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the data from 1040 patients in the Federal Medical Center Abuja Hypertension registry, recruited between 2016 and 2021. Statin use was examined among patients classified as high risk by the World Health Organization/International Society of Hypertension (WHO/ISH), the Predicting the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations, and the pooled cohort equation (PCE) scores.
RESULTS: The mean age of high-risk patients was 62.7 ± 9.3 years using the WHO/ISH model, with no difference between males and females. The prevalence rate of dyslipidemia of the total cohort was 70.7% (735), while the prevalence of statin use was 61.9% (78), 50.0% (119), and 43.3% (345) using the 10-year CV WHO/ISH, PREVENT, and PCE risk scores, respectively. Furthermore, the proportions of those with high 10-year CV risk were 12.1% (126), 22.9% (238), and 76.6% (797) for the WHO/ISH, PREVENT, and PCE risk scores, respectively. Adjusted multivariable logistic regression showed that increasing age (odds ratio [OR] =1.03 [confidence interval (CI): 1.01-1.05]), diabetes mellitus (OR = 2.45 [CI: 1.69-3.55]), and increased total (OR = 1.90 [CI 1.38-2.60]) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR = 1.83 [CI 1.32-2.52]) (P < 0.05) were the factors associated with statin use.
CONCLUSION: Our study revealed suboptimal statin utilization and significant CV risk scores disparities in identifying high-risk hypertensive patients. Co-ordinated efforts are crucial for enhancing statin use and developing locally validated CV risk prediction tools.

Title: Cardiovascular and Cancer Mortality Among Texas Residents With Cancer: A Population-Based Study in Texas.
Journal: Cancer control : journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center
Abstract: IntroductionCancer and cardiovascular disease (CVD) are leading causes of death among Texas residents. While advances in cancer treatment have increased survival, long-term survivors face elevated CVD risk. We examined temporal trends in cancer- and CVD-related incidence-based mortality (IBM) rates among Texas residents diagnosed with cancer by cancer stage, primary site, and county, and associations between the CVD-to-cancer IBM ratio and survival.MethodsUsing Texas Cancer Registry data, this retrospective cohort study calculated cancer- and CVD-related IBM rates overall and by stage and the five sites with the highest cancer- and CVD-related deaths, and assessed annual percentage change (APC) using Joinpoint regression. County-level heatmaps displayed cumulative IBM rates and CVD-to-cancer IBM ratios, defined as CVD-related IBM rate divided by cancer-related IBM rate, by these groupings. Weighted Pearson correlations with bootstrap standard errors examined associations between CVD-to-cancer IBM ratios and 1- and 5-year survival among patients diagnosed during 2010-2015, followed through 2020.ResultsIn 2010-2019, cancer-related IBM rates declined (APC = -2.51%, 95% CI -3.02 to -2.01, p < 0.001), while CVD-related IBM rates increased (APC = +1.87%, 95% CI 0.81-2.93, p < 0.001). Cancer-related IBM rates decreased, and CVD-related IBM rates generally increased across localized, regional, and distant-stage groups. CVD-to-cancer IBM ratios were higher for high-survival cancers including prostate and breast cancers. Across stages (n=4), correlations between CVD-to-cancer IBM ratio and survival were r = 0.81 (1-year) and r = 0.86 (5-year); inferential statistics were unobtainable. Across sites (n=29), correlations were r = 0.86 (5-year; 95% CI 0.80-0.93, p < 0.001) and r = 0.81 (1-year; 95% CI 0.74-0.89, p < 0.001).ConclusionsCancer-related IBM rates declined while CVD-related IBM rates increased, especially in localized-stage, high-survival sites, and specific Texas counties. Incorporating cardiovascular risk assessment and prevention early in cancer care, focusing on underserved areas, may improve long-term survival.

Title: Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood.
METHODS: Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts.
RESULTS: Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

Title: Advantages and Limitations of the Use of Robots in Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Results From a Matched Direct Comparison.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the surgical outcomes of nonrobotic and robotic minimally invasive mitral valve repair.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair from January 2014 to March 2024. After excluding the learning curve cases, early and midterm outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: A total of 422 patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair (nonrobotic, n = 103; robotic, n = 319) were enrolled. The robotic group had a higher EuroSCORE II (P < 0.001). After propensity matching, the final cohort included 84 and 168 patients in each group. In the robotic group after matching, concomitant procedures remained significantly more frequent (P = 0.030). However, operative time (P = 0.782) and cross-clamping time (P = 0.452) were comparable, whereas cardiopulmonary bypass time was significantly longer in the robotic group (P = 0.031). Postoperative blood transfusion (P < 0.001), chest tube output within 24 h (P < 0.001), and intensive care unit stay (P = 0.042) remained higher in the robotic group after matching. Postoperative mitral regurgitation was no greater than mild in both groups (P = 0.146). At 4 years, overall survival was 94.4% versus 98.4% (P = 0.215), and freedom from recurrence of moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 98.5% versus 97.9% (P = 0.230) after matching. These results are consistent with those observed before matching.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic mitral valve repair demonstrated comparable perioperative and midterm outcomes despite greater transfusion requirements and a higher frequency of concomitant procedures. The higher rate of concomitant procedures should be interpreted with caution because it may partly reflect differences in surgical era and patient selection.

Title: Optimizing Saphenous Vein Grafts: From Workhorse to an Evidence-Based Conduit Strategy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The saphenous vein graft (SVG) remains the most common conduit in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) but suffers from inferior long-term patency compared with arterial grafts. This review evaluates the concept of viewing the SVG not as an inherently flawed conduit but as one that can be systematically optimized through evidence-based strategies.
METHODS: A narrative review was conducted to address the following clinical question: "In patients undergoing CABG, how do contemporary surgical harvesting techniques, intraoperative preservation methods, and postoperative pharmacologic strategies interact to optimize the long-term patency of saphenous vein grafts?" We synthesized evidence from recent landmark randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses to define a comprehensive optimization strategy.
RESULTS: SVG failure is a cascade initiated by surgical trauma and propagated by hemodynamic stress. The "no-touch" harvesting technique, which preserves protective perivascular tissue, has demonstrated superior long-term patency in classic trials, although recent evidence has sparked debate regarding its universal reproducibility. Intraoperative preservation with endothelial-sparing solutions and aggressive postoperative pharmacotherapy-including high-intensity statins and tailored antiplatelet strategies-provide crucial secondary protection. Notably, when graft failure occurs, recent randomized evidence challenges the dogma of a strict "native vessel first" approach, supporting instead an individualized, anatomy-driven strategy that balances early procedural hazard against long-term durability.
CONCLUSIONS: The SVG is an optimizable conduit. A modern, integrated approach-combining meticulous harvesting, biological preservation, and aggressive secondary prevention-can substantially improve graft durability. By shifting focus from simple conduit selection to comprehensive conduit optimization and appropriate patient-specific target selection, the Heart Team can significantly improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Xinshuaifang improves oxidative stress injury and myocardial remodeling in acute heart failure: Association with the gut-heart axis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute heart failure (AHF) is a leading cause of death from cardiovascular disease and effective treatments are lacking.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether Xinshuaifang improves oxidative stress injury and myocardial remodeling in AHF mice by regulating the gut-heart axis.
METHODS: C57BL/6 mice aged 8-10 weeks and weighing 20-25 g were randomized into 7 groups (n=8/group): control, AHF model, AHF+Xinshuaifang, AHF+control FMT, AHF+intervention FMT, AHF+Xinshuaifang+antibiotics and antibiotics-only control. AHF was induced by isoproterenol injection (5 mg/kg, 7 days). Gut microbiota composition, oxidative stress markers (MDA, GSH, SOD, MPO), cardiac function (LVDd, LVDs, LVEF, NT-proBNP), myocardial fibrosis and tight junction protein expression (ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin-1, Zonulin) were assessed.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, model mice showed significantly reduced Verrucomicrobia and Akkermansia abundance (P<0.01), increased MDA and GSH levels, decreased SOD activity and MPO levels, reduced LVEF, elevated NT-proBNP (P<0.01), decreased ZO-1, Occludin and Claudin-1 expression and increased Zonulin expression. Xinshuaifang intervention significantly reversed all these changes (P<0.01): it increased beneficial bacteria, reduced oxidative stress, improved cardiac function, upregulated ZO-1/Occludin/Claudin-1 and downregulated Zonulin. The FMT intervention group showed similar protective effects, whereas the Xinshuaifang+antibiotics group showed attenuated protection.
CONCLUSION: Xinshuaifang improves cardiac function and alleviates oxidative stress and fibrosis in AHF mice by regulating gut microbiota, upregulating tight junction proteins and restoring intestinal barrier function.

Title: Pressure-guided pneumatic radial compression and radial artery occlusion after transradial coronary procedures: a retrospective historical cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate a pressure-measured pneumatic radial compression protocol and its association with radial artery occlusion (RAO) after transradial coronary procedures.
DESIGN: This single-center retrospective historical cohort included 514 consecutive patients treated between February and December 2025. The control group received conventional screw-type compression with clinically guided staged adjustment (n = 260), whereas the observation group received pneumatic compression with quantitative pressure measurement and individualized staged adjustment (n = 254). The primary outcome was RAO at 24 hours; RAO at 7 days and other clinical outcomes were secondary outcomes.
RESULTS: The observation group had lower observed RAO rates than the control group at 24 hours [2.8% (7/254) vs. 7.7% (20/260), P = 0.012] and 7 days [2.0% (5/254) vs. 5.4% (14/260), P = 0.040]. After Firth penalized logistic regression, the protocol remained associated with lower odds of RAO at 24 hours (adjusted OR = 0.358, 95% CI: 0.143-0.809; P = 0.013). The observation group also had lower pain scores at 6 and 24 hours (both P < 0.001), higher digital SpO2 values at 2, 4, and 24 hours (all P < 0.001), higher primary hemostatic success [97.2% vs. 93.5%, P = 0.042], and fewer patients with puncture-site oozing [2.8% vs. 6.9%, P = 0.028] or at least one local complication [11.4% vs. 28.1%, P < 0.001].
CONCLUSIONS: Pressure-guided pneumatic compression was associated with lower observed RAO rates and more favorable hemostatic and local outcomes than conventional screw-type compression.

Title: Psychosocial Screening with an Integrated Consultation Pathway for Cardiology Inpatients: A Randomised.
Physical Activity and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes With Normal Body Mass Index and Abdominal Obesity: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic implications of abdominal obesity and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in patients with type 2 diabetes who have a normal body mass index remain unclear.
METHODS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 323 029 adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index (<23 kg/m2) between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2023, from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Abdominal obesity was defined using sex-specific waist circumference thresholds (≥90 cm for men, ≥80 cm for women). MVPA was assessed through standardized self-reported questionnaires administered during routine health screenings. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, defined as a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.
RESULTS: Among the study population, 34 033 (10.5%) had abdominal obesity. During a median follow-up of 6.0 years (interquartile range, 2.6-9.0 years), abdominal obesity was associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.09-1.17]). Among patients with abdominal obesity, regular MVPA after diagnosis (27.1%) was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted HR 0.74 [95% CI, 0.68-0.80]), all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.72 [95% CI, 0.65-0.80]), ischemic stroke (adjusted HR 0.77 [95% CI, 0.66-0.89]), and hospitalization for heart failure (adjusted HR 0.75 [95% CI, 0.60-0.93]). The cardiovascular protective effects of MVPA were consistent regardless of statin or antidiabetic medication use.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index, abdominal obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Regular engagement in MVPA showed consistent cardiovascular benefits in this population, irrespective of pharmacotherapy.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT07071545.

Title: Residual Risk From Remnant Cholesterol and Inflammation Despite Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Association With Incident Peripheral Artery Disease in Type 2 Diabetes.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite guideline-recommended lipid-lowering therapy, patients with type 2 diabetes retain a significant residual risk for peripheral artery disease (PAD). The contributions of remnant cholesterol (RC) and systemic inflammation in this treated population, particularly beyond achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 18 741 participants with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank who were free of PAD and were on lipid-lowering therapy at baseline. Plasma RC and hsCRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) levels were measured at baseline. Incident PAD was ascertained over a median follow-up of 13.6 years. Multivariable Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios after adjustment for demographic, clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related covariates, including low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and baseline coronary artery disease.
RESULTS: During follow-up, incident PAD occurred in 1223 participants (6.5%). Elevated RC and hsCRP levels were each independently linked to an increased risk of PAD. Participants with concurrent elevations in both RC and hsCRP exhibited the highest risk of incident PAD. These associations remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of participants with baseline coronary artery disease, removal of events within the initial 2-year follow-up, elimination of individuals with hsCRP >10 mg/L, competing-risk analyses accounting for death, and further adjustment for detailed lipid-lowering therapy categories.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes receiving lipid-lowering therapy for primary prevention of PAD, elevated RC and systemic inflammation are independently and jointly associated with future PAD risk. These findings highlight substantial residual risk beyond managed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and support the need for further strategies targeting both remnant lipoproteins and inflammation in this high-risk population.

Title: Role of Plasma Proteins in the Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Cardiovascular Disease Events: Results From Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine Cohorts.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Socioeconomic status (SES) is strongly associated with cardiovascular disease burden and risk. Plasma proteins may elucidate a biological mechanism through which low SES increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.
METHODS: Participants from the following 3 cohorts were included: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (n=2139), Jackson Heart Study (n=967), and Women's Health Initiative (n=1104). SES was approximated using a cumulative score (range 0-3) across education, income, and employment status. A meta-analysis of Cox proportional hazards ratios was used to assess the association between SES and incident events for coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke. Linear regression was used within each cohort to determine associations between SES and Olink proteins (n=1270 proteins) and the results were meta-analyzed across cohorts. Regression-based mediation analysis was used to determine whether the identified proteins were statistical mediators of the association of SES and incident events.
RESULTS: Higher SES scores were associated with a lower risk of CHD (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.87]) and stroke (HR, 0.81 [95% CI, 0.66-1.00]). After correcting for multiple testing (P<3.937×10-5), 233 proteins were associated with SES in the meta-analysis. Of these 233 proteins, 21 had a significant indirect effect on SES and CHD. Because the SES-stroke association was not statistically significant, proteins were not tested as mediators.
CONCLUSIONS: Our analysis of multiple cohorts identified evidence of different proteomic pathways associated with SES and cardiovascular disease. This work suggests that exogenous social factors (eg, SES) may influence cardiovascular disease via proteomic profiles.

Title: Multivariate Trajectories of Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Complications in Elderly Chinese Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current study aimed to identify the multivariate trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes and investigate their associations with cardiovascular disease and diabetic kidney disease (DKD).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 27 288 patients with type 2 diabetes aged ≥60 years from China's National Basic Public Health Service Program was analyzed. All participants had ≥3 medical examinations from 2018 to 2023. A multivariate latent class mixed model was used to identify the sex-specific multitrajectories of fasting plasma glucose, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and diastolic blood pressure. Binary logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for associations with cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease, stroke, and DKD.
RESULTS: Among elderly male patients, 3 quadratic trajectory groups were identified: stable (87.16%; n=7997), U shape (3.78%; n=347), and inverse U shape (9.06%; n=831). In elderly women, 2 quadratic trajectory groups were identified: stable (87.29%; n=15 810) and inverse U shape (12.71%; n=2303). In men, the U-shape group had elevated risks of cardiovascular disease (OR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.26-2.20]), coronary heart disease (OR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.09-2.33]), stroke (OR, 1.58 [95% CI, 1.12-2.23]), and DKD (OR, 1.39 [95% CI, 1.11-1.74]); the inverse U-shape group had increased DKD risk (OR, 1.35 [95% CI, 1.16-1.57]). In women, the inverse U-shape group was associated with coronary heart disease (OR, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.12-1.53]) and DKD (OR, 1.65 [95% CI, 1.51-1.81]).
CONCLUSIONS: Distinct sex-specific trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors were associated with different risks of cardiovascular and diabetic kidney complications in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes. These findings support early identification and personalized management of adverse trajectories to potentially reduce long-term complications in this population.

Title: Testosterone, Testosterone Replacement Therapy, and Cardiovascular Disease: A Contemporary Review.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract: Whether low endogenous testosterone is causal for cardiovascular disease, and how the cardiovascular risk of testosterone replacement therapy should now be classified, remain contested, while US labeling has moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months. We conducted a targeted narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles, searching MEDLINE and primary regulatory documents from January 2000 through July 2026. Evidence was graded with a prespecified 3-tier structured author-consensus rating separating established randomized findings, unresolved secondary signals, and evidentiary absence. Low endogenous testosterone is consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality but most plausibly marks multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. Observational analyses linking normalization to lower mortality were not reproduced under randomization. Atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, fracture, and noncalcified plaque progression remain unresolved. Blood pressure rises across the class; on ambulatory monitoring the magnitude differs by individual product rather than by route. Long-term exposure and nontransdermal formulations remain untested, and the age-related-hypogonadism limitation of use is now proposed for removal. Noninferiority over 3 years should not be read as long-term clinical equivalence. Safe use of testosterone replacement therapy requires appropriate patient selection, distinction between pathologic hypogonadism and functional or age-associated low testosterone, mapping of each recommendation to its evidentiary tier, and close multidisciplinary collaboration.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Pharmacologic Therapies in Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) affects approximately one-third of all patients with HCM and carries substantial morbidity, yet no approved disease-modifying therapies exist. We conducted a systematic review of prospective interventional studies evaluating pharmacologic therapies in adults with nonobstructive HCM.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Clinicaltrials.gov was performed through September 2025. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized prospective interventional trials. A narrative synthesis was performed by pharmacologic class and outcome domain.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine clinical trials evaluating 9 pharmacologic classes were identified: cardiac myosin inhibitors, cardiac sarcomere modulators, metabolic modulators, angiotensin II receptor blockers, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2) inhibitors, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers. Cardiac myosin inhibitors demonstrated reductions in left ventricular hypertrophy, improvements in diastolic function, and marked reductions in cardiac biomarkers, although improvements in exercise capacity and symptoms were variable. SGLT2 inhibition showed concordant improvements in diastolic function, atrial remodeling, biomarkers, and functional status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive HCM and comorbid type 2 diabetes. Angiotensin receptor blockade showed signals of structural remodeling with valsartan and candesartan without consistent functional benefit. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition demonstrated largely neutral effects. Among metabolic modulators, ninerafaxstat improved ventilatory efficiency and quality of life in patients with greater baseline symptom burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic responsiveness in nonobstructive HCM is variable and appears to be mechanism- and disease stage-dependent. Ongoing trials evaluating cardiac myosin inhibitors, SGLT inhibitors, and novel therapeutic agents including ninerafaxstat and EDG-7500 will be critical in further defining the therapeutic landscape.

Title: Integrative Genomic Analyses Identify Collagen Type XXI Alpha 1 Chain and ENPEP-Fibroblast Growth Factor 5 Regulatory Pathways for Blood Pressure Variation in East Asian People.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and diabetes are common cardiometabolic disorders that may share genetic and environmental risk factors. However, the regulatory genes and tissue-specific mechanisms underlying blood pressure variations remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: Leveraging a well-characterized prospective population-based cohort comprised of 27 308 participants from the SCHS (Singapore Chinese Health Study), we evaluated genome-wide genetic associations for 5 blood pressure traits: hypertension status, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure and pulse pressure. Additionally, we conducted a transcriptome-wide association study, integrating gene expression data from 49 tissues, followed by colocalization and fine-mapping to prioritize regulatory genes. Association of identified variants with incident diabetes was additionally evaluated in the longitudinal data.
RESULTS: We validated 10 blood pressure loci (P between 1.64×10-20-4.10×10-8) and identified an East Asian-specific splice donor variant at the COL21A1 gene associated with pulse pressure (rs149344559, P=6.78×10-10). Integrative analyses prioritized FGF5 in kidney cortex and ENPEP in pituitary tissue as candidate regulatory genes. The blood pressure-lowering allele at ENPEP (T allele, rs1879056) was associated with reduced risk of incident diabetes. Mediation analysis demonstrated that ∼20.1% of the genetic association with diabetes was mediated through mean arterial pressure (Pindirect-effect<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This study refines genetic predispositions for blood pressure among East Asian individuals. We further delineate tissue-specific regulatory pathways underlying blood pressure variations and identify ENPEP-mediated dysfunctions linking blood pressure genetics to diabetes risk, underscoring integrated disease mechanisms.

Title: Greater Neighborhood Resources Predict Reduced In-Hospital Death for Children With Heart Failure and Cardiomyopathy.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with pediatric heart failure (HF) face significant morbidity and death. However, there are limited data describing neighborhood characteristics in pediatric patients with HF or exploring the relationship of these factors to resource use and clinical outcomes. We used the Child Opportunity Index 3.0 (COI), a composite index of community resources pertinent to child health, to describe neighborhood characteristics for children with HF and identify its associations with in-hospital death.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Pediatric Health Information System, a national administrative database of tertiary care pediatric hospitals. Inpatient encounters between January 2014 and December 2024 for pediatric patients (aged <18 years) with HF and cardiomyopathy were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes. The primary exposure of interest was the COI, and the primary outcome of interest was in-hospital death. Mixed logistic regression models were estimated, unadjusted and adjusted for administrative sex, age, race, and primary payor.
RESULTS: Our cohort consisted of index HF admissions in 7060 patients. Half of the cohort was in either the very low (n=2034 [29%]) or low (n=1521 [22%]) COI quintile. After adjustment, patients with a very high COI were less likely to experience in-hospital death than those living in very low COI neighborhoods (odds ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]; P=0.048).
CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of children admitted with HF have limited neighborhood resources. Those with higher neighborhood resources are more likely to survive to discharge, emphasizing the relationship between environmental factors and clinical outcomes in pediatric HF.

Title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).
METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.
RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).
CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

Title: Evaluation of Acute Electrical and Hemodynamic Improvement During Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing Modalities for Resynchronization Therapy.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While cardiac resynchronization therapy is effective in dyssynchronous heart failure, suboptimal response remains frequent. The acute hemodynamic profile of different left bundle-branch (LBB) area pacing modalities is poorly defined. Moreover, atrioventricular optimization guided by QRS duration (QRSd) may not yield the greatest hemodynamic benefit.
METHODS: Twenty-four patients with heart failure, reduced ejection fraction, and LBB block underwent sequential testing of right ventricular septal pacing, left ventricular septal pacing, nonselective LBB pacing, and selective LBB pacing during cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation in a prospective, within-subject physiological study. At each modality, electrical end points were QRSd and vectorcardiographic QRS area; hemodynamics were assessed with beat-to-beat systolic blood pressure (SBP). The atrioventricular interval producing maximal SBP improvement was compared with that producing the narrowest QRSd.
RESULTS: LBB area pacing modalities significantly reduced QRSd, compared with right ventricular septal pacing (nonselective LBB pacing, 114.0±16.8 milliseconds; selective LBB pacing, 118.4±14.1 milliseconds; left ventricular septal pacing, 124.6±16.0 milliseconds; right ventricular septal pacing, 144.4±27.6 milliseconds; all P<0.01). At the atrioventricular interval that produced maximized SBP improvement, QRSd remained narrower with LBB area pacing than right ventricular septal pacing, and selective LBB pacing provided the greatest hemodynamic improvement (ΔSBP 16.3±5.2 mm Hg), exceeding left ventricular septal pacing (13.5±6.2 mm Hg) and nonselective LBB pacing (12.8±6.3 mm Hg; all P<0.05). Across modalities, the atrioventricular interval that maximized ΔSBP was consistently shorter than that minimizing QRSd (mean difference, 18-29 milliseconds).
CONCLUSIONS: Selective LBB pacing yields the greatest acute hemodynamic benefit, and the hemodynamic-optimal atrioventricular interval is shorter than the electrical-optimal atrioventricular interval, suggesting that modest atrioventricular interval shortening after electrical optimization may better maximize hemodynamics.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT07032064.

Title: Dietary Approaches to Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Translating Mechanistic Pathways into Clinical Practice.
Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a highly prevalent and heterogeneous sleep disorder characterized by recurrent upper airway collapse during sleep, resulting in intermittent hypoxia, sleep fragmentation, sympathetic activation, and increased cardiometabolic risk. Although obesity is the most recognized modifiable risk factor, growing evidence indicates that nutritional factors influence OSA through mechanisms extending beyond body weight regulation, including systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, gut microbiota alterations, and metabolic dysregulation. The emergence of precision medicine and incretin-based therapies has further highlighted the need to integrate personalized nutritional approaches into OSA management. A literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify experimental studies, observational studies, randomized clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and international clinical guidelines addressing nutritional mechanisms, dietary patterns, gut microbiota, chrononutrition, incretin-based therapies, and precision nutrition in adults with OSA. Current evidence suggests that nutritional interventions may influence OSA through multiple biological pathways beyond weight reduction. Mediterranean and DASH dietary patterns are associated with favorable cardiometabolic effects, while dietary fiber, polyphenols, omega-3 fatty acids, and other antioxidant compounds may modulate pathways related to inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial function, and metabolic regulation. However, evidence directly demonstrating improvements in objective respiratory outcomes remains limited and heterogeneous. Emerging research also suggests potential roles for gut microbiota modulation and chrononutrition in metabolic and sleep regulation, although most evidence remains mechanistic, observational, or indirect. In addition, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual incretin agonists have demonstrated clinically relevant reductions in body weight and OSA severity, providing opportunities for integration with nutritional management. Nevertheless, evidence supporting phenotype-specific and biomarker-guided nutritional interventions remains insufficient. Nutrition represents a promising adjunctive strategy in the multidisciplinary management of OSA by targeting inflammatory, metabolic, vascular, and microbiome-related mechanisms that extend beyond weight loss alone. Future research should focus on precision nutrition approaches integrating metabolic phenotyping, biomarkers, gut microbiota, and digital health technologies to optimize personalized treatment and improve long-term clinical outcomes.

Title: Report from the 2026 Barth Syndrome Foundation International Scientific, Medical & Family Conference: Advances in Barth Syndrome Research, Therapy Development, and Clinical Care.
Abstract: The 2026 Barth Syndrome International Scientific, Medical & Family Conference was held at the Hyatt Regency Coconut Point, Bonita Springs, Florida, USA, from 19th to 25th July 2026 with scientific programming beginning 22nd July. This biennial event assembled researchers, clinicians, and affected community members for its first gathering since the U.S. FDA granted accelerated approval to elamipretide (Forzinity™; Mighty Therapeutics), the first therapy for Barth syndrome and first ever mitochondrially targeted therapy, in September 2025. Scientific sessions addressed: (1) emerging cardiolipin biology; (2) convergent identification of ABHD18 as a therapeutic target for correction of the cardiolipin phenotype; (3) advancing therapeutic strategies including AAV gene therapy, enzyme replacement therapy, and ABHD18 inhibition; (4) the elamipretide post-approval program, including the SPIBA-401 confirmatory trial; (5) natural history characterization covering infant outcomes, extra-cardiac manifestations, diaphragm weakness, neutropenia, and amino acid metabolism; (6) regulatory and drug development strategies in ultra-rare indications; and (7) international Centers of Expertise models and the launch of the BarthINSIGHTS registry. This report summarizes the key scientific advances, discussions, and future priorities as they relate to Barth syndrome biology, therapeutic development, and clinical care.

Title: DNA Methylation and Metabolic Syndrome in Midlife Women of the ELEMENT Cohort.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a cluster of metabolic risk factors that markedly increase the risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. Its prevalence exceeds 50% among Mexican women. A growing number of studies suggest that DNA methylation, an epigenetic mechanism, is linked to MetS. Methylation risk scores (MRS) may be able to predict future disease risk, yet prospective studies with MRS and MetS are rare, especially in Hispanic populations. We aimed to (1) replicate previously reported locus-specific DNA methylation-MetS associations, (2) identify additional loci, and (3) evaluate an MRS for predicting MetS among a sample of midlife Mexican women. Methods: We analyzed 149 women from the Early Life Exposure in Mexico to Environmental Toxicants (ELEMENT) cohort with DNA methylation measured in blood leukocytes collected around 2008 and MetS assessed approximately ten years later. Logistic regression was applied to a priori loci, and then all loci on the Infinium EPICv1 array. MRS performance was evaluated by cross-validation. Results: Four loci-probe ID cg11024682 (SREBF1), cg06500161 (ABCG1), cg22891070 (HIF3A), and cg02650017 (PHOSPHO1)-showed consistent associations with MetS. For example, each 1-percentage-point increase in methylation at cg11024682 (SREBF1) was associated with higher odds of MetS in the fully adjusted model (OR = 1.30; 95% CI: 1.12-1.52). No additional loci reached Bonferroni significance, though marginal associations with MetS components were observed. The MRS derived from four replicated loci was associated with higher odds of MetS per 1-SD increase in the training set (OR = 3.55; 95% CI: 2.03-6.22). In the independent testing set, the MRS-only model improved prediction compared with the baseline covariate-only model (AUC = 0.652 vs. 0.398; ΔAUC = +0.254). Conclusions: This study provides prospective evidence that specific DNA methylation markers are associated with MetS risk in midlife Mexican women. These loci, now replicated in several cohorts, are promising biomarkers for early identification and prevention of MetS.

Title: A Combined Workplace Intervention Including Exercise and Nutrition for Health Promotion in Obese Office Workers: A Randomized Controlled Study.
Journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
Abstract: Background: During the last decades, the office workplace setting has increasingly become an inherently "obesogenic" environment, promoting unhealthy behaviors. The main objective of this study was to investigate the efficacy of a 6-month workplace combined (exercise and nutrition) intervention in obese office workers, using a randomized controlled study. An additional objective of this study was to evaluate the individual responses per participant following the program. Methods: In total, 36 obese office workers (BMI: ≥30) were randomly assigned to two equal groups: intervention (IG; age: 48.06 ± 6.60 yrs; BMI: 33.57 ± 1.58 kg/m2) and control (CG; age: 47.95 ± 5.95 yrs; BMI: 33.54 ± 1.74 kg/m2). The IG participated in a daily supervised 6-month workplace program (during working hours), including (a) exercise (flexibility, balance, strength, and aerobic) and (b) counseling and educational activities for healthy diet and hydration. The CG did not participate in any intervention. Before and after the 6-month period, the following were measured: (a) health indices (body fat, body circumferences, blood pressure, respiratory function, and lipidemic profile), (b) functional capacity indices (flexibility, balance, handgrip strength, and cardiovascular fitness), and (c) adherence to the Mediterranean diet (MedDietScore) and daily water consumption. Results: All the participants of the IG reduced body mass, body fat, and circumferences (-4.47 to -18.95%), blood pressure (-4.08 to -46.15%), lipidemic profile indicators (-2.50 to -212.67%), and heart rate recovery (-9.62 to -57.33%), while increased respiratory function (1.82-20.26%), flexibility (5.13-50%), balance (15.38-88.83%), handgrip strength (5-25%), MedDietScore (12.5-56%), and water consumption (23.08-50%). In CG, all aforementioned indices remained unchanged (p = 0.16-0.99). Conclusions: A combined workplace intervention (exercise and nutrition) constitutes an effective approach for health promotion in obese office workers.

Title: Musculoskeletal Findings Following Pre-Participation Screening in Young Athletes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
Journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
Abstract: Background: Pre-participation screening (PPS) is widely used to evaluate athletes before sport participation, traditionally focusing on cardiovascular risk prevention. However, musculoskeletal assessment performed during PPS may also allow early identification of biomechanical and structural abnormalities that can affect sport participation during growth. Objectives: This study aimed to describe the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and management pathways of musculoskeletal alterations detected during PPS in young athletes, with particular focus on referral patterns to pediatric Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) specialists. Methods: This retrospective observational study included athletes aged ≤15 years who underwent PPS between January 2022 and December 2023 at the Sports Medicine Unit of Noale (ULSS 3 Serenissima, Venice, Italy). Musculoskeletal screening was systematically performed during PPS. Athletes presenting newly detected abnormalities were either managed conservatively by the sports physician or referred for PM&R evaluation. Clinical indications for referral, imaging investigations, diagnoses, and treatment strategies were analyzed. Results: A total of 707 athletes underwent PPS during the study period. After applying exclusion criteria, 635 athletes were eligible for analysis. Musculoskeletal alterations were identified in 141 athletes (22.2%). Among them, 54 athletes were referred for PM&R evaluation and 40 completed the consultation. No statistically significant differences were observed between referred and non-referred athletes. The most frequent reasons for referral were suspected scoliosis (n = 22), foot alignment disorders n = 18), thoracic hyperkyphosis (n = 5), and lower limb length discrepancy (n = 4). Specialist evaluation resulted in conservative management in most cases, including corrective exercise programs and orthotic interventions, while one athlete required surgical treatment for congenital scoliosis. Conclusions: Musculoskeletal screening during PPS identified a broad spectrum of findings in young athletes, including clinically relevant abnormalities requiring specialist evaluation and management. These findings suggest that musculoskeletal assessment may provide an opportunity for early clinical identification within PPS; however, prospective studies are needed to evaluate diagnostic accuracy, long-term clinical benefit, injury prevention, and cost-effectiveness before routine implementation can be recommended.

Title: Reappraising the safety of menopausal hormone therapy for women-implications for the clinic.
Journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
Abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is currently the most effective treatment for vasomotor and other estrogen deficiency-related symptoms. Despite its proven efficacy, concerns regarding long-term safety, particularly breast cancer, venous thromboembolism, and cardiovascular disease, have influenced clinical practice and patterns of MHT use over the past decades. This review summarizes the evolution of evidence regarding the safety of systemic MHT, from the introduction of conjugated equine estrogens in the 1940s through landmark randomized clinical trials to contemporary evidence and international guideline recommendations. Early concerns regarding endometrial safety with estrogen-only treatment were largely resolved by the addition of progestogens for women with an intact uterus. The Women's Health Initiative trial fundamentally changed perceptions of MHT cardiovascular safety, but subsequent analyses established the "timing hypothesis," demonstrating that the benefit-risk profile depends on age and time since menopause at treatment initiation. More recent evidence has highlighted clinically relevant differences between estrogen formulations, routes of administration, and type of progestogen. Transdermal estradiol is associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism than oral estrogen, while micronized progesterone and dydrogesterone may offer a more favorable breast safety profile than some synthetic progestins, although randomized evidence is lacking. Current evidence supports an individualized approach to MHT, with treatment decisions based on symptom burden, age, time since menopause, route of estrogen administration, type of progestogen, and individual risk factors. For healthy women initiating therapy before age 60 years or within 10 years of menopause, the overall benefit-risk profile is favorable. Future research should focus on optimizing formulation-specific safety, generating comparative randomized evidence, and further refining personalized treatment strategies to maximize benefits while minimizing risks.

Title: The association between prolactin and myocardial function in type 2 diabetes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prolactin has been associated with cardiovascular mortality. The primary objective was to assess the association between prolactin and systolic function in patients with type 2 diabetes. Secondly, to assess the association between prolactin and diastolic function, NYHA classification, glucose, and lipid levels.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study of the Thousand&2 cohort, including 1,030 individuals with type 2 diabetes from secondary care. Echocardiography and biochemical assessment were performed at baseline. Systolic function was estimated primarily as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), secondly as global longitudinal strain (GLS), and E/e' as a marker of diastolic function. The association between echocardiography and prolactin was assessed using linear regression, presented with crude as well as adjusted estimates for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Prolactin assessments were available for 937/1030 (91%), and 14/937 (1.5%) individuals had prolactin levels above the upper reference limit. Prolactin was not associated with LVEF or GLS, whereas prolactin was associated with E/e' and NYHA classification in fully adjusted analysis in men but not in women. Prolactin was not associated with glucose or lipid levels in men or women.
CONCLUSION: Prolactin was not associated with impaired systolic function in men or women with type 2 diabetes; on the other hand, prolactin was associated with poorer diastolic function in men with type 2 diabetes. The current results point towards a gender specific effect of prolactin on the diastolic function of the heart.

Title: Genetic and functional analysis of CDH2 reveals new insights into CDH2-related disorders.
Journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Pathogenic variants in CDH2 cause agenesis of the corpus callosum, cardiac, ocular, and genital syndrome (ACOGS). We aimed to define the clinical and molecular landscape of CDH2-related developmental disorders.
METHODS: Newly identified and previously reported families were analyzed for genotype-phenotype correlations; variants were assessed using protein modeling and splicing assays.
RESULTS: Screening identified 20 new families carrying (likely) pathogenic ((L)P) alleles (n=16) or high-priority variants of uncertain significance (VUS) (n=4), including 12 novel CDH2 alleles. The combined (L)P cohort (37 individuals) showed variable ACOGS core features (mean 3; range 1-5), along with abdominal wall and/or diaphragmatic hernias and nipple, spine or gastrointestinal anomalies, each seen in ∼20% of individuals. Novel ACOGS findings included ambiguous genitalia, female genital malformations and dilated cardiomyopathy. Missense variants, principally within extracellular cadherin domains, accounted for 86% of unique (L)P alleles with clusters in EC1 and EC4-EC5; the remainder produce late protein truncations or in-frame deletions. Disruption of calcium binding was predicted by modeling. Conversely, VUS were primarily nonsense-mediated decay-sensitive or deletions (71%), linked to neurodevelopmental, kidney or other anomalies.
CONCLUSION: We expand the ACOGS spectrum and highlight its striking clinical variability. Additionally, we identify a possible milder phenotype associated with CDH2 haploinsufficiency.

Title: GDF-15 as an early marker for prognosis in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest - Experience from the HAnnover COoling REgistry.
Journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

Title: Soluble E-selectin and QRISK3-based Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Prospective Case-control Study from India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with metabolic abnormalities and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Endothelial dysfunction is considered an early event in atherogenesis, and soluble E-selectin has been proposed as a marker of endothelial activation. However, its role in cardiovascular risk assessment in PCOS remains uncertain.
AIM: The study aimed to compare circulating soluble E-selectin levels between women with PCOS and healthy controls and evaluate their association with metabolic parameters and QRISK3-based cardiovascular risk scores.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: Prospective hospital-based case-control study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two hundred women with PCOS diagnosed according to the Rotterdam criteria and 50 age-matched healthy controls aged 18-40 years were enrolled. Clinical assessment, anthropometry, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, C-reactive protein and soluble E-selectin levels were evaluated. Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk was calculated using the QRISK3 algorithm.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Group comparisons, correlation analyses and multivariable linear regression were performed.
RESULTS: Mean soluble E-selectin levels were comparable between women with PCOS and controls (0.61 ± 0.33 vs. 0.61 ± 0.29 ng/mL, P = 0.935). Within the PCOS group, soluble E-selectin correlated positively with HbA1c (r = 0.326, P = 0.001) and fasting blood glucose (r = 0.271, P = 0.001), while no significant associations were observed with anthropometric measures, lipid parameters, blood pressure or QRISK3 scores. In multivariable analysis, fasting blood glucose remained independently associated with soluble E-selectin.
CONCLUSION: Soluble E-selectin levels did not differ between women with PCOS and controls and showed limited associations with cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not support a major role for soluble E-selectin in cardiovascular risk assessment among young women with PCOS.

Title: Kidney Outcomes in Structural Heart and Cardiac Surgical Trials: The Case for Longitudinal Endpoint Reporting.
Abstract: The 2026 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/American Diabetes Association/American Society of Nephrology guideline on cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome establishes kidney function as a determinant of cardiovascular risk rather than an adjacent comorbidity. Endpoint architecture in structural heart and cardiac surgical research has not been revised accordingly. Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 standardized acute kidney injury reporting with considerable rigor, staging injury on Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes serum creatinine criteria and requiring that new renal replacement therapy be reported discretely, but its scope is confined to the periprocedural window. No endpoint tracks filtration trajectory across follow-up, no threshold within the standard defines chronic kidney disease stage progression, and initiation of maintenance dialysis years after intervention has no reporting convention distinct from temporary replacement therapy in the immediate postoperative period. Pivotal trials consequently adjudicate cardiovascular outcomes for five years and kidney outcomes for 30 days. Registry evidence suggests the omission is consequential, with rapid filtration decline documented in more than a third of patients carrying preexisting kidney impairment within five years of cardiac surgery. This editorial argues for longitudinal reporting of estimated glomerular filtration rate, prespecification of stage progression and maintenance dialysis as adjudicated endpoints, and nephrology representation on trial steering committees with a defined role in kidney endpoint specification.

Title: Cardiac camp: An outreach program to build health literacy among underrepresented in medicine adolescents and increase diversity in medicine.
Journal: Journal of education and health promotion
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eliminating racial and ethnic disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires multilevel action, including improving health literacy and diversifying the healthcare workforce. To contribute to this goal, UCSF medical students designed an immersive summer camp to teach underrepresented minority backgrounds in medical professions (URM) high school students about CVD and encourage interest in healthcare careers.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A stipend-supported, 1-week cardiology summer camp for URM Bay Area high school students was implemented by medical students. Participating students completed a preprogram and postprogram survey to assess various metrics, including knowledge of CVD, comfort discussing and teaching concepts of CVD, and interest in medical careers on a Likert scale of 1-5. The mean differences in preprogram and postprogram scores in the second cohort in 2024 (n = 25) were assessed.
RESULTS: Twenty-five students participated in the second iteration of Cardiac Camp @ UCSF (80% female) from July 24 to 28, 2024. Most identified as URM (84%), and many came from households where English was not the primary language (76%). Postcamp surveys showed increased mean scores in CVD knowledge and awareness of medical careers. Open-ended responses indicated that students enjoyed the camp activities and felt more motivated to pursue healthcare careers.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac Camp @ UCSF provides a novel framework for a pipeline program aimed at inspiring URM high school students to pursue careers in medicine. Short-term survey results showed increased CVD knowledge and confidence teaching others, aligning with Healthy People 2030 goals to reduce cardiovascular disparities and strengthen workforce diversity.

Title: A randomised controlled trial comparing a 100% chitosan haemostatic dressing and a manual compression device following transradial coronary intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemostasis at radial access sites following transradial coronary intervention (TRCI) is usually achieved using manual compression devices (MCDs). Despite their widespread use, MCDs have limitations, including prolonged compression and haemostasis times as well as increased risk of radial artery occlusion (RAO), thus highlighting the need for alternative strategies to achieve faster and safer radial haemostasis.
AIMS: We sought to compare the safety and efficacy of a 100% chitosan haemostatic dressing (CHD) with an MCD in achieving radial access site haemostasis following TRCI.
METHODS: A total of 258 patients were randomly assigned to receive either a CHD (n=130; Axiostat) or an MCD (n=128; TR Band) for radial haemostasis following TRCI. Time to haemostasis, post-application pain, and access site complications - including rebleeding, haematoma, RAO, and allergic reactions - were assessed.
RESULTS: Both groups had similar baseline and procedural characteristics. The CHD significantly reduced haemostasis time (5.84±2.19 min) compared with the MCD (120.2±21.88 min; p<0.001). Post-application pain scores were low and comparable between both groups. The CHD was associated with lower rates of haematoma and rebleeding. RAO occurred in 3.12% of MCD patients, while no RAO events were observed with the CHD. No serious adverse events or device-related complications were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: The CHD provided rapid haemostasis with a shorter compression time, lower RAO risk, and reduced patient-reported pain, along with minimal rebleeding, few haematomas, and no allergic events compared with MCD, without compromising safety. This clearly illustrates that the CHD is a safe and effective alternative for achieving haemostasis following TRCI, potentially enabling earlier patient ambulation and discharge.

Title: A semi-rapid deployment workflow to reduce device time in Evolut FX self-expanding transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: As transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) expands, improving deployment efficiency is increasingly important. We developed and implemented a semi-rapid pacing-assisted deployment workflow for the Evolut platform.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the procedural efficiency and early safety of this workflow for transfemoral (TF) Evolut FX TAVI.
METHODS: In a single-centre registry, we performed a retrospective before-and-after analysis of consecutive TF Evolut FX procedures: semi-rapid deployment (n=48) versus conventional deployment (n=53). Device time was defined as the interval from initial advancement of the delivery system to final release of the Evolut FX valve. Prolonged device time was defined as >14 minutes (>75th percentile), and determinants were assessed using Firth's penalised logistic regression.
RESULTS: The device time was shorter with semi-rapid deployment (9.0 [interquartile range [IQR] 6.0-13.0] minutes vs 14.0 [IQR 11.0-16.0] minutes; p<0.001), while operation and procedure times were similar (p=0.13 and p=0.16, respectively). The mean recapture count was higher in the semi-rapid group (0.85±1.09 vs 0.53±0.70; p=0.08), and contrast volume was higher (32.0 [IQR 25.0-42.0] mL vs 25.0 [IQR 15.0-33.0] mL; p=0.008). Paravalvular leak >=mild (31.2% vs 32.1%; p=1.0) and in-hospital pacemaker implantation (2.1% vs 7.5%; p=0.37) did not differ significantly between the groups. In multivariable analysis, recapture predicted a prolonged device time (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.75-14.19; p=0.002), whereas the semi-rapid workflow predicted a reduced device time (adjusted OR 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01-0.66; p=0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Semi-rapid pacing-assisted Evolut FX deployment selectively reduced device time without compromising early in-hospital safety outcomes. Deployment efficiency represents a practical procedural target for workflow refinement in self-expanding TAVI.

Title: γ-Butyrobetaine, L-carnitine and acylcarnitines and their association with incident atrial fibrillation among men and women with suspected chronic coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
AIMS: Carnitine-metabolites play a key role in cell energy metabolism and have been implicated in the pathogenesis of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, any associations between L-carnitine and the precursor γ-butyrobetaine (γBB) with new-onset AF are not established. We therefore examined the relationship between serum γBB, L-carnitine and selected acylcarnitines with incident AF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied 3815 patients who underwent coronary angiography due to suspected chronic coronary syndrome and followed up for incident CVD events, including new-onset AF. Risk associations between the biomarkers and incident AF were explored by logistic regression for the total population and stratified according to sex. The majority (71.6%) of the patients were men, the median age was 61 years. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years, 412 (10.8%) were reported with new-onset AF. In a multivariate model higher serum γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine [OR per 1SD (95% CI): 1.15 (1.01-1.31), P = 0.04; 1.14 (1.01-1.27), P = 0.03 and 1.15 (1.03-1.28), P = 0.01] were associated with increased risk of incident AF. These associations were particularly stronger among women (P for interaction < 0.04, all).
CONCLUSION: In this large cohort of patients with suspected chronic coronary syndrome elevated circulating levels of γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine were associated with increased risk of incident AF, with stronger associations among women. Our results motivate further studies examining the relationship between carnitine metabolites and cardiac arrhythmias and highlight the need for sex specific analyses.

Title: First Report of Real World Utilization of an Activin Signaling Inhibitor in Patients With Severe Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in the Middle East PH RISE-ME Study.
Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality despite advances in combination therapy. Sotatercept, an activin-signaling inhibitor, is a novel disease-modifying therapy targeting pulmonary vascular remodeling. Real-world data from Middle Eastern populations remain limited. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study evaluating the real-world effectiveness and safety of Sotatercept in adults with PAH treated at a tertiary pulmonary hypertension expert center in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, between January 2025 and September 2026. Clinical, echocardiographic, biochemical, and risk-stratification data were extracted from electronic medical records. Primary outcomes were changes in right atrial (RA) area and NT-proBNP. Secondary outcomes included systolic pulmonary arterial pressure (SPAP), TAPSE/SPAP ratio, 6-min walk distance (6MWD), risk profile, and safety. Thirty-six patients were prescribed Sotatercept, of whom 33 received at least one dose. Most patients were female (80.6%), with a mean age of 55 years. Significant reductions occurred in RA area (- 2.67 cm2; 95% CI, -4.16 to -1.18; p < 0.001), NT-proBNP (- 46.7 pmol/L; 95% CI, -87.19 to -20.39; p < 0.001), and SPAP (- 6.00 mmHg; 95% CI, -12.00 to -0.50; p = 0.031). TAPSE increased significantly (+ 0.25 cm; 95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33; p < 0.001), and TAPSE/SPAP improved significantly (+ 0.064; 95% CI, 0.030 to 0.108; p < 0.001). Patients improved by at least one risk category. The 6MWD did not change significantly. Treatment was well tolerated, with no adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation or death; two all-cause deaths occurred during follow-up. In this real-world Middle Eastern PAH cohort, Sotatercept was associated with improved right-heart remodeling, NT-proBNP, and risk profile, with acceptable short-term safety. These findings complement trial evidence and provide early regional support for activin pathway inhibition in routine practice.

Title: Cenobamate in super-refractory status epilepticus: current evidence from a patient-level synthesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Super-refractory status epilepticus (SRSE) represents a challenging neurological emergency, with limited therapeutic options after conventional intravenous antiseizure medications (ASMs) and continuous anesthetic therapy have failed. Cenobamate has shown remarkable efficacy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but its role in SRSE is currently supported only by isolated case reports.
METHODS: We performed a patient-level synthesis of published cases of cenobamate-treated SRSE, focusing on treatment latency, titration strategy, electroclinical response, concomitant therapies, safety, and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: Three publications reporting six patients were identified. Cenobamate was introduced between 13 and 103 days after SRSE onset, following failure of multiple intravenous and oral ASMs, anesthetic agents, and, in most cases, immunomodulatory therapies. Although the timing of treatment initiation varied substantially, electroencephalographic improvement generally occurred within two weeks after cenobamate initiation and was usually accompanied by clinical recovery, successful withdrawal of anesthetic therapy, and liberation from the intensive care unit. Most patients initiated cenobamate at the recommended dose of 12.5 mg/day but underwent individualized dose-escalation schedules compared with the approved outpatient regimen.
