No cases of drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms, severe cardiac adverse events, or treatment discontinuation attributable to cenobamate were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the available evidence remains limited to a small number of observational reports, this patient-level synthesis identified consistent clinical patterns that support further investigation of cenobamate as an adjunctive therapy for SRSE. At present, no conclusions regarding treatment efficacy can be drawn. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to clarify cenobamate optimal timing, titration strategy, safety, and potential role within SRSE treatment algorithms.

Title: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) in right ventricular failure and preserved LV ejection fraction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) failure with preserved left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF ≥50%) is a distinct clinical entity often associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH), chronic lung diseases, or congenital heart defects, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI), such as sacubitril/valsartan, have demonstrated efficacy in left-sided heart failure, but their role in isolated RV failure remains understudied.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted from 2010 to 2025 for RCTs and prospective cohorts assessing ARNI in patients with RV failure and preserved LVEF. Inclusion: Adults with RV dysfunction (e.g., TAPSE <17 mm or RV S' <9.5 cm/s) and LVEF ≥50%; ARNI vs. standard care or pre-treatment; reporting RV parameters, sPAP, NT-proBNP, 6MWD, or NYHA class.
RESULTS: Three studies (1 RCT, 2 prospective cohorts; n=120 patients) were included. ARNI improved TAPSE (WMD 1.2 mm, 95% CI 0.7-1.7; p<0.001; I²=0%), RV S' (WMD 0.5 cm/s, 95% CI 0.2-0.8; P=0.002; I²=0%), and reduced sPAP (WMD -7.5 mmHg, 95% CI -10.2 to -4.8; p<0.001; I²=15%). NT-proBNP decreased (WMD -1200 pg/mL, 95% CI -1700 to -700; p<0.001; I²=0%). 6MWD increased (WMD 30 m, 95% CI 10-50; P=0.003; I²=0%). NYHA class improved (RR 1.65 for ≥1 class improvement, 95% CI 1.15-2.37; P=0.007; I²=0%).
CONCLUSION: ARNI enhances RV function, reduces pulmonary pressures, and improves functional status in RV failure with preserved LVEF.

Title: Outcomes by Comorbidities with Tremelimumab and Durvalumab in the Randomized, Controlled Phase 3 HIMALAYA Study in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often have underlying comorbidities, which may impact prognosis and lead to safety challenges following treatment. This exploratory, post hoc analysis of the phase 3 HIMALAYA study (NCT03298451) assessed outcomes in participants with unresectable HCC and cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities at baseline.
METHODS: Participants with unresectable HCC were randomized to STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab), durvalumab monotherapy, or sorafenib. Comorbidities were based on medical history assessed at baseline and qualified using preferred terms from cardiovascular or metabolic Standardised Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Queries. Overall survival (OS) rates were evaluated in participants with or without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities within and by treatment group. The proportion of long-term survivors (alive ≥36 months post-randomization) and safety were assessed in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities. Data cutoffs: August 27, 2021 (primary analysis); January 23, 2023 (4-year updated analysis, OS, and serious treatment-related adverse events).
RESULTS: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus were the most common cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities, respectively. The 48-month OS rates with STRIDE were 28.0% and 21.7% in participants with and without cardiovascular comorbidities and 20.4% and 28.5% in those with and without metabolic comorbidities, respectively. In total, 28.2% of participants with cardiovascular comorbidities and 22.6% of participants with metabolic comorbidities experienced long-term survival with STRIDE. Safety in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities was generally consistent with all participants in the safety analysis set; no new safety signals were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: OS benefits with STRIDE were similar in participants with vs. without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities, with manageable safety in participants with comorbidities. These results support the durable benefits of STRIDE in a broad population reflective of unresectable HCC globally.

Title: Fetal arrhythmia and heart disease during COVID-19 pandemic in patients who underwent echocardiography.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the characteristics and the occurrence of fetal heart diseases and arrhythmias in pregnancies that underwent fetal echocardiography examination during COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data extracted from the Fetal Ultrasound and Fetal Medicine Departments of Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, a tertiary hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, from January to December 2021. The sample was analyzed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney test. Logistic regression was performed to assess the risk of fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease.
RESULTS: A total of 148 fetuses were included in the analysis. The prevalence of fetal heart disease/arrhythmia was higher among patients with maternal comorbidities (73.3% vs. 39.1%), fetal defects (14.3% vs. 0.8%), and functional abnormalities (26.7% vs. 4.5%). Maternal COVID-19 showed no significant association with fetal cardiac outcomes. Maternal comorbidity, fetal malformation, and the presence of functional abnormalities were identified as independent risk factors.
CONCLUSION: Maternal comorbidities were associated with fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease, but no causal relationship was found between COVID-19 and adverse fetal cardiac outcome.

Title: Biolimus- versus sirolimus-eluting stents in percutaneous coronary intervention: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-eluting stents (SES) are a benchmark in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), while biolimus-eluting stents (BES), which combine a more lipophilic analogue with a biodegradable polymer, may enhance healing and reduce thrombosis. Whether these BES features translate into improved survival and cardiac outcomes compared with SES remains uncertain.
AIMS: We sought to perform a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials evaluating BES compared with SES in adult patients undergoing PCI.
METHODS: This meta-analysis encompassed randomised and controlled clinical trials that directly compared BES with SES in the setting of percutaneous coronary intervention. A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials up to June 2025. The main outcomes assessed were all-cause and cardiac mortality, while secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularisation (TLR), and stent thrombosis (ST). Outcomes were evaluated at <=1 year (early) and >1-5 years (midterm) using pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) in random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed by the I2 test.
RESULTS: Six trials (12,109 patients: 6,088 BES, 6,021 SES) were analysed. BES reduced 1-year cardiac death by 30% (RR 0.70, 95% CI: 0.52-0.93) and showed a non-significant 19% reduction in all-cause death (RR 0.81; p=0.058). MACE, myocardial infarction, and TLR were similar between stents across timepoints. BES showed a non-significant early increase in ST (RR 1.85; p=0.12) but a 46% reduction in late ST (RR 0.54, 95% CI: 0.33-0.88). Mortality rates converged after 1 year.
CONCLUSIONS: BES offer a short-term reduction in cardiac mortality and late stent thrombosis compared with SES, with otherwise similar morbidity outcomes. These results support the short-term safety of BES and indicate a possible long-term thrombotic and cardiac survival benefit, warranting confirmation in longer-term trials.

Title: Classic case report: concomitant pulsed field ablation, cavotricuspid isthmus ablation and percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion in a patient with prior intracranial haemorrhage.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (pLAAO) offers single-procedure rhythm control and stroke prevention in patients unable to tolerate long-term oral anticoagulation. Patients with prior intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) from suspected cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) have among the strongest contraindications to anticoagulation yet are absent from randomized trials of concomitant procedures, and combining pulsed field ablation (PFA) with pLAAO introduces energy-specific considerations.
CASE SUMMARY: A 66-year-old woman with persistent AF, cavotricuspid isthmus-dependent atrial flutter and a CHA2DS2-VA score of 3 had been off anticoagulation for 2 years after an ICH. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed microhaemorrhages and siderosis suggestive of CAA. Through a single transseptal puncture, four-vein PFA was performed first to avoid electrical interaction with the nitinol pLAAO frame, followed by WATCHMAN FLX deployment under transoesophageal echocardiographic and computed tomography (CT)-fluoroscopy guidance and radiofrequency cavotricuspid isthmus ablation. She received edoxaban without aspirin for three months. Cardiac CT then confirmed device seal without device-related thrombus, and all antithrombotic therapy was withdrawn.
DISCUSSION: Randomized trials show that anticoagulation after ICH prevents ischaemic stroke at the cost of a marked increase in recurrent haemorrhage, and lobar or CAA-related haemorrhage carries the least favourable balance. Concomitant ablation and pLAAO delivers rhythm control and stroke prevention with one transseptal access and one time-limited exposure to anticoagulation. Combining PFA with pLAAO requires sizing the occluder before ablation, because PFA induces acute pulmonary ridge oedema, and completing pulmonary vein isolation before deployment to avoid arcing against the nitinol frame.

Title: Dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for pure native aortic regurgitation via transfemoral access: a meta-analysis of contemporary outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR) poses unique technical challenges for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), including annular dilatation and absent calcification for anchoring. Whilst dedicated aortic regurgitation (AR) devices have been developed, their comparative performance against off-label devices specifically via transfemoral access - the contemporary standard approach - remains incompletely defined.
AIMS: We aimed to compare the outcomes of dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for PNAR via transfemoral access in contemporary practice.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed (MEDLINE) and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2020-November 2025) for studies reporting transfemoral TAVI outcomes in PNAR. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression was performed.
RESULTS: Twenty-four studies (2,956 patients) were included comprising 25 cohorts: 4 cohorts (537 patients) evaluated dedicated devices, and 21 cohorts (2,419 patients) assessed off-label devices. Overall, 30-day mortality was 3.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.3-4.8%). Dedicated devices showed a trend towards lower mortality (1.9% vs 4.1%, odds ratio [OR] 0.45, 95% CI: 0.20-1.00; p=0.051; risk ratio 0.40, 95% CI: 0.19-0.83). Dedicated devices achieved higher device success (95.8% vs 85.7%, OR 3.64; p=0.012), lower rates of residual AR >=moderate (0.6% vs 6.2%, OR 0.11; p=0.048), reduced valve embolisation (2.0% vs 7.3%, OR 0.26; p=0.048), and fewer reinterventions (2.0% vs 7.9%, OR 0.22; p=0.010). Permanent pacemaker implantation (20.8%), stroke (2.6%), and major bleeding (3.0%) were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary transfemoral TAVI for PNAR, dedicated devices demonstrated superior procedural outcomes compared with off-label devices. These findings support the preferential use of dedicated devices in this population, though randomised trials are needed to establish definite treatment recommendations.

Title: Vascular aging biomarkers: the role of ADMA, SDMA, and inflammation.
Abstract: Cardiovascular risk assessment based on traditional risk factors may not fully capture subclinical vascular injury and vascular aging, supporting interest in biomarkers reflecting underlying vascular mechanisms. Endothelial dysfunction, altered methylarginine metabolism, and chronic low-grade inflammation represent interconnected processes that may contribute to vascular aging. This narrative review summarizes evidence on the associations of asymmetric dimethylarginine, symmetric dimethylarginine, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with subclinical atherosclerosis and vascular aging. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched between January and August 2026, with priority given to studies evaluating associations of these biomarkers with subclinical vascular changes, vascular aging, and cardiovascular outcomes. ADMA shows the most consistent associations with subclinical atherosclerosis, although these vary across arterial territories and vascular measures. Evidence for SDMA in early vascular disease is more limited, and interpretation is complicated by its dependence on renal function, although some associations persist after adjustment for renal function. IL-6 has biological and genetic evidence supporting a role in atherogenesis, but its associations with subclinical atherosclerosis are not consistently independent of traditional cardiovascular risk factors. hsCRP is an established cardiovascular risk marker and has also been associated with progression of carotid stenosis and arterial stiffness. Differences in vascular endpoints, study populations, confounder adjustment, and analytical methods contribute to heterogeneity across studies. Overall, these biomarkers appear to reflect partly distinct but interconnected components of vascular aging. Their potential relevance may lie in their complementarity; however, current evidence does not establish that combined assessment improves evaluation beyond conventional approaches. Prospective studies should determine whether their combined assessment improves identification of accelerated vascular aging beyond conventional risk assessment.

Title: Optimal depolarization sequence for cardiac resynchronization therapy patients.
Abstract:
AIMS: Electrical ventricular dyssynchrony is a hallmark of intraventricular conduction disease in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Although cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is effective, a proportion of patients with electrical dyssynchrony evidenced by an electrocardiogram (ECG) remain non-responders. Besides the QRS duration, visualization and quantification of the depolarization sequence could contribute to improving CRT response. The study aimed to evaluate the CineECG-derived mean temporo-spatial isochrone trajectory of depolarization in CRT patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Among the adult cohort of 121 patients who underwent CRT implantation, there were 93 (33% female) responders and 28 (7% female) non-responders. ECGs recorded before and immediately after CRT implantation were collected and analysed using the CineECG modality with a generic heart/torso model. The CineECG-derived path directions were computed for the QRS on anteroposterior, interventricular, and apicobasal axes within the cardiac anatomy. Spatial depolarization characteristics were tested for the association with left ventricle reverse-remodelling at 6-month follow-up. The pre-implantation depolarization sequence was predominantly from the right to the left ventricle, and after the CRT implant, it has been transformed into an apicobasal direction. In multivariate logistic regression, the pre-implant QRS duration, apicobasal depolarization gradient, and CRT-induced QRS shortening independently predicted CRT response. The Akaike information criterion indicated that combining all three yielded the strongest predictive model.
CONCLUSION: CineECG-derived depolarization gradients, which reflect ventricular activation sequence, changed significantly after CRT, and the pre-implantation apicobasal gradient independently predicted echocardiographic outcome, with a less pronounced gradient associated with better haemodynamic response.

Title: Plasma neurofilament light chain and risk of death and stroke in community-dwelling elderly individuals.
Abstract:
AIMS: Circulating neuroinjury biomarkers such as neurofilament light chain (NFL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) have emerged as indicators of brain health. While NFL predicts stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation, its prognostic value in unselected elderly populations is uncertain. We investigated the associations of NFL and GFAP with cardiovascular events and death in community-dwelling older adults.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Baseline plasma NFL and GFAP concentrations were determined using high-sensitivity Simoa® assays in 806 participants aged 75 years from the Prospective Investigation of the Vasculature in Uppsala Seniors (PIVUS) study. Cox regression models with sequential adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, renal function, and NT-proBNP assessed associations with ischaemic stroke, myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death, all-cause death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; stroke, myocardial infarction, and all-cause death). During a median follow-up of 10 years, 55 ischaemic strokes, 48 myocardial infarctions, 52 cardiovascular deaths, and 188 all-cause deaths occurred. Neurofilament light chain was not independently associated with ischaemic stroke or myocardial infarction and showed no independent association with cardiovascular death after adjustment including NT-proBNP. In contrast, higher NFL was independently associated with all-cause death (adjusted hazard ratio per doubling 1.91; 95% CI 1.49-2.46) and MACE (1.53; 95% CI 1.21-1.93), and improved discrimination for all-cause death beyond established risk factors. Glial fibrillary acidic protein was not associated with any outcome.
CONCLUSION: In community-dwelling elderly individuals, higher NFL was associated with increased risk of death but not with specific cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that NFL reflects overall physiological vulnerability rather than discrete vascular risk.

Title: Sex-Specific Cross-Sectional Associations and Exploratory Mediation Analysis of Cardiovascular Disease Risk by Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio in Cadmium-Exposed Populations.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, with its burden continuing to rise. Environmental cadmium (Cd) exposure has emerged as a potential risk factor for CVD. This study aimed to investigate the associations between Cd exposure and CVD risk, and to explore cross-sectional associations and a potential inflammatory pathway using exploratory mediation analysis.
METHODS: This study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Logistic regression models were used to identify factors influencing CVD risk. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using restricted cubic splines (RCS). Exploratory mediation analysis was conducted to assess the potential mediating role of NLR in the association between Cd exposure and CVD risk.
RESULTS: Individuals with CVD had significantly higher levels of blood Cd, urinary Cd, and NLR than controls (p < 0.05) in both sexes. In males, the highest quartile (Q4) of blood Cd (OR = 3.06, 95% CI: 1.45-6.46, p = 0.004) and urinary Cd (OR = 3.02, 95% CI: 1.52-6.02, p = 0.002) were significantly associated with higher CVD prevalence. Conversely, no significant association was observed in females for blood Cd (p = 0.505), and the association for urinary Cd (p = 0.046) was notably weaker and less robust than that in males. Interaction analyses confirmed sex-specific differences (p-interaction < 0.05). NLR showed significant exploratory mediating effects (indirect effects), accounting for 9.4% (95% CI: 3.5%-15.2%) of the blood Cd-CVD link and 5.0% (95% CI: 1.9%-8.1%) of the urinary Cd-CVD link in males. Similar significant mediation was observed in the general population for blood Cd: 7.2% (95% CI: 2.2%-12.2%), and for urinary Cd: 6.4% (95% CI: 2.8%-10.0%).
CONCLUSIONS: This cross-sectional study identified significant sex-specific and dose-dependent associations between Cd exposure and CVD risk. Inflammatory responses, particularly those reflected by elevated NLR, were cross-sectionally associated with the observed Cd-CVD link, suggesting a potential pathway that warrants prospective validation, especially in males.

Title: SGLT-2 inhibitor dapagliflozin improves left ventricular diastolic function and reduces circulating inflammatory markers in HFpEF patients: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study sought to evaluate the efficacy of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor Dapagliflozin in ameliorating left ventricular diastolic function (LVDF) and attenuating systemic inflammatory biomarkers in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
METHODS: A total of 114 patients diagnosed with HFpEF were retrospectively enrolled and allocated into either the SGLT-2 inhibitor group (Dapagliflozin combined with standard guideline-directed therapy; n = 58) or the Control group (standard guideline-directed therapy alone; n = 56). Echocardiographic parameters at baseline and 6-month follow-up were measured, including early diastolic transmitral flow velocity/early diastolic mitral annular velocity ratio (E/e') and left atrial volume index (LAVI). Circulating inflammatory markers comprising high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) were examined. In addition, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels and Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ) scores were collected for functional and symptomatic assessments.
RESULTS: After six months of treatment, the SGLT-2 inhibitor group exhibited significant improvements in cardiac diastolic parameters. E/e' ratio decreased significantly from 14.8 ± 3.2 to 12.1 ± 2.7 (P < 0.001), and LAVI decreased from 38.6 ± 8.4 to 34.2 ± 7.1 mL/m2 (P = 0.003). Consistently, systemic inflammation was markedly alleviated. hs-CRP decreased from 4.82 ± 1.73 to 2.94 ± 1.28 mg/L (P < 0.001), IL-6 decreased from 8.46 ± 2.91 to 5.73 ± 2.14 pg/mL (P = 0.002), and TNF-α decreased from 12.8 ± 4.6 to 9.4 ± 3.8 pg/mL (P = 0.011). Moreover, NT-proBNP levels in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group exhibited a substantial 28.4% reduction, which was significantly greater than the 8.7% reduction observed in the Control group (P = 0.004). There was also a striking reduction in MLHFQ scores in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group (average reduction: -8.6 ± 4.2 points, P < 0.001), demonstrating significant symptomatic improvement.
CONCLUSION: SGLT-2 inhibitor Dapagliflozin effectively improved LVDF and reduced systemic inflammatory burden in patients with HFpEF. These findings support the role of Dapagliflozin as a promising disease-modifying therapeutic agent for HFpEF.

Title: Prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes of infective endocarditis in people living with HIV: A systematic review and meta-analysis of intravenous drug use and microbiological profiles.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis (IE) poses a significant challenge in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLWH), with risk factors and outcomes potentially differing from HIV-negative counterparts. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to explore the prevalence, risk factors, mortality, and clinical characteristics of IE in PLWH versus HIV-negative patients.
METHODS: Methods : Six databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Embase, and ProQuest) were searched up to January 2025 using terms including "Infective Endocarditis" and "Human Immunodeficiency Virus." Random-effects meta-analyses with Freeman-Tukey transformation were used to estimate pooled prevalence, mortality, and odds ratios (ORs) for IE by HIV status. Between-study heterogeneity (I²) and meta-regression were assessed to explore sources of variation.
RESULTS: Results : Seventeen independent studies collectively reported 3,082 IE cases (2,095 among PLWH and 987 among HIV-negative individuals), analyzed as separate study-level data rather than a single combined cohort. The pooled prevalence of IE among PLWH was 33.2% (95% CI: 14.97-54.45%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² > 90%), highlighting the exploratory nature of these estimates. Among PLWH with IE, 85.5% (95% CI: 65.8-98.1%) reported intravenous drug use (IVDU), and 60-80% had right-sided IE (predominantly tricuspid valve), contrasting with left-sided predominance in HIV-negative patients. Mortality among PLWH with IE was 14.7%, compared with 22.3% in HIV-negative individuals. Staphylococcus aureus was the leading pathogen (24-73%).
CONCLUSIONS: Given the high and persistent heterogeneity, findings should be interpreted as exploratory. PLWH with IE frequently exhibit IVDU and right-sided involvement, while mortality appears comparable to HIV-negative patients after accounting for IVDU, emphasizing behavioral rather than virologic determinants of risk.

Title: Quality of Care of Patients with Stable and Stabilized Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction at the Medical Wards of a Tertiary Center in the Philippines: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) remains a major contributor to morbidity and mortality among Filipinos. Contemporary ESC and ACC/AHA guidelines emphasize quality indicators aimed at optimizing outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to evaluate the quality of care received by stable and stabilized HFrEF patients admitted to the medical wards of a tertiary center in the Philippines, focusing on physician adherence to guideline-recommended quality indicators.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was done through review of charts involving all adult HFrEF patients aged ≥19 years admitted to the medical wards of a tertiary hospital from November 2022 to April 2023. Quality-of-care assessment included prescription of Class I guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) at discharge for eligible patients, as well as non-pharmacologic indicators such as scheduling of post-discharge follow-up and referrals to a heart failure clinic or cardiac rehabilitation. Descriptive statistics were used; analyses were performed using STATA 13.1. QI of 80% was considered to be optimal quality of care.
RESULTS: A total of 148 patients were included; most were male (69.6%) with a mean age of 56 ± 14 years. Hypertension (62.8%) and diabetes (41.2%) were the most frequent comorbidities. Beta-blockers, ACEi / ARB / ARNI, and diuretic prescription were high (95.17%, 91.41%, and 100%, respectively). In contrast, prescription of MRA and SGLT2i was 68.50% and 55.56%, respectively. Post-discharge physician appointments within 4 weeks were arranged in 91.54%. Only 27.7% were referred to cardiac rehabilitation, and 2.31% were referred to the heart failure clinic.
CONCLUSION: Quality of heart failure care at the medical wards upon discharge is acceptable for pharmacologic quality indicators and post-discharge appointments. However, referrals to specialized heart failure services and cardiac rehabilitation remain suboptimal and represent opportunities for quality improvement.

Title: Severe Pulmonary Hypertension in Critically Ill Children: A 10-Year Single-Center Case Series and Practical Management Considerations.
Abstract: Severe pulmonary hypertension (PH) in children may decompensate rapidly during intercurrent illness and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). We describe the clinical presentation, intensive care management, and outcomes of four children with severe PH admitted to a tertiary PICU between January 2014 and December 2024. Three patients were infants, and one was an 11-year-old girl with a history of extreme prematurity and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. All four presented with acute respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and cardiovascular compromise following a recent respiratory tract infection. PH was documented predominantly by echocardiography, with findings including elevated estimated pulmonary pressures, right ventricular (RV) pressure overload, interventricular septal flattening, and/or RV dysfunction. Right heart catheterization was performed in one patient. All patients received supplemental oxygen, diuretics, and sildenafil. Two required invasive mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support, while one patient received additional prostanoid and endothelin receptor antagonist therapy. The median PICU length of stay was 15 days (range: 10-24 days). Two patients survived to hospital discharge, whereas two died following refractory pulmonary hypertensive crises. These cases highlight respiratory infection as an important potential precipitant of acute decompensation in children with severe PH and illustrate the challenges of supporting the failing RV in the PICU. Although the small sample size and retrospective design preclude conclusions regarding treatment efficacy or prognostic factors, the cases emphasize several practical management priorities: early recognition of deterioration, prompt correction of factors that increase pulmonary vascular resistance, preservation of RV function and systemic perfusion, cautious escalation of respiratory support, and early multidisciplinary involvement. Based on these principles and the published pediatric PH literature, we propose a practical, physiology-based management algorithm for severe PH and pulmonary hypertensive crisis in the PICU.

Title: SGLT2 inhibitors and exercise in diabetic kidney disease: mechanistic rationale, emerging clinical evidence, and future perspectives.
Abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major complication of diabetes and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure worldwide. Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, residual risks of renal and cardiovascular disease remain considerable, underscoring the need for complementary therapeutic strategies. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have emerged as cornerstone therapies for DKD because of their glucose-independent renoprotective and cardioprotective effects. Exercise, meanwhile, provides broad metabolic, cardiovascular, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant benefits and is recommended as an integral component of diabetes and chronic kidney disease management. Increasing evidence suggests that these two interventions may exert complementary effects on several interconnected pathways involved in DKD progression, including glomerular hyperfiltration, metabolic dysregulation, oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and renal fibrosis. This review summarizes the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying DKD and examines the mechanistic rationale for integrating SGLT2 inhibitors with exercise. We further discuss emerging experimental and clinical evidence regarding their potential effects on renal function, metabolic control, cardiovascular health, and exercise capacity, together with important safety considerations and challenges in individualized exercise prescription. Although available evidence provides a biologically plausible basis for potentially additive interactions between these interventions, direct clinical evidence supporting the superiority of combined therapy over either intervention alone remains limited. We therefore highlight key knowledge gaps, including the lack of adequately powered randomized controlled trials, standardized exercise protocols, and validated biomarkers for monitoring treatment response. Future studies should establish the efficacy, safety, and optimal implementation of combined SGLT2 inhibitor and exercise strategies across different stages and phenotypes of DKD, thereby facilitating their translation into individualized cardiorenal care.

Title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in a Pacemaker-Dependent Child with Syndromic Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: A Case Report with Prospective 9-Month Follow-Up.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is an emerging noninvasive neuromodulation therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). However, evidence regarding its use in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices, particularly pacemaker-dependent children, remains extremely limited.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 6-year-old boy with genetically confirmed TAF6-related Alazami-Yuan syndrome, severe developmental impairment, complete atrioventricular block requiring permanent epicardial VVIR pacing, and syndromic DRE refractory to multiple antiseizure medications (ASMs). Auricular taVNS was initiated at the cymba conchae under multidisciplinary supervision using stimulation parameters of 25 Hz, pulse width 250 μs, intensity titrated to tolerance up to 1.7 mA, for 4 h/day. Treatment initiation was performed in the pediatric intensive care unit with continuous electrocardiographic monitoring for 5 days. The patient underwent prospective follow-up over 9 months using caregiver-maintained seizure diaries, serial electroencephalography (EEG), serial electrocardiography, repeated pacemaker interrogation, adverse event surveillance, and Pediatric Quality of Life Family Impact Module (PedsQL-FIM) assessments. No arrhythmias, pacing abnormalities, device malfunction, or clinically significant pacemaker parameter changes were observed during follow-up. A mild transient local skin irritation resolved with conservative care. Seizure burden decreased from 2 to 4 prolonged seizures daily at baseline to approximately two brief generalized tonic seizures weekly, with sustained improvement through month 9. Reduction of ASM burden began only after clinical improvement had already been observed. Follow-up EEGs remained markedly abnormal with only limited interval electrographic change. PedsQL-FIM improved progressively from 10.4 at baseline to 54.9 at month 3, 80.6 at month 7, and 84.0 at month 9.
CONCLUSION: Auricular taVNS was successfully administered in a pacemaker-dependent child under structured multidisciplinary monitoring without identifiable cardiac or pacemaker-related adverse events during 9 months of follow-up. Although efficacy and safety conclusions cannot be inferred from a single case, this report supports the clinical feasibility of combining noninvasive vagal neuromodulation with permanent cardiac pacing in carefully selected pediatric patients.

Title: Vagal Response and Cough Reflex During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Under Deep Sedation: A Comparison Across Pulsed Field Ablation Systems.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is increasingly used for atrial fibrillation (AF), but device-specific autonomic and respiratory reflex responses remain insufficiently characterized. We aimed to compare vagal responses and cough reflexes among three commercially available PFA systems across individual pulmonary veins and the posterior wall.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 200 consecutive patients who underwent AF ablation with FARAPULSE (n = 83), PULSESELECT (n = 83), or VARIPULSE (n = 34). Vagal response was operationally defined as bradyarrhythmia requiring temporary back-up pacing during energy delivery. Cough reflex was assessed intraprocedurally at the left superior pulmonary vein (LSPV), left inferior pulmonary vein (LIPV), right superior pulmonary vein (RSPV), right inferior pulmonary vein (RIPV), and posterior wall.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally similar among groups, although heart failure and diabetes mellitus (DM) differed significantly. Overall vagal response rates did not differ among FARAPULSE, PULSESELECT, and VARIPULSE (61.4%, 67.5%, and 58.8%, respectively; p = 0.596). In contrast, overall cough reflex rates differed significantly (75.9%, 91.6%, and 55.9%; p < 0.001), driven by consistently higher rates with PULSESELECT. On logistic regression, male sex, body mass index, and use of PULSESELECT versus FARAPULSE were independently associated with cough reflex.
CONCLUSIONS: Cough reflex was most frequent with PULSESELECT, whereas no significant difference in vagal response was observed among platforms. Recognizing these differences may improve procedural planning, sedation strategy, and prophylactic management during PFA.

Title: Combined aromatherapy and music or sound for emotional distress: a systematic review of controlled studies published between 2019 and 2026.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emotional distress is common around clinical procedures, cancer supportive care, and health-professions training. Aromatherapy and music are easy to deliver, yet it remains unclear when combining them is worthwhile and whether the combination offers more than either component alone.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize experimental studies of aromatherapy combined with music or sound published from January 2019 through September 7, 2026; identify the populations and settings in which benefits were most consistent; and separate benefit over inactive care from incremental benefit over a single sensory intervention.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, APA PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, CENTRAL, CNKI, and Dentistry & Oral Sciences Source from January 1, 2019, to September 7, 2026. Randomized trials and controlled nonrandomized or quasi-experimental studies were eligible when they included an identifiable arm combining aromatherapy with music or sound and reported emotional-distress or related physiological outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized narratively using SWiM guidance.
RESULTS: Twenty-four studies involving 2,530 participants from 12 countries or regions were included. Of these, 21 were randomized studies and three were controlled nonrandomized or quasi-experimental studies. The evidence covered procedural and perioperative care, dentistry, nursing education and occupational stress, and cancer or palliative care. Results were most consistent in pediatric dentistry, magnetic resonance imaging, nursing examinations or skills testing, and some repeated cancer-support programs. Two lithotripsy trials and the adult endodontic study did not show a clear benefit. Although combined treatment often outperformed inactive care, it frequently failed to outperform aromatherapy or music alone. Adverse events, acceptability, and economic outcomes were poorly reported.
CONCLUSION: Combined aromatherapy and music or sound showed the most consistent reductions in anxiety or distress in pediatric dentistry, MRI examinations, nursing examinations or skills training, and some perioperative and cancer-support settings. Clear benefit was not demonstrated in lithotripsy or endodontic care; in general surgery, pregnancy non-stress testing, coronary angiography, palliative care, and outpatient oncology, the combination generally did not outperform a single modality. Future adequately powered factorial trials should standardize the interventions and use prespecified between-group comparisons, longer follow-up, and systematic reporting of adverse events and costs.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024570691, CRD42024570691.

Title: Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS) Inhibitors in High-Risk Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Cardio-Renal Risk.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASi) are recommended as first-line therapy for patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly in the presence of hypertension or albuminuria. This study assessed the treatment patterns in a cohort of high-risk T2D patients.
METHODS: This cross-sectional, retrospective study included 33,524 adults with T2D from the Imperial College London Diabetes Centre (United Arab Emirates). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters (estimated glomerular filtration rate, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and blood pressure (BP)), and medication usage were analysed. The primary outcome was the analysis of treatment patterns in patients undergoing RASi; secondary outcomes included prescribing trends in CKD risk categories and among hypertensive and albuminuric subgroups.
RESULTS: Among 33,524 patients with T2D, mean age was 59.2 years, BMI 29.4 kg/m2, and 67.1% (n=22,508) of the patients were classified as KDIGO (Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes) G1 and 73.3% (n=24,580) as A1 albuminuria. Overall, 35.3% (n=13,705) received RASi, while 64.7% (n=25,128) were treated with alternative therapies including SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, or finerenone. Among patients with albuminuria >3.5 mg/mmol, only 62% (n=4944) were prescribed RASi, despite meeting clear indications for treatment. In KDIGO-based risk stratification, only 39% (n=4406) of patients in the high and very high CKD progression risk categories were on RASi. Among the hypertensive subgroup (n=4,824; defined as BP >130/80 mmHg), 48.96% (n=2,362) were prescribed RASi, leaving over 50% of patients untreated with this guideline-recommended therapy. Furthermore, 7.46% (n=2,462) of the entire cohort had hypertension but were not receiving RASi. This gap was more prominent among those with coexisting albuminuria or CKD. These findings reflect under-treatment even among those at greatest risk of renal and cardiovascular events.
CONCLUSION: In patients with T2D and established renal or cardiovascular risk, treatment patterns remain variable in real-world practice. Less than half of hypertensive or albuminuric patients received RASi, highlighting a significant implementation gap. Addressing barriers to RASi prescription is essential to align real-world clinical practice with international guidelines and improve patient outcomes.

Title: Changes in triglyceride-glucose index and progression of coronary artery calcification in asymptomatic adults: a longitudinal cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a readily available surrogate marker of insulin resistance; however, the association between changes in TyG index and coronary artery calcification (CAC) progression remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 14,407 Korean adults without cardiovascular disease who underwent two baseline examinations during 2012-2018 and at least three examinations overall. At each baseline examination, TyG index status was classified as low or high using a predefined cutoff, yielding low-to-low (L-L), low-to-high (L-H), high-to-low (H-L), and high-to-high (H-H) groups. CAC progression was defined as a difference of ≥2.5 between the square root-transformed coronary artery calcium score (CACS) of the follow-up and index examination. Cox proportional hazards and linear mixed-effects models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 5-year fold changes, respectively.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 5.34 years, 4,139 participants experienced CAC progression. Compared with the L-L group, the risk of CAC progression increased across the L-H, H-L, and H-H groups, with adjusted HRs (95% confidence intervals) of 1.07 (0.96-1.19), 1.14 (1.02-1.27), and 1.30 (1.20-1.41), respectively. Associations differed between CAC subgroups (p for interaction <0.001), with more pronounced associations observed among participants with CACS of zero at both the first and index examinations. The 5-year fold change was 11% higher in the L-H group than in the L-L group and 9% lower in the H-L group than in the H-H group.
CONCLUSION: Changes in TyG index status were associated with CAC progression, particularly among individuals without detectable CAC. Serial TyG index assessment may aid in cardiovascular risk stratification.

Title: Ultrasound-guided circulatory management strategy for improving microcirculatory dysfunction and promoting organ function recovery in critically ill shock patients.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate whether ultrasound-guided circulatory management improves microcirculatory perfusion, accelerates organ function recovery, and enhances clinical outcomes in critically ill shock patients compared with standard care.
METHODS: Our retrospective cohort study was performed in the adult ICUs of Xuanwu Hospital and consecutive screening of ICU admissions of January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025. In total, 200 eligible shock patients were categorized in accordance with the leading initial circulatory management approach following shock detection: conventional guideline consistent care (control, n=100) and organized point-of-care ultrasound guided care (observation, n=100) on the basis of protocolized evaluation at pre-arranged decision points to phenotype hemodynamics and progressively oversee the administration of fluids and vasoactive introduction/adjustment with reassessment. The primary outcome was organ support-free days until day 28 (death = 0). While time to shock resolution, shock-free days to day 7, ICU/hospital length of stay, ICU mortality, ICU readmission, discharge disposition, and 90-day EQ-5D were some of the secondary outcomes. Mechanistic endpoints included 0-6 h metrics of resuscitation, 24-h hemodynamic/ultrasound phenotype, SOFA trajectory, day 5 and baseline/24-h biomarkers.
RESULTS: Compared with usual care, the ultrasound-guided strategy reduced early fluid exposure and net fluid balance within 6 h (P=0.004 and P=0.001, respectively) and lowered norepinephrine dose and norepinephrine ≥0.30 μg/kg/min use at 6 h (P<0.001 and P=0.010). At 24 h, patients receiving ultrasound-guided management had higher MAP, improved cardiac performance, and less vasopressor dependence (all P≤0.015), with a lower prevalence of moderate-severe LV dysfunction (P=0.001). Clinically, the intervention shortened time to shock resolution (P<0.001) and increased organ support-free days to day 28 (P<0.001). SOFA scores improved more rapidly (P<0.01 at 24 h; P<0.001 at 48 h, 72 h, and 5 days), accompanied by better renal perfusion and lower injury biomarkers (all P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Optimized early resuscitation (less fluid and lower vasopressor exposure), better 24-h hemodynamic and renal microcirculatory phenotypes, faster SOFA recovery, more organ support-free days, and faster shock resolution, with at least a partial association with reduced renal injury, were observed in patients receiving ultrasound-guided circulatory management. These findings indicate potential benefits but do not establish causality due to the retrospective, single-center study design.

Title: The association between migraine and SCORE2 - a Swedish cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Migraine affects more than one billion people globally and is associated with higher cardiovascular risk. In clinical practice in Europe, cardiovascular risk is often assessed with SCORE2, to identify patients who need preventive care. This study aims to explore the potential association between a register-based diagnosis of migraine and SCORE2 in a cross-sectional study of 40- and 50-year-old people screened for unhealthy lifestyle habits and cardiovascular risk, in Sweden.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was performed with data from a cardiovascular screening program, called Targeted Health Dialogues, which included questionnaires, blood pressure measurements and blood samples. Diagnoses of migraine were collected from a regional patient register, from year 2000 and ahead. Firth's penalized logistic regression was used to calculate odds ratios (ORs) for moderate/high SCORE2 dependent on diagnosis of migraine. The regressions were stratified by sex and stepwise adjusted for age, level of education and country of birth. Multivariable linear regression models with SCORE2 as a continuous variable were also used to assess the association.
RESULTS: Of the 9 190 participants, 875 (9.5%) had a diagnosis of migraine. In 628 cases (72%) it was not possible to distinguish between migraine with and without aura; therefore, these groups were analyzed together. The unadjusted ORs for having a moderate SCORE2 was 0.60 (0.22-1.32) for women with migraine and 1.13 (0.80-1.58) for men with migraine. Adjustments led to almost unaltered results.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cross-sectional cohort, the OR of medium/high SCORE2 was not significantly different between individuals with and without a register-based diagnosis of migraine. However, this study could not rule out an existing association. Future studies should include samples that allow for separate analyses of current and past migraine as well as migraine with and without aura.

Title: Triglyceride-glucose-body mass index as an integrated marker for ultrasound-defined diastolic dysfunction: variable importance via machine learning and SHAP analysis in a Chinese community cohort.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The triglyceride-glucose-body mass index, which integrates the triglyceride-glucose index with body mass index, has emerged as a promising marker of metabolic risk for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; however, its association with subclinical diastolic dysfunction remains underexplored.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 1,467 participants from a Chinese community-based population who underwent echocardiographic evaluation and metabolic profiling. The triglyceride-glucose-body mass index was calculated as the natural logarithm of triglycerides multiplied by fasting blood glucose divided by 2, then multiplied by body mass index. Ultrasound-defined diastolic dysfunction was diagnosed according to the 2025 American Society of Echocardiography criteria. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and machine learning were employed to evaluate the association.
RESULTS: The prevalence of ultrasound-defined diastolic dysfunction was 33.6%. The optimal Youden-derived triglyceride-glucose-body mass index cutoff was 220.000, categorizing participants into low ( n =  543 ) and high ( n =  924 ) groups. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-standard deviation increase was not significantly associated with ultrasound-defined diastolic dysfunction in continuous analysis (odds ratio=1.35; 95% confidence interval: 0.42-4.40; P =  0.616 ); however, the binary comparison showed a significant association (odds ratio=1.60; 95% confidence interval: 1.11-2.31; P =  0.013 ). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant overall association ( P overall   < 0.001 ) without significant nonlinearity ( P nonlinear   = 0.194 ).
DISCUSSION: In this cohort, the triglyceride-glucose-body mass index demonstrated a significant independent association with ultrasound-defined diastolic dysfunction in the binary analysis, supporting its potential as a screening index for subclinical diastolic dysfunction, although external validation in independent populations is needed.

Title: Integrated hs-cTnI, global longitudinal strain, and coronary artery calcium for risk stratification of anthracycline-related cardiac dysfunction in multiple myeloma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracycline-related cardiac dysfunction remains a major concern in multiple myeloma, yet conventional left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) surveillance may miss early injury. We evaluated whether pre-anthracycline baseline measurements of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and coronary artery calcium (CAC), obtained before anthracycline initiation, improve risk stratification for cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD).
METHODS: In this retrospective study of 312 myeloma patients receiving anthracycline-based therapy, CTRCD was defined as LVEF decline >10% to <53% or relative GLS decline >15%. Predictive performance was assessed using competing-risk models and time-dependent ROC analysis. A simplified risk score (MY-CARD) was derived and temporally validated in a separate cohort.
RESULTS: CTRCD occurred in 91 patients (29.2%). hs-cTnI elevation and GLS worsening preceded LVEF decline, with median intervals of 8.4 and 12.6 weeks. The full model (hs-cTnI + GLS + CAC) achieved an AUC of 0.91, outperforming hs-cTnI + LVEF (0.83) and LVEF alone (0.66). The MY-CARD score stratified 12-month CTRCD risk into low (6.2%), intermediate (28.7%), and high (71.4%) categories. Patients with both hs-cTnI elevation and GLS worsening had the highest subsequent CTRCD risk (adjusted HR 5.42-7.86).
CONCLUSIONS: Integrating baseline hs-cTnI, GLS, and CAC improved CTRCD risk stratification in myeloma patients. The MY-CARD score provides a practical framework for baseline and on-treatment risk assessment, supporting closer surveillance in high-risk patients. External validation and prospective studies are warranted.

Title: The effects of aquatic exercise therapy on blood pressure in elderly people with hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains one of the most common controllable risk factors for cardiovascular disease morbidity and mortality in the elderly. Aquatic exercise therapy (AET), as a safe and low-impact form of exercise, has attracted considerable attention due to its potential cardiovascular benefits; however, its impact on blood pressure control in elderly patients with hypertension remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to investigate the effects of AET on blood pressure and heart rate in elderly patients with hypertension.
METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and CINAHL was conducted from inception to July 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of AET compared with control interventions in older adults with hypertension were included. The primary outcomes were systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), while HR was considered a secondary outcome. Random-effects models were applied for meta-analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed based on the type of control intervention.
RESULTS: Four RCTs involving 123 participants were included in this meta-analysis. Compared with control conditions, aquatic exercise therapy (AET) significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (SBP) (MD -10.98 mmHg, 95% CI -17.41 to -4.56, P = 0.001; I² = 29%), diastolic blood pressure (DBP) (MD -5.97 mmHg, 95% CI -6.57 to -5.36, P = 0.001; I² = 0%), and heart rate (HR) (MD -5.91 beats/min, 95% CI -6.70 to -5.12, P = 0.001; I² = 0%). According to the GRADE assessment, the certainty of evidence for the main outcomes was rated as moderate.
CONCLUSIONS: AET may be an effective non-pharmacological intervention for improving blood pressure control and reducing heart rate in older adults with hypertension. However, further well-designed RCTs with larger sample sizes are needed to confirm its long-term clinical effects.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261462262, PROSPERO: CRD420261462262.

Title: Intravenous iron supplementation in heart failure and iron deficiency: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iron deficiency is frequently encountered in patients with heart failure. It is related not only to anemia, but also to exercise intolerance, impaired health status, and repeated hospitalization. Intravenous iron has been evaluated in randomized trials and in many systematic reviews, but the review conclusions are not completely aligned, particularly for mortality and functional outcomes. We therefore reviewed the existing review-level evidence, with particular attention to methodological quality and repeated use of the same primary trials.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from January 2016 to 31 March 2026. Eligible studies were systematic reviews and meta-analyses evaluating iron supplementation in patients with heart failure and iron deficiency. Reviews including mixed iron formulations were considered only when intravenous iron outcomes were separately reported or intravenous iron represented the predominant intervention of interest. AMSTAR2 was used to assess review quality. Trial overlap was examined using the corrected covered area (CCA), and GRADE was used to judge certainty of evidence.
RESULTS: Forty-five eligible reviews were identified, and 18 representative reviews were included in the detailed synthesis. Across the available evidence, intravenous iron showed the most consistent association with reduced heart failure hospitalization, including recurrent hospitalization and composite endpoints combining heart failure hospitalization with cardiovascular death. The randomized evidence was derived predominantly from populations with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), with some trials extending eligibility into the mildly reduced ejection fraction range. Evidence for cardiovascular mortality and all-cause mortality remained inconsistent. Findings for functional capacity and health status were generally favorable but remained uncertain because of heterogeneity and very low certainty evidence, whereas effects on cardiac function were uncertain. No clear increase in serious adverse events was identified with intravenous iron therapy, although the certainty of safety evidence remained limited. According to AMSTAR2, methodological confidence was low in seven reviews and critically low in eleven reviews. The evidence base comprised 23 unique randomized controlled trials with 163 trial occurrences, yielding a CCA of 35.81%, indicating substantial redundancy among representative reviews included in the quantitative synthesis. GRADE certainty was moderate for overall heart failure hospitalization, low for total/recurrent hospitalization, composite hospitalization-cardiovascular death outcomes, all-cause mortality, and serious adverse events, and very low for first hospitalization, cardiovascular mortality, functional outcomes, and cardiac function.
CONCLUSIONS: Current review-level evidence, derived predominantly from populations with reduced or mildly reduced LVEF, suggests a potential reduction in heart failure hospitalization. This potential benefit should be interpreted in relation to the patient populations, clinical settings, and iron formulations studied in major randomized trials. The clinical certainty of these findings remains constrained by substantial trial overlap, prominent methodological limitations of the published reviews, and inconsistent outcome definitions. Evidence regarding mortality reduction, functional status, and structural cardiac remodeling remains uncertain and requires cautious interpretation.

Title: Effect of delayed remote ischemic preconditioning on major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in major vascular surgery: the protocol of DRIPC randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although endovascular therapy has become the mainstream approach for major vascular surgery, patients undergoing such procedures are still classified as high-risk according to clinical guidelines. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a promising perioperative intervention strategy that has demonstrated acceptable safety and efficacy. Existing research indicates that delayed remote ischemic preconditioning (DRIPC) offers superior protective effects compared to preconditioning performed within 24 h before surgery. However, there is currently a lack of Level I evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of DRIPC in the perioperative period for vascular surgery patients. This study aims to provide high-level evidence on the effectiveness and safety of this intervention in a clinical setting.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The trial is a single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial. A total of 1,054 patients will be recruited. The primary endpoints of the study include major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 30 days postoperatively.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital of Sichuan University (approval number:2025-1846). The results will be submitted to a major clinical journal for peer review and publication.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: identifier ChiCTR2600116987.

Title: Long-term survival after transcatheter aortic valve implantation in nonagenarian patients: a multicenter real-world study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The growing number of nonagenarian patients with severe aortic stenosis has increased interest in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in this population. However, data on long-term outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate long-term survival and procedural outcomes of TAVI in nonagenarians and to explore clinical factors associated with long-term mortality.
METHODS: We conducted an ambispective multicenter observational cohort study including patients aged ≥90 years who underwent TAVI for severe aortic stenosis between 2013 and 2021 at six centers in the Emilia-Romagna region, Italy. Baseline and procedural data were collected retrospectively, while outcome ascertainment combined prospective follow-up contacts with retrospective verification of dates of death or last confirmed vital status. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and associations with mortality were examined using an exploratory Cox regression analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 60 nonagenarian patients (mean age 91 ± 1.5 years; 67% female) were included. Procedural success was achieved in 97% of cases. In-hospital mortality was 5%, and 30-day mortality was 8.3%. Over a mean observation period of 5.7 years from TAVI to death or the last confirmed vital-status assessment, the Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 35%. In the exploratory multivariable analysis, male sex and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) were associated with higher long-term mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients aged ≥90 years selected by the Heart Team for TAVI, the Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 35%. The procedure demonstrated a high success rate and an acceptable safety profile. Male sex and COPD showed an exploratory association with worse prognosis. These findings suggest that TAVI may be a feasible option in carefully selected nonagenarians when guided by comprehensive clinical assessment and individualized decision-making.

Title: Association of NT-proBNP/LVEF with angiographic coronary disease burden in acute myocardial infarction: a retrospective study with machine learning analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) reflect complementary dimensions of ventricular stress and systolic function. Whether the NT-proBNP/LVEF ratio is consistently associated with angiographic coronary disease burden in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), and whether its predictive contribution is robust across conventional and machine-learning approaches, remains uncertain.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 375 patients with AMI who underwent coronary angiography. The continuous Gensini score was the primary outcome, while clinically anchored anatomical outcomes, including multivessel disease and high-burden coronary anatomy, served as sensitivity outcomes. Associations between log-transformed NT-proBNP/LVEF and Gensini score were assessed using multivariable median regression. Direct discrimination of NT-proBNP/LVEF versus NT-proBNP alone was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and paired DeLong testing; the incremental information provided by adding LVEF to NT-proBNP was additionally assessed using continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Six multivariable models-logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and CatBoost-were internally validated using leakage-controlled repeated fivefold cross-validation with five repeats. Calibration, decision curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP)-based model interpretation were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Higher NT-proBNP/LVEF was consistently associated with greater angiographic coronary disease burden. In the fully adjusted model, each doubling of NT-proBNP/LVEF was associated with a 12.20-point increase in median Gensini score (95% confidence interval [CI], 9.33-15.07; P < 0.001). Comparable associations were observed for high-burden anatomy (odds ratio [OR] per doubling, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.44-1.97) and multivessel disease (OR per doubling, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.36-1.84). For the secondary high-Gensini-burden outcome, NT-proBNP/LVEF and NT-proBNP showed comparable discrimination (AUC, 0.783 vs. 0.780; ΔAUC = 0.004; P = 0.362). Adding LVEF to NT-proBNP did not show clear incremental improvement by NRI or IDI. Among the six multivariable models, SVM yielded the numerically highest AUC (0.763; 95% CI, 0.715-0.811), but no pairwise AUC difference remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. XGBoost and CatBoost showed highly concordant SHAP importance rankings (Spearman ρ = 0.978), with NT-proBNP/LVEF ranked first in both models.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher NT-proBNP/LVEF was consistently associated with greater angiographic coronary disease burden across the continuous Gensini score and clinically anchored anatomical outcomes in patients with AMI. The ratio provides a parsimonious representation of ventricular stress and systolic function and showed stable predictive importance across the two boosting algorithms examined. Its discriminative performance was comparable, rather than superior, to that of NT-proBNP alone, supporting its potential role as a readily available adjunctive marker of coronary disease burden rather than a replacement for established clinical assessment.

Title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Community-Based, Family Network Heart Health Intervention - the SERVE OC Trial: Design, Rationale and Baseline Findings.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) disproportionately burdens underserved communities, where social determinants of health (SDOH) perpetuate persistent disparities. Family-based interventions leveraging social support represent a promising yet understudied approach. We describe the rationale, design, and methods of the Skills-based Educational strategies for the Reduction of Vascular Events in Orange County (SERVE OC) RCT and present baseline characteristics of enrolled families.
METHODS: SERVE OC is a 2-arm RCT of 190 Latino and Vietnamese families (486 individuals) randomized to the family-based intervention or individual self-management. The intervention was grounded in social network theory while employing community engaged strategies. Primary outcomes include achieving ideal cardiovascular health (CVH) defined by AHA Life's Essential 8 (LE8) and systolic blood pressure reduction at 12, 24, and 36 months. Baseline assessments include demographics, LE8, psychosocial factors, food security, and SDOH. Descriptive statistics and regression analyses examined cohort characteristics and associations between SDOH, food security, and LE8.
RESULTS: Over 83% of participants had suboptimal LE8 scores. Average adult total LE8 scores were 66.61 ±11.96, with physical activity as the weakest domain, compared to an average of 76.52±10.15 in children. Greater SDOH burden and food security were associated with significantly lower odds of ideal CVH and lower LE8 scores respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: SERVE OC demonstrates the feasibility of enrolling families in community-engaged RCT targeting CVD disparities in underserved population. Baseline findings confirm substantial CVD risk and SDOH burden underscoring the need for multi-level, culturally tailored interventions. Trials results will inform scalable, family-focused strategies for CVD prevention across the life course.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/ ; Unique Identifier: NCT05641519 .
CLINICAL PERSPECTIVE: The SERVE OC study evaluates a novel, family-based cardiovascular risk reduction intervention utilizing a community health worker model that strategically leverages social networks to promote sustainable, healthy behavior change.The approach fosters support with a focus on optimizing primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease within the family unit.Engaging family support systems in clinical prevention strategies may improve overall adherence to lifestyle modifications and risk factor management across diverse communities.

Title: Multidimensional Social Vulnerability and Hepatic and Extrahepatic Outcomes in Adults With HIV/HBV Coinfection in the United States.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: HIV/HBV coinfection is associated with substantial liver-related morbidity and mortality, yet the impact of social vulnerability (SV) on clinical outcomes has not been systematically assessed. We evaluated associations of multidimensional SV with mortality, hepatic, virologic, and extrahepatic organ outcomes among adults with HIV/HBV.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data from 110 U.S. healthcare organizations (2010-2026). We propensity score matched adults with HIV/HBV with and without documented SV 1:1 (2,024 per group). SV was defined using a four-domain framework encompassing material, healthcare access and engagement, interpersonal, and psychosocial vulnerability.
RESULTS: Over 15,900 person-years, SV was associated with higher mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 2.06; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.72-2.47), liver composite events (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.07-1.76), hepatic decompensation (HR, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.39-2.70), hepatic failure (HR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.53-3.73), HBV viremia (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.32-2.16), and HIV viremia (HR, 2.05; 95% CI, 1.71-2.46). SV was also associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.47), chronic kidney disease (HR, 1.49), and diabetes (HR, 1.25). Multidomain SV generally showed stronger associations than single-domain SV for most hepatic and virologic outcomes, with HR ranges of 1.76-2.62 versus 1.35-1.76 for single-domain SV. Healthcare access and engagement vulnerability was most consistently associated with mortality and hepatic outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: SV was associated with mortality, hepatic disease, impaired HIV/HBV control, extrahepatic organ morbidity, and acute care utilization in adults with HIV/HBV. SV assessment may improve risk stratification and identify actionable intervention targets during HIV/HBV care.

Title: Identification and characterization of a human antibody profile inversely associated with adverse cardiovascular events.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The immune response is linked to the progression of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD). We sought to characterize a predictive cardiovascular antibody biomarker using two independent cohorts.
APPROACH AND RESULTS: A human IgG profile serendipitously identified by ELISA was quantified in a well characterized cohort of 359 patients with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) who experienced a total of 71 incident adverse CVD events (death, myocardial infarction, and stroke) over a median 4.1-year follow-up. Using Cox proportional hazard regression analysis, low biomarker levels were an independent predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, estimated glomerular filtration rate, presence of obstructive CAD, heart failure, total cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol (adjusted hazard ratio of 1.90 [95% CI: 1.03-3.49; p=0.038] between lowest and highest tertiles). Validation was then performed in a larger secondary cohort using 4356 baseline samples from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), a prospective study of cardiovascular outcomes resulting in adjusted odds ratio of 50.5 per unit decrease in log-transformed biomarker [95% CI: 2.4-2773.1; p=0.030] over one year by logistic regression analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Low levels of human IgG antibodies targeting Bovidae IgG are independently associated with increased incidence of CVD events in patients with or without a history of CAD, indicating the potential clinical predictive power of this antibody profile as an inverse biomarker for CVD.

Title: Sex Differences in the Impact of Allosensitization on Waitlist Access and Post-Transplant Outcomes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) patients are prone to HLA-antibody formation from multiple surgeries, transfusions, and prosthetic surgical material. Females with ACHD may accrue additional, non-surgical alloantigen exposure. Whether sex modifies the impact of allosensitization on heart transplant (HT) access and outcomes in ACHD remains unknown.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the OPTN/UNOS registry of adults with ACHD listed for first-time HT (2018-2025). Sensitization was defined by calculated panel reactive antibodies (cPRA) at listing. We tested the sex × sensitization (highly sensitized, cPRA >50%) interaction on transplant access using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression, treating transplantation as the event of interest and death or removal from the waitlist as competing events, and on post-transplant survival using multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression, both adjusted for age at listing, mechanical support at listing, and the number of distinct prior cardiac surgery categories.
RESULTS: Among 856 candidates (38% female), females were more often highly sensitized than males (23% vs 14%; age-adjusted OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.26-2.61), even after adjusting for surgical burden. Sensitization reduced transplant access in females (84% to 71%; median wait 60 to 110 days, p < 0.001) but not males (79% vs 79%, median wait 88 vs 98 days). In adjusted Fine-Gray models, the subdistribution hazard for transplant was reduced in sensitized females (sHR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.72) with no effect in males (sHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.73-1.26), and the sex × sensitization interaction was significant (interaction sHR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44-0.94, p = 0.02). Post-transplant mortality was numerically higher in sensitized than non-sensitized candidates in both sexes and the sex × sensitization interaction on 1-year mortality was not significant. The sex-asymmetric effect persisted and was more pronounced in the multiorgan candidates.
CONCLUSIONS: Allosensitization is not a sex-neutral barrier to transplant in HT candidates with ACHD. Females are more sensitized and have reduced transplant access without differences in 1-year mortality. The female excess in sensitization is not accounted for by surgical burden, and the exposures responsible remain to be defined. These findings warrant a sex-aware listing strategy and further studies.

Title: Clinical Reference Percentiles for AI-derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue: A Multicenter Study.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has emerged as an important cardiovascular biomarker that reflects both inflammatory and cardiometabolic risk. EAT volume and density vary significantly across populations, yet there is a lack of multicenter studies investigating the predictive value of population-specific EAT percentiles.
METHODS: In this multicenter study, we retrospectively analyzed low-dose computed tomography correction scans from 42,842 patients undergoing myocardial perfusion imaging. A derivation cohort of 15,082 patients was used to establish sex- and age-specific nomograms for EAT density and EAT volume indexed to body surface area. Percentile-based thresholds were tested for outcome prediction in a validation cohort of 27,760 patients. For clinical implementation, we developed an online EAT percentile calculator.
RESULTS: Percentile curves demonstrated increased BSA-indexed EAT volume and decreasing EAT density with age. Over a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR: 1.83 - 5.14), 4,956 patients experienced a nonfatal myocardial infarction or death. In multivariable Cox models, patients above the 95th sex- and age-specific percentile had significantly worse outcomes for BSA-indexed EAT volume [adjusted hazard ratio 1.30, 95% CI: 1.14 - 1.49, p < 0.001] and EAT density [adjusted hazard ratio 1.7, 95% CI: 1.51 - 1.92, p<0.001] when compared to patients below the 50th percentile (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Age- and sex-specific EAT percentiles provide a clinically interpretable framework for contextualizing automated EAT measurements and identifying patients at increased cardiovascular risk. EAT density was a stronger prognostic marker and identified elevated risk even among patients with normal BMI, supporting its potential to provide information beyond conventional anthropometric assessment.

Title: TRPV1-cardiac afferent ablation after completed myocardial infarction prevents arrhythmogenic remodeling.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
STRUCTURED ABSTRACT BACKGROUND: Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias after completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited. Although TRPV1 afferent ablation at acute MI improves cardiac remodeling, the effect of delayed subacute targeting remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated whether ablating cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute post-MI window mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmias.
METHODS: Yorkshire pigs underwent sham surgery or anterior MI creation. Two weeks post-MI, animals were randomized to percutaneous epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX, for cardiac-selective TRPV1 afferent depletion) or vehicle administration. Four weeks later, terminal studies assessed the effects of RTX on cardiac structure and function, ventricular arrhythmogenesis, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling using in vivo electrophysiologic mapping, real-time neurotransmitter sensing, immunohistochemistry, and transcriptomic profiling.
RESULTS: Cardiac TRPV1 afferent depletion was confirmed by blunted responses to TRPV1 agonists.
