RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced end-diastolic diameter, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility. Endocardial electroanatomic mapping revealed improved VT/VF electrophysiologic correlates in RTX-treated animals, including fewer deceleration zones and late potentials. Epicardial multielectrode mapping demonstrated reduced electrophysiologic heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time release of adrenergic neurotransmitters (noradrenaline and neuropeptide Y) was normalized during sympathoexcitation in RTX-treated animals. Histologically, RTX treatment attenuated scar border zone myocardial fibrosis and sympathetic nerve sprouting, while suppressing T cell infiltration in cardiac sensory ganglia. Bulk RNA-sequencing of stellate ganglia revealed downregulation of adrenergic genes.
CONCLUSION: Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation post-completed MI alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural, functional, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling. Targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents represents a promising subacute post-MI therapeutic strategy.
UNSTRUCTURED ABSTRACT: Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias following completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited, and the impact of targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute phase is unknown. We evaluated whether epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX) administration two weeks post-MI in swine mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmogenesis. Four weeks post-treatment, RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced chamber dilation, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility compared with controls. Electroanatomic and multielectrode mapping revealed fewer deceleration zones, smaller late potential areas, and reduced repolarization heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time neurotransmitter sensing demonstrated normalized adrenergic release during sympathoexcitation. Histological and transcriptomic profiling showed that RTX attenuated border-zone fibrosis, decreased sympathetic nerve sprouting, suppressed sensory ganglion T-cell infiltration, and downregulated stellate ganglion adrenergic gene expression. Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation during the subacute post-MI window alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural and autonomic remodeling, representing a promising disease-modifying therapeutic strategy.

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Despite continuous improvements in diagnostic tools, the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is still based on electrocardiogram (ECG) and cardiac biomarkers supported by other non-invasive imaging techniques. However, ECG has limited sensitivity, while high-sensitivity troponin assays may show reduced specificity, particularly in older or multimorbid patients. Widely adopted clinical pathways (e.g. ESC 0/1 h algorithm) have reported high diagnostic discrimination in external cohorts (with AUC ranging from 0.93 to 0.96) which provides clinical context for interpreting our findings. These diagnostic tests have limitations that can be addressed through automated computer-based diagnostic systems using Artificial Intelligence (AI). Several studies in the literature have presented machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) models to quickly and accurately assess the diagnosis of AMI to optimize treatment.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The aim of our analysis was to evaluate the performance of AI-based models for the diagnosis of AMI using data from all validation and test cohorts available in literature. Sensitivity and specificity for all MIs, and for STEMI and NSTEMI separately, were analysed for different types of AI approach (non-DL or DL) and for different data sources (ECG or troponin-based). Hierarchical models were used to estimate the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity and specificity.A total of 24 studies evaluating 27 AI-based diagnostic algorithms were included encompassing 166.052 patients, of which 18.850 (11.3%) had a final diagnosis of AMI. Patients were predominantly male (61.8%) with a median age of 60.7 (IQR 59.0-64.1) years. Discrimination of AI-based algorithms for the diagnosis of AMI was high with an AUC of 0.97 (sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.92). This result remained consistent when considering the ability to diagnose STEMI (AUC 0.96, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.94) or NSTEMI (AUC 0.97, sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.90) separately. No significant difference was found regarding type of AI. ECG and troponin-based models were both extremely accurate, with the first ones being less sensitive and the latter less specific.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based diagnostic algorithms for AMI diagnosis were associated with particularly efficient performance. These results were consistent for both STEMI and NSTEMI considered separately. Rather than replacing conventional diagnostic pathways, AI has the potential to enhance existing tools by identifying subtle ECG features and integrating multiple data streams. While direct head-to-head comparisons with traditional statistical models are currently limited, future prospective studies evaluating AI and conventional approaches within the same clinical populations are warranted.AI did not lose accuracy depending on the data source or the type of AI applied.

Title: Caries experience in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CHD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, sharing several behavioral and metabolic risk factors with dental caries. While extensive research has explored links between periodontal disease and cardiovascular health, the association between dental caries experience and coronary artery disease is less understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize existing evidence regarding dental caries burden, measured by decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT), among individuals with coronary artery disease.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed in April 2025 across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Studies published from 1966 to 2025 were eligible if they assessed adult patients with CHD, ischemic heart disease (IHD), myocardial infarction (MI), or related conditions and reported dental caries experience using the DMFT index. Observational studies, including cross-sectional, case-control, or cohort designs, were included. Duplicate records were removed using specialized software. Two independent reviewers screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, resolving discrepancies by discussion. Data extraction included study characteristics, caries indices, and key findings. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Due to heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: From 2339 records identified, 1677 unique studies were screened, leading to 38 full-text articles reviewed for eligibility. Ultimately, 4 studies met inclusion criteria, representing populations from Iran, Sweden, Poland, and India, with sample sizes ranging from 100 to nearly 4000 participants. All studies employed either cross-sectional or case-control designs. Findings generally indicated higher mean values of DMFT among individuals with coronary artery disease, particularly for missing teeth. Some studies showed significantly greater untreated decay and tooth loss in patients with coronary artery disease compared to controls, while restorative care levels were often similar between groups. The small number of studies and their observational nature limit definitive conclusions.
CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review suggests that patients with coronary artery disease may experience a higher burden of dental caries, primarily through increased missing and decayed teeth. These findings underscore the potential shared risk environment and highlight the importance of integrating oral health within cardiovascular prevention frameworks. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship and explore whether managing caries can contribute to cardiovascular risk reduction.

Title: Early detection of emergent central apnoea in patients on positive airway pressure therapy: A five-year telemonitoring cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Treatment-emergent central sleep apnoea (TE-CSA) during positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy is recognised, yet its onset timing and contributing factors remain unclear. This study aimed to ascertain the onset time of TE-CSA via telemonitoring (TM) and identify associated factors.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 4,021 obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) patients treated with PAP and monitored via TM from 2017 to 2022 was analysed. TE-CSA was defined as a residual apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) >15 with 50% or more central events. Moreover, if the obstructive apnoea index (OAI) was > 5, patients were excluded. Patients with a central apnoea index (CAI) ≥5 at baseline were excluded. TE-CSA was categorised as transient (<12 weeks), prolonged (12-24 weeks), or persistent (>24 weeks without resolution during the follow-up period). Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed time to TE-CSA onset. A nested case-control study evaluated demographic, cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, sedative use, and PAP treatment type as risk factors.
RESULTS: TE-CSA occurred in 171 (4.3%, 95% CI: 3.7-4.9) patients, predominantly prolonged (90.6%), with transient (5.9%) and persistent (3.5%) forms. TE-CSA primarily emerged within the first 60 days of PAP therapy. Multivariate analysis identified older age (Odds Ratio (OR) = 1.03, p < 0.001) and male sex (OR = 2.35, p = 0.003) as significant predictors of TE-CSA development.
CONCLUSION: Telemonitoring detected that TE-CSA onset was most commonly identified within the first 2 months of PAP therapy. Older age and male sex are key predictors. Early detection through TM could facilitate timely interventions, although therapeutic adjustments were implemented throughout the observation period and may have influenced the temporal patterns observed.

Title: Non-cancer causes of death following cervical cancer diagnosis: a SEER database study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify non-cancer mortality after cervical cancer diagnosis and examine how these risks vary over time, by disease stage, race, and registry-recorded treatment patterns.
METHODS: We analyzed 65,852 women diagnosed with cervical cancer in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-17 (2000-2021). Standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) compared observed deaths with age-, race-, sex-, and calendar-period-specific mortality in the U.S. general population. Fine-Gray models retained every death other than the target cause as a competing event.
RESULTS: Of 24,857 deaths, 19,975 (80.4%) were cancer-related and 4,882 (19.6%) were non-cancer-related. The overall non-cancer SMR was 1.65 (95% confidence interval [CI]=1.60-1.70). After International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage- and race-exact propensity score matching (4,506 pairs; maximum absolute standardized mean difference, 0.079), registry-inferred combined radiotherapy plus chemotherapy without surgery was not associated with overall non-cancer death (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]=1.01; 95% CI=0.88-1.16); the infectious-disease (sHR=1.72; 95% CI=0.75-3.95) and septicemia estimates (sHR=1.60; 95% CI=0.69-3.72; 23 events) were imprecise. Among 31,617 patients surviving beyond 5 years, the conditional non-cancer SMR remained elevated (1.44; 95% CI=1.38-1.49).
CONCLUSION: Non-cancer mortality remains elevated among cervical cancer survivors, including beyond the 5-year landmark. Treatment-group contrasts are strongly affected by disease stage, treatment-selection mechanisms, and unmeasured clinical factors; they should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal. Survivorship care should integrate cardiovascular, infectious, renal, respiratory, and metabolic risk management.

Title: Albuminuria as a Clinical Marker of Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical myocardial dysfunction is common in diabetes and may precede clinically overt heart failure by several years. Albuminuria reflects systemic microvascular injury, but its relationship with the severity of myocardial dysfunction in patients with diabetes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether adults with diabetes and albuminuria have greater echocardiographic evidence of subclinical myocardial dysfunction than those with diabetes and normoalbuminuria.
METHODS: Four electronic databases were searched from inception to March 2026 for observational studies comparing adults with diabetes and albuminuria with those with normoalbuminuria. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences in global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', left ventricular mass index, e', and ejection fraction. Adjusted regression coefficients and odds ratios were also synthesized, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Eighteen reports representing 17 independent cohorts were included, with eight contributing to quantitative synthesis. Absolute GLS was significantly lower in patients with albuminuria (MD, -1.38 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.13 to -0.63; P < 0.001; I² = 82%). A greater strain deficit was observed from microalbuminuria to macroalbuminuria, although formal trend analysis was not possible. E/e' was higher in albuminuric patients (MD, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.18-2.24; P = 0.021), whereas ejection fraction did not differ. Albuminuria remained independently associated with impaired strain (pooled β = 1.06; 95% CI, 0.44-1.68) and higher odds of subclinical dysfunction (OR = 5.55; 95% CI, 3.43-8.98).
CONCLUSIONS: Albuminuria identifies patients with diabetes who have greater subclinical systolic and diastolic myocardial impairment despite preserved ejection fraction. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio may help identify asymptomatic patients who could benefit from deformation imaging, although prospective validation is required.

Title: Acute-phase HOMA2-IR and in-hospital cardiovascular complications in patients with acute coronary syndrome without known diabetes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance measured during acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may reflect pre-existing metabolic vulnerability as well as the response to acute illness. We examined its association with cardiovascular complications arising during the index hospitalization in patients with ACS and no known diabetes.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort, 252 patients with ACS and an admission HbA1c <6.5% had fasting glucose and insulin measured 24-48 hours after admission. Insulin resistance was defined by a HOMA2-IR threshold of ≥1.35 prespecified from independent healthy controls. The composite MACE outcome comprised five prespecified complications occurring between sampling and discharge or death. Logistic and modified Poisson regression were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking, and hypertension.
RESULTS: Insulin resistance was present in 137 patients (54.4%), and the composite MACE occurred in 57 (22.6%): 28.5% with versus 15.7% without insulin resistance; risk difference 12.8 percentage points (95% CI 2.5-22.6). Insulin resistance was associated with the composite (adjusted OR 3.08, 95% CI 1.55-6.14; adjusted RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.39-3.75); each doubling of HOMA2-IR was associated with higher odds (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.09-1.99). The association persisted after GRACE adjustment (adjusted OR 2.83, 95% CI 1.32-6.06) and was attenuated after adding left ventricular ejection fraction, a possible mediator (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 0.97-5.22). Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, or pulmonary edema accounted for 53 of the 57 events.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute-phase HOMA2-IR-defined insulin resistance was associated with cardiovascular complications during the index hospitalization, mainly heart-failure-related events. These findings are associational and require confirmation in multicenter cohorts.

Title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease phenotypes and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease remains uncertain. We evaluated 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in lean versus non-lean MAFLD.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 193 adults with MAFLD and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-defined obstructive coronary artery disease at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. Lean MAFLD was defined as a body mass index <23 kg/m² and non-lean MAFLD as a body mass index ≥23 kg/m². The primary outcome was the first expanded major adverse cardiovascular event (eMACE) within 365 days, including ischemia-driven coronary revascularization. Planned first percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) after baseline CCTA was included. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 115 patients (59.6%) experienced eMACE. The eMACE rate was higher in lean than in non-lean MAFLD (86.2% vs 54.9%, P=0.002). Among these cases, recorded components were revascularization (108), myocardial infarction (13), unstable angina (26), acute heart failure (1), stroke (0), and cardiovascular death (0); components overlapped. These counts do not establish first-event attribution. Lean MAFLD remained associated with eMACE after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary artery disease (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.32-3.26, P=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with MAFLD and obstructive coronary artery disease, lean MAFLD was associated with a higher 1-year hazard of eMACE than non-lean MAFLD, after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary disease. The small lean group and inclusion of planned revascularization limit extrapolation to non-revascularization events, confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

Title: The impact of periodontitis in cardiac autonomic dysfunction by hrv analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. This research ascertains periodontitis and its correlation to autonomic dysfunction by HRV analysis.
METHODOLOGY: In total, 54 periodontitis patients were involved in the study, categorized under four groups, namely Gingivitis (n=14), Mild Periodontitis (n=13), Moderate Periodontitis (n=13), and Severe Periodontitis (n=14). Kubios HRV software version 3.5 was used for the analysis of time-domain and frequency-domain parameters of lead II ECG for HRV analysis. The indices of SNS and PNS were calculated for the assessment of autonomic balance. The correlation between the HRV parameters with the severity of periodontal disease was performed statistically.
RESULTS: The SNS index was higher in the periodontitis groups than in the gingivitis group (Gingivitis: 1.09 ± 0.60; Mild: 4.25 ± 2.4; Moderate: 3.82 ± 2.2; Severe: 4.45 ± 1.5; p < 0.001), although the pattern was not strictly progressive.
CONCLUSION: Differences in autonomic regulation, including higher SNS index and lower PNS index values, were associated with periodontal disease categories. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study lacked a healthy control group and was cross-sectional.

Title: Frequency and Risk Factors of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in Patients Receiving Chemotherapy: A Prospective Cohort Study at a Tertiary Centre.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an increasingly recognised consequence of contemporary oncological treatment. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is insensitive to subclinical myocardial injury, and locally validated thresholds for global longitudinal strain (GLS) are lacking in Vietnamese patients.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the frequency and risk factors of CTRCD in patients receiving chemotherapy, and to validate a localised GLS threshold and a biomarker-based surveillance strategy for early detection.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 235 patients at Cho Ray Hospital (September 2023-December 2025). Patients were assessed at baseline and every three months with two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (GLS), high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). CTRCD was defined by international consensus criteria. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis; as the outcome was common, associations were quantified as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated by modified Poisson regression.
RESULTS: CTRCD occurred in 82 patients (34.9%). Incidence was highest with anthracyclines (41.2%) and HER2-targeted therapy (37.2%). A relative GLS reduction ≥12.1% predicted CTRCD with 73% sensitivity and 83% specificity. hs-TnT achieved a 100% negative predictive value (NPV), and combining GLS with hs-TnT in parallel retained a 100% NPV. Hypertension (RR 2.50, 95% CI 1.78-3.50), coronary artery disease (RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.82-3.35) and dyslipidaemia (RR 2.10, 95% CI 1.49-2.97) were associated with CTRCD. HFA-ICOS stratification was strongly predictive, with a stepwise increase in risk up to the very-high-risk category (RR 18.6, 95% CI 7.94-43.6 versus low risk; 100% event rate).
CONCLUSIONS: CTRCD affected one-third of patients. A locally validated GLS threshold combined with hs-TnT enables early, resource-efficient detection, supporting a shift from reactive to proactive cardiac surveillance.

Title: A Systematic Approach to Nontraumatic Falls: Integrating Tilt Table Testing and Amnesia Screening in Clinical Practice.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic falls in older adults pose a significant public health issue. Syncope, a temporary loss of consciousness due to global cerebral hypoperfusion, is a frequent and often underrecognized cause of falls. Early identification of syncope is vital for effective management and fall prevention.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to assess the prevalence of syncope as a cause of nontraumatic falls in individuals over fifty years of age, characterize their clinical profiles, and evaluate the effectiveness of the Tilt Table Test (TTT) in diagnosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational study was conducted in patients over 50 years of age presenting with nontraumatic falls. Those with recent transient ischaemic attack/stroke, significant carotid stenosis, severe cardiac conditions, or inability to comply with instructions were excluded. Data collection involved a proforma covering demographics, fall characteristics, and diagnostic evaluations, including TTT and carotid sinus massage (CSM), following ESC 2018 guidelines. Statistical analysis was performed via SPSS (version 29).
RESULTS: Sixty-five participants were included, with a mean age of 68.34 ± 10.95 years; 63.1% were male. Intrinsic factors were responsible for falls in 72.3% of cases. TTT results indicated 32.7% positive results for syncope. A significant association was noted between syncope and amnesia (p=0.015).
CONCLUSION: Syncope is an overlooked cause of nontraumatic falls in elderly individuals. The TTT proved valuable in diagnosing syncope-related falls. The strong association between amnesia and syncope in our study emphasizes the need for detailed evaluation to improve outcomes and reduce the incidence of recurrent falls.

Title: Levels of Physical Activity and Ischemic Heart Disease Risk Among Adult Hospital Attendees in Mangalore. A cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of mortality globally, with physical inactivity identified as a major modifiable risk factor. There is limited data from Indian settings assessing physical activity using standardized tools and its association with ischemic heart disease (IHD) risk.
AIM: This study aimed to assess physical activity levels and examine their association with 10-year IHD risk among adults in Mangalore.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 101 patient bystanders aged 40-74 years at Government Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore. Physical activity was assessed using the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire (GPAQ), and metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week) were calculated. Participants were categorized based on WHO recommendations (≥600 MET-min/week). The 10-year IHD risk was estimated using WHO/ISH non-laboratory-based risk charts. Data were analyzed using Jamovi, and associations were tested using the Chi-square test with p<0.05 considered significant.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 48.9±7.1 years, with 58.4% males. A majority (93.1%) met WHO physical activity recommendations, with a mean activity level of 5803±2964 MET-min/week. Most participants (67.3%) had a low IHD risk (<5%), while 24.8% and 7.9% had moderate (5-<10%) and high (10-<20%) risk, respectively. A statistically significant inverse association was observed between physical activity and IHD risk (χ²=13.22, p=0.001). Among those meeting activity recommendations, 71.3% had low IHD risk, compared to only 14.3% among those not meeting recommendations.
CONCLUSIONS: Adequate physical activity is strongly associated with lower IHD risk. Promoting active lifestyles and integrating routine risk assessment using standardized tools can play a crucial role in reducing cardiovascular disease burden in similar populations.

Title: Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery versus Thoracotomy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Survival Analysis and Exploratory Predictive Modelling.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component.
METHOD: Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded.
RESULTS: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology.
CONCLUSIONS: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Observational Study

Title: Myocardial remodelling during sacubitril/valsartan therapy in patients with chronic heart failure.
Abstract: The aim of the study was to identify differences between aliskiren and sacubitril/valsartan in their ability to influence cardiac remodelling, metabolic balance, neurohumoral activation, and clinical symptom severity. A comparative assessment of the clinical effectiveness and impact on the structural and functional state of the myocardium was conducted for two therapeutic strategies in patients with chronic heart failure in Georgia over a 12-month follow-up. The results demonstrated fundamentally different trajectories of therapeutic response. In the sacubitril/valsartan group, early clinical improvement was observed by 6 months, including significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (-6.2%, p<0.001), respiratory rate (-4.5%, p<0.001), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (-10.0%, p<0.05), along with improved oxygen saturation (+3.5%, p<0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction increased significantly already at 6 months (from 34.2±4.7% to 37.4±4.0%, p<0.001) and further at 12 months (40.5±3.5%, p<0.001), accompanied by rapid improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, with 9.3% of patients achieving New York Heart Association I by study end. In contrast, the aliskiren group exhibited slower but more pronounced structural reverse remodelling. Significant reductions in left ventricular end-systolic volume (-15.8%, p=0.009), end-diastolic volume (-17.6%, p=0.016), and end-systolic diameter (p=0.002) were observed only at 12 months, along with a modest but significant increase in ejection fraction (p=0.030). Regression of functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation and a significant decrease in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (-19.7%, p<0.05) were more prominent in this group. Both therapies led to significant improvements in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, including reductions in glycated haemoglobin, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides (p<0.05 for all), indicating a favourable systemic metabolic effect. Overall, findings suggest that sacubitril/valsartan may be preferable when rapid clinical stabilization is required, whereas aliskiren may represent an effective therapeutic option for patients with advanced structural cardiac remodelling.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Randomized Controlled Trial; Clinical Trial

Title: Association of Risk-Stratified WeChat-Based Tele-Nursing With Self-Care Outcomes and Short-Term Readmission Among Patients With Chronic Heart Failure: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is frequently complicated by post-discharge readmission. This study evaluated structured risk-stratified WeChat-based tele-nursing in routine post-discharge care. This retrospective cohort study included 112 patients with CHF hospitalized during 2023-2024; 58 received tele-nursing and 54 routine follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed. The primary outcome was 6-month heart failure-related readmission. Six-month readmission occurred in 13.8% versus 31.5% in the unmatched cohort (p = 0.02) and 15.2% versus 32.6% after 1:1 PSM (46 pairs; p = 0.04). The unmatched adjusted Cox estimate was HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.18-0.99), whereas the matched Cox estimate was HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.18-1.08); penalized, complete-case, and Fine-Gray sensitivity analyses were also not statistically significant. The exploratory 12-month HR was 0.55 (95% CI 0.30-1.02; n = 94). All three SCHFI v7.2-C subscales improved more with tele-nursing (all p < 0.001). Tele-nursing was associated with greater improvement in patient-reported self-care and a possible association with lower short-term readmission, which requires prospective confirmation.

Title: BCG Scar Reactivation (BCGitis) in Kawasaki Disease: A Scoping Literature Review.
Journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) scar reactivation (BCGitis) is a distinctive clinical sign reported in Kawasaki disease (KD), yet evidence remains scarce across the literature. We aimed to summarize the epidemiology, chronology, clinical correlates, and coronary outcomes associated with BCGitis in KD.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of studies describing BCGitis in KD. Data were synthesized descriptively across retrospective cohorts and case reports/series.
RESULTS: Forty studies published between 1997 and 2024 were included (10 retrospective cohorts; 30 reports of 36 cases). BCGitis was most frequently described in infants and young children (< 2 years, often < 6-12 months) and was commonly associated with earlier recognition and treatment. Reported BCGitis prevalence varied across cohorts, from 11.8% to 49.9%. Coronary artery lesions (CAL) and IVIG resistance were reported at lower rates in some cohorts; however, these findings were not statistically significant. In the case reports, most patients were infants, male predominance was observed, and incomplete KD was frequent. BCGitis was often reported during the early febrile phase, sometimes preceding complete KD diagnostic criteria. Most reported cases responded to IVIG. Coronary abnormalities were usually mild or transient, although two giant aneurysms, one case of Kawasaki disease shock syndrome, and one mortality were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: BCGitis may support earlier recognition of KD, particularly in incomplete presentations, potentially facilitating timely recognition and treatment. Incorporation of BCGitis into diagnostic algorithms may improve patient outcomes. Future studies should standardize reporting of BCGitis chronology, coronary outcomes, and evaluate the incremental diagnostic value of BCGitis in prospective cohorts.

Title: Pre-Existing and Post-Cancer Major Cardiovascular Disease and Their Association With Mortality Outcomes Among Cancer Survivors in Australia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: As cancer survival improves, cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as a major competing cause of death. However, population-level evidence on the burden of pre-existing and post-cancer CVD remains limited. This study aims to quantify pre-existing and post-cancer newly documented major CVD and their association with mortality outcomes among people with cancer.
METHODS: Major CVD was identified using linked hospital records among 344,336 adults registered with primary invasive cancer in the New South Wales Cancer Registry from 2006 to 2016. The cohort was followed up until 31 December 2021. Fine-Grey modelling estimated sub-distributional hazard ratios (sHR) for cancer and cardiovascular mortality, and Cox proportional hazard modelling estimated hazard ratio for mortality from any cause across 20 common cancers.
RESULTS: Overall, 18% (n = 62,675) of participants had pre-existing CVD within 5 years before cancer diagnosis, varying by age (3% for age < 50 vs. 40% for ≥ 80). Of those without pre-existing CVD (n = 281,661), 27% (n = 76,924) had post-cancer newly documented CVD, with the highest age-standardised incidence rates in pancreatic cancer (716 per 10,000 person-years), followed by lung (657). The median follow-up period was 6.8 years with an interquartile range: 2.1-10.3 The sHR of pre-existing CVD for cancer mortality ranged from 0.99 (95% CI: 0.85-1.13) in cancer of kidney to 1.81 (95% CI = 1.71-1.91) in lymphoma, and for cardiovascular mortality, 1.98 (1.78-2.18) in lymphoma to 4.74 (4.39-5.09) in pancreatic cancer. The sHR of post-cancer newly documented CVD for cancer mortality, ranging from 0.87 (95% CI: 0.69-1.05) in liver cancer to 2.33 (95% CI = 2.04-2.62) in cervical cancer and cardiovascular mortality, ranging from 1.45 (95% CI: 1.18-1.72) in myeloma to 3.39 (95% CI = 2.90-3.88) in liver cancer.
CONCLUSION: CVD is prevalent both before and after cancer diagnosis, with strong relations to increased cancer, cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Population-based strategies to strengthen holistic survivorship care and address key risk factors are essential to improve both cancer and cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Colchicine usage and recurrent pericarditis in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
Abstract: ObjectivePericarditis is a common and recurring manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). While guidelines for the management of SLE include the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), colchicine, and glucocorticoids, the evidence for various treatments in SLE is limited. Evidence for the usage of colchicine for pericarditis in patients with SLE exists primarily in case reports and case series. The purpose of this study was to investigate colchicine usage and rates of recurrent pericarditis among patients with SLE.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients with SLE treated at a tertiary care center between 2015 and 2025. Patients were included if they presented to the hospital with pericarditis based on the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines and had follow-up for at least 1 year. Based on the ESC guidelines, recurrent pericarditis was defined as new symptoms or disease activity after clinical remission and was captured within 1 year of the initial presentation.ResultsOf the 55 patients included in the study, 47.3% received colchicine, 52.7% received NSAIDs and 56.4% received glucocorticoids. Recurrent pericarditis occurred in 45.5% of patients. In univariate analyses, age less than 40 years at first presentation of pericarditis was significantly associated with recurrent pericarditis as was treatment with an initiation or increase of glucocorticoids. Treatment with colchicine trended toward reduced recurrence, but the result was not statistically significant. In multivariate logistic regression including age, treatment with colchicine, and treatment with glucocorticoids, only treatment with glucocorticoids was significantly associated with recurrent pericarditis (odds ratio 4.31; 95% confidence interval 1.12-16.55).ConclusionsIn this study, recurrent pericarditis was common among patients with SLE and was associated with treatment with glucocorticoids. Colchicine was associated with a trend toward decreased recurrence rates, but this was not statistically significant. Given high recurrence rates among patients treated with steroids, additional studies are needed on non-steroidal therapies for pericarditis in SLE, including further research on colchicine.

Title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
Journal: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death.
CONTENT: This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning.
SUMMARY: Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs.
OUTLOOK: Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.

Title: National Trends and Predictors of Adverse Outcomes in Hypoglycemia Hospitalizations in the United States, 2017-2022.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess national trends and inpatient outcomes among adults hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of hypoglycemia in the United States from 2017 to 2022.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample. Adult hospitalizations aged 18 years or older with a principal ICD-10-CM diagnosis of hypoglycemia were included. The annual share of primary hypoglycemia hospitalizations was calculated per 100,000 adult NIS discharges. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, length of stay(LOS), and inflation-adjusted hospital cost standardized to 2022 US dollars. Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression was used for mortality, a survey-weighted generalized linear model (GLM) with a quasi-Poisson distribution and log link was used for LOS, and a survey-weighted GLM with a gamma distribution and log link was used for inflation-adjusted hospital cost.
RESULTS: The analysis included 330,910 weighted hypoglycemia hospitalizations. Mean age was 67 years; 52% were women; and 70% were Medicare-insured. Diabetes mellitus (91%) was the most common comorbidity, while obesity (17%) was least common. Primary-hypoglycemia discharges peaked in 2019 (195 per 100,000 adult NIS discharges), declined in 2021 (180), and increased again in 2022 (190). Mortality occurred in 1.6%, and median LOS was 3 days. Compared with 2017, adjusted mortality odds were higher in 2020 (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.04-1.61), 2021 (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.16-1.79), and 2022 (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.07-1.65). Similarly, LOS and hospital costs were also higher in 2020, 2021, and 2022 compared to 2017. Congestive heart failure (CHF) and AF were associated with higher mortality odds, LOS, and cost.
CONCLUSION: Primary hypoglycemia hospitalizations declined during the pandemic years but became more severe and resource-intensive over time. Patients with CHF or AF had higher mortality, higher LOS, and higher hospital costs, highlighting the need for integrated hypoglycemia surveillance and cardiometabolic care.

Title: Embolic complications of cardiac myxoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis of frequency, clinical characteristics, anatomical distribution and outcomes in contemporary cohorts.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiac myxomas are the most common benign primary cardiac tumours and embolise, causing stroke, acute coronary syndrome, limb ischaemia, and visceral infarction. Although previous reviews examined clinical features and embolic risk factors, the frequency, anatomical distribution, management, and outcomes of myxoma-related embolisation have not been comprehensively synthesised.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, and PubMed from inception to February 2026 for observational studies reporting embolic complications of confirmed cardiac myxoma; small (≤10-patient) and pre-2000 case series were excluded. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions estimated patient-level embolic prevalence and event-level anatomical distribution.
RESULTS: Across 47 studies (4,964 patients), pooled embolic prevalence was 19.7% (95% CI 16.7-23.1; I²=75.4%, 95% CI 62.8-87.5). Cerebral events predominated (75.6%), followed by peripheral limb (17.0%). Pooled early mortality was 1.9% (95% CI 1.3-2.7). Villous morphology and high tumour mobility were more associated with embolisation than size. Recurrence was uncommon (crude rate 2.0%) and mainly in familial disease or Carney complex.
CONCLUSION: Embolism is common and predominantly cerebral. Villous surface and tumour mobility were more consistently associated with embolisation than size and may inform the urgency of resection. However, evidence is retrospective; the optimal timing after embolic presentation remains undefined, and prospective validation is required.

Title: Fetal Echocardiography After a Normal Anatomy Assessment: A Retrospective Cohort of In Vitro Fertilization Pregnancies.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the detection rate of congenital heart disease (CHD) on fetal echocardiogram after a normal and complete detailed fetal ultrasound among pregnancies conceived by in vitro fertilization (IVF).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study examined singleton IVF pregnancies that underwent a detailed fetal anatomic survey without any identified abnormalities, followed by fetal echocardiogram. The primary outcome was the rate of CHD diagnosis after normal and complete anatomic ultrasound. Patients with multifetal gestation, pre-gestational diabetes, a known family history of CHD, fetal abnormalities on anatomy ultrasound, or patients who had an incomplete initial anatomy ultrasound were excluded. Prenatal CHD was confirmed with neonatal imaging and infants were followed after birth.
RESULTS: 300 pregnancies were included, and of these 266 had a normal and complete anatomy ultrasound. 1.5% (n = 4) of pregnancies had minor CHD identified on fetal echocardiography which was not identified on the anatomy ultrasound. None of the infants required cardiac-related interventions in the first year of life.
CONCLUSION: No major CHD was identified at fetal echocardiography after a normal and complete anatomic survey. Our results support the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine guidelines that state a dedicated fetal echocardiogram may be considered, but is not recommended, for singleton IVF pregnancies.

Title: Ability of intravenous small-volume hypertonic sodium bicarbonate, sodium chloride, and glucose solutions to rapidly reverse electrocardiographic abnormalities in hyperkalemic calves with neonatal diarrhea.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperkalemia is common in dehydrated calves with neonatal diarrhea and can result in life-threatening cardiac conduction abnormalities.
HYPOTHESIS/OBJECTIVES: Compare the effects of IV small-volume hypertonic solutions of NaHCO3, NaCl, and glucose in correcting electrocardiographic abnormalities.
ANIMALS: Twenty-two neonatal diarrheic calves with plasma potassium concentrations (cK) > 5.8 mmol/L.
METHODS: Prospective randomized clinical trial. Calves randomly received either 8.4% NaHCO3 (6.4 mL/kg; n = 7), 7.5% NaCl (5 mL/kg; n = 8), or 46.2% glucose (5 mL/kg; n = 7) IV over 5 min and were subsequently allowed to suckle 2 L of an oral electrolyte solution. Lead II ECG variables were determined before the infusion, during infusion, and 7, 15, 30, 60, 90, and 120 min after the start of infusion.
RESULTS: Seven minutes after initiation of infusions, administration of hypertonic sodium solutions but not glucose resulted in a significant (P < .05) increase in heart rate and ST segment duration as well as a decrease in heart rate variability, QRS duration, and T wave amplitude. Generalized linear mixed model analysis identified cK, the interaction between cK and plasma sodium concentrations, or both, as significant predictors of most electrocardiographic variables. Posttreatment increase in cK in 2 calves in group NaCl was associated with the loss of P waves, prolonged QRS duration, and increased T wave amplitude.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPORTANCE: Hypertonic sodium solutions allow for a rapid reversal of the cardiotoxic effect of hyperkalemia. Hypertonic NaHCO3 should be preferred over hypertonic NaCl or glucose.

Title: Prospective evaluation of the prevalence and characteristics of heart murmurs and gallop sounds in anemic cats.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart murmurs and gallop sounds are common in anemic cats; however, their association with underlying cardiac disease is unclear.
HYPOTHESIS/OBJECTIVES: Determine the prevalence of murmurs and gallops in anemic cats. Investigate the association of auscultatory abnormalities with anemia severity and heart disease. Investigate whether change in anemia severity affects the audibility of murmurs and gallop sounds.
ANIMALS: Sixty-four anemic cats (packed cell volume [PCV] below 30%) presenting to a referral hospital.
METHODS: Single-center prospective observational study. On presentation, cats were examined and had PCV measurement. Each cat underwent echocardiography. Cats had PCV checks and daily auscultation to document heart sounds.
RESULTS: Fifty-eight percent (37/64) had a murmur and 23% (15/64) had a gallop. Mean PCV at enrollment was 18% (±6). Lower PCV was associated with the presence of a murmur (P = .03) and gallop (P = .016). Cardiac disease was present in 34% (22/64) of cats. After adjusting for anemia severity, murmur presence showed no statistically significant association with cardiac disease (P = .636 (OR: 1.31, 95% CI, 0.43-3.95)). A gallop sound was associated with greater odds of cardiac disease (P = .037 (OR: 3.97, 95% CI, 1.09-14.5)). Murmur intensity (P = .001) and likelihood of a gallop sound (P = .022) were lower in individuals when their PCVs increased.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPORTANCE: Murmurs and gallop sounds are common in anemic cats with and without cardiac disease. Anemic cats with gallops are more likely to have underlying cardiac disease than anemic cats without gallops.

Title: Is adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines related to a lower risk of cardiovascular events? A prospective cohort study including 13 897 participants from the SUN project.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading global cause of death, and preventive interventions are likely to be the most effective strategies. The 24-hour movement guidelines emphasize an integrated score, including physical activity (PA), sedentary time, and sleep. The combined effect of adhering to all three 24-hour movement guidelines on CVD events remains unclear. In a prospective assessment of 13 897 Spanish university graduates from the Seguimiento Universidad de Navarra cohort, the relationship between a comprehensive exposure (adherence to all three 24-hour movement guidelines) and CVD incidence was investigated. Participants completed baseline questionnaires from 1999, with biennial follow-up. Exposure was assessed using the Canadian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines: ≥ 150 minutes/week of moderate-to-vigorous PA, ≤ 8 hours/day sitting, and 7-9 hours/night sleep (or 7-8 hours for ≥ 65 years). A composite score (0-3 points) was calculated for the exposure. The primary endpoint was incident CVD (nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death). Nearly half (46.68%) of participants met all three guidelines, while only 0.96% met none. Over a mean follow-up of 14.48 years, 148 cardiovascular event (CVE) occurred. Fully adjusted models revealed a significantly reduced CVE risk for participants meeting two [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.37; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.14-0.99], or three (HR = 0.36; 95% CI: 0.14-0.95) guidelines compared to meeting none. Adherence to at least two of the 24-hour movement guidelines appears to be associated with a lower risk of CVEs. These findings suggest that a comprehensive approach to daily movement behaviors may play a beneficial role in CVD prevention. Public health strategies could consider promoting these integrated guidelines as part of broader efforts to improve cardiovascular health.

Title: Prognostic Factors for One-Year Adverse Outcomes in Chronic Coronary Syndrome with Concomitant Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
Abstract: Chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexist, yet prognostic evidence for patients with both conditions remains limited. This retrospective cohort study evaluated factors associated with one-year adverse clinical outcomes and developed a clinical risk score in 214 hospitalized patients with CCS and concomitant COPD. Baseline clinical and laboratory data were collected, and patients were followed for one year. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), rehospitalization for heart failure (HF), or rehospitalization for acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) within one year. Independent prognostic factors were identified using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Model performance was evaluated through discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap internal validation. During follow-up, 53 patients (24.8%) experienced the composite endpoint, including 7 all-cause deaths (3.3%), 8 non-fatal MIs (3.7%), 17 HF-related rehospitalizations (7.9%), and 21 AECOPD-related rehospitalizations (9.8%). Smoking history (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.962, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.093-3.521, P = 0.024), previous percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (HR = 2.017, 95% CI: 1.157-3.517, P = 0.013), higher Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) grade (HR = 1.488, 95% CI: 1.092-2.028, P = 0.012), and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (HR = 0.933, 95% CI: 0.893-0.975, P = 0.002) were independently associated with the composite endpoint. The model demonstrated a concordance index (C-index) of 0.736 and a one-year area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.773. Event-free survival differed significantly among the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (log-rank P < 0.001). These findings support integrated cardiovascular and respiratory risk assessment in patients with CCS and COPD. However, external validation is required before the risk score can be recommended for broader clinical application.

Title: A Comparative Evaluation of YOLO-Segmentation Models for Coronary Artery Segmentation on the ARCADE Dataset.
Abstract: Coronary X-ray angiography is the clinical reference for visualizing coronary anatomy, but automated instance-level segment labeling remains difficult because of low contrast, overlapping branches, class imbalance across 25 SYNTAX-defined segments, and heterogeneous published protocols. This protocol therefore provides a reproducible, image-level comparison of five You Only Look Once (YOLO) segmentation models-YOLOv8-seg, YOLOv9c-seg, YOLO11-seg, YOLO12-seg, and YOLO26-seg-on the public Roboflow v1 ARCADE release of 3,587 expert-annotated frames divided into 3,138 training, 299 validation, and 150 test frames. Models were initialized from official segmentation checkpoints, trained only on the training split with shared stochastic gradient descent (SGD) settings and validation-based early stopping and checkpoint selection, and evaluated once post hoc on the untouched test split; mask mean average precision (mAP) at intersection over union (IoU) thresholds of 0.50-0.95 (mAP@50-95) was the primary accuracy metric and A100 model-level latency at 32-bit floating-point precision (FP32) was a secondary efficiency descriptor. On validation, the larger YOLOv9c-seg obtained the highest observed mask mAP@50-95 of 0.210; on the test split, compact YOLO11-seg obtained the highest observed mask mAP@50-95 of 0.241, followed by YOLO26-seg (0.239) and YOLOv9c-seg (0.235). Major proximal segments were consistently easier to segment than rare distal variants, while recorded inference times of 0.6 ms versus 3.0 ms per frame describe model-level throughput rather than end-to-end clinical latency. These single-seed, image-level results do not establish patient-level independence, statistical superiority, or clinical utility; they are intended as a methodological benchmark that others can reimplement, with prospective, hardware-specific, and patient-level validation still required before any workflow claim.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Video-Audio Media; Comparative Study

Title: Prognostic value of Fibrosis-4 Index and preoperative dynamic changes in heart transplantation.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) Index has shown prognostic value in cardiovascular diseases, but its role in heart transplantation (HTx) and the impact of dynamic preoperative changes remain unclear. This study evaluated the prognostic value of preoperative FIB-4 for mortality after HTx and investigated whether dynamic changes in FIB-4 before transplantation are associated with post-transplant survival.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 791 adult patients who underwent orthotopic HTx between January 2015 and December 2024, with follow-up through June 2025. Patients were stratified by preoperative FIB-4 into low (<1.30), intermediate (1.30-2.67), and high (>2.67) risk groups. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Analyses employed Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and five machine learning survival models, including Random Survival Forest (RSF).
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 28.8 months, 218 patients (27.6%) died. Preoperative FIB-4 showed a non-linear association with mortality (inflection point: 2.03) and was an independent predictor of death [hazard ratio (HR) per unit increase, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.02-1.07; P < .001]. In the RSF model, FIB-4 was the most important prognostic variable (Variable Importance = 0.068), outperforming traditional donor and surgical factors. Sensitivity analyses confirmed that FIB-4's prognostic value was independent of age (interaction P = .745) and superior to its individual components (aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and platelet count). Correlation analyses showed no significant association between FIB-4 and invasive haemodynamic parameters, tricuspid regurgitation severity, or MELD/MELD-XI scores, supporting its distinction from haemodynamic congestion. Among high-risk patients (n = 153), preoperative improvement in FIB-4 category was associated with significantly lower mortality (adjusted HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.29-0.82; P = .007). Preoperative use of glutathione was independently associated with FIB-4 improvement [odds ratios (OR), 1.50; 95% CI, 1.01-2.22; P = .04].
CONCLUSION: Preoperative FIB-4 is a robust and independent predictor of post-transplant mortality, with greater predictive importance than traditional surgical risk factors. Dynamic improvement in FIB-4 before transplantation is associated with better survival. Integrating FIB-4 into routine preoperative assessment may refine risk stratification and guide pre-transplant management.

Title: The mediating role of sleep blood pressure in the association between B-type natriuretic peptide and cardiovascular events: The Nagahama Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is a risk marker for not only heart failure but also cardiovascular diseases (CVD). This study investigated the possible mediating role of sleep blood pressure (BP) in the association between BNP and CVD events.
METHODS: Data for 5,751 participants were obtained from the Nagahama Study, a longitudinal cohort study of the general Japanese population. Circulating BNP levels were determined from blood specimens. BP was measured at home in the morning and evening, and three times per night during sleep using a timer-equipped cuff-oscillometric device.
RESULTS: During the mean follow-up period of 9.4 years (54,350 person-years), 169 CVD cases were observed (Incidence rate: 31.1 per 10,000 person-year, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 26.7, 36.2). BNP levels ≥40 pg/mL were independently associated with CVD. The sleep BP-adjusted hazard ratio of high BNP for CVD was 1.80 (95% CI: 1.18, 2.74), while the awake home BP-adjusted hazard ratio was 1.92 (95% CI: 1.26, 2.91). Causal mediation analysis indicated a greater mediation rate of sleep SBP (14.3%, 95% CI: -2.8, 31.3) than awake home SBP (5.8%, 95% CI; -2.6, 14.2) in the association between BNP and CVD incidence. Factors associated with log-normalized BNP levels were age, sex, body mass index, sleep SBP, and nocturnal urination frequency.
CONCLUSION: Prognostic significance of BNP for CVD events was partially mediated by BP particularly BP during sleep.

Title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.
METHODS: In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.
RESULTS: Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

Title: Perinatal death and mode of delivery among term singleton breech births: A retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in Ghana.
Journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify the burden of perinatal death and identify factors associated with perinatal death and with cesarean delivery among term singleton breech births at Cape Coast Teaching Hospital, Ghana.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included term singleton breech births with documented fetal cardiac activity at admission from 2015 to 2021; antepartum stillbirths were excluded. Multivariable logistic regression examined factors associated with perinatal death. Mixed-effects logistic regression, with a random intercept for delivery year, examined factors associated with cesarean delivery. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) are reported.
RESULTS: Among 695 eligible births, 542 (78.0%) were by cesarean delivery. There were 41 perinatal deaths (5.9%; 59.0 per 1000 births), comprising 25 intrapartum stillbirths and 16 early neonatal deaths. Perinatal death occurred in 32 of 153 vaginal breech births (20.9%) and in nine of 542 cesarean deliveries (1.7%). These figures describe outcomes according to actual rather than intended mode of delivery and should not be interpreted causally or as a comparison of planned delivery strategies. Higher parity was associated with increased odds of perinatal death (aOR = 1.32, 95% CI = 1.04-1.68). Older maternal age was associated with higher odds of cesarean delivery (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI = 1.005-1.09), whereas higher parity was associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery (aOR = 0.72, 95% CI = 0.63-0.83).
CONCLUSION: The burden of perinatal death was substantial among term singleton breech births at this Ghanaian tertiary hospital. Most deaths were intrapartum stillbirths. Strengthening antenatal detection, timely referral, intrapartum care, operative readiness, neonatal care, and proficiency in emergency vaginal breech birth may improve outcomes.

Title: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number and Mitochondrial Homeostasis Genes in Acute and Stable Coronary Artery Disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in coronary artery disease (CAD), but the relationship between mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA-CN) and mitochondrial homeostasis across CAD presentations remains unclear. We investigated mtDNA-CN together with the expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α and TFAM) and mitophagy (PINK1) in patients with stable angina (SA) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
METHODS: This observational study included 334 patients: 170 ACS, 117 SA and 47 individuals with non-obstructive coronary arteries (NCA). Peripheral blood mtDNA-CN and the expression of PGC-1α, TFAM and PINK1 were quantified by real-time PCR. Associations with clinical characteristics, inflammatory markers and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were evaluated.
RESULTS: ACS patients exhibited significantly lower mtDNA-CN than SA and NCA groups (p = 0.01 and p = 0.004, respectively). PINK1 expression was reduced in both ACS (p = 0.005) and SA (p = 0.01) compared with NCA. TFAM expression was increased in SA (p = 0.009), while PGC-1α expression was higher in ACS (p = 0.02). MtDNA-CN and mitochondrial biomarkers were inversely associated with inflammatory markers, whereas mtDNA-CN and TFAM correlated positively with LVEF. Lower mtDNA-CN was independently associated with ACS (OR = 0.98, p = 0.0004) and SA (OR = 0.99, p = 0.04), while higher PINK1 expression was associated with reduced odds of SA (p = 0.03) and ACS (p = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Mitochondrial markers are altered across CAD phenotypes. ACS is characterized by lower mtDNA-CN and altered expression of mitochondrial homeostasis-related genes, whereas SA shows a pattern consistent with a possible compensatory response. Combined assessment of mtDNA-CN and mitochondrial homeostasis-related gene expression may provide a novel biomarker strategy for CAD risk stratification and targeted therapies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: VICTORIA study, (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06313645).

Title: Lifestyle Medicine in the 21st Century: Evidence-Based Strategies for Noncommunicable Disease Risk Reduction.
Abstract: Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) account for over 74% of global mortality, with cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes, cancers, and chronic respiratory diseases comprising the largest share. These conditions impose substantial health, social, and economic burdens worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the role of lifestyle medicine, a clinical discipline employing evidence-based lifestyle interventions in the prevention, management, and potential reversal of NCDs. Relevant randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, and large-scale cohort studies were reviewed, focusing on the six core pillars of lifestyle medicine: optimal nutrition, regular physical activity, restorative sleep, effective stress management, avoidance of risky substances, and positive social connections. Robust evidence indicates that plant-based and Mediterranean dietary patterns, structured physical activity, adequate sleep, mindfulness-based stress reduction, tobacco avoidance, and fostering social connectedness significantly lower NCD incidence and progression. Advances in digital health, wearable devices, and precision-based strategies enhance personalization, monitoring, and adherence to lifestyle interventions. Persistent gaps include limited long-term adherence data, underrepresentation of diverse populations in clinical research, insufficient integration of sociocultural determinants, and lack of standardized implementation frameworks in healthcare systems. Lifestyle medicine provides a comprehensive, cost-effective approach to NCD prevention and control. Scaling culturally adaptable, technology-enabled, and equity-focused strategies is essential to establish lifestyle-based prevention as a global standard in combating the rising NCD epidemic.

Title: Clinical and Echocardiographic Characterization of Stage B Heart Failure in Asymptomatic Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stage B heart failure (pre-HF) is characterized by objective cardiac abnormalities without HF symptoms. This study assessed the prevalence and clinical and echocardiographic characteristics of those who were asymptomatic yet had cardiovascular risk factors and Stage B HF.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 900 asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors, consecutively recruited from participating hospitals from October 2025 to July 2026. We performed clinical evaluation and a standardized transthoracic echocardiogram. Stage B/pre-HF was defined as the presence of objective cardiac structural or functional abnormalities in the absence of heart failure symptoms or signs. We evaluated independent factors associated with Stage B/pre-HF using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: In this hospital-based cohort, Stage B/pre-HF was determined in 261 (29.0%) participants. Hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and obesity were more prevalent in the Stage B group, occurring in 154 (59.0%), 118 (45.2%), and 109 (41.8%), respectively. Stage B/pre-HF was characterized descriptively by lower left ventricular ejection fraction and higher left ventricular mass index, left atrial volume index, E/e' ratio, and tricuspid regurgitation velocity, along with impaired diastolic function. Hypertension was the strongest independent association (OR = 5.930, 95% CI: 3.815-9.217), followed by diabetes (OR = 2.945, 95% CI: 1.913-4.532), age, sex, and BMI. The model showed good fit (Nagelkerke R² = 0.565; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.449).
CONCLUSION: Stage B/pre-HF was common among asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors and was characterized by structural and functional cardiac abnormalities. These findings support the potential value of early identification and management of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors in asymptomatic adults at risk for HF.

Title: Weight Gain During Successful Tuberculosis Treatment Increases the Risk of Post-tuberculosis Metabolic Syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about the relationship between weight gain during treatment and the subsequent risk of cardiovascular and metabolic (cardiometabolic) diseases. We assessed the relationship between changes in body mass index (BMI) during tuberculosis (TB) treatment and prevalence of post-TB metabolic syndrome, a strong predictor of cardiometabolic diseases.
METHODS: We enrolled a prospective cohort of individuals successfully treated for TB disease in Tbilisi, Georgia, from 2019 to 2022. Eligible participants were HIV-negative individuals aged ≥16 years with newly diagnosed and laboratory-confirmed pulmonary TB. The primary exposure was relative change in BMI from treatment initiation to treatment completion, dichotomized at a ≥5% relative increase. Our primary study outcome was prevalence of post-TB metabolic syndrome (≥3 of the following: elevated blood pressure, elevated triglycerides, low high-density lipoprotein, elevated glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c], and abdominal obesity) at any study visit (including the end of treatment, 6 months post-TB treatment, and 12 months post-TB treatment). Multilevel models were used to estimate the effect of BMI change on post-TB metabolic syndrome.
RESULTS: Among 120 participants, the adjusted risk of having metabolic syndrome after TB treatment among those with a ≥5% relative increase in BMI was 2.1 times (95% CI, 1.1-4.0) the risk of those with a <5% relative increase in BMI during treatment. Additionally, the adjusted mean of post-TB HbA1c among those with a ≥5% relative increase in BMI was 0.4 (95% CI, 0.0-0.7) points higher compared with those with a <5% relative increase in BMI.
CONCLUSIONS: Among individuals who were successfully treated, individuals who had a ≥5% increase in BMI during TB treatment had a significantly increased risk of metabolic syndrome and higher HbA1c levels up to 12 months after TB treatment.

Title: Comment on "Rationale and design of a pilot randomized control trial of permissive hypotension after cardiac surgery: The PHACS trial".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: A chronological framework for atherosclerosis: from environmental pressure to clinical disease, with vascular aging as a cross-cutting dimension.
Abstract: Atherosclerosis is a multiphase disease, yet contemporary cardiovascular risk stratification relies predominantly on calculators that estimate event probability within a limited pathophysiological window. Framingham, SCORE2, GLOBORISK and PREVENT capture lipid burden, metabolic parameters, and renal function, but they do not organize the chronological sequence of atherogenesis, assign measurable biomarkers to each stage, or integrate vascular aging. We propose CASCADE (Chronological Atherosclerosis Staging: Connecting Aging, Disease, and Environment), a conceptual framework that applies disease staging to atherosclerosis, organizing it into seven pathophysiological phases (F1-F7) preceded by an upstream environmental and behavioral pressure layer (F0), and spanning the trajectory from adaptive metabolic response to clinical cardiovascular disease. Each phase is mapped to a proposed dominant biomarker - from insulin resistance indices through apolipoprotein B, lipoprotein(a), and coronary artery calcium - and to a reversibility zone (largely reversible, transition, or stabilization only). Vascular aging - characterized by arterial stiffness, cellular senescence, epigenetic drift, and clonal hematopoiesis - traverses all phases as a modifiable cross-cutting dimension, with specific biological clocks applicable at each stage. The framework is developed through narrative synthesis of mechanistic, epidemiological, and clinical trial evidence, integrating current international guidelines and emerging evidence on biological aging and environmental determinants of cardiovascular risk. CASCADE complements existing risk calculators by providing chronological context for the upstream phases (F0-F3), where conventional tools offer limited guidance and the potential for disease modification is greatest. It is proposed as a hypothesis-generating framework, not a validated scoring system, and invites prospective evaluation of whether individuals traverse identifiable, modifiable phases of atherosclerotic disease - and whether integrating vascular aging measurement at each stage improves risk assessment and therapeutic decision-making.

Title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Education and Training: A Review of Current Practices and Future Directions at a Single Center in Phoenix, Arizona.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of the study is to describe extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) training and education practices at our institution and participants' self-reported comfort with ECMO tasks before and after training sessions.
BACKGROUND: ECMO is a life-sustaining intervention for critically ill patients with cardiac and/or respiratory failure. ECMO circuit management is complex and requires specialized training. This study describes pediatric and neonatal ECMO education practices at Phoenix Children's Hospital (PCH).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected program-evaluation data. The education program ran from 2021 to 2025; anonymous pre- and post-training survey data were available only for 2024-2025. Registered nurses and ECMO primers completed surveys around 2024 water labs, and fellows completed surveys around boot camps in 2024 and 2025.
RESULTS: Survey response rates were 90% (27/30) for spring 2024 water labs and 83% (25/30) for fall 2024 water labs. Among registered nurses and ECMO primers, self-reported comfort was numerically higher after training for managing ECMO emergencies (52% to 74%), ambulating patients (56% to 74%), independently maintaining circuit components (60% to 84%), and escalating pump issues (84% to 96%); all 95% confidence intervals for differences included zero. Fellow item-level response counts varied. Between 2021 and 2025, 273 patients were cannulated onto ECMO at PCH.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center descriptive evaluation, self-reported comfort was numerically higher after sessions, with imprecise estimates; findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Neither competence nor patient outcomes were measured.

Title: Race-Free Equations and Cardiovascular Risk Assessment: Much Ado About Something.
Abstract: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is central to kidney-function assessment and cardiovascular risk prediction. The equations long used to compute it incorporated a race coefficient that artificially raised values in people of African descent. Because race is a sociocultural construct rather than a biological variable, a 2021 consensus statement recommended adoption of race-free eGFR equations-paralleling cardiology's move from the race-based 2013 Pooled Cohort Equations to the race-free PREVENT equations. Whether removing race meaningfully alters cardiovascular risk stratification has remained largely untested in diverse populations outside North America. The HELIUS study addresses this gap, examining 21,617 Amsterdam adults from six ethnic groups, collapsed into non-African descent, African Surinamese, and Ghanaian categories. Replacing the 2009 race-corrected equation with the 2021 race-free equation lowered eGFR by roughly 9-10 mL/min/1.73 m² in the African Surinamese and Ghanaian groups, while estimates changed little in the non-African descent group. Agreement for composite chronic kidney disease (CKD) classification was near-perfect (Cohen's κ 0.94-0.99), though driven largely by albuminuria, which is unaffected by the eGFR equation; isolating the eGFR component showed the prevalence of eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² roughly doubling in Ghanaian and rising about three-quarters in African Surinamese participants, while falling in those of non-African descent. Within the SCORE2 CKD add-on model, equation choice did not materially change median risk or categorization at the population level. These reassurances are bounded by the cohort's youth (mean age 44 years) and low burden of impaired function (1.2% with eGFR <60). As a cross-sectional study without events, HELIUS demonstrates classificational concordance but cannot establish equal predictive performance, and may not generalize to older or higher-risk populations.
