Title: No clinically relevant QTc prolongation with ceftibuten or ledaborbactam etzadroxil: concentration-QTc analyses from two phase I studies.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ceftibuten and ledaborbactam etzadroxil are being developed as an oral fixed-dose combination for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections caused by multidrug-resistant Enterobacterales. This study evaluated their effects on cardiac repolarization using concentration-QTc analyses.
METHODS: ECG and pharmacokinetic data from two randomized, single-centre, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase I, dose-escalation studies in healthy adults (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04314206 and NCT04243863) were analysed using concentration-QTc modelling. Thirty-six participants were randomized to the ceftibuten study (27 active, nine placebo) and 48 to the ledaborbactam etzadroxil study (36 active, 12 placebo). Linear mixed-effects models characterized the relationship between plasma concentrations and placebo-corrected change from baseline in Fridericia-corrected QT interval (ΔΔQTcF). Model-based predictions estimated QTc effects across observed and clinically relevant plasma concentrations.
RESULTS: Neither agent produced clinically relevant changes in ECG parameters. Concentration-QTc analyses demonstrated no statistically or clinically meaningful relationship between plasma concentrations and ΔΔQTcF. An effect on ΔΔQTcF exceeding the regulatory threshold of 10 ms could be excluded at plasma concentrations up to 44 µg/mL for cis-ceftibuten (the predominant and more potent isomer), 2.2 µg/mL for trans-ceftibuten, 30.3 µg/mL for ledaborbactam (active drug), and 2.6 µg/mL for ledaborbactam etzadroxil (prodrug). A small, transient, not clinically relevant increase in heart rate was observed with ceftibuten, whereas ledaborbactam etzadroxil had no clinically meaningful effect on heart rate.
CONCLUSIONS: Ceftibuten and ledaborbactam etzadroxil demonstrated no clinically relevant effects on cardiac repolarization or ECG parameters. Concentration-QTc analyses excluded clinically meaningful QTc effects at and above anticipated therapeutic plasma concentrations, supporting the cardiac safety profile of this oral fixed-dose combination.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Clinical Trial, Phase I

Title: Influence of perfusion pressure on image quality in postmortem CT angiography (PMCTA) of coronary arteries: a pilot study.
Abstract: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of perfusion pressure in postmortem computed tomography angiography (PMCTA) on the visualisation of the coronary arteries. Coronary artery disease is a frequent cause of sudden cardiac death, and PMCTA is used alongside autopsy to assess the coronary arteries, including bypass grafts and stents. Reliable opacification of the coronary arteries is required to identify stenoses and acute occlusions and to assess their contribution to the mechanism of death. However, contrast distribution in PMCTA varies between cases, and perfusion-related artefacts can limit interpretation. Perfusion pressure is one parameter that can be controlled. An important step in this direction has been the recent demonstration that perfusion pressure can be continuously monitored during PMCTA. In this study of twelve postmortem cases (six evaluable), we examined three intravascular pressure groups (40, 60, and 80 mmHg) to assess coronary artery visualisation using a modified contrast agent pump with coupled real-time pressure monitoring and control. In this pilot study, 60 mmHg was the lowest perfusion pressure at which homogeneous coronary opacification with minimal perfusion-related artefacts was observed in all evaluable cases (two cases per pressure group). In one case a perfusion pressure of 80 mmHg depicted the peripheral coronary branches more completely, an observation that requires confirmation in a larger cohort. These findings may contribute to the methodological standardisation of pressure-based PMCTA protocols in forensic practice.

Title: The evolution and future of conduction system pacing.
Abstract: Cardiac pacing has undergone a fundamental paradigm shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing towards physiological activation of the native conduction system of the heart. Decades of evidence have established that chronic right ventricular pacing induces ventricular dyssynchrony, contributing to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing, which engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network of the heart, has emerged as a transformative approach that preserves or restores the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing, the earliest form of conduction system pacing, provided proof of concept but is limited by technical challenges and high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has since become the dominant modality, offering greater procedural success, lead stability and broader applicability: from management of bradycardia and prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy to cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is an emerging atrial counterpart: by capturing a preferential interatrial conduction pathway, this approach reduces interatrial conduction delay and produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence than conventional right atrial appendage pacing. Bachmann bundle area pacing might, therefore, help to prevent atrial fibrillation. In this Review, we bring these ventricular and atrial strategies together under the unifying principle of physiological pacing, describe their mechanistic basis and technical evolution, appraise the latest evidence from randomized trials and address the practical questions that arise in clinical application, indicating where more evidence is required.

Title: Cardiovascular dietary guidance at an inflection point: the 2025-2030 US dietary guidelines versus the 2026 AHA scientific statement.
Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Decreases Intraoperative Allogeneic Transfusion in Cyanotic Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of autologous platelet-rich plasma (aPRP) on perioperative allogeneic blood product transfusion requirement in patients undergoing cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) surgery and patients' prognosis.
DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: A tertiary university hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 95 patients with CCHD who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) between January 2020 and August 2025 were included, of whom 81 (85.3%) underwent redo operation.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were divided into the aPRP group and the control group according to whether aPRP apheresis was employed. In the aPRP group, aPRP was harvested after anesthesia and transfused back to the patient after protamine neutralization, whereas the concurrently collected concentrated red blood cells (cRBCs) were reinfused during CPB or chest closure (from weaning from CPB to skin closure).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In the original cohort, the aPRP group had significantly lower packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion rates, as well as PRBC and fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion volume, than the control group. After propensity score matching, the intraoperative PRBC transfusion rate no longer differed significantly between groups (aPRP v control: 17.4% v 43.5%, p = 0.180). However, the PRBC transfusion volume remained significantly lower in the aPRP group, both as total volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 400] mL; p = 0.037) and as weight-adjusted volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 15.7] mL/kg; p = 0.045). The matched intraoperative FFP transfusion requirements were also significantly reduced in the aPRP group (200 [0, 600] v 600 [400, 1,000] mL, p < 0.05). Viscoelastic testing indicated significantly improved coagulation and platelet function following aPRP administration in the treatment group. No difference in intraoperative blood loss, postoperative allogeneic blood products, 24-hour chest tube drainage, use of coagulation agents, postoperative ventilation time, or intensive care unit stay was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In a predominantly redo cohort of patients with CCHD undergoing cardiac surgery, the use of aPRP was associated with reduced intraoperative allogeneic blood and plasma transfusion requirements, and it also effectively preserved hemostatic function in these patients. However, the reduction in allogeneic product use may not be primarily due to the preserved hemostatic function conferred by aPRP but rather to autologous substitution of allogeneic products.

Title: Association of Enteral Chloral Hydrate with Benzodiazepine Exposure and Delirium After Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Before-and-After Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol and benzodiazepine exposure, sedation quality, withdrawal, delirium, and short-term clinical outcomes in children undergoing congenital heart surgery.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective before-and-after cohort study.
SETTING: Pediatric cardiac intensive care unit of a tertiary referral center.
PARTICIPANTS: Eighty-six children who underwent congenital heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, required postoperative mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours, and received sedation for at least 24 hours.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were treated according to the institutional postoperative sedation protocol before (July 2021-June 2023) and after (August 2023-July 2025) implementation of enteral chloral hydrate as an adjunctive sedative.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary endpoint was cumulative midazolam exposure during the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit stay. Secondary endpoints included sedative and analgesic requirements, sedation and pain scores, withdrawal, delirium, and clinical outcomes. Compared with the preprotocol group, the chloral hydrate group had significantly lower cumulative midazolam exposure (10.2 v 13.2 mg/kg, p = 0.010) and peak midazolam infusion rates (0.15 v 0.20 mg/kg/h, p < 0.001), and a lower observed frequency of delirium (14.6% v 37.8%, p = 0.015). No significant between-group differences were observed in sedation quality, pain scores, withdrawal, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of stay in the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit or hospital, or mortality.
CONCLUSION: Addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol was associated with reduced benzodiazepine exposure and a lower observed frequency of delirium without statistically significant differences in sedation quality or short-term clinical outcomes. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

Title: Real-world Data to Assess the Applicability of Randomized Controlled Trials in Newly Metastatic Prostate Cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concerns persist regarding the applicability of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) to real-world clinical practice.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the generalizability of RCTs using data from PIONEER.
DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Trial eligibility criteria were extracted from RCTs enrolling patients with mHSPC published between 2013 and 2023 and identified through a literature review. Patients with newly diagnosed mHSPC were identified from insurance claim databases mapped to the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model.
OUTCOME MEASUREMENTS AND STATISTICAL ANALYSES: The proportion of patients failing to meet at least one RCT eligibility criterion was assessed for each trial. The proportion of men receiving RCT-investigated treatments who would have been ineligible for the corresponding trials was estimated.
RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: Overall, 12 trials were identified. From ∼398 000 patients with prostate cancer included in three databases, we identified 32 585 newly diagnosed mHSPC cases. The percentage of patients who would have been excluded from each RCT ranged between 8.6% and 55%. The percentage of patients who would be excluded from all trials ranged between 5.9% and 12% and increased to 26-44% when excluding the HORRAD trial. The most common reasons for exclusion were anemia (16-29%), heart failure (6.2-13%), and renal failure (3.9-19%). Between 18% and 52% of the patients receiving a drug would have been excluded from RCTs evaluating that drug. Limitations include database representativeness, incomplete clinical data, and limited generalizability to metachronous mHSPC.
CONCLUSIONS: Up to half of real-world patients with newly diagnosed mHSPC would have been ineligible for RCT participation, yet many received therapies despite trial ineligibility. This highlights the need for more inclusive and representative research and a comprehensive examination of real-world data for clinical decision-making.
PATIENTS SUMMARY: Up to half of real-world patients with newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer would have not been eligible for participation in clinical trials. A substantial proportion of patients receiving trial-tested therapies in routine clinical practice would have been excluded from the corresponding randomized controlled trials.

Title: Cardiovascular risk among individuals with and without a genetic mutation for familial hypercholesterolemia: A long-term study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) are exposed to elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels from early life. Whether FH independently increases risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the risk of developing ASCVD between individuals with and without FH mutations across different levels of LDL-C.
METHODS: A registry-based cohort study including patients genetically tested for FH from 1991 to 2023. Exposure was genetic mutation in the LDL, APOB, or PCSK-9 genes within the different LDL groups: LDL-C <5 mmol/L, LDL-C 5 to 7 mmol/L, and LDL-C >7 mmol/L. ASCVD was defined as composite major adverse cardiac events (MACE) comprising myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death, angina pectoris, and stroke. An adjusted Cox proportional hazards model was used.
RESULTS: The study included 2327 patients, comprising 958 with FH mutation and 1369 without. Mean follow-up time was 13.9 ± 9.8 years. LDL-C was significantly associated with the risk of future ASCVD, with a multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of 1.17 (95%CI: 1.13-1.22, P < .001) per 1 mmol/L increase in LDL-C. No significant difference in risk of MACE was found between those with vs without a genetic FH mutation (LDL-C <5 mmol/L HR 0.91 [95%CI: 0.48;1.74], LDL-C 5 to 7 mmol/L HR 0.91 [95%CI: 0.68;1.21] and LDL-C >7 mmol/L HR 1.13 [95%CI: 0.91;1.41]) using patients without FH as reference.
CONCLUSION: Genetic FH mutation did not confer additional risk when compared to individuals without an FH mutation but with similar LDL-C levels. These findings suggest that LDL-C levels - rather than FH mutation status - should guide the intensity of lipid-lowering therapy.

Title: Comparison of oral and intravenous methadone for postoperative analgesia after cardiac surgery: a pilot randomized clinical trial.
Occurrence Proportion and Associated Factors of Respiratory Failure During Hospitalization in Chinese Patients With AECOPD: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the occurrence proportion and associated factors of respiratory failure during hospitalization in Chinese patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD).
METHODS: Eight databases (CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, CBM, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library) were searched from inception to March 1, 2026. Studies reporting multivariable-adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for factors associated with respiratory failure in AECOPD patients were included. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used for quality assessment. A single-group rate meta-analysis with Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation was performed to pool the occurrence proportion. Subgroup analyses were conducted by study design, geographical region (Qinling-Huaihe Line), and respiratory failure type. Factors associated with respiratory failure were stratified by definitions and cutoff values; only subgroups with ≥ 3 studies were pooled.
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (5 cohort, 18 case-control) with 4212 patients were included. The pooled occurrence proportion of respiratory failure was 41% (95% CI: 0.37-0.46). Meta-analysis identified nine factors associated with respiratory failure: comorbid cardiac disease (OR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.68-2.67), advanced age (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.13-1.33), elevated NLR (OR = 1.87, 95% CI: 1.50-2.33), elevated PCT (OR = 2.27, 95% CI: 1.29-4.00), elevated D-dimer (OR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.01-2.90), ≥ 2 annual exacerbations (OR = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.71-3.60), higher APACHE II score (OR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.17-1.43), elevated CRP (OR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.02-1.24), and decreased FEV1% predicted (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.67-0.99). Model dependence analysis showed that ALB was statistically significant only under the fixed-effects model but not under the random-effects model. NE was not statistically significant under either model. Therefore, ALB and NE were not included among the nine factors that were statistically significant in the primary analysis.
CONCLUSION: The occurrence proportion of respiratory failure in hospitalized Chinese AECOPD patients is high and associated with comorbidities, clinical characteristics, severity scores, and inflammatory/coagulation markers. These findings support risk identification and monitoring, but prospective studies are needed to validate their predictive and interventional value.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Comparative Analysis of Tracheal Intubation-Associated Cardiac Arrest in 2015-2023: A Report From the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children Multicenter Registry.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the contemporary incidence of tracheal intubation-associated cardiac arrest (TI-CA) in critically ill children and identify potentially modifiable factors to prevent TI-CA in PICUs and pediatric cardiac ICUs (PCICUs).
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Seventy international PICUs and PCICUs.
PATIENTS: Critically ill children requiring tracheal intubation in PICUs and PCICUs.
INTERVENTIONS: Tracheal intubation data were prospectively collected for all initial intubations in 68 PICUs and PCICUs from January 2015 to December 2023 using the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children registry.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: TI-CA was defined as CA occurrence or receipt of chest compressions for at least 1 minute within 20 minutes of endotracheal tube placement. TI during ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation was not considered TI-CA. A total of 27,773 TIs were evaluated, with TI-CA reported in 1.2% (n = 331). Pre-TI oxygenation failure and shock were associated with higher odds of TI-CA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.29; 95% CI, 1.81-2.89 and aOR, 4.67; 95% CI, 3.68-5.92, respectively). Each additional TI attempt required was associated with increased odds of TI-CA (aOR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.56-1.85, for each attempt). Use of ketamine (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.49-0.82), propofol (aOR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72), neuromuscular blockade (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.49-0.91), and video laryngoscopy (aOR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.6-0.97) were associated with lower odds of TI-CA. Mediation analysis indicated that 13% of video laryngoscopy's protective effect was due to a reduction in TI attempt counts. The protective effects of ketamine, propofol, and neuromuscular blockade were minimally mediated by reduced TI attempt counts (5%, 4%, and 7%).
CONCLUSIONS: TI-CA occurred in 1.2% of TIs performed in the PICUs. Odds of TI-CA increased incrementally with successive TI attempts. Video laryngoscopy was protective against TI-CA. Mediation analysis revealed that reduced TI attempts accounted for 13% of the protective benefit associated with video laryngoscopy.

Title: SGLT2 inhibitor therapy following aortic valve intervention for aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of mortality, heart failure, rhythm, renal, and valve-related outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual mortality and heart-failure events remain common after aortic valve intervention for severe aortic stenosis. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes in heart-failure, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease populations, but their role following transcatheter or surgical aortic valve intervention remains uncertain.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, citation tracking, and manually identified eligible studies were screened through June 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing SGLT2i with usual care or no SGLT2i after aortic valve intervention. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251059332). Eligible populations included TAVR, SAVR, and bioprosthetic aortic valve evidence where available. Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models while non-HR estimates and non-comparable endpoints were summarized narratively.
RESULTS: Twelve eligible reports were included, comprising one randomized trial and 11 observational studies. Most time-to-event estimates were reported from TAVR cohorts; two SAVR-only studies and one mixed bioprosthetic AVR study added complementary surgical and valve-durability data. In the pooled time-to-event analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60-0.79; I²=5%; p < 0.001). The study-defined composite clinical outcome was also lower (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53-0.89; I²=57%; p = 0.005), although component definitions differed across studies. Estimates for heart-failure hospitalization or exacerbation, atrial fibrillation, and acute kidney injury were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i use after aortic valve intervention was associated with lower all-cause mortality in pooled time-to-event analysis. SAVR data were clinically informative but were not sufficiently homogeneous for separate quantitative pooling. Findings for composite, heart-failure, rhythm, renal, and valve-related outcomes remain less certain. Dedicated randomized trials are needed to confirm whether the observed association reflects a treatment effect and to define patient selection, treatment timing, and peri-procedural safety.

Title: Randomized pilot trial of intraoperative hemoadsorption in clopidogrel treated patients undergoing urgent coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving clopidogrel who undergo urgent CABG before the recommended 5-day washout period are at increased risk of perioperative bleeding. This study evaluated whether intraoperative hemoadsorption can reduce bleeding in such patients.
METHODS: Patients undergoing CABG within 24 h of clopidogrel discontinuation were randomized 1:1 to intraoperative hemoadsorption (Group 1) or control (Group 2). In the intervention group, the device was incorporated into the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuit. Efficacy was assessed by 24-hour chest tube drainage (CTD), blood product transfusions and surgical revisions for bleeding control.
RESULTS: A total of 50 patients were randomized (mean age 64 ± 8.6 years, 82% male). There were no differences in baseline characteristics between groups. Group 1 showed significantly reduced median 24-hr CTD of 300mL [250-400] vs. 500mL [400-700], p = 0.0003, transfusions of packed red blood cells 0 [0-1] vs. 1 [0-2] units, p = 0.047), fresh frozen plasma 0 [0-0] vs. 2 [2-3] units, p < 0.0001) and platelets 0 [0-0] vs. 2 [1-3] units, p < 0.0001 compared with Group 2. One revision for bleeding control occurred in Group 2 (4.0%). No device-related serious adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of clopidogrel-treated patients undergoing CABG within 24 h of discontinuation, intraoperative hemoadsorption was associated with lower postoperative bleeding and transfusion requirements.

Title: Association of the serum uric acid/albumin ratio with kidney composite events in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The serum uric acid-to-albumin ratio (sUAR) has been implicated in various cardiovascular and kidney diseases. However, its association with kidney composite events in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains underexplored. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between sUAR and kidney composite events in T2DM patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 3,618 patients with T2DM from Chengdu Integrated TCM & Western Medicine Hospital between January 2018 and December 2025. The sUAR was calculated as serum uric acid divided by serum albumin. Participants were categorized into tertiles (T1: 1.99-7.65; T2: 7.66-10.21; T3: 10.22-31.67) based on sUAR. The primary outcome was a composite kidney endpoint, defined as initiation of maintenance dialysis, chronic kidney disease stage 5, or a eGFR decline ≥ 40% from baseline. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, Kaplan-Meier curves, subgroup analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were performed to evaluate the association between sUAR and kidney composite events.
RESULTS: During a median follow‑up of 28.7 months (IQR: 14.1-52.6), 591 (16.3%) kidney composite events occurred. Compared with the lowest tertile (T1), the highest tertile (T3) of sUAR was associated with a 44% increased risk of kidney composite events after full adjustment (HR = 1.44, 95% CI: 1.12-1.85, P = 0.005). RCS analysis revealed a non-linear relationship between sUAR and kidney composite events. Kaplan-Meier curves demonstrated significant differences in events-free survival across tertiles (log-rank P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses identified age as a significant effect modifier (P < 0.001), with a stronger association observed in younger patients (< 65 years). Among the 22 candidate variables included in the model, sUAR ranked as the sixth most important predictor of kidney composite events, following cystatin C, hemoglobin, albumin, eGFR, and HbA1c.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated sUAR is independently associated with an increased risk of kidney composite events in patients with T2DM, with a non-linear relationship.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Exercise tolerance test in Kawasaki patients without coronary lesions.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a systemic vasculitis of unknown origin and the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children in developed countries. If untreated, it can cause coronary artery damage in up to 25% of cases. Lifelong follow-up is essential, even for patients without obvious coronary lesions (risk level-I KD). Since some cardiac abnormalities may not be apparent at rest, stress testing offers valuable insight. This study aimed to evaluate exercise tolerance test (ETT) outcomes in children with a history of risk level-I KD compared to a control group.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This case-control study included children aged 5-17 years with documented KD without coronary lesions and at least six months since disease onset. After ethics approval, participants underwent a standardized treadmill test (modified Bruce protocol). A control group of healthy children was also included; however, exact age-matched analysis was not possible due to recruitment constraints.
RESULTS: Sixty children were divided equally into KD and control groups. The KD group had significantly lower mean age, height, weight, and BSA compared to the control group. After adjusting for these variables, most exercise indices showed no significant difference between groups, except for chronotropic incompetence which was more prevalent in the KD group. However, most differences became non-significant after adjusting for age and BMI.
CONCLUSION: Children with KD generally showed normal exercise tolerance, but a reduced chronotropic response may indicate subtle residual cardiac effects. These findings suggest a potential for subtle cardiac effects and may support the consideration of stress-based evaluation in select patients; however, further larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these observations.

Title: Prevailing income-based disparities in cardiovascular events in young hospitalized adults with cannabis use disorder: insights from a population-based analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cannabis use and low socioeconomic status are recognized as distinct risk factors for cardiovascular pathologies. This retrospective cross-sectional study aims to investigate the association between income status and cardiovascular disease risk among young hospitalized adults with recreational cannabis use or cannabis use disorder (CUD).
METHODS: We analyzed young adult hospitalizations (18-44 years) with known CUD from the 2020 National Inpatient Sample. Propensity score-matched analysis (1:1) was used to compare comorbidities and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) between the high-income quartile (HIQ) and low-income quartile (LIQ) within the CUD cohort.
RESULTS: Out of the young adult admissions, a total of 286,855 individuals were identified as recreational cannabis users. After propensity matching, we divided the CUD cohort into 63,355 patients with HIQ (41.1% female) and LIQ (41.4% female). While both cohorts exhibited comparable ages and racial distribution (> 65% white), the individuals from the LIQ cohort were predominantly from the South (45.7% vs. 27.9%), visiting rural hospitals (13.9% vs. 1.3%), with Medicaid (56.3% vs. 41.1%) as the predominant payer. Additionally, the LIQ cohort had a higher prevalence of drug abuse (65.5% vs. 58.4%), tobacco use (24.9% vs. 22.6%), HTN (17% vs. 14.7%), chronic pulmonary disease (13.2% vs. 12.7%), DM (8% vs. 6.6%), and obesity (10.9% vs. 10.0%). Additionally, in-hospital outcomes like MACCE (2% vs. 0.8%) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS) (0.5% vs. 0.3%) were higher in the LIQ cohort (Graphical Abstract). After adjusting for confounding factors, the risk of AIS in the HIQ cohort was 37% lower than in the LIQ cohort (OR: 0.63 [95% CI: 0.42-0.96]). All p values < 0.05.
CONCLUSION: Higher prevalence of CVD risk factors in the LIQ-CUD group and lower odds of AIS-related admissions in the HIQ-CUD group warrant targeted interventions and policy measures to understand and address the behavioral risk of cannabis use by economic status and disparities in MACCE.

Title: Data-driven phenotyping of infective endocarditis using unsupervised machine learning: toward a personalized approach.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Infective endocarditis (IE) is a heterogeneous disease with diverse clinical presentations, microbiological profiles, and outcomes. Conventional classification systems may not fully capture this complexity. We aimed to identify data-driven clinical phenotypes in IE using an unsupervised machine learning (ML) approach.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, 335 patients with definite IE from three hospitals were included. A total of 55 clinical, microbiological, and echocardiographic variables were analyzed. Missing data were imputed using the MissForest algorithm. Clustering was performed using spectral clustering based on a Gower dissimilarity matrix and supported by a Bayesian non-parametric approach. Associations between cluster assignment and clinical outcomes were assessed using regression analyses.
RESULTS: Two distinct clusters were identified, reflecting different clinical profiles. Cluster 1 was characterized by native valve endocarditis, a higher burden of comorbidities, inflammatory activation, and larger vegetations. Cluster 2 was characterized by prosthetic valve and device-related IE, higher rates of atrial fibrillation, and larger cardiac dimensions. Cluster assignment was not significantly associated with in-hospital mortality in either unadjusted or adjusted analyses. Increasing age emerged as an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality. In the adjusted model, Cluster 2 was independently associated with longer hospital stay, whereas no significant difference was observed in ICU stay.
CONCLUSION: Unsupervised ML identified two clinically distinct phenotypes in IE, reflecting disease heterogeneity. Although these phenotypes were not associated with major clinical outcomes, they provide a data-driven framework for understanding disease heterogeneity and may contribute to future personalized approaches in the management of IE. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine their clinical applicability.

Title: Genetic variations underlying bitter and sweet taste perception are associated with food and beverage intake habits and taste-modifying behaviors among Dutch adults with a prior myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Taste perception influences eating behaviors and varies partly based on genetics. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many variants related to bitter, sweet, salt, sour, and umami perception (taste-related variants), but whether these variants inform eating behaviors among patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) is unknown. This study investigated the associations of taste-related variants with eating behaviors in adults with a prior myocardial infarction (MI) and explored the potential for sex-specific effects.
METHODS: Analyzed, were 4,204 Dutch adults with a prior MI from the Alpha Omega Cohort (60-80 years; 21% female; BMI: 27.7 ± 3.8 kg/m2). We selected 39 taste-related variants identified in prior GWAS and determined their associations with reported intake frequency of 19 food and beverage groups and 7 taste-modifying behaviors (e.g. adding sugar to coffee) using multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, lifestyle and socioeconomic factors.
MAIN FINDINGS: 32/39 taste-related variants were nominally (p < 0.05) associated with at least one food or beverage group or taste-modifying behavior, of which 6 passed Bonferroni adjustment (p < 0.05/19 or 0.05/7, respectively). The strongest associations were for rs1726866--a functional variant in the TAS2R38 bitter taste receptor gene--for which each additional G allele related to higher bitter perception was associated with less frequent coffee (β = -1.1 servings/week; 95% CI: -1.75, -0.42) and more frequent tea intake (β = 1.0 servings/week: 95% CI: 0.42, 1.64). Other significant associations were identified for bitter-related variants with less frequent legume intake and addition of full-fat milk to coffee and sweet-related variants with more frequent red/orange vegetable and full-fat dairy intake. Exploratory interaction analyses also suggested potential sex-specific effects; for example, rs1726866 (G) was associated with adding less sugar to coffee among females, but more among males.
CONCLUSIONS: Bitter- and sweet-related variants were associated with food and beverage intake habits and taste-modifying behaviors in adults with a prior MI, with some evidence for sex-specificity. These findings support the relevance of taste-related variants to eating behaviors among CVD patients and suggest the benefit of leveraging these genetic factors when tailoring dietary recommendations for reducing secondary cardiovascular risk.

Title: Predictive value of cardiometabolic index combined with N-Terminal pro-B-Type natriuretic peptide for moderate- to high-risk patients with acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the correlation between the cardiometabolic index (CMI), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and early risk stratification in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and to evaluate the predictive value of their combination for identifying intermediate- and high-risk patients.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 298 patients with ACS admitted to the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of South China University of Technology from March 2024 to December 2025. According to the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) score, patients were divided into low-risk (n=209), intermediate-risk (n=67), and high-risk (n=22) groups. Univariate analysis and multiple linear regression were used to explore the associations of CMI and NT-proBNP with early risk. Spearman correlation analysis was applied to examine the correlations of CMI and NT-proBNP with early risk. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess the predictive efficacy of CMI combined with NT-proBNP for intermediate- and high-risk patients.
RESULTS: Baseline data analysis showed that CMI and NT-proBNP levels in the high-risk group were significantly higher than those in the intermediate- and low-risk groups ( P < 0.001). Spearman correlation analysis indicated that CMI and NT-proBNP were positively correlated with early risk in ACS patients. Multiple linear regression models revealed that CMI and NT-proBNP were independent influencing factors for early risk. The ROC curve showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of CMI combined with NT-proBNP for identifying intermediate- and high-risk patients was 0.782 (95% CI: 0.718-0.847), with an optimal cut-off value of 0.3, a sensitivity of 74.2%, and a specificity of 83.7%.
CONCLUSION: CMI and NT-proBNP are positively correlated with early risk in ACS patients and serve as independent influencing factors. The combination of CMI and NT-proBNP demonstrates good predictive value for intermediate- and high-risk ACS patients.

Title: Prediction of death by neurologic criteria in patients with non-traumatic acute brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robust predictors of death by neurologic criteria (DNC) after non-traumatic acute brain injury remain insufficiently defined. We therefore aimed to systematically synthesize the available evidence on prediction of DNC in non-traumatic brain injury.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched to August 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, observational studies, case series and registry data. Studies were included in the quantitative synthesis when sufficient comparable data for the same prognostic factor were available from at least two studies. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: The database search identified 2,091 records. Eighteen studies comprising reported study cohorts of 9,070 participants were included. Quantitative synthesis included four studies (n=1,738), comprising two post-cardiac arrest and two stroke cohorts. In stroke populations, CT markers of severe intracranial mass effect were associated with a more than threefold increased odds of DNC (pooled OR 3.14, 95%CI 1.98-4.96; p<0.0001; I2=0%), while in post-cardiac arrest cohorts lower gray-white matter ratio values were associated with progression to DNC (pooled mean difference -0.15, 95%CI -0.22 to -0.07; p<0.001; I2=72%).
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on predictors of DNC after non-traumatic acute brain injury remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous, with only a small number of studies providing robust analyses. Across these studies, CT-based markers - particularly indicators of diffuse cerebral edema or intracranial mass effect - show the most reproducible associations with progression to DNC.

Title: A novel method for biological age assessment utilizing hospitalization risk of cardiovascular disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aging is a complex process involving physiological changes that gradually impair function in organisms. Chronological age (CA) does not fully account for variability in the aging process, whereas biological age (BA) better reflects disease risk. This study introduces Cardiovascular Disease Probability-based Biological Age (CDPBA), a novel BA algorithm.
METHODS: We analyzed clinical data from 11.7 million individuals aged ≥ 40 years in the National Health Insurance Service database. Using a Cox proportional hazards model, clinical biomarkers, lifestyle factors, fine particulate matter exposure, and family history were used to estimate the 10-year risk of CVD hospitalization. Individual CDPBA was computed by comparing each subject's CVD risk with the median risk profile of the corresponding age group, thereby capturing the nonlinear relationship between CDPBA and biomarkers while maintaining interpretability.
RESULTS: Our CDPBA algorithm exhibited a strong correlation with CA (r > 0.92), and the estimated CDPBA distribution was symmetric with respect to CA. All-cause mortality prediction was robust (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]: 0.849 and 0.871 in men and women, respectively), outperforming the regression-based BA approach (AUROC: 0.777 and 0.683 for men and women, respectively). The slow-aging group mostly maintained their health, whereas the accelerated-aging group showed increasingly worse health over time. Using CVD median risk profiles, the CDPBA algorithm shows a high correlation with CA and demonstrates superior performance in predicting all-cause mortality compared to conventional regression methods.
CONCLUSION: The CDPBA provides a novel, interpretable approach to biological age estimation based on cardiovascular disease hospitalization risk.

Title: Multimodal non-invasive ultrasound for predicting severe coronary artery stenosis in right coronary dominant patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess the predictive value of multimodal non-invasive ultrasound in detecting severe coronary artery stenosis (CAS) in patients with right coronary artery dominance.
METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing coronary angiography and non-invasive echocardiography at the Department of Cardiology, Luzhou People's Hospital, between December 2021 and August 2023. Severe CAS (SCAS) was defined as CAS ≥ 75% based on angiographic results. Patients were categorized into the SCAS group and the NSCAS group (non-severe CAS).
RESULTS: A total of 121 patients were included, with 98 in the NSCAS group and 23 in the SCAS group. Compared to the NSCAS group, the SCAS group showed a lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (49.3 ± 9.8% vs. 58.9 ± 5.2%, p = 0.028), a higher left ventricular end-systolic diameter(LVsd) (35.2 ± 7.7 mm vs. 29.8 ± 5.0 mm, p = 0.020), and a higher end-systolic volume༈ESV༉ (54.0 ± 23.0 ml vs. 35.7 ± 21.8 ml, p = 0.041). According to the receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, the optimal cutoff values for predicting SCAS are as follows: motion score, 1.5; ESV, 47.5 ml; LVsd, 30.5 mm; LVEF, 53.5%; mitral annular systolic velocity༈Smv༉, 8.5 cm/s; and global longitudinal peak strain༈GLPS༉, -16.5% (all p < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression showed that LVEF was associated with SCAS (OR = 1.600, 95% CI:1.037-2.468, P = 0.034).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that LVEF may play a role in predicting SCAS, validating non-invasive ultrasound as an effective early diagnostic tool for patients with right coronary artery dominance.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

Title: Association between rhythm control strategy and clinical outcomes in postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management strategy for postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains debated. While rhythm control aims to restore sinus rhythm, its impact on clinical resource utilization and long-term outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between an initial rhythm control strategy (as an escalation to rate control) and clinical outcomes compared to rate control alone.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study identified 663 adult patients who developed POAF after isolated CABG from the MIMIC-IV database. We used two statistical approaches to control for confounding: a primary analysis on a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort and a sensitivity analysis using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) on the entire cohort. The primary outcome was sinus rhythm (SR) conversion within 24 h. Secondary outcomes included length of ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and long-term mortality.
RESULTS: The rhythm control strategy was associated with a higher 24-hour SR conversion rate compared to rate control (PSM cohort: 71.7% vs. 32.3%; OR, 2.65; P = 0.010). However, patients in the rhythm control group had a significantly longer ICU length of stay (median 3.42 vs. 3.08 days; P = 0.026). No significant differences were found in AKI incidence or long-term mortality. Subgroup analysis indicated that the benefit of SR conversion was attenuated in patients with diabetes (P for interaction < 0.05). Findings were consistent in the IPTW sensitivity analysis.
CONCLUSION: Although effective for early rhythm restoration, an initial rhythm control strategy is associated with longer ICU stays and no survival benefit compared to rate control.

Title: Reduced Risk of MASLD and Cardiometabolic Disease Following Renal Denervation Therapy in Patients With Resistant Hypertension.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autonomic dysfunction increases the risk of cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Renal denervation reduces renal sympathetic nerve activity and lowers blood pressure independent of long-term pharmacotherapy, with potential downstream effects on metabolic and hepatic pathways. We aimed to evaluate the impact of renal denervation, compared with intensive antihypertensive therapy, on cardiometabolic disease risk.
METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation using the TriNetX global federated health research network. Eligible participants were adults with hypertension (ICD-10 code I10) who were treated with either renal denervation therapy and pharmacological treatment (identified via ICD-10 or Current Procedural Terminology codes), acting as the treatment group, or an intensive pharmacological antihypertensive regime (four of a beta blocker, calcium channel blocker, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, angiotensin II receptor blocker, alpha blocker or diuretic), acting as the control group. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced the treatment and control groups, accounting for confounding variables. The primary outcome was of MASLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), while secondary outcomes included T2D, CKD and a composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): sudden cardiac death, ischaemic heart disease (IHD), cerebrovascular accident (CVA), peripheral vascular disease (PVD) and heart failure (HF). Cox regression generated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: After matching, 1735 patients remained in each group, with well-balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 42 vs. 41 years; standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.05; 52.6% vs. 54.3% male; SMD 0.03). After PSM, renal denervation was associated with a lower risk of MASLD (HR 0.38 [0.29, 0.51]), T2D (HR 0.21 [0.13, 0.33]), CKD (HR 0.26 [0.20, 0.35]), MACE (HR 0.46 [0.34, 0.62]), IHD (HR 0.56 [0.39, 0.80]), CVA (HR 0.33 [0.20, 0.52]) and HF (HR 0.39 [0.25, 0.62]).
CONCLUSION: Control of the sympathetic nervous system with renal denervation therapy in patients with resistant hypertension is associated with a lower risk of incident CKM syndrome including MASLD, T2D, CVD and CKD, supporting the role of autonomic dysfunction in the progression of cardiometabolic disease.

Title: Clinical heterogeneity in chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy: data-driven subtypes challenge current classification.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) presents with substantial phenotypic heterogeneity, yet current classifications do not adequately capture clinically meaningful subgroups. Thus, we aimed to discover novel, clinically meaningful CIDP subgroups using unbiased clustering.
METHODS: In this observational, multicenter retrospective cohort study we screened 425 patients diagnosed with typical CIDP or CIDP variants from 10 German centers. Standardized data including demographic, clinical, electrophysiological, laboratory, comorbidity, and treatment information were collected. 325 patients were then randomly assigned to the discovery cohort and 100 to the validation cohort. We performed unbiased clustering and post-hoc analysis to identify clusters and define subtypes.
FINDINGS: Four distinct clusters showed marked differences: Cluster 1: Female patients with high symptom level, high disability scores, ANA positivity and autoimmune comorbidities Cluster 2: Moderate to low symptom level with low disability scores, demyelination-dominant and less comorbidities Cluster 3: High symptom level, axonal-demyelinating damage and cardiovascular comorbidities Cluster 4: Multifocal CIDP with high disability scores as well as frequent ataxia and areflexia Post hoc analyses showed marked differences in disease progression and therapeutic strategies, with clusters 1 and 4 showing particularly high rates of progression and disability.
INTERPRETATION: Unbiased clustering revealed four clinically meaningful CIDP subtypes, each exhibiting distinct presentations and trajectories. We identified two red flag subgroups suggesting that CIDP comprises biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease phenotypes. These findings may support more individualized monitoring and therapeutic strategies for high-risk patients and raise the possibility of distinct underlying pathomechanisms across CIDP subgroups.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: GLP-1-based therapies in cardiovascular disease: outcomes, mechanisms, and emerging clinical applications.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have shown cardiovascular benefits beyond their established role in treating type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This review evaluates recent clinical evidence, potential mechanisms, and the expanding use of GLP-1-based therapies in cardiovascular disease.
METHODS: We reviewed major randomized clinical trials assessing cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure outcomes, along with related mechanistic studies and clinical guidelines published through July 2026.
RESULTS: Early trials, including LEADER, SUSTAIN-6, and REWIND, reported 12%-26% reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with T2DM. More recent trials have extended these findings to other populations. SELECT showed a 20% reduction in MACE among individuals with obesity and established cardiovascular disease but without diabetes, while FLOW demonstrated a 24% reduction in its primary kidney composite outcome. SOUL reported a 14% reduction in MACE with oral semaglutide, and SUMMIT showed a 38% reduction in cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure with tirzepatide. SURPASS-CVOT found tirzepatide to be noninferior, but not superior, to dulaglutide for MACE. These benefits likely involve several mechanisms beyond glucose lowering and weight loss, although gastrointestinal adverse effects still remain a concern.
CONCLUSIONS: Growing clinical evidence supports the use of GLP-1-based therapies beyond diabetes management, particularly in patients with cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, or obesity-related heart failure. Further studies will be needed to understand their mechanisms better, long-term safety, and optimal use in clinical practice.

Title: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood.
METHODS: This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD (n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1-4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development.
RESULTS: White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency (p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive (p = 0.001), language (p < 0.001), and motor (p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64-12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors.
CONCLUSION: In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population.
IMPACT: In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

Title: Fish intake and mortality in Japan, a high fish-consuming country: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies.
Abstract: Fish consumption has been linked to decreased mortality risk in several prospective studies. However, most existing evidence is based on multi-regional analyses, and the dose-response relationship in populations with high habitual fish intake remains insufficiently characterised. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies among Japanese adults to assess the associations between fish consumption and all-cause and cause-specific mortality and to investigate potential dose-response relationships in a high-fish-intake population. We systematically searched the MEDLINE and Ichushi-Web databases. Prospective cohort studies conducted in Japan that reported hazard ratios or relative risks for fish intake and mortality outcomes were included. The protocol was registered a priori in the PROSPERO database (CRD42025635066). Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled estimates by comparing the highest and lowest intake categories. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using generalised least-squares trend estimation and restricted cubic spline models. A total of 113 articles were assessed for eligibility, and 16 studies met the inclusion criteria, and nine were eligible for meta-analysis. Higher fish intake was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.89-0.98) and cardiovascular disease mortality (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.80-0.91), with low heterogeneity. According to the GRADE framework, the certainty of evidence was rated low. Visual inspection suggested that mortality risk reduced with increasing fish intake up to approximately 100 g/day, after which the decline slowed, implying a plateau effect at higher intake levels. Among Japanese adults, high fish consumption was associated with a lower risk of all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality. Further research is required to clarify the dose-response relationship in populations with high fish consumption.

Title: The Impact of Postoperative Mechanical Ventilation Duration on Visual and Auditory Hallucinations After Cardiac Surgery: Insights from the VAACS Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether postoperative mechanical ventilation duration is associated with the risk and timing of visual and auditory hallucinations after adult cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: Prospective multicenter cohort study.
SETTING: Ten major cardiac surgery centers in the West Bank, Palestine.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1,332 adults undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting or valve surgery, stratified by postoperative ventilation duration: ≤6 hours or >6 hours.
INTERVENTIONS: No experimental intervention was performed; patients were grouped by early versus delayed postoperative extubation.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Visual and auditory hallucinations were assessed during the first 7 postoperative days using the Questionnaire for Psychotic Experiences. Cox regression and restricted mean survival time analyses evaluated associations between ventilation duration and hallucination outcomes. Delayed extubation (>6 hours) was associated with lower overall adjusted risk of visual hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.62-0.80; p < .001) and auditory hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.49; 95% confidence interval, 0.31-0.77; p = .002). However, time-varying analysis showed increased immediate postoperative hazard in the delayed-extubation group, with risk declining rapidly over time. Restricted mean survival time analysis showed that auditory hallucination-free time was approximately 0.24 days shorter in patients with delayed extubation (p < .001). Preoperative white blood cell count was the most consistent predictor.
CONCLUSION: Delayed postoperative extubation was associated with lower overall 7-day hallucination risk but higher immediate postoperative vulnerability, suggesting that the early postextubation period may represent a critical window for targeted monitoring and preventive neuropsychiatric care after cardiac surgery.

Title: Indocyanine green dosing and imaging conditions for intraoperative fluorescence assessment during coronary artery bypass grafting: A systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative indocyanine green fluorescence is used to assess graft filling and myocardial perfusion during coronary artery bypass grafting, although dosing and imaging protocols vary. This review evaluated dose, imaging conditions, visualization, technical abnormality detection, revision, quantitative perfusion, and safety.
METHODS: Ovid MEDLINE, CINAHL Plus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched. Three reviewers selected studies and extracted data. Overlapping reports were reconciled into clusters. Doses were normalized to milligrams per injection. Risk of bias was assessed with design-appropriate instruments and certainty with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework. Findings were synthesized by application and imaging method.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven reports represented 20 clusters. Fluorescence appeared within 2-20 seconds. Fluorescence was detected in 525 of 533 conduits, and 379 of 507 grafts were fully analyzable. Indocyanine green findings prompted correction or revision in 5 of 348 conduits and 6 of 289, 8 of 533, and 4 of 107 grafts, with restored fluorescence or confirmed patency after intervention. In 139 grafts assessed against angiography, indocyanine green identified stenosis or occlusion with 83.3% sensitivity and 100% specificity. One randomized study reported normal indocyanine green findings in all 8 grafts meeting combined revision criteria. Quantitative fluorescence identified reduced intensity in 5 of 6 graft failures. Perfusion thresholds were met in 275 of 359 and 63 of 75 myocardial territories. Fixed doses ranged from 0.0125 to 6.25 mg per injection, without direct evidence defining an optimal regimen.
CONCLUSION: Indocyanine green fluorescence supports rapid visualization of graft filling and may assist intraoperative reassessment during coronary artery bypass grafting. This review defines the reported dose range and identifies the exposure, acquisition, outcome, and safety variables required for more consistent comparison and interpretation.

Title: Electrocardiogram Embeddings Beyond Chronological Age for Prediagnostic Cognitive Impairment and Dementia: Development and External Validation Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia is a growing health burden worldwide; however, scalable, low-cost strategies for early risk identification are lacking. Because cardiac and cognitive aging are closely associated, a routinely collected 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), interpreted using foundation model embeddings, is a promising and accessible candidate marker. However, it is unclear whether such embeddings carry predictive information independent of chronological age-the dominant risk factor for dementia-and whether the underlying changes follow a detectable prediagnostic trajectory.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate whether foundation model embeddings of routine ECGs carry information that distinguishes patients later diagnosed with cognitive impairment or dementia from matched controls, beyond chronological age, and, if so, whether the underlying ECG changes intensify as diagnosis approaches.
METHODS: In a retrospective two-site Korean cohort (Severance Hospital, development n=52,355; Yongin Severance Hospital, external n=6500), embeddings from the knowledge-enhanced diagnosis foundation model supported an ECG-only classifier that discriminated patients diagnosed with cognitive impairment or dementia within the following 10 years from matched controls, using only ECGs interpreted as normal sinus rhythm. We compared an age-only model with a late fusion of age and ECG-derived probability and tested whether age-residualized embedding is predictive as direct evidence of age-independent information. Discrimination was summarized by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with 95% bootstrap CIs, and DeLong tests and net reclassification improvement (NRI) were used for between-model comparisons. To trace the prediagnostic time course, we analyzed ECG phenotype labels across four windows before diagnosis in an exact-age-matched case-control set.
RESULTS: Chronological age strongly discriminated cases from controls in both cohorts (external AUROC 0.809, 95% CI 0.799-0.819). Adding ECG-derived probability improved discrimination, calibration, and net benefit over age alone (external AUROC 0.825, 95% CI 0.816-0.834; DeLong P<.001; positive NRI). Critically, even after removing the age-predictable component, age-residualized embedding retained modest but reproducible discrimination in both internal (AUROC 0.590, 95% CI 0.581-0.599) and external (AUROC 0.579, 95% CI 0.567-0.592) validation (both P<.001), indicating dementia-relevant information that was not explained by chronological age. Of the 105 ECG labels, 19 (18.1%) showed a case-control difference that widened significantly toward diagnosis, dominated by nonspecific ST segment and T wave changes, acute ischemic patterns (acute myocardial infarction), and atrial and junctional arrhythmias (atrial flutter, ectopic atrial, and accelerated junctional rhythms), with divergence emerging mainly in the proximal (1-3-year) and imminent (0-1-year) windows.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine ECG foundation model embeddings encode aging-related electrophysiological information that is complementary to and not fully explained by chronological age and intensifies as diagnosis approaches, with concurrent shifts toward ischemic and arrhythmic ECG patterns whose mechanism cannot be determined from these data. These findings suggest that routine ECG is a low-cost, age-complementary triage signal for cognitive impairment and dementia screening, rather than a stand-alone diagnostic test.

Title: Clinical triage concordance of a point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay using the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm.
Journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) assays have demonstrated good analytical agreement with central laboratory (CL) testing, it remains uncertain whether they yield the same clinical triage decisions. We evaluated the clinical concordance of a POC hs-cTnI assay with a CL assay using the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h algorithm.
METHODS: This prospective diagnostic agreement study included 127 patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected acute coronary syndrome. The primary outcome was concordance of patient classification according to the 0/1-h algorithm, assessed using the quadratic weighted kappa (κ) statistic. Secondary outcomes included quantitative agreement assessed by the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis, and analytical comparability between whole blood and plasma on the POC platform.
RESULTS: Overall, 114/127 patients (89.8%) were assigned to the same triage category (κ = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.878-0.964). All 13 discordant classifications (10.2%) occurred between adjacent categories, with no CL rule-in patient classified as POC rule-out. Quantitative agreement between assays was good (ICC = 0.882; 95%CI 0.835-0.917), with a mean bias of -5.27 ng/L. Whole blood and plasma showed close agreement (ICC = 0.999; 95%CI 0.998-0.999), with a mean bias of 0.50 ng/L.
CONCLUSIONS: The POC assay showed high clinical concordance with CL-based ESC 0/1-h triage classification, with all discordances confined to adjacent categories. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence supporting further prospective evaluation of POC hs-cTnI testing under routine bedside conditions.

Title: Cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks of sex hormone therapy: from contraception to transgender care.
Abstract: The risk of venous thromboembolism is increased with combined oral contraceptives, rises with the dose of ethinylestradiol, and is higher with desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone or cyproterone acetate than with levonorgestrel; the determinant is not the generation of the pill but the residual androgen-receptor activity of the progestin, which modulates the hepatic effect of the estrogen. Age over 35 years, obesity, smoking and a family history of thrombosis amplify it. Pills based on a native estrogen have a more limited hepatic impact and rank below most ethinylestradiol combinations in contemporary cohorts, but their clinical safety is not demonstrated and no comparative outcome data exist for estetrol/drospirenone. Androgenicity is not a general marker of venous safety: injectable depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, given alone at supraphysiological doses, carries an increased risk. Myocardial infarction and stroke are also more frequent, but against a very low background - about 21 additional strokes and 10 additional infarctions per 100,000 person-years, four times fewer than the venous excess - and, unlike venous events, independent of progestin type. Menopause hormone therapy increases venous thromboembolic risk, especially in the first year; the route of administration is the main determinant, transdermal estradiol with micronized progesterone appearing safest. In cisgender men, testosterone deficiency carries increased cardiovascular risk, and randomized and real-world data support the safety of transdermal replacement, although more pulmonary embolism and atrial fibrillation have been observed. In trans women, observational data show an increased risk of stroke and venous thromboembolism, particularly with oral estradiol and cyproterone acetate, whereas recent large-scale data show no excess of major cardiovascular events with testosterone in trans men. The practical consequences are specific: no combined pill is acceptable after a venous thromboembolic event, with a thrombogenic mutation or with migraine with aura, native-estrogen pills included; transdermal estradiol should be preferred for menopause and feminising hormone therapy; and haematocrit should guide the dose and route of testosterone.

Title: Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry.
METHODS: This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria.
RESULTS: Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis.
CONCLUSION: In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

Title: Leadless Atrial Pacing Targeting Bachmann Bundle for Atrial Resynchronization: A Single Center Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial conduction delay (IACD) resulting from fibrosis or functional block in Bachmann bundle (BB) occurs often in patients with sinus node dysfunction (SND) and increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pacing the BB in patients with SND may reduce AF burden. Little is known of the feasibility and effectiveness of BB leadless atrial pacemaker (BBLAP) implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine if BBLAP is safe, feasible and improves IACD.
METHODS: This registry prospectively enrolled 21 consecutive adults with baseline P wave duration (PWD) >120ms undergoing BBLAP for SND. Fluoroscopy, intracardiac echocardiography and left atrial conduction time (LACT) measurements from a decapolar coronary sinus (CS) catheter were used to facilitate implantation. BBLAP implant success was defined as improved PWD, P wave morphology, and LACT. Baseline and BBLAP LACT and PWD, axis, and morphology were compared.
RESULTS: Of the 21 patients enrolled, 17 had successful BBLAP (81%). Among those with successful BBLAP, baseline PWD was 150 (±21) ms, BBLAP PWD was 113 (±23) ms, a reduction of 37 (±13) ms, p < 0.001. BBLAP P wave axis was inferiorly directed in all cases. 8/8 patients with a negative terminal P wave in the inferior leads at baseline had correction with BBLAP. LACT decreased from 113 (±35) ms to 78 (±33) ms, mean difference 35 (±15) ms, p <0.001, with BBLAP. 13/17 patients demonstrated a shift in CS activation from proximal-distal activation to mid- or distal-proximal activation during BBLAP. In all cases there were no complications.
CONCLUSION: The BBLAP implant technique presented in this registry is feasible and reduced IACD. Further study on the effect of BBLAP on AF burden is needed.

Title: High- and Moderate-Intensity Interval Training for Cardiac-Psychological Comorbidity: Results from a 4-Week Intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common in patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and are associated with poorer prognosis. Exercise-based rehabilitation may improve both psychological and cardiopulmonary outcomes in this population.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the short-term effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity interval training (MIIT) in CVD patients with comorbid anxiety and/or depression.
METHODS: This retrospective real-world study screened 1,020 cardiac rehabilitation patients, of whom 112 were included in the final analysis. All participants completed a 4-week supervised outpatient HIIT or MIIT. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using the GAD-7 and PHQ-9, and cardiopulmonary fitness was evaluated by standardized cardiopulmonary exercise testing.
RESULTS: After 4 weeks, in the HIIT group, GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores decreased by 4.4 ± 4.3 and 3.7 ± 4.3 points (Cohen's d = -1.023 and -0.860; p < 0.001); in the MIIT group, the corresponding reductions were 4.8 ± 4.9 and 3.5 ± 4.0 points (Cohen's d = -0.980 and -0.875; p < 0.001). Both groups also demonstrated significant improvements in multiple cardiopulmonary parameters (all p < 0.05). Nominal between-group differences were observed for AT VO₂ and PETCO₂ before multiplicity correction, but neither difference remained statistically significant after FDR correction.
CONCLUSIONS: In clinical practice, short-term HIIT and MIIT may both be feasible strategies to alleviate psychological symptoms and improve cardiopulmonary fitness in CVD patients with comorbid anxiety or depression.

Title: Exercise Capacity, Muscle Mass, and Quality of Life in Pediatric Patients with Fontan Circulation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how measures of cardiac, vascular, and muscle health relate to Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory TM (PedsQL) score in a cohort of children and adolescents with Fontan circulation.
STUDY DESIGN: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from children and adolescents (8-19 years) with Fontan circulation enrolled in a prospective study. Participants underwent a series of tests, including a cardiopulmonary exercise test, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry measures of appendicular lean mass index (ALMI, kg/m2), leg dynamometry, and the 23-item PedsQL. The survey quantifies Physical, Emotional, Social, and School functioning into 1 total score and 2 summary scores for physical and psychosocial health.
RESULTS: 135 patients (median age 12.7 [IQR 10.2, 15.6] years) completed the baseline visit. Median time from Fontan operation was 8.7 years [IQR 5.9, 12.0]. Peak VO2 was 1309 [IQR 1070, 1670] mL/min, and indexed peak VO2 was 31.1 [IQR 25.2, 36.1] mL/kg/min. Physical and Psychosocial PedsQL summary scores were 78.1 [IQR 67.2,90.6] and 76.7 [IQR 63.3, 90], respectively, and the total score was 76.1 [IQR 65.2, 88.0]. Absolute peak VO2 was weakly correlated with PedsQL Physical Summary Score (ρ=0.21, P=0.015), but indexed peak VO2, % predicted peak VO2, and Fontan-specific peak VO2 z-score were not ALMI z-score was -0.84 [IQR -1.56, -0.14] and positively correlated with total PedsQL score (ρ=0.28, P=0.001) and the Physical Functioning domain (ρ=0.30, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal muscle mass was associated with quality of life in children with Fontan circulation. The association between VO2 and physical function was attenuated with body-size normalization.

Title: Life's Essential 8 Cardiovascular Health Characteristics in Children and Adolescents with Congenital Heart Disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the cardiovascular health (CVH) characteristics in children and adolescents with congenital heart disease (CHD) using a modified version of the American Heart Association (AHA) Life's Essential 8 criteria and examine differences in CVH by CHD complexity.
STUDY DESIGN: This single-center, cross-sectional study included youth 8-19 years old with CHD and an available total cholesterol within 3 years of a clinic visit. Patients were categorized into simple, moderate, or complex anatomic groups according to AHA anatomic classification guidelines for CHD. Modified CVH scores were calculated using 3 to 5 CVH metrics: nicotine exposure, body mass index (BMI), blood lipids, blood glucose, and blood pressure. The association between anatomic complexity and CVH was assessed using multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: The study cohort included 629 patients. Modified CVH scores were low or moderate in 46.1% of patients, with prevalent low or moderate scores in blood lipids (49.4%), blood pressure (42.4%), and BMI (31.9%). Median CVH scores differed across anatomic groups (simple 83 vs moderate 78 vs complex 84, P=0.01). Complex CHD was associated with a higher (more favorable) modified CVH score and blood pressure score than moderate CHD and a higher blood lipids score than simple and moderate CHD.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite vulnerable cardiac anatomy, almost half of youth with CHD had suboptimal CVH, with prevalent deficits in blood lipids, blood pressure, and BMI. Complex CHD anatomy was associated with a more favorable CVH profile. These findings highlight the need to incorporate health screening and promotion into the routine care of the pediatric CHD population.

Title: Pharmacotherapy for MASLD: current evidence and challenges in clinical practice.
Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by a complex pathophysiology driven by intertwined metabolic and hepatic pathways, enabling the identification of multiple therapeutic targets and a rapidly expanding drug development pipeline. This review summarizes the current and emerging therapeutic landscape for MASLD and discusses key challenges for clinical implementation. The imminent availability of several new therapies is expected to pose important clinical challenges, particularly in accurately identifying patients most likely to benefit. Currently, resmetirom and semaglutide are the only two drugs conditionally approved for patients with fibrosis stages 2-3, pending final phase 3 outcomes, and represent the main liver-directed and metabolic-focused therapeutic strategies, respectively. Treatment selection should follow a phenotype-based approach integrating metabolic profile and liver disease stage. Non-invasive tests are central for assessing treatment eligibility; however, strategies incorporating metabolic risk profiling and longitudinal monitoring will be essential to optimize real-world management of MASH.
