Title: Myocardial Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder with Anxious Distress: Evidence from Oxygenation-Sensitive CMR and Entropy Analysis.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with major depressive disorder with anxious distress (MDD-A) frequently experience cardiovascular symptoms (CVS), which are associated with impaired quality of life and poorer long-term prognosis. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate myocardial alterations in MDD-A patients using oxygenation-sensitive cardiovascular magnetic resonance (OS-CMR) and mapping-derived entropy analysis, and to explore their associations with CVS as well as the severity of depressive and anxiety symptoms.
METHODS: In this prospective study, 58 consecutively enrolled medication-naïve patients with MDD-A diagnosed according to DSM-5 criteria and 61 healthy controls were included. All participants underwent CMR examinations at 3.0T. Left ventricular (LV) function, native T1 and T2 values, T1-entropy and T2-entropy, LV strain parameters, and oxygenation-sensitive signal intensity change (OS-SI%) were measured and compared between the two groups. Associations between CMR-derived parameters and CVS, anxiety symptom severity, and depressive symptom severity were assessed separately. A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, patients with MDD-A exhibited significantly higher T1-entropy (8.3 ± 0.3 vs. 7.5 ± 0.3, p < 0.001) and T2-entropy (9.2 ± 0.4 vs. 8.1 ± 0.3, p < 0.001), whereas OS-SI% was significantly lower (11.4 ± 7.5% vs. 14.5 ± 4.5%, p = 0.007). After adjustment for age, sex, smoking status, and heart rate, multivariable regression analyses revealed that OS-SI% was inversely associated with HAMD scores (β = -0.205, p = 0.043) and HAMA scores (β = -0.453, p < 0.001), and inversely associated with CVS (OR= 0.801, p = 0.002). T1-entropy (β = 4.105, p = 0.022) and T2-entropy (β = 2.793, p = 0.042) were positively associated with HAMD scores.
CONCLUSION: OS-SI% and mapping-derived myocardial entropy measures may serve as valuable noninvasive imaging biomarkers for assessing early myocardial alterations in patients with MDD-A.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 inhibitor use during or after acute kidney injury and the risk of major adverse kidney events and Mortality: A systematic review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, and pharmacologic strategies to improve outcomes after AKI remain limited. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have established cardiovascular and renal benefits, but their role during or after AKI remains less clearly defined.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420261298733). Six databases were searched through February 9, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults with established AKI, compared SGLT2i use with control or nonuse, and reported at least one clinical outcome. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse kidney events (MAKE). Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality and odds ratios (ORs) from crude event counts for MAKE.
RESULTS: Seven studies were included (six observational, one randomized). SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.59-0.71; I2 = 32%; three cohorts) and lower odds of MAKE (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.44-0.88; I2 = 91%; five studies), but the MAKE estimate was not robust to exclusion of individual studies and MAKE definitions varied. Kidney replacement therapy (two studies) was not pooled. The randomized trial (n = 200) was inconclusive for mortality (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.12-1.29) and MAKE (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.52-1.67). Certainty of evidence was very low.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i use during or after AKI was associated with lower mortality and MAKE in observational studies (very low certainty of evidence), whereas the only randomized trial was too small to be conclusive. Confounding by indication is likely, and the evidence remains limited by heterogeneity and the predominance of observational data. Randomized trials are needed.

Title: Sepsis Prior to Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Elevated Rates of Myocardial Infarction and Deep Vein Thrombosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients who have sepsis often experience persistent physiological instability, which may increase vulnerability to postoperative complications. However, the impact of preoperative sepsis on outcomes following elective total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains poorly defined. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate the association of preoperative sepsis with 90-day and two-year postoperative complications following TKA.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted utilizing an insurance database. Patients who had a preoperative diagnosis of sepsis within two years prior to TKA were matched 1:3 to controls based on demographics and comorbidities. Patients who had sepsis were stratified according to the following timeline: sepsis three months prior to surgery, three to six months prior, six to 12 months prior, 12 to 18 months prior, and 18 to 24 months prior. Medical and surgical complications were assessed at 90 days and two years following surgery. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: Patients who had sepsis within two years prior to surgery exhibited increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) (odds ratio (OR): 1.6), postoperative sepsis (OR: 2.7), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.4), urinary tract infection (OR: 1.8), blood transfusion (OR: 2.0), readmission (OR: 1.3), and wound dehiscence (OR: 1.4) within 90 days of surgery. At two years following surgery, sepsis was associated with elevated rates of revision surgery (OR: 1.3), PJI (OR: 1.6), osteomyelitis (OR: 1.9), and mortality (OR: 1.3). Sepsis within three months of operation was associated with elevated rates of myocardial infarction (OR: 2.1) and deep vein thrombosis (OR: 2.0). All findings were statistically significant at P < 0.05.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative sepsis is associated with increased complications following TKA, including periprosthetic joint infection and mortality. Sepsis within three months of surgery confers a particularly elevated risk of myocardial infarction and deep vein thrombosis following TKA.

Title: Novel Relationships between the ICAD, CD53, GRM1, and GSTmu Protein Levels and Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Outcomes.
Abstract: The aim of the present study was to identify serum proteins associated with atherosclerosis and its comorbidities. The 3-year follow-up included 216 patients subjected to coronary angiography. Gensini score was used to quantify coronary atherosclerosis, and peripheral atherosclerosis was assessed by B-mode ultrasound. Serum proteins were profiled using an Explorer antibody microarray (Full Moon Biosystems, USA). In-house ELISA or commercial ELISA kits were used to validate the microarray data in the total cohort for the top five proteins from the atherosclerotic profile. Only ICAD (DNA fragmentation factor subunit, DFF45/ICAD) was linked to type 2 diabetes and the presence of coronary artery stenosis regardless of the severity of stenosis. CD53 was also associated with coronary stenosis. IL-6 was associated with diabetes, and GSTmu (glutathione S-transferase Mu3) was associated with brachiocephalic stenosis ≥ 60% and with femoral and coronary arterial lesions. Only GRM1 (glutamate metabotropic receptor 1) showed inverse associations with coronary stenosis and cardiovascular outcomes (r = -0.24 and P = 0.025 and r = -0.31 and P = 0.007, respectively). Moreover, GRM1 was inversely associated with femoral lesions ≥ 30%. Thus, we identified previously unreported associations of the ICAD, CD53, GRM1, and GSTmu proteins with atherosclerosis, diabetes, and nonfatal cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Urinary Proteomic Panel Distinguishes Acute Myocarditis from Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Reliable noninvasive discrimination of acute myocarditis (AM) from acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in patients presenting with acute chest pain remains an unmet clinical need. We aimed to identify urinary proteomic markers using mass spectrometry and LASSO regression. Patients with suspected AM or AMI were prospectively enrolled. Urinary proteomes were profiled by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. The discovery cohort was stratified by age and sex and randomly divided into training and internal validation sets at a 3:1 ratio. Differentially expressed proteins were screened, and a diagnostic model was constructed using LASSO with 1000 bootstrap resamplings in the training set. The model was validated internally and further verified in an independent cohort using ELISA. A total of 42 AM and 80 AMI patients were included in the discovery cohort. Differential expression analysis in the training set identified 880 and 1099 differentially expressed proteins in AM and AMI, respectively, compared with controls. A three-protein panel comprising TNFRSF1A, F9, and PRDX3 achieved an AUC of 0.954 in the training set and exceeded the clinical models (all DeLong's P < 0.05). Addition of the protein panel to either clinical model further improved diagnostic performance (both P < 0.001). Similar performance was confirmed in the validation cohorts. A urinary proteomic panel comprising TNFRSF1A, F9, and PRDX3 may provide a noninvasive approach for differentiating AM from AMI.

Title: Age-Dependent Heterogeneity Trends in the Associations between Urban Green Space and Cardiovascular Health in a Humid-Subtropical Megacity.
Abstract: Urban green space (UGS) is a promising nature-based solution for cardiovascular health, yet its associative pathways in pollution-saturated, high-density environments remain contested. We applied a two-stage framework combining gradient boosting decision trees and structural equation modeling to a clinical cohort of 23,312 patients in Nanjing, China. Air-quality-related pathways accounted for more than 75% of the relative statistical contribution to model variance, exceeding psychological restoration proxies. At the macroscale, the aggregated air-quality pathway showed a marginal positive coefficient; although this may conceptually resemble aerodynamic interference, the interpretation remains speculative because no morphological or fluid-dynamics data were available. Stage 2 models identified distinct protective associative networks. For chronic ischemic heart disease, vegetation vitality was inversely associated with NO2 and SO2 and was linked to more favorable metabolic markers. For heart failure, the vegetation condition was associated with mixed pollutants and hemodynamic-metabolic indicators. Age-stratified analyses suggested heterogeneity in canopy density-PM2.5 associations, but subgroup slopes were nonsignificant, and effect sizes were extremely small, indicating fragile relative fluctuations rather than structural reversal. These findings characterize UGS primarily as a biophysical modulator and support targeted ecological strategies in traffic corridors and aging communities.

Title: Strontium and Lead Accelerate, Calcium Protects: Arterial Stiffness Progression in an 11-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Arterial stiffness measured by estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is an established predictor of cardiovascular disease. Long-term metal exposure may drive arterial stiffness progression, but prior studies largely relied on single-time assessments of exposure or outcome, overlooking heterogeneity in ePWV progression and its longitudinal links to long-term metal exposure. In an 11-year prospective study of 707 participants from the Manganese-Exposed Workers Healthy Cohort, we repeatedly quantified blood cell metals and computed cumulative exposure indices (CEIs). Latent class mixed models identified low and high ePWV trajectories. A one-quantile increase in CEI of a five-metal mixture [strontium (Sr), calcium (Ca), lead (Pb), magnesium, and manganese] was associated with belonging to the high ePWV trajectory (OR = 1.62; 95% CI: 1.14-2.31), with CEI_Sr and CEI_Pb as positive drivers and CEI_Ca inversely associated. The stronger CEI_Sr and CEI_Pb effects were observed in participants with high body mass index or smokers. The distinct trajectories of metal exposure were further identified; we found that the high-decreasing Pb trajectory was associated with higher odds of the high ePWV trajectory compared with the low-decreasing Pb trajectory (OR = 3.98; 95% CI: 1.28-13.26). We provided insights into the longitudinal links between long-term metal exposure and arterial stiffness progression, emphasizing the critical role of metal biomonitoring and primary prevention of arteriosclerosis in high-risk populations.

Title: Learning curve and clinical outcomes of robotic-assisted heart bypass surgery: Real-world evidence from India.
Abstract: BackgroundRobotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) using bilateral internal mammary arteries (BIMA) provides a minimally invasive option for advanced coronary artery disease (CAD), but evidence on its learning curve and outcomes in the Indian population remains limited.ObjectivesTo evaluate the learning curve associated with robotic CABG using BIMA and to compare perioperative and clinical outcomes between the early and late phases of surgical experience in a real-world setting.DesignRetrospective, single-center, observational chart review conducted at a high-volume quaternary cardiac care center in India.MethodsThis retrospective chart review was performed for 341 patients who underwent robotic-assisted BIMA CABG between 2020 and 2025. The learning curve was assessed using risk-adjusted cumulative summation (CUSUM), while complication trends were examined through sequential probability CUSUM failure analysis.ResultsThe cohort comprised 295 (86.51%) males with a mean age of 59.56 ± 9.93 years and a body mass index (BMI) of 25.98 ± 3.74 kg/m2. Mean console time was 101.66 ± 29.99 minutes, ICU stay 2.85 ± 0.98 days, and hospital stay 6.01 ± 2.38 days; conversion to open surgery occurred in 2.93% of cases, with in-hospital mortality of 3.52%. CUSUM analysis identified case 125 as the proficiency inflection point, after which console time significantly decreased (94.95 ± 24.32 vs. 113.38 ± 35.04 minutes; p<0.001), while ventilator duration, ICU and hospital stay, complications, and mortality remained comparable between phases. Readmission and re-exploration rates were low (2.05% each), with no deaths at 6-month follow-up. CUSUM failure analysis confirmed complication rates remained within acceptable thresholds throughout the study.ConclusionsRobotic-assisted BIMA CABG demonstrated acceptable outcomes, with operative efficiency improving after approximately 125 cases. These findings support its feasibility in experienced, high-volume centers and warrant further multicentre evaluation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Machine-learning differentiation of precordial T-wave inversion in pulmonary embolism and acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiating acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and acute pulmonary embolism (PE) in emergency settings is a notorious diagnostic challenge due to their overlapping symptoms and shared electrocardiographic abnormalities, such as precordial T-wave inversion (TWI). This study evaluated the ability of machine learning (ML) algorithms to distinguish acute PE from ACS by analyzing the morphology of inverted T waves in precordial leads.
METHODS: This retrospective, case-control study included 200 patients (100 ACS confirmed by coronary angiography; 100 PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography) admitted to Shahid Madani Hospital, Tabriz, Iran (2023-2024), who exhibited precordial TWI. Image processing with a region-growing technique traced negative T waves in leads V1, V2, and V3. Signals were filtered using Savitzky-Golay and Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT) methods to extract time-frequency statistical parameters. Multiple supervised ML models were trained (80% training, 20% test with 5-fold cross-validation) over 50 random iterations.
RESULTS: The Ensemble (AdaBoost) model achieved the highest diagnostic performance, yielding an accuracy of 84.44%, sensitivity of 83.96%, specificity of 84.87%, and F1-score of 83.56%. Neural Network models performed comparably, achieving 84.00% accuracy and 85.14% sensitivity. Other evaluated algorithms (SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes) also generated acceptable discriminative accuracy (ranging from 78% to 82%).
CONCLUSION: Machine-learning algorithms can extract potentially disease-specific features from precordial T-wave morphology to differentiate PE from ACS. These findings support further investigation of AI-enhanced ECG interpretation as a rapid, low-cost, non-invasive adjunct to clinical decision-making in acute care. External validation in larger, clinically representative populations is required before clinical application.

Title: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy is an electrocardiographic pattern characterized by a regular alternation of two distinct cardiac events. It can arise from normal operation of device algorithms or indicate underlying dysfunction, such as sensing abnormalities. Accurate differentiation is crucial to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate clinical intervention.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically elucidate the mechanisms underlying pacemaker-associated bigeminy and establish a practical diagnostic framework.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of six patients exhibiting pacemaker-associated bigeminy on ambulatory electrocardiograms (ECGs). The patients were identified from the databases of the Children's Hospital of Soochow University and the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between March 2020 and December 2025.
RESULTS: We delineate six distinct mechanisms: 1) Non-competitive atrial pacing (NCAP) triggered by sinus tachycardia; 2) Fusion beat exclusion due to evoked response (ER) undersensing; 3) Auto capture (AC) operation with start-stop pattern constrained by maximum tracking rate (MTR); 4) Window of atrial rate acceleration detection (WARAD) activation by non-conducted atrial premature complexes; 5) A Pace on Premature Ventricular Contraction (A Pace on PVC) triggered by PVCs; and 6) Dynamic atrioventricular (AV) delay operation following atrial premature beats.
CONCLUSIONS: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy represents a spectrum of phenomena driven by specific "algorithm-rhythm interactions." Recognition of these characteristic patterns is essential for correctly distinguishing normal device function from malfunction, thereby guiding appropriate clinical management and optimizing patient outcomes.

Title: Finerenone-Empagliflozin Combination Therapy in Apparent Resistant Hypertension: A CONFIDENCE Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apparent treatment-resistant hypertension (aTRH) is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with type 2 diabetes and predicts worse outcomes. Spironolactone, the established fourth-line agent, is limited by hyperkalemia in CKD.
OBJECTIVES: This analysis assessed whether finerenone plus empagliflozin lowers blood pressure (BP) meaningfully in aTRH, and whether aTRH modifies these agents' efficacy and safety.
METHODS: Post hoc analysis of CONFIDENCE (NCT05254002), a double-blind randomized trial of finerenone, empagliflozin, or both in CKD with albuminuria and type 2 diabetes. aTRH was BP ≥130/80 mm Hg on 3 antihypertensive drugs, or ≥4 drugs regardless of BP. Mixed models and logistic regression identified predictors of BP response.
RESULTS: Of the 796 participants, 307 (39%) had aTRH; they were older, more obese, and had more atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, higher albuminuria, and higher systolic BP (140.9 vs 131.5 mm Hg) but similar estimated glomerular filtration rate (53 vs 55 mL/min/1.73 m2). Combination therapy lowered systolic BP more than either monotherapy. Independent predictors of a ≥10 mm Hg systolic BP fall were aTRH (OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.08-2.25) and higher baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (OR: 1.15 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2; 95% CI: 1.05-1.26); diuretic use and albuminuria were not. The aTRH effect was treatment-independent (interaction P = 0.21). Adverse events were more frequent with aTRH (63.8% vs 51.1%), yet on combination therapy hyperkalemia was less frequent (11.2% vs 17.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: aTRH affected approximately 40% of participants and marked a higher-risk phenotype responsive to finerenone-empagliflozin, with BP reductions comparable to spironolactone but without the excess hyperkalemia that limits its use in CKD.

Title: Apixaban for thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiology patients: Real-world data from a single institution.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombosis is a major complication in children with congenital or acquired heart disease, contributing to significant morbidity and mortality. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), including apixaban, are increasingly used for thromboprophylaxis in this population yet real-world paediatric data remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of apixaban as thromboprophylaxis in paediatric cardiac patients receiving commercially available adult tablet formulations outside a clinical trial setting.
PATIENTS/METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≤18 years with congenital or acquired heart disease who received apixaban at the University Children's Hospital Zurich from October 2022 to June 2025. Dosing was approximated to the SAXOPHONE trial using commercially available tablets that were split or crushed, without therapeutic laboratory monitoring. Outcomes included incident thrombosis (primary), major bleeding, clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB), and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients were included with a median age of 4.6 years (IQR 3.3-9.8) and median apixaban exposure of 210 days (IQR 83-461), totalling 18,799 patient-days (51.5 patient-years). Single ventricle physiology was the most common underlying diagnosis (40/67, 60%) and Fontan circulation the most frequent indication (34/67, 51%). Two thrombotic events occurred (incidence rate 3.9 per 100 patient-years), both in the context of additional thrombotic risk factors. No major bleeding or CRNMB events were recorded.
CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban appeared safe and effective as thromboprophylaxis in this paediatric cardiology cohort, with no major or CRNMB and a low rate of thrombotic events. These findings add to the growing body of real-world evidence supporting DOAC use in children with cardiac disease.

Title: Biological markers of grief in bereaved family members: A systematic review of cortisol, inflammatory and cardiovascular studies.
Abstract: Bereavement is among life's most stressful events, and a minority of mourners develop prolonged and disabling grief. Biological markers have been proposed as signals of this risk, but no systematic review has examined them across bereaved family members or asked how well bereaved parents (parents who have lost a child) are represented. We systematically reviewed observational studies linking a cortisol/HPA-axis, inflammatory/immune, or cardiovascular/autonomic biomarker to a validated measure of coping or grief in bereaved family members of any age or relationship to the deceased (PROSPERO CRD420261446539). Five databases were searched, with citation searching of a related review. Eighteen studies met inclusion criteria across the three domains. More severe grief was linked to blunted or flatter diurnal cortisol in three of five cortisol studies. Bereavement and greater grief were linked to raised inflammatory markers (IL-6, IL-1RA, and related cytokines), although five of seven inflammatory studies appear to come from one research programme, and one study found divergent Type I interferon gene transcription in complicated relative to uncomplicated grief. Cardiovascular and autonomic findings were mixed and depended on moderators such as coping style and childhood adversity. Some cortisol associations weakened with time since loss, so they may not be stable markers of grief severity. Only one participant across all 18 studies was an identifiable bereaved parent. Biological markers show domain-specific associations with grief, but the evidence is exploratory, and bereaved parents are largely absent from it. They should be a priority for future prospective work.

Title: Associations between vascular aging and 12 lipid composite indices: A large cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Vascular aging is an important antecedent of cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet affordable, widely available biomarkers for its early detection remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive value of 12 lipid composite indices for vascular aging in a large cross-sectional sample of adults from Shenzhen, China.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis of 5518 adults screened in Shenzhen (2021-2023), vascular aging (baPWV ≥ 1400 cm/s) was evaluated against 12 indices (TyG, TyG-BMI, RC, TG/HDL-C, AC, AIP, LCI, CRI-II, NHR, MHR, LHR, PHR) derived from routine laboratory and hematological data. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression across four sequentially adjusted models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) and two-piece linear models were used to evaluate dose-response relationships and thresholds. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis compared the discriminative performance of each index alone and in combination with age. Subgroup and interaction analyses examined effect modification by BMI, gender, age, hypertension, and diabetes.
RESULTS: All 12 indices remained independently associated with vascular aging after multivariable adjustment. In the fully adjusted model (Model 4), each 1-unit increase in TyG was associated with an odds ratio (OR) of 2.21 (95% CI, 1.88-2.58; P < 0.001), and individuals in the highest TyG quartile (Q4) had an OR of 4.27 (95% CI, 3.16-5.77) compared with Q1; other indices showed similar effects. RCS analyses revealed significant nonlinear positive associations for several indices, with risk increasing below these thresholds. Individually, the indices had modest discrimination (AUC range, 0.562-0.726), but adding age improved all models; the TyG + age model achieved the best performance (AUC, 0.850; 95% CI, 0.838-0.862). BMI, gender, and diabetes status significantly modified several associations.
CONCLUSIONS: Among the 12 lipid composite indices evaluated, TyG-especially when combined with age-demonstrated the strongest predictive value for vascular aging in this large Chinese population, suggesting it may serve as a low-incremental-cost preliminary screening marker. However, prospective validation and intervention trials are needed to confirm the threshold and to determine whether lowering TyG attenuates vascular aging and subsequent CVD risk.

Title: Clinical Implementation of Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve for Revascularization Guidance: Initial Multicenter United States Experience.
Abstract: Real-world data on the adoption and clinical performance of angiography-derived physiology in the United States (U.S.) remain limited. We evaluated the implementation of FFRangio (CathWorks, Tel Aviv, Israel) and associated clinical outcomes across a multicenter U.S. healthcare system. We performed a multicenter observational cohort study across 4 centers involving consecutive adult patients undergoing invasive coronary angiography in whom FFRangio was performed in at least 1 coronary vessel based on clinical indication. The primary endpoint was target-vessel failure (TVF), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction and target vessel revascularization during follow-up, stratified by FFRangio values >0.80 versus ≤0.80. A total of 675 vessels in 469 patients were assessed by FFRangio; 240 (36%) had values ≤0.80 and 435 (64%) >0.80. Among lesions with FFRangio ≤0.80, 182 (76%) underwent PCI, 27 (11%) CABG, and 32 (13%) were managed medically. Among lesions with FFRangio >0.80, revascularization was deferred in 406 (92%), with 22 (5%) undergoing PCI and 12 (3%) CABG. The LAD was the most frequently treated vessel (51%). At a median follow-up of 10.2 months, the incidence rate of TVF was 1.55% per 100 lesion-years (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57-3.36) in the FFRangio >0.80 group versus 6.30 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI, 3.25-11.0) in the FFRangio ≤0.80 group (hazard ratio [HR] 4.61, 95% CI: 1.61-13.2; p=0.002). Among deferred lesions with FFRangio >0.80, TVF rate was 1.73 per 100 lesion-years (95% CI: 0.64-3.77). In conclusion, FFRangio supported safe deferral of revascularization and risk-stratification, with low event rates among lesions with values >0.80.

Title: Management of Antiplatelet Regimen During Surgical Procedures: a Report from the MARS Registry.
Abstract: Optimal perioperative management of patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial, with substantial variability in current clinical practice. The MARS registry is a prospective multicenter observational study evaluating perioperative outcomes in post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing surgery within 2 years of PCI. We assessed the incidence of Net Adverse Cardiovascular Events (NACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type ≥3 bleeding. A total of 132 consecutive patients undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery were followed from 14 days preoperatively to 30 days postoperatively. Of the 132 patients, 79 underwent non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and 53 underwent cardiac surgery (CS). The mean age was 66 years, and 68% were male. Diabetes mellitus was present in 48%, chronic kidney disease in 29%, and 42% had undergone PCI for an acute coronary syndrome. Mean time from PCI to surgery was 269 ± 217 days. Prior bleeding and stent thrombosis were reported in 11% and 5% of patients, respectively. Aspirin was continued in 60% and P2Y12 inhibitors in 36%, with mean discontinuation 4 and 6 days preoperatively, respectively. Intravenous antiplatelet bridging with cangrelor was used in 12 patients (9.1%) and unfractionated heparin as anticoagulant therapy in 15 patients (11.0%). NACE occurred more frequently after CS compared with NCS (18.9% vs. 10.1%, p=0.17). Major bleeding (BARC ≥3) occurred in 5.3% with no difference between CS and NCS. There were no cardiovascular deaths and no difference in all-cause mortality. Compared with no bridging, cangrelor bridging was associated with numerically higher NACE (25.0% vs. 12.5%, p=0.22), without differences in bleeding. On multivariable logistic regression, cangrelor bridging was not independently associated with NACE (adjusted OR 2.18, 95% CI 0.43-8.71, p=0.34). In conclusion, among post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery, aspirin was continued in 60%, cangrelor bridging was used in 9.1%, and although NACE rates were numerically higher after cardiac surgery and with bridging, these differences were not significant after multivariable adjustment, consistent with confounding by indication.

Title: Depressive Symptoms and Incident Peripheral Arterial Disease Among Adults With CKD: Findings From the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) Study.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Depression is associated with cardiovascular disease among adults with CKD, but its relationship with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) has not been thoroughly examined despite both conditions being common in this population. We evaluated the risk for incident PAD and death associated with elevated depressive symptoms among adults with CKD.
STUDY DESIGN: Observational prospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Adults with mild to moderate CKD in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort Study (CRIC) Study.
EXPOSURES: Elevated depressive symptoms as defined by a Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) score ≥ 11.
OUTCOMES: Incident PAD, defined as an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) < 0.9 or confirmed clinical PAD event (amputation or angioplasty). Composite outcome of incident PAD or death.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: The association between baseline elevated depressive symptoms and incident PAD, as well as a composite of incident PAD or death, was examined with Cox proportional hazard models. Mediation analysis explored the pathways between elevated depressive symptoms and these outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 2,757 individuals, 25% had elevated depressive symptoms (BDI ≥11) at baseline. During a median follow-up of 10 years, 24% of participants developed incident PAD. The rate of incident PAD was higher in those with elevated depressive symptoms (3.6 events per 100 person-years) compared with those without (2.2 events per 100 person-years). After accounting for other factors, baseline elevated depressive symptoms were associated with a higher risk of incident PAD (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.02-1.47). Smoking and physical inactivity mediated 20% and 10%, respectively, of this association. Similar associations were found between baseline elevated depressive symptoms and a composite of incident PAD or death. Findings were not different when elevated depressive symptoms were defined by BDI >14 and BDI ≥16.
LIMITATIONS: Residual bias and confounding. Absence of depression diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated depressive symptoms were associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD in adults with CKD, which is partly mediated by smoking and physical inactivity.
INDEX WORDS: Renal failure, depression, peripheral vascular disease, mortality, health behaviors.

Title: Outcomes Following Kidney Failure From IgA Nephropathy Compared to Diabetic Kidney Disease and Other Glomerular Diseases.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is a major cause of kidney disease worldwide, yet contemporary comparative outcome data following kidney failure are limited. We compared trends in access to kidney transplantation and mortality among patients with kidney failure due to IgAN, to those with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) or other glomerular diseases (GD).
STUDY DESIGN: Longitudinal cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients with kidney failure initiating maintenance dialysis (1965-2023) due to IgAN, DKD, or other GD in Australia.
EXPOSURE: Kidney failure etiology.
OUTCOMES: All-cause death, death from cardiovascular disease and cancer, and entry onto the deceased donor kidney transplant waitlist.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Age-standardized incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates and temporal trends assessed using log-linear regression-derived estimated annual percentage change (EAPC). Associations between kidney failure etiology and outcomes estimated using inverse probability treatment-weight (IPTW)- adjusted Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: 44,659 patients (4,925 with IgAN; 15,079 with other GD; 24,655 with DKD) were studied with a median follow-up of 53 months (IQR 23.3-109.8). The age-standardized incidence of IgAN remained stable over the past two decades (EAPC -0.01%, 95% CI - 0.80 to 0.78). Compared with other GD, patients with IgAN experienced lower all-cause (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.65-0.73; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.60-0.74; p < 0.001) mortality, and increased rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.39-1.73; p < 0.001). Compared with IgAN, patients with DKD had higher all-cause (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.53-1.64, p<0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.71-1.91, p<0.001), lower cancer-related mortality (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.95, p=0.009), and lower rates of being placed on the transplant waitlist (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.60-0.69, p<0.001).
LIMITATIONS: Residual confounding, diagnostic misclassification due to variation in biopsy practices.
CONCLUSION: Differences in survival and placement onto the kidney transplant waitlist exist across patients with different etiologies of kidney failure. Individuals with IgAN have longer survival and enter the transplant waitlist more often than those with DKD or other GD.

Title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation With Contact-Force-Sensing Large-Tip Focal Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter With 3D Mapping for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month Results.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omny-IRE (NCT05971693) evaluated safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact-force-sensing, pulsed field ablation, basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration.
OBJECTIVE: Report 12-month (M) study outcomes.
METHODS: Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE platform. Patients underwent follow-up through 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness endpoint was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 s) and acute procedural failure. Device/procedure-related serious adverse events (SAEs), quality-of-life assessed by Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) scores, and healthcare-utilization (cardiovascular-hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug [AAD] use) were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main-phase-cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device/procedure-related SAEs occurred in 2.9% of main-phase patients. Mean overall AFEQT score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% versus the 12M preprocedure period, and Class I/III AAD use decreased by 49.3% 6-12M postablation versus baseline.
CONCLUSIONS: Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and healthcare benefits of PFA with the OMNYPULSE platform.

Title: Interventricular septal LGE predicts response trajectories and clinical prognosis in heart failure patients undergoing left bundle branch area pacing.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an alternative strategy for heart failure (HF) patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). Interventricular septal (IVS) fibrosis is linked to LBBAP efficacy.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between IVS late gadolinium enhancement percentage (IVS LGE%) and LBBAP response in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) patients with LBBB.
METHODS: This was a two-center prospective observational study. Patients with NICM and complete LBBB were consecutively enrolled and received LBBAP from January 2021 to December 2024. Patients were divided into early, delayed, and non-response groups based on absolute left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement ≥5% at 6 and 12 months.
RESULTS: A total of 113 patients were included, with 86 (76.1%) early responders, 13 (11.5%) delayed responders, and 14 (12.4%) non-responders. IVS LGE% linearly increased the risk of non-early response, with each 1% increase conferring a 14% higher risk of adverse response progression (early to delayed or non-response) (adjusted OR=1.14, 95%CI 1.05-1.23; P=0.002). 75.3% of IVS fibrosis-related 6-month impairment was mediated by failed LBB captured (direct effect P=0.204), while the direct inhibitory effect of IVS fibrosis emerged at 12 months (mediation proportion 60.8%, β=-0.33, P=0.005). Optimal IVS LGE% cut-off values were 7.62% for early response and 12.33% for delayed response, with 12-month response rates of 95.06%, 93.75% and 43.75% across low, intermediate and high IVS LGE% groups, respectively.
CONCLUSION: IVS fibrosis independently predicts LBBAP response and prognosis in NICM patients with complete LBBB, and modulates LBBAP efficacy through a time-dependent biphasic mechanism.

Title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model.
RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Association of Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat Infiltration With Atrial Arrhythmia Recurrence After Pulsed-Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat infiltration (inFAT) is an emerging imaging phenotype of the atrial substrate in atrial fibrillation (AF).
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate inFAT and peri-left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) using artificial intelligence-based CT analysis software (ADAS 3D) and to assess their association with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after persistent AF ablation.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 59 patients who underwent pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF. inFAT and LA-EAT were quantified using a semi-automated algorithm. Cox regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association of inFAT and LA-EAT with recurrence. Kaplan-Meier analysis was performed after stratification according to the tertile of each parameter.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up period of 11.2 [6.4-11.9] months, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 21 (36%) patients. The inFAT volume was significantly greater in patients with recurrence than those without (1.25 [0.78-1.53] vs. 0.72 [0.45-1.09] cm3, p=0.021). In contrast, LA-EAT volume was comparable between the groups (21.8 [13.7-30.4] vs. 17.5 [14.1-26.8] cm3, p=0.419). In Cox regression analysis, higher inFAT was significantly associated with recurrence, whereas LA-EAT was not significantly associated (inFAT: hazard ratio [HR], 1.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-3.27; p=0.015; LA-EAT: HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.99-1.06; p=0.227). The significant association between inFAT and recurrence remained consistent after adjustment for body mass index.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater inFAT volume was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF, suggesting that inFAT may represent a candidate imaging marker of recurrence risk.

Title: Sex-based differences in bi-atrial voltage in atrial fibrillation: a multimodal and digital twin approach to distinguish physiological variation from pathological remodelling.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in atrial voltage have been reported in atrial fibrillation (AF), but it is unclear whether these differences reflect pathological remodelling or physiological variation.
OBJECTIVE: To assess sex-based differences in voltage, contextualised by complementary measures of substrate remodelling and AF mechanisms.
METHODS: A multicentre, prospective study was conducted in patients scheduled for AF ablation. Bi-atrial voltage mapping was combined with electrophysiological assessment, structural and functional assessment using cardiac MRI, and mechanistic interrogation using patient-specific digital twins. Propensity score matching was used to account for baseline differences between sexes. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis was conducted to estimate sex-specific mean left atrial voltage cutoffs based on 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status.
RESULTS: Seventy patients (62±12 years; 31% female) were included. Women demonstrated lower mean bipolar voltages than men, with this difference persisting after 1:1 propensity score matching (n=44) in both left (1.66±0.71mV versus 2.12±0.55mV, p=0.028) and right atria (1.79±0.49mV versus 2.20±0.59mV, p=0.025). Propensity score-matched analyses revealed no significant differences in other structural, functional, or electrophysiological parameters, with digital twin analyses demonstrating no significant differences in AF termination, phase singularity count, wave dynamics, or response to virtual ablation. Women had lower mean left atrial voltage cutoffs calibrated to 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status than men (1.74mV versus 2.26mV).
CONCLUSIONS: Women with AF exhibit lower bi-atrial voltages despite comparable substrate characteristics and AF mechanisms, suggesting that observed voltage differences may reflect physiological variation rather than pathological remodelling. Sex-specific voltage thresholds may improve the accuracy of substrate assessment and facilitate personalised treatment.

Title: Ten-year Performance of the Multi-Layer Insulated Defibrillation Lead in the Medicare Population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures may emerge years after implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead (Abbott, Sylmar, CA) in a large real-world Medicare population.
METHODS: Manufacturer device-tracking records were linked to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. Patients receiving an Optisure lead from February 2014 through December 2024 were included. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims containing both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario including confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario also including potentially related events.
RESULTS: The cohort included 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. Mean age was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy ICDs. Overall, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related and 606 as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario and 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%) in the worst-case scenario. Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type.
CONCLUSION: The Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice. These findings support both the long-term durability of Optisure and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

Title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and mortality and liver-related outcomes in patients with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2-i1) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes in type 2 diabetes mellitus, but their safety and clinical impact in advanced liver disease remain uncertain because patients with cirrhosis were underrepresented in major trials.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX research network, we identified adults with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity and compared outcomes according to SGLT2-i exposure. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 5,128 matched pairs were analyzed. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included all-cause hospitalization, ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, and variceal bleeding.
RESULTS: In the matched cohort, SGLT2-i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.78), hospitalization (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.80 to 0.89), ascites (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.77), spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.87), and variceal bleeding (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.99), with no difference in hepatic encephalopathy.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with alcoholic cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and obesity, SGLT2-i use was associated with improved survival and fewer liver-related complications.

Title: Infant Feeding Practices Are Associated with Cardiovascular Profiles in Early Childhood: Findings from a Prospective Australian Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding is associated with reduced risk of childhood obesity, but associations with cardiovascular risks in childhood are less well understood.
OBJECTIVES: This study investigated associations between infant feeding practices and cardiovascular profiles in early childhood and the potential mediating role of infant rapid weight gain (RWG).
DESIGN: This secondary data analysis was conducted using data from the Barwon Infant Study, an ongoing prospective pre-birth cohort in Australia commenced between 2010 and 2017, recruited through an unselected antenatal sampling frame.
PARTICIPANTS/SETTING: Children aged 4 years (n=606) who participated in the 4-year cardiovascular risk assessment follow-up.
MAIN OUTCOMES: Infant feeding variables, including breastfeeding duration, exclusive breastfeeding at 3 months, and predominant breastfeeding at 6 months, were collected via caregiver questionnaires at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months, and 2 years post-birth. Latent profile analysis, including 4-7 cardiovascular risk markers measured at age 4 years, was used to derive cardiovascular profiles.
STATISTICAL ANALYSES: Multivariable logistic regression with adjustment for gestational age, maternal education, and pre-pregnancy maternal body mass index (BMI), examined the association between infant feeding practices and cardiovascular profiles, and whether these associations were mediated by RWG in infancy.
RESULTS: Three cardiovascular profiles of 'Low' (44.1% of children), 'Medium' (46.4%), and 'High' (9.5%) were identified at age 4 years. Infants who were exclusively breastfed at age 3 months and predominantly breastfed at age 6 months were less likely to belong to the 'Medium' versus 'Low' cardiovascular profile (RRR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.95, p= 0.034; and RRR 0.43, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.99, p= 0.048, respectively) than those who were not. No significant association was observed for the 'High' versus 'Low' cardiovascular profile or between breastfeeding duration and cardiovascular profiles. Mediation analyses suggested indirect associations between infant feeding practices and cardiovascular profiles involving infant RWG.
CONCLUSIONS: Exclusive breastfeeding to age 3 months and predominant breastfeeding to age 6 months were linked with a more favorable cardiovascular profile at age 4 years. Mediation analyses suggested that infant RWG may partly account for these associations. Further studies are needed to investigate the mechanisms that may underlie the observed associations between breastfeeding practices and cardiovascular profiles.

Title: Arrhythmias detected by implanted cardiac rhythm recorders in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Arrhythmias are a common complication of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM). We sought to characterize the prevalence, risk factors, and prognosis of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM using implantable loop recorders (ILRs).
METHODS: ILRs were implanted in 49 patients with ATTR-CM (84% male; median age, 73.2 [66.2-78.8] years; 71% wild-type, 51% with known atrial fibrillation [AF]). Factors associated with the development of AF or pacemaker implantation were analyzed, and clinical outcomes were compared with those of a contemporary cohort of patients with 125 ATTR-CM without an ILR.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 37.2 [26.6-41.1] months, an advanced conduction disorder (ACD) prompting pacemaker implantation was detected in 16 individuals (33%) and new-onset AF was detected in 17 patients (71% of those without previous AF). Patients with new-onset AF more frequently had wild-type ATTR-CM. Those who needed pacemaker implantation were older and had a higher prevalence of hypertension and right bundle branch block, and a longer PR interval. Compared with patients without an ILR, early detection of arrhythmias by ILR was not associated with a prognostic benefit in terms of survival (P = .57), reduction of syncope (P = 1), heart failure admissions (P = .34), or embolic events (P = .999).
CONCLUSIONS: Although a higher incidence of arrhythmias was identified through ILR monitoring in patients with ATTR-CM, no significant benefits were observed in terms of survival or other hard clinical endpoints. Significant differences were identified in patients who developed new-onset AF and ACD. These differences should be considered during the clinical follow-up of this population.

Title: Impact of surgical timing in left-sided infective endocarditis with persistently positive blood cultures.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Guidelines define persistent infection in infective endocarditis (IE) as positive blood cultures after 7 days of adequate antibiotic therapy. However, persistently positive blood cultures (PPBC) at 48 to 72 hours are already associated with a worse prognosis. We aimed to assess the clinical profile, temporal trends, and impact of surgical timing on outcomes in patients with left-sided IE and PPBC at 48 to 72 hours.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from 3 Spanish tertiary centers (1998-2024). We compared patients with PPBC with those with blood culture clearance and assessed the effect of surgical timing using a time-dependent Cox model, inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, and a day-7 landmark analysis to minimize immortal time bias and confounding by indication.
RESULTS: Among 1265 patients with positive baseline cultures, 283 (22.4%) had PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. These patients exhibited a more severe clinical and microbiological profile and higher in-hospital mortality (36.0% vs 22.3%; P < .001). In the day-7 landmark analysis, surgery within the first 7 days was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (HR, 0.53; 95%CI, 0.30-0.95), with consistent trends across the time-dependent Cox and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting models.
CONCLUSIONS: PPBC at 48 to 72 hours identifies a high-risk subgroup of patients with left-sided IE. In these patients, early surgery within the first 7 days was associated with a potential survival benefit in adjusted models, supporting earlier reassessment of infection control to optimize surgical timing.

Title: Escalation of Resting Heart Rate and Tachycardia as a Response to Thoracic Radiotherapy: Implications for Cardiovascular Outcomes after Radiotherapy.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac toxicity is a well-recognized, but poorly understood complication of radiotherapy (RT). In non-oncological settings, there is an established relationship between resting heart rate and cardiovascular health.
OBJECTIVES: To study the incidence and pattern of resting heart rate (rHR) as an early sign of cardiotoxicity among patients with non-metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with RT.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed serial rHR measurements of consecutive patients with locally advanced NSCLC treated with definitive chemoradiation (CRT) over 6-7 weeks of daily radiation treatments followed by immunotherapy (durvalumab) between 2017-2022. Radiation dose to the heart and 17 cardiac substructures were extracted. Associations between heart rate elevation, tachycardia, cardiac substructure dose and outcomes were evaluated using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) and regression analysis.
RESULTS: We identified 110 patients, 56.4% with pre-existing heart disease. Median follow-up was 33.6 months. Median age was 70.4 years. Median rHR increased significantly during RT, rising from 81.5 bpm to 93 bpm at end of RT (p < 0.0001), remaining elevated in 30.6% of patients 12 months post-RT. Tachycardia incidence rose from 11.2% at baseline to 36.5% at 1-month post-RT (p < 0.0001). After adjusting for comorbidities, higher mean sinoatrial node (SAN) dose was associated with higher rHR elevation, delayed HR recovery and persistent tachycardia (all p < 0.05). Higher rHR during and after RT (β = 0.23, p = 0.005, and β = 13.49, p = 0.049, respectively), as well as the incidence of tachycardia episodes during RT were associated with increased odds of developing an arrhythmia (OR, 2.97, 95% CI, 1.17-7.52, p = 0.022).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated rHR and tachycardia are observed during and after RT for NSCLC and are associated with higher mean SAN dose. HR elevation was associated with increased risk of de novo arrhythmias, suggesting that heart rate may represent a non-invasive biomarker of subclinical cardiac injury. Prospective studies might be warranted to test the potential of routine HR monitoring and proactive dose reductions to the SAN to enable early detection and help mitigate the risk of post-treatment arrhythmia.

Title: Dose-Response Associations of Exercise Modalities With Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Exercise training improves cardiorespiratory fitness in patients with heart failure, yet the dose-response relationship across different exercise modalities remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities and their standardized doses on peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) in patients with heart failure.
METHODS: We systematically searched multiple databases from inception through March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with controls. Exercise modalities were categorized as interval aerobic training (IAT), continuous aerobic training (CAT), resistance training (RT), mind-body training (MBT), and their combinations. Exercise dose was uniformly quantified as weekly metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week). A Bayesian model-based network dose-response meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 100 trials involving 5,353 patients were included. The dose-response relationship followed an Emax curve, with ED50 values clustering around 80-90 MET-min/week. A weekly dose of 500 MET-min yielded considerable benefit, and 750-1000 MET-min approached maximal benefit for nearly all modalities. The top three ranked interventions were IAT (Emax = 3.50, 95% CrI: 2.49-4.60), RT (Emax = 3.66, 95% CrI: 1.96-5.85), and IAT+RT (Emax = 3.49, 95% CrI: 1.26-5.79).
CONCLUSIONS: The exercise dose-response relationship in heart failure follows an Emax curve, with distinct dose-benefit profiles across different exercise modalities. Based on the current evidence, the following preliminary considerations may be offered: for patients with limited exercise tolerance, MBT may be considered as one of the preferred options; for those with moderate exercise tolerance, IAT+RT or CAT+RT may be suitable choices; for patients with good exercise tolerance, IAT or RT may be considered; and for patients with comorbid obesity, CAT may be incorporated into a comprehensive management program.

Title: An update on post-marketing safety signals of sugammadex: A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).
Abstract: ObjectiveWith the expanding use of sugammadex, continued post-marketing surveillance remains warranted. This study aimed to characterize reporting patterns and update potential sugammadex-associated safety signals in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).MethodsWe conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study of FAERS reports from January 2012 through September 2025 in which sugammadex was the primary suspect drug. Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) preferred terms (PTs) were compared with all other drugs in the OpenVigil 2.1 FAERS reference set using the proportional reporting ratio (PRR), reporting odds ratio (ROR), and chi-square statistic. Signals were hypothesis-generating and did not establish incidence, comparative risk, or causality.ResultsA total of 1,077 unique cases were included. Among 887 cases with known sex, 443 (49.9%) were male and 444 (50.1%) were female; the median age among 710 age-known cases was 51 years (interquartile range, 29-66 years). Of 501 PTs evaluated, 92 met the prespecified statistical criteria. After separating 15 medication-error/product-use terms, 2 exposure terms, and 4 procedure/management descriptors, 71 clinical adverse-reaction PTs remained. In sensitivity analyses, 59 of 92 signals and 43 of 71 clinical PTs persisted at a ≥ 5; IC025 was >0 for 80 signals and conservative BH q-value upper bounds were <0.05 for 87 signals. Prominent clinical clusters involved hypersensitivity, cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuromuscular events. Kounis syndrome, complete atrioventricular block, and hypercapnia were absent from the approved adverse-reaction list, whereas post-procedural hemorrhage was interpreted in the context of labeled coagulation warnings.ConclusionsFAERS identified patterns of disproportionate reporting for sugammadex that warrant further evaluation, particularly for hypersensitivity and selected cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuromuscular events. These findings are signals rather than estimates of incidence, comparative risk, or causality. The three PTs absent from the approved adverse-reaction list require independent confirmation, and the post-procedural hemorrhage signal should be interpreted alongside labeled coagulation warnings.

Title: Respiratory Instability-driven Cardiac Dose Deviation in Postmastectomy Deep Inspiration Breath-hold Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (DIBH VMAT): Development and External Validation of a Respiratory-informed Predictive Framework.
Journal: Clinical oncology (Royal College of Radiologists (Great Britain))
Abstract:
AIMS: Deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) reduces cardiac exposure during left-sided breast radiotherapy; however, treatment-day cardiac dose may differ from the planned dose because of variations in respiratory reproducibility and anatomy. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a framework for predicting fraction-level cardiac dose variation using routinely acquired respiratory, anatomical, and dosimetric information.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 150 patients treated with postmastectomy DIBH VMAT (volumetric modulated arc therapy) was analyzed. Models were developed using a 30-patient development cohort with patient-wise-nested cross-validation, externally validated in 20 independent patients using cone-beam CT-derived synthetic CT dose recalculation, and applied to a 100-patient deployment cohort. Separate models predicted deviation from planned per-fraction mean heart dose (ΔMHD) and left anterior descending coronary artery dose (ΔLADCA D0.03 cc) using treatment-day real-time position management (RPM)--derived respiratory features, planning computed tomography (CT)-derived geometric variables, and plan-derived dosimetric parameters. SHAP-based analysis was performed to identify influential predictors.
RESULTS: The final Gradient Boosting model for ΔMHD achieved an internal validation mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.541 ± 0.035 centigray (cGy) and coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.642 ± 0.069. The Ridge Regression model for left anterior descending coronary artery (ΔLADCA) achieved an MAE of 23.413 ± 1.617 cGy and R2 of 0.413 ± 0.082. External validation demonstrated good agreement for ΔMHD (MAE 0.58 cGy, R2 = 0.641), whereas ΔLADCA showed lower performance (MAE 24.14 cGy, R2 = 0.435). Stability index and baseline drift were key predictors.
CONCLUSION: Treatment-day-respiratory characteristics combined with anatomical and dosimetric variables can estimate fraction-level cardiac dose variation during DIBH radiotherapy. The framework may support verification-based clinical review, with further validation required before implementation.

Title: Decoding Atrial Fibrillation Heterogeneity: A Nationwide Phenome-Wide Association Study in England.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Age and sex influence atrial fibrillation (AF) prevalence and outcomes, yet comprehensive data on sex- and age-specific health care utilization in patients newly diagnosed with AF remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to address this gap using a phenome-wide association study (Phe-WAS) approach.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using nationwide Clinical Practice Research Datalink data linked to Hospital Episodes Statistics. Adults diagnosed with AF between 1998 and 2016 (n = 199,433) were matched 1:1 by age and sex to non-AF control subjects. Primary and secondary care interactions 5 years post diagnosis were analyzed using Phe-WAS with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios for conditions in AF vs control groups, stratified by sex and age. Associations were assessed for novelty through literature review and causality using published Mendelian randomization studies.
RESULTS: Patients with AF had higher rates of cardiovascular and noncardiovascular conditions than control subjects, with marked sex- and age-specific patterns. Women had more bleeding complications, pneumonia, Clostridium difficile enterocolitis, cholangitis, and electrolyte disturbances, whereas men had higher rates of alcohol-related disorders, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, and cardiomyopathy. Younger patients with AF (<50 years) more often had alcohol-related mental and behavioral disorders, gout, and dilated cardiomyopathy, while older patients (>60 years) more often had heart failure, ischemic stroke, renal failure, and respiratory infections. Of 51 phenotypes more common in AF, 28 were previously reported, and 23 were potentially novel. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested AF was causal for 19 associations.
CONCLUSIONS: This Phe-WAS demonstrates the broad spectrum of health care interactions in AF beyond traditional cardiovascular complications.

Title: AGraphHF: Adversarial graph-based multimodal learning for heart failure risk prediction.
Abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization worldwide, yet early risk stratification remains challenging because prognostic information is distributed across heterogeneous clinical narratives and subtle electrophysiological abnormalities. We propose AGraphHF, a multimodal framework for incident HF risk prediction that integrates 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) with demographic-aware clinical text under a survival objective. The prediction task is temporally anchored at an index ECG and estimates the relative risk of subsequent HF onset under a longitudinal time-to-event formulation. The ECG encoder models individual leads as graph nodes and learns both inter-lead relationships and temporal dependencies using dual graph attention mechanisms. To enhance sensitivity to weak but prognostically relevant signal deviations, the model employs a two-phase adversarial training strategy with dual decoders, where stable reconstruction of typical ECG morphology is followed by deviation-focused refinement conditioned on reconstruction residuals. In parallel, clinical notes are encoded using a demographic-aware language model that extends BioClinicalBERT through age- and sex-conditioned contrastive pre-training. ECG and text representations are aligned in a shared latent space and fused hierarchically to produce patient-level risk estimates. We evaluate AGraphHF on high-risk cohorts derived from the MIMIC-IV database, including patients with hypertension and myocardial infarction. Experimental results demonstrate improved survival risk discrimination compared with established baselines on the hypertension and myocardial infarction cohorts, while also revealing cohort-dependent differences in the contribution of ECG and clinical text. These findings support the use of coordinated graph-based ECG modelling and demographic-aware multimodal integration for HF risk stratification, while emphasizing the need for cohort-specific interpretation of model performance.

Title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant.
CONCLUSION: This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

Title: Recurrence analysis of cardiac arrhythmias: A systematic review of methods, substrate characterisation and clinical translation.
Abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias are a major cause of morbidity and mortality, and catheter ablation depends on accurate identification of the underlying substrate. Cardiac signals are nonlinear and non-stationary, which limits Fourier-based analysis. Recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) and related recurrence methods make fewer assumptions, but their use in arrhythmia research has not been systematically synthesised. This review examines what recurrence analysis has demonstrated, how consistently its methods have been applied, and what remains before it can support clinical substrate characterisation. Of 309 records retrieved from four databases (207 after deduplication), 48 studies met the eligibility criteria and citation searching added one, giving 49. Each study was examined in full text for its signals, cohorts, embedding parameters, threshold selection, metrics and results, and assigned to one of six methodological categories. The three studies that tested recurrence against surrogate or shuffled data each found structure in fibrillatory signals that matched stochastic surrogates did not reproduce. Recurrence metrics and dominant frequency were weakly correlated and diverged in substrate characterisation, so they are not interchangeable. Threshold selection was the most consequential uncontrolled variable: five strategies were in use, ten of the 35 studies that apply a threshold reported no selection rule, and only three examined how their results depended on it. Determinism and laminarity, although the most frequently reported metrics, were not consistently the strongest discriminators. Clinical readiness is not established: only one study used recurrence mapping prospectively to guide ablation, in ten patients without randomisation. A shared threshold-selection standard and prospective multicentre validation are needed.

Title: Outcomes and Challenges of Redo Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Propensity-Matched Comparative Analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aims to compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of reoperative coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with primary CABG in a propensity score-matched patient cohort.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 2,021 patients who underwent CABG between January 2003 and January 2024. Among them, 35 (1.7%) patients underwent redo CABG. Using 1:1 propensity score matching based on age, ejection fraction, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension, 36 patients who underwent primary CABG were selected for comparison. Patients with incomplete records or combined cardiac procedures were excluded. Perioperative variables, in-hospital mortality, and long-term survival were analyzed.
RESULTS: The redo CABG group had significantly longer intensive care unit stays (2.15 ± 2.37 vs. 1.39 ± 1.36 days, P = 0.006), hospital stays (12.11 ± 17.40 vs. 7.36 ± 2.21 days, P = 0.009), and postoperative bleeding (899.12 ± 445.17 vs. 576.39 ± 323.92 ml, P = 0.001). Hospital mortality occurred in two patients (5.7%) in the redo group and one patient (2.8%) in the primary group (P = 0.614). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showed higher long-term survival in the redo CABG group (77.1%) compared to the primary CABG group (58.3%), though not statistically significant (P = 0.168).
CONCLUSION: Despite the increased perioperative complexity, redo CABG is associated with low in-hospital mortality and promising long-term outcomes when appropriate patient selection and meticulous surgical technique are employed. These findings are especially relevant in guiding revascularization strategies for patients with prior CABG, where redo surgery is often underutilized despite its clinical viability.

Title: Wireless Home Blood Pressure Monitoring With Health Coaching for Hypertension Management at a Federally Qualified Health Center: Pilot Randomized Controlled Feasibility and Acceptability Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Only approximately half of adults with hypertension, a leading cardiovascular risk factor, achieve blood pressure (BP) control, with persistent disparities among low-income and minority populations. Wireless home BP monitoring (HBPM) with remote patient monitoring can improve BP control, but evidence is limited in medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic populations served by federally qualified health centers (FQHCs).
OBJECTIVE: The primary objective was to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of wireless HBPM among predominantly Hispanic adults with hypertension receiving FQHC care. Comparing BP outcomes between wireless and conventional HBPM was a secondary exploratory objective.
METHODS: We conducted a 6-month, 2-arm randomized controlled pilot feasibility and acceptability trial nested within the San Diego: Heart Attack and Stroke Free Zone program. Adults aged ≥18 years with uncontrolled or newly diagnosed hypertension (BP ≥140/90 mm Hg) were enrolled across 3 FQHC networks and randomized 1:1 by unrestricted simple randomization to wireless HBPM (Bluetooth cuff and cellular hub; weekly transmitted summaries reviewed by health coaches) or standard HBPM (home monitor with paper log). Both arms received standardized health coaching. The primary outcomes were feasibility (proportion of 210 expected BP readings transmitted) and acceptability (postintervention satisfaction survey in the wireless arm). Exploratory analyses compared BP outcomes between arms among participants with >2 BP measurements.
RESULTS: Of 316 recruited participants, 290 (92%) were eligible, and 200 (63%) were analyzed (wireless: n=73, 23%; and standard: n=127, 40%); arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The mean age was 61 years (SD 9.1), 57% (115/200) were women, and 51% (n=102) self-identified as Hispanic, with no significant baseline differences between arms. Among analyzed wireless-arm participants, 86% (63/73) transmitted multiple readings (mean 160.6, SD 129.1) over 6 months, corresponding to 76.2% (160/210) of expected readings among transmitting participants and 66% across all 73; only 5% (7/127) of standard-arm participants returned paper logs. Of 60 respondents (82.2% response rate), 95% (n=57) agreed or strongly agreed that the device was easy to set up and use. Both arms showed significant within-arm BP reductions at 6 months (P<.001). At 6 months, 63% (46/73) of the wireless arm and 74% (94/127) of the standard arm achieved systolic BP <140 mm Hg (P=.08; adjusted odds ratio, standard vs wireless, 1.6, 95% CI 0.78-3.4; P=.19).
