These exploratory comparisons were not powered and do not constitute evidence of equivalence.
CONCLUSIONS: Among analyzed participants, wireless HBPM was feasible, and survey respondents reported high acceptability in a medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic FQHC population. Feasibility among all randomized participants could not be estimated because arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The absence of a between-arm difference in BP control is not evidence of equivalence because this pilot was not powered to compare clinical effectiveness; the BP findings are hypothesis generating.

Title: Temporal Patterns of Multimorbidity Progression Among Inpatients With a Recorded Hypertension Diagnosis Across Three Counties in Rural Henan, China: Retrospective Cohort Study Using Temporal Network Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a key driver of multimorbidity; however, its role in shaping dynamic disease progression, especially in rural populations, remains underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize temporal patterns of multimorbidity progression among inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis and to examine whether these patterns differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county.
METHODS: We analyzed electronic health record data from 34,099 inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis across 3 rural counties in Henan, China (2019-2023), constructing a temporal comorbidity network of 250 disease nodes and 1512 disease transitions. Statistical validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, case-dropping, and permutation tests. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, insurance type, and county.
RESULTS: The temporal comorbidity network revealed a densely interconnected core involving hypertension, atherosclerotic heart disease, and cerebral infarction, with type 2 diabetes occupying a bridging position between cardiovascular and multisystem disease clusters. The ordering of dominant recorded pathways differed by sex (earlier coronary involvement among female inpatients vs more direct progression to stroke among male inpatients), was more complex in inpatients older than 70 years of age, and was more diffuse among those covered by urban-rural resident insurance compared with urban employee insurance.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimorbidity among inpatients with recorded hypertension followed structured and heterogeneous temporal patterns that differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county. Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular conditions formed the principal recorded progression pathways, while type 2 diabetes connected cardiovascular pathways with broader multisystem complications. These findings support further evaluation of risk-stratified and locally adapted approaches to chronic disease prevention and longitudinal care.

Title: Risk of myocardial infarction in adults with gout treated with allopurinol: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: AimsAlthough allopurinol is used for urate-lowering therapy, its effect on myocardial infarction risk remains unclear. This study assessed the association between allopurinol use and myocardial infarction in adults with gout.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PROSPERO registration (CRD420261305257). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 2026. Observational studies of adults with confirmed gout that reported adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for myocardial infarction and separately identifiable allopurinol exposure were included. Pooled estimates were calculated using an inverse-variance random-effects model with the Paule-Mandel estimator. Robustness was assessed through leave-one-out, active-comparator, and Hartung-Knapp sensitivity analyses.ResultsFour retrospective cohort studies met the revised eligibility criteria. In the primary random-effects analysis, allopurinol use was associated with a lower risk of myocardial infarction (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.76-0.94; I2 = 0%). However, the association was not statistically significant after excluding the study contributing the greatest weight (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), when restricted to active comparators (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), or using the Hartung-Knapp adjustment (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.71-1.00).ConclusionAllopurinol therapy was associated with a modest but significant reduction in myocardial infarction risk in adults with gout.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Search for the glycated hemoglobin target minimizing mortality among people with type 2 diabetes with rare incidence of treatment-related severe hypoglycemia - Epidemiologic analysis of J-DOIT3 randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In recent years, with the considerable changes in the therapeutic armamentarium for diabetes, the incidence of hypoglycemia events, especially severe hypoglycemia events, associated with drug treatment in people with diabetes has markedly decreased. We were prompted to evaluate the threshold for each intervention target, especially glycemic control, associated with a minimized risk of the macrovascular complications of diabetes in this setting.
METHODS: In the Japan Diabetes Optimal Integrated Treatment study for 3 major risk factors of cardiovascular diseases (J-DOIT3) conducted by us previously, we recruited 2542 participants and assigned them to a conventional therapy group (n = 1271) and an intensive therapy group (n = 1271; two ineligible participants were removed from all analyses afterwards), and the incidence of severe hypoglycemia events was low in both groups (7 in the intensive therapy group and 4 in the conventional therapy group during a median 8.5 years' follow-up). Towards the objective of this study, we undertook a landmark analysis with a landmark time-point of 1 year after the baseline of the J-DOIT3 study. Then, using the updated mean values of the glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), systolic blood pressure, and LDL-cholesterol and HDL-cholesterol levels, we determined the optimal levels of each of these variables associated with the lowest hazard ratios for outcomes, including the primary and cardiovascular outcomes.
RESULTS: For glycemic control, our results revealed no clear lower threshold of the glycated hemoglobin associated with the lowest risk of myocardial infarction or all-cause mortality; for other risk factors, it might be an important treatment target to maintain the LDL-cholesterol levels at below 80 mg/dL to minimize the risk of stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: The present analysis suggested that the treatment target for HbA1c to minimize the risk of all-cause mortality in participants with diabetes with a low incidence of severe hypoglycemia episodes could be < 6.5% (ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00300976).

Title: Q-AortaECG: A Quantum-Inspired Multi-Agent 12-Lead ECG System for Early Triage of Acute Aortic Syndrome.
Journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
Abstract: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a time-critical vascular emergency in which delayed recognition may occur because the presenting symptoms and electrocardiographic phenotypes often overlap with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, and other emergency diagnoses. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) remains the confirmatory standard, but the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is usually obtained earlier, is universally available at triage, and may carry distributed signatures of malperfusion, ischemia mimicry, autonomic stress, conduction delay, and hemodynamic compromise. We developed Q-AortaECG, a classically implemented quantum-inspired multi-agent ECG system that integrates multiscale waveform representations, specialist ECG agents, density-state uncertainty fusion, a variational-circuit style consensus layer, and a safety-gated multidisciplinary team-style report for early AAS triage. The system was evaluated in three suspected-AAS/CTA-evaluable cohorts comprising 1,251 patients, including 467 with CTA-, surgery-, or autopsy-confirmed AAS. Across 700 locked-test patients, Q-AortaECG achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.881 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.852-0.908), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.743 (95% CI, 0.695-0.790), sensitivity of 0.955 (231/242; 95% CI, 0.920-0.977), specificity of 0.721 (330/458; 95% CI, 0.677-0.761), positive predictive value (PPV) of 0.643, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.968 at the prespecified high-sensitivity threshold. Performance remained consistent in external retrospective validation and prospective silent-run evaluation, although AUPRC decreased in the lower-prevalence prospective cohort. Ablation experiments supported the contributions of self-supervised ECG pretraining, agent specialization, density-matrix uncertainty fusion, and differential diagnosis modeling. In a counterbalanced paired reader study, Q-AortaECG assistance improved overall clinician sensitivity from 0.696 to 0.870 while preserving specificity (0.851 ver sus 0.846). In prospective silent-run analysis, counterfactual alerts would have advanced the median time to the correct diagnostic pathway from 187 to 61 minutes among initially unsuspected AAS presentations. These findings support ECG first, calibrated, safety-gated decision support as an early warning scaffold for AAS triage, while preserving CTA and expert imaging interpretation as the diagnostic standard.

Title: Dietary Behaviors and Urinary Biomarkers in a Self-Management Support Program Among Low-Income Adults with CKD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: CKD disproportionately affects socioeconomically disadvantaged populations, among whom adoption of kidney-friendly diets is often constrained by structural barriers. Self-management support (SMS) programs can improve CKD awareness and cardiovascular risk factors; however, their ability to influence dietary behaviors and diet-related physiologic markers when nutrition content is limited remains uncertain. We evaluated whether participation in a culturally tailored SMS program with modest dietary education was associated with changes in self-reported dietary behaviors and urinary biomarkers among low-income adults with CKD.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary exploratory analysis of a randomized controlled trial (NCT01530958) among low-income adults with early-to-moderate CKD. Participants were randomized to an SMS program that included limited dietary education focused on reducing sodium, refined sugar, and fast-food consumption. Outcomes included self-reported intake of soda, fruit-flavored drinks, and fast food, as well as urinary biomarkers reflecting sodium-potassium balance and inflammation, including sodium-to-potassium ratio (Na/K), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1). Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and body mass index were used to assess associations at intervention completion and 6-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Among 266 participants (mean age 57.5 years; 51% men; 34% African American, 36% Hispanic, 19% Asian/Pacific Islander, and 9% non-Hispanic White), 97% reported annual household income below $50,000. The intervention was not associated with significant changes in self-reported dietary behaviors, urinary Na/K ratio (β [95% CI]: 0.24 [ -0.61, 1.09]), urinary IL-6 (-1.86 [-4.96, 1.25]), or urinary TGF-β1 (5.41 [-1.08, 11.54]). A modest reduction in urinary TNF-α was observed (-0.24 [-0.43, -0.02]).
CONCLUSIONS: In this low-income CKD population, an SMS program with limited dietary content was not sufficient to produce measurable changes in dietary behaviors or most diet-related urinary biomarkers. These findings underscore the need for more intensive, nutrition-focused, and structurally supported interventions to achieve meaningful dietary and physiologic change in CKD.

Title: High cardiometabolic burden among people with HIV and obesity in Peru.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiometabolic disease has been studied in people with HIV, but evidence focused on people with HIV and obesity remains limited. This study assessed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, metabolic abnormalities, markers of inflammation, and cardiovascular risk scores among people with HIV and obesity.
METHODS: We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study in clinically stable people with HIV aged ≥35 years and BMI >30 kg/m² in Lima-Callao, Peru, in 2024.
RESULTS: Participants enroled were 126; 77.7% were male, mean age was 50.6 years, mean time on antiretroviral therapy (ART) was 12.4 years, mean CD4 count was 759.8 cells/µL, and 97.6% had HIV-RNA <200 copies/µL. Mean BMI was 34.0. Clinical cardiovascular disease history was uncommon (2.4%); however, carotid Doppler ultrasound showed atherosclerotic changes in 34.4% (increased CIMT or carotid plaque), which associated with older age and longer time of ART. Abnormal glucose metabolism was identified in 89.7%, dyslipidemia in 82.5%, metabolic syndrome in 50.8%, elevated inflammatory markers in 28.2%, and low apolipoprotein A1 in 22.6%. Only 8.1% had normal findings across all evaluations. High cardiovascular risk was observed in 19.4% by Framingham, 9.4% by ACC/AHA, and 75.4% by HIV-CARDIO-PREDICT score.
CONCLUSIONS: This population of middle-aged, clinically stable people with HIV and obesity presented substantial burden of subclinical atherosclerosis and metabolic abnormalities despite low reported cardiovascular disease history. Cardiovascular risk estimates varied substantially across scores, with an HIV-specific score identifying a much higher proportion of patients as high risk than general-population scores. Targeted evaluation and timely preventive management may help reduce cardiometabolic complications.

Title: Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a well-established tool for predicting cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic value in young adults remains unclear. As early preventive intervention may yield substantial lifetime benefit, understanding long-term implications of elevated CAC in young adults is important for informing prevention strategies.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans. Using multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis, the association of CAC with all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality was assessed, adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived for these outcomes in 5-year increments up to 30 years using a mixed approach involving the Kaplan-Meier method and Weibull modeling. The proportion of deaths attributable to CVD and CHD across CAC groups was evaluated. Four institutions across the US provided patient-level data to assemble the CAC Consortium. Included in the analysis were adults aged 30 to 45 years from the CAC Consortium. They were followed up for a median of 22.6 years. Study data were analyzed from October 2025 to September 2026.
EXPOSURE: Elevated CAC in adults aged 30 to 45 years, specifically CAC score greater than 90%.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Participants were followed up for underlying cause of mortality.
RESULTS: Among 12 847 participants, the mean (SD) age was 40.5 (3.6) years, and 9922 (77.2%) were male; 9262 (72.1%) had CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a CAC score between 75% to 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a CAC score greater than 90%. In total, there were 624 deaths (149 CVD and 81 CHD). Multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for CAC score greater than 90% vs CAC score of 0 were 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27), 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82), and 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16), for all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, respectively. Over 30 years, the group with a CAC score greater than 90% had significantly higher modeled risk of all-cause (12.9% vs 7.5%), CVD (4.5% vs 1.5%), and CHD (3.0% vs 0.6%) mortality, compared with the group with a CAC score of 0.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study suggest that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, suggesting potential implications for guiding the intensification of preventive intervention in this high-risk phenotype.

Title: Race- and Neighborhood-Level Social Determinants of Health in Diagnosis and Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Early diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF) is critical for preventing stroke, heart failure, and mortality. Understanding patterns in diagnosis and treatment of AF may improve detection and reduce disparities.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the interactions between race and ethnicity and neighborhood social determinants of health on AF diagnosis and treatment.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Retrospective cohort study using administrative claims for greater Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, area residents aged 18 years or older from Independence Blue Cross from 2017 to 2021. Baseline characteristics were assessed in 2017, and participants were followed up from 2018 through 2021. Data were analyzed from October 2023 to July 2026.
EXPOSURES: Exposures included Non-Hispanic Black race and ethnicity, neighborhood-level social determinants of health as measured by the social barrier index (SBI), and the interaction between the two.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was AF diagnosis ascertained from International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision diagnosis codes. The secondary outcome was anticoagulant prescription among individuals with AF diagnoses as ascertained from pharmacy claims.
RESULTS: Of the 504 876 patients included, the mean (SD) age was 48 (18) years; 267 596 (53.0%) were female; 67 362 (13.3%) non-Hispanic Black, and 437 514 (86.7%) were non-Hispanic White. A total of 27 249 patients (5.1%) were diagnosed with AF during the study period. Non-Hispanic Black patients were less likely to be diagnosed with AF compared with non-Hispanic White patients (odds ratio [OR], 0.91; 95% CI, 0.82-1.00). The relative difference increased with increased SBI (which denotes more vulnerable neighborhoods) as shown by a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95). Among those diagnosed with AF, 15 722 (58%) had an anticoagulant prescription. There was a significant interaction between race and ethnicity and SBI (OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.00-1.20), suggesting that filled prescription patterns differed by race and ethnicity with SBI. For Black individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with decreased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.90-0.99). For White individuals one unit increase in SBI was associated with increased odds of AF diagnosis (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.03-1.07).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This cohort study of Medicare Advantage and commercially insured individuals found that AF diagnosis rates declined with worsening neighborhood-level disadvantage among non-Hispanic Black individuals but increased among non-Hispanic White individuals. Conditional on diagnoses, rates of prescription of anticoagulants were similar across race and ethnicity groups. Targeted interventions, especially in more marginalized neighborhoods, are needed to increase detection of AF.

Title: The cardiovascular risk of metabolically healthy obesity: an inflammatory perspective.
Journal: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) is a heterogeneous phenotype characterized by preserved traditional metabolic markers despite excess adiposity. However, accumulating evidence suggests that MHO may not be uniformly benign and may confer increased long-term cardiovascular risk through inflammatory and adipose tissue-mediated mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on cardiovascular risk in MHO, focusing on visceral adiposity, ectopic fat, and immune metabolic pathways. Literature published between January 2010 and December 2025 was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. Across the reviewed evidence, MHO is frequently associated with the progression to metabolically unhealthy obesity, although transition rates and cardiovascular risk estimates vary according to MHO definitions. Visceral and ectopic fat are associated with subclinical atherosclerosis, coronary calcification, and cardiovascular events, including in individuals without overt metabolic abnormalities. Evidence regarding heart failure and ventricular dysfunction remains limited and inconsistent. Low-grade inflammation and adipose immune remodeling, including NLRP3 inflammasome activation, provide plausible mechanisms, although human evidence remains predominantly observational. Key gaps include inconsistent MHO definitions, limited longitudinal imaging and biomarker integration, population diversity, and lack of validated MHO-specific risk models. Standardized phenotyping and prospective validation of inflammation-based risk stratification are required.

Title: Institutional volume and postoperative efficiency as determinants of in-hospital mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting: a multilevel analysis in São Paulo, Brazil.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between hospital procedural volume, postoperative efficiency, and in-hospital mortality and costs among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting in the public health system of the State of São Paulo, Brazil.
METHODS: This retrospective ecological study analyzed isolated coronary artery bypass grafting procedures recorded in the Brazilian Hospital Information System in São Paulo between 2008 and 2024. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, postoperative length of stay, and inflation-adjusted hospitalization costs. We assessed mortality using Poisson regression models, while we analyzed costs and length of stay using linear mixed-effects models with hospital-level random intercepts. We performed sensitivity analyses using alternative inclusion criteria.
RESULTS: We included 82,398 procedures from 45 hospitals. Median annual hospital volume was 71 procedures. Overall in-hospital mortality was 6.75%, and mean length of stay was 12.2 days. High-performing centers showed substantially lower mortality (4.82% versus 9.94%), shorter length of stay (12.3 versus 16.5 days), and lower adjusted costs (R$24,246 versus R$28,633) compared with low-performing institutions. At the institutional level, longer mean postoperative stay was positively associated with higher hospital-level mortality rates (incidence rate ratios: 1.015 per day; 95%CI 1.006 - 1.024), though reverse causation cannot be excluded given the ecological study design. Higher annual procedural volume was independently associated with lower costs, whereas prolonged hospitalization significantly increased expenditures. Between 2008 and 2024, total surgical volume declined, while mortality decreased, suggesting progressive improvements in care quality.
CONCLUSION: Higher institutional volume and greater postoperative efficiency are associated with lower mortality and reduced costs after coronary artery bypass grafting in the public health system of the State of São Paulo, Brazil. Postoperative length of stay emerged as a key marker of institutional performance and clinical course.

Title: Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation after stroke and the risk of incident dementia: an observational study from a global federated network.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dementia is a common and disabling complication after stroke. Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (EXCR) may influence vascular and inflammatory mechanisms relevant to cognitive decline. We investigated the association between EXCR initiation after stroke and incident dementia.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Using TriNetX, we identified adults with ischaemic stroke or TIA. Patients with recorded ICD-10-CM codes indicating an NIHSS score ≥ 16 were excluded from the primary analysis. Patients initiating EXCR within 6 months were compared with those without documented post-index EXCR. Propensity score matching balanced demographics, comorbidities, medication use and available stroke-severity measures. Outcomes were assessed at 3 and 5 years.
RESULTS: The unmatched cohorts included 4226 patients initiating EXCR (mean age, 64.7 years; 60.8% male) and 1,889,796 without EXCR (mean age, 66.3 years; 48.2% male). After matching, 4138 patients remained in each cohort. At 5 years, EXCR was associated with lower hazards of incident dementia (HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82), all-cause mortality (HR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.45-0.55) and recurrent stroke (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.61-0.91), but a higher hazard of rehospitalisation (HR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.06-1.38); no significant association was observed for acute myocardial infarction. The association with incident dementia remained consistent across sensitivity analyses.
DISCUSSION: The observed association with lower dementia risk suggests that the potential benefits of post-stroke EXCR may extend beyond cardiovascular and functional outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: EXCR initiation after ischaemic stroke or TIA was associated with a lower hazard of incident dementia. This association remained consistent across the 3-year, 30-day landmark, 1-year lagged and all-stroke-severity sensitivity analyses.

Title: Rapid Transport to Extracorporeal CPR: Urging Caution Prior to Implementation.
Abstract: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) has survival that remains near 10% despite years of research and advancements in care. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has been explored as an option for patients who suffer OHCA and are refractory to traditional therapies. In nearly every system that implements ECPR for OHCA, there is a requirement to incorporate intra-arrest transport (IAT). There are three major randomized controlled trials which have evaluated the role of ECPR in OHCA. These include ARREST, INCEPTION, and Prague OHCA. While ARREST has the strongest data to support ECPR, it includes only 30 patients. The larger trials such as INCEPTION and Prague OHCA did not show statistically significant results in favor of ECPR. Each trial has a unique study design and statistical analysis.The current evidence is not strong enough to support widespread adoption of ECPR into the prehospital systems of care. Examining the statistical pitfalls, potential biases, and methodological confounders of the existing ECPR literature against the background of previously reported data surrounding IAT─the full impact of effect of ECPR cannot exclude consideration of the impact of the effect of IAT. As more data is needed to better understand the full impact of implementing ECPR into a system of care, we encourage caution and thoughtful analysis to leaders who may be considering the addition of ECPR into an existing system of care. ECPR shows early promise for select patients. The development of an ECPR system is complex and has numerous facets, typically including the incorporation of early IAT for OHCA. At this time, more studies are needed on the full impacts of implementing ECPR into a system of care for OHCA.

Title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Predicting Early Onset Hypertension in the US.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early onset hypertension is often overlooked despite its association with lifelong cardiovascular disease risk. We developed an interpretable machine learning model to predict early onset hypertension in US adults using the 2022 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, incorporating demographic, socioeconomic, health care utilization, and comorbidity features.
METHODS: We analyzed data on adults aged 55 years or younger. Hypertension was defined by International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification code number I10 or self-reported physician diagnosis at or before age 55 years. Eighty-four variables were screened; Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator reduced the set to 45 variables. Extreme gradient boosting was trained with stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F2 score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC), and area under the precision-recall curve (PR AUC). We assessed fairness across subgroups and used Shapley Additive Explanations to quantify feature influence.
RESULTS: Among 9,850 adults, 1,647 (weighted prevalence, 15.2%) had hypertension. Discrimination was strong, with a ROC AUC of 0.807 (95% CI, 0.787-0.827), PR AUC of 0.486 (95% CI, 0.439-0.530), recall of 0.848 (95% CI, 0.816-0.878), and F2 score of 0.606 (95% CI, 0.578-0.634). Key predictors included older age, high body mass index, and a diagnosis of high cholesterol. Fairness analyses showed slightly higher true positive rates for Hispanic (+0.11) and Asian (+0.08) people, with performance for African American people modestly lower than that for White people.
CONCLUSION: Both medical and nonmedical predictors contributed meaningfully, with high cholesterol particularly influential among adults older than 40 years and race and ethnicity especially important among African American adults. Prospective validation and routine fairness audits are warranted to ensure equitable benefit across populations. This interpretable model supports recall-oriented screening to identify younger adults at risk of hypertension for further evaluation and early intervention.

Title: Modern antidiabetic therapy in older adults with type 2 diabetes: evidence, best practice and a clinical pharmacist's framework.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Older adults with type 2 diabetes require treatment that balances cardiovascular and kidney protection against hypoglycemia, treatment burden, undernutrition, and functional vulnerability.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review considers PubMed-indexed literature and ClinicalTrials.gov records covering January 2010-October 2026, with targeted updating on 12 October 2026. It examines sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, tirzepatide, and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. Age-stratified outcome evidence is distinguished from whole-trial results and the limited evidence in adults aged 80 years or older. Body-composition findings, neurodegenerative outcomes, kidney-protective treatment, and pharmacist-supported regimen modification are critically appraised.
EXPERT OPINION: Organ protection and glycemic simplification should be considered separately. Frailty is not synonymous with kidney impairment, and reductions in lean mass do not establish treatment-induced sarcopenia. Weight-neutral therapy remains useful when weight loss is undesirable. A structured medication review should integrate patient priorities, nutrition, physical performance, renal function, and hypoglycemia risk, followed by explicit monitoring and communication across care transitions. Prospective validation of this integrated framework in the oldest and most vulnerable populations is needed.

Title: Patiromer Efficacy across Kidney Function and Hyperkalemia Subgroups in Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction: A DIAMOND Post Hoc Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the DIAMOND (Patiromer for the Management of Hyperkalemia in Subjects Receiving RAASi Medications for the Treatment of Heart Failure) trial, patiromer enabled optimization of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors (RAASi) for patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and current or recent hyperkalemia. Impaired kidney function substantially increases hyperkalemia risk due to impaired potassium excretion. Therefore, in this post hoc analysis, we examined the efficacy of patiromer across baseline kidney function and hyperkalemia subgroups.
METHODS: We classified all patients randomized to patiromer (N=439) or placebo (N=439), after successful run-in optimization, into 4 subgroups according to estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <45 vs ≥45 mL/min/1.73m2 (trial eligibility criterion: ≥30 mL/min/1.73m2) and baseline hyperkalemia (≤5.0 vs >5.0 mEq/L; trial required K >5.0 or prior RAASi discontinuation for hyperkalemia).
RESULTS: Patiromer reduced adjusted mean change in serum potassium (primary outcome) across all subgroups, with the largest effect in patients with eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m2 and hyperkalemia (-0.28 mEq/L, 95% CI -0.38 to -0.18, P<0.001) and the smallest in those with eGFR ≥45 mL/min/1.73m2 and normokalemia (-0.08 mEq/L, 95% CI -0.12 to -0.04, P<0.001; Pinteraction <0.001). Patiromer reduced time-to-first hyperkalemia consistently across subgroups. Patients with eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m2 and baseline hyperkalemia derived the numerically greatest effect in prevention of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist down-titration (hazard ratio 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.84, P=0.02) and had the highest win ratio for hyperkalemia-related morbidity-adjusted outcomes (3.03, 95% CI 1.96-4.70, P<0.001). However, Pinteraction values for these secondary endpoints were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Patiromer reduced serum potassium across baseline kidney function and hyperkalemia subgroups, with greater effect in patients with reduced kidney function and baseline hyperkalemia. These findings suggest potential heterogeneity in potassium-lowering effects of patiromer across subgroups, although the analysis is exploratory and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Title: Low Daily Protein Intake and Risk of Kidney Failure and Mortality in Chronic Kidney Disease.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: While protein restriction is a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease (CKD) management, its long-term benefits on clinical outcomes in Asian populations, who often have lower body mass and muscle reserves, remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between daily protein intake (DPI) and the risk of kidney failure requiring replacement therapy (KFRT) and all-cause mortality in patients with non-dialysis-dependent CKD.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective cohort study used data from the Korean Cohort Study for Outcomes in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease (KNOW-CKD). Participants with CKD at stages ranging from 1 to predialysis 5 were enrolled between 2011 and 2016 from 9 tertiary hospitals in South Korea. The study observation period ended on January 31, 2024. Data analysis was performed from February 2024 to May 2026.
EXPOSURES: DPI was objectively estimated using 24-hour urinary nitrogen excretion at baseline. The participants were categorized by DPI: less than 0.6, 0.6 to less than 0.8, 0.8 to less than 1.0, 1.0 to less than 1.2, and 1.2 or greater.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the onset of KFRT. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were used to account for the competing risk of death.
RESULTS: A total of 1861 participants (mean [SD] age, 53.7 [12.0] years; 1304 [61.1%] male) were analyzed, with a median (range) follow-up of 9.3 (0.01-12.37) years. The lowest DPI group (<0.6 g/kg/d) was associated with increased risk of KFRT (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.42; 95% CI, 1.09-1.85) as well as all-cause mortality (sHR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.17-4.03), but not MACEs, compared with the highest DPI group (>1.2 g/kg/d). Furthermore, a nonlinear association was observed, where excessively low protein intake was associated with an increased risk of KFRT.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 1861 patients with nondialysis CKD, low protein intake was not associated with significant nephroprotection and was associated with a higher risk of KFRT and all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that rigid protein restriction should be balanced with nutritional monitoring to prevent protein-energy wasting, particularly in populations with lower muscle mass, and a more individualized approach to dietary protein management in CKD may be warranted.

Title: Quantitative Flow Ratio- vs Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Secondary Analysis of the FAVOR III China Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Whether the association of quantitative flow ratio (QFR)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with long-term outcomes differs according to multivessel disease (MVD) status is uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association of QFR-guided vs angiography-guided PCI with 3-year outcomes according to MVD status.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this prespecified secondary analysis of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial, patients were screened across 26 centers in China from December 25, 2018, to January 19, 2020. Eligible participants were adults undergoing PCI for stable or unstable angina or for myocardial infarction (MI) occurring at least 72 hours before screening who had at least 1 lesion with 50% to 90% diameter stenosis in a vessel of 2.5 mm or larger. The analysis compared QFR-guided with angiography-guided PCI according to MVD status. MVD was defined by involvement of at least 2 epicardial vessels or the left main coronary artery. The primary analyses of the current prespecified secondary analysis were completed in October 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: Randomization 1:1 to QFR-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, MI, and ischemia-driven revascularization. The current analysis evaluated 3-year MACE.
RESULTS: Among 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population (mean [SD] age, 62.7 [10.0] years; 2699 [70.6%] male), 2066 (54.0%) had MVD. In the MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 124 of 1023 patients (12.1%) in the QFR-guided group and 188 of 1043 patients (18.1%) in the angiography-guided group (hazard ratio, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.52-0.81; P < .001), driven by lower rates of MI and revascularization. In the non-MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 76 of 890 patients (8.6%) and 95 of 869 patients (11.0%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.04; P = .09). The treatment × MVD interaction was not statistically significant (P for interaction = .35). The findings of landmark, per-protocol, competing-risk, sensitivity, and hierarchical win-ratio analyses were directionally consistent with the main findings.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this prespecified secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial of patients undergoing PCI, QFR-guided PCI was associated with a lower 3-year MACE rate among patients with MVD; however, no significant interaction was observed between treatment effect and MVD status. These findings provide longer-term randomized evidence supporting QFR-guided PCI across MVD strata and warrant further confirmation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03656848.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Mitral Annular Disjunction: Regional Strain Abnormalities Associated With Life-Threatening Ventricular Arrhythmias.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been linked to malignant ventricular arrhythmias in mitral valve prolapse, but the mechanisms and risk predictors are not well established. We aimed to identify clinical and echocardiographic factors with a focus on left ventricular (LV) strain.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 69 patients with MAD confirmed on echocardiogram. Clinical data and echocardiographic measurements were collected, including chamber dimensions, MAD distance, mitral regurgitation grade, and 2D global and segmental longitudinal strain by speckle-tracking. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to determine independent predictors of arrhythmia.
RESULTS: All patients had preserved LV ejection fraction. Patients with arrhythmias demonstrated trends toward larger chamber dimensions and a larger MAD distance. Global longitudinal strain did not significantly differ between groups. Differences between patients with and without life-threatening arrhythmias localized specifically to the inferolateral region at the mid-ventricular level, where mid-inferolateral strain was significantly worse in arrhythmic patients (median -12.6% [IQR 13.5] vs. -18.9% [IQR 6.0], p = 0.0069). In univariate models, factors associated with arrhythmias included larger LV chamber diameters, greater MAD distance, a history of syncope, and worse strain in the mid-inferior and mid-inferolateral segments. On exploratory multivariate analysis, mid-inferolateral strain impairment appears to be independently associated with LTA (OR 1.11 per 1% strain increase, p = 0.012).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with MAD, impaired mid-inferolateral segment strain was associated with LTA, suggesting that regional myocardial deformation may provide incremental arrhythmic risk stratification beyond global measures. These findings are, however, exploratory, hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts with independent validation to ascertain clinical utility.

Title: NaV1.8 Inhibition and the Future of Nonopioid Analgesia in Otolaryngology: A Narrative Review.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Postoperative pain management in otolaryngology requires balancing effective analgesia while minimizing adverse effects, such as opioid-related complications. Suzetrigine is a first-in-class selective voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV1.8) inhibitor that has been recently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. Suzetrigine selectively inhibits NaV1.8 channels expressed in peripheral nociceptive neurons, thereby reducing pain signaling without the respiratory depression, sedation, or misuse potential associated with opioids. This review summarizes the pharmacology, efficacy, safety profile, limitations, and potential applications of suzetrigine in otolaryngology.
OBSERVATIONS: Prospective clinical trials consist of 2 phase 2 randomized clinical trials, 2 phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials, and 1 phase 3 open-label study involving more than 3000 patients. Across abdominoplasty and bunionectomy pain models, suzetrigine demonstrated superior analgesia compared with placebo and mixed efficacy comparable to hydrocodone/acetaminophen. The drug was generally well tolerated, with adverse event rates similar to placebo and no significant respiratory, cardiac, or sedating adverse effects reported. Additionally, 1 retrospective cohort study has reported results in patients undergoing free flap reconstruction and transoral robotic surgery.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Suzetrigine is a promising nonopioid analgesic with demonstrated efficacy compared to placebo in acute postoperative pain and a favorable safety profile. In otolaryngology, suzetrigine may serve as an adjunct to multimodal analgesia and an opioid-sparing option for patients with contraindications to traditional analgesics, opioid use disorder, or procedures that are expected to have high opioid utilization such as tonsillectomy, sleep surgery, and major head and neck surgery. Future studies in otolaryngology are warranted to evaluate whether suzetrigine can meaningfully reduce postoperative opioid exposure without compromising analgesic effectiveness.

Title: Lung Transplantation for Interstitial Lung Disease: A Northern Ireland Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lung transplantation (LTx) is the definitive treatment for advanced fibrotic interstitial lung disease (ILD), but referral timing remains challenging. Data on outcomes of Northern Ireland (NI) patients referred for LTx are limited.
METHODS: In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, all ILD referrals for LTx from the five NI healthcare trusts between January 2014 and March 2024 were analysed. Demographic, clinical, lung function and transplant outcome data were extracted from electronic health records. Patients were classified according to transplant assessment and listing outcomes.
RESULTS: One hundred thirty-eight patients were referred (median age 60.5 years; 64.5% male; 35.5% female); idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis was the most common diagnosis (44.2%). Of 138 referred patients, 64 (46.4%) were considered suitable for advanced LTx assessment, while 68 (49.3%) were unsuitable and 6 (4.3%) declined further assessment. Of those suitable for advanced assessment, 28 (43.8%) were listed for transplantation and 11 (17.2%) died before completion of assessment. Age was the only independent predictor of mortality before assessment completion, increasing risk by 13.9% per year (p = 0.011). The median interval between initial referral to LTx satellite clinic review was 131.5 days for the eligible cohort. The median interval from initial transplant clinic review to advanced assessment was 80 days excluding those patients with intentional pathway prolongation due to a watch-and-wait approach. Forty-five per cent of pre-transplant investigations, particularly coronary angiography, occurred > 6 months after satellite clinic review and may have contributed to some delays from referral to advanced assessment. Of patients listed for transplantation, 14 (50.0%) died while waiting, 11 (39.3%) underwent LTx, and 3 remained active on the waiting list.
CONCLUSION: Nearly half of ILD referrals were unsuitable for advanced LTx assessment, largely because of age and comorbidity. Delays in assessment pathways, for example watchful waiting and access to coronary angiography, may contribute to high pre-transplant mortality. Earlier referral and streamlined investigation pathways may improve transplantation outcomes.

Title: The FIBR-CMR score: a novel risk model integrating fibrinogen and cardiac magnetic resonance for major adverse events after STEMI.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification.
METHODS: In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).
RESULTS: Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).
CONCLUSION: The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.

Title: Evidence Suggests Linoleic Acid Exerts Health Benefits Beyond Cardiovascular Disease: A Brief Review of Clinical and Observational Studies.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Questions challenging the healthfulness of diets high in linoleic acid (LA) and seed oils, which are major sources of this essential fatty acid, have recently arisen. These questions are especially relevant to adherents of plant-based diets as their LA intake is higher than the general population. Some maintain that LA increases inflammation and oxidative stress and for these reasons, despite its ability to lower circulating LDL-cholesterol levels when replacing saturated fat, does not lower cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Because most of the discussion about LA has focused on CVD, the primary focus of this manuscript is to examine the effects of LA on health outcomes aside from CVD.
RECENT FINDINGS: Interventional and observational studies indicate increasing LA intake lowers risk of CVD. Beyond CVD, possible benefits include preventing hepatic fat accumulation, increasing muscle mass, decreasing risk of skin cancer, decreasing epigenetic aging, increasing the healthspan, and improving cognitive function and decreasing risk of developing neurocognitive disorders. Support for these proposed benefits comes from observational studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs), although more from the former. The observational evidence is especially robust in the case of cognitive function and neurological disorders, as the results of all but one of the eight recently published cohort studies show LA exposure, as assessed by dietary intake or circulating levels, is supportive of benefit, although much of the data come from analyses of one cohort. While it is premature to conclude that LA intake exerts benefits beyond CVD, evidence is sufficient to warrant that this possibility should be included in discussions about the role of LA and seed oils in the diet. Given the large contribution LA makes to energy intake, particularly among consumers of plant-based diets, research aimed at more definitively determining the range of possible benefits, especially related to cognitive function, is warranted.

Title: Pneumothorax rates following cardiac surgery with versus without continuous serratus anterior plane catheters: a secondary analysis of trial data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort.
Journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Moderate to severe pain is common after cardiac surgery, especially in the first two postoperative days. Inadequate pain control may prolong intensive care unit (ICU) stay, may increase cost, and contributes to chronic pain. Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols prioritize multimodal analgesia, including regional anesthesia techniques. In a recent randomized trial with continuous serratus anterior plane (SAP) catheters, we found unexpectedly high pneumothorax rates. To address this, we aimed to design a propensity-score-matched comparison using patients from the same institution to control for institutional practice patterns, surgical techniques, and patient demographics that could confound comparisons with published literature rates from other centres.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of RCT data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort. We compared the pneumothorax rates in patients receiving continuous SAP catheters in our previous Cardiac-Serratus Anterior Plane (Cardiac-SAP) trial with those in a retrospective institutional database cohort of patients receiving standard care undergoing cardiac surgery via sternotomy. The two groups were propensity score matched in a 1:20 ratio based on age, sex, smoking status, surgery type, and pre-existing respiratory disease. We analyzed univariate comparisons using Fisher's exact test or the percentile bootstrapping method.
RESULTS: We matched 50 patients from the Cardiac-SAP trial to 989 retrospective cohort patients. After matching, the SAP catheter group was associated with a significantly higher risk of pneumothorax (12% vs 3%; odds ratio, 5.3; 95% confidence interval, 2.1 to 13.6; P < 0.001). There were no significant differences for other outcomes, including ICU readmissions, length of ventilation, and length of ICU or hospital stay. Patients who developed a pneumothorax had longer ventilation time and longer hospital stays.
CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggest that SAP catheter use as a part of a randomized trial for cardiac surgery was associated with a higher rate of pneumothorax in trial participants than in a historic cohort of a similar population, though causality is unclear. Differences in monitoring within the trial and the inherent risks in this population may have contributed.

Title: Self-Prognostic Electronic Skin for Reliability-Aware Wearable Sensing.
Abstract: Flexible wearable sensors are increasingly used for long-duration monitoring of body-state information, but they can degrade silently during operation while continuing to output physiologically plausible signals, making it difficult to determine whether an incoming measurement remains trustworthy. Here, we report a self-prognostic electronic skin platform that couples multimodal body-state sensing with autonomous sensor-health assessment. The device monolithically co-integrates piezoelectric and triboelectric transduction by origami folding into an ultrathin, six-channel wrist-mounted array (∼0.1 mm, <1 g), so that a single mechanoelectrical stream simultaneously encodes cardiovascular pulsation, wrist activity, and the device's own degradation state. A two-stage self-diagnostic framework uses an autoencoder-CUSUM pipeline to establish device-specific failure labels from degradation trajectories, followed by an LSTM-Transformer model for remaining useful lifetime prediction. Across a twenty-device cohort with a nearly sevenfold variation in lifetime, the model predicts remaining useful lifetime across the cohort's degradation trajectories with R2 = 0.95 and captures uncertainty that increases as degradation becomes more severe. In single-participant daily-use proof-of-concept testing, the system estimates physiological parameters and sensor remaining lifetime from the same stream. The predicted lifetime of a newly fabricated device remained near 100% during a representative 1.5 h segment and declined modestly to 97.2% over approximately 12 h of wear distributed across multiple days; this single-device demonstration illustrates the operation of the diagnostic channel during daily use rather than validated cross-device predictive accuracy. These results establish reliability-aware wearable sensing, in which each body-state measurement is interpreted together with the operational health of the sensor itself, with potential value for long-duration applications such as health monitoring and embodied intelligence.

Title: Patterns, and outcomes of airbag -related penetrating injuries: a retrospective analysis from a level 1 trauma center.
Journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The deployment of defective airbag inflators can generate high-velocity metallic fragments that cause face, neck or chest penetrating injuries with potentially lethal consequences. This study aimed to describe the injury patterns, management, and outcomes of suspected airbag-related penetrating injuries (ARPI) among patients in a Middle Eastern country.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study of patients presenting with penetrating injuries suspected of being related to defective airbag deployment. Data were obtained from the Qatar National Trauma Registry (QNTR), electronic medical records, emergency medical services (EMS), emergency department (ED), and Mortuary. Data were collected and analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: A total of 16 patients had suspected ARPIs between April 2019 and February 2026. The mean age was 33.1 ± 8.3 years, and 93.8% were male. Metallic foreign bodies (FBs) from airbag inflator fragmentation were documented in 11/16 (68.8%) patients by imaging, and surgical removal while in 4/16 patients there were only entry-exit wounds after deployment of airbags following car crash. In one case, airbag deployed while mechanic was repairing a car steering wheel. Penetrating neck (43.8%), thoracic (31.3%), and maxillofacial injuries (31.3%), predominantly mandibular fractures, were most common. Surgical intervention was required in 11 (68.8%) patients and 7/16 required intensive care unit admissions. Five patients died (31.3%), including one at the scene (transported directly by the EMS, no CPR, and moved to the hospital mortuary), two died at the ED after unsuccessful CPR and two died during the hospital course (one presented with cardiac arrest and died on the sixth day and the other one required prolonged ECMO for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and died after 4 months).
CONCLUSIONS: Airbag inflator rupture can produce serious injury patterns resembling patterns of ballistic trauma, characterized by penetrating neck wounds, maxillofacial fractures and thoracic injuries. These injuries are potentially associated with high mortality, surgical intervention, and critical care utilization. The full extent of these injuries is undetermined as some victims may have simply died at the scene without the benefit of trauma center evaluation or post-mortem examination.

Title: Aveir VR for Atrial Leadless Pacing in Young Patients.
Abstract: Atrial Leadless pacemaker implantspresent a new treatment for sinus node dysfunction in complex cardiac anatomies. The Aveir-VR single chamber pacemaker can be placed in the atrium to control atrial flutter, or in the ventricle to control bradycardia. In this case report, we present four cases of the implantation of the Aveir VR in the atrium of male pediatric patients to treat sinus node dysfunction. Retrospective review of patients with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and atrially placed Aveir-VRs was performed at UC Davis between April 2024 and April 2026. Femoral access was the route of implantation for all 5 patients. Trans-esophageal echocardiography was used in all cases. The patients' ages ranged between 14-17-years and follow-up appointments were held between 1-23-months. Immediately post-procedure, impedances were 380-1460 Ohms, thresholds at 0.4 ms were 2.25-3.5 V, and P-waves were between 1.7-3 mV. Follow-up impedance was between 390-720 Ohms for the patients, thresholds were 0.5-1.25 V at 0.2-0.4 ms, P-waves were between 4.5-9.1 mV, and pacing percentages were between 12-69%. This case series demonstrates the successful implant of Aveir VR leadless pacemaker in five young patients for sinus node dysfunction.

Title: Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Children and Adolescents with Celiac Disease: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Study.
Abstract: Celiac disease (CD) is recognized as a systemic disorder extending beyond the gastrointestinal tract, with evidence of subclinical cardiovascular involvement emerging even in childhood. We aimed to evaluate myocardial function in children with CD compared to healthy controls, and to investigate whether echocardiographic parameters differ according to gluten-free diet adherence. This cross-sectional case-control study included 142 children with CD and 120 healthy controls. Conventional and advanced echocardiography were performed in all participants. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for sex, age, and body mass index (BMI) z-score was used for all echocardiographic outcomes. Patients were stratified by anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (anti-tTG IgA) into tTG-negative (n = 55), borderline (n = 13), and positive (n = 74) subgroups. Ejection Fraction (EF) and Fractional Shortening (FS) were modestly but significantly reduced in CD patients, while left ventricular (LV) dimensions and LV mass were not significantly different. All Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) parameters were significantly impaired in CD patients, including elevated Myocardial Performance Index (MPI) and E/e' ratios at both septal and lateral mitral annulus (p < 0.001). Myocardial function was impaired across all serological subgroups compared to controls, with no significant differences among celiac subgroups in multivariable analysis. ROC analysis demonstrated excellent discriminatory ability of MPI between celiac patients and healthy controls, after adjustment for age, sex and z-score BMI. Children with CD demonstrate significant subclinical myocardial dysfunction, detectable by TDI, independently of serological disease activity. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to establish the long-term cardiovascular implications and the role of routine cardiac monitoring in this population.

Title: Long-term outcomes of tracheostomy in patients with congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Data on long-term follow-up after tracheostomy in patients with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) are limited. We assessed current tracheostomy status and clinical characteristics in relation to decannulation during long-term follow-up.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, we analyzed the Japanese CDH Study Group database records from 2006 to 2023. Clinical characteristics of patients undergoing tracheostomy during hospitalization were reviewed. Using long-term follow-up data, decannulation status was assessed and decannulation rates were estimated via Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: We included 1284 patients, 38 of whom underwent tracheostomy during hospitalization. Compared with the non-tracheostomy group, the tracheostomy group had higher rates of severe cardiac anomalies (21% vs. 9%), more chromosomal abnormalities (26% vs. 7%), greater gestational age (median 37w6d vs. 37w1d), and lower birth weight (median 2468 g vs. 2704 g). Survival among the tracheostomy cohort was 74.4%, 63.7%, and 53.1% at 6, 9, and 12 years, respectively. The cumulative decannulation rate at age 6 years was 36%. Pulmonary vasodilator use at discharge was significantly more common in non-decannulated patients.
CONCLUSION: Among all CDH infants, 3.0% required tracheostomy. The cumulative decannulation rate at 6 years was 36%. Pulmonary vasodilator use at discharge was more common in non-decannulated patients.

Title: Effect heterogeneity of loneliness and social support on incident hypertension in older, normotensive populations.
Abstract: Although social isolation is known to impact those with cardiovascular disease, its relationship with incident hypertension is unclear. In this retrospective cohort study, we used data from the All of Us research program. Participants were enrolled between May 2017-April 2023, aged 50+ years, and had at least 60-days of EHR data pre-index date. We identified incident hypertension during follow-up. Those classified as hypertensive at or prior to the index date were excluded. We defined low social support and loneliness as binary variables. Using causal forests, we estimated treatment effects as unweighted and overlap-weighted risk differences (RD). A total of 24,720 participants with a median follow-up of 2.6 years were included. While loneliness and social support were not significantly associated with incident hypertension in the overall population, causal forests revealed meaningful effect heterogeneity, with socially isolated male (RD: 0.038, 95% CI 0.002 to 0.075; overlap-weighted RD: 0.027, 95% CI -0.005 to 0.059) and Gay or Lesbian participants (RD: 0.108, 95% CI 0.011 to 0.205; overlap-weighted RD: 0.11, 95% CI 0.008 to 0.211) experiencing a significantly elevated risk. This illustrates how machine learning, when embedded within epidemiologic frameworks, can detect subgroup vulnerability that other approaches may obscure, enabling targeting of limited resources.

Title: Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America.
OBJECTIVES: The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort.
METHODS: The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years.
RESULTS: The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

Title: Cardiomonostack: A postoperative heart failure risk prediction model for total hip arthroplasty driven by ensemble learning.
Journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
Abstract: BackgroundAccurate perioperative risk prediction remains challenging because of class imbalance, cohort heterogeneity, unstable probability estimates and limited interpretability.ObjectiveTo develop and externally evaluate CardioMonoStack, an ensemble architecture integrating heterogeneous base learners, branch-level monotonicity priors, stacked meta-learning and feature-dependent residual logit correction.MethodsWe conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 1911 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing total hip arthroplasty across five healthcare databases. CardioMonoStack was developed using MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, validated in INSPIRE, and externally tested in eICU and MOVER. Performance was assessed using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, threshold-dependent classification measures, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Interpretability was examined using SHAP, interaction and individual conditional expectation analyses.ResultsCardioMonoStack achieved the highest AUROC point estimates among evaluated models in eICU (0.790; 95% CI 0.711-0.865) and MOVER (0.866; 95% CI 0.761-0.949), with AUPRC values of 0.569 (95% CI 0.415-0.717) and 0.571 (95% CI 0.328-0.792), respectively. Calibration and net benefit varied across cohorts and comparators. Omission of L3 increased Brier-score and log-loss point estimates in both external cohorts; paired confidence intervals supported these differences in MOVER but were inconclusive in eICU. SHAP analyses prioritised blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, age, and metabolic and demographic factors.ConclusionCardioMonoStack is a candidate framework for estimating in-hospital heart-failure risk after total hip arthroplasty. Despite promising external discrimination, prospective validation, local recalibration, and clinical impact evaluation are required before implementation.

Title: Age-stratified mortality following operative management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury.
Journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
Abstract:
CONTEXT/OBJECTIVE: Postoperative mortality following traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI) remains substantial, yet the combined influence of neurologic completeness and age on survival is poorly characterized in operatively treated patients. This study evaluated age-stratified mortality after surgical management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cSCI.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using risk ratio analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards.
SETTING: Global federated electronic health record database (TriNetX).
PARTICIPANTS: Adults who underwent surgery for traumatic subaxial cSCI, identified using ICD-10 and CPT codes, with injury classified as complete or incomplete (n = 5,477).
INTERVENTIONS: Operative management of traumatic subaxial cSCI.
OUTCOME MEASURES: All-cause mortality at 3, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Independent predictors of mortality were identified via Cox regression.
RESULTS: Complete cSCI was associated with significantly higher mortality at 3 months (10.73% vs. 7.7%; RR 1.39), 6 months (12.5% vs. 9.2%; RR 1.36), and 1 year (14.7% vs. 11.2%; RR 1.31) (all P < 0.001). Mortality differences were most pronounced in patients aged 61-80 years, with approximately twofold higher risk in complete injuries. Increasing age, male sex, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease independently predicted mortality.
CONCLUSION: Complete traumatic cSCI carries significantly higher postoperative mortality than incomplete injury, particularly among patients aged 61-80 years. These findings underscore the combined prognostic impact of neurologic severity and age, and may guide perioperative counseling and risk stratification, but should not be interpreted as demonstrating formal age-dependent effect modification.

Title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control.
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.
METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index.
RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Clinical Trial

Title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
AIMS: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials.
METHODS: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding.
RESULTS: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis

Title: Interleukin-35 Ameliorates Obesity-Associated Impairment of Endothelium-Dependent Vasodilation via the STAT3-MAPK/ERK-eNOS Signaling Axis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity impairs endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS)-nitric oxide (NO) signaling, triggering chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction and defective vasodilation, which drives cardiometabolic diseases. Existing metabolic therapies provide only indirect vascular protection and fail to resolve residual inflammatory-mediated cardiovascular risk. As an anti-inflammatory interleukin 12 (IL-12) family cytokine, interleukin 35 (IL-35) is suppressed in obesity and exerts vascular protective effects under inflammatory conditions, yet its function and underlying mechanisms in obesity‑related endothelial vasodilator dysfunction remain undefined.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An obese mouse model was established by 8-week high-fat diet (HFD) feeding, followed by 4-week intraperitoneal administration of recombinant mouse IL-35. Aortic-ring assays evaluated vasodilatory function. Palmitic acid (PA)-treated human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), recapitulate lipotoxic endothelial injury, were treated with recombinant human IL-35. Western blotting, immunofluorescence, 4-amino-5-methylamino-2',7'-difluorofluorescein diacetate (DAF-FM DA) detection and immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS) were applied to detect IL-35-subunit (Epstein-Barr virus-induced gene 3 [EBI3] and interleukin-12 subunit alpha [IL-12A]) levels, eNOS Ser1177 phosphorylation, phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (MAPK/ERK) signaling molecules (cellular rapidly accelerated fibrosarcoma [cRAF], mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase [MEK], and ERK) and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) activation, NO production, and eNOS-binding partners. Rescue assays were performed using Raf or ERK specific inhibitors and STAT3 small interfering RNA (siRNA).
RESULTS: HFD mice displayed reduced aortic endothelial EBI3 expression, impaired endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation, decreased eNOS Ser1177 phosphorylation and lowered NO production; all these phenotypes were rescued by exogenous IL-35. IP-MS and immunoblotting demonstrated that IL-35 strengthened eNOS-ERK1 interaction and restored PA-repressed phosphorylation of cRAF, MEK, ERK and eNOS Ser1177, which were abrogated by Raf or ERK blockade. Furthermore, IL-35 recovered STAT3 phosphorylation suppressed by PA, while STAT3 knockdown blunted IL-35-driven MAPK/ERK activation, eNOS phosphorylation and subsequent NO production.
CONCLUSION: IL-35 alleviates obesity-induced impairment of endothelium-dependent vasodilation via the STAT3-MAPK/ERK-eNOS axis, which elevates eNOS Ser1177 phosphorylation and NO synthesis. This work supports IL-35 as a prospective therapeutic candidate for obesity-associated vascular complications.

Title: The START-SIAPAV-PAD Registry - Rationale, study design, and baseline characteristics of an ongoing Italian multicentre registry.
Abstract: Background: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with a high burden of cardiovascular and limb events, yet guideline-directed medical therapy remains suboptimal. The START-SIAPAV-PAD registry was designed to describe characteristics, management and clinical history of patients with PAD in Italy. Baseline characteristics and treatment are reported. Patients and methods: START-SIAPAV-PAD is a prospective, multicentre, observational registry enrolling consecutive adults with PAD managed at 20 Italian Vascular centres, starting in February 2023. Standardised electronic case-report forms collect demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, haemodynamic parameters, vascular anatomy, therapies. Follow-up is planned for a minimum of 3 years. PAD severity is classified according to the Leriche-Fontaine scale, and risk-factor targets follow the 2024 ESC guidelines. Results: The present analysis includes 517 patients (72.0% male; median age 71 years) with a high prevalence of hypertension (79.2%), dyslipidaemia (85.0%), diabetes (36.9%), smoking (96.1% current or former) and chronic kidney disease (21.2%). Nearly half reported a walking distance <200 m, 77.5% had a resting ankle-brachial index ≤.80, and 17.2% presented with Leriche-Fontaine stage IV. Femoropopliteal disease was most frequent (69.8%), with multilevel involvement in 43.4%. Previous revascularisation was common, major amputation was rare. LDL cholesterol target (<55mg dL) was achieved in 27.9% of patients despite lipid-lowering therapy in 82.1%.
