Dual pathway inhibition, advanced lipid-lowering therapies, supervised exercise and structured smoking-cessation programmes were insufficiently adopted. Conclusions: In a population with advanced PAD and multiple risk factors we observed a substantial gap between guideline recommendations and real-world practice. Longitudinal follow-up will assess outcomes and opportunities to improve PAD management.

Title: Associations of the Baseline Level and Change in Triglyceride Glucose-Body Roundness Index With Cardiovascular Diseases: Two Large Prospective Cohorts in Europe and Asia.
Journal: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences
Abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the association of baseline and changes of TyG-BRI with incident CVD based on the UK Biobank and China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 418,510 and 7923 individuals from the UK Biobank and CHARLS were included in Analysis 1 (baseline TyG-BRI with CVD risk). In Analysis 2 (change in TyG-BRI with CVD risk), a total of 11,682 and 4637 participants were included in Cox proportional hazard models. We found participants with the highest baseline TyG-BRI level were associated with increased risk of incident CVD in UK Biobank (HR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.39-1.52) and CHARLS (HR = 1.35, 95% CI: 1.13-1.61). Multivariable-adjusted restricted cubic spline analyses presented positive linear associations between TyG-BRI and CVD risk. Compared to persistently low levels of TyG-BRI (Class 1), those with persistently high levels (Class 3: 1.23 (1.02-1.49) and 1.42 (1.11-1.55); Class 4: 1.48 (1.17-1.87) and 1.45 (1.16-2.28); Class 5: 2.58 (1.86-3.58) and 1.63 (1.16-2.28) for UK Biobank and CHARLS) in follow-up were associated with increased risks of incident CVD. In conclusion, a high baseline TyG-BRI level and different changes in TyG-BRI level are associated with increased risks of incident CVD.

Title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Acute Coronary Occlusion in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary occlusion (ACO) occurs in approximately one-quarter of patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model for ACO.
METHODS: Consecutive patients admitted with NSTEMI between January 2016 and June 2023 who underwent coronary angiography were enrolled. Demographic, electrocardiographic, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected. Patients admitted during 2016-2020 were assigned to the training cohort (n = 670), and those admitted during 2021-2023 were assigned to the validation cohort (n = 334). Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and a nomogram was constructed based on multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Among 1,004 patients, 262 (26.1%) had ACO. Seven predictors, including smoking history, ST-segment depression ≥ 1 mm, regional wall motion abnormality, left ventricular ejection fraction, admission cardiac troponin I, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, were incorporated into the model. The area under the ROC curve was 0.731 (95% CI, 0.688-0.773) in the training cohort and 0.715 (95% CI, 0.654-0.776) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA demonstrated favorable clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: This study developed and validated a multidimensional prediction model for ACO in patients with NSTEMI. The model showed acceptable performance and may aid early identification before coronary angiography, although reliance on IL-6, which is not routinely available in all centers, may limit its generalizability.

Title: Prolonged QT Interval in Hospitalized Internal Medicine Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Determinants and Reversibility.
Journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: QT interval prolongation is a common electrocardiographic abnormality in hospitalized patients, associated with malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Its determinants in internal medicine, and the reliability of correction formulas used to identify it, remain insufficiently characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including 277 patients hospitalized with QTc prolongation - defined by Bazett correction (QTcB >450 ms in men; ≥460 ms in women) - between January 2016 and December 2023. QTc was independently calculated using Bazett (QTcB) and Framingham (QTcF) formulas, and agreement between the two was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable logistic regression (complete-case analysis) explored predictors of QTcF-confirmed prolongation, and reversibility was assessed by repeat ECG performed after correction of the underlying reversible cause, or within 72 hours when no such cause was identified.
RESULTS: Mean age was 59.2 ±17.2 years, with a slight female predominance (54.2%). Only 78 patients (28.1%) had QTcF-confirmed prolongation despite all meeting QTcB inclusion criteria. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +31.7 ms between QTcB and QTcF (SD 18.9; 95% limits of agreement: -5.3 to +68.7 ms), strongly correlated with heart rate (r=0.92, p<0.001): the overcorrection increased from +3.6 ms at heart rate <70 bpm to +64.4 ms at >110 bpm. QTcB normalized on the follow-up ECG in 68.2% of patients. In a complete-case multivariable model (n=96 with available serum bicarbonate), no variable reached conventional statistical significance; serum bicarbonate (OR=1.121 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 0.991-1.268; p=0.069) and hypertension (OR=2.522; 95% CI: 0.875-7.275; p=0.087) showed borderline associations with QTcF-confirmed prolongation. In an exploratory analysis of the diabetic subgroup (n=148), peripheral neuropathy (DN4 ≥4) was associated with a 15.8 ms higher mean QTcB (age-adjusted 95% CI: 4.7-27.0 ms; p=0.006).
CONCLUSION: Bazett's formula substantially and heart-rate-dependently overestimates QT prolongation compared with the Framingham formula, a discrepancy now precisely quantified. QT prolongation in hospitalized internal medicine patients is predominantly acquired and reversible. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy was associated with higher QTcB values in an exploratory analysis. Serum bicarbonate showed only a non-significant trend toward association with QTcF-confirmed prolongation after complete-case multivariable adjustment; this hypothesis warrants confirmation in prospective studies with complete acid-base characterization before any clinical application.

Title: An Early Longitudinal Decrease in Platelet Count Is Associated With Poor Prognosis in Acute Myocardial Infarction Patients: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data are available on the association between early longitudinal changes in platelet count and mortality.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the early longitudinal changes in platelet count between survivors and non-survivors.
METHODS: This was a retrospective multi-center cohort study using data from the eICU Collaborative Research Database. A total of 6,769 patients diagnosed with AMI were included in the study. The analysis employed a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) and a Generalized Additive Mixed Model (GAMM) to compare longitudinal changes in platelet count between survivors and non-survivors.
RESULTS: The ICU 28-day and ICU 7-day all-cause mortality were 6.1% and 4.6%, respectively. During the first 5 days of ICU admission, GAM showed that non-survivors exhibited a significantly greater decline in platelet count than survivors. Specifically, the GAMM results showed that the difference in platelet count between ICU 28-day non-survivors and ICU 28-day survivors increased by an average of 15.4 × 109/L daily (95% Confidence Interval [CI], 14.1 to 16.7; p < 0.001). Similarly, the difference in platelet count between ICU 7-day non-survivors and ICU 7-day survivors increased by an average of 18.0 × 109/L daily (95% CI, 16.1-19.8; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: An early longitudinal decline in platelet count was associated with a poor prognosis in patients with AMI. However, this study is observational, and causality cannot be inferred.

Title: Multi-Trait GWAS Analyses of Blood Pressure Traits Provide Limited Gains in Locus Discovery or Polygenic Risk Score Performance Compared to Single-Trait GWAS.
Abstract: High blood pressure (BP) represents a major cause of life-threatening cardiovascular conditions. GWAS have identified >2000 BP-associated signals. BP-GWAS usually analyze each BP trait individually. However, multi-trait GWAS may yield novel loci and improve polygenic risk scores (PRS) prediction. We explored whether multi-trait BP-GWAS can: (i) find novel loci undetected by single-trait GWAS; (ii) increase heritability estimates; (iii) improve PRS prediction of hypertension within the Lifelines Cohort Study. We investigate the utility of multi-trait GWAS approaches of correlated BP traits (systolic BP, diastolic BP, pulse pressure). We tested two multi-trait methods inputting results from the latest N > 1 million single-trait BP-GWAS: (a) Multi-Trait Analysis of GWAS (MTAG); (b) genomic structural equation modeling (GenomicSEM); and compared results with single-trait results. We only identified one novel locus from multi-trait GWAS: ZNF268. Neither heritability estimates nor PRS performance improved using multi-trait GWAS. In this scenario of complete sample overlap across BP-GWAS, we observed little gain in results from multi-trait BP-GWAS over single-trait BP-GWAS. Our findings quantify the limited benefit of multi-trait methods under this specific setting. Future BP genetic discoveries are more likely to come from larger GWAS adding new cohort data. However, conclusions may differ for other traits, depending on trait-specific genetic architecture.

Title: Mid-Term Clinical Outcomes According to CTO Revascularization Status in Patients With NSTEMI and Multivessel Disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical relevance of chronic total occlusion (CTO) revascularization in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and multivessel disease (MVD) remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 632 patients with NSTEMI, MVD, and CTO were included. Patients were categorized into a complete revascularization group involving successful CTO recanalization (CR-CTO, n = 119) and an incomplete revascularization group without successful CTO recanalization (ICR-CTO, n = 513). The primary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 528 ± 201 days, the incidences of MACCE (11.8% vs. 28.5%) and MACE (7.6% vs. 24.2%) were significantly lower in the CR-CTO group than in the ICR-CTO group (both p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analyses, CR-CTO was independently associated with lower risks of MACCE (hazard ratio [HR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20-0.61) and MACE (HR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.13-0.51). Among patients without successful CTO recanalization, additional revascularization of non-CTO lesions was not associated with improved outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with NSTEMI, MVD, and CTO, complete revascularization involving successful CTO recanalization was associated with improved mid-term clinical outcomes. In contrast, additional revascularization of non-CTO lesions alone was not associated with a prognostic benefit when CTO lesions remained unrevascularized. These findings suggest that CTO revascularization status may warrant specific consideration when revascularization strategies are evaluated in this patient population.

Title: Computed-Tomography Angiography-Based Carotid Plaque-RADS, Recurrent Vascular Events, and the Effect of Colchicine: An Imaging Substudy of the CONVINCE Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) provides a standardized framework for evaluating plaque morphology, but prospective validation remains limited. We investigated the association between computed tomography angiography-based Plaque-RADS categories and subsequent ischemic events in patients with noncardioembolic stroke/transient ischemic attack, from a completed clinical trial of colchicine. Second, we assessed whether the effect of colchicine differed by Plaque-RADS risk classification.
METHODS: We conducted a posthoc observational cohort analysis of 517 participants in the CONVINCE trial (Colchicine for Prevention of Vascular Inflammation in Non-CardioEmbolic Stroke) from 13 European sites. Associations between Plaque-RADS and recurrent ipsilateral stroke, any stroke/transient ischemic attack, and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Plaque-RADS was analyzed as both dichotomized (<3 versus ≥3) and ordinal (per 1-point increase) variables. Treatment effects were assessed by Plaque-RADS classification using interaction and stratified analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 510 patients (median age, 67.0 years; 72.2% male) with 966 internal carotid arteries were included. Among 321 internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, 12 recurrent ipsilateral strokes, 32 any strokes/transient ischemic attacks, and 37 major adverse cardiovascular events occurred over a median 35.7-month follow-up. Plaque-RADS ≥3 (n=140) was independently associated with recurrent ipsilateral stroke (adjusted hazard ratio, 7.80 [95% CI, 1.55-39.30]; P=0.01), any stroke/transient ischemic attack (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.94 [95% CI, 1.68-9.24]; P<0.01), and major adverse cardiovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.52 [95% CI, 1.19-5.34]; P=0.02) after adjustment for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors. A significant interaction with colchicine treatment was observed for major adverse cardiovascular events (P=0.047), with greater benefit among patients with Plaque-RADS scores ≥3 (hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15-0.82]).
CONCLUSIONS: In internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, computed tomography angiography-based carotid Plaque-RADS was associated with recurrent ischemic stroke and cardiovascular events. Importantly, treatment effects of colchicine varied across Plaque-RADS classification (<3 versus ≥3), suggesting that plaque vulnerability assessment may help refine patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy beyond stenosis-based classification.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02898610.

Title: Impact of Guideline-Recommended LDL-C Goals on Coronary Plaque in a Post-PCI Setting: A Posthoc OCT Substudy of the CUT-DRESS Trial.
Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

Title: Supine versus prone percutaneous nephrolithotomy: A narrative and analytical review of technique.
Journal: Indian journal of urology : IJU : journal of the Urological Society of India
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) remains the gold standard for large and complex renal calculi. Although the prone position has traditionally been used since the introduction of PCNL in 1976, supine PCNL and its modifications have gained increasing acceptance with growing evidence supporting their efficacy and safety. This narrative review aims to compare supine and prone PCNL across various domains.
METHODS: Databases, PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were included. Priority was given to randomized-controlled trials, meta-analyses, and large prospective studies (>100 patients). Evidence was synthesized across operative, anesthetic, safety and technological domains.
RESULTS: Supine PCNL demonstrated stone-free rates comparable to prone PCNL. Multiple meta-analyses showed significantly shorter operative times (by 13-25 min), improved anesthetic safety, reduced radiation exposure, shorter learning curve, lower infectious complications, and superior ergonomics with the supine approach. Supine PCNL facilitates Endoscopic Combined Intrarenal Surgery and is particularly advantageous in obese, pediatric, elderly, and cardiovascular high-risk patients. Miniaturized PCNL techniques further enhance these benefits. Ultrasound-guided access contributes to improved procedural safety, whereas gravity-assisted drainage helps maintain low intrarenal pressure and facilitates gravity-assisted fragment evacuation. Emerging technologies such as vacuum-assisted systems and robotic-assisted PCNL appear inherently more compatible with the supine position.
CONCLUSION: Supine PCNL offers significant operative, anesthetic, and technological advantages while maintaining equivalent stone-free outcomes. It can be considered an equally useful approach in most clinical scenarios, whereas prone PCNL has definite advantages in selected anatomical situations.

Title: Early Post-transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) Haemodynamics With SAPIEN Balloon-Expandable and Evolut Self-Expanding Valve Platforms: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study.
Abstract: Introduction Balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) and self-expanding valves (SEVs) have different frame architectures, leaflet positions and distinct deployment mechanics that may influence prosthetic haemodynamics. We compared early echocardiographic gradients after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) between SAPIEN BEV and Evolut SEV platforms in a routine-practice cohort spanning several device generations. Materials and methods We retrospectively analysed 665 TAVI procedures: 250 BEV procedures using SAPIEN 3 variants and 415 SEV procedures using Evolut variants. The primary endpoint was the early post-TAVI echocardiographic mean transvalvular gradient obtained within three months of TAVI. Secondary endpoints were absolute and relative gradient reductions, achievement of a post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg, and a residual mean gradient ≥20 mmHg. Because the continuous variables were skewed, they were compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Results were reported as medians with interquartile ranges, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for differences in medians. Categorical variables were compared using Pearson chi-square tests without continuity correction when expected counts were adequate and Fisher's exact tests when cell counts were small. Paired pre- and post-TAVI measurements were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Multivariable ordinary least-squares regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors was used to adjust the post-TAVI gradient for the baseline gradient and available prespecified covariates. Results Complete pre- and post-TAVI gradients were available for 664 procedures (249 BEV and 415 SEV). The median post-TAVI gradient was 8.4 (5.85-11.63) mmHg with SEV and 10.0 (7.93-13.90) mmHg with BEV (median difference, -1.60 mmHg; bootstrap 95% CI: -2.97 to -1.00; Mann-Whitney U test: p < 0.001). The median absolute gradient reduction was also greater with SEVs (36.0 vs 32.0 mmHg; median difference, 4.0 mmHg; p < 0.001), as was the relative gradient reduction (81.52% vs 76.19%; median difference, 5.33 percentage points; p < 0.001), although SEVs had a higher pre-procedural baseline transvalvular gradient. A post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg was recorded in 61.2% of SEV procedures compared with 43.4% of BEV procedures (risk ratio 1.41; p < 0.001). Residual gradients of ≥20 mmHg were uncommon and did not differ between the two groups (6.0% in SEV procedures vs 5.6% in BEV procedures; p = 0.831). After adjustment, in 575 completed cases, SEV use remained associated with a 1.48 mmHg lower post-TAVI mean gradient (95% CI: -2.42 to -0.55; p = 0.0019). Conclusions In this cohort, Evolut SEV procedures were associated with a modestly lower early post-TAVI mean gradient than SAPIEN BEV procedures. The magnitude of this association, and its interpretation alongside baseline gradient, anatomy, and other device-selection factors, can inform further comparative evaluation. No clinical outcomes or valve-durability measures were assessed.

Title: Digital technology-enabled healthcare services and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with cardiovascular disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: Digital technology-enabled healthcare services may support secondary prevention in patients with cardiovascular disease; however, their effects on clinical outcomes remain uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate their impact on cardiovascular outcomes. PubMed and Embase were searched from inception to 11 March 2025. Randomized controlled trials evaluating digital technology-enabled healthcare services in patients with established cardiovascular disease were included. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), as defined in each trial. Secondary outcomes included rehospitalization, coronary artery disease-related events, all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, revascularization, and adverse events. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251186138) Among 3603 records identified, 14 randomized controlled trials were included. Digital technology-enabled healthcare services were associated with a reduced risk of MACCE (risk ratio 0.595; 95% confidence interval 0.471-0.752; I 2 = 0%). Rehospitalization (risk ratio 0.676; 95% confidence interval 0.496-0.923; I 2 = 73.9%) and coronary artery disease-related events (risk ratio 0.594; 95% confidence interval 0.354-0.996; I 2 = 0%) were also reduced. There were no significant differences in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, or revascularization (all I 2 = 0%). No significant difference in adverse events was observed between groups (I 2 = 45.9%). Digital technology-enabled healthcare services were associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular events in patients with established cardiovascular disease. However, substantial heterogeneity was observed for rehospitalization, and no significant reductions were observed in mortality outcomes. Registration PROSPERO identifier: CRD420251186138.

Title: 2026 Focused Update of the Saudi Heart Association Guidelines on Best Practices in the Management of Chronic Coronary Syndromes.
Journal: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) continue to impose a substantial clinical and economic burden in Saudi Arabia. Since publication of the 2022 Saudi Heart Association (SHA) CCS guidelines, important advances have emerged in diagnosis, pharmacotherapy, cardiometabolic risk reduction, antiplatelet management, and revascularization. This 2026 focused update selectively revises and clarifies key recommendations to reflect these advances within the Saudi context.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary SHA expert panel conducted a structured review of randomized trials, meta-analyses, and relevant international guidance published since 2022. Updates were restricted to areas with substantive new evidence or evolving clinical practice. Recommendations were formulated through expert consensus in accordance with SHA methodological standards. This document complements the 2022 guideline and does not replace it.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: This focused update advances a more personalized, risk-driven approach to CCS management. Diagnostic algorithms now explicitly integrate pre-test probability, reinforce coronary computed tomography angiography as the preferred initial modality in low-to-intermediate probability, and refine the positioning of functional stress imaging. Residual risk assessment and preventive strategies are also strengthened. Importantly, this update introduces a dedicated diagnostic and management framework for angina and ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA/INOCA), emphasizing endotype-specific evaluation and targeted therapy for this historically under-recognized population. Anti-anginal therapy positions beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers as equivalent first-line agents, upgrades long-acting nitrates, and integrates ranolazine, ivabradine, and trimetazidine as evidence-based add-on options. Antiplatelet guidance emphasizes individualized dual antiplatelet therapy duration after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), early de-escalation strategies, and selective use of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy. Lipid management and cardiovascular risk reduction options are now expanded and revascularization recommendations are restructured. Collectively, these updates strengthen the delivery of contemporary, evidence-based, and patient-centered CCS care and provide a clear framework for implementation across diverse healthcare settings.

Title: Heart Failure Progression in the Setting of Persistent Atrial Fibrillation, Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes, and Malignancy-Related Limitations to Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy: A Case Report.
Abstract: Persistent atrial fibrillation and frequent premature ventricular complexes may contribute to worsening heart failure, particularly when malignancy limits guideline-directed medical therapy. In patients with progressive ventricular dysfunction and limited pharmacologic options, atrioventricular nodal ablation with cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation may provide durable rate control and support subsequent ventricular functional recovery.

Title: Reduction in Right Ventricular Stroke Work Index After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty is Associated With Long-Term Prognosis in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract: The prognostic relevance of the relative change in right ventricular stroke work index (RVSWI) after balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) remains uncertain. This retrospective single-center study included 38 patients with CTEPH. Follow-up began at post-BPA catheterization. Relative change in RVSWI (%RVSWI; negative values indicate reduction) and conventional measures were compared using Cox models and direction-fixed C-indices. Bootstrap resampling assessed selection optimism across 14 candidates. RVSWI decreased from 16.96 to 9.83 g·m/m2/beat. During a median 4.1 years, 7 patients reached the composite endpoint of all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. A smaller reduction was associated with higher risk (hazard ratio 1.24 per 1 percentage-point increase in %RVSWI, 95% confidence interval 1.06-1.44; p = 0.007). %RVSWI had the highest apparent C-index (0.942, 95% confidence interval 0.86-0.99), but its difference from achieved mean pulmonary artery pressure (C-index 0.855) was not statistically distinguishable. %RVSWI ranked first in 62% of bootstrap resamples; the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.922. Component log-ratios were essentially uncorrelated (r = 0.01, 95% confidence interval -0.31 to 0.33). Greater RVSWI reduction after BPA was associated with better prognosis. With seven events, these findings are hypothesis-generating; superiority over conventional measures and the physiological interpretation of the SVI component remain unestablished.

Title: Chronic Complications Following Dengue Infection: A Scoping Review.
Abstract: Dengue virus infection has increased substantially in Latin America, prompting epidemiological alerts from regional health authorities in recent years. While most published research focuses on the acute phase, chronic multisystemic sequelae remain poorly characterized. This scoping review aimed to identify and describe chronic complications in adult patients following dengue infection, as reported in the available scientific literature. A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A structured Population, Concept, Context (PCC) question guided searches of PubMed (National Library of Medicine, Bethesda, Maryland), Scopus (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), Google Scholar (Google, Mountain View, California), EMBASE (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), Cochrane Library (John Wiley & Sons, Hoboken, New Jersey), and LILACS (BIREME, São Paulo, Brazil), and gray literature from January 2005 to June 15, 2026. Articles were screened independently by eight reviewers using Rayyan; inter-rater reliability was assessed using Fleiss' kappa (κ = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.74-0.88), and disagreements were resolved by consensus. Of the 222 identified records, 62 studies met the inclusion criteria after deduplication and full-text screening. Neurological complications were the most frequently represented category among the included publications (30.6%, n = 19), followed by ophthalmological (19.4%, n = 12), heterogeneous persistent symptoms (12.9%, n = 8), fatigue (9.7%, n = 6), multisystemic (9.7%, n = 6), psychiatric (9.7%, n = 6), cardiological (4.8%, n = 3), and immunological (3.2%, n = 2) complications. These proportions reflect the distribution of the published literature rather than the clinical prevalence of complications among dengue patients, given that approximately one-third of the included studies were case reports or case series. The evidence base includes the largest population-based cohort of post-acute dengue sequelae to date (n = 55,870, Singapore), a two-year disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) burden analysis from the same registry, the first systematic review of dengue-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome, the first reported case of chronic dengue encephalitis with brain-tissue DENV RNA confirmed by metagenomic sequencing, and two narrative reviews that substantially expanded the evidence base on psychiatric sequelae. Dengue infection is associated with a broad and heterogeneous spectrum of chronic complications affecting multiple organ systems, including elevated post-acute cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric, and autoimmune risks, as well as a measurable disease and healthcare cost burden. The absence of a consistent relationship between acute severity and chronic outcomes supports structured, evidence-based, long-term post-dengue follow-up, particularly for patients with persistent symptoms or clinically relevant risk factors and for underrepresented Latin American populations.

Title: Conduction System Pacing Versus Biventricular Pacing for Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) is an emerging alternative to biventricular pacing (BVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded divergent results, creating uncertainty about the comparative effectiveness.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CSP with BVP for CRT, searching PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through May 2026 (updating a prior review). The primary outcome was change in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF), analyzed with random-effects models and prediction intervals.
RESULTS: Eight parallel-group RCTs including 799 patients (396 CSP, 403 BVP) were included. Pooled ΔLVEF did not differ significantly (MD +2.40%, 95% CI -0.49 to 5.29, p = 0.091; I 2 = 75%). CSP showed a non-significant trend toward shorter paced QRS (MD -7.6 ms, p = 0.14) and improved NYHA class (SMD -0.33, p = 0.12). Heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.69), mortality (RR 1.17), complications (RR 0.84), and procedure time did not differ. The four trials enrolling exclusively LBBB patients favored CSP (MD +5.00%, 95% CI 3.01 to 6.98, p = 0.004; I 2 = 0%), consistent in the three using confirmed LBBAP/LBBP (MD +5.37%, 95% CI 3.23 to 7.52, p = 0.008; I 2 = 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis of randomized trials of CRT, no statistically significant difference was observed between CSP and BVP for any outcome. Because no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and the clinical-event analyses were underpowered, these findings should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence or comparable safety. Exploratory analyses suggest that patients with LBBB undergoing LBBAP/LBBP may derive incremental benefit, warranting confirmation in adequately powered trials.

Title: Orexin-A and Periosteal Pressure Sensitivity during acute mental and physical stress: a randomized cross-over study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Objective physiological markers reflecting central autonomic regulation remain limited. The orexin (hypocretin) system, localized in the lateral hypothalamus, integrates arousal, metabolic state, cardiovascular control, homeostatic control, and stress responsiveness. Periosteal Pressure Sensitivity (PPS) at the sternum has been proposed as a peripheral marker for central sympathetic activation. The present study examined for the first time the association between PPS and salivary orexin-A during experimentally induced mental and physical stress and subsequent recovery.
METHODS: In this randomized cross-over study, 20 healthy female participants (20-28 years) completed two experimental procedures in randomized order: Maastricht Acute Stress Test (MAST) and Moderate-Intensity Interval Training (MIIT). PPS, systolic blood pressure, heart rate, Pressure-Rate Product (i.e., systolic blood pressure × heart rate) and salivary orexin-A were measured at baseline, immediately post-procedure, as well as 15 and 30 mins into recovery. MIIT results were analyzed both for the full sample (n = 20) and for the participants who fulfilled the protocol-defined cardiovascular response criterion (n = 12).
RESULTS: MAST did not induce significant baseline-to-post-stress changes in PRP, PPS, or salivary orexin-A, although PRP decreased significantly during early recovery from S2 to S3 (p = 0.045). A significant negative correlation was observed between ΔPPS and ΔPRP from S1 to S2 (r = -0.47, p = 0.035). MIIT induced a marked increase in PRP followed by a decrease during recovery. Changes in PPS and salivary orexin-A were not significantly correlated in the full MIIT sample. In the separate MIIT sub-analysis, a positive correlation was observed during the 30-min recovery period (r = 0.76, p = 0.029, and n = 8).
CONCLUSION: MIIT produced a clear cardiovascular response, whereas MAST did not produce the expected immediate cardiovascular stress response. The MIIT sub-analysis supports a possible association between changes in salivary orexin-A and PPS during recovery but does not establish a causal or central orexin-mediated mechanism. Replication in a larger population using technically successful and standardized MIIT and MAST procedures is required.

Title: Artificial intelligence in cardiology: an evidence map across subspecialties, 2014-26.
Abstract:
AIMS: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied in healthcare, including cardiology, with growing interest in its potential to support diagnosis, prognosis, and clinical decision-making. The rapid pace of technological advancements is not matched by equivalent progress in the regulation and appraisal of these systems. This review aims to provide a structured evidence map of AI models in cardiology, by grading the robustness of clinical validation and mapping it against the quantity of publications across main subspecialties.
METHODS AND RESULTS: To assess the strength of evidence, we defined, developed, and applied a novel classification tailored for AI models that ranks evidence into five Grades of Validation according to the level of clinical validity. We screened literature from 2014 to 2026 according to the PRISMA guidelines, identifying a total of 2807 articles on AI applications within cardiology, 490 of which met the inclusion criteria (validation was performed in at least one external, independent patient population), revealing a highly heterogeneous distribution of evidence across subspecialties. Most studies in AI focused on improved diagnostics (n = 322, 65.7%); however, advanced integration in prognostic (n = 122, 24.9%) and therapeutic applications remains limited (n = 46, 9.4%). Cardiovascular imaging leads AI applications, especially in coronary computed tomography and echocardiography, followed by non-invasive electrophysiology, predominantly in atrial fibrillation screening and ventricular dysfunction detection.
CONCLUSION: The scarcity of prospective validations across different resources and geographical settings (n = 134, 27.3%) and randomized controlled trials (n = 35, 3.8%) limits the adoption by clinical guidelines and widespread implementation of AI algorithms.

Title: Hippo signaling-linked circulating microRNA networks are associated with cardiovascular disease in type 2 diabetes.
Abstract:
CONTEXT: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) markedly increases the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers for patient stratification and may provide mechanistic insight into dysregulated pathways in T2D-associated CVD.
OBJECTIVE: This work aimed to identify circulating miRNA signatures in T2D patients with CVD (T2D-CVD) vs T2D patients without CVD using a novel network-based medicine approach.
METHODS: Patients (n = 110) were stratified into T2D and T2D-CVD groups based on the absence or presence of macrovascular complications. Circulating miRNAs, proinflammatory cytokines, and growth factors were profiled in a discovery cohort (n = 80) and confirmed in a validation cohort (n = 30). Differential expression, network-based approaches, and pathway enrichment analyses identified miRNA signatures, coexpression communities, hub miRNAs, and associated signaling pathways.
RESULTS: T2D-CVD patients showed a set of elevated inflammatory cytokines and circulating miRNAs. Particularly, 19 miRNAs were differentially expressed between T2D-CVD and T2D patients. Pathway enrichment of these miRNAs highlighted Hippo signaling together with transforming growth factor-β, mechanistic target of rapamycin, Wnt, and PI3K-Akt pathways. Network analysis identified a coexpression community of 34 miRNAs, including hub miRNAs let-7a-5p, miR-132-3p, and miR-1306-3p, all linked to Hippo signaling. Key miRNA interactions were validated, and differentially expressed and hub miRNAs both correlated with inflammatory mediators such as PAR-1, CXCL1, and NEMO, which are linked to Hippo pathway regulation.
CONCLUSION: This study identified a network of circulating miRNAs associated with inflammatory cytokines and Hippo signaling pathway in T2D-CVD. These findings reveal novel molecular aspects of the systemic inflammation characterizing T2D-CVD and support the potential of Hippo-related circulating miRNAs as mechanistic biomarkers for cardiovascular risk in T2D.

Title: Predictors and Patterns of Metastatic Candidozyma auris Infection, Spain, 2016-2024.
Abstract: Metastatic infection after Candidozyma auris candidemia remains poorly characterized. We retrospectively studied patients with C. auris candidemia at a tertiary hospital in Spain during 2016-2024. Of 108 patients, 24 (22.2%) experienced metastatic infections; endocarditis was most frequent (7.4%), followed by osteoarticular infection, meningitis, and hepatosplenic infection (3.7% each). In multivariable Fine-Gray regression, a cardiac device or prosthetic valve was independently associated with metastatic infection (subdistribution hazard ratio [HR] 2.89 [95% CI 1.21-6.91]), although that association was attenuated in a sensitivity analysis restricted to echocardiographed patients. Persistent candidemia showed a higher, nonsignificant risk for metastatic infection in the day-5 landmark analysis (subdistribution HR 2.67 [95% CI 0.86-8.32]). Metastatic infection was associated with increased deaths in time-dependent analyses at 60 days (adjusted HR 2.21 [95% CI 1.04-4.67]) and 90 days (adjusted HR 2.26 [95% CI 1.09-4.67]). Our findings support echocardiography in patients with intracardiac devices.

Title: Invasive Enterovirus and Parechovirus Infections in Adults, Alberta, Canada, 2023-2025.
Abstract: We conducted a retrospective, population-based laboratory surveillance study during May 2023-December 2025 in Alberta, Canada, to characterize adult invasive enterovirus and parechovirus infections and to identify groups at high risk for those infections. Of 15,621 samples tested, 162 (1.0%) were virus positive, of which 51 (31.5%) samples from 39 patients indicated invasive infections. Cerebrospinal fluid, blood, and cardiac tissue were the most frequent virus-positive specimens. The invasive enterovirus and parechovirus incidence rate was 0.37 cases/100,000 person-years; rates were higher in patients <50 versus >50 years of age (incidence rate ratio 8.2; p<0.001). The annual incidence rates were 0.20-0.56 cases/100,000 person-years; rates appeared higher in 2025 than in 2024 (incidence rate ratio 2.1; p = 0.11). Severe disseminated enterovirus infection occurred in 2 patients who received ocrelizumab. Continuous surveillance and ongoing optimization of enterovirus and parechovirus detection assays is essential for comprehensive public health tracking.

Title: Polysocial risk score predicts chronic kidney disease incidence and prognosis: mechanistic insights from plasma metabolome, proteome and lifestyle.
Abstract: The cumulative impact of multiple social determinants of health (SDHs) on chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly understood. This prospective study examined the association of a polysocial risk score (PsRS) with CKD incidence and subsequent risks of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, and explored potential mediating pathways via multi-omics profiling and lifestyle factors. We analyzed 279,548 participants free of CKD at baseline and 19,761 patients with established CKD in the UK Biobank. The PsRS integrated 15 factors across economic, educational, healthcare, neighborhood, and social domains. Plasma metabolomic and proteomic profiles were analyzed to identify omics signatures associated with the PsRS. An unhealthy lifestyle score (uHLS) was derived based on body mass index, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, sleep, and diet. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between the PsRS and outcomes. Mediation analyses were performed in subsets with available omics and lifestyle data. Over a median follow-up of 13 years, 6,628 incident CKD cases, 3,724 CVD events, and 2,486 deaths were documented. The PsRS demonstrated a positive association with incident CKD risk among CKD-free participants (per 1-point increase: HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.11-1.14), as well as with CVD (HR=1.08; 95% CI: 1.07-1.10) and all-cause mortality (HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.10-1.14) in CKD patients. The PsRS significantly improved the predictive performance of conventional clinical models across all outcomes, as indicated by increases in the C-index, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Multi-omics analyses revealed a PsRS-associated metabolomic signature (94 metabolites primarily involved in amino acids, fatty acids, and lipoproteins) and a proteomic signature (428 proteins primarily involved in immune/inflammatory responses, cellular signaling, and fibrosis). These omics signatures mediated substantial proportions of the PsRS-outcome associations (metabolomic: 16.64%-27.09%; proteomic: 53.09%-85.21%), as did the uHLS (8.26%-12.51%). In conclusion, the PsRS effectively predicts CKD development and prognosis, largely mediated through metabolomic and proteomic pathways.

Title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches.
RECENT FINDINGS: Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational "digital twins" are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances. Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.

Title: The AGT M235T variant and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system parameters in a predominantly hypertensive elderly black South African cohort: a hypothesis-generating descriptive case series.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension (HTN) is a key cardiovascular risk factor, with its pathogenesis remaining incompletely understood. Blood pressure (BP) regulation involves the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), including the Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), Angiotensin I (Ang I) and Angiotensin II (Ang II). The rs699 variant (M235T) may influence BP via the RAAS.
AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the relationships between the rs699 genotypes, RAAS parameters, BP, Body mass index (BMI) and gender in a black elderly population.
METHODS: Data were collected from 48 participants aged ≥60 years, using World Health Organization (WHO) obesity guidelines and South African Hypertension Society (SAHS) 2019 standards for HTN categories. Statistical analysis was performed using IBM SPSS version 27 and Python 3.14.
RESULTS: Most participants possessed the rs699 variant (GG: 93.8%, AG: 4.2%). ACE levels were low in 64.6%, while Ang II was elevated in the same percentage. The majority were classified as hypertensive and obese. No significant associations were found between the rs699 variant and ACE, Ang I, Ang II, HTN, BMI or gender, though BMI showed sex-related differences in females.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest no significant association of the rs699 variant on RAAS or cardiometabolic parameters within the study population, warranting cautious interpretation. These findings require validation in larger and more diverse populations, as meaningful statistical inferences cannot be drawn from the current data.

Title: Amyloid-targeted PET after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy for cardiac amyloidosis: a systematic review.
Journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
Abstract: To assess myocardial positron emission tomography (PET) positivity after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy, while distinguishing test discordance from independently confirmed cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through 5 August 2026, with targeted source assessment through 2 October 2026. Negative and low-grade imaging denoted Perugini grades 0 and 1, respectively; study-defined negative results were described separately. Eligibility required linked PET and bone-scan results with an extractable denominator. Acquisition modality, PET thresholds and cardiac reference standards were examined. A restricted synthesis required documented tomographic acquisition; a broader three-report synthesis was exploratory. Nine reports provided extractable paired results. In the hereditary transthyretin subgroup examined with carbon-11 Pittsburgh compound B, 20/23 participants were PET-positive after excluding one acquired, domino-transplant case. The exploratory pooled proportion was 87.0% (95% profile-likelihood confidence interval, 68.5-97.8%). Restriction to clearly documented cohort-wide tomography retained only two reports, precluding the planned pooled analysis. Uptake definitions and cardiac verification differed substantially. General diagnostic studies without complete bone-grade denominators, including REVEAL, were excluded from the eligible synthesis and retained as context. PET positivity is common in selected hereditary transthyretin cohorts with negative or low-grade bone scans, but does not establish cardiac amyloidosis or earlier diagnosis. Conditional diagnostic accuracy remains unresolved. Prospective paired studies require tomographic localization, tracer-specific thresholds and independent cardiac verification.

Title: Maternal Anxiety Surrounding Fetal Cardiac Evaluation: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
Abstract: Fetal echocardiography has transformed prenatal cardiac diagnosis, yet the emotional burden of referral and evaluation remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify maternal anxiety before and after fetal cardiac evaluation (FCE), identify clinical predictors of anxiety, and assess whether anxiety changes following evaluation and consultation regardless of outcome. In this prospective cohort study, 117 pregnant women undergoing initial or follow-up FCE completed pre- and post-consultation assessments using a seven-item symptom inventory adapted from the Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SASRQ; score range 7-42). Participants were classified as anxious or non-anxious by direct self-report. Scores were compared with paired t-tests; exploratory multivariable models adjusted for clinical, demographic, and referral covariates, including prior pregnancy loss, psychiatric history, and diagnostic outcome. 80% of participants (94/117) reported anxiety about the FCE before evaluation; prior pregnancy loss was associated with anxious state (p = 0.049). Following FCE and consultation, mean symptom scores in the anxious group fell from 15.07 to 9.03, a 6.04-point (40.1%) reduction (p < 0.001), with reductions across symptom domains regardless of diagnostic outcome. Scores in the non-anxious group did not change significantly (8.48 to 7.87; p = 0.27). Most women referred for FCE report anxiety before evaluation. FCE with consultation was associated with a substantial reduction in anxiety symptoms in these women, irrespective of whether a cardiac abnormality was found. Although the uncontrolled pre-post design cannot establish causation, these findings suggest that diagnostic clarity and expert consultation may themselves be anxiety-reducing and support evaluation of integrated psychosocial care models in fetal cardiology.

Title: The role of extracardiac radiotracer biodistribution in the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis: a retrospective multicenter study on [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP.
Journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone scintigraphy using [99mTc]Tc-DPD or [99mTc]Tc-HMDP is a non-invasive cornerstone for diagnosing transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). However, their interchangeability and the clinical relevance of systemic extracardiac uptake (ExtCU) remain poorly defined.
AIM: To systematically compare the diagnostic performance and whole-body biodistribution profiles of [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP in patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA).
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated a multicenter cohort of patients investigated for suspected CA who underwent late planar whole-body scintigraphy and targeted SPECT/CT with either radiotracer as part of their diagnostic workup. Inclusion required a final, confirmed diagnosis of ATTRwt, ATTRv, or AL amyloidosis. Myocardial visual Perugini score (VISUAL_PS) and systemic ExtCU (pulmonary, appendicular muscular, visceral, and miscellaneous) were recorded.
RESULTS: The study included 224 patients (DPD: n = 109, comprising 70 ATTRwt, 20 ATTRv, 19 AL; HMDP: n = 115, comprising 90 ATTRwt, 13 ATTRv, 12 AL). In ATTRwt, the DPD cohort presented predominantly with Perugini Grade 2 (76%), whereas the HMDP cohort skewed toward Grade 3 (72%, p < 0.001). DPD was significantly associated with appendicular muscular uptake (ATTRwt: 84% vs. 38%, p < 0.001), creating a competitive "soft-tissue sink effect". Conversely, HMDP demonstrated a unique predilection for pulmonary retention (ATTRwt: 68% vs. 46%, p = 0.008; ATTRv: 61% vs. 10%, p = 0.006). Visceral uptake was rare in ATTR but was a robust negative predictor strongly favoring AL amyloidosis (OR 0.016, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP possess distinct biodistribution profiles precluding direct interchangeability. HMDP maximizes myocardial contrast, whereas DPD provides a superior representation of the systemic musculoskeletal amyloid burden. Nuclear medicine physicians must adopt tracer-specific interpretive approaches to optimize non-invasive phenotyping.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: not applicable.

Title: Combined multimodal monitoring during neonatal transition in preterm infants: feasibility, safety and post-implementation evaluation.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: The transitional period involves major cardiovascular adaptations that could affect cerebral perfusion. Combined multimodal monitoring (CMM) may provide a more comprehensive physiological assessment than individual monitoring modalities. We aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of CMM integrating near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG), targeted neonatal echocardiography (TNE), and head ultrasound (HUS) during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and to explore healthcare professionals' perceptions following its implementation. Prospective observational cohort study. Participants underwent continuous NIRS and aEEG monitoring, two TNE assessment and one HUS during the first 72 h of life. Feasibility was defined as acquisition of ≥ 75% of intended NIRS and aEEG recording time, and completion of all imaging studies. Safety outcomes included TNE-related procedural intolerance and NIRS-related skin reactions. Healthcare professionals completed a post-implementation survey assessing acceptability and perceived clinical usefulness. Forty-seven infants were included. Overall CMM feasibility was 78.7%. Individual monitoring completion was 93.6% for NIRS, 95.7% for aEEG, 89.3% for TNE and 100% for HUS. Transient desaturations occurred in 7.9% of 89 TNE assessments, while mild NIRS-related erythema occurred in 11.3% of monitored infants. Healthcare professionals reported favorable perceptions of CMM, particularly regarding clinical relevance and complementarity with standard monitoring.
CONCLUSION: CMM was feasible and well tolerated during the first 72 h of life in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and was perceived favorably by healthcare professionals. Future studies are needed to explore its impact on clinically relevant outcomes.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • The transitional period in preterm infants involves complex cardiovascular and cerebral adaptations associated with an increased risk of brain injury. • Individual monitoring modalities (NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS) provide complementary information on cardiovascular and cerebral physiology but are commonly assessed separately.
WHAT IS NEW: • Structured CMM integrating NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS is feasible and well tolerated during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation. • Healthcare professionals perceive CMM as clinically relevant and complementary to standard monitoring, supporting further evaluation of integrated multimodal assessment in neonatal care.

Title: [Evidence-based treatment of valvular heart disease].
Abstract: Valvular heart disease is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. As the prevalence of most valvular heart diseases increases with age, population ageing has led to a substantial increase in disease burden. Due to advanced age or significant comorbidities, many patients are considered unsuitable for conventional surgery. Whereas medical therapy was therefore often the only treatment option in the past, the rapid evolution of transcatheter interventions has fundamentally transformed the management of valvular heart disease over the past two decades. Today, effective catheter-based treatment options are available for virtually all valvular pathologies. For patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, the prognostic benefit of transcatheter aortic valve replacement is firmly established. Large randomized trials have demonstrated non-inferiority of transcatheter aortic valve replacement compared with surgical aortic valve replacement across most patient populations, leading to an expanding use of this approach in younger and lower-risk patients. Similarly, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral and tricuspid regurgitation has been shown to improve symptoms, quality of life, and heart failure-related hospitalizations. In carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, this strategy also confers a survival benefit. In addition, dedicated transcatheter devices have recently emerged as promising treatment options for native aortic regurgitation. Given the rapid evolution of transcatheter therapies, current efforts are increasingly focused on selecting the optimal treatment strategy for the individual patient and determining the optimal timing of intervention.

Title: Heart Rate Surge Improves Cardiovascular Risk Stratification Beyond Hypoxic Burden in Sleep Apnea.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) imposes cardiovascular stress through intermittent hypoxia and event-related responses. Whether heart rate surge adds prognostic information beyond hypoxic burden (HB) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to evaluate heart rate surge for cardiovascular mortality and its incremental value beyond HB in OSA.
METHODS: We analyzed 4,790 participants from a community-based cohort with overnight polysomnography. Heart rate surge was defined as peak heart rate within the event-aligned window minus mean heart rate during the 60-second pre-event baseline. Associations with cardiovascular mortality were assessed using Cox models. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by C-index, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 11.6 years (IQR: 10.4-12.4), 334/4,790 participants (7.0%) died of cardiovascular causes. Heart rate surge was weakly correlated with HB (Spearman ρ = 0.08; 95% CI: 0.04-0.10). The highest vs lowest heart rate surge quintile was associated with higher cardiovascular mortality risk (HR: 3.00; 95% CI: 2.10-4.30; P < 0.001) and each 1-SD increment was associated with a 27% higher risk (HR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.19-1.35). Participants with elevated HB and heart rate surge had the highest risk (HR: 2.65; 95% CI: 1.79-3.92). Adding heart rate surge increased the C-index from 0.77 (95% CI: 0.74-0.79) to 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.83), with ΔC of 0.04 (95% CI: 0.03-0.06), continuous NRI of 0.62 (95% CI: 0.51-0.74), categorical NRI of 0.16 (95% CI: 0.09-0.24), and integrated discrimination improvement of 0.05 (95% CI: 0.04-0.06).
CONCLUSIONS: Heart rate surge was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality and improved risk stratification beyond HB in OSA.

Title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT.
METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT).
RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients.
CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

Title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia.
RESULTS: A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

Title: Acute Myocardial Infarction in Cancer Patients Treated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium.
OBJECTIVE: To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia.
RESULTS: Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35).
CONCLUSION: Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

Title: Very low HDL cholesterol in infectious mononucleosis with hepatitis: a real-world evidence study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infectious mononucleosis (IM) with hepatitis suppresses HDL cholesterol (HDL-C), but its magnitude, specificity, recovery, and cardiovascular implications are uncharacterised.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence, specificity, recovery, and long-term cardiovascular significance of very low HDL-C in IM hepatitis.
METHODS: In the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (∼190 million patients), we studied 1,944 adults with IM and hepatitis. Presenting HDL-C distributions were compared against 15 propensity-score-matched (PSM) comparator cohorts and characterised by Gaussian mixture modelling; longitudinal trajectory was assessed across six post-index windows. Long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were analysed in PSM cohorts with very low HDL (≤20 mg/dL, n = 979/arm) versus without, over up to 20 years, with independent COVID-19 (n = 83,888/arm) and pharyngitis (n = 10,618/arm) cohorts as external validation. Robustness was tested with E-values. All cross-sectional and survival analyses were repeated in sex-specific PSM cohorts, and pre-illness HDL-C was retrieved for patients with a lipid measurement recorded at least three months before the index illness.
RESULTS: Mean presenting HDL was 36.7±22.6 mg/dL versus 49.7 pre-illness; 23.9% had HDL ≤20 mg/dL. Suppression matched CMV hepatitis but exceeded pharyngitis and IM without hepatitis, indicating a hepatitis-driven mechanism. Mixture modelling identified a discrete suppressed subpopulation (mean 16 mg/dL, 41%) absent in non-hepatitis controls. Across repeated cross-sectional sampling, HDL returned to pre-illness values by 16-30 days in the cohort overall and by 31-90 days in patients presenting ≤20 mg/dL. Patients who suppressed most deeply had pre-illness values ∼10 mg/dL below the rest of the cohort, and referred to their own baseline had recovered fully by 1-3 years. Very low acute HDL predicted higher long-term MACE (HR 1.92-2.47), reproduced in COVID-19 (HR 2.04-2.70) and pharyngitis (HR 1.43-1.69). Women presented with higher HDL-C than men (36.8 vs 31.3 mg/dL; p < 0.001), but the proportion ≤20 mg/dL did not differ by sex (28.3% vs 31.2%; RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.77-1.07), and hazard ratios were similar in women and men for every outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Very low HDL-C is a prevalent, hepatitis-driven finding in IM that identifies a subgroup at elevated long-term cardiovascular risk. However, the acute HDL-C dip is likely a marker of lipid phenotype rather than an independent risk factor, warranting prospective evaluation of cardiovascular follow-up.

Title: Association of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential with cardiovascular mortality in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: a large prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents a progressive pathophysiological continuum. While clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is known to increase the risk of CKM disease onset and adverse prognoses, its overall and stage-specific impacts on cardiovascular mortality within the CKM framework, alongside the circulating proteomic mechanisms mediating this excess risk, remain largely unknown.
METHODS: Participants from the UK Biobank with available CHIP data across the CKM syndrome continuum were included. The primary outcome was cardiovascular mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were utilized to evaluate the incremental risk conferred by CHIP. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted to ascertain result robustness. Within UKB Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP), circulating proteins jointly associated with CHIP and cardiovascular mortality were identified, followed by functional enrichment and mediation analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 16.5 years, 6,515 cardiovascular deaths were recorded among 288,384 participants across CKM stages 1-4. Across all varying CKM stages, individuals harboring Large CHIP exhibited a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular mortality compared to the non-CHIP group (all log-rank P < 0.05). Following multivariable adjustment, Large CHIP emerged as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.24; 95% confidence interval, 1.09-1.40), with subgroup analyses confirming consistent effects regardless of CKM stage or established cardiometabolic and renal diseases. Proteomic profiling, corroborated by UKB-PPP, revealed that the mechanisms driving this excess risk predominantly involve immune-inflammatory dysregulation and tissue structural remodeling. This pathway was highlighted by critical downstream mediators, including the structural component DSC2 (mediating 34.3% of the risk) and key immune-regulatory receptors such as VSIG4 (33.1%) and CD300C (29.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: CHIP is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular mortality across all stages of CKM syndrome. Mechanistically, CHIP exacerbates this adverse outcome primarily by driving systemic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and aberrant tissue remodeling.

Title: Retinal and coronary imaging in type 1 diabetes: links between retinopathy and subclinical cardiovascular disease.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality in individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), despite advances in glycemic management and cardiovascular prevention. Conventional cardiovascular risk assessment may underestimate risk in T1DM, particularly among younger asymptomatic individuals, highlighting the need for markers of early vascular injury. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a microvascular complication of T1DM, is increasingly recognized as a marker of systemic vascular dysfunction rather than an isolated ocular disorder. Non-invasive retinal visualization may provide insight into vascular and atherosclerotic disease. This mini-review summarizes evidence linking DR with subclinical coronary artery disease (CAD) and cardiovascular outcomes in T1DM, focusing on coronary artery calcium (CAC) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Observational and longitudinal studies consistently link DR severity with CAC burden, coronary plaque burden, silent CAD, and cardiovascular outcomes, independent of traditional risk factors. Albuminuria and diabetic kidney disease may provide complementary evidence of a broader microvascular phenotype associated with cardiovascular risk. Advances in retinal imaging, including optical coherence tomography angiography and artificial intelligence-based oculomics, support the role of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular risk prediction. CAC scoring remains valuable for detecting subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, while CCTA characterizes calcified and non-calcified plaque. Emerging evidence suggests that integrating retinal and microvascular markers with coronary imaging may improve identification of asymptomatic individuals at increased cardiovascular risk and support intervention. Although data are observational and prospective validation is required, multimodal strategies combining clinical risk factors, retinal biomarkers, albuminuria, CAC, and CCTA may enhance cardiovascular risk stratification in T1DM.

Title: Chronic Non-Communicable Disease Burden among Recently Arrived Refugees in Syracuse, New York.
Abstract: Background: Refugees resettling in the United States often come from regions with limited healthcare infrastructure. While communicable diseases are routinely screened for, non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including hypertension and diabetes mellitus, remain underrecognized. Lifetime adverse events contributing to chronic stress further increase cardiovascular disease risk in refugees. Objective: To evaluate the chronic disease burden of blood pressure measurements in the hypertensive range and point-of-care capillary glucose values in the prediabetic and diabetic ranges among refugees arriving in Syracuse, New York and to examine how a community-based health screening program informs current U.S. refugee screening practices. Associations between elevated cardiometabolic measures (blood glucose, blood pressure, and heart rate) and demographic and clinical characteristics are explored. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of health screening data collected from recently arrived adult refugees in Syracuse, New York, between May 2023 and March 2025. Health screenings were conducted within the first few months of arrival and were offered to refugees aged 18 and older, with 529 total participants. Findings: Participants were 55.8% female, with 69.8% of participants between 18 and 44 years old. Predominant regions of origin included the Eastern Mediterranean region (39.3%, including Somalia 14.2%, Syria 13.2%), the African region (36.1%, including Democratic Republic of Congo 17.8%), and region of the Americas (12.5%, including Venezuela 7.0%). Elevated heart rate was associated with glucose values in the diabetic range and gender. Glucose values in diabetic range were associated with blood pressure and age. Blood pressure was associated with age, gender, and BMI. Conclusions: Our refugee cohort showed a notable burden of undiagnosed NCDs, including hypertension and hyperglycemia in the prediabetic/diabetic ranges. Statistically significant associations between cardiometabolic risk factors, including increased BMI, age, and gender, with chronic diseases underscore the need for continued interventions to improve access and uptake of preventive health services for refugees.

Title: Inhaled nitric oxide: Expanding indications beyond traditional boundaries.
Abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that improves ventilation-perfusion matching with minimal effect on systemic blood pressure. Although the FDA approval is restricted to neonatal hypoxic respiratory failure associated with pulmonary hypertension, many clinicians now use iNO in adults with conditions where elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular dysfunction threaten stability and hypoxic respiratory failure. This review examines both the mechanistic rationale and the available evidence for such off-label use. Examples range from acute RV failure in the ICU to perioperative support in cardiac surgery, heart and lung transplantation, and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, including COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). In these settings, iNO offers rapid afterload reduction and short-term improvement in oxygenation, but randomized trials are lacking and limited studies to date have failed to consistently show outcome benefits.
