Adverse effects such as methemoglobinemia, nitrogen dioxide toxicity, rebound pulmonary hypertension, and a potential increase in acute kidney injury risk in certain non-cardiac surgical populations. Additionally, cost considerations and other practical limitations must be weighed carefully. Overall, current evidence supports the use of iNO as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected critically ill patients.

Title: Burden of cardiovascular disease in Brazil, 1996-2023: a retrospective descriptive study of the epidemiology and impact on public healthcare.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of death worldwide, and their epidemiology is correlated with genetic predisposition and exposure to risk. Brazil is a developing country with a vast territory, which leads to structural inequalities. We aimed to comprehensively characterise the epidemiology and burden of CVD in Brazil between 1996 and 2023, examining temporal trends, regional disparities, demographic patterns, healthcare costs, and heart transplantation.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective descriptive ecological study using aggregated administrative data from the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), Brazil's publicly funded national health system. Mortality, hospitalization, and heart transplantation data from 1996 to 2023 were analysed according to sex, race/ethnicity, age, and geographic region. We estimated mortality rates for the major CVD, hospital length of stay, healthcare expenditures, and heart transplantation activity.
FINDINGS: Acute myocardial infarction remained the leading cause of cardiovascular mortality throughout the study period, while hypertensive diseases overtook heart failure after 2016 as the second leading cause of death. The overall CVD mortality rate-calculated as the number of CVD-related deaths divided by the total population and expressed as a percentage-increased from 7.3% in 1998 to 8.3% in 2023, peaking at 10.1% in 2021. Marked regional, age-, sex-, and race/ethnicity-related disparities were observed, including the complete absence of heart transplantation in the North region throughout the study period. Although hospitalization rates remained relatively stable, CVD-related healthcare expenditures and heart transplantation activity increased over time.
INTERPRETATION: CVD remains a major and growing public health challenge in Brazil, with substantial regional and demographic inequalities in disease burden and access to specialised care. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health strategies and more equitable allocation of healthcare resources to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.
FUNDING: This study was funded by CNPq, CAPES, FAPEMIG, INCT.

Title: Lipoprotein(a): a potential target for the reduction of residual cardiovascular risk in patients with chronic kidney disease.
Abstract: Epidemiological evidence demonstrates that atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a major cause of death and disability in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). From the early stages of CKD, and in addition to specifically related conditions, the coexistence of traditional risk factors contributes to a process of accelerated atherosclerosis. In patients with CKD, increased cardiovascular risk persists even after correction of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes, indicating a residual risk likely related to additional subtle factors. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an LDL-like particle containing apoB100 covalently linked to apo(a) and is now recognized as a genetically determined risk factor for ASCVD. Following its initial description, Lp(a) aroused extraordinary interest, which then waned in the late-1990s due to the controversial results of some prospective studies and the lack of effective interventions to reduce its circulating levels. Over the past two decades, clinical studies have provided robust evidence supporting the causal and independent contribution of Lp(a) to ASCVD, also suggesting a significant contribution to residual cardiovascular risk. This contribution may be particularly significant in patients with CKD, who exhibit elevated Lp(a) levels from the earliest stages of disease. The recent development of potent Lp(a)-lowering drugs offers an exciting opportunity to effectively address residual risk in the general population and in patients with CKD. No data are yet available on their use in patients with CKD but pending future definition of their efficacy on cardiovascular outcomes, approval, dosing, and long-term safety, these drugs might possibly represent a useful tool for cardiovascular prevention in these patients.

Title: A standardized ECPR activation protocol and resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load: a retrospective multicenter study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load associated with implementation of a standardized extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) activation protocol.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter observational study included 103 consecutive patients with in-hospital cardiac arrest who underwent ECPR at three tertiary hospitals in Guangdong Province, China. The control group included 30 patients treated from September 2019 to December 2023, and the post-implementation group included 73 patients treated from January 2024 to December 2025. Outcomes included resuscitation-process measures, clinical outcomes, and perceived nursing workload assessed using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), a multidimensional measure of perceived workload.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the post-implementation group had shorter ECPR preparation time (2.87 ± 2.32 vs. 8.60 ± 1.34 min), ECMO priming time (14.83 ± 2.88 vs. 19.07 ± 1.18 min), and ECMO initiation time (35.01 ± 2.36 vs. 54.12 ± 3.55 min), and a higher one-time readiness rate of disposable supplies (100% vs. 50.0%; all P < 0.001). The total NASA-TLX score was lower after implementation (415 ± 26 vs. 452 ± 25, P < 0.001). Thirty-day survival was numerically higher in the post-implementation group but did not differ statistically (42.5% vs. 23.3%; crude OR 2.43, 95% CI 0.92-6.37; P = 0.069). Favorable neurological outcome at discharge was more frequent after implementation (30.1% vs. 10.0%; crude OR 3.88, 95% CI 1.07-14.15; P = 0.036), and the association persisted after adjustment for SAVE score and time-to-ECPR-decision (adjusted OR 3.79, 95% CI 1.02-14.08; P = 0.047).
CONCLUSION: Implementation of the standardized ECPR activation protocol was associated with shorter ECPR preparation, priming, and initiation times, lower perceived nursing workload, and higher odds of favorable neurological outcome at discharge. Thirty-day survival was numerically higher but did not differ statistically. Given the retrospective pre-post design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

Title: The Obesity Paradox in Chronic Kidney Disease: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Is Associated With Mortality Independent of Body Mass Index.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: The obesity paradox, in which a higher body mass index (BMI) is associated with better survival, has been observed in chronic disease populations. However, the interaction between BMI, cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), and mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains incompletely understood. We examined the association between BMI, age-adjusted CRF, and all-cause mortality in a large CKD cohort.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: 13,521 predominantly male US veterans (97.4% male) with CKD from the Exercise Testing and Health Outcomes Study within the Veterans Affairs health care system.
PREDICTORS: BMI categories (normal weight <25.0, overweight 25.0-29.9, and obese ≥30.0 kg/m2) and age-adjusted CRF quartiles based on metabolic equivalents achieved during maximal exercise tolerance testing using the Bruce protocol. The index date was the date of exercise testing.
OUTCOME: All-cause mortality.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease assessed mortality risk across BMI-fitness combinations, with normal BMI and least fit as references.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up period of 7.4 years, 5,144 (38.0%) deaths occurred. A higher BMI was associated with a lower mortality risk: overweight (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.95) and obese (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.61-0.82) versus normal BMI. Higher CRF was associated with progressively lower mortality: moderate fit (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.50-0.74) and most fit (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.40-0.60) versus least fit. The combination of obese BMI and highest fitness was associated with a 64% lower mortality risk (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.25-0.51).
LIMITATIONS: Predominantly male veteran population; single baseline BMI and fitness measurements; observational design precludes causal inference.
CONCLUSIONS: In this predominantly male veteran CKD cohort, a higher BMI was associated with lower all-cause mortality across all fitness levels. Age-adjusted CRF demonstrated a strong, graded inverse association with mortality independent of BMI. These observational findings support integrating fitness assessment into CKD management.

Title: Enhancing Inpatient Echocardiogram Request Appropriateness and Timeliness Using British Society of Echocardiography Guidelines: A Quality Improvement Project.
Abstract: Introduction Inpatient echocardiography is an important component of cardiovascular assessment, but inappropriate requests and inadequate clinical information may complicate prioritisation and delay diagnostic imaging. This quality improvement project aimed to improve the appropriateness of inpatient echocardiography requests in accordance with British Society of Echocardiography (BSE) guidance and to improve the timeliness of echocardiogram completion. Methodology This was an uncontrolled before-and-after quality improvement study conducted at Colchester Hospital, England, using two measurement points. The baseline audit covered 15-24 March 2025, and the reaudit covered 6-15 June 2025. The latest 100 eligible inpatient echocardiography requests from each period were reviewed using a pragmatic sampling approach. Pre-operative and peri-operative requests and requests relating to patients who had been discharged before audit assessment were excluded. The intervention, delivered between April and May 2025, comprised clinician education, dissemination of BSE guidance and baseline findings by email, educational posters, and teaching sessions. Appropriateness was assessed against BSE recommendations by a single cardiology consultant blinded to the audit period. Time to completion was measured from the recorded request timestamp to echocardiographic image acquisition. Results Appropriate requests increased from 82/100 (82%) at baseline to 90/100 (90%) at reaudit, an absolute change of 8 percentage points (95% CI -1.7 to +17.8; Fisher's exact p=0.153). Completion within 24 hours changed from 77/100 (77%) to 79/100 (79%), an absolute change of 2 percentage points (95% CI -9.5 to +13.4; Fisher's exact p=0.865). The median time to completion was 14.8 hours (IQR 5.6-21.4) at baseline and 17.5 hours (IQR 3.3-23.4) at reaudit. Retrospective BSE urgency adjudication classified 71/100 (71%) baseline and 77/100 (77%) reaudit requests as urgent. Among urgent requests, 55/71 (77.5%) at baseline and 59/77 (76.6%) at reaudit were completed within 24 hours. Conclusion Following the implementation of a guideline-based educational intervention, an increase in request appropriateness was observed, while overall completion within 24 hours changed only modestly. The findings support continued use of guideline-based education and iterative audit while highlighting the need to evaluate service-level and process measures when assessing echocardiography timeliness.

Title: Metabolic syndrome in stable long-term antipsychotic monotherapy and polypharmacy among patients with schizophrenia: a real-world comparative study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome is a major contributor to premature cardiovascular morbidity and mortality among people with schizophrenia. Antipsychotic polypharmacy is common, but its independent metabolic burden remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To compare metabolic syndrome in patients receiving stable long-term antipsychotic monotherapy or polypharmacy and to examine high metabolic-risk exposure, chlorpromazine-equivalent dose, and long-acting injectable (LAI) use.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 370 adults with schizophrenia spectrum disorders receiving an unchanged antipsychotic regimen for at least five years at a community mental health center. Patients received monotherapy (n=144) or polypharmacy (n=226). Metabolic syndrome was defined using International Diabetes Federation criteria. Antipsychotic dose was standardized to chlorpromazine equivalents, and multivariable logistic regression was used.
RESULTS: Metabolic syndrome was present in 143 patients (38.6%) and was numerically more frequent with polypharmacy than monotherapy (41.2% vs. 34.7%, p=0.216). LAI use (67.3% vs. 37.5%, p<0.001) and median chlorpromazine-equivalent dose (1010.0 vs. 454.5 mg/day, p<0.001) were higher with polypharmacy. However, neither LAI use (adjusted OR = 1.220, 95% CI 0.767-1.941, p=0.401) nor chlorpromazine-equivalent dose per 100 mg/day (adjusted OR = 1.003, 95% CI 0.954-1.055, p=0.899) was independently associated with metabolic syndrome. Current smoking remained associated with metabolic syndrome (adjusted OR = 1.996, 95% CI 1.251-3.185, p=0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort with stable long-term treatment, polypharmacy was associated with greater dose and LAI exposure, but independent associations of treatment modality, current dose, LAI use, or olanzapine/clozapine exposure with metabolic syndrome were not detected. Comprehensive cardiometabolic monitoring and smoking cessation remain priorities.

Title: Cardiovascular Autonomic Function and HRV in Healthy Adults of Rajasthan: A Cross-sectional Study on the Influence of Age and Gender.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart rate variability (HRV) and cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests (CARTs) serve as non-invasive clinical indicators of central autonomic network function and cardiovagal regulation.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to establish regional normative reference values for HRV and CART parameters in healthy adults from northwestern India to evaluate the modulating effects of age, biological sex and subclinical cardiometabolic risk factors.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study evaluated 142 healthy subjects (74 males, 68 females) aged 18-70 years. Baseline vital signs and time-domain HRV parameters (standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN) and root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD)) were recorded. Autonomic reactivity was assessed using deep breathing (expiration-to-inspiration (E:I) ratio), the Valsalva manoeuvre, isometric handgrip and orthostatic challenge. A high-risk sub-cohort (n = 21) with subclinical obesity or elevated blood pressure was analysed. Adherence to Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines was maintained.
RESULTS: The total study sample comprised 142 participants, including 74 males (52.1%) and 68 females (47.9%). The high-risk subset comprised 11 males (52.4%) and 10 females (47.6%). Resting heart rate was higher in females (74.6 ± 8.2 bpm) than in males (70.1 ± 7.6 bpm; t(140) = 3.39, p = .02), while blood pressure was higher in males (p = .03). Time-domain HRV and reflex indices declined significantly with age (p < .001), with optimal thresholds for autonomic senescence occurring at 47 years (SDNN, area under the curve (AUC) = 0.82) and 49 years (Valsalva, AUC = 0.79). Healthy females exhibited enhanced cardiovagal responses (E:I, Valsalva and 30:15 ratios; p < .05). This female autonomic advantage was entirely blunted in the high-risk subset (n = 21), where autonomic parameters fell below the 5th percentile limits (SDNN = 25 ms, RMSSD = 18 ms, Valsalva ratio = 1.09).
CONCLUSION: Healthy adults exhibit an age-related decline in parasympathetic function and a female-specific cardiovagal advantage. Subclinical cardiometabolic risk factors override these physiological buffers, blunting gender-related protection and accelerating autonomic senescence.

Title: Use of intraoperative right ventricular strain as a predictor of outcomes in adult heart transplant patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricle (RV) evaluation in the perioperative period is challenging for anesthesiologists, given the limited objective assessment methods available for transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Speckle-tracking strain imaging may offer a more objective evaluation of RV function. This study evaluated the predictive value of intraoperative RV free wall strain (RVFWS) for early outcomes following orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT).
METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of 147 adults who underwent isolated OHT between January 2025 and December 2025. Patients with multiorgan transplant, congenital cases, and those without measurable intraoperative RVFWS were excluded. Post-bypass RVFWS was measured using TEE at a single time point with speckle-tracking analysis. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included severe primary graft dysfunction, 30-day mortality, need for postoperative venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), vasoactive-inotropic score, and cardiac index at 24 and 72 h, and intensive care unit length of stay. Multivariable Firth-penalized logistic and median quantile regressions were used, adjusted for a priori pre-transplant weighted risk score.
RESULTS: The median post-bypass RVFWS was -13.9% IQR (interquartile range) -19.3 to -9.6. Fourteen recipients (9.5%) died within 90 days of transplantation. After adjusting for the pre-transplant risk score, RVFWS was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality [odds ratio (OR) 2.84 per 5% decrease in magnitude, 95% confidence interval 1.65-5.58; p < 0.001]. Among the secondary outcomes, the associations with severe primary graft dysfunction (OR 2.70; raw p = 0.001), CRRT (OR 1.58; raw p = 0.001), and 30-day mortality (OR 2.94; raw p = 0.002) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni adjustment for eleven secondary comparisons (adjusted p = 0.011, 0.011, and 0.022, respectively). RVFWS demonstrated higher discrimination for 90-day mortality [area under the curve (AUC) 0.83] than qualitative intraoperative RV grading (AUC 0.68), although this difference in AUC did not reach statistical significance. RVFWS retained independent prognostic value in a combined model.
CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative post-bypass RVFWS is a feasible and objective intraoperative measure that is independently associated with early adverse outcomes after adult OHT. RVFWS shows promise as a signal of early allograft dysfunction that is not fully explained by pre-transplant risk factors.

Title: Potential role of platelet-derived growth factor D in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk.
Abstract: A considerable residual cardiovascular risk persists despite contemporary therapies, highlighting the urgent need to identify potential targets for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) onset and progression. Accumulating evidence suggests that platelet-derived growth factor D (PDGFD) may be involved in the development of ASCVD. Herein, we leveraged 20-year longitudinal data from the Chinese Multi-provincial Cohort Study-Proteomics Project, with up to four repeated PDGFD measurements per participant, to estimate the serum PDGFD-ASCVD association. We then emulated the effectiveness of hypothetical reductions in PDGFD serum levels on ASCVD prevention. Our findings suggest that elevated circulating PDGFD levels are associated with higher ASCVD risk and that hypothetical PDGFD-lowering strategies may be associated with reduced long-term ASCVD risk, with an estimated absolute risk reduction of up to approximately 9% under the most intensive intervention scenario. We anticipate that these findings may motivate further investigation of PDGFD-lowering strategies as a potential approach for ASCVD risk reduction.

Title: Comparison of virtual and true ECG-gated coronary CT angiography in patients with acute chest pain: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the clinical value of true electrocardiogram-gated and virtual electrocardiogram-gated coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), and to provide a reasonable and effective imaging strategy for patients with acute chest pain.
METHODS: A total of 254 patients with acute chest pain and suspected coronary artery disease who underwent CCTA were prospectively enrolled. Patients were alternately assigned according to examination date to the virtual ECG-gated group (n = 126), or the true ECG-gated group (n = 128). Examination time and radiation dose were recorded. Objectiveand subjective image quality parameters were evaluated. Objective parameters included image background noise, CT values of the aorta and coronary artery branches, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). Subjective image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale. In patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography (ICA) within 30 days after CCTA, diagnostic agreement was evaluated using ICA as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was assessed at the vessel level using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, with the four major coronary arteries from each patient considered as the units of analysis.
RESULTS: (1) The virtual ECG-gated group demonstrated significantly improved examination efficiency compared with the true ECG-gated group, with a shorter total examination time (2.83 ± 0.37 min vs. 4.15 ± 0.49 min, P < 0.001) and positioning time (0.89 ± 0.26 min vs. 2.03 ± 0.35 min, P < 0.001). However, the radiation dose was higher in the virtual ECG-gated group than in the true ECG-gated group (3.58 ± 0.69 mSv vs. 3.18 ± 0.54 mSv, P < 0.001). (2) Image quality analysis showed that the virtual ECG-gated group had lower image noise than the true ECG-gated group, as well as higher SNR and CNR values for the aorta and coronary artery branches (all P < 0.001). However, CT values and subjective image quality scores were comparable between the two groups (all P > 0.05). (3) In the ICA-validated subgroup, the virtual ECG-gated group showed a higher diagnostic agreement rate than the true ECG-gated group (92.00% vs. 85.58%), with corresponding vessel-level AUC values of 0.89 and 0.82, respectively. However, the virtual ECG-gated group was associated with a higher radiation dose than the true ECG-gated group (3.58 ± 0.69 mSv vs. 3.18 ± 0.54 mSv), representing a trade-off for achieving an ECG-independent acquisition strategy and maintaining diagnostic image quality.
CONCLUSION: Virtual ECG-gated CCTA can significantly improve examination efficiency while maintaining comparable image quality and diagnostic performance to true ECG-gated CCTA. Although this approach was associated with a modest increase in radiation dose, this represents a trade-off for reducing dependence on real-time ECG acquisition and simplifying the CCTA workflow. Therefore, virtual ECG-gated CCTA may serve as a feasible and efficient imaging strategy for selected patients with acute chest pain, particularly in clinical scenarios requiring rapid evaluation or simplified workflow.

Title: Ventricular arrhythmic burden before and after mitral valve repair in mitral valve prolapse: the role of mitral annular disjunction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is increasingly recognized as an arrhythmogenic condition, with a subset of patients exhibiting ventricular arrhythmias beyond the hemodynamic effects of mitral regurgitation (MR). Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been proposed as a structural marker associated with arrhythmic risk, but its relationship with postoperative ventricular arrhythmias after mitral valve repair remains incompletely understood. We aimed to evaluate changes in ventricular arrhythmic burden following mitral valve repair and to investigate the association between preoperative MAD and postoperative ventricular ectopy.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 77 patients with MVP who underwent surgical mitral valve repair for severe MR and had both preoperative and postoperative 24-h Holter recordings. Premature ventricular complex (PVC) burden and ventricular arrhythmias were assessed before and after surgery. MAD was evaluated retrospectively using transthoracic echocardiography. Multivariable linear regression, sensitivity analyses, and sequential model comparison were performed to evaluate the independent and incremental association of MAD with postoperative PVC burden.
RESULTS: Overall PVC burden decreased significantly after mitral valve repair. Patients with preoperative MAD had a substantially higher PVC burden both before surgery [7,800 (7,000-9,575) vs. 4,200 (3,200-6,200) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] and after surgery [5,700 (5,175-6,425) vs. 2,200 (1,800-3,500) PVCs/24 h, p < 0.001] than those without MAD. The relative reduction in PVC burden was comparable between groups (-35.4 ± 20.6% vs. -39.5 ± 29.5%, p = 0.113). In multivariable analysis, preoperative MAD remained independently associated with higher postoperative PVC burden after adjustment for clinical covariates, prolapse phenotype, residual mitral regurgitation, and baseline PVC burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Mitral valve repair was associated with a significant reduction in ventricular ectopic burden in patients with MVP. However, preoperative MAD identified patients with a higher postoperative ventricular ectopic burden despite a similar proportional reduction in PVCs. These findings support the potential value of postoperative rhythm surveillance in patients with preoperative MAD.

Title: Postoperative platelet dynamic trajectories in patients with type A aortic dissection and development of a predictive model for thrombocytopenia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombocytopenia is common after cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, platelet counts are typically assessed at single time points, and longitudinal platelet trajectories after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) surgery remain poorly characterized. This study used trajectory analysis to identify perioperative platelet count trajectories in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery.
METHODS: We retrospectively included 773 patients who underwent surgery for Stanford type A aortic dissection in this study. Platelet count data were collected over time within the first seven days after surgery. Trajectory patterns of platelet counts were determined using growth mixture modeling (GMM). The Kaplan-Meier method and log-rank test were applied to compare intergroup survival differences, and Cox regression analysis was performed to estimate mortality risks and stratify patient phenotypes. With trajectory phenotype as the outcome, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection, followed by the construction of a logistic regression predictive model.
RESULTS: GMM identified three distinct nonlinear postoperative platelet trajectories, designated as TrajeA, TrajeB, and TrajeC. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated significant differences in both early (postoperative days 7-30) and long-term survival among trajectory groups (log-rank P < 0.001). TrajeC was associated with the highest mortality risk. Five clinical variables, namely age, preoperative creatinine, total transfusion volume, end-stage renal disease, and operative duration, were ultimately incorporated into the final logistic regression model. The model achieved an AUC of 0.73 (95% CI: 0.69-0.78) in the training cohort and 0.69 (95% CI: 0.61-0.76) in the validation cohort, demonstrating moderate, stable discriminative performance and no apparent overfitting.
CONCLUSIONS: A persistently low postoperative platelet trajectory is associated with elevated short- and long-term mortality in patients undergoing acute type A aortic dissection surgery.

Title: Trajectories of kinesiophobia over the first six months after cardiac pacemaker or defibrillator implantation: clinical, psychological, and rehabilitation predictors and their relation to functional capacity.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Kinesiophobia, an excessive fear of physical movement, is common after implantation of a cardiac pacemaker or implantable cardioverter defibrillator and may limit rehabilitation and recovery. Because fear of movement changes over time, a single measurement cannot capture how it evolves. We aimed to identify distinct trajectories of kinesiophobia during the first six months after implantation, to relate them to functional capacity, and to identify baseline factors that predict an unfavourable course.
METHODS: In a single centre retrospective cohort based on routinely collected structured follow-up data, 160 consecutive patients undergoing first implantation of a pacemaker or defibrillator were assessed 24 to 48 h after the procedure and again at 1, 3, and 6 months. Kinesiophobia was measured with the Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia Heart and functional capacity with the six-minute walk distance. Group-based trajectory modelling identified latent trajectories. Baseline characteristics were compared across classes, and multinomial logistic regression identified independent predictors of class membership.
RESULTS: Mean kinesiophobia fell from 42.9 to 35.2 over six months, and the proportion above the high-fear threshold fell from 76.2% to 37.5%. Three trajectories emerged: low and declining (28.8%), moderate and declining (45.0%), and high and persistent (26.2%). The persistent group stayed above the clinical threshold throughout and walked the shortest distance at every visit. Compared with the low group, independent predictors of a persistent course were higher depression (odds ratio 2.26), higher anxiety (1.68), lower exercise self-efficacy (0.89), shorter baseline walk distance (0.55 per 10 m), and absence of exercise guidance (0.04 for having received guidance).
CONCLUSION: Kinesiophobia after device implantation follows three trajectories, separated mainly by the overall level of fear. About one quarter of patients remain persistently fearful and physically limited; they can be identified early by distress, low self-efficacy, poor functional capacity, and lack of exercise guidance. Early screening and targeted exercise-based rehabilitation are warranted.

Title: Hybrid surgical thromboembolectomy and crossover endovascular revascularization for acute lower-limb ischemia in a patient with active ovarian cancer receiving a PARP inhibitor (fuzuloparib): a case report and literature review.
Abstract: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is both limb- and life-threatening, and represents a vascular emergency. Malignancy produces a systemic hypercoagulable state that predisposes to arterial as well as venous thrombosis, and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors-now central to maintenance therapy in ovarian cancer-have, in aggregate randomized data, been associated with only a borderline venous signal and no clearly demonstrated independent arterial signal. We report a 60-year-old woman with active high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma maintained on oral fuzuloparib who presented with Rutherford category IIa ALI of the right lower limb on a background of chronic bilateral atherosclerosis. Angiography demonstrated occlusion of the right common iliac-external iliac-common femoral-proximal superficial femoral segment with collateral reconstitution and, after dedicated cardiac evaluation (regular sinus rhythm on ECG, no arrhythmia on perioperative telemetry, normal transthoracic echocardiography without intracardiac thrombus or vegetation, and no critical carotid stenosis), no identifiable cardioembolic source. A single-stage hybrid procedure-open common femoral thromboembolectomy followed by contralateral (crossover) endovascular treatment of a residual flow-limiting dissection with overlapping self-expanding and balloon-expandable covered stents-restored inline flow and salvaged the limb; the retrieved material was submitted for histopathology, which demonstrated bland fibrin-platelet-red-cell thrombus with lines of Zahn and negative AE1/AE3 immunostaining, excluding tumour embolism. The patient was transitioned to therapeutic anticoagulation within a multidisciplinary framework, and at 3 months the limb remained viable with palpable distal pulses. This case illustrates cancer-associated arterial thrombosis superimposed on atherosclerosis-on a background that also included PARP-inhibitor exposure, whose independent contribution remains speculative-highlights a hybrid open-endovascular strategy for definitive single-setting revascularization, and underscores the importance of excluding a cardioembolic source and confirming thrombus nature histologically, while individualizing long-term anticoagulation that is necessarily extrapolated from cancer-associated venous thromboembolism evidence, with attention to drug-drug interactions, thrombocytopenia and bleeding risk.

Title: DNA methylation analysis of aortic wall tissue in ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection.
Abstract: Ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection are life-threatening cardiovascular conditions. However, the epigenetic regulatory mechanisms within aortic cells underlying these pathologies remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated genes (DMGs) in aortic tissues from patients with ascending aortic dilatation/aneurysm and dissection by performing a re-analysis of publicly available DNA methylation datasets. A re-analysis was conducted on three DNA methylation datasets (GSE50192, GSE202047, GSE84274) from the Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip. To account for tissue heterogeneity, cellular deconvolution was performed using the HEpiDISH algorithm and a custom reference panel of cell-type-specific CpG sites for key vascular cell types (endothelial cells, fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells, immune cells). Our re-analysis revealed that aortic dissection and bicuspid aortic valve patients with aortic dilatation/aneurysm exhibit distinct DNA methylation profiles compared to intact aorta. These pathologies differ from each other in the number and the spectrum of DMGs. The adjustment for cellular heterogeneity eliminated the majority of the initially identified DMGs. However, this correction helped to make an assessment of vascular inflammation, characterize its impact on aortic wall stability, and identify genes with differential DNA methylation associated with the disease phenotypes, rather than with inter-group heterogeneity. The genes NFIX, PCDH7, MED13L, LMO4, DIP2C, PLEKHF1, NKD1, C10orf41 (ZNF503-AS2), ARAP2, TBX3, and TBX5, which remained in the DMG status after adjustment for cellular composition and are expressed in individual cells/whole aortic tissue, can be considered as new candidate genes for the development of aortic dilatation/aneurysm in patients with bicuspid aortic valve. NFIX, LMO4, DIP2C, C10orf41 (ZNF503- AS2), MED13L, TBX3, TBX5 are transcriptional regulators or modulators; NKD1 is a recognized inhibitor of the Wnt pathway. Our findings highlight the necessity of a rigorous approach to cohort design, which includes comprehensive phenotyping (encompassing aortic valve morphology) and underscore the importance of future single-cell investigations.

Title: Prognostic value of absolute global longitudinal strain for chemotherapy-related cardiac dysfunction in breast cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the general predictive effect of absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) in predicting chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity (CTRCD) for breast cancer patients.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted on the PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang and VIP databases to identify cohort studies published up to May 31, 2026, on the application of GLS for predicting CTRCD in breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy. Two researchers independently carried out the article filtering, data collection and quality assessment. RevMan 5.4 and Stata 18.0 software were used for meta-analysis; the size of the general effect was presented as an odds ratio (OR), and a hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curve was constructed to assess diagnostic accuracy. Subgroup analysis and meta-regression were used to identify the sources of heterogeneity; sensitivity analysis was conducted by a stepwise exclusion strategy; and a funnel plot was employed to examine publication bias.
RESULT: 12 papers included data from 955 breast cancer patients. A meta-analysis indicated that the odds of being affected by CTRCD were significantly higher in the low-GLS group (absolute drop in GLS) compared with the high-GLS group (OR = 11.88, 95% CI: 7.88-17.92, P<0.00001), and there was low heterogeneity across trials (I2 = 18%, P = 0.26). The area under the HSROC curve (AUC) was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.89), and the combined sensitivity and combined specificity were 83.0% and 73.0% (95% CI: 75.4%-88.6%, 95% CI: 65.1%-79.6%), respectively. Subgroup analysis and meta-regression showed that research type, breast cancer subtype and the CTRCD definition were not significant sources of heterogeneity (all P>0.05). Exclusion of one study at a time in sensitivity analysis did not change the combined results. The funnel plot was symmetrical, and therefore publication bias is likely not present.
CONCLUSION: the absolute GLS value can be used as a good prognostic index for chemotherapy-induced CTRCD in breast cancer patients, and a lower absolute GLS is associated with a significantly increased risk of CTRCD. An index has been developed to determine the risk of damage to the heart muscle after chemotherapy in breast cancer at a specific time, and scientific support will be provided for treatment decisions.

Title: Associations of insulin resistance-related metabolic indices with albuminuria in primary hypertension without diabetes: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance-related metabolic indices have been associated with albuminuria in general populations and in patients with diabetes, but evidence in patients with primary hypertension without diabetes remains limited. Whether mean arterial pressure (MAP) statistically accounts for part of these associations is unclear.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed cross-sectional data from 509 hospitalised cardiology patients with primary hypertension without diabetes at a single tertiary centre who underwent urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) testing. Albuminuria was defined as a UACR ≥30 mg/g. Associations of the triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI), metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR), and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index with albuminuria and log10-transformed UACR were examined using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed the shape of the associations. Supplementary logistic models additionally adjusted for MAP, and exploratory indirect-effect analyses assessed statistical indirect components involving MAP.
RESULTS: Among the 509 participants, 99 (19.4%) had albuminuria. After multivariable adjustment, the odds ratios (ORs) for albuminuria per 1-SD increment in TyG-BMI, METS-IR, and the TyG index were 1.610 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.262-2.055], 1.557 (95% CI, 1.215-1.995), and 1.436 (95% CI, 1.128-1.829), respectively. Corresponding Q4-vs.-Q1 ORs were 2.464 (95% CI, 1.228-4.943), 2.665 (95% CI, 1.268-5.600), and 2.137 (95% CI, 1.092-4.181), with overall categorical P-values of 0.018, 0.059, and 0.099, respectively. RCS analyses showed significant overall associations for all three indices, with no statistical evidence of departure from linearity. All three indices were positively associated with log10-transformed UACR. After additional MAP adjustment, the continuous associations with albuminuria were attenuated but remained statistically significant for all three indices, whereas the overall tests across quartiles were not statistically significant for any of the three indices. Exploratory analyses suggested statistical indirect components involving MAP for TyG-BMI and METS-IR, but not for the TyG index.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher TyG-BMI, METS-IR, and TyG index values were associated with albuminuria and higher UACR in patients with primary hypertension without diabetes. Exploratory analyses suggested statistical indirect components involving MAP for TyG-BMI and METS-IR, but did not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

Title: Higher fibrosis-4 index is associated with 2-year cardiovascular events in Vietnamese adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is a major extrahepatic outcome in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and metabolic fatty liver disease, but prospective data integrating transient elastography and the fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) with observed cardiovascular events remain limited in Southeast Asia.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of adults with T2DM consecutively recruited at a Vietnamese tertiary hospital from June 2023 through January 2025 and followed for up to 24 months. Hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness were assessed by FibroScan©, and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) was defined using the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver framework. Expanded major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were the principal time-to-event outcome. Sparse-event associations were estimated with Firth-penalized Cox regression.
RESULTS: Of 452 patients screened, 301 consented and 284 entered the baseline cohort; 280 contributed follow-up. At baseline, MAFLD was present in 72.5% and significant liver fibrosis (liver stiffness measurement ≥7.0 kPa) in 23.9%. During 544.92 person-years, 11 expanded MACE and 5 conventional MACE occurred, corresponding to incidence rates of 20.19 (95% CI 10.08-36.12) and 9.18 (95% CI 2.98-21.41) per 1,000 person-years. In the main Firth model adjusted for age and MAFLD, each increase of 1 interquartile range (IQR; 0.696 units) in FIB-4 was associated with expanded MACE (adjusted hazard ratio 1.56, 95% CI 1.09-1.99; p = 0.022), whereas MAFLD was not statistically significant (adjusted hazard ratio 3.51, 95% CI 0.79-33.09; p = 0.105); the point estimate was above unity but imprecise because of the limited number of events.
CONCLUSION: Higher FIB-4 was associated with short-term cardiovascular events in adults with T2DM. Given the small number of events, these findings require confirmation in larger multicenter cohorts.

Title: Antiplatelet therapy for primary prevention of stroke in patients with carotid web: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid webs have emerged as an etiology for ischemic stroke in younger patients, with a high recurrence rate. However, the optimal prevention strategy for asymptomatic carotid webs remains uncertain.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University between June 2017 and June 2022, including patients diagnosed with asymptomatic carotid webs via CT angiography (CTA), to evaluate the efficacy of antiplatelet therapy as primary prevention of stroke. The primary outcome was the incidence of ischemic stroke. Patients receiving oral anticoagulants or with other etiologies for stroke were excluded. Cox regression with Firth's penalized maximum likelihood method was used to evaluate the association between antiplatelet therapy and stroke. Propensity scores were applied in sensitive analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 105 patients (median age, 61 years; range, 19-80 years), including 53 (50.5%) male patients, were included. Altogether 31 patients received single antiplatelet therapy. During a median follow-up of 31 months (range from 9 to 89 months), ischemic stroke occurred in 3 of 31 patients (incidence rate, 3.51 per 100 person-years, 95% CI = 0.72-10.25) in the antiplatelet group and 10 of 74 patients (5.16 per 100 person-years, 95% CI = 2.18-9.50) in the non-antiplatelet group. The estimated association favored antiplatelet therapy but was imprecise (HR = 0.755, 95% CI = 0.215-2.653, p = 0.642). Similar results were observed after adjustment for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk and concurrent stenosis, as well as in propensity score-adjusted analyses. Subgroup analysis of patients without high ASCVD risk demonstrated no significant association between antiplatelet therapy and stroke (HR = 0.671, 95% CI = 0.108-4.191, p = 0.638).
CONCLUSION: In this prospective cohort, stroke incidence was numerically lower with single antiplatelet therapy, but estimates were imprecise and compatible with both benefit and harm.

Title: A machine learning-driven and explainable prediction model for in-hospital mortality in patients with diabetes mellitus and congestive heart failure: integrating XGBoost and SHAP approaches.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with congestive heart failure (CHF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at elevated risk of in-hospital mortality, particularly in intensive care units (ICUs). Conventional scoring systems may not fully capture the clinical complexity of such comorbidities. This study aimed to construct an interpretable machine learning model to predict in-hospital mortality in this high-risk group.
METHODS: A retrospective study included 573 ICU patients with CHF and T2DM admitted to three hospitals in Henan, China (Jan 2025-Jun 2026). Seven predictors-body mass index (BMI), myocardial infarction, mild liver disease, SOFA score, LODS score, white blood cell (WBC) count, and serum creatinine-were identified via stepwise logistic regression. XGBoost and four other machine learning algorithms (KNN, SVM, CatBoost, AdaBoost) were trained and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was used to interpret XGBoost predictions.
RESULTS: XGBoost achieved the best performance (AUC 0.917, sensitivity 86.8%, specificity 96.6%, accuracy 74.8%). SHAP analysis indicated that mild liver disease, LODS score, BMI, WBC count, and SOFA score were the top contributors, jointly explaining over 77% of the predictive power. Myocardial infarction, liver disease, elevated WBC, and higher SOFA/LODS scores increased mortality risk, while higher BMI and serum creatinine were protective-supporting the obesity paradox and sarcopenia hypothesis.
CONCLUSION: An XGBoost model with SHAP interpretation provides accurate, explainable prediction of in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with CHF and T2DM, offering a valuable tool for early risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

Title: Linking liver fibrosis to cardiac structure, function, and heart disease: a community-based fibrosis-4 index study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) is a non-invasive tool used to assess advanced liver fibrosis. Although liver fibrosis has been linked to heart disease, its relationship with cardiac structure and function remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined associations of FIB-4 with incident heart disease and cardiac morpho-functional phenotypes and explored whether cardiac phenotypes statistically accounted for part of the association.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study using the UK Biobank, 416,001 participants without known heart or liver disease at baseline (mean age 56.15 ± 8.09 years; 55.78% female) were followed for up to 17 years. FIB-4, calculated from age, AST, ALT, and platelet count, was analyzed continuously and using a high-risk threshold of >2.67. Incident coronary heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias (CA), and heart failure (HF) were identified from linked records. A subset of 33,927 participants underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging a median of 10.20 years after baseline.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 14.61 years, 57,207 participants (13.75%) developed heart disease. Higher FIB-4 was associated with CA (HR = 1.32, 95% CI 1.24-1.41), HF (HR = 1.29, 95% CI 1.14-1.47), greater LV mass (β=0.014, 95% CI 0.0003-0.027), chamber dilation, reduced atrial ejection fractions, and LV remodeling. Exploratory pathway analysis indicated that LA ejection fraction statistically accounted for 36.38% of the FIB-4-CA/HF association; causal mediation cannot be inferred.
CONCLUSION: Elevated FIB-4 was associated with incident CA and HF and with adverse CMR phenotypes. Exploratory pathway results were consistent with indirect pathways through cardiac remodeling, but the observational design and single CMR assessment preclude causal or temporal interpretation. FIB-4 may help identify people at higher cardiovascular risk.

Title: External validation of EuroSCORE II, additive EuroSCORE, and the STS predicted risk of mortality at 2,600 meters above sea level: a retrospective cohort study from a Latin American cardiac surgery centre.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: EuroSCORE II, the Additive EuroSCORE, and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS PROM) are widely used cardiac surgery risk models, but their performance has not been evaluated in a cardiac surgery centre located at high altitude (≥2,500 m asl).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective external validation study using prospectively collected registry data from consecutive adult cardiac surgery procedures performed at Hospital Universitario Mayor-Méderi (2,600 m asl), Bogotá, Colombia, between January 2019 and February 2026 (N = 1,486). EuroSCORE II and the Additive EuroSCORE were calculated from the registry with the published models and evaluated in the full cohort; STS PROM was obtained from the official STS online calculator (2018 models) for the procedures within its scope (n = 1,076). The outcome was in-hospital mortality. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and calibration with the observed to expected (O/E) ratio, calibration in the large, calibration slope, and calibration plots.
RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was 7.9% (117/1,486), and 82.3% of procedures were non-elective. The AUC was 0.736 (95% CI 0.687 to 0.785) for EuroSCORE II, 0.733 (0.684 to 0.783) for the Additive EuroSCORE, and 0.815 (0.757 to 0.873) for STS PROM. All three models underestimated mortality: the O/E ratio was 2.50 (2.09 to 3.00) for EuroSCORE II, 1.50 (1.25 to 1.79) for the Additive EuroSCORE, and 2.72 (2.14 to 3.47) for STS PROM. Calibration slopes were 1.04 (0.82 to 1.26), 1.94 (1.46 to 2.41), and 1.31 (1.01 to 1.60), respectively. Underestimation was present across procedure types, risk strata, and calendar years, and persisted in sensitivity analyses of variable mapping and missing data (EuroSCORE II O/E 2.37 to 3.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In this high-altitude Colombian centre, EuroSCORE II, the Additive EuroSCORE, and STS PROM ranked patients acceptably, STS PROM best, but all underestimated in-hospital mortality, EuroSCORE II and STS PROM by more than twofold. The study design cannot separate an effect of altitude from differences in case mix, urgency, and local care. Local recalibration is needed before these models are used for counselling or benchmarking in this setting.

Title: Association between radiotherapy laterality and cardiovascular disease mortality in male breast cancer patients receiving postoperative radiotherapy: a competing risks analysis and standardized mortality ratio assessment using SEER data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between radiotherapy (RT) laterality and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in male breast cancer (MBC) remains unknown. We evaluated whether left-sided RT confers higher CVD mortality than right-sided RT in MBC patients, and quantified excess CVD mortality relative to the general U.S. male population.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2,152 MBC patients receiving postoperative RT from the SEER database (2000-2020). Fine-Gray competing risks regression estimated subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) for CVD death comparing left- vs. right-sided RT. Multiple sensitivity analyses were performed, including propensity score matching (PSM). Standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) were calculated using age-specific CVD mortality rates from CDC WONDER.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 5.6 years, no significant difference in CVD mortality was observed between left- and right-sided RT (fully adjusted sHR = 1.03; 95% CI: 0.71-1.49; P = 0.887). Results remained consistent across all sensitivity analyses (all P > 0.750). Compared with the general U.S. male population, irradiated MBC patients had a significantly elevated risk of CVD death (SMR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.15-1.61). Age-stratified analysis showed the numerically highest point estimate in the 45-54 age group (SMR = 2.08; 95% CI: 0.84-4.29), though this did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: In MBC patients receiving modern RT, left- and right-sided treatment confer comparable risks of CVD mortality. Nevertheless, overall CVD mortality remains significantly higher than in the general U.S. male population, warranting comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment and management for all RT recipients.

Title: Therapeutic role of granulocyte-colony stimulating factor and aspirin in unexplained recurrent pregnancy loss: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), the loss of two or more clinically confirmed pregnancies, is observed in approximately 1%-5% of couples trying to conceive. Immune dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a contributing factor. This study evaluated pregnancy outcomes among women with unexplained RPL treated with combined recombinant human granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (rhG-CSF) and low-dose aspirin, while acknowledging that the evidence base for rhG-CSF in unexplained RPL remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 300 women aged 18-45 years with at least two consecutive unexplained pregnancy losses were treated with subcutaneous rhG-CSF and low-dose aspirin. Eligible women had documented ovulation, no major uterine abnormality, and no male-factor infertility. Source records were reviewed for mode of conception; all 300 index pregnancies were documented as spontaneous conceptions, and no pregnancies achieved by assisted reproductive technology (ART) were included. rhG-CSF was initiated on the sixth day after ovulation and continued until menstruation or completion of 9 gestational weeks; aspirin 75 mg/day was initiated at the same post-ovulatory time point and continued until 36 gestational weeks unless pregnancy loss or a safety indication required discontinuation. Clinical pregnancy, live birth, miscarriage, stillbirth, neonatal outcomes, and adverse events were assessed. Maternal age was treated as a clinically relevant covariate. Analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS version 27.
RESULTS: Live birth at or after 20 weeks of gestation occurred in 211/300 women (70.3%) according to the institutional obstetric registry definition used in the source records. All index pregnancies were verified as spontaneous conceptions, with no ART pregnancies included. Clinical pregnancy, defined as an intrauterine gestational sac with fetal cardiac activity at 6-7 gestational weeks, was observed in 99.3% of participants. In the age-adjusted model, a higher pretreatment systolic/diastolic ratio remained associated with lower odds of live birth (adjusted OR = 0.34, 95% CI 0.22-0.52, p < 0.001), while increasing maternal age was also associated with lower live-birth odds (adjusted OR per year = 0.94, 95% CI 0.89-0.99, p = 0.031). The miscarriage rate was 29.7%, median neonatal birth weight was 3,012 g, and congenital anomalies were documented in 12.6% of recorded neonatal outcomes.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, combined rhG-CSF and aspirin therapy was associated with improved uterine Doppler indices and a 70.3% live-birth rate among women with unexplained RPL. Because the study lacked an untreated control group and rhG-CSF use for unexplained RPL remains off-label with conflicting trial evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in adequately powered controlled studies.

Title: Mortality risk stratification in contemporary myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock: development of AMICS-ADMIT prediction model and benchmarking of established scores.
Journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality risk stratification in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains challenging with heterogeneous temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) use. We developed and temporally validated the admission-based AMICS-ADMIT model and bedside score and benchmarked them against established scores.
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study, reported according to TRIPOD+AI, included 479 consecutive patients with AMI-CS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) between January 2017 and July 2025. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. AMICS-ADMIT was developed using multivariable logistic regression in the 2017-2022 cohort, internally evaluated by bootstrap resampling, and temporally validated in the 2023-2025 cohort. Missing data were multiply imputed. Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and Brier scores. Benchmarking against CardShock, IABP-SHOCK II, and GRACE was restricted to temporal validation; tMCS-stratified performance was exploratory.
RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was 42.6% (204/479). The final model included age, left ventricular ejection fraction, prior cardiopulmonary resuscitation, estimated glomerular filtration rate, vasoactive-inotropic score, and ST-segment elevation status. The continuous model achieved AUCs of 0.809 (95% CI 0.764-0.855) in development and 0.834 (95% CI 0.769-0.899) in temporal validation, with Brier scores of 0.176 and 0.167 and favourable calibration. The bedside score achieved AUCs of 0.777 (95% CI 0.728-0.826) and 0.775 (95% CI 0.699-0.851), respectively, with stepwise mortality separation across predefined risk categories. Discrimination did not differ significantly from CardShock, IABP-SHOCK II, or GRACE.
CONCLUSIONS: AMICS-ADMIT showed stable temporal performance and clinically interpretable early risk stratification in contemporary PCI-treated AMI-CS. External multicentre validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Hypertension and pain: A state-based framework for cardiovascular-nociceptive coupling.
Abstract: Experimental and epidemiological studies suggest that blood pressure (BP)-pain associations vary across normotension, hypertension, and chronic pain, but the mechanisms underlying these differences remain unclear. In pain-free individuals, higher resting BP is often associated with lower experimental pain sensitivity. Similar hypoalgesia is reported in some normotensive individuals with familial hypertension risk and in established hypertension, suggesting that reduced pain sensitivity is unlikely to be attributable to elevated BP alone. Acute baroreceptor activation can inhibit nociceptive reflexes and pain ratings, and current evidence points to contributions from baroreflex, autonomic, opioid, sensory, vascular, and renin-angiotensin pathways in BP-related hypoalgesia across groups. In chronic pain, the inverse BP-pain association is often weaker, absent, or reversed for selected pain facilitation measures. Prospective epidemiological studies suggest that chronic pain may be associated with increased later hypertension risk, although these observational findings do not establish causality. This review organizes the literature into four states: familial hypertension risk without sustained hypertension, inverse BP-pain associations in normotensive individuals, hypoalgesia in established hypertension, and attenuated or reversed BP-pain associations in chronic pain. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these patterns reflect distinct phenotypes, transitional processes, overlapping mechanisms, or study-context differences.

Title: Association of a history of type 2 diabetes with short-term mortality in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and mortality in patients with liver cirrhosis remains controversial. This study aimed to evaluate whether a history of T2DM influences short-term all-cause mortality in hospitalized patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis (DLC).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of hospitalized patients with DLC at three medical centers in China between November 2019 and June 2024. The study endpoint was the 6-month mortality. The association between T2DM and mortality was assessed using multivariable logistic regression, and stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) analysis was applied for sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Among 984 eligible patients, 239 (24.3%) had a history of T2DM. Patients with T2DM were older and had a higher prevalence of hypertension and coronary artery disease; however, no significant difference in 6-month mortality was observed between patients with and without T2DM. Multivariable logistic regression showed no independent association between a history of T2DM and mortality (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.51-1.23), this result remained consistent using sIPTW analysis (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.51-1.21).
CONCLUSIONS: A history of T2DM may not be independently associated with short-term mortality in patients with DLC. These findings suggest that T2DM status may not be prioritized over liver-specific prognostic factors when assessing the short-term mortality risk in patients with DLC.

Title: Cardiac troponin T and 28-day mortality in traumatic brain injury: a retrospective cohort study and machine learning prediction model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) frequently induces cardiac dysfunction via the brain-heart axis, yet the prognostic value of cardiac troponin T (cTnT) in TBI remains incompletely characterized. This study investigated thye association between cTnT levels and 28-day all-cause mortality in TBI patients and developed a machine learning-based prediction model.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 837 adult TBI patients from the MIMIC-III/IV databases (development cohort) and 121 patients from a single Chinese center (external validation cohort). The first cTnT measurement within 24 h of ICU admission was analyzed. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression was used to explore nonlinear relationships. cTnT was categorized into quartiles (Q1 ≤ 0.03, Q2 0.03-0.06, Q3 0.06-0.17, Q4 > 0.17 ng/mL). A two-step Boruta plus LASSO feature selection identified 13 robust predictors. Five machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, BART, GBM, CTREE, SVM) were trained. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Among 837 patients, 217 (25.9%) died within 28 days. RCS revealed a significant nonlinear association (P for nonlinearity < 0.001). In multivariable Cox regression adjusted for the 12 LASSO-selected covariates (excluding cTnT quartile itself), patients in Q3 and Q4 had nearly twofold higher mortality risks compared with Q1 (HR = 2.01, 95% CI: 1.37-2.95, p < 0.001; and HR = 1.96, 95% CI: 1.31-2.93, p = 0.001, respectively). Random Forest achieved the best discriminative performance, with an internal AUC of 0.783 and an external validation AUC of 0.706 (95% CI: 0.584-0.828). The model also demonstrated good calibration (Brier score = 0.155) and favorable clinical utility across clinically relevant threshold probabilities as shown by decision curve analysis.
CONCLUSION: Elevated cTnT is independently associated with 28-day mortality in TBI patients, with a potential risk threshold of ≥0.06 ng/mL. The Random Forest model integrating cTnT with clinical variables provides moderate mortality prediction. cTnT may serve as an integrative marker of systemic stress and multi-organ dysfunction in TBI.

Title: Estimated pulse wave velocity and dipstick proteinuria in young adults with MASLD: a cross-sectional health-check analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a non-invasive surrogate measure of arterial stiffness that has been associated with cardiovascular risk and renal abnormalities. However, studies exploring the association between ePWV and dipstick proteinuria in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-a condition associated with an increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD)-are scarce. This study aimed to investigate the association between ePWV and dipstick proteinuria in patients with MASLD.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 1,641 MASLD patients from a cohort of individuals who underwent health check-ups at a tertiary hospital in Beijing, China. ePWV was calculated using an established equation based on age and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Participants were stratified based on ePWV tertiles. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the relationship between ePWV and dipstick proteinuria, adjusting for potential confounders such as age, sex, BMI, and comorbid conditions. Subgroup analyses were performed according to sex, diabetes, hyperuricemia, dyslipidemia, H. pylori infection, and urolithiasis.
RESULTS: Unadjusted and adjusted models consistently showed that higher ePWV was associated with higher odds of dipstick proteinuria. In the highest ePWV tertile, the odds of dipstick proteinuria were higher compared to the lowest tertile (OR: 2.44, 95% CI: 1.20-5.67, P for trend = 0.002). Subgroup analysis revealed a statistically significant interaction by dyslipidemia status, with a stronger association observed among participants without dyslipidemia (OR: 4.59, 95% CI: 2.18-9.76, P = 0.001), while no statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, hyperuricemia, H. pylori infection, diabetes mellitus, or urolithiasis.
DISCUSSION: Higher ePWV was associated with an increased likelihood of dipstick proteinuria among patients with MASLD. Further longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether ePWV is associated with subsequent urinary protein abnormalities and kidney outcomes.

Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early acute kidney injury and altered consciousness in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the intensive care unit: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and altered consciousness are common and serious complications following cardiac surgery, both associated with increased morbidity and mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU). Early prediction of these complications is essential for timely intervention. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting early AKI and altered consciousness risk in this population.
METHODS: We retrospectively extracted data from the MIMIC-IV database. Adult patients who underwent cardiac surgery within 24 h before ICU admission were included. The primary outcome was early AKI defined by KDIGO criteria within 48 h after ICU admission. The secondary outcome was altered consciousness within 24 h after ICU admission, defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score ≤12. A comprehensive set of candidate variables was screened using four feature selection methods (LassoCV, mRMR, mutual information, and F-test) with a voting strategy. Eight machine learning models were developed and compared. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were used to interpret the best-performing model. External validation was performed using data from cardiac surgery patients at Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2025.
RESULT: A total of 5,288 patients were included, with an AKI incidence of 76.2% (4,031/5,288) and an altered consciousness incidence of 22.8% (1,206/5,288). For the primary outcome of AKI, the XGBoost model achieved a training AUC of 0.787 (95% CI: 0.770-0.804) and an internal test AUC of 0.659 (95% CI: 0.629-0.688). For the secondary outcome of altered consciousness, the XGBoost model achieved an internal test AUC of 0.951 (95% CI: 0.936-0.963). Calibration curve and decision curve analysis confirmed good calibration and clinical utility for both models. SHAP analysis identified SpO2, age, APSIII score, creatinine, and white blood cell count as the top 5 most important predictors for AKI. External validation was performed in an independent cohort of 395 cardiac surgery ICU patients from Wuxi No.2 People's Hospital, in whom the incidence of AKI and altered consciousness was 28.1% and 67.3%, respectively. The models retained acceptable discrimination in this external cohort (AKI: AUC 0.764, 95% CI: 0.711-0.818; altered consciousness: AUC 0.679, 95% CI: 0.615-0.737).
CONCLUSION: We developed interpretable XGBoost-based prediction models for both early AKI and altered consciousness risk in cardiac surgery patients admitted to the ICU. The models exhibited excellent discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, which may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and guide personalized interventions.

Title: Predictors of recurrent stroke among patients with lacunar stroke receiving intensive blood pressure control: a secondary analysis of the secondary prevention of small subcortical strokes trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intensive systolic blood pressure (SBP) lowering to <130 mm Hg is recommended in contemporary secondary stroke prevention guidelines; however, it did not significantly reduce overall recurrent ischemic stroke in the Secondary Prevention of Small Subcortical Strokes (SPS3) trial. In this post hoc secondary analysis of participant-level SPS3 trial data, we sought to identify baseline predictors of recurrent ischemic stroke among patients with lacunar stroke assigned to the lower SBP target in SPS3.
METHODS: This post hoc secondary analysis included SPS3 participants randomized to the lower SBP target (<130 mm Hg). The primary outcome was centrally adjudicated recurrent ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Candidate predictors were evaluated with multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and reported as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Among 1501 participants (41.1% aged ≥ 65 years; 60.8% were men), 120 (8.0%) experienced recurrent ischemic stroke over a median follow-up of 3.49 years (interquartile range, 1.80-5.08), corresponding to an incidence rate of 2.43 events per 100 person-years. In unadjusted comparisons, recurrent ischemic stroke was associated with diabetes mellitus (44.2% vs 34.2%; p = .036), coronary artery bypass grafting/coronary stent (9.2% vs 4.1%; p = .018), Black race (24.2% vs 14.4%; p = .007), elevated serum creatinine (14.2% vs 7.7%; p = .022), aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (44.2% vs 28.5%; p < .001), large-vessel atherosclerosis (29.3% vs 17.9%; p = .004), and lower prevalence of a subcortical qualifying stroke (21.7% vs 46.1%; p < .001). In multivariable analysis, aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.14-2.50; p = .009) and large-vessel atherosclerosis (HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.08-2.413; p = .020) were independently associated with recurrence. Randomization to aspirin plus clopidogrel was not associated with recurrent ischemic stroke (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.75-1.57; p = .661).
CONCLUSIONS: In SPS3 participants assigned to intensive SBP control, 8.0% experienced recurrent ischemic stroke. Aspirin or clopidogrel use at the qualifying lacunar stroke and large-vessel atherosclerosis remained independent predictors of recurrence. These findings may help identify patients who require preventive strategies beyond intensive SBP lowering.

Title: An interval-based approach to measuring eating jet lag in female healthcare shift workers.
Abstract: Circadian rhythms regulate physiological and metabolic functions, and their disruption, particularly from shift work, is associated with adverse health outcomes such as obesity or cardiovascular disease. Meal timing variability, or eating jet lag, has emerged as a valuable marker of circadian misalignment. This study introduces a novel method to assess eating jet lag through direct comparison of food intake intervals, addressing limitations of traditional midpoint-based approaches reducing intervals to single values, potentially overlooking meaningful overlap. We conducted a cross-sectional study on 290 female healthcare professionals in Asturias, Spain, from a larger cohort of 679 participants with complete temporal data for meals across morning, afternoon, and night shifts. The proposed method calculates the degree of embedding between intake intervals during work shifts and rest days, and a global index is derived by aggregating alignment values across shifts. Results show that the interval-based method captures temporal overlap not represented by the midpoint-based approach, especially where the midpoint method underestimates alignment. Bland-Altman analysis showed systematic and proportional disagreement between the two approaches, with discrepancies greater at lower levels of alignment. This approach provides complementary information for evaluating eating-window alignment and provides a basis for future studies between eating-window alignment and health-related outcomes.

Title: Early Prediction of Cardiomyopathy in Pediatric Cancer Survivors Using Echocardiographic Video-Based Deep Learning.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiomyopathy (CM) is a leading cause of late mortality in childhood cancer survivors, but it is often identified only after irreversible cardiac remodeling has already occurred. In this proof-of-concept study, we assessed whether deep learning applied to routine echocardiographic videos can identify features predictive of future CM.
METHODS: We analyzed parasternal short-axis clips from cancer survivors ≤21 years old at cancer diagnosis. 3D deep convolutional neural networks were trained to classify CM-positive versus CM-negative studies from echocardiograms conducted up to five years prior to CM diagnosis. The performance was assessed on internal hold-out validation (Center 1) and external validation cohorts (Centers 2, 3). The model's prognostic value was evaluated by stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups for developing CM, and probability of future CM was assessed using cumulative incidence and proportional hazards regression analysis.
RESULTS: The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.87±0.05 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.74±0.07 on the internal hold-out set. External validation showed near-chance single-study discrimination (AUROC 0.55±0.02 and 0.60±0.03; AUPRC 0.22±0.02 and 0.21±0.03 for Centers 2 and 3, respectively). Nevertheless, analysis of the external cohort showed significantly higher probability of CM in high- versus low-risk groups (hazard ratio 2.78, 95% CI = 1.52-5.10, p = 0.00056).
CONCLUSION: Deep learning models have the potential to identify subtle echocardiographic markers years before CM diagnosis in pediatric cancer survivors and could serve as a preliminary step toward risk-guided CM surveillance. Further refinement and validation are needed to determine the utility of deep learning for early identification of pathologic cardiac remodeling in this population.

Title: One-Year Clinical Outcomes of Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Patients With and Without Acute Coronary Syndrome: The ALLIANCE Registry.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-world data after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are limited.
AIMS: We compared 1-year clinical outcomes after PCI with paclitaxel DCBs between the ACS and non-ACS patients.
METHODS: The ALLIANCE is a prospective, multicenter registry of PCI using paclitaxel DCBs. Primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality at 1 year. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences between the ACS and non-ACS patients.
RESULTS: From July 2023 to February 2024, 1794 patients with de novo lesions (ACS 513 [28.6%] and non-ACS 1281 [71.4%]) were enrolled at 57 medical institutions in Japan. Mean age was 71 years, and 76% were male. Among ACS patients, 34.7% had ST-segment elevation MI, 33.9% non-ST-segment elevation MI, and 31.4% unstable angina. Intracoronary imaging was used in 88.5% of lesions. Bailout stenting after DCB angioplasty was required in only 1.1% of 1984 lesions. Technical success, defined as post-procedural residual stenosis < 40% and absence of flow-limiting coronary dissection, was significantly lower in patients with ACS than those with non-ACS. At 1 year, TLF occurred in 7.0% of ACS and 3.8% of non-ACS patients (adjusted HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.06-3.17, p = 0.03). All-cause mortality was 6.4% and 3.3%, respectively (adjusted HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.13-3.75, p = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: One-year TLF and all-cause mortality were significantly higher in ACS than non-ACS patients treated with paclitaxel DCBs in real-world clinical settings.
REGISTRATION: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp); unique identifier: jRCT1032230218.

Title: An early risk prediction nomogram for coronary artery lesions in Kawasaki disease: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery lesions remain a major concern in Kawasaki disease. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a practical nomogram for early identification of children at risk for Coronary artery lesions.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 216 children with Kawasaki disease divided into a training cohort (n = 151) and a validation cohort (n = 65). Coronary artery lesions was defined as early coronary dilatation and/or coronary aneurysm. XGBoost and SHapley Additive exPlanations were applied to explore age's nonlinear effect. Predictors were screened via multivariable logistic regression with elastic-net regression for supplementary assessment. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis.
RESULTS: Overall, 46 children (21.3%) developed Coronary artery lesions. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified a U-shaped age-risk pattern with cut-off points at 17 and 58 months.
