Male sex, age group, fever duration, systemic immune-inflammation index, C-reactive protein/albumin ratio, and intravenous immunoglobulin resistance were independent Coronary artery lesions risk factors incorporated into the nomogram. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve reached 0.835 (95% CI 0.804-0.867) in the training cohort and 0.818 (95% CI 0.767-0.869) in the validation cohort. Calibration and decision-curve analysis confirmed good consistency and favourable clinical net benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: This nomogram integrates routine clinical variables and interpretable machine learning to identify nonlinear age-related Coronary artery lesions risk and provide individualised early risk estimation. External validation in large prospective multicentre cohorts is needed before wide clinical application.

Title: Impact of Cardiometabolic Risk Factors Control on Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis in Chronic Hepatitis B.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) on the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) axis in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains poorly defined.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis enrolling patients with CHB who were on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs). CMRFs were defined as per established criteria; poorly-controlled CMRFs were defined with specific cut-offs measured across 5 years. Study outcomes include fibrosis progression (liver stiffness [LS] increase by ≥ 20%), liver-related events (LREs), chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 714 NUC-treated patients (median age: 61.0 [54.5-66.7] years; 69.6% male; 90.5% undetectable HBV DNA, median NUCs duration of 14.1 [11.3-16.5] years) were followed up for 9.7 (7.2-10.2) years. LREs occurred in 112 (15.7%) patients, with annual incidence rate of 1.62 events per 100 person-years. All-cause mortality was observed in 86 (12%) patients, including 47 (6.6%) liver-related mortality. The number or types of CMRFs did not display a linear positive relationship with adverse clinical outcomes. The presence of ≥ 1 poorly controlled CMRFs is independently associated with LREs (aHR: 2.001, 95% CI: 1.350-2.965), MACE (aHR: 1.042, 95% CI: 1.030-1.081), and all-cause mortality (aHR: 2.082, 95% CI: 1.006-4.310), whereas patients having ≥ 2 and ≥ 3 poorly controlled CMRFs are independently associated with CKD progression (aOR: 1.887, 95% CI: 1.115-3.221) and fibrosis progression (aOR: 1.624, 95% CI: 1.164-2.266), respectively. The results remain robust in patients without advanced fibrosis (LS ≤ 10 kPa) at baseline.
CONCLUSION: Active optimization of CMRFs should be an integral component of CHB management in addition to NUCs therapy.

Title: Accuracy of Large Language Model Chatbots in Retrieving MRI Safety Conditions for Medical Implants.
Journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retrieving MRI safety conditions for implanted devices is increasingly complex and time-consuming.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the accuracy of internet-enabled large language model (LLM) chatbots in retrieving implant-specific MRI safety conditions, using manufacturer documentation as the reference standard.
STUDY TYPE: Prospective comparative evaluation in a constructed device cohort, followed by a retrospective clinical pilot.
POPULATION: Fifty purposively selected device configurations and 20 patients (10 with cardiac and 10 with noncardiac devices) referred to the MRI Safety Committee.
FIELD STRENGTH: No field-strength or sequence restrictions.
ASSESSMENT: Standardized single-shot prompts requested eight parameters from ChatGPT-5.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.5: MRI safety label, field strengths, eligible regions/centering, transmit-coil restrictions, RF exposure limits, maximum spatial gradient, maximum gradient slew rate, and scan duration. Two radiologists (10 and 25 years' experience) and an MRI technologist (32 years) independently scored 1200 parameter-level outputs against manufacturer Instructions for use and technical manuals using a 5-point scale (5, fully correct; 1, substantively incorrect or fabricated); scores of 4-5 indicated accuracy. In the pilot, 160 outputs from ChatGPT-5.6, a newer version of the best-performing chatbot, were scored identically.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Intraclass correlation coefficient; Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1); Friedman test; Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; device-clustered bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs); two-sided significance threshold, p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Mean ordinal scores were 4.76 (ChatGPT), 4.20 (Gemini), and 4.17 (Claude); ChatGPT scored significantly higher. Respective pooled parameter-level accuracies were 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-0.98), 0.79 (0.71-0.86), and 0.78 (0.69-0.87). Pilot accuracy with ChatGPT-5.6 was 0.98 (95% CI, 0.94-1.00).
DATA CONCLUSION: Internet-enabled LLM chatbots correctly retrieved up to 94% of MRI safety parameters in the constructed cohort and 98% in the clinical pilot. Errors occurred even with the best-performing chatbot, requiring direct verification against current manufacturer documentation before clinical use.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: Stage 2.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

Title: Speech- and Text-Based Emotion Recognition in Anesthesiology Residents During Critical Incident Simulation Training: Exploratory Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Communication during crisis management involves not only the exchange of clinical information but also the expression and regulation of emotional tone and sentiment, which may reflect clinician performance during a critical incident. In simulation-based medical education, these emotional dynamics are rarely measured objectively, limiting the ability to capture aspects of performance relevant to competency assessment.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine whether automatically extracted speech- and text-based emotion signals varied across predefined phases of critical incident simulation training and whether these signals were associated with expert-rated performance among anesthesiology residents.
METHODS: In this exploratory observational study, we analyzed 164 simulated crisis scenarios performed by 90 anesthesiology residents from 17 hospitals during a national board preparation workshop. Each high-fidelity simulation comprised 4 predefined phases: initial condition, extreme deterioration, advanced cardiovascular life support (ACLS) management, and recovery. Resident speech was isolated and analyzed using a speech-based emotion recognition (SER) model that estimated 8 emotion categories per utterance. Speech was also automatically transcribed and analyzed using text-based emotion recognition (TER), which estimated 9 emotion categories. Expert anesthesiologists rated performance on a 1-5 scale. ANOVA tested associations between emotion categories and performance, as well as variation across simulation phases. Exploratory mixed-effects sensitivity analyses accounted for repeated simulations and scenario-level clustering.
RESULTS: After 7 recordings were excluded because of technical issues, 65 of 164 (39.6%) simulations were classified as poor performance (score ≤2), 72 (43.9%) as intermediate, and 27 (16.5%) as excellent (score=5). SER categories differed across performance groups (F2,161=4.61; P=.02): poor performance showed more fear and surprise, whereas excellent performance showed more calm, happiness, and neutrality. In mixed-effects analyses, performance group remained associated with happy, angry, fearful, surprise, calm, and neutral speech-emotion proportions after false discovery rate correction. The largest excellent vs poor differences were observed for neutral (+4.24 percentage points), happy (+4.11), and surprise (-3.17) speech affect. TER showed a directionally similar but nonsignificant omnibus association (F2,161=2.57; P=.08); mixed-effects analyses identified associations with happy and sad text-emotion proportions after correction. During extreme deterioration and ACLS management, fear and surprise together accounted for 64.1% and 64.6% of classified speech emotions, respectively, among poor performances. During ACLS management, neutral and calm emotions accounted for 49.1% and 37.7%, respectively, among excellent performances.
CONCLUSIONS: Automated speech- and text-based emotion recognition captured phase-dependent affective communication patterns during critical incident simulations. Speech-derived features were more consistently associated with expert-rated performance, whereas text-derived findings were more exploratory and emotion-specific. These markers may complement simulation debriefing and formative feedback, but validation using multirater outcomes, preregistered adjusted models, and larger multicenter datasets is needed before they inform competency assessment.

Title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: BackgroundAcute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) is a surgical emergency associated with high mortality. While patient-related risk factors are well-established, beliefs persist regarding the influence of lunar phases, meteorological conditions, and astrological signs on disease occurrence and outcomes.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed all patients who underwent emergency surgery for ATAAD at Bordeaux University Hospital between 1996 and 2020. The primary objective was to assess the association between environmental factors (lunar phases, atmospheric pressure, temperature, and astrological signs) and ATAAD incidence. Secondary objectives included assessing their association with 30-day mortality and postoperative morbidity (intensive care unit length of stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use, and mesenteric infarction). Meteorological data were available for 603 patients from 2010 onward.ResultsAmong 920 patients (70% male; mean age 63 ± 13 years), the 30-day mortality rate was 9.7%. Lunar phases were not associated with ATAAD incidence (first quarter 26%, last quarter 25%, new moon 25%, full moon 24%; p = 0.91), mortality, or complications. Atmospheric pressure showed no association with ATAAD occurrence or outcomes. Temperature showed a weak correlation with ATAAD incidence (r = 0.11, p = 0.01), but not with mortality. Astrological signs were not associated with ATAAD incidence, mortality, or morbidity. Longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (odds ratio [OR] = 0.994 per minute; p = 0.01) and diabetes (OR = 4.63; p = 0.01) were associated with 30-day mortality.ConclusionsEnvironmental factors were not associated with ATAAD incidence or outcomes. Established clinical factors remain the primary determinants of mortality.

Title: Learning Curve of Robotic Atrial Septal Defect Repair: A Multidimensional CUSUM Analysis of 284 Consecutive Cases.
Journal: The international journal of medical robotics + computer assisted surgery : MRCAS
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterise the learning curve of robotic atrial septal defect (ASD) repair using a multidimensional cumulative sum (CUSUM) framework.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 284 consecutive adult patients undergoing robotic ASD repair were analysed. CUSUM analysis was applied to operative time, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and hospital stay. Learning phases were identified according to inflection points of the CUSUM curves.
RESULTS: Four distinct learning phases were observed. Technical proficiency was achieved at Case 158, marked by significant reductions in operative (186.8 ± 43.3 vs. 133.7 ± 27.7 min), bypass, and cross-clamp times (p < 0.001). ICU stay and transfusion requirements progressively declined, while mortality remained low across all phases. Notably, postoperative care optimisation lagged behind technical mastery.
CONCLUSIONS: Multidimensional CUSUM analysis provides an objective, performance-based assessment of robotic ASD learning. Competency acquisition required substantial case volume, underscoring the need for structured training and longitudinal performance monitoring in robotic cardiac surgery.

Title: Evaluating the therapeutic benefits and safety of ecnoglutide for type 2 diabetes: evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a growing global health challenge, necessitating effective therapies that improve glycemic control and promote weight loss. Ecnoglutide, a novel cAMP-biased GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonist, has emerged as a promising therapeutic option.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted following PRISMA and AMSTAR-2 guidelines. Electronic databases were searched up to February 2026. Eligible studies included adult patients with T2DM comparing ecnoglutide with placebo or active comparators. Outcomes included glycemic parameters, anthropometric measures, metabolic indices, and safety. Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Three RCTs comprising 979 participants were included. Ecnoglutide significantly reduced HbA1c (MD -0.57%, 95% CI -0.86 to -0.29) and fasting plasma glucose (MD -1.11 mmol/L, 95% CI -1.58 to -0.65), with a higher proportion achieving target HbA1c (RR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37-1.80). Significant reductions in body weight (MD -1.83 kg) and waist circumference (MD -1.53 cm) were also observed. Improvements in insulin resistance and lipid parameters were noted. Exploratory subgroup analyses did not establish a clear dose response relationship, while short-term trials showed larger glycemic reductions compared with longer follow up. Adverse events were more frequent but not statistically significant, with no increase in serious adverse events.
CONCLUSION: Ecnoglutide demonstrates significant efficacy in improving glycemic control and weight-related outcomes in T2DM, with a safety profile comparable to existing GLP-1 receptor agonists. However, larger and longer-term studies are needed to confirm its cardiovascular benefits and long-term safety.

Title: Comparison of the effects of aquatic HIIT and MICT on central hemodynamics, endothelial function, and aerobic fitness in obese school-aged children: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aquatic exercise may be a feasible strategy for improving cardiovascular health in children with obesity, but evidence comparing aquatic high-intensity interval training (aHIIT) and aquatic moderate-intensity continuous training (aMICT) remains limited. This pilot randomized controlled trial compared the effects of 8 weeks of aHIIT and aMICT on endothelial function, estimated cardiorespiratory fitness, central hemodynamic indices, arterial stiffness, and anthropometric indicators in school-aged children with obesity.
METHODS: Thirty-three children with obesity were randomized to the aHIIT group (n = 11), aMICT group (n = 11), or non-exercise control group (n = 11). The two aquatic exercise groups trained 3 days/week for 8 weeks. The aHIIT protocol consisted of 10 × 30-s high-intensity aquatic exercise (such as freestyle swimming or freestyle kicking) bouts at 80%-90% HRmax, separated by 60-s recovery intervals, whereas the aMICT protocol consisted of two 15-min continuous breaststroke bouts at 60%-70% HRmax, separated by a 5-min recovery interval. Brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) was used as the principal vascular outcome. Central hemodynamic indices were assessed using applanation tonometry, and estimated VO2max was obtained from the 20-m shuttle run test. Intervention effects were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, with the group × time interaction used as the primary test for differential intervention effects.
RESULTS: Significant group × time interactions were observed for estimated VO2max, FMD, AIx, and AIx@HR75. Estimated VO2max increased in both aquatic exercise groups compared with the control group. FMD improved in both exercise groups, with a greater increase observed after aHIIT. AIx and AIx@HR75 showed favorable changes after aMICT. No significant group × time interactions were observed for resting blood pressure, SEVR, ABI, cfPWV, or baPWV.
CONCLUSION: This pilot trial suggests that both aHIIT and aMICT may improve estimated cardiorespiratory fitness in school-aged children with obesity. aHIIT may be associated with greater improvement in brachial artery endothelial function, whereas aMICT may have favorable effects on selected wave-reflection-related indices. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the small sample size, indirect estimated VO2max estimation, lack of maturation assessment, and unmatched exercise workload.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registration, ChiCTR2400080687.05/02/2024.

Title: Persistent pocket-site pain after cardiac implantable electronic device implantation: a prospective observational study of prevalence, neuropathic characteristics, and quality of life.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transvenous cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation is generally considered a minor procedure, long-lasting pocket-site pain may represent an underrecognized clinical problem. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, characteristics, and clinical impact of persistent pain after CIED implantation.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients who underwent first-time CIED implantation and attended routine outpatient follow-up visits. Pain intensity was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and neuropathic pain characteristics were evaluated using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 Questions (DN-4) questionnaire. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the Short Form-12 (SF-12). Demographic and clinical data were also recorded.
RESULTS: A total of 102 patients were included in the analysis. Persistent implantation-site pain (VAS ≥ 4) was reported by 22.5% of patients. Neuropathic pain characteristics (DN-4 ≥ 4) were identified in 26.5% of patients. A moderate positive correlation was observed between VAS and DN-4 scores (ρ = 0.473, p < 0.001). However, the association between VAS ≥ 4 and DN-4 ≥ 4 was not statistically significant and had a small effect size (p = 0.118; φ = 0.15). Pain intensity was moderately negatively correlated with the SF-12 physical component score, indicating reduced physical quality of life with increasing pain severity, while mental quality of life was not significantly affected.
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent pocket-site pain after CIED implantation affected a clinically meaningful proportion of patients despite generally low overall pain scores. Higher DN-4 scores were associated with poorer physical and mental quality of life and may provide additional clinical information in selected patients. However, because the categorical association between VAS-defined persistent pain and DN-4 positivity was not statistically significant, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger prospective studies.

Title: Triglyceride glucose index, metabolic comorbidity, and cardiovascular disease: a national cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a widely accepted surrogate biomarker of insulin resistance, strongly predicts cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. However, the mediating role of metabolic comorbidities in explaining the relationship between the TyG index and cardiovascular disease remains underexplored. Leveraging the longitudinal data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), this longitudinal study investigates how metabolic comorbidities mediate the association between the TyG index and cardiovascular risk.
METHODS: This analysis included 9,400 participants aged ≥ 45 years from CHARLS without baseline CVD. The TyG index was computed as Ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Incident cardiovascular events, which were defined as physician-confirmed heart disease or stroke, were monitored until 2020. Adjusted Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HR). The mediation analysis quantified the percentage of excess risk (PERM) attributable to metabolic comorbidities.
RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was 59.0 ± 9.5 years, and 4 862 (51.7%) were females. Among eligible participants, 2,152 developed cardiovascular diseases over a 9-year follow-up, with 1,627 heart disease cases and 765 strokes. Compared with people with a lower TyG index (< 8.59 [median level]) and no comorbidity, those concurrently with a higher TyG and comorbidity had the highest risk of CVD (adjusted HR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.47-1.88), coronary heart disease (aHR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.25-1.66) and stroke (aHR, 2.94; 95% CI, 2.31-3.75). Metabolic comorbidities mediated 48.3% of the TyG-associated CVD risk, predominantly through hypertension, renal impairment, inflammation, and obesity.
CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the partial mediating role of metabolic comorbidities in the TyG index-CVD association. Future research should explore residual pathways to fully elucidate this association.

Title: ApoB/ApoA-I ratio and all-cause mortality in maintenance hemodialysis: a cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional lipid markers have limited and inconsistent prognostic value in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD), a phenomenon often described as the lipid paradox. We evaluated whether lipid and apolipoprotein-related markers, particularly the ApoB/ApoA-I ratio, were associated with mortality in MHD patients.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 409 MHD patients. Lipid and apolipoprotein-related markers were analyzed as standardized continuous variables. Cox regression was used for all-cause mortality, and cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray models were used for cardiovascular mortality.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 55.7 months, 148 all-cause deaths occurred, including 61 cardiovascular deaths. ApoB/ApoA-I was not associated with all-cause mortality in the unadjusted model, but was independently associated with all-cause mortality in Model 3 (hazard ratio [HR] 1.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-1.44; p = 0.012). The association was similar in sensitivity analyses. ApoB/ApoA-I was not significantly associated with cardiovascular mortality in exploratory Fine-Gray regression (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.12, 95% CI 0.89-1.43; p = 0.337) and did not improve discrimination beyond the base clinical model.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ApoB/ApoA-I may contribute to risk characterization and etiologic understanding in MHD, but do not support its use as a stand-alone clinical prediction marker.

Title: Development and external validation of a preoperative prediction model for in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events after hip fracture surgery in older adults: a retrospective two-center study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with hip fracture are vulnerable to postoperative major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) during hospitalization. However, early risk stratification remains difficult because existing assessments may require complex or late-available information. A simple model based on variables routinely available before surgery may support perioperative decision-making.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective two-center cohort study of patients ≥ 60 years who underwent surgery for traumatic hip fracture at 2 hospitals in China. The development cohort included 935 patients treated between January 2024 and December 2025, and the external validation cohort included 168 patients treated between January 2020 and December 2025. Candidate preoperative predictors were screened using penalized regression. Six candidate prediction models were developed and compared using the same preprocessing pipeline. The final model was calibrated using Platt scaling. Model performance was assessed in an internal test set and an external validation cohort.
RESULTS: In the development cohort, 122 of 935 patients developed postoperative in-hospital MACE. The final model was a Platt-calibrated logistic regression model including age, baseline electrocardiographic abnormality, chronic heart failure, serum potassium, albumin, and hemoglobin. In the internal test set, the model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.814, with a 95% CI of 0.748-0.876, and a Brier score of 0.102. At the prespecified threshold of 0.147, sensitivity was 0.710 and specificity was 0.754. In the external validation cohort, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.760, with a 95% CI of 0.657-0.849. The Brier score was 0.141, sensitivity was 0.788, specificity was 0.630, and negative predictive value was 0.924.
CONCLUSIONS: A simple preoperative logistic regression model based on routinely available clinical variables showed moderate discrimination in internal testing and provided preliminary external validation evidence for predicting postoperative in-hospital MACE after hip fracture surgery in older adults. The model may support early perioperative risk stratification and postoperative surveillance, although prospective multicenter validation and recalibration are needed before wider clinical use.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Validation Study

Title: Development and validation of a predictive model for delayed emergence from anesthesia in elderly patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed emergence from anesthesia is a common perioperative complication in elderly patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), which may lead to prolonged recovery and increased healthcare burden. However, predictive tools specifically developed for this population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a practical model to identify patients at increased risk of delayed emergence from anesthesia.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 1,400 elderly patients who underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) at a tertiary hospital in Beijing between January 2020 and April 2026. An additional temporally independent cohort of 300 patients was used for temporal validation. Perioperative variables, including baseline characteristics, comorbidities, intraoperative parameters, and laboratory indicators, were collected. Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by multivariable logistic regression to construct the model. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and temporal validation with subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: Delayed emergence occurred in 210 patients (15.00%). Six independent predictors were identified: myocardial infarction, colloid solution use, bradycardia, end-tidal CO2 < 35 mmHg, hypothermia, and APTT. The model showed excellent discrimination in the derivation cohort (AUC = 0.909, 95% CI 0.888-0.929) with good calibration and clinical utility. In the temporal validation cohort, it maintained good discrimination (AUC = 0.863) and clinical usefulness, although calibration showed some deviation from ideal agreement. Subgroup analysis suggested better performance in patients aged ≥ 80 years.
CONCLUSIONS: The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination and clinical utility for predicting delayed emergence from anesthesia in elderly patients undergoing VATS. It may facilitate perioperative risk assessment and individualized perioperative management, although further recalibration may be required before external application.

Title: Exploring the application value of preoperative femoral artery and vein cannulation in redo cardiac surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To explore the clinical value of preoperative femoral vessel cannulation in redo cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 106 patients who underwent redo cardiac surgery in our hospital from January 2022 to December 2024. According to the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) cannulation technique adopted, the patients were divided into the Femoral Cannulation group (n = 79) and the Traditional Central Cannulation group (n = 37). Preoperative baseline data, intraoperative CPB-related parameters, blood product consumption, and the incidence of postoperative complications were recorded and compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: There were no statistically significant differences in preoperative baseline data or intraoperative parameters between the two groups (all P > 0.05). Similarly, no significant statistical differences were found in postoperative mortality, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) utilization rate, acute kidney injury (AKI) incidence, or cognitive dysfunction incidence between the two groups. However, compared with the Traditional Central Cannulation group, the Femoral Cannulation group had significantly lower intraoperative packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion volume and a significantly lower incidence of major cardiovascular injuries (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In redo cardiac surgery, preoperative femoral vessel cannulation can significantly reduce the incidence of major cardiovascular injuries and the demand for intraoperative blood transfusion, which is worthy of promotion and application in clinical practice.

Title: Risk factors and outcomes of early postoperative complications following congenital heart surgery: a retrospective study at a tertiary care hospital in Nairobi, Kenya.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) remains a major health challenge globally, with surgical interventions being the primary treatment modality for many defects. While advancements in cardiac surgery have improved survival rates, early postoperative complications continue to pose risks, particularly in settings with limited resources like Kenya. The study aimed to assess the rate of any early postoperative complications and identify factors associated with it in children after cardiac surgery at a tertiary care hospital in Nairobi, Kenya from 2019 to 2024.
METHODS: This was an single-center retrospective study including children (< 18 years) who underwent cardiac surgery due to congenital heart disease at a tertiary care hospital in Nairobi, Kenya, over a 5-year period. Categorical variables were described as frequencies and percentages, while continuous variables were described as medians with interquartile ranges (IQR). Categorical variables were compared using chi-square or Fisher exact test and continuous variables compared using Mann-Whitney U test. Variables with p-value < 0.1 in the univariable analysis were included in the multivariable logistic regression, with p-value < 0.05 set as the level of significance. All analyses were performed using Rstudio version 4.5.1.
RESULTS: A total of 97 children were included in the study. The median age in months was 25.0 (IQR: 8.5-67.5) and 50 (51.5%) were male. Patent ductus arteriosus, ventricular septal defect, and atrial septal defect were the predominant preoperative diagnoses. At least one early postoperative complication occurred in 52.6% (95%CI: 42.6% to 62.5%) of the children. Preoperative oxygen saturation (AOR: 0.92; 95%CI: 0.85-0.98, p = 0.021) and closed heart surgery (AOR:0.32; 95%CI:0.11-0.86, p = 0.027) were significantly associated with early postoperative complications.
CONCLUSION: The study findings highlight gaps and opportunities in perioperative care of children undergoing congenital heart surgery at a tertiary care center in Kenya. Preoperative oxygen saturation and closed heart surgery were independently associated with reduced odds of early postoperative complications. These findings suggest that optimizing preoperative physiological status and further investigating the factors driving the association between surgical approach and outcomes may inform strategies to improve perioperative care in this setting.

Title: Proteomic signatures characterized by inflammatory signaling and metabolic processes have divergent associations with 30-year incidence of coronary artery disease in type 1 diabetes: the Pittsburgh Epidemiology of Diabetes Complications cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While inflammation is hypothesized to be a possible driver of the excess coronary artery disease (CAD) observed in type 1 diabetes, prior biomarker studies have focused on candidate proteins, overlooking the complex systemic processes underlying atherosclerosis. We thus applied a high-throughput proteomics approach to identify proteins prospectively associated with CAD in type 1 diabetes. We further hypothesized inflammatory proteins would partially mediate the effect of glycemic exposure on CAD risk.
METHODS: We measured 184 circulating proteins (Olink CVD II and III panels) in earliest available serum samples from the Pittsburgh Epidemiology of Diabetes Complications cohort of childhood-onset (< 17 years) type 1 diabetes (n = 417, baseline mean age 30, mean diabetes duration 22 years). Protein modules were identified using weighted correlation network analysis. Prospective associations between modules (per eigenvalue SD) and 30-year incident hard CAD (hCAD; CAD death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, revascularization, or blockage ≥ 50%) were estimated in Cox models. Causal mediation analysis estimated mediation of the HbA1c-hCAD association by the modules.
RESULTS: Incident hCAD occurred in 151 participants (36.2%). We identified three protein modules: one comprising 56 proteins, enriched for TNF/Notch signaling, T-cell activation, and necroptosis; another comprising 33 proteins, enriched for lipid catabolism, epithelial cell apoptosis, vitamin D response; and a third comprising 33 proteins, enriched for hemostasis, wound healing, and vascular growth factors. After adjusting for traditional covariates and HbA1c, greater abundance of proteins in the first module was associated with increased hCAD incidence (HR = 1.35, 95% CI: 1.06-1.72, p = 0.014) while the second module was protective (HR = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.70-0.96, p = 0.017). The third module was not associated with hCAD (HR = 1.03, 95%CI: 0.86-1.23, p = 0.751). The first module mediated 14% of the total HbA1c effect on hCAD.
CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective analysis of a type 1 diabetes cohort, a protein signature characterized by inflammatory signaling partially mediated the effect of hyperglycemia on hCAD, while a signature characterized by metabolic processes including lipid catabolism and hormone response was associated with hCAD protection independent of glycemia. These findings move beyond single-marker associations, identifying distinct protein signatures that warrant further study as intervention targets for CAD prevention in type 1 diabetes.

Title: Nomogram construction and validation for hypoalbuminemia after total hip arthroplasty in patients with hip fractures.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the risk factors for hypoalbuminemia after total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients with hip fractures and to establish and validate a risk prediction nomogram.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 688 patients with hip fractures who underwent THA at The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University between January 2021 and June 2025. There were 261 males and 427 females. Fracture types included 441 cases of femoral neck fracture and 247 cases of femoral intertrochanteric fracture. Patients were divided into a hypoalbuminemia group (n = 209) and a normal albumin group (n = 479) according to whether hypoalbuminemia occurred postoperatively. Differences in general data were compared between the two groups, including age, gender, body mass index (BMI), smoking history, drinking history, comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes, cerebrovascular disease, cardiovascular disease), fracture type, American Society of Anesthesiologists classification, anesthesia type, operative duration, intraoperative blood loss and postoperative drainage volume. Preoperative laboratory examinations, including albumin (ALB), red blood cell count, hemoglobin (HB), C-reactive protein (CRP), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), platelet count (PLT), fibrinogen, activated partial thromboplastin time, D-dimer and serum calcium, were also included in the analysis. Parameters with P < 0.05 in univariate logistic regression were included in multivariate logistic regression to identify independent risk factors for postoperative hypoalbuminemia. The nomogram was developed using R software. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate the model. ROC curve analysis was performed to evaluate predictive performance, and the DeLong test was used to compare AUCs.
RESULTS: Significant differences were observed between the hypoalbuminemia group and the normal albumin group in age, BMI, diabetes, operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, preoperative ALB, preoperative HB, preoperative CRP, preoperative ESR, preoperative PLT and preoperative D-dimer (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression showed that age, diabetes mellitus, BMI, operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, preoperative ALB, preoperative HB and preoperative ESR were independent risk factors for postoperative hypoalbuminemia in hip fracture patients undergoing THA (P < 0.05). The nomogram incorporating these risk factors yielded an area under the ROC curve of 0.880 (95% CI 0.849-0.911) in the training set and 0.889 (95% CI 0.840-0.938) in the validation set. Both calibration curve and DCA indicated favorable accuracy and clinical utility in both cohorts. ROC curve analysis showed that the combined model achieved the optimal predictive performance for the target outcome, which was significantly superior to all single indicators (all P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced age, lower BMI, diabetes mellitus, longer operative duration, more intraoperative blood loss, lower preoperative albumin, lower preoperative hemoglobin and higher preoperative ESR are independent risk factors for postoperative hypoalbuminemia in patients undergoing THA for hip fractures. The nomogram prediction model established for these factors can integrate preoperative clinical data, is suitable for rapid clinical evaluation, and has good predictive ability.

Title: Unraveling the dual role of fibroblast growth factor 5 (FGF5) in cardiorenal diseases through multi-omics causal inference.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: As populations age worldwide, multimorbidity has become an increasingly prominent public health challenge. Among age-associated conditions, cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are among the most prevalent and life-threatening, and they frequently coexist with other chronic disorders, particularly chronic kidney disease (CKD). Pleiotropic molecules may provide an important entry point for elucidating comorbidity mechanisms and identifying therapeutic opportunities. However, the clinical translational value of different pleiotropic candidates exhibits substantial heterogeneity, and their directional effects remain poorly understood.
METHODS: In this study, we integrated four large-scale protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) cohorts from European and East Asian populations, and applied a dual-window Bayesian colocalization strategy to systematically screen for shared genetic signals across 2719 plasma proteins and 34 age-related diseases. We further conducted causal inference and integrative functional characterization of the core candidate protein via Mendelian randomization (MR), observational cross-sectional analysis, genetic fine-mapping, cis-regulatory element analysis and single-cell transcriptomics.
RESULTS: Following systematic cross-ancestry screening of 2719 plasma proteins, FGF5 was identified as the core candidate protein, with its circulating pQTL signals showing strong colocalization with CVDs, CKD, and cardiorenal-related phenotypes. Notably, this genetic regulatory effect of FGF5 exhibited marked renal tissue specificity, with its pQTL signals colocalizing strongly with expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) signals exclusively in the renal cortex, glomeruli, and renal tubules (PP.H4 > 0.97). MR analysis suggested that genetically predicted elevation in circulating FGF5 levels was significantly associated with an increased risk of CVD, with 42.9-66.7% of this association potentially mediated by blood pressure. In contrast, MR analyses suggested a potentially protective effect of elevated FGF5 levels on CKD, with 8.4-11.8% of the association potentially mediated by uric acid. Clinical observational analyses provided complementary support for this bidirectional association pattern, with plasma FGF5 levels showing a positive linear association with CVD risk and a nonlinear U-shaped association with CKD prevalence. Genetic fine-mapping prioritized rs2903657 and rs17004846 as the most likely candidate causal variants within the same strongly linked cis-regulatory haplotype. Phenome-wide association scan (PheWAS) further supported the pleiotropic involvement of these two variants across blood pressure, renal function, and metabolic traits. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further showed that FGF5 was preferentially enriched in proximal tubular epithelial cells in the injury-repair state.
CONCLUSIONS: This study systematically elucidates the potential antagonistic pleiotropic effects of FGF5 across cardiorenal diseases. These findings provide clues for understanding the shared genetic mechanisms of cardiorenal multimorbidity and offer genetic evidence to guide future functional translation and precision intervention strategies.

Title: Diabetic retinopathy enhances coronary artery calcium-based cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with type 2 diabetes: insights from the ACCoDiab study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coronary artery calcium (CAC) score is a validated imaging biomarker enhancing cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, residual risk persists, particularly among patients with moderate CAC scores. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a microvascular complication of diabetes, may reflect systemic vascular vulnerability and provide additional prognostic information.
METHODS: This observational cohort study was conducted as part of the primary prevention ACCoDiab study. 424 patients with T2DM (175 females and 249 males, with a mean age of 61 years) and no history of cardiovascular events underwent CAC scoring and clinical assessments, including DR screening. Patients were monitored for seven years or until the first cardiovascular events, including nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, hospitalization for heart failure, peripheral artery disease revascularization, and cardiovascular death. Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and net reclassification improvement (NRI) were used to evaluate the added prognostic value of DR to CAC scoring and to develop a simple integrated cardiovascular risk score.
RESULTS: Fifty patients (11.8%) had incident cardiovascular events. DR was significantly more prevalent among those who experienced events (58% vs. 25%, p < 0.001). Both CAC score and DR were independently associated with cardiovascular events. When incorporating DR into the CAC-based risk model, the predictive power was significantly enhanced AUC 75 [0.69-0.82] vs. 68 [0.61-0.75], p = 0.01). Further improvement was observed after adjusting for traditional risk factors (AUC 79 [0.73-0.86] vs. 73 [0.66-0.81], p = 0.04). The presence of DR reclassified a significant proportion of patients into higher-risk categories, particularly those with low and moderate CAC scores. Additionally, the severity of DR was also found to provide incremental prognostic information but did not provide significant additional stratification beyond the binary presence of DR.
CONCLUSION: The combination of diabetic retinopathy and CAC score significantly enhances cardiovascular risk stratification in T2DM patients, beyond traditional risk factors, highlighting that both microvascular and macrovascular factors should be considered in comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment. This approach, integrated to clinical routine, may help identify patients for earlier intervention and more personalized treatment strategies. Trial registration NCT03920683.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: From numbers to trajectories: a pragmatic hs-cTnT/NT-proBNP delta-check for 12-month risk stratification in chronic heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) are widely used in heart failure (HF), but outpatient interpretation often depends on isolated values rather than within-person change. We evaluated a pragmatic dual-biomarker delta-check framework for 12-month risk stratification in chronic HF.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults with chronic HF who had paired hs-cTnT and NT-proBNP measurements obtained during a clinically stable anchor visit and repeated within 3-6 months. The second paired measurement served as the index date. Patients were classified a priori into Green, Yellow, or Red trajectory tiers using combined relative and absolute biomarker changes, interpreted with a minimum clinical context bundle including rhythm, renal function, and clinical state. Meaningful adverse change was defined as hs-cTnT rise ≥ 20% and ≥ 5 ng/L, and NT-proBNP rise ≥ 30% and ≥ 500 pg/mL, or ≥ 300 pg/mL when anchor NT-proBNP was < 1,000 pg/mL. The primary endpoint was HF hospitalization or all-cause death within 12 months.
RESULTS: Among 520 patients, 229 (44%) were Green, 187 (36%) Yellow, and 104 (20%) Red. Anchor median NT-proBNP was 1,850 pg/mL [780-4,400], and hs-cTnT was 21 ng/L [13-36]. The primary endpoint occurred in 140 patients (26.9%). Event rates increased stepwise across tiers: Green 17.9%, Yellow 27.8%, and Red 45.2% (log-rank p < 0.001). In adjusted Cox models, Yellow showed an intermediate signal (HR 1.4, 95% CI 1.0-2.0; p = 0.06), whereas Red remained independently associated with higher risk (HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.4-3.2; p < 0.001). In a sensitivity model excluding anchor hs-cTnT and anchor NT-proBNP, the associations were preserved: Yellow HR 1.5 (95% CI 1.1-2.2; p = 0.03) and Red HR 2.5 (95% CI 1.7-3.6; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: A pragmatic hs-cTnT/NT-proBNP delta-check stratified 12-month risk in chronic HF. Concordant worsening across both biomarkers identified a high-risk trajectory, while isolated or borderline change was best interpreted as a lower-intensity review signal. Prospective testing is needed before this framework is used to guide outcome-modifying interventions.

Title: Vascular risk factors after stroke in the older people: a population-based study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The risk of recurrent stroke can be reduced by controlling modifiable risk factors such as hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and diabetes. We aim to assess control of these key factors in a representative cohort of stroke survivors residing in Catalonia, Spain. The analysis was conducted according to the current European Stroke Organisation (ESO) guidelines, with special emphasis on an older population.
METHODS: An observational, retrospective, longitudinal study was conducted using data from the population-based database of the Health Quality and Assessment Agency of Catalonia. Patients diagnosed with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) between 2014 and 2019 were included. Follow-up data comprised all measurements recorded during the first year after the index event. Data were collected on blood pressure, cholesterol, and HbA1c levels, as well as on pharmacological treatment, including antithrombotic agents. A comparative analysis was performed across age groups, focusing particularly on older people (> 67 years) and very older people (> 87 years) stroke survivors. In total, 35,918 patients were included in the analysis.
RESULTS: Of 35,918 included patients, 54% were men and the median age was 77 years (IQR 68-88); 9336 (23%) were older than 87 years. During the first year after stroke, blood pressure data were available for 63% of patients. Among them, 49% of individuals aged 18-67 years and 42% of the very older people achieved the target of < 130 mmHg. Despite blood tests with total cholesterol were available for 59%, LDL-cholesterol was specifically assessed only in 5% of patients, with 31% of the younger group and 35% of the very older people reaching the < 70 mg/dL target. Among patients with diabetes, HbA1c was assessed in 84%, and 81% of younger versus 83% of older people met the < 7% target. The prevalence of atrial fibrillation increased significantly with age; however, older people were less likely to receive oral anticoagulants (63% vs. 72-73%).
CONCLUSION: A substantial proportion of stroke survivors did not achieve the targets recommended by the ESO for secondary prevention. In the older people population, fewer patients reached optimal blood pressure control, and anticoagulant use among those with atrial fibrillation was suboptimal. Our findings highlight the need for structured post-stroke follow-up pathways, improved communication between stroke specialists and primary care physicians, and targeted interventions to optimize cardiovascular risk factor management in older people.

Title: Prognostic value of early point-of-care blood gas analysis in critically ill non-trauma patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department have a high risk of in-hospital mortality. While point-of-care diagnostics such as blood gas analysis are established tools for urgent management, data on their prognostic value in this specific patient cohort remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether initial blood gas parameters are independently associated with in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult critically ill non-trauma patients treated in the emergency department of a German university hospital. Initial blood gas parameters and clinical data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression to assess their association with in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Of 879 screened patients, 542 met the inclusion criteria. In-hospital mortality was 20% (n = 110). In addition to older age and out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, anemia (hemoglobin < 12 g/dL; OR of 2.07, 95% CI 1.20-3.58; p = 0.009), acidosis (pH < 7.35; OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.09-4.95; p = 0.033) and hypobicarbonatemia (< 22 mmol/L; OR 2.79, 95% CI 1.42-5.69; p = 0.004) were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. The association for hyperlactatemia was borderline (> 2.2 mmol/L; OR 1.85, 95% CI 0.93-3.77; p = 0.08). Multivariate analysis did not reveal significant associations between other electrolyte imbalances and in-hospital mortality in this cohort.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, the presence of anemia, acidosis or hypobicarbonatemia on admission to the resuscitation room were independently associated with an elevated risk of in-hospital mortality in critically ill non-trauma patients. These readily available point-of-care parameters may support early risk stratification. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

Title: Prognostic Impact of Diabetes Status on Outcomes After Physiology-Guided Revascularization　- Insights From the J-PRIDE Registry.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of diabetes status on outcomes after physiology-guided revascularization remains unclear. This study evaluated clinical outcomes in patients with insulin-treated diabetes (ITD), non-ITD (NITD), and without diabetes after physiology-guided revascularization.
METHODS AND RESULTS: From the J-PRIDE registry, 3,140 patients were categorized into non-diabetes (n=1,797), NITD (n=1,133), and ITD (n=210) groups. The primary endpoint was the 1-year incidence of target vessel failure (TVF), a composite of cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target vessel revascularization. The 1-year TVF rate was significantly higher in the ITD and NITD groups than in the non-diabetes group (6.1% and 4.1% vs. 2.0%, respectively), with adjusted hazard ratios for the ITD and NTD groups of 2.14 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-4.19; P=0.027) and 1.63 (95 CI 1.02-2.61; P=0.041), respectively. The non-hyperemic pressure ratio cut-off predicting fractional flow reserve (FFR) ≤0.80 was lower in the ITD than NITD and non-diabetes groups (0.87 vs. 0.89 and 0.90, respectively). The ITD group had the highest risk of TVF across all FFR values, followed by the NITD and non-diabetes groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with ITD and NITD exhibit worse clinical outcomes than those without diabetes. Notably, patients with ITD remained at elevated risk across the entire FFR spectrum, suggesting that physiological severity alone may not fully capture their residual cardiovascular risk.

Title: Magnesium Administration as a Treatment for Perioperative Atrial Fibrillation following Cardiac Surgery: Safety and Efficacy.
Journal: Annals of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery : official journal of the Association of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons of Asia
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common complication after cardiac surgery, impacting recovery and outcomes. Magnesium has electrophysiological and rate-controlling effects in AF. This study evaluated the safety and the temporal association between therapeutic intravenous magnesium administration and rhythm outcomes in patients with postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: Between January 2009 and December 2016, 714 patients undergoing cardiac surgery were evaluated. After excluding 49 patients with a history of AF, 130 developed new-onset POAF. Of these, 111 patients (85.4%) received intravenous magnesium according to our institutional protocol, whereas 19 patients (14.6%) did not. Magnesium (20 mEq per dose, 1-3 doses) was administered with other antiarrhythmic agents in 40 patients (36.0%) and as monotherapy in 71 patients (64.0%). The principal efficacy analyses were restricted to the magnesium-monotherapy cohort. Serum magnesium levels after administration were monitored in 35 patients.
RESULTS: Among the 71 patients treated with magnesium monotherapy, the heart rate significantly decreased from 114 ± 32.3 bpm to 100 ± 39.7 bpm (P <0.01), with no significant change in blood pressure. Sinus rhythm conversion occurred in 34 patients (47.9%) within 3 hours and in 60 patients (84.5%) within 24 hours. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, a higher preoperative serum magnesium concentration (adjusted OR, 1.31 per 0.1 mg/dL increase; 95% profile-likelihood CI, 1.07-1.65; P = 0.014) and later postoperative onset of POAF (adjusted OR, 1.32 per postoperative day; 95% CI, 1.07-1.68; P = 0.015) were associated with 3-hour conversion. No serious adverse events attributable to magnesium were observed in the monotherapy cohort. However, because no untreated-comparator group was available, spontaneous conversion cannot be distinguished from a treatment effect.
CONCLUSION: Intravenous magnesium monotherapy was associated with heart rate reduction without significant blood pressure deterioration and was followed by early sinus rhythm conversion in a substantial proportion of patients with POAF. These observational findings support the feasibility and apparent safety of this approach, but do not establish a causal antiarrhythmic effect. Prospective controlled studies are required.

Title: Joint associations of leisure-time physical activity and daily sitting time with mortality among US adults classified as CKM stages 0-3: a prospective cohort study of NHANES 2007-2018.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies have linked physical activity to cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) prevalence or mortality and sedentary behavior to CKM severity, and both behaviors are established mortality risk factors in the general population; however, prospective evidence on their joint associations with cause-specific mortality across CKM stages 0-3 remains limited.
METHODS: We analyzed 8,556 NHANES 2007-2018 participants aged ≥20 years with CKM stages 0-3, complete prespecified covariates, and a positive fasting-subsample weight. Leisure-time physical activity (LTPA) was categorized as inactive (0 min/week), insufficient (>0 to <150 min/week), or sufficient (≥150 min/week); daily sitting time was categorized as <6, 6 to <8, or ≥8 h/day. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; cardiovascular disease (CVD) and non-CVD mortality were secondary outcomes. Survey-design-based Cox models incorporated the 12-year fasting weight, strata, and primary sampling units. Multiplicative and additive interactions were assessed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 6.75 years, 670 deaths occurred, including 175 CVD and 495 non-CVD deaths. In fully adjusted models, sufficient versus no LTPA was associated with lower all-cause (hazard ratio [HR], 0.630; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.483-0.822), CVD (HR, 0.536; 95% CI, 0.297-0.969), and non-CVD mortality (HR, 0.662; 95% CI, 0.478-0.916). Sitting ≥8 versus <6 h/day was associated with higher all-cause (HR, 1.506; 95% CI, 1.253-1.810), CVD (HR, 1.845; 95% CI, 1.246-2.732), and non-CVD mortality (HR, 1.406; 95% CI, 1.109-1.782). Compared with sufficient LTPA and sitting <6 h/day, <150 min/week of LTPA combined with sitting ≥8 h/day was associated with all-cause (HR, 1.972; 95% CI, 1.429-2.721), CVD (HR, 2.493; 95% CI, 1.232-5.045), and non-CVD mortality (HR, 1.806; 95% CI, 1.202-2.712). Multiplicative interaction was not detected for all-cause (P = 0.951) or non-CVD mortality (P = 0.274); the CVD interaction signal (P = 0.016) was exploratory because it depended on a joint category with few events.
CONCLUSION: Higher LTPA and shorter sitting time were independently associated with lower mortality among US adults with CKM stages 0-3. Joint categories identified a higher-risk behavioral pattern, but did not establish that LTPA offsets the risk of prolonged sitting.

Title: Determinants and Clinical Impact of Direct Stenting in Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction　- An ATLAS-OCT Substudy.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct stenting (DS) is a simplified strategy for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); however, its role in the era of advanced intravascular imaging remains incompletely defined. We aimed to identify determinants of DS use and its impact on procedural efficiency and optical coherence tomography (OCT)-defined stent implantation quality in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The ATLAS-OCT trial was a prospective multicenter nationwide study mandating OCT guidance in Japan. In this subanalysis, clinical characteristics, angiographic and OCT findings, procedural metrics, and clinical outcomes were compared between patients undergoing DS and those treated with balloon predilatation. Among 436 patients, DS was performed in 32.1% (n=140), with marked interinstitutional variability (0-68.3%; P<0.01), suggesting a strong influence of operator preference. DS use was not associated with angiographic features or OCT-defined culprit plaque morphology. DS significantly reduced contrast volume and procedure time. Post-PCI OCT showed a trend towards a larger minimum stent area and greater stent expansion index with DS. These benefits were not associated with in-hospital or 1-year outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary OCT-guided primary PCI for STEMI, DS appears to be driven primarily by operator preference rather than lesion characteristics. In this study, DS was associated with improved procedural efficiency without significantly compromising OCT-assessed stent implantation quality or mid-term clinical safety.

Title: Incidence and predictors of urinary tract infections after sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor initiation in older adults hospitalized for heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors are recommended for heart failure treatment across the spectrum of ejection fraction; however, by promoting glycosuria, they may increase the risk of urinary tract infection, particularly in older adults.
AIMS: To assess the 6-month incidence of urinary tract infection following sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor initiation in older patients hospitalized for heart failure, and to identify associated factors.
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included patients aged≥75 years hospitalized for heart failure in geriatric and cardiology wards, and initiated on a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor between January 2022 and December 2024. The primary outcome was physician-diagnosed antibiotic-treated suspected urinary tract infection within 6 months, investigated using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 260 included patients, 147 were hospitalized in the cardiology ward and 113 in the geriatric ward. Physician-diagnosed antibiotic-treated suspected urinary tract infection was recorded in 45 patients, corresponding to 17.3% of the total cohort and 21.0% of patients with an ascertainable outcome; the upper bound under the extreme worst-case assumption was 35.0%. Incidence was higher in the geriatric ward than in the cardiology ward (26.6 vs. 10.2%). After age matching, female sex (odds ratio 3.15, 95% confidence interval 1.22-8.14), history of urinary tract infection (odds ratio 3.05, 95% confidence interval 1.25-7.42), diabetes mellitus (odds ratio 3.17, 95% confidence interval 1.32-7.60) and geriatric ward hospitalization (odds ratio 3.84, 95% confidence interval 1.62-9.07) were associated with increased odds of urinary tract infection, although only history of urinary tract infection remained robust across missing-outcome sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Suspected urinary tract infection was frequent after sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor initiation in hospitalized older adults. History of urinary tract infection was the most robust predictor, supporting individualized risk assessment and monitoring rather than routine prophylaxis.

Title: Correlation Between Respiratory Blood Flow Velocity Variation and Dynamic Preload Variables During Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery: A Pilot Observational Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate correlations between pressure-based dynamic preload indices and echocardiographic flow velocity variations during coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
DESIGN: Prospective observational pilot study.
SETTING: Single university hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: Thirty adults undergoing elective CABG.
INTERVENTIONS: Modified passive leg raising (PLR) at 3 intraoperative time points.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Mean arterial pressure increased after PLR at all 3 time points. In pooled analyses, stroke volume variation decreased from 13% ± 4% to 10% ± 4% and pulse pressure variation decreased from 10% ± 2% to 7% ± 3% (both p < 0.05). Respiratory peak velocity variations in the left ventricular outflow tract and descending aorta did not change significantly. Pulse contour-derived cardiac output also did not change (5.1 ± 1.1 L/min v 5.1 ± 1.1 L/min, p = 0.71). Stroke volume variation and pulse pressure variation correlated strongly (r = 0.720), whereas correlations between pressure- and flow-derived indices were weak (r = 0.147-0.351).
CONCLUSIONS: Pressure-derived indices correlated only weakly with echocardiographic respiratory peak velocity variations in patients undergoing CABG. As forward flow did not measurably increase following modified PLR, the physiological significance of these weak correlations remains uncertain.

Title: Association of serum complement levels with failure of low-density-lipoprotein-cholesterol target attainment in patients after acute coronary syndrome: A prospective, observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The interplay between inflammation and atherosclerosis is well acknowledged. However, the role of the complement system in lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association of serum-complement levels with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
METHODS: Adult hospitalized patients with ACS received rosuvastatin 40 mg with an LDL-C target of <55 mg/dL and a reduction of >50% of baseline. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein, complement C3c, C4, C5a levels, LDL-C, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and apolipoprotein B levels were measured before treatment initiation, 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months afterward. Patients were followed up for 12 months for major adverse cardiovascular events (nonfatal stroke, nonfatal myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death).
RESULTS: Among 130 patients (91.5% male; mean age 56 ± 9 years), 42 (32.3%) achieved the target at 6 weeks, 61 (46.9%) at 6 months, and 63 (48.5%) at 12 months. Serum C3c levels were lower at baseline in 6-week target achievers (median [Q1-Q3], 98.9 [86.9-107.3]) vs nonachievers (126.0 [112.0-136.0]; P < .001). Similarly, C4 levels were 21.4 (18.2-26.4) mg/dL in achievers vs nonachievers (26.8 [22.1-31.6] mg/dL; P < .001); C5a levels did not differ between groups. C3c predicted failure of target attainment at 6 weeks (area under the curve, 95% CI: 0.94, 0.90-0.98; P < .001). A cut-off value of 112.5 mg/dL demonstrated sensitivity 77.3%, specificity 92.3%, and independently predicted failure (adjusted odds ratio 52.54; 95% CI, 12.49-221.0).
CONCLUSION: In patients with ACS treated with rosuvastatin 40 mg, serum C3c levels are associated with failure of LDL-C target attainment. Further research is needed to determine if they may be used to guide LLT.

Title: Periprocedural Cardiac Hemodynamic Changes and Clinical Outcomes After Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt.
Abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To characterize serial changes in cardiac structure and function before and after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) using comprehensive echocardiographic assessment and to explore their clinical relevance.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 149 patients with decompensated cirrhosis who underwent TIPS between January 2018 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, within 5 days after TIPS, and at 3-6 months of follow-up. Additional echocardiographic parameters were assessed preoperatively and early after TIPS during hospitalization to further characterize periprocedural cardiac functional changes. Echocardiographic parameters were compared across time points using repeated-measures analysis or paired tests. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to examine associations with clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: After TIPS, right atrial diameter and right ventricular end-diastolic diameter increased significantly (both P < 0.001), accompanied by a modest increase in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.029), while left ventricular structure and systolic function showed no significant changes. The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio showed a numerical decrease early after TIPS, followed by partial recovery during follow-up, although the changes were not statistically significant. Among the additional echocardiographic parameters, color M-mode flow propagation velocity (Vp) increased significantly from 62.8 to 75.1 cm/s (P = 0.04), whereas E/A, E/e', and other diastolic parameters remained largely unchanged. During a median follow-up of 1057 days, one patient developed early postoperative heart failure. Survival and overt hepatic encephalopathy did not differ significantly among groups stratified by baseline E/A ratio.
CONCLUSION: In patients with relatively preserved baseline cardiac function following appropriate pre-TIPS cardiovascular assessment, TIPS was associated predominantly with mild and transient right-sided cardiac changes, without significant deterioration in conventional left ventricular systolic function. The low incidence of clinically overt cardiac decompensation observed during follow-up suggests an acceptable cardiac risk profile in appropriately evaluated patients.

Title: [Clinical characteristics and prognosis of patients with atrial functional mitral regurgitation].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical characteristics and prognosis of atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR). Methods: This was a single-center retrospective study. Patients hospitalized at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University between January 2020 and March 2022 and diagnosed with significant functional mitral regurgitation were enrolled. According to the type of regurgitation, patients were divided into the AFMR group and the ventricular functional mitral regurgitation (VFMR) group. Clinical and echocardiographic data were compared between the two groups. The patients were followed up until April 2024. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoint was the composite of cardiac death and hospitalization for heart failure. Survival was compared between the two groups using Kaplan-Meier survival curves. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with all-cause mortality in patients with functional mitral regurgitation. Results: The study cohort consisted of 269 patients, with a median age of 66.0 (57.5, 76.0) years, among whom 172 (63.9%) were male. Patients were divided into the AFMR group (n=61, 22.7%) and the VFMR group (n=208, 77.3%). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group had a higher proportion of female patients, older age, a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, lower prevalences of coronary artery disease, fewer patients with heart failure symptoms, and a lower proportion of prior visits to cardiovascular departments (all P<0.05). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group demonstrated significantly larger anteroposterior left atrial diameter, right atrial transverse diameter, and right ventricular transverse diameter, along with a higher LVEF and a higher prevalence of moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (all P<0.05). The follow-up duration was 24.6 (5.8, 37.6) months. The AFMR group exhibited lower all-cause mortality (21.3% (13/61) vs. 38.9% (81/208), P=0.011) and a lower rate of the composite endpoint of cardiac death and heart failure hospitalization (24.6% (15/61) vs. 42.8% (89/208), P=0.010) than the VFMR group. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis also revealed that the AFMR group had a higher cumulative event-free survival rate than the VFMR group (Plog-rank=0.002). Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression analysis demonstrated that age (HR=1.038, 95%CI 1.019-1.057, P<0.001), cerebrovascular disease (HR=2.014, 95%CI 1.200-3.382, P=0.008), AFMR (HR=0.341, 95%CI 0.175-0.667, P=0.002), and moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (HR=2.297, 95%CI 1.467-3.596, P<0.001) were independent predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with functional mitral regurgitation. Conclusions: Compared with VFMR, AFMR is more common among elderly patients, female patients, and patients with atrial fibrillation and is less frequently accompanied by heart failure symptoms. The rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure are both lower in the AFMR group than those in the VFMR group.

Title: [Dual association of peripheral blood eosinophil count with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and long-term cardiac death in patients with coronary artery disease: a large-scale cohort study].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the association of baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and its clinical prognostic value in patients with coronary artery disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and receiving clopidogrel. Methods: This was a single-center prospective cohort study. Consecutive patients with coronary artery disease who underwent PCI at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January and December 2013 were enrolled; those receiving dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and clopidogrel were included. Baseline data were collected, and platelet reactivity was assessed using thromboelastography. Patients were followed up for 5 years, with cardiac death as the endpoint. Baseline eosinophil count was analyzed as a continuous variable and was also categorized into quartiles (Q1-Q4). Multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze the association between eosinophil count and high on-treatment platelet reactivity. Multivariable restricted cubic spline models were used to analyze the dose-response relationship. Subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed according to age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to assess the predictive value of eosinophil count for cardiac death. Results: A total of 6 524 patients were included. The mean age was (58.21±10.26) years, and 5 059 (77.54%) were male. Among them, 6 050 patients completed the 5-year follow-up, and 140 cardiac deaths (2.31%) occurred. Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was negatively associated with the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (OR=0.94, 95%CI: 0.90-0.98, P=0.003). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the lowest quartile group (Q1), the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity was lower in patients in the highest quartile group (Q4) (OR=0.77, 95%CI: 0.65-0.91, P=0.003). Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis showed a linear negative correlation between eosinophil count and the risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity (P for overall=0.012, P for nonlinearity=0.362). Further subgroup analysis showed that the above association remained consistent across clinical subgroups stratified by age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, acute coronary syndrome, body mass index, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels (all P for interaction>0.05). Multivariable Cox regression analysis showed that peripheral blood eosinophil count was positively associated with the risk of cardiac death (HR=1.14, 95%CI: 1.07-1.21, P<0.001). When analyzed as a categorical variable, compared with the Q1 group, the risk of cardiac death was higher in patients in the Q4 group (HR=2.12, 95%CI: 1.25-3.59, P<0.001). Conclusions: In patients with coronary artery disease undergoing PCI and receiving clopidogrel, baseline peripheral blood eosinophil count showed a dual association with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and long-term cardiac death. A lower count was associated with an increased risk of high on-treatment platelet reactivity, whereas an elevated count was associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiac death.

Title: [The incidence and 1-year prognosis of heart failure following myocardial infarction during hospitalization in patients with first STEMI].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the incidence of in-hospital heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) and 1-year mortality in patients with first ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to compare the 1-year mortality risk among different types of HF. Methods: Data were derived from the Henan STEMI registry, which was a multicentre, prospective, observational study in central China. After excluding patients with a history of MI or HF, patients with first STEMI were divided into the HF and non-HF groups according to the occurrence of in-hospital HF. Based on the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measured on the last echocardiogram during hospitalization, patients with HF were classified into HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, LVEF≥50%), HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF, LVEF 41%-49%), HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF≤40%), and HF with missing LVEF. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and differences between groups were assessed with the log-rank test. Multivariate Cox frailty models were used to analyze the associations of HF status (present vs. absent) and different LVEF subgroups with 1-year mortality, using the non-HF group as the reference. Results: A total of 4 737 patients with first STEMI were included in the final analysis, with a median age of 62.8 (52.4, 70.8) years, of whom 1 158 (24.4%) were female. During hospitalization, 1 978 cases (41.8%) developed HF following MI, including 268 (13.5%) with HFrEF, 309 (15.6%) with HFmrEF, 707 (35.7%) with HFpEF, and 694 (35.1%) with missing LVEF. A total of 3 967 (83.7%) patients completed the 1-year follow-up. The 1-year mortality was significantly higher among STEMI patients complicated by HF than in those without (23.3% (391/1 680) vs. 5.8% (132/2 287), log-rank P<0.001). Specifically, the rates were 29.6% (67/226) for HFrEF, 20.8% (53/255) for HFmrEF, 11.7% (72/615) for HFpEF and 34.1% (199/584) for HF with missing LVEF. Multivariate Cox frailty models identified in-hospital HF following MI as a risk factor for 1-year mortality (HR=2.13, 95%CI: 1.70-2.67). Notably, HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk of 1-year mortality (HR=1.59, 95%CI: 1.16-2.17), while the HF group with missing LVEF carried the highest risk (HR=2.49, 95%CI: 1.91-3.26). Conclusions: The incidence of HF following first STEMI during hospitalization was 41.8%, with a corresponding 1-year mortality of 23.3%. In-hospital HF following MI is a risk factor for 1-year mortality in patients with STEMI. Prognosis differed notably across HF subgroups: HFpEF was associated with the lowest risk, whereas patients with missing LVEF had the worst outcome.
Publication Types: English Abstract; Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: [The predictive value of left ventricular strain on cardiac magnetic resonance for adverse events in children and adolescent patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy].
Journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the role of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS) derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature-tracking in evaluating left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), as well as its prognostic value for adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Methods: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study.
