Patients with primary HCM aged ≤21 years who underwent standard CMR examination at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January 2010 and December 2018 were included. Baseline clinical and CMR data were collected, and follow-up was completed. The primary endpoint was composite adverse cardiovascular events, and the secondary endpoint was heart failure-related events. Patients were divided into the event group and the non-event group according to whether the primary endpoint occurred. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Using the cohort median left ventricular GLS of -9.2% as the cut-off value, patients were stratified into the preserved GLS group (≤-9.2%) and the impaired GLS group (>-9.2%). Kaplan-Meier survival curves were plotted, and the log-rank test was performed to compare survival differences between groups. Results: A total of 249 children and adolescents with HCM were included, aged (14.81±3.71)years, of whom 163 were males (65.5%). The follow-up duration was (66.59±33.00)months. Composite endpoint events occurred in 37 patients, including 17 heart failure-related events and 20 sudden cardiac death events; 212 patients remained event-free. After adjusting for confounders such as left ventricular ejection fraction and history of unexplained syncope, multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that the percentage of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and left ventricular GLS were independently associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.18, 95%CI 1.04-1.35, P=0.014; LGE extent: HR=1.12, 95%CI 1.06-1.18,P<0.001) and heart failure-related events (left ventricular GLS: HR=1.52, 95%CI 1.18-1.96, P=0.001; LGE extent: HR=1.14, 95%CI 1.04-1.24, P=0.003). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with impaired left ventricular GLS had lower cumulative event-free survival for both composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events compared with those with preserved GLS (log-rank all P<0.001). Conclusions: CMR feature-tracking can effectively assess left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary HCM. Left ventricular GLS and LGE percentage are independently associated with the risk of adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events in this patient population.

Title: [The principles of trend-in-trend design and its applications in real-world causal inference].
Journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
Abstract: The trend-in-trend (TIT) design is an emerging hybrid ecological- epidemiological research method. Based on cumulative exposure probability stratification and cross-stratum temporal trend differentiation, TIT compares differences in outcome temporal slopes across populations with distinct exposure rates. When its core assumptions are met, TIT effectively controls unmeasured confounding by indication and time-varying confounding, thereby inferring causal associations between exposure and outcomes and yielding more robust effect estimates than traditional cohort studies. This article systematically elaborates the statistical principles and core assumptions of the TIT design, compares its methodological characteristics with quasi-experimental methods including difference-in-differences and interrupted time series, and illustrates its implementation procedures through a case study evaluating the cardiovascular risk of rofecoxib. As a reliable methodological tool for real-world study, TIT is particularly applicable to post-marketing drug re-evaluation and scenarios with strong temporal trends and unmeasured confounding.

Title: [Association between fine particulate matter exposure and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in urban and rural elderly population in Beijing].
Journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
Abstract: Objective: To understand the association between PM2.5 exposure and all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in elderly populations in urban and rural areas of Beijing. Methods: Based on the Beijing Elderly Comprehensive Health Cohort Study, a total of 3 472 study participants with complete baseline data were enrolled according to the inclusion and exclusion criteria, and the information about their survival and mortality outcomes were obtained by follow up. Annual average PM2.5 exposure values were matched using remote sensing grid data and grouped by tertiles. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the associations between PM2.5 exposure and all-cause as well as CVD mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to verify the robustness of the results. Additionally, the interaction between outdoor physical activity and PM2.5 exposure was evaluated. Results: The average annual PM2.5 concentration in living area of the study participants was 79.80 μg/m³ from 2010 to 2014 , much higher than the national grade Ⅱ limit (35 μg/m³). After adjusting for confounding factors, for each 1 μg/m³ increase in PM2.5 concentration, the risk for all-cause mortality increased by 5.3% (HR=1.053, 95%CI: 1.026-1.080), and the risk for CVD mortality increased by 4.6% (HR=1.046, 95%CI: 1.001-1.100). Subgroup analysis revealed a significant interaction between outdoor physical activity level and PM2.5 concentration on all-cause mortality (P=0.022). In the group without outdoor physical activity, each 1 μg/m³ increase in PM2.5 concentration was associated with an 8.7% increase of risk for all-cause mortality (HR=1.087, 95%CI:1.042-1.134); whereas in the group with outdoor physical activity, the risk increased by 2.6% (HR=1.026, 95%CI: 1.001-1.062). In the group with outdoor physical activity, compared with the reference group, the study participants in the highest PM2.5 T3 group had a 52.3% increased risk for all-cause mortality (HR=1.523, 95%CI:1.171-1.979) and a 79.1% increased risk for CVD mortality (HR=1.791, 95%CI: 1.004-3.192). Conclusions: PM2.5 exposure increases the risks for all-cause mortality and CVD mortality in the elderly population in urban and rural areas in Beijing. Regular physical activity might partially offset the adverse health effects of PM2.5 exposure, but this protective effect is limited under extremely high pollution levels. It is suggested to encourage the elderly to maintain regular physical activity but have indoor physical activity in days when air PM2.5 concentrations are high.

Title: Association of Iron Deficiency Anemia with Outcomes in Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently have iron deficiency anemia (IDA), but the mechanism by which this condition affects clinical outcomes is not well understood. The purpose of this study was to assess whether IDA is associated with mortality in patients with AF.
METHODS: Data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) for 2021-2022 examined IDA and inpatient outcomes in a nationally representative cohort of hospitalized adults diagnosed with AF. Patients were categorized by IDA status. The factors assessed were mortality, hospital and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, thromboembolic and cardiovascular complications, and overall hospital expenses. Hospital, clinical, and demographic factors were included in multivariable logistic and linear regression models.
RESULTS: Of the 8.35 million AF hospitalizations, 7.1% had associated IDA. IDA was linked to multiple comorbidities along with increased risk of hypotension (OR: 1.15, 95% CI 1.12-1.17, P<0.001), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.25, 95% CI 1.23-1.27, P<0.001), and heart failure (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR]: 1.29, 95% CI 1.27-1.31, P<0.001). Ironically, IDA was linked independently to decreased risks of cardiac arrest (AOR: 0.70, 95% CI 0.66-0.73, P<0.001), transient ischemic attack (AOR: 0.58, 95% CI 0.53-0.63, P<0.001), stroke (OR: 0.49,95% CI 0.47-0.51, P<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.66, 95% CI 0.64-0.68, P<0.001). IDA was also associated with increased hospital expenses and increased LOS (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: IDA was linked to higher morbidity and healthcare use in those with AF admitted to the hospital, but there was a decrease in mortality and thromboembolic events. These results suggest the possibility of tailored iron therapy and imply a complex interaction between IDA and AF-related outcomes.

Title: Impact of type 2 diabetes mellitus in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD): a study from the Australian National CHD Registry.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects approximately 1% of live births. Advances in diagnosis and treatment have markedly improved survival, resulting in a growing adult CHD population with an increasing burden of chronic disease. Here we investigate the prevalence and impact of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in patients with CHD.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Cohort study from the Australian National CHD Registry, linked to national administrative health data. Control patients without T2DM were selected from the Registry and matched 3:1 by age, sex, rurality, and CHD complexity.
RESULTS: Of the 58 523 individuals with CHD in the registry, 2077 (3.55%) were identified as having T2DM. Median age was 43.1 (IQR 32.0–57.9) years, and 51% were female. T2DM was associated with a hazard ratio for all-cause mortality or heart transplantation of 1.51 (95% CI 1.31 to 1.73; p<0.001). 27.6% of CHD patients with T2DM experienced any major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) versus 10.2% of controls (p<0.001). Patients with T2DM had a higher MACE rate (rate ratio 2.87, p<0.001) and had more MACE per patient (odds ratio 4.11, p<0.001) compared with controls. Individuals with T2DM also had significantly higher rates of emergency department presentations than controls (incidence rate ratio 2.35, p<0.001) and higher rates of hospital admissions (incidence rate ratio 2.87, p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: T2DM in patients with CHD is associated with significantly lower transplant-free survival, substantially increased MACE, and greater healthcare utilization compared to matched CHD controls.

Title: Effect of perioperative opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia on early postoperative sleep disturbance in adults undergoing elective non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery under general anaesthesia: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
INTRODUCTION: Early postoperative sleep disturbance is common after adult non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia and has been consistently associated with worse pain control, increased risk of postoperative delirium, impaired functional recovery and prolonged hospital stay, which imposes a significant burden on both patients and healthcare systems. Opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia is increasingly recommended within enhanced recovery after surgery pathways because it can effectively reduce opioid exposure while maintaining adequate analgesia; however, its specific effect on early postoperative sleep outcomes has not been systematically synthesised to date, leaving a critical gap in evidence-based perioperative care.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: We will conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials enrolling adults aged 18 years or older undergoing elective non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery under general anaesthesia. Eligible studies must evaluate a perioperative opioid-sparing multimodal analgesic strategy, with multimodality defined at the level of the overall perioperative analgesic regimen. A single investigational adjunct may be eligible when it has a perioperative analgesic role and is incorporated into a common background analgesic regimen, such that the intervention arm as a whole constitutes multimodal analgesia. Eligible comparators will include opioid-dominant analgesia, placebo, no additional intervention or a common or otherwise comparable background analgesic regimen without the opioid-sparing component of interest. The coprimary outcomes will be subjective sleep quality during the night of surgery or, if unavailable, during the night of postoperative day 1 (POD1), and the incidence of early postoperative sleep disturbance within 3 days after surgery (including the night of surgery). Secondary outcomes will include objective sleep parameters (eg, total sleep time and sleep efficiency), postoperative opioid consumption (converted to intravenous morphine milligram equivalents where possible), pain scores, patient-reported quality of recovery assessed using validated instruments, postoperative nausea and vomiting, delirium, length of hospital stay and intervention-related adverse events. We will search MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials and Web of Science Core Collection from inception to 30 April 2026 as the initial search cut-off date without language restrictions. The searches will be updated before the final analysis of the systematic review. ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform will also be searched for ongoing or unpublished trials, and the reference lists of included studies and relevant systematic reviews will be screened for additional eligible studies. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data and assess risk of bias (ROB) using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses will be performed where studies are clinically and methodologically comparable, and the certainty of evidence for the coprimary outcomes will be appraised using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval is not required because the review will synthesise only published aggregate data and will not involve identifiable patient information. Findings will be submitted to a peer-reviewed journal, presented at relevant scientific meetings, and disseminated through academic networks to inform clinical practice. Important protocol amendments will be documented in PROSPERO and in the final review.

Title: High-intensity interval training and moderate-intensity continuous training versus usual care in adults with familial hypercholesterolaemia: protocol for the UPPA-FH three-arm randomised trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) is an inherited disorder associated with lifelong exposure to elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c) and substantially increased risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Although intensive lipid-lowering therapy is the cornerstone of management, many individuals remain at elevated residual cardiovascular risk. Exercise training may improve cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), vascular function and cardiometabolic health; however, randomised evidence comparing different exercise modalities in adults with FH is lacking. The UPPA-FH trial aims to evaluate the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT), compared with usual care, on CRF, subclinical atherosclerosis and cardiometabolic health in adults with FH.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The UPPA-FH is a single-centre, three-arm, parallel-group superiority randomised controlled trial. 75 adults with genetically confirmed FH will be randomly allocated (1:1:1) to 16 weeks of supervised HIIT, supervised MICT or usual care. The primary outcome is change in maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max) from baseline to 16 weeks, measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Key secondary outcomes include markers of subclinical atherosclerosis (vascular inflammation, carotid intima-media thickness), arterial stiffness, biomarkers of cardiometabolic health (inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction and lipid metabolism), as well as body composition, physical function and estimated cardiovascular risk. The primary analyses will be conducted in the intention-to-treat population using a mixed model for repeated measures, adjusted for baseline outcome values and prespecified covariates. Treatment effects will be presented as adjusted between-group differences with corresponding 95% CIs. Confirmatory treatment comparisons will follow a prespecified fixed-sequence hierarchical testing procedure: (1) HIIT versus usual care; (2) MICT versus usual care and (3) HIIT versus MICT. Each comparison will be tested using a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study has been approved by the Biomedical Research Ethics Committee of Granada (reference 1417 N-23). Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences and communication with healthcare professionals and patient organisations.

Title: KDOQI Commentary on the 2025 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract: Hypertension prevention, diagnosis, and management are central to modifying the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although the nephrology community has long recognized CKD as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease, CKD has not historically been incorporated in cardiovascular risk prediction models. The new 2025 American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults addresses this gap by formally adopting the PREVENT calculator, which combines cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic health parameters to guide risk assessment and clinical decision making. The AHA/ACC guideline reinforces the broad blood pressure target of <130/80 mm Hg as well as makes recommendations for complex and resistant hypertension. Given the impact of these recommendations on persons living with kidney disease, the Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) convened an expert work group to review and comment on the guideline. This KDOQI commentary focuses on recommendations from the AHA/ACC guideline that are pertinent to individuals at risk of CKD or with non-dialysis-dependent CKD (stages 1-5), hence excluding commentary on hypertension management in patients receiving maintenance dialysis. In areas where the AHA/ACC guideline does not offer formal recommendations (eg, medication interactions, electrolyte imbalances, and kidney injury), the work group provides expert commentary about implications for people with CKD. Overall, the work group supports the majority of the AHA/ACC recommendations and identifies areas where evidence remains limited or management in CKD warrants additional consideration.

Title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nomenclature change from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) better encapsulates the associated metabolic milieu. While MASLD is associated with increased heart failure (HF) risk, characteristics and outcomes of MASLD in patients with HF remain unclear. This paper aims to examine the prevalence and clinical correlates of MASLD in patients with HF from the Asian Sudden Cardiac Death in Heart Failure (ASIAN-HF) Registry.
METHODS: MASLD was defined as evidence of hepatic steatosis, with at least one of five metabolic criteria (among body mass index, glucose, blood pressure, triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein thresholds). Findings were externally validated in Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS), a Hong Kong HF cohort and BIOlogy Study to TAilored Treatment in Chronic Heart Failure (BIOSTAT-CHF), a HF cohort across 11 European countries.
RESULTS: Of 2698 patients with HF in ASIAN-HF, 927 (34.4%) had MASLD. They were younger, more often women and more likely to have HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) compared with those without MASLD. All-cause mortality was lower in MASLD versus non-MASLD (7.1% vs 11.7%, p=0.001), even after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR (aHR) 0.58, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.86, p=0.007). All-cause mortality was also lower in MASLD versus non-MASLD in CDARS and BIOSTAT-CHF; however, after multivariable adjustment, the association remained significant only in CDARS (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.84, p<0.001) and was attenuated in BIOSTAT-CHF (aHR 1.08, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.73, p=0.750). Using waist-to-height ratio instead of body mass index in the MASLD definition reclassified <3% of patients.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HF, MASLD is highly prevalent, especially in younger women with HFpEF and is associated with better 1-year survival than in those without MASLD.

Title: Whether to hold and what to measure: perioperative euglycemic ketoacidosis in patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors.
Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used for type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, including in patients without diabetes. Their ketogenic effects may be amplified perioperatively by fasting, surgical stress, and volume loss, resulting in ketoacidosis without marked hyperglycemia. Reported frequencies depend on ascertainment. Where ketones were measured against a diagnostic threshold, cohorts reported 0-1.8% in non-cardiac and mixed populations and 0-15.1% in cardiac surgery; one prospective study using a lower threshold (≥ 0.6 mmol/L) reported a far higher figure, and studies without ketone measurement reported surrogate metabolic-acidosis endpoints of 30-41%. None of these are comparable incidence estimates. Severe and fatal cases have been reported. Because plasma glucose may be normal, diagnosis requires attention to acid-base status and ketones. Quantitative blood β-hydroxybutyrate is preferred when SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i)-associated ketoacidosis is suspected; urine ketone tests may screen when blood testing is unavailable, but a negative result does not exclude it. Perioperative guidance remains inconsistent: some bodies recommend withholding SGLT2i for 3 days (4 days for ertugliflozin), whereas others support risk-stratified continuation in selected patients under specified fasting and dietary conditions. No randomized trial has compared continuation with discontinuation using perioperative ketoacidosis as an endpoint; observational evidence remains limited and conflicting, and ketone thresholds and monitoring intervals lack prospective validation. This review summarizes evidence on recognition, diagnosis, withholding, monitoring, and postoperative restart.

Title: Low-grade inflammation and cardiovascular events among patients with chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
AIMS: Chronic inflammation is associated with cardiovascular disease in the general population, but data on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. We sought to assess whether systemic low-grade inflammation is independently associated with cardiovascular events in CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, with or without a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).
METHODS: CKD-REIN is a prospective cohort study of adults with CKD stages 2-5, conducted in 40 French nephrology outpatient facilities. Baseline high-sensitivity plasma C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was centrally measured using an immunoturbidimetric method. Systemic low-grade inflammation was defined as hs-CRP ≥2 mg/L. Cox proportional hazards models estimated cause-specific hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death) or hospitalization for heart failure (HHF).
RESULTS: We included 2078 patients: 67% men, mean (SD) age 67(13) years, mean eGFR 36(12) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38% with history of ASCVD, median hs-CRP concentration 2.4 mg/L (inter-quartile range 1.1-5.1). After median follow-up of 5 years, 171 patients had a MACE and 207 had HHF. After controlling for potential confounders, a twofold increase in hs-CRP was associated with a 12% (95% CI 0-26) higher cause-specific hazard of MACE and a 26% (95% CI 13-40) higher cause-specific hazard of HHF.
CONCLUSION: In CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, systemic low-grade inflammation, measured through hs-CRP, is associated with occurrence of cardiovascular events independently of traditional risk factors, including a history of ASCVD.

Title: Preoperative respiratory muscle strength, muscle mass, and respiratory sarcopenia as predictors of postoperative pulmonary complications after thoracic and cardiac surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after thoracic, upper abdominal, and cardiac surgery and are associated with adverse outcomes. Respiratory sarcopenia (RS), characterized by coexisting reductions in respiratory muscle mass and strength, may represent a clinically relevant prognostic phenotype, but its prognostic value remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess whether low preoperative respiratory muscle mass, reduced strength, or their coexistence as RS or probable RS predicts PPCs after thoracic and cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL from January 1990 to February 2026 for studies relating preoperative respiratory muscle mass, strength or flow, or RS to PPCs. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies tool. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects models after harmonizing effect directions such that ORs >1 denoted higher risk.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included; all involved thoracic or cardiac surgery, and none included an upper abdominal cohort. Cutoff-based respiratory muscle strength or flow impairment was associated with increased odds of PPCs (OR 2.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.50-3.37; I2 = 51.2%), with the most consistent association observed for percent-predicted peak expiratory flow (PEF) (OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.43-2.90; I2 = 0%). Continuous PEF was associated with PPCs, whereas ultrasound-based diaphragm indices showed smaller, non-significant associations. RS or probable RS was associated with PPCs (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.33-3.26; I2 = 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative functional respiratory muscle impairment, particularly reduced PEF, and RS or probable RS were associated with PPCs. Given that the evidence was limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly derived from thoracic surgery, prospective confirmation is needed.

Title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Cardio-Oncology: An Expert Consensus Statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance. Endorsed by the International Cardio-Oncology Society (ICOS).
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract: This document represents a position statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance (SCMR) on recommendations for clinical utilization of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with cancer. The document was prepared by the SCMR Consensus Group on CMR Imaging for Cardio-Oncology and endorsed by the SCMR Publications Committee and SCMR Executive Committee. This document aims to: (1) guide the informed selection and timing of CMR; (2) inform clinical decision-making based on CMR findings; (3) educate stakeholders on the advantages and limitations of CMR in specific clinical scenarios; and (4) provide suggested protocols to tailor the CMR exam to the particular clinical question. The statements of clinical utility presented in the current document focus on the following clinical scenarios: evaluating left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction and volumes; identifying pre-clinical left ventricular (LV) dysfunction with myocardial strain; and myocardial injury or edema with parametric mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE); myocarditis; vascular toxicity, with a focus on coronary artery disease (CAD); iron overload; cardiac amyloidosis; pericardial disease; valvular disease; pulmonary hypertension; and cardiac masses. Sections devoted to the special situations of radiation therapy (RT), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and survivorship and pediatrics are also included. As an expert consensus statement, some recommendations are based on expert opinion and accepted best practices. This position statement emphasizes the optimal utilization of CMR in oncology patients with known or suspected cardiovascular disease; however, the authors acknowledge that CMR is not always locally available or accessible. Finally, the principal aim of this position statement is to provide specific recommendations on the use of CMR to help improve the health of cancer patients with cardiovascular disease.

Title: Dual antithrombic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI: results from the ReDUAL PCI real life registry-based randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Balancing thrombotic and bleeding risk in patients requiring direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains challenging. This study evaluated the safety of dual antithrombotic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel in patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndrome or with high thrombotic risk.
METHODS: The ReDUAL PCI Real Life study was a Dutch, open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomized controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry (ZON-HR), aiming to enrol 850 patients. Patients requiring DOAC were randomized 1:1 to DOAC plus ticagrelor or DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI. The primary endpoint was any bleeding (BARC ≥2) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and net adverse clinical events (NACE: MACCE plus major bleeding). Outcomes were compared with a non-randomized ZON-HR cohort eligible for inclusion.
RESULTS: The study was terminated prematurely due to slow recruitment, with 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel). Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance. In 397 eligible non-randomized clopidogrel-treated patients, major bleeding rate was 3.4%, MACCE occurred in 12.5% and NACE in 14.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing PCI requiring oral anticoagulation, DOAC plus ticagrelor showed similar overall bleeding but numerical increase in major bleeding without apparent ischemic benefit compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel. This prematurely terminated study was underpowered, limiting abilities to draw definitive conclusions.

Title: Multimodality imaging for predicting regional wall motion recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting regional left ventricular (LV) functional recovery is essential for optimizing patient selection for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in chronic total occlusion (CTO), yet direct comparisons of imaging modalities remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), alone and in combination, for regional LV wall motion recovery after PCI for CTO.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We prospectively examined 66 patients with CTO undergoing successful PCI. Multimodality imaging was performed within 3 months prior to PCI. Wall motion recovery was defined as an improvement of ≥1 grade in segmental wall motion score assessed by resting echocardiography at 6 to 8 months post-PCI. Among 153 dysfunctional segments within the CTO territory, recovery was observed in 115 (75%). DSE at 20 μg/kg/min demonstrated high sensitivity (96.5%), CMR demonstrated high specificity (68.4%), and SPECT showed moderate sensitivity (76.5%) and specificity (52.6%). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of CMR and DSE (0.819) was comparable to that of all three modalities combined (0.825) and significantly exceeded that of any single modality (CMR: 0.738, DSE: 0.733; both P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CTO undergoing PCI, multimodality imaging provides complementary information for predicting regional LV wall motion recovery. An imaging strategy in which modalities are selected and combined according to the clinical context may help optimize decision-making for revascularization.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000046847). Short tweet: Can multimodality imaging predict LV wall motion recovery after PCI for chronic total occlusion? Combining dobutamine stress echo and cardiac MRI matched 3-modality performance, aiding CTO revascularization decisions. #CTO #CardioTwitter.

Title: The triglyceride-glucose index and intramyocardial hemorrhage identify a high-risk phenotype in STEMI.
Abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic value of combining the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) in STEMI is unclear. We assessed their individual and combined association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 456 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. TyG index was calculated from admission blood samples; IMH was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was MACE (median follow-up 4 years). Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, incremental prognostic assessment (C-index, NRI, IDI), and interaction testing were performed.
RESULTS: MACE increased across TyG tertiles (15.79% → 27.63% → 43.42%). The highest tertile remained independently associated with MACE (adjusted HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.09-3.20). Patients with high TyG (≥8.66) plus IMH had the worst prognosis (HR 4.00; 95% CI 2.49-6.39; P < 0.001), far exceeding either factor alone. Adding the combined variable to a base model improved discrimination and reclassification (C-index 0.640 → 0.658; NRI = 0.216, P = 0.020; IDI = 0.025, P = 0.008). Neither additive nor multiplicative interaction was significant, and results were consistent in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. A significant interaction was observed between TyG index and infarct location (P for interaction = 0.037), with a stronger effect in anterior (HR 1.59) than non-anterior infarction (HR 0.75).
CONCLUSIONS: The TyG index independently predicts long-term MACE in STEMI. Combining high TyG with IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with a 4.0-fold higher MACE risk and incremental prognostic value. The TyG effect is stronger in anterior infarction, suggesting infarct location should be considered in metabolic risk stratification.

Title: Clinical phenotypes, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic signatures in inflammatory myocardial disease: A prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory myocardial disease encompasses diverse clinical phenotypes, from subtle symptoms to fulminant heart failure. Differentiating myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis (CS), and non-confirmed cardiomyopathy (NC) remains diagnostically and prognostically challenging. We compared clinical presentation, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic profiles across these groups.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 218 adults undergoing evaluation for cardiomyopathy were classified as myocarditis (n = 81), CS (n = 84), or NC (n = 53). The primary composite outcome was all-cause mortality, mechanical circulatory support, or heart transplantation. RNA sequencing of endomyocardial biopsies was performed in 53 patients with differential expression analysis adjusted for age, RNA integrity number, and systolic blood pressure.
RESULTS: Patients with myocarditis were younger than those with CS or NC (34.7 ± 15.8 vs 57.4 ± 8.7 vs 57.6 ± 14.0 years); 70-75% were male. Myocarditis was characterized by chest pain and elevated inflammatory biomarkers, whereas CS was associated with arrhythmias and right ventricular dysfunction. Although unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested differences in event-free survival, adjusted Cox regression showed no significant between-group differences (myocarditis vs NC: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.22-4.43, p = 0.985; CS vs NC: HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.63-4.43, p = 0.307). Transcriptomic profiling revealed a more pronounced inflammatory gene expression profile in myocarditis, whereas CS showed limited differential expression and substantial overlap with NC.
CONCLUSIONS: Inflammatory myocardial disease shows distinct clinical presentations, while adjusted analyses did not demonstrate significant differences in long-term outcomes. Myocarditis showed a stronger inflammatory transcriptional signature, whereas CS exhibited limited transcriptomic differences. These findings support further investigation of RNA-based profiling as a complementary tool.

Title: Hemoadsorption to prevent acute kidney injury in elective cardiac surgery: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials with meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) improves postoperative outcomes compared with the standard of care.
METHODS: We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing hemoadsorption versus standard care in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Data were analyzed using a frequentist approach and trial sequential analysis (TSA). The primary outcome was the incidence of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) within 7 days after surgery. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025634991).
RESULTS: A total of six RCTs comprising 798 patients were included. Four RCTs (n = 723; 355 hemoadsorption, 368 control) reported CSA-AKI incidence, which did not significantly differ between groups (RR = 0.93 [95% CI: 0.71-1.21], p =  0.57; I² = 42.0%). Hemoadsorption was not associated with significant differences in secondary outcomes: interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor, 28-day mortality, SOFA score, and ICU length of stay.
CONCLUSION: Hemoadsorption during CPB was not associated with a reduction in CSA-AKI or with improvement in secondary clinical outcomes in elective patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, the accrued sample represented only 48% of the heterogeneity-adjusted required information size (1,491 patients), and the cumulative Z-curve crossed neither the monitoring nor the futility boundary.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO International Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025634991; January 31, 2025).

Title: Initiation of Apixaban Versus Warfarin in Patients With Kidney Failure on Hemodialysis With Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation: A Target Trial Emulation.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Patients with kidney failure on hemodialysis (KFHD) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at high risk of ischemic stroke. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) may reduce this risk but at the expense of excess bleeding. We emulated a randomized comparative effectiveness trial of apixaban versus warfarin initiation in patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF.
STUDY DESIGN: Trial emulation embedded in the US Renal Data System.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Medicare-insured patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF without recent OAC use (2014-2019).
EXPOSURES: Initiation of apixaban versus warfarin within 30 days from AF diagnosis.
OUTCOMES: Ischemic stroke, clinically important bleeding (co-primary outcomes). Other thromboembolic and bleeding events, death (secondary).
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: We compared propensity-matched new users of apixaban and warfarin using Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Among previously OAC-naïve patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed with AF, 3985 initiated apixaban and 6426 initiated warfarin. Propensity matching 3978 apixaban users with 3978 warfarin users balanced all measured characteristics. Median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4 (IQR: 3-5). Apixaban was initiated a median 6 (IQR: 3-12) days after AF and used for a median 58 (IQR:37-135) days; warfarin was initiated a median 5 (IQR: 2-12) days after AF and used for a median 93 (IQR:38-238) days. In intention-to-treat analyses, rates of ischemic stroke were 34% lower (HRITT=0.66; 95%CI, 0.47-0.94; p=0.02) and rates of clinically important bleeding were 28% lower (HRITT=0.72; 95%CI, 0.63-0.83; p<0.001) in patients who initiated apixaban. All-cause mortality did not differ between groups; neither did negative control outcomes of hip fracture and pneumonia. Results were robust when restricting analyses to patients with CHA2DS2-VASc score of ≥2.
LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding.
CONCLUSIONS: Initiating apixaban soon after newly diagnosed AF was associated with lower risks of ischemic stroke and clinically important bleeding compared with initiating warfarin.

Title: Doxapram increases respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood lactate concentration in juvenile green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the physiologic effects of IM doxapram compared to a control on respiratory rate, heart rate, venous blood gas, electrolytes, glucose, and lactate parameters in clinically healthy, rehabilitated juvenile green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas).
METHODS: In a randomized, complete crossover design completed from 2023 through 2025 with a 24-hour washout period, juvenile green sea turtles (2.9 to 7.6 kg) under care at a sea turtle rehabilitation center received either IM doxapram (5 mg/kg) or 0.9% sodium chloride (equivalent volume) in the pectoral muscle. Turtles were left unstimulated out of water, and venous blood was collected for blood gas, electrolyte, glucose, and lactate evaluation at 0, 30, and 60 minutes. Serial heart and respiratory rates (0 to 60 minutes) were collected by a blinded observer. Data were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models (P < .05).
RESULTS: 8 turtles were included. Doxapram administration resulted in significantly higher respiratory rate (5 to 30 minutes; 2.3 to 3.9 times higher), heart rate (15 to 60 minutes; 9.1 to 10.2 beats/min higher), and blood lactate concentration (30 to 60 minutes; 1.6 to 2.5 times higher) compared to control.
CONCLUSIONS: IM doxapram, 5 mg/kg, increased respiratory rate and heart rate for up to 30 and at least 60 minutes, respectively, and increased blood lactate concentration for at least 60 minutes in juvenile green sea turtles.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: While net effects of oxygenation are unknown, potential outcomes should be evaluated, and clinical discretion should be used when considering doxapram administration as a short-lived respiratory and/or cardiac stimulant in juvenile green sea turtles.

Title: Weight loss during intermittent fasting, not Mediterranean diet quality alone, is associated with lower inflammation: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract: Whether the anti-inflammatory effects of a Mediterranean diet reflect diet quality itself or accompanying weight loss is unclear. In a 16-week randomized controlled-feeding trial, 53 adults (77% female; mean age 54.7 years) with metabolic risk factors received a fully provided Mediterranean diet or their habitual western diet for 8 weeks, then added twice-weekly fasting days for a further 8 weeks. The primary outcome, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, did not change during the diet-only phase despite clear dietary separation. After fasting began, C-reactive protein fell in the Mediterranean-diet group relative to controls, alongside greater weight loss, improved insulin sensitivity, and lower blood pressure; lipid improvements had already emerged during the diet-only phase. Multi-omic analyses showed parallel reductions in inflammatory signaling, with gut microbiome composition largely stable. Thus, diet quality alone does not lower inflammation over 8 weeks; negative energy balance and weight loss during fasting appear to be the stronger drivers. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02148458).

Title: COVID-19 severity among individuals with chronic diseases.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies reported that individuals with underlying chronic diseases who are infected with COVID-19 are at greater risk for more severe outcomes. In this study, we measured these risks among a wide range of comorbidities in a large cohort.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analyzed the risk for hospitalization and the severity and mortality risk of COVID-19 among adults with obstructive lung diseases, hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, kidney diseases, malignancies and immunosuppression states before the emergence of the Omicron variant. We used univariant analyses and adjusted for age, sex, Body Mass Index (BMI), smoking habits, Socioeconomic Status (SES) and the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).
RESULTS: Of the 44,866 individuals who were positive for COVID-19, 2358 were hospitalized. The adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) for hospitalization was significantly greater for most chronic diseases, with the highest risk for individuals who underwent a kidney transplant (15.06; 95% Confidence Interval [95% CI 7.86-28.73]). A significantly greater risk for severe COVID-19 than for mild to moderate disease (602 and 1657 patients, respectively) was found for patients with cerebrovascular diseases (aOR = 1.46; 95% CI 1.07-1.99). A greater mortality risk was demonstrated for individuals who had undergone kidney transplantation (aOR = 4.23; 95% CI 1.36-11.82) and those with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) (aOR = 1.43; 95% CI 1.02-1.99).
CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with cerebrovascular disease were at increased risk for severe COVID-19, whereas individuals with CKD and past kidney transplantation were at increased mortality risk. These individuals should receive early medical intervention when they are diagnosed.

Title: Cardiovascular disease-specific mortality after partial versus radical nephrectomy for stage II renal cancer: A SEER-based propensity-matched analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgery remains standard treatment for localized renal cancer. Whether partial nephrectomy (PN), compared with radical nephrectomy (RN), affects long-term cardiovascular disease-specific mortality (CVD-SM) in stage II disease is uncertain. We assessed this association using competing-risk methods.
METHODS: Patients with T2N0M0 renal cancer diagnosed in the SEER database from 2004 to 2022 were included. Missing tumor grade and unspecified T2 subclassification were addressed by multiple imputation. Propensity-score matching was performed within 10 imputed datasets. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Fine-Gray models were primary, with cause-specific Cox models as supportive analyses; estimates were pooled across imputations.
RESULTS: The cohort included 14,602 patients (PN, n = 1294; RN, n = 13,308), with a median follow-up of 85 months. After matching, 1290-1292 patients per group were retained. Five-year CVD-SM cumulative incidence was 2.68% after PN and 3.07% after RN; 10-year estimates were 7.18% and 6.63%, respectively. No significant association was observed (Fine-Gray sHR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.69-1.74; P = 0.690; Cox HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.66-1.64; P = 0.867). PN was associated with lower cancer-specific mortality (Fine-Gray sHR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.42-0.80; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with stage II renal cancer, surgical approach was not significantly associated with CVD-SM. However, estimate imprecision and unavailable cardiovascular and renal risk factors preclude claims of equivalence or exclusion of clinically meaningful effects. The potential cardiovascular benefit of PN remains uncertain. Its lower cancer-specific mortality should be interpreted cautiously because residual surgical-selection confounding may persist.
SYNOPSIS: Cardiovascular disease-specific mortality represents an important long-term competing risk in patients with stage II renal cancer. No statistically significant association between surgical approach and cardiovascular disease-specific mortality was detected, leaving the cardiovascular survival advantage of partial nephrectomy uncertain.

Title: Impact of diabetes mellitus on clinical outcome in burns patients managed in a national burns centre.
Journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of diabetes mellitus on outcomes following burn injury remains unclear. This study aimed to characterise diabetic burn patients and their outcomes at a national burns centre.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed at the National Burns Unit, St. James's Hospital, Dublin, reviewing admissions from 2012 to 2022. Patients with complete data (n = 870) were divided into diabetic (n = 55) and non-diabetic (n = 815) groups. Demographics, comorbidities, injury characteristics, complications, length of stay and mortality were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was conducted to determine the association between diabetes and mortality, adjusting for age and total body surface area (TBSA).
RESULTS: Diabetic patients were older (mean age 65.6 vs 47.8 years, p <0.001) and had increased rates of cardiovascular, respiratory and renal comorbidities. They experienced more complications including acute decompensated heart failure, acute kidney injury and urinary tract infection. Median length of stay was longer (13 vs 9 days, p <0.001). Mortality was higher in diabetic patients on univariable analysis (13% vs 4.4%; OR 3.16, 95% CI 1.33 - 7.46, p = 0.009). However, after adjusting for age and TBSA, diabetes was no longer significantly associated with mortality (Adjusted OR 1.29, 95% CI 0.41 - 4.10, p = 0.667).
CONCLUSION: At Ireland's national burns centre, diabetic burn patients were older, more comorbid, suffered greater morbidity and required longer hospital stays. Their higher mortality rate may be attributable to increased age rather than diabetes itself. These single-centre findings require confirmation elsewhere.

Title: Effects of atropine on hemodynamic parameters following electroconvulsive therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) plays an important role in the treatment of refractory psychiatric disorders. However, it poses hemodynamic risks, such as blood pressure and heart rate elevation, arrhythmias, and transient asystole. Although atropine administration during ECT was considered a standard procedure in Western countries until the 1970s, in recent years, its use is generally limited to patients at high risk of bradycardia and asystole. We performed this meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to understand the effects of atropine on post-ECT hemodynamics and adverse events.
METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Embase was conducted to identify RCTs investigating the relationship between atropine administration and post-ECT hemodynamics through September 30, 2025. The primary outcomes included maximum heart rate and maximum blood pressure after ECT, as well as the incidence of ECT-related adverse events. The secondary outcomes included seizure duration, arrhythmia incidence, severe salivation, and cognitive function.
RESULTS: Of the 2465 studies identified, eight RCTs were included in the meta-analysis. Maximum heart rate after ECT was significantly higher in the atropine group (p < .001). There was no significant difference in the risk of serious adverse cardiovascular events requiring intervention. Bradyarrhythmia was significantly less frequent in the atropine group (risk ratio 0.35, p < .0001).
CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first meta-analysis to evaluate the hemodynamic effects of atropine administration during ECT. The findings suggest that atropine increases maximum heart rate after ECT reduces the incidence of bradyarrhythmia. Although no increased risk of cardiovascular adverse events requiring intervention was observed, the small sample size remains an important limitation.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero) registration number: CRD 42022346729.

Title: Right ventricular function across different non-invasive respiratory support strategies in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) systolic impairment is clinically relevant in acute respiratory failure, but its relationship with respiratory support modality in severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) outside the intensive care unit (ICU) is poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: To compare RV longitudinal systolic performance and hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), or Venturi-mask oxygen therapy.
METHODS: In this single-centre prospective observational study, adults with severe CAP (Pneumonia Severity Index class IV-V) requiring high-concentration oxygen or non-invasive respiratory support were enrolled. The modality was selected in the emergency department according to the treating physician's clinical and gas-exchange assessment. Echocardiography was performed shortly after ward admission while patients remained on the initial support modality.
RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (NIV, n = 21; HFNC, n = 22; Venturi mask, n = 27). Baseline demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics were comparable across groups. TAPSE and lateral tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S') showed a graded pattern, with the lowest values during NIV, intermediate values during HFNC, and the highest values with the Venturi mask (p < 0.001 for both). Mean LOS was 27.8 ± 5.0, 27.4 ± 2.9, and 15.2 ± 4.0 days, respectively (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, age and respiratory support modality were associated with LOS.
CONCLUSIONS: RV systolic performance and LOS differed across clinically selected respiratory support groups. These associations may reflect clinical severity rather than device-related effects. These findings reinforce the often-overlooked clinical importance of RV assessment in acute respiratory failure, extending observations from ARDS cohorts to severe CAP outside the ICU.

Title: Early Rhythm Control vs Usual Care After Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Early rhythm control reduces cardiovascular events in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF); however, its effectiveness in the setting of acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. We aimed to examine whether early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of recurrent stroke or systemic embolism (SE) in patients with AF.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study used the DeSC-IQVIA integrated database, an administrative claims database covering approximately 16 million individuals in Japan. Adults hospitalized for acute ischemic stroke with AF present at admission between 2014 and 2025 were included. The exposure was initiation of rhythm control (antiarrhythmic drugs, catheter ablation, or electrical cardioversion) within 8 weeks of admission (early rhythm control) vs no initiation (usual care), assessed at a landmark. The primary outcome was hospitalization for recurrent ischemic stroke or SE. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. Baseline differences were adjusted using propensity score overlap weighting. Cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs), cumulative incidence with death as a competing risk, and risk differences at 5 years were estimated.
RESULTS: Among 14,355 patients who survived event-free through the 8-week landmark (median age, 83 years [IQR, 78-88]; 6,935 [48.3%] women), 268 (1.9%) received early rhythm control. During 23,583 person-years, early rhythm control was associated with a lower risk of stroke/SE (HR, 0.56; 95% CI 0.32-0.97; weighted 5-year cumulative incidence, 8.0% vs 13.8%; risk difference, -5.9 percentage points [95% CI -11.0 to 0.8]). Among secondary outcomes, no association was observed with major bleeding (HR, 1.44; 95% CI 0.74-2.82) or HF hospitalization (HR, 0.73; 95% CI 0.39-1.38); early rhythm control was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.72; 95% CI 0.53-0.97). Results were consistent across landmark periods of 4-24 weeks.
DISCUSSION: In this nationwide cohort study, early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke in patients with AF was associated with a reduced risk of recurrent stroke or SE. These findings suggest that early rhythm control may serve as an additional secondary prevention strategy for ischemic stroke, with flexible timing of initiation. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

Title: 25 Years of Cardiac Ion Channel QSAR: From hERG Dominance to Multi-Channel Modeling.
Journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
Abstract: In 2013 the Comprehensive In Vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) initiative proposed multi-channel assessment for proarrhythmic risk evaluation, yet ligand-based predictive modeling has remained largely single-channel. To quantify and explain this mismatch, we survey 155 ligand-based modeling studies on cardiac ion channels (including conventional QSAR, machine learning, and pharmacophore- and other 3D ligand-based approaches) published between 2001 and mid-2026. Across this period, 88.4% of studies target hERG as their sole ion channel endpoint, a proportion that reflects data availability, regulatory incentives, and research inertia rather than scientific necessity. Although public data for Nav1.5 and Cav1.2 were sufficient for modeling years earlier, both channels received only isolated studies until 2022. Since then, multi-channel modeling has expanded substantially, with multiple groups now addressing the primary channels (hERG, Nav1.5, and Cav1.2) jointly. In contrast, the secondary channels (Kv7.1, Kv4.3, and Kir2.1) remain largely understudied: Kv4.3 and Kir2.1 are entirely unmodeled in the surveyed literature, and models for Kv7.1 remain scarce, likely due to the sparsity and heterogeneity of public data. A retrospective analysis of the reported model performance found no discernible improvements attributable to methodological advances. Reliability-related aspects, such as applicability domain and uncertainty quantification, were also rarely addressed. The field should treat joint modeling of the primary channels as the expected standard rather than a novel contribution. Other important aspects include the development of standardized benchmarks for multi-channel evaluation, integration with physiological models, and greater emphasis on prediction reliability. For the secondary channels, progress would additionally require coordinated data release or federated learning, methods suited to data-scarce targets, and community coordination, none of which individual research groups can establish alone.

Title: Changes of serum fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) and Klotho in diabetic kidney disease and their correlation with coronary artery calcification: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association among fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), Klotho, and coronary artery calcification (CAC) in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD).
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: A total of 176 DKD patients and 160 age-and diabetes-matched controls were retrospectively analyzed. We measured serum FGF23 and Klotho levels by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and assessed CAC by CAC scoring. Correlation and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of these biomarkers with CAC and their ability to discriminate CAC.
RESULTS: FGF23 levels were significantly higher and Klotho levels were lower in patients with DKD than in controls. FGF23 correlated negatively with estimated glomerular filtration rate and positively with the albumin-to-creatinine ratio and blood urea nitrogen, whereas Klotho correlated positively with estimated glomerular filtration rate and negatively with albumin-to-creatinine ratio and blood urea nitrogen. In patients with CAC, FGF23 levels were higher and Klotho levels were lower. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that both FGF23 and Klotho discriminated CAC, and FGF23 showed a higher area under curve than Klotho. Correlation analysis further confirmed the association of FGF23 and Klotho with CAC severity.
CONCLUSION: FGF23 and Klotho were associated with renal impairment and CAC in patients with DKD and may serve as potential biomarkers of renal and cardiovascular risk.

Title: The impact of recreational beach tennis associated with nutritional counseling on cardiometabolic risk factors in adolescents: a randomized clinical trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether combining nutritional counseling with recreational sports confers greater improvements in cardiovascular risk factors among adolescents compared to recreational sports alone.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This 12-week randomized clinical trial included 40 adolescents (aged 11-14 years; 67% female; 45% overweight/obese) randomly assigned to a beach tennis (BT, n = 20) or BT plus nutrition counseling (BT+N, n = 20) group. Sports sessions (BT) were performed twice a week and nutritional counseling (BT+N) once a week. Outcomes assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks included biochemical parameters (high- and low-density lipoprotein, total cholesterol; triglycerides; fasting glucose; and insulin), blood pressure, and body composition. Analyses were performed following the intention-to-treat principle.
RESULTS: Both groups showed significantly higher high-density lipoprotein levels (BT: +3.8 mg/dL, p < 0.05; BT+N: +5.9 mg/dL, p < 0.001) and no differences between groups. Fasting glucose decreased only in the BT+N group. Time x group interactions significantly differed between groups for triglycerides (p < 0.01), waist circumference (p < 0.001), body fat percentage (p < 0.05), and systolic blood pressure (p < 0.001), favoring the BT+N group. No significant changes were observed in low-density lipoprotein, total cholesterol, or insulin levels.
CONCLUSION: Recreational BT alone improved some cardiometabolic parameters; however, its combination with nutritional counseling provided broader benefits, underscoring the value of integrated lifestyle interventions for reducing cardiometabolic risk factors in adolescents.

Title: Workplace and age associated with severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies: a nationwide study in Japan.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Among working-age populations globally, occupational injuries and workplace cardiovascular emergencies remain major contributors to morbidity and mortality. This study examined the associations between workplace settings, age groups, and the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective registry-based observational study using emergency medical services data from Japan, including 454 043 working-age individuals recorded in 2021-2023. Workplace settings (office, indoor worksite, factory, outdoor worksite, construction, agriculture, and others) and age groups were analysed in relation to event severity, categorized as non-life-threatening or life-threatening. Multivariable regression models estimated the associations, and workplace-age interactions were assessed.
RESULTS: Compared with office settings, all other workplaces were associated with higher odds of life-threatening injuries, particularly agriculture and construction. Increasing age groups were progressively associated with greater injury severity. The workplace setting was associated with the severity of stroke and ischaemic heart disease, particularly in uncontrolled outdoor environments. Stroke severity was elevated in those aged 45-59 and 60-69 years, while all older age groups were associated with severe ischaemic heart disease. Workplace-age interactions were significant only for occupational injuries.
CONCLUSIONS: Workplace and age were interactively and independently associated with the severity of occupational injuries and cardiovascular emergencies.

Title: Association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and functional outcomes in elderly patients receiving ferric carboxymaltose: a retrospective observational cohort study.
Abstract: Anemia and iron deficiency (ID) are extremely common comorbidities in elderly patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), and are associated with reduced functional capacity and worse prognosis. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association of one-year therapy with SGLT2i as add-on to intravenous infusion of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) with improvement in functional abilities, in a cohort of elderly patients with HFrEF/HFmrEF with ID anemia. This study enrolled outpatients with CHF with ID anemia receiving intravenous administration of FCM and stratified into two groups according to SGLT2i use. The study endpoint was an achievement of Short physical performance battery (SPPB)>8pt at one year of follow-up. 222 patients, with a mean age of 75.5±6.0 years were enrolled and 53 received SGLT2i while 169 not. After 1 year of follow-up, a significant improvement in the main clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic and CGA parameters were observed in both groups; however, these improvements were statistically greater in those patients receiving also SGLT2i. The mean dose of FCM administered to the entire population at baseline was 734.2 ± 331.7 mg, with no significant differences between the two groups (p=0.475). Add on therapy with SGLT2i was associated with a greater improvement in functional abilities (OR 7.66; CI 95% 3.70-15.9, p<0.0001), while the presence of obesity was associated with a reduced probability of functional abilities improvement of 68% (OR 0.32; CI 95% 0.14-0.71, p=0.005). In patients with CHF and ID anemia, improvements in clinical symptoms and physical function were observed at one-year follow-up, as reflected by changes in SPPB scores. These improvements were greater among patients receiving concomitant SGLT2i therapy.

Title: Decoding the Safety Profile of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: Facts, Myths, and Ongoing Controversies.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) represent one of the most significant therapeutic advances in the management of type 2 diabetes and obesity. As their indications have expanded to include cardiovascular and kidney disease, safety concerns involving multiple organ systems have received increasing attention. This narrative review examines the spectrum of adverse effects linked to GLP-1RAs and provides a clinically relevant platform for assessing their safe prescription.
RECENT FINDINGS: Gastrointestinal intolerance, modest increases in heart rate, and a modest but reproducible increase in the risk of gallbladder and biliary disease represent the most consistently supported adverse effects of GLP-1RAs. A risk of pancreatitis is also considered to exist, although some studies have challenged this association. Conversely, correlations with neuropsychiatric and dermatological disorders, diabetic retinopathy, nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, perioperative aspiration, sexual and reproductive disturbances, sarcopenia, and malignancy remain controversial. Most available evidence derives from pharmacovigilance databases, retrospective observational studies, and secondary analyses of randomized trials, which are limited by reporting bias, residual confounding, and inability to establish causality. Heterogeneity in study design, statistical methodology, outcome definitions, and patient populations further complicates interpretation. Although several proposed adverse effects have biologically plausible mechanisms, prospective clinical validation remains limited. Notably, recent regulatory decisions, including the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)'s removal of the suicidality warning from GLP-1RA prescribing information, reflect the evolving nature of these safety assessments. The overall benefit-risk profile of GLP-1RAs is favorable. Most emerging safety concerns should currently be regarded as hypothesis-generating signals rather than established toxicities. Individualized risk assessment and appropriate clinical monitoring remain important as ongoing and future prospective studies further define the long-term safety of this rapidly expanding therapeutic class.

Title: Real-World Effectiveness and Tolerability of Rimegepant as Second- or Third-Line Acute Treatment for Migraine: A Prospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rimegepant is an oral calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist approved for both acute and preventive treatment of migraine. However, limited information is available regarding its effectiveness and tolerability when used as a second- or third-line acute treatment in patients for whom triptans and/or lasmiditan are ineffective, poorly tolerated, contraindicated, or otherwise unsuitable. This study evaluated the effectiveness and tolerability of rimegepant in this real-world clinical setting.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in 89 patients (76 female; mean age 40.6 ± 12.2 years) prescribed rimegepant 75 mg after prior use of triptans and/or lasmiditan. Participants self-recorded headache intensity using a visual analog scale (VAS) before and 2 and 4 h after taking rimegepant. Pain freedom was defined as a VAS score of 0, and treatment efficacy as a ≥ 50% reduction in VAS score. The Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) was assessed at 2 h. Continuation was defined as a request for ongoing prescription after the initial dose.
RESULTS: The study population included 35 patients (39.3%) with chronic migraine and 65 (73.0%) with prior calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibody exposure. Median VAS scores decreased from 77.0 at baseline to 18.0 at 2 h and 0.0 at 4 h (p < 0.001). Pain-free rates were 24.7% (95% CI 16.2-35.0%) at 2 h and 52.8% (95% CI 41.9-63.5%) at 4 h. Efficacy rates (≥ 50% VAS reduction) were 68.5% and 87.6% at 2 and 4 h, respectively. The continuation rate was 82.0%. Meaningful improvement on the PGIC was reported by 65.2% of patients. Adverse events occurred in 13.5% of patients. No adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were observed.
CONCLUSION: Rimegepant was associated with clinically meaningful pain relief and favorable patient-reported outcomes when used as a second- or third-line acute treatment in real-world clinical practice.

Title: Effectiveness of cardiac resynchronization therapy in cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Advances in cancer treatment have increased the number of survivors, making cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) an important concern. While cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is established for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and conduction disorders, its role in CTRCD remains unclear. We conducted a meta-analysis to assess the benefit of CRT in patients with CTRCD.
METHODS: We performed a literature search of studies showing CRT outcomes in the specific group of CTRCD patients. The outcomes of interest were left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and LV volume improvement. A random effects meta-analysis was done to estimate 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: This analysis included four studies (one prospective and three retrospective) comprising 110 patients with CTRCD, the majority (91%, n = 100) being survivors of breast cancer or lymphoma/leukemia. Baseline LVEF ranged from 18.6% ± 7.6% to 28.5% ± 3.8% (mean 24% ± 7%). After a mean follow-up of 9 ± 5 months, LVEF increased by 9.95% (95% CI 7.79-12.11) and end-systolic volume decreased by 39.17 mL (95% CI 24.99-53.35). Three studies included a control group of patients with other forms of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy who underwent CRT implantation, showing no significant difference in LVEF improvement between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests that CRT improves LVEF and LV volumes in selected patients with CTRCD, with a magnitude of reverse remodeling that appears similar to that observed in other etiologies of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. However, the evidence is limited to small observational studies, so conclusions about clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Thus, CRT may be considered in cancer patients who meet standard criteria for CRT implantation, but the decision should be individualized and guided by multidisciplinary assessment, cancer prognosis, and competing clinical risks.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
Journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model.
RESULTS: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

Title: Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® in treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
Abstract: Aim: To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus Zilver® PTX® drug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database. Materials & methods: This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI. Results: A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup. Conclusion: Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

Title: Conduction System Pacing for Resynchronization Therapy in Heart Failure: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) has emerged as a promising modality for cardiac resynchronization therapy, but evidence of CSP in heart failure (HF) remains controversial.
