OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of CSP, including left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) and His bundle pacing, to biventricular pacing (BiVP) in HF.
METHODS: The MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL databases were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) and all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included clinical endpoints (HHF, all-cause mortality), cardiac resynchronization therapy responses (predefined and super-response), echocardiographic parameters (left ventricular ejection fraction and left ventricular end-systolic volume), electrophysiologic parameters (paced QRS duration and capture threshold), functional status (NYHA functional class and 6-minute walk test distance), procedural performance (procedural time, fluoroscopy time, lead implantation time), and device-related complications. (PROSPERO registration: CRD420261388077).
RESULTS: Twelve randomized controlled trials involving 1,054 patients (566 CSP and 488 BiVP) were included. CSP showed a significant reduction in primary composite endpoint (OR: 0.30; 95% CI: 0.18-0.52; I2 = 0%), improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (mean difference: 3.06%; 95% CI: 0.82%-5.30%; I2 = 55%), and shorter paced QRS duration (mean difference:-11.49 ms; 95% CI: -20.70 to -2.28; I2 = 85%), compared with BiVP. In the LBBAP group, there were greater reductions in primary composite endpoint with higher rates of super-response (OR: 2.18; 95% CI: 1.44-3.30; I2 = 54%) compared with BiVP. No differences were observed in functional status or device-related complications.
CONCLUSIONS: CSP, and potentially LBBAP, was associated with a significantly lower composite endpoint of HHF and all-cause mortality compared with BiVP, supporting CSP as an alternative to BiVP in HF.

Title: Validation of the "Pathobiological Determinants of Atherosclerosis in Youth Risk Score" in a Norwegian Cohort of Young Adults.
[Safety of diet therapy using ϖ-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids].
Journal: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: to study the dose-dependent hypolipidemic effect of ϖ-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) in patients with cardiovascular diseases.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: An open, single-center, prospective study was conducted at the clinic of the Federal Research Center for Nutrition and Biotechnology. The tolerability, safety, and effectiveness of dietary therapy enriched with various sources of ϖ-3 PUFAs at dosages ranging from 300 to 3000 mg per day were evaluated in patients with cardiovascular diseases.
RESULTS: The study of different sources and dosages of ω-3 PUFAs demonstrated their good tolerability and safety, and revealed a dose-dependent effect on lipid profile parameters. The study demonstrated the dominant effect of different sources of ω-3 PUFAs on serum TG levels in patients with CVD.
CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest that the inclusion of ω-3 PUFAs in the basic diet of patients with CVD and hyperlipidemia has an additional anti-atherogenic effect.

Title: Age-Friendly Health System Recognition and Its Association with Improved Clinical Outcome Measures.
Journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
Abstract: The number of adults 65 years of age and older is rapidly increasing, as is health care utilization by older adults with multiple chronic conditions. The Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) movement, with a focus on What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility (the 4Ms), was launched in 2017 to improve management of older adults across health care settings. However, evidence of impact on outcomes remains limited. Using a national cohort of 4002 hospitals (388 with AFHS recognition from the Institute for Healthcare Improvement, as of December 31, 2024, and 3614 controls), the authors explore the associations between AFHS recognition and hospital readmission rates, mortality, and patient-reported experiences. Using difference-in-differences analyses, the authors find that level 2 AFHS recognition (i.e., hospitals with at least 3 months of data of older patients who have received 4Ms care) is associated with lower 30-day mortality rates for acute myocardial infarction (-0.41 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.75 to -0.06), pneumonia (-0.71; 95% CI, -1.29 to -0.13), and stroke (-0.56; 95% CI, -1.06 to -0.07). Level 1 recognition (i.e., hospitals that have successfully developed plans to implement the 4Ms) is associated with lower readmission rates only for pneumonia (-0.40; 95% CI, -0.69 to -0.10). Furthermore, both level 1 and level 2 recognition are associated with modest reductions in Medicare spending per beneficiary. No determinative associations were identified between AFHS recognition and patient-reported experience measures. These findings provide one of the first national studies to suggest that organizations with AFHS recognition could be associated with improvement in certain outcomes and spending.

Title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T and I Discordance in Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serial troponin monitoring is used during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, but guidelines do not specify whether high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) or T (hs-cTnT) should be measured. Unlike cardiac-specific hs-cTnI, hs-cTnT can rise from noncardiac sources.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to determine the prevalence and temporal stability of hs-cTnT/hs-cTnI discordance, identify clinical correlates, and evaluate prognostic implications in ambulatory ICI-treated patients.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center cohort, patients starting ICI therapy underwent paired hs-cTnT (Roche Elecsys) and hs-cTnI (Siemens Atellica) measurements in the same banked samples at baseline and 1 month. Patients with adjudicated ICI-associated myocarditis or myositis were excluded by design.
RESULTS: Among 433 patients with paired baseline measurements, hs-cTnT was elevated in 37.9% and hs-cTnI in 1.8%; 158 (36.5%) were discordant (elevated hs-cTnT, normal hs-cTnI), and 267 (61.7%) had normal levels of both (κ = 0.036). Among 329 patients with paired data at baseline and 1 month, discordance prevalence was unchanged (38.3% vs 38.0%; McNemar P > 0.99). Independent correlates were older age, male sex, and chronic kidney disease (all P < 0.05). Over a median follow-up of 30.1 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier), elevated hs-cTnT was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted HR: 1.35; 95% CI: 1.00-1.81; P = 0.048); only 8 of 231 deaths (3.5%) were cardiac.
CONCLUSIONS: In ambulatory patients with cancer receiving ICI therapy, over one-third had elevated hs-cTnT with normal hs-cTnI: a stable, nonspecific pattern present before ICI exposure and consistent with noncardiac sources rather than acute cardiac injury. hs-cTnI is the more cardiac-specific assay; paired baseline measurement of both troponins may help contextualize later elevations when myocarditis is suspected.

Title: Immune Responses in Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Cardiovascular Immune-Related Adverse Events: JACC: CardioOncology State-of-the-Art Review.
Abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have improved cancer outcomes, their use can trigger autoimmune toxicities affecting essentially any organ system. In the cardiovascular system, these immune-related adverse events can manifest as myocarditis, pericarditis, accelerated atherosclerosis, vasculitis, arrhythmias, and other conditions. These cardiovascular toxicities are driven by the loss of peripheral tolerance, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Recent murine and human studies, particularly in immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated atherosclerosis and myocarditis, have begun to reveal the cellular and molecular mediators. Disinhibited T cell function is a central driver, but other immune and nonimmune cell types have also been implicated. Multiple inflammatory and chemokine receptor signaling pathways are activated, offering potential targets for intervention. The growing mechanistic understanding of these cardiovascular toxicities has begun to inform new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, though additional prospective trials are needed.

Title: Early and Mid-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Five-Year Experience from the KOSUTAVI Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) outcomes are well-documented, predictors of mortality beyond conventional surgical risk scores and valve-related factors in real-world, high-risk cohorts require further elucidation. This study aimed to identify the key determinants of 30-day and 1-year mortality following TAVI, with a focus on both patient-specific and procedure-specific complications.
METHODS: The KOSUTAVI study is a single-center, retrospective cohort analysis of 859 consecutive high-risk individuals with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to identify independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Mean age was 78.7 ± 6.5 years, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score was 7.4 ± 2.2. The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 6.5% (n = 56) and 12.4% (n = 107), respectively. The 5-year all-cause mortality rate was 26.3%. In multiple Cox's analysis, chronic renal failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.75, P = .008, 95% CI = 1.29-16.54), presentation with cardiogenic shock (HR = 5.83, P = .028, 95% CI = 1.19-15.41), major vascular injury (HR = 22.7, P = .019, 95% CI = 1.89-45.91), and cardiac tamponade (HR = 17.9, P = .012, 95% CI = 8.13-52.62) were independently associated with 30-day mortality. While these factors were all significant in univariate analysis for 1-year mortality, they did not retain independence in the multiple model. Valve type, access route, and sex were not associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: In a high-risk TAVI population, early mortality is predominantly driven by pre-existing renal dysfunction and acute procedural complications (shock, vascular injury, and tamponade), rather than valve-specific factors. These findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing renal function before the procedure and implementing advanced vascular protection strategies to improve early survival after TAVI.

Title: Metabolic, Atherogenic, and Anthropometric Markers for Discrimination of Premature Coronary Artery Disease in a Predominantly Statin-Treated Cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) is increasingly recognized in younger adults and requires improved risk stratification. Conventional lipid markers may have limited discriminative value, particularly when lipid levels reflect ongoing statin therapy. This study evaluated the associations and discriminatory performance of metabolic, atherogenic, and anthropometric indices for PCAD and developed internally validated dynamic nomograms for PCAD case discrimination.
PATIENT AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective case-control study used data from the Iran Premature Coronary Artery Disease registry. A total of 3063 adults undergoing coronary angiography were included, comprising 1929 patients with PCAD and 1134 controls. Twelve metabolic, lipid-based, and anthropometric indices were calculated from fasting glucose, lipid profiles, and body measurements. Participants were randomly divided into training and validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. Logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration assessment, integrated discrimination improvement, net reclassification improvement, and decision-curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance.
RESULTS: Atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), and a body shape index (ABSI) showed consistent independent associations with PCAD. Individually, these indices showed modest discrimination. The conventional clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.677. Adding AIP and binary ABSI increased the AUC to 0.721, while the TyG plus binary ABSI model showed the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.724, representing modest but statistically significant improvements over the conventional model. Both final models showed favorable internal calibration, and improvement in reclassification metrics, and decision-curve net benefit. Two dynamic web-based nomograms were developed for individualized PCAD case discrimination.
CONCLUSION: TyG, AIP, and ABSI were independently associated with PCAD and provided modest incremental discrimination beyond conventional risk factors in this predominantly statin-treated case-control cohort. The resulting dynamic nomograms provide an accessible framework for PCAD case discrimination; however, their clinical applicability and estimation of absolute risk require external validation in independent, preferably prospective, populations.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study; Validation Study

Title: Brain edema progression rate on serial CT predicts neurological outcome after cardiac arrest: a region-specific biomarker of hypoxic-ischemic brain injury.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prognostic performance of the attenuation change rate on serial brain computed tomography (CT), a novel quantitative marker of temporal cerebral attenuation change, for predicting poor neurological outcome after cardiac arrest (CA).
METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort. CA patients who underwent cranial CT both within 12 h and between 12 h and one week after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) were included. The attenuation change rate, calculated as the HU difference between paired scans divided by the time interval, was measured in 12 predefined brain regions. Neurological outcome was assessed using the Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) at discharge.
RESULTS: Of 53 patients enrolled, 17 (32.1%) had favorable neurological outcomes at discharge. Patients with poor outcomes exhibited significantly greater attenuation decline rates in all gray matter regions except for gray matter at the centrum semiovale level, including the caudate nucleus (-0.01 vs. 0.02 HU/h), putamen (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), thalamus (-0.02 vs. 0.01 HU/h), gray matter of the high convexity (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), and cerebellar gray matter (-0.02 vs. 0.03 HU/h) (all P < 0.01), whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in any of the white matter regions. ROC analysis demonstrated AUCs ranging from 0.725 to 0.778, with cerebellar gray matter achieving the highest AUC (0.778; sensitivity, 75.0%; specificity, 76.5%). At the 100% specificity threshold, the caudate nucleus showed the highest sensitivity for predicting poor outcome (36.1% at a decline rate of -0.040 HU/h).
CONCLUSION: Serial CT-derived attenuation change rate may serve as an exploratory quantitative marker of cerebral edema progression after cardiac arrest. However, this single-center, small-sample study does not support its use for withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment decisions. Multicenter validation is warranted.

Title: Acute Effects of Inspiratory Muscle Training with Different Loads on Peripheral Muscle Oxygenation Kinetics and Autonomic Response in Patients with COPD: A Protocol for a Randomized Crossover Study.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) leads to inspiratory muscle weakness, which may contribute to an altered cardiovascular response during the respiratory cycle. In this context, inspiratory muscle training (IMT) emerges as one of the available tools for the treatment and monitoring of patients with respiratory muscle dysfunction.
METHODS: This is a randomized crossover study, with blinding of both the evaluator and the researcher responsible for statistical analysis. The study will evaluate the acute effects of IMT on peripheral muscle metabolism and the autonomic response in 30 patients with COPD. The primary outcomes will be peripheral muscle oxygenation kinetics, assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), and autonomic response, assessed through heart rate variability (HRV). Participants will be randomly assigned to undergo three different intervention conditions at separate times, with a minimum interval of 48 hours between each session: IMT-S (Strength), aimed at improving inspiratory muscle strength; IMT-E (Endurance), focused on enhancing inspiratory muscle endurance; and Sham, consisting of a Sham IMT intervention. For statistical analysis, continuous variables will be presented as mean ± standard deviation, and data normality will be assessed using histograms and the Shapiro-Wilk test. All analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. In cases of missing data due to dropouts or absence in crossover sessions, participants with incomplete data will be retained in the analysis, assuming that data are missing at random. Between-intervention differences will be analyzed using mixed linear models with Bonferroni adjustment for multiple comparisons. The level of statistical significance will be set at 0.05.
CONCLUSION: This study may help to better understand the effects of IMT performed at different loads on peripheral muscle oxygenation behavior, as well on the autonomic response in patients with COPD. These findings may improve the understanding of the physiological impacts of this therapy and support its application in pulmonary rehabilitation programs.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry NCT06827379.

Title: Left atrial and left ventricular radiation exposure predict long-term cardiovascular events after breast cancer radiotherapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant breast cancer (BC) radiotherapy (RT) improves survival and local control, but cardiovascular (CV) toxicity remains a concern.
AIM: This retrospective study investigated the association between RT doses to cardiac substructures and CV toxicity 15 years after BC RT.
METHODS: Women with unilateral BC diagnosed between 2007 and 2008, treated with RT at [Anonymous] were retrospectively included. Patients with major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were matched to controls by CV risk factors, anthracycline and anti-HER2 therapy. Cardiac substructures were delineated on simulation scans, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess associations between RT doses to these substructures and MACE or other CV events.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 16.5 years (IQR 16.1-17.1), and inclusion of 878 patients, 173 patients experienced MACE and were matched to 167 controls. All patients underwent adjuvant RT using 3-dimensional conformal RT to a total dose of 50 Gy in 25 fractions, with or without a boost to the tumor bed. New individual cardiac toxicities included: atrial fibrillation (AF) 98/878 (11.16%), heart failure (HF) 82/878 (9.34%), coronary artery disease (CAD) 46/878 (5.24%) and valvular disease 180/878 (20.50%). Mean heart doses were 6.62 ± 5.20Gy (MACE) and 5.76 ± 4.96Gy (controls) (p = 0.0916). Compared with controls, patients with MACE had significantly higher disease stage and more frequent histories of CAD, AF and HF. Maximum RT doses to the left atrium (LA) were associated with MACE, new-onset HF, AF and valvular disease, while mean RT dose to the left ventricle (LV) was associated with development of CAD (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that patients treated with RT for BC may experience diverse CV toxicities during long-term follow-up. Higher doses to left-sided cardiac substructures, particularly the LA and LV, were associated with specific CV endpoints, while MHD was not associated with toxicity.

Title: Associations of post-traumatic stress disorder and metabolic syndrome with accelerated brain aging in South African adults: A case-control study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and metabolic syndrome (MetS) are both associated with childhood trauma (CT) and accelerated brain aging. We examined the putative moderating effects of CT exposure on the associations of PTSD diagnosis and MetS status with brain aging in cases (n = 97) compared to trauma-exposed controls (n = 87). Brain age predictions were generated from T1-weighted magnetic resonance image scans using a pre-trained machine learning pipeline (brainageR). A measure of relative brain aging known as "predicted age difference" (PAD) was calculated by subtracting chronological age from the predicted brain age. Results showed that increased waist circumference was associated with a higher PAD, while CAPS-5 scores were associated with a lower PAD. MetS status was also associated with increased PAD in adults with lower CT exposure. The association between higher brain age difference scores and CT were more pronounced in participants with lower triglyceride levels. We found that increased waist circumference correlated with an increased PAD, independent of PTSD diagnosis. Future research should elucidate the possible mechanisms of accelerated brain aging and the protective factors that may slow its progression.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Adults with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) frequently develop metabolic syndrome (MetS), and scientists have found that people with either condition may exhibit similar patterns of neurodegeneration in certain regions of the brain - a process known as brain aging. This study examined the extent to which PTSD, MetS, the PTSD-MetS comorbidity, and childhood trauma were associated with brain aging. While PTSD, MetS, and its interaction were not related to brain aging patterns, we identified risk factors for accelerated brain aging, including greater waist circumference, MetS among adults with lower childhood trauma, and lower triglycerides among those with greater childhood trauma. These results demonstrate that developmental, metabolic, and cardiovascular risk factors may also pose increased risks for accelerated brain aging in adulthood.

Title: The 'Upstairs-Downstairs' heart with complete main pulmonary artery agenesis and PDA-dependent pulmonary circulation: A rare structural intersection characterized by multi detector computed tomography.
Abstract: Superior-inferior ventricular arrangement is an exceedingly rare form of congenital cardiac malposition, representing fewer than 0.1% of all congenital heart diseases, and is almost invariably associated with complex intracardiac anomalies. We report a 3-year-old male who presented with persistent cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and failure to thrive. Prospective ECG-gated CT angiography demonstrated situs solitus with levocardia. A superior-inferior ventricular arrangement was present, with the morphologic left ventricle positioned superior to the morphologic right ventricle. The great arteries were normally related, with a left-sided aortic arch. A large ventricular septal defect was identified. Pulmonary atresia was present, characterized by the absence of the right ventricular outflow tract, pulmonary valve, and main pulmonary artery. Native confluent branch pulmonary arteries were present and received pulmonary blood flow through a large patent ductus arteriosus supplying the left pulmonary artery, with additional small systemic-to-pulmonary collateral vessels. The morphologic right ventricle was dilated and hypertrophied, with associated enlargement of the right atrium. Pulmonary venous drainage was normal, and no abnormalities of the systemic venous drainage were identified. This case underscores the critical role of cardiac CT angiography in comprehensive anatomical delineation of rare and complex congenital cardiac malformations, with direct implications for surgical planning and prognostication.

Title: Validity of Administrative ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes for Ventricular Arrhythmia and Cardiac Arrest in a French University Hospital.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Drug-induced QT interval prolongation increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Assessing these outcomes in electronic health databases and evaluating their association with drug exposure requires prior validation of administrative diagnostic codes. This study aimed to evaluate the positive predictive value (PPV) of International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision (ICD-10) codes for ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac arrest in the French hospital discharge summary database (Programme de Médicalisation des Systèmes d'Information (PMSI)).
METHODS: In a retrospective validation study, we examined PMSI data recorded at Amiens University Medical Center (Amiens, France). Hospital stays between September 2022 and August 2025 with ICD-10 codes for cardiac arrest (I46.0, I46.9), ventricular tachycardia (I47.2), or ventricular fibrillation/flutter (I49.0) were identified. Events were confirmed by electronic medical record review. PPVs with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. The study design prevented the estimation of sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive values. Sensitivity analyses were stratified by year, and by type of care unit. Exposure to QT-prolonging medications prior to events was also assessed.
RESULTS: In a population of 182 patients (median age: 66 years; 75% males; in-hospital mortality rate: 45%), PPVs [95% CI] for all diagnosis codes were high: 0.98 [0.95; 1.00] for cardiac arrest with successful resuscitation, 0.96 [0.79; 1.00] for unspecified cardiac arrest, 0.99 [0.94; 1.00] for ventricular tachycardia, and 0.93 [0.87; 0.97] for ventricular fibrillation/flutter. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. Overall, 49.7% of patients had been exposed to ≥1 QT-prolonging medications prior to a validated event, and 26.5% to ≥2 of these medications concomitantly.
CONCLUSION: The high PPVs in PMSI data supports the use of the evaluated ICD-10 codes for outcome identification in pharmacoepidemiological studies of electronic health databases in general, and those investigating QT-prolonging medication use and the risk of serious cardiac events in particular.

Title: Periodontal diseases and coronary artery disease: epidemiological links, pathogenic mechanisms and prospects for comorbidity integrated management.
Journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
Abstract: Periodontal disease (PD) and coronary artery disease (CAD) are two highly prevalent chronic systemic disorders with overlapping population risk profiles. Accumulating observational, cellular, and genetic studies have suggested potential positive correlations between PD severity, periodontal pathogen load, and CAD incidence, coronary lesion severity, and major adverse cardiac events, whereas Mendelian randomization analyses may not support a direct causal link between the two illnesses. Several synergistic pathogenic pathways may mediate their association: periodontal pathogens may translocate into peripheral circulation to colonize atherosclerotic plaques and exert potential direct vascular toxicity; sustained systemic low-grade inflammation may disrupt endothelial homeostasis; molecular mimicry may induce cross-autoimmune vascular impairment; shared susceptibility loci and conventional cardiovascular risk factors may jointly amplify vascular damage. Standard non-surgical periodontal therapy may reduce systemic inflammatory burden and improve endothelial function, and clinical and microbial periodontal markers may serve as non-invasive biomarkers for CAD risk stratification. This review synthesizes epidemiological evidence and multilayered pathogenic mechanisms and proposes bidirectional collaborative interventions and multidisciplinary cardiostomatological management frameworks for comorbid patients. Further large-scale randomized controlled trials and multi-ethnic genetic analyses are still required to clarify causal inference and potential long-term cardiovascular benefits of periodontal intervention.

Title: Correction: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health, genetic susceptibility, and incident cancer risk: a prospective UK biobank cohort and machine learning study.

Title: Artificial intelligence-enabled deep clinical phenotyping in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: from patient subtypes to precision care.
Abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a clinical syndrome defined by shared manifestations but produced by diverse combinations of cardiometabolic, vascular, inflammatory, renal, pulmonary, atrial, skeletal-muscle, and aging-related mechanisms. This heterogeneity limits the value of classifications based only on left ventricular ejection fraction and helps explain why many mechanistically plausible interventions have produced neutral average results. Deep phenotyping can move the field from descriptive heterogeneity toward biologically coherent and clinically actionable subtypes by integrating clinical trajectories, advanced imaging, exercise and invasive hemodynamics, circulating biomarkers, multiomics, and digital physiology. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers methods to combine these high-dimensional data, but statistical clusters should not be equated with disease endotypes. A useful subtype must be reproducible across cohorts, anchored to plausible biology, associated with a distinct clinical course, and able to improve diagnosis, therapeutic selection, or clinical-trial design. This Review examines the translational continuum from experimental HFpEF models to human patient subtypes, summarizes the main deep-phenotyping domains and AI approaches, and proposes seven clinically interpretable subtype families: cardiometabolic-inflammatory, hypertensive-vascular aging, atrial myopathy, pulmonary vascular-right ventricular, cardiorenal-congestive, peripheral-frailty, and specific etiologic phenocopies. Current evidence supports a layered treatment strategy in which broadly effective therapies, particularly sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, are combined with phenotype-directed management of obesity, diabetes, mineralocorticoid receptor activation, atrial fibrillation, congestion, pulmonary vascular disease, and physical deconditioning. The central next step is prospective validation of dynamic subtype assignments in external populations and phenotype-enriched trials. Phenogroup labels should therefore be regarded as pragmatic, transitional proxies for dominant mechanisms when those mechanisms cannot yet be measured directly at the individual-patient level; their value lies in improving decisions while the field moves toward fully individualized mechanism-based treatment. Deep phenotyping will be clinically valuable only when it changes a decision and improves an outcome, rather than merely increasing descriptive complexity.

Title: Lion Hearts: applying implementation mapping to plan the delivery of a family-based physical activity intervention in community CrossFit affiliates.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community-based physical activity interventions face challenges in adoption, implementation, and sustainability. Lion Hearts is a family-based physical activity intervention designed to promote cardiovascular health among mothers and children aged 3-6 years. This study applied Implementation Mapping during intervention development to identify implementation determinants and develop stakeholder-informed strategies for subsequent pilot testing.
METHODS: The five iterative tasks of Implementation Mapping were applied through a co-design process with seven CrossFit affiliate owner-coaches: (1) conducting an implementation needs and assets assessment and identifying adopters and implementers; (2) specifying implementation outcomes, performance objectives, determinants, and change objectives; (3) selecting theoretical change methods and implementation strategies; (4) producing implementation protocols and materials; and (5) developing a prospective implementation-evaluation plan. Two 60-min co-design sessions were conducted approximately eight weeks apart. The first elicited barriers and facilitators to adoption and delivery within affiliate settings. Audio recordings were transcribed verbatim, and three researchers reviewed and coded both transcripts using structured matrices, supplemented by facilitator notes. Findings were synthesized using rapid qualitative analysis and integrated with behavioral theory and implementation science frameworks to identify implementation determinants and develop implementation strategies and materials. This study applied the five tasks of Implementation Mapping to identify implementation determinants and develop stakeholder-informed strategies, delivery supports, and a prospective evaluation plan for subsequent pilot testing.
RESULTS: Stakeholders identified implementation determinants related to coach knowledge and self-efficacy, participant engagement and competing demands, class structure and flow, scheduling, staffing, equipment availability, and compatibility with affiliate workflows. These findings informed implementation strategies and delivery supports targeting affiliate owners and coaches, including coach training resources, structured session templates, class-flow guidance, and fidelity-monitoring tools. Performance objectives and an implementation logic model were developed to specify hypothesized pathways linking determinants and strategies to prospective implementation outcomes. An evaluation plan was developed to assess reach, adoption, feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, and maintenance during subsequent pilot implementation.
CONCLUSION: Implementation Mapping and stakeholder co-design produced a theory-informed, contextually responsive implementation package for Lion Hearts. Although implementation outcomes have not yet been evaluated, the resulting strategies, materials, and prospective evaluation plan are positioned for testing and refinement in community fitness settings.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07147387.

Title: Left atrial appendage morphology and hemodynamics: potential new markers for individualized thromboembolic risk assessment in atrial fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional CHA₂DS₂-VASc scoring has well-recognized limitations in thromboembolic risk assessment for atrial fibrillation (AF), particularly in low-score patients who nevertheless thrombose, high-score event-free individuals, cancer patients, and post-ablation cohorts. The left atrial appendage (LAA) is the source of 98% of thrombi in non-valvular AF and exhibits marked inter-individual morphological and hemodynamic variability that traditional scores completely ignore.
AIMS: This narrative review critically evaluates current evidence on LAA morphology, hemodynamics, computational fluid dynamics/fluid-structure interaction (CFD/FSI) studies, and digital twin technology, and proposes a mechanism-driven, individualized risk assessment framework for AF-related thromboembolism.
METHODS: A literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science (1990-May 2026) using combinations of keywords related to LAA morphology, hemodynamics, AF, and thromboembolism. Priority was given to landmark original studies, high-quality observational studies with multivariable adjustment, meta-analyses, and contemporary CFD/digital twin studies. A narrative synthesis was adopted owing to heterogeneity in study designs and outcomes.
RESULTS: LAA morphological subtypes are associated with long-term stroke risk, with chicken-wing being protective (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.05-0.91) and cauliflower carrying the highest risk (OR 8.02, 95% CI 0.92-27.86). However, risk is highly context-dependent, with chicken-wing unexpectedly increasing peri-ablation thromboembolic risk (OR 7.2, 95% CI 1.35-38.33) and windsock morphology independently predicting post-ablation AF recurrence (OR 2.72, 95% CI 1.21-6.12). Importantly, traditional morphological classification does not correlate directly with blood stasis (p = 0.365), whereas quantitative geometric parameters such as trabecular number, normalized stroke volume, and ostial area are far more sensitive predictors (R² = 74%). Digital twins integrating multimodal clinical, morphological, and hemodynamic data identify a high-risk phenogroup with a 70% thrombus history rate.
CONCLUSION: Based on these findings, we propose a practical two-tier assessment framework combining basic morphological classification with multimodal refined evaluation (digital twin) for intermediate-/high-risk or clinically challenging cases. This framework represents a paradigm shift from static clinical scores toward mechanism-driven, individualized risk management. Prospective validation of this approach is now warranted.

Title: Widening educational inequalities in type 2 diabetes risk and mediators across successive generations: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower educational attainment has been associated with incident T2DM and adverse outcomes among people with established diabetes, but these stages have largely been studied separately. Whether education-related inequalities span the trajectory from T2DM onset to subsequent cardiovascular disease (CVD) and death, and whether these inequalities differ across birth cohorts, remains uncertain.
METHODS: This study included participants from the UK Biobank who were free of diabetes at baseline. Participants were stratified into three birth cohorts (pre-1949, 1950-1959, and post-1960) to investigate intergenerational differences in educational inequalities. We employed Fine-Gray proportional subdistribution hazards models and multi-state competing risks models to evaluate the impact of education on the risk of incident T2DM and its subsequent progression to cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality. The Relative Index of Inequality (RII) was calculated to quantify the magnitude of disparities. Pathway analysis was conducted to estimate the extent to which socioeconomic, behavioral, and metabolic factors explained the association between educational attainment and T2DM risk.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 16.5 years, 19,931 incident cases of T2DM were documented among the 460,797 included participants. Primary education or less was associated with increased risks of incident T2DM (HR 1.92, 1.85-1.99), progression to CVD (HR 1.33, 1.30-1.37), and mortality (HR 1.53, 1.49-1.57) compared with college education, and these disparities widened across successive birth cohorts. Overall, the adjusted RII was 2.37 (2.25-2.50), increasing from 2.31 (2.16-2.47) in the pre-1949 cohort to 2.53 (2.29-2.79) in the 1950-1959 cohort and 2.53 (2.18-2.93) in the post-1960 cohort. Socioeconomic, metabolic, and behavioral factors mediated a substantial proportion of the educational inequality, accounting for 42.2% (39.2%-45.2%), 42.6% (38.2%-47.3%), and 20.5% (18.9%-22.2%), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Education-related inequalities extend from T2DM incidence to subsequent progression and have widened across successive birth cohorts. Socioeconomic, behavioral, and metabolic factors mediated a substantial proportion of these disparities.

Title: Assessment of Pulmonary Thromboembolism on Chest Radiographs Using Quantitative AI-Based Cardiovascular-Border Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the Korean Society of Radiology
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To address the utility of an AI-based cardiovascular border analysis of chest radiographs (CXRs) in patients with pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included patients with PTE diagnosed using cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) pulmonary angiography between January 2023 and June 2024, along with age-matched and sex-matched controls. The AI model quantified distances from the midline to the cardiovascular borders, including the superior vena cava/ascending aorta (SVC/AO), right atrium (RA), aortic arch, pulmonary trunk (PT), left atrial appendage (LAA), and left ventricle (LV), as well as the CTR. Measurements were standardized as age-adjusted and sex-adjusted Z-scores. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
RESULTS: In total, 390 participants (195 with PTE and 195 controls; median age, 68 years) were included in the study. Patients with PTE showed greater values for the PT, SVC/AO, LAA, LV, and CTRs than the controls (p < 0.05). Among 165 patients with follow-up CXRs, post-treatment reductions in values for the PT, SVC/AO, RA, LAA, LV, and CTRs were observed (p < 0.05). ROC analysis showed modest discriminative performance, with the PT Z-score demonstrating the highest area under the curve (AUC, 0.658), improving further in the central PTE subgroup (AUC, 0.700).
CONCLUSION: AI-based cardiovascular-border analysis of CXRs demonstrated modest diagnostic performance but may support treatment monitoring in patient with PTE.

Title: The Impact of Immunoglobulins on Cardiovascular Diseases and Lipid Profiles in Elderly and Middle-Aged Chinese Individuals: A 15-Year Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Humoral immunity defends via immunoglobulins. This study aimed to evaluate the association between immunoglobulins and CVDs and lipid profiles in a cohort of individuals aged 45 years and older.
METHODS: Data from 982 subjects were analyzed. The cohort had a median age of 61 years (IQR 56-72), was predominantly male (84.8%), and had a high prevalence of CVDs at baseline, including hypertension (30.3%), dyslipidemia (20.7%), arrhythmia (22.3%), coronary heart disease (12.1%), and atrial fibrillation (4.5%). Logistic regression analysis was used to examine the association between baseline and time-varying serum levels of IgG, IgA, and IgM and the presence of five CVDs: coronary heart disease, atrial fibrillation, arrhythmia, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. We additionally explored the relationship between these immunoglobulin levels and lipid profiles.
RESULTS: No significant differences in immunoglobulin levels were found between CVD and non-CVD groups at baseline, and baseline immunoglobulin levels were not associated with any CVD. However, longitudinal changes in IgG and IgA levels were positively associated with changes in free fatty acids (FFAs). Intriguingly, longitudinal increases in IgM levels were positively associated with total cholesterol, LDL-C, non-HDL-C, and HDL-C.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides longitudinal evidence that increases in IgG and IgA levels are associated with elevated FFA levels, while increases in IgM are associated with an adverse lipid profile characterized by higher total cholesterol, LDL-C, and non-HDL-C, and lower HDL-C. These findings suggest a link between humoral immunity and lipid metabolism that warrants further investigation, with potential implications for cardiovascular risk assessment.

Title: Association of alkaline phosphatase with mortality in patients on peritoneal dialysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) experience high mortality rates, necessitating the establishment of reliable prognostic markers. Although serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is routinely measured while assessing chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder, its clinical relevance for mortality risk in patients undergoing PD has not been fully established.
METHODS: Using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, this retrospective cohort study examined the association between baseline ALP levels and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in 1,108 patients with ESKD who newly initiated PD between 2000 and 2020.
RESULTS: The median ALP level of the overall cohort was 76.0 IU/L (interquartile range, 60.0-95.3 IU/L). The mean age of the patients was 60.6 years (standard deviation [SD], 14.4 years), and 55.8% were male. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years, a 1-SD increase in ALP level was significantly associated with a 23% and 64% higher risk of all-cause mortality (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-1.38) and cardiovascular mortality (95% CI, 1.21-2.24), respectively. The patients were stratified into tertiles (T1-T3) based on ALP level. Compared with the T1 group, the adjusted hazard ratios for all-cause mortality were 1.11 (95% CI, 0.84-1.48) in T2 and 1.39 (95% CI, 1.05-1.85) in T3. The relationship between elevated ALP and higher risk of all-cause mortality was consistent when ALP was treated as a time-dependent variable.
CONCLUSION: Elevated ALP levels were associated with increased risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients undergoing PD.

Title: Association between dietary inflammatory index and mortality in adults with chronic kidney disease: a retrospective study from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence and mortality of chronic kidney disease (CKD) are high. Systemic inflammation often occurs in patients with CKD and limits overall survival. The dietary inflammatory index (DII), developed to assess the inflammatory potential of diet, may be an underrecognized risk factor for CKD mortality.
METHODS: This study included 7,113 adult participants from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 2005 and 2018. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was used to assess the association between DII scores and mortality in patients with CKD, with hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) models were used to evaluate non-linear associations, whereas subgroup and mediation analyses explored potential effect modifications and mediation effects.
RESULTS: The all-cause mortality rate among patients with CKD was 19.3%. After full adjustment (model 3), the highest DII quartile showed a 23% higher mortality risk (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.07-1.42; Ptrend<0.001) compared with the lowest quartile. RCS confirmed a linear dose-response relationship (Poverall<0.001, Pnon-linear=0.549). No associations were observed for cardiovascular or malignant tumor mortality. The effect of DII scores on all-cause mortality was more pronounced in patients with lower body weight.
CONCLUSION: Higher DII scores are associated with elevated all-cause mortality in patients with CKD, supporting the potential benefit of anti-inflammatory diets.

Title: Risk Factors and Emerging Therapies for Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-related Myocarditis: A Narrative Review.
Journal: The Journal of the Association of Physicians of India
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) represent a groundbreaking development in immunotherapy, offering significant promise in the treatment of various malignancies previously considered incurable. However, despite their potential benefits, the increasing use of ICIs is associated with a spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Myocarditis is a rare and potentially underestimated complication that represents the highest mortality rate among irAEs.
OBJECTIVE: The review aims to evaluate the current understanding of ICI-myocarditis (ICI-M) through providing a detailed overview of diagnostic challenges, screening strategies, and, in particular, the risk factors and evolving treatment agents beyond corticosteroids.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive literature review was conducted on PubMed, analyzing data from relevant clinical studies, case reports, preclinical models, and expert consensus guidelines. In addition, data from one ongoing clinical trial (ATRIUM trial) not yet indexed in PubMed were included to reflect emerging therapeutic developments.
RESULTS: Despite the low incidence of ICI-M (0.06%-1%), which is likely underestimated, the mortality rate is the highest among irAEs; the most identifiable risk factors include combination therapy with ICI agents (anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA-4), preexisting cardiovascular and autoimmune diseases, use of ICIs alongside other anticancer treatments, certain tumor types, older age, and female sex. Diagnosis of the condition is faced with challenges such as nonspecific clinical features and often requires multimodal evaluation including biomarkers, imaging, and biopsy. High-dose corticosteroids remain the first-line treatment; however, steroid-refractory cases are increasingly reported. Promising second-line options include mycophenolate mofetil, antithymocyte globulin, abatacept, and tacrolimus; however, there is a lack of prospective data to support their efficacy. Studies conducted on various preclinical models highlight potential therapeutic targets such as CXCR3.
CONCLUSION: ICI-M poses a significant challenge in cardio-oncology practice due to its underestimation, high mortality rate, and lack of robust clinical data evaluating standardized screening protocols and second-line treatment measures. Although several second-line agents show promise, the evidence supporting their usage is largely on the basis of expert consensus and case reports, hence representing a strong need for prospective studies offering direct comparisons. Likewise, preclinical studies show great promise in identifying the pathophysiology and potential therapeutic targets for ICI-M; however, translational studies are necessary to validate these findings.

Title: Real-world Challenges and Predictors of Success in Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy.
Journal: The Journal of the Association of Physicians of India
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (RAs) have revolutionized the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, demonstrating robust efficacy in landmark trials for glycemic control, weight reduction, and cardiovascular protection. However, real-world discontinuation rates exceed trial-reported rates, highlighting a gap between clinical efficacy and practical outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This review synthesizes evidence from 2018 to 2024, including trial data, population studies, and registry analyses, to identify and contextualize major real-world barriers. High rates of gastrointestinal side effects, substantial out-of-pocket costs, and patient aversion to injectable formulations often result in 1-year discontinuation rates ranging from 27 to 41%. These challenges are compounded by heterogeneity in patient response, with predictors of successful long-term use including higher baseline HbA1c, elevated body mass index (BMI), absence of severe gastrointestinal disorders, and robust early response to therapy.
METHODS: A proposed clinical scoring model is presented to improve patient selection and predict adherence, while digital health tools and emerging combination therapies offer additional avenues to enhance persistence and outcomes. Despite promising advances such as dual- and triple-incretin agents and oral GLP-1 RA formulations, cost and access remain major hurdles.
RESULTS: Key factors, including baseline HbA1c >8.0%, BMI >30 kg/m2, absence of severe gastrointestinal (GI) disorders, and prior adherence success, correlate strongly with higher persistence. Real-world data reveal that discontinuation rates for GLP-1 receptor agonists remain high, with 1-year discontinuation ranging from approximately 28% to around 41%, depending on the patient population and indication. Discontinuation is more common among patients using GLP-1 RAs for obesity without diabetes, reaching rates above 50% in some cohorts. The primary reasons for stopping therapy include gastrointestinal side effects, reported in over 25% of discontinuations, high medication costs, and issues with insurance coverage or medication access. Persistence is generally higher among patients with T2DM, those with higher baseline BMI, and those who experience greater early weight loss or favorable tolerability, while frequent adverse effects and logistical barriers contribute to poorer long-term adherence. Although emerging clinical tools and digital health interventions are proposed to help address these barriers, further prospective data are needed to quantify their impact on persistence at scale.
CONCLUSION: Bridging trial evidence with real-world practice requires proactive candidate profiling and side-effect management. Combining predictive scoring, artificial intelligence (AI)-supported adherence tools, and emerging dual-incretin agents may transform GLP-1 RA therapy from short-term use to durable metabolic benefit.

Title: Etiology and Left Ventricular Function in Right Bundle Branch Block: A Prospective Observational Study.
Journal: The Journal of the Association of Physicians of India
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF STUDY: Right bundle branch block (RBBB) is a common ECG finding. It may be caused by coronary artery disease, dilated cardiomyopathy, chronic obstructive lung disease, or degenerative disease of the conduction system of the heart. The purpose of the study was to find out the etiology and left ventricular function in patients with RBBB coming to a tertiary care hospital.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: All consecutive patients coming to our hospital on an outdoor or inpatient basis with ECG showing RBBB were studied. Detailed history and physical examination were done. All patients were subjected to echocardiography.
RESULTS: 201 patients with RBBB were studied. Mean age was 61.01 ± 12.92 years. 157 were male (78.11%), and 44 (21.89%) were female. The most Common symptom was dyspnea in 81 patients (40.29%) and chest pain in 15 patients(7.46%). Four patients presented with syncope and were proved to have intermittent complete heart block. 95 persons (47.26%) with RBBB had no symptoms, 43 out of which had come for clearance for noncardiac surgery. On echocardiography, left ventricular hypertrophy was present in 32 patients (15.92%), regional wall motion abnormality in 45 patients (22.38%), and left ventricular global hypokinesia in 13 patients (6.46%). LV systolic dysfunction was present in 43 patients (21.39%), and 85 (42.28%) patients had a normal study.
CONCLUSION: The most common presentation in patients was dyspnea. About half of the patients were asymptomatic. Around 20% were detected to have RBBB when they came for clearance for noncardiac surgery. Common causes were coronary artery disease, dilated cardiomyopathy, and cor pulmonale.

Title: A Consensus Statement on the Role of Bisoprolol across the CV Continuum.
Journal: The Journal of the Association of Physicians of India
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death globally, affecting populations in both developed and low- and middle-income countries. Although age-adjusted mortality rates from coronary artery disease (CAD) have declined in regions such as the United States and Europe, sudden cardiac death continues to account for a significant proportion of CVD-related fatalities. The concept of the "cardiovascular continuum," introduced more than a decade ago, describes the progressive nature of CVD-beginning with modifiable risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes, and smoking, which collectively drive oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and inflammation. Over time, these pathophysiological changes lead to atherosclerosis and end-organ damage, often well before clinical symptoms become apparent.
ABSTRACT: In India, the burden of CVD has risen sharply in recent decades, particularly due to increasing rates of coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular events. Emerging evidence identifies an elevated resting heart rate as an independent predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, particularly in individuals with hypertension, myocardial infarction (MI), and heart failure (HF). Among available pharmacological options, beta-blockers-particularly bisoprolol-have demonstrated strong efficacy in managing angina, atrial fibrillation (AF), and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). By acting at multiple stages of the cardiovascular continuum, bisoprolol provides both symptomatic relief and disease-modifying effects, underscoring its importance in contemporary cardiovascular management.

Title: Oral Versus Injectable Incretin-Based Anti-Obesity Therapies: An Integrated Computational and Evidence-Based Comparison of Orforglipron, Semaglutide, and Tirzepatide.
Journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
Abstract: Incretin-based agents are transforming obesity pharmacotherapy, and orforglipron, the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist to complete phase 3 testing, invites direct comparison with the injectable agents semaglutide and tirzepatide. We integrated clinical trial evidence, including the direct head-to-head SURMOUNT-5 trial, independently verified molecular descriptors, a fully specified drug-target-disease network with permutation-tested hub significance, hypergeometric pathway enrichment, and multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) across four weighting schemes with formal sensitivity analysis. Tirzepatide produced significantly greater weight loss than semaglutide under randomized, head-to-head conditions (20.2% vs. 13.7% at week 72) and ranked highest under balanced, efficacy-, and safety-dominant MCDA models once a composite ADMET score misapplied to two large peptides was removed. Orforglipron's lipophilicity exceeds the Lipinski ceiling, showing that its oral absorption reflects deliberate chemistry rather than default small-molecule developability; it nonetheless ranked highest under an accessibility-dominant model driven by oral feasibility and manufacturing scalability. These rankings were stable under Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis for three of four weighting schemes, with the balanced model comparatively fragile. Tirzepatide's cardiovascular evidence has also advanced, with SURPASS-CVOT reporting non-inferiority to dulaglutide. No single agent dominates every criterion; treatment selection should match the clinical priority the individual patient weights most heavily.

Title: Evidence-Based Nursing Practices to Prevent Perioperative Unintentional Hypothermia in Elective Surgeries: An Observational Study.
Abstract: Although evidence-based recommendations for preventing perioperative unintentional hypothermia have long been available, observational studies evaluating their implementation in hospital practice and the effectiveness of preventive interventions in at-risk patients are limited. This study aimed to determine the scope of nursing interventions for preventing perioperative unintentional hypothermia and examine the relationship between patient characteristics and these practices. This study employed a descriptive observational design. Patients undergoing elective surgery in the surgical units (orthopedics, gynecology, urology, neurosurgery, general surgery, and cardiovascular surgery) of a tertiary hospital in Turkey were observed preoperatively, intraoperatively, and on the first postoperative day. The mean age of the participants was 51.30 ± 19.32 years; 77% were overweight or obese, 55.2% had chronic diseases, and 39.6% underwent surgeries lasting more than 2 hours. The findings indicated that the duration of surgery was a significant determinant of nurses' perioperative hypothermia prevention practices. In longer procedures, nurses' awareness of hypothermia risk increased, which was reflected in patient education, environmental temperature management, and the use of active and passive warming methods (p < 0.05). This study highlights the importance of educational programs, strengthening standard care protocols, and policy development to enhance nurses' awareness and practice in preventing perioperative unintentional hypothermia. In conclusion, effective strategies are needed to improve nursing practice and promote evidence-based interventions in this area.

Title: Words That Heal: A Systematic Review of Healthcare Providers-Patient Communication to Enhance Chronic Care Management and Practice Recommendations.
Abstract: Chronic diseases represent a major global health burden, and suboptimal treatment adherence remains a key obstacle to long-term management. Healthcare provider (HCP)-patient communication is a modifiable determinant of adherence and psychological functioning, yet evidence remains fragmented across conditions and communication domains. This review builds on patient-centered communication scholarship and established models of communication functions and pathways linking clinician-patient communication to health outcomes. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on HCP-patient communication strategies associated with treatment adherence and psychological outcomes among adults with chronic diseases, including diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular, and respiratory conditions. Following PRISMA guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD42020171690), five databases (Scopus, PubMed, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar) were searched. Results: Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Communication strategies clustered into four macro-domains: (1) trust and interpersonal relationship; (2) information exchange and decision processes; (3) active involvement, empowerment, and autonomy; and (4) change processes, emotional regulation, and management of difficulties. Domains were defined a priori from patient-centered communication, self-management, and behavior-change literature and refined during data extraction. Across conditions, integrated communication patterns addressing multiple domains were generally associated with favorable adherence, self-management, clinical, quality-of-life, and healthcare-utilization outcomes, although evidence strength varied by study design, disease context, and methodological quality. Findings support a provisional, evidence-informed framework in which HCP-patient communication strategies, organized within relational, informational, participatory, and change-regulatory macro-domains, may engage proximal regulatory processes that, in turn, may be associated with adherence and other chronic-care outcomes. Prospective studies are needed to test these pathways.

Title: Bipolar Disorder and the Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a chronic psychiatric illness characterized by recurrent manic and depressive episodes, affecting 2% of the global population. It is associated with premature mortality, including cardiovascular disease (CVD)-related mortality. Although clinically important, the absolute burden and incidence of cardiovascular outcomes in BD remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized observational evidence on CVD prevalence and incidence in adults with BD.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023484712), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and PsycInfo, screening 11,909 records. Thirty-two observational studies in adults with BD were included after Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessment. Data were extracted on overall CVD, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease, comorbidities, and psychotropic exposure. Pooled prevalence and incidence rate ratios were calculated using random-effects models when data were comparable.
RESULTS: The pooled CVD prevalence in BD was 7.70% (95% CI: 5.07-11.52), with coronary artery disease at 6.89% (95% CI: 4.05-11.47), cerebrovascular disease at 4.45% (95% CI: 2.13-9.05), and peripheral arterial disease at 3.30% (95% CI: 1.66-6.45). However, prevalence estimates showed extreme heterogeneity and should be interpreted as broad indicators of absolute burden rather than precise estimates for a single BD population. In controlled incidence studies, BD was associated with increased CVD incidence (IRR 1.66, 95% CI: 1.32-2.08), with elevated coronary and cerebrovascular estimates. Clinical variable analyses involving medication use, lifestyle factors, and cardiometabolic comorbidities were not feasible because reporting was insufficient and noncomparable.
CONCLUSION: Adults with BD show substantial cardiovascular burden and increased incidence. However, extreme heterogeneity, limited incidence data, observational designs, and insufficient moderator reporting limit the precision and generalizability of pooled estimates. These findings support integrated cardiovascular screening in BD populations and future prospective studies.
TRAIL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42023484712.

Title: Finerenone versus Steroidal MRAs in Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease without Prior Heart Failure.
Abstract:
AIMS: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) markedly increase the risk of heart failure (HF) and death. While finerenone improves outcomes in clinical trials, real-world evidence and direct comparisons with steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) are limited. We evaluated finerenone versus steroidal MRAs (spironolactone and eplerenone) in patients without prior HF.
METHODS: Using the TriNetX platform, we conducted a retrospective multi-center observational study. We identified patients aged ≥18 years with T2D and CKD without prior HF and ischemic heart disease, who initiated MRAs after receiving a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor as first-line therapy between 2021 and 2024 (N=3,680). Of these, 724 initiated finerenone and 1,542 initiated a steroidal MRA. After propensity score matching, each group included 551 patients. The primary outcome was all-cause death during the 18-month follow-up period; the secondary outcome was new-onset HF and renal outcome (a composite of end-stage renal disease and dialysis).
RESULTS: Over 18-month, finerenone initiation was associated with lower incidence rates of all-cause death (2.1 vs 4.5 events/100 person-years; incidence rate difference, -2.41; 95% CI, -4.38 to -0.44) and new-onset HF (6.5 vs 12.9; -6.38; 95% CI, -9.75 to -3.02), whereas no significant difference was observed for the renal outcome (8.3 vs 9.1; -0.81; 95% CI, -3.99 to 2.37).
CONCLUSIONS: Finerenone was associated with a lower 18-month risk of all-cause death compared with steroidal MRAs in patients aged ≥18 years with T2D and CKD without prior HF, who received an SGLT2 inhibitor as first-line therapy; however, residual confounding cannot be excluded, and these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Title: Cardiac magnetic resonance with myocardial strain as a predictor of anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity in patients with lymphoma: a prospective multimodality study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is a frequent and clinically relevant complication in patients with lymphoma treated with anthracyclines. Early identification of subclinical myocardial injury is critical to prevent progression to overt heart failure and to avoid chemotherapy dose reductions that may compromise oncologic outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with T1 mapping and feature-tracking myocardial strain, in comparison with transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) and circulating biomarkers, for the early detection of CTRCD in lymphoma patients receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center observational study, forty-nine adult patients with lymphoma scheduled for anthracycline-based chemotherapy underwent serial assessment of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), NT-proBNP, TTE, and CMR at baseline (visit 0), after the third chemotherapy cycle (visit 1), and at chemotherapy completion (visit 2). TTE was repeated at 12-month follow-up (visit 3). CMR included cine imaging, T1 mapping with extracellular volume (ECV) quantification, late gadolinium enhancement, and feature-tracking strain analysis (global longitudinal [GLS], circumferential [GCS], and radial [GRS] strain). CTRCD was defined and graded according to the 2022 ESC Cardio-Oncology Guidelines.
RESULTS: The median age of patients was 46 (29.5-62) years; 53.1% were female. The mean cumulative doxorubicin dose was 295 ± 57 mg/m². hs-cTnT levels increased progressively from baseline (0.006 ± 0.005 ng/mL) to visit 2 (0.022 ± 0.016 ng/mL; p < 0.001), while NT-proBNP did not change significantly (p = 0.086). TTE showed a significant decline in LVEF by the Simpson method (62.92 ± 5.61% to 60.23 ± 5.41%; p = 0.037) and progressive worsening of GLS (- 19.84 ± 2.35% to - 18.31 ± 2.73%; p = 0.001). CMR-derived LVEF also declined (61.98 ± 6.08% to 57.34 ± 7.29%; p < 0.001), accompanied by significant deterioration of GLS, GCS, and GRS (p < 0.001 for all). CTRCD was identified in 7 patients (14.9%) by CMR and 5 (10.6%) by TTE (p = 0.625), with substantial agreement between modalities (κ = 0.619; p < 0.001). A relative GLS decline > 15% was observed by CMR in 34.1% of patients at visit 1 and 43.9% at visit 2, exceeding the corresponding TTE-detected rates (15.2% and 18.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: CMR-derived strain identified myocardial functional abnormalities during anthracycline therapy. Whether these abnormalities represent earlier manifestations of clinically relevant cardiotoxicity requires confirmation in larger prospective studies with longer follow-up.

Title: Crystalloid vs colloid for Hemodynamics during Anesthesia INduction in TAVR patients (CHAIN-T): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether preload with colloids could reduce hypotension during induction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared to crystalloids.
METHODS: This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled trial conducted at Xijing Hospital. A total of 116 patients scheduled for elective TAVR under general anesthesia will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the colloid group or the crystalloid group, receiving either 5 ml/kg of colloid or crystalloid solution before anesthesia induction infused over 15 min. The primary outcome is the area under curve (AUC) of the change in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline during the induction period (until 15 min after induction). Secondary outcomes include the incidence of intraoperative hemodynamic instability, the use of intraoperative vasoactive drugs, the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on the first postoperative day, postoperative hospital length of stay, the rate of intensive care unit (ICU) admission postoperatively, all-cause mortality during hospitalization and by 30 days after surgery, and the incidence of renal replacement therapy by 30 days after surgery.
DISCUSSION: The results of this study will provide evidence on optimizing fluid preload to prevent hypotension during induction, reduce postoperative complications, and enhance recovery for patients undergoing TAVR. The findings are expected to promote anesthesia protocols in this patient population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol and statistical analysis plan were approved by the institutional Ethics Committee of Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (XJLL-KY-20252560). The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07329660) on December 29, 2025.

Title: Total and beverage-specific alcohol use at mid-life and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While detrimental health impacts of excessive alcohol use are well-established, potential effects of low-to-moderate drinking remain controversial. We examined the associations between total and beverage-specific alcohol intake and mortality, including cardiovascular disease (CVD), cancer (e.g., 20 site-specific cancers), and other mortality.
METHODS: We included 340,924 participants from UK Biobank (2006-2022). Alcohol use was categorized as: never or occasional alcohol consumption (≤ 20 g/week), low consumption (> 20 g/week to ≤ 20 g/d for men, > 20 g/week to ≤ 10 g/d for women), moderate consumption (> 20 to ≤ 40 g/d for men, > 10 to ≤ 20 g/d for women), and high consumption (> 40 g/d for men and > 20 g/d for women). We used Cox proportional hazard models to examine the associations of alcohol intake and mortality.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 13.4 years, we documented 22,381 deaths. Compared with never or occasional alcohol intake, high total alcohol intake was associated with higher mortality from all-causes (HR and 95%CI: 1.24 (1.17, 1.31)), CVD (1.14 (1.01, 1.28)), cancer (1.36 (1.26, 1.47)), and other causes (1.12 (1.02, 1.22)), whereas moderate alcohol use was associated with higher cancer mortality (1.11 (1.03, 1.20)) only. Alcohol consumption from spirits and beer/cider, even at low to moderate levels, was associated with higher mortality from all-causes, CVD, cancer, and other diseases (HRs ranging from 1.07 to 1.83). Yet, low and moderate alcohol intake from wine was associated with lower all-cause, CVD, cancer, or other mortality. Importantly, moderate to high intake of total alcohol and alcohol from beer/cider and spirits, and high wine use were particularly associated with higher mortality from multiple site-specific cancers, including mortality from head/neck, respiratory system, gastrointestinal, liver/gallbladder, hematological, female breast, and female/male genital cancers.
CONCLUSIONS: The results suggested that low to moderate alcohol intake from spirits and beer/cider was associated with higher all-cause, CVD, cancer, and other mortality, whereas low to moderate alcohol use from wine was associated with lower all-cause, CVD, cancer, and other mortality. However, high alcohol use, regardless of beverage-type, mortality from various site-specific cancers was elevated.

Title: Multidomain Autonomic Dysfunction assessed with COMPASS-31 among patients with type 2 diabetes in Zanzibar: prevalence and associated factors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autonomic dysfunction is an important but frequently under-recognized complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), particularly in settings where objective autonomic testing is not routinely available. The Composite Autonomic Symptom Score-31 (COMPASS-31) provides a practical symptom-based approach for assessing autonomic dysfunction across multiple domains. This study compared socioeconomic, lifestyle, and clinical characteristics among adults with T2DM in Zanzibar according to COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction and examined factors associated with its presence.
METHODS: This hospital-based cross-sectional study included 665 adults with T2DM attending the diabetes clinic at Mnazi Mmoja Hospital, Zanzibar. Autonomic symptoms were assessed using COMPASS-31, including the orthostatic intolerance, gastrointestinal, and bladder domains. Participants were classified as having autonomic dysfunction when they met the prespecified threshold for dysfunction in at least one assessed domain. Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) was assessed separately using standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests performed with an automated CAN Analyzer and was not included in the COMPASS-31 composite outcome. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation was used to calculate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Overall, 309 participants (46.5%) had COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction. Orthostatic intolerance was the most common domain, affecting 271 participants (40.8%), followed by gastrointestinal dysfunction in 177 (26.6%) and urinary dysfunction in 123 (18.5%). Separately, 305 participants (45.9%) met the analyzer-based criteria for CAN. In the multivariable analysis, autonomic dysfunction was more prevalent among participants without a family history of diabetes (aPR = 1.37, 95% CI: 1.16-1.61; p < 0.001), those with diabetes duration of ≥ 10 years (aPR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.14-1.75; p < 0.001), those not using oral hypoglycemic agents (aPR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.39-1.97; p < 0.001), and those who rarely consumed vegetables or consumed one portion per day (aPR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.37-2.34; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Approximately half of the adults with T2DM in this tertiary-care population had COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction. Higher prevalence was associated with no family history of diabetes, longer diabetes duration, non-use of oral hypoglycemic agents, and lower vegetable intake. These findings highlight the potential value of symptom-based autonomic assessment and support further prospective research to better understand the clinical and lifestyle factors associated with autonomic dysfunction among adults with T2DM in Zanzibar.

Title: Comorbidity patterns and inpatient expenditure among patients with coronary heart disease in China.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary heart disease (CHD) often co-occurs with other chronic conditions. This increases care complexity and hospital costs. Most previous studies have relied on single diseases or simple comorbidity counts. Less is known about whether different multimorbidity patterns are associated with different levels and structures of inpatient expenditure. We aimed to identify comorbidity patterns among middle-aged and older inpatients with CHD and to examine their associations with hospital costs.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study using electronic health record data from a tertiary hospital in Shanxi Province, China, from 2020 to 2024. Patients aged 45 years or older with a principal discharge diagnosis of CHD (ICD-10: I20-I25) were included. The outcome was total inpatient expenditure per admission. Latent class analysis was applied to 14 comorbidities with prevalence of at least 1%. We then used generalised linear models with a gamma family and log link to examine the association between latent classes and inpatient expenditure, adjusting for sociodemographic and clinical covariates.
RESULTS: Among 33,044 patients used for pattern identification, 85.16% (28,140) had at least one included comorbidity. Five classes were identified: low comorbidity (39.89%), vascular disease (5.20%), hypertension-dominant (42.27%), diabetes-renal (3.16%), and cardiac dysfunction (9.48%). Compared with the low-comorbidity class, all other classes were associated with higher inpatient expenditure, with the largest increases observed in the cardiac dysfunction class (ER = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.30-1.36) and the diabetes-renal class (ER = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.23-1.32). Predicted mean expenditure was highest in the cardiac dysfunction class ($2,615.77; 95% CI: 2,562.30-2,669.24) and the diabetes-renal class ($2,502.99; 95% CI: 2,421.49-2,584.49), compared with $1,964.85 (95% CI: 1,943.54-1,986.16) in the low-comorbidity class. Medical consumables accounted for the largest share of expenditure in all groups, while the cardiac dysfunction class had the highest proportions of diagnostic and medication costs.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimorbidity was highly prevalent among middle-aged and older inpatients with CHD. Distinct comorbidity patterns were associated with different levels and structures of inpatient expenditure. These findings may help inform more tailored care planning and more refined payment adjustment in tertiary inpatient settings.

Title: Integrated proteomics and machine learning reveal AHNAK as a discriminative biomarker of atrial fibrillation in heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a frequent complication of heart failure (HF), markedly increasing morbidity and mortality. Although atrial fibrosis is increasingly recognized as a central mechanistic substrate linking HF to AF, the molecular determinants driving fibrotic remodeling and enabling early AF discrimination in HF remain poorly defined.
