Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy (KRT) is associated with a substantial and growing economic burden. While the costs directly attributable to KRT modalities are well documented, the resource use and costs unrelated to KRT modalities remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To quantify healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and costs in patients receiving dialysis or kidney transplantation, excluding technique-related costs.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study used BIG-PAC real-world data to analyze dialysis or kidney transplant patients as of January 1, 2018, with a two-year follow-up. Patients were identified based on related diagnostic or procedure codes recorded in electronic health records (EHRs) prior to the index date. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), hospitalization for CKD and mortality were evaluated. HCRU, direct healthcare costs, and indirect productivity costs due to sick leave were assessed, excluding technique-related KRT costs.
RESULTS: Of 70,973 individuals, 356 (0.5%) were on dialysis and 232 (0.3%) had kidney transplantation. Over two years, MACE per 1000 patient-years were 276.3 for dialysis and 85.9 for transplantation. CKD hospitalization rates were 245.7 and 183.0, with mortality rates of 253.8 and 35.6, respectively. First-year health costs averaged €25,410.4 (SD €17,369.0) for dialysis patients and €4,472.8 (SD €2,859.1) for transplant recipients. Most costs among dialysis and kidney transplant patients were driven by hospitalization, 72.4% and 39.8%, respectively. Indirect costs due to sick leave were also substantial.
CONCLUSION: Non-technique-related costs represent a substantial component of the overall economic burden in patients receiving KRT, largely driven by hospitalizations. These findings provide important context for healthcare planning, although they do not represent total costs of care and should be interpreted as descriptive estimates.

Title: Antihypertensive treatment non-adherence and spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a prospective observational study from Northern India.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a leading cause of stroke-related mortality and long-term disability, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. Hypertension, and particularly non-adherence to antihypertensive therapy, represents the most important modifiable risk factor. This study aimed to evaluate the epidemiological, clinical, and radiological characteristics of hypertensive ICH and to identify preventable risk factors with public health relevance.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary-care referral center in Northern India between March 2023 and February 2024. Adult patients with non-traumatic spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage were enrolled. Data on demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, antihypertensive treatment adherence, clinical severity, and radiological characteristics were collected and analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: One hundred patients were included (mean age 61.2 ± 12.4 years; 63% male). Hypertension was present in 78% of patients; among these, 70.5% (95% CI 59.6 to 79.5) reported non-adherence to antihypertensive therapy. Active smoking was observed in 62%. Deep hemorrhages involving the basal ganglia (46%) and thalamus (26%) accounted for 72% of cases. Hydrocephalus occurred in 28%. Higher admission blood pressure was observed in patients with larger hematoma volumes.
CONCLUSIONS: Hypertensive ICH in this Northern Indian cohort disproportionately affects individuals in the sixth decade of life and is strongly associated with uncontrolled blood pressure, antihypertensive treatment non-adherence, and tobacco use. Targeted primary prevention through strengthened antihypertensive care and behavioral risk factor programs is essential to reducing the regional burden of this largely preventable condition.

Title: Association of preoperative forced vital capacity with prolonged mechanical ventilation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV) is a serious complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), yet the association between preoperative pulmonary function and PMV risk remains to be comprehensively evaluated.
METHODS: This study included adult patients who underwent isolated CABG with preoperative pulmonary function testing. Predicted forced vital capacity (FVC), predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV₁), and the FEV₁/FVC ratio were assessed for their association with PMV.
RESULTS: Among 1,702 patients, 151 (8.9%) experienced PMV. Patients with PMV were older (65.1 ± 8.5 vs. 62.8 ± 8.8 years, P = 0.003), had higher rates of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (9.9% vs. 5.4%, P = 0.034) and on-pump CABG (8.6% vs. 1.2%, P < 0.001), lower left ventricular ejection fraction (57.1 ± 10.3% vs. 59.1 ± 8.7%, P = 0.007), lower predicted FVC (82.9 ± 14.0% vs. 88.1 ± 14.9%, P < 0.001), and lower predicted FEV₁ (88.7 ± 15.5% vs. 92.6 ± 16.2%, P = 0.007). They also had higher perioperative mortality (4.0% vs. 0.1%, P < 0.001), longer postoperative hospital stays (10.9 ± 4.2 vs. 8.0 ± 2.6 days, P < 0.001), and greater hospitalization costs (25,309.4 [22,119.4-33,359.3] vs. 18,155.4 [16,665.8-20,001.5] USD, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no non-linear relationship between pulmonary function parameters and PMV. After multivariable adjustment, predicted FVC remained independently associated with PMV (odds ratio [OR] 0.97, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.95-0.99, P = 0.005), whereas predicted FEV₁ did not.
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-tenth of patients undergoing CABG required PMV, which was associated with greater healthcare resource utilization and higher perioperative complications. Predicted FVC, but not predicted FEV₁, is an independent predictor of PMV.

Title: Advancing care coordination to enhance shared care for complex cancer survivors in primary care (ACCESS-PC): protocol for a hybrid type 3 effectiveness-implementation trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer survivors with chronic conditions (e.g., complex cancer survivors) are a growing population that faces greater cancer-specific and cardiovascular disease (CVD) related morbidity and mortality. A shared care model, which involves primary care and cancer clinicians, is the optimal care delivery model for complex cancer survivors. Yet, there is little guidance on how to effectively implement and support complex cancer survivors' continued engagement with primary care during the cancer treatment phase.
METHODS: This protocol describes a multi-phase, mixed methods, stakeholder-engaged research process that tailors and tests a multi-level health system intervention to improve primary care provider and cancer team 'shared care' for complex cancer survivors. This study employs a design-for-dissemination, theory-guided perspective, blending implementation science and care delivery conceptual frameworks: Exploration, Planning, Implementation, and Sustainment (EPIS) and Cancer Multi-team System (cMTS). These frameworks guide our understanding and strategies deployed on the multi-level factors of implementing shared care in a health system. Primary Care Connect (PCC) is a health system intervention designed to align complex cancer survivors, healthcare team members, and health system implementation actors' understandings, capacities, and practices to promote the adoption of shared care delivery models for complex cancer survivors. A hybrid type 3 effectiveness-implementation study design will test the effectiveness of PCC (n = 266 patients) in a patient-level randomized controlled trial on primary care connection, chronic disease management, and patient-reported outcomes. PCC implementation (e.g., feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness) will be evaluated using a mixed methods approach to inform sustainable usage of the intervention. A concurrent learning evaluation will assess PCC's adaptations over time and convene health system stakeholders to explore intervention properties to inform adoption and sustainment considerations.
DISCUSSION: The overarching goal of this protocol is to examine whether cancer survivors becoming "lost in transition" is a preventable problem. PCC tests whether the challenge of transitioning patients back to primary care can be avoided altogether by re-engineering care coordination with primary care at the outset of cancer treatment. Study findings are poised to have a profound impact on the adoption of shared care delivery models throughout the U.S. to optimally mitigate complex cancer survivors' CVD risks.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered with ClinicalTrials.gov on February 19, 2025: NCT06834204.

Title: Association between PM2.5 and coronary artery dilatation with Kawasaki disease in China.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Kawasaki disease is an acute febrile systemic vasculitis that predominantly affects children and can lead to coronary artery dilatation (CAD), coronary artery aneurysm, and/or thrombosis. This study aimed to investigate whether exposure to particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 µm (PM2.5) is associated with an increased risk of CAD. A case-crossover study was conducted to investigate the relationship between PM2.5 exposure and coronary Z value in children. The study included 847 participants from 2017 to 2021. The Z value was calculated for each participant, and PM2.5 exposure levels were assigned. The risk effect of PM2.5 on the Z value was assessed using the distributed lag Poisson generalized linear model. Correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the mechanisms underlying CAD, and sensitivity analysis was conducted to verify the stability of the model. PM2.5 exposure was found to increase the risk of CAD at lag 2-4 days. On the 3rd day of lag, PM2.5 exposure led to the highest risk of CAD, with RR = 1.11, (95%CI = 1.02, 1.21). Mediation analysis showed that PM2.5 may induce CAD through C-reactive protein (CRP), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and hemoglobin (HB), and the effect size was significant, indicating that CRP, ALT and HB were the main mediating factors between PM2.5 and CAD.
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that PM2.5 exposure is a potential risk factor for CAD in children. CRP, alanine aminotransferase, and hemoglobin were identified as the main mediators regulating the relationship between PM2.5 and CAD.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • PM2.5 may lead to an increased incidence of Kawasaki disease in children.
WHAT IS NEW: • We found that inhalation of PM2.5 may cause coronary artery dilatation in Kawasaki disease through a population-based cohort study. • This process may be mediated by increasing C-reactive protein. • The model results remained stable after sensitivity analysis.

Title: Real-world renoprotective effects of polyethylene glycol-loxenatide in type 2 diabetes: a multicenter, ambispective cohort study.
Abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort (hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

Title: Weight Regain After Incretin Treatment: The Lean Mass Deficit Hypothesis and a Role for Testosterone Combination Therapy in Men.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1RA and triple (GIP)/GLP-1RA/glucagon agonists achieve placebo-subtracted weight loss of 15% to 22%. Their long-term value depends on how well the weight loss is maintained and on the composition of weight loss, not only amount of weight loss. Part of incretin-induced weight loss is lean tissue. It is unknown whether the proportion of lean mass, and especially, muscle mass loss is greater than with other weight-loss interventions, and whether it may cause clinically meaningful harm. Men with obesity commonly have low or low-normal testosterone, which is associated with reduced muscle mass, increased visceral adiposity, impaired insulin sensitivity, and increased cardiovascular risk.
HYPOTHESIS: We propose, as an exploratory hypothesis, that in men with obesity and low testosterone, combining incretin therapy with testosterone therapy may preserve muscle mass, increase the proportion of weight lost as fat mass, and reduce fat-predominant weight regain after incretin discontinuation.
RATIONALE: Resistance exercise and adequate protein intake are first-line measures for preserving muscle mass during weight loss. No lifestyle measure reliably prevents the fat-predominant weight regain that follows diet discontinuation, and long-term adherence to lifestyle interventions is poor. We position testosterone therapy as a pharmacological adjunct for weight loss maintenance in men with obesity and low testosterone, to be evaluated in clinical trials.
CONCLUSIONS: The only direct human data come from a small, non-randomized pilot study and are hypothesis-generating. The clinical consequences of incretin-associated loss of lean mass, and particularly muscle mass, should be investigated in future studies. The hypothesis requires evaluation in randomized controlled trials that properly assess changes in lean mass and muscle mass, along with safety monitoring, before it can inform clinical practice.

Title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Insulin Degludec Versus Insulin Glargine in Trial-Eligible and Ineligible Populations: A DEVOTE-Inspired Target Trial Emulation Using the Swedish National Diabetes Register.
Abstract:
AIMS: To compare cardiovascular outcomes associated with the initiation of insulin degludec versus insulin glargine using a target trial emulation approach in nationwide real-world data.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a nationwide observational cohort study using Swedish health registers, including the National Diabetes Register. Individuals with type 2 diabetes initiating insulin degludec or insulin glargine between 2012 and 2022 were included. Two complementary approaches were applied: a trial-eligible emulation cohort reflecting the eligibility criteria of the DEVOTE trial, and a trial-ineligible emulation cohort representing routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, i.e., myocardial infarction, stroke and cardiovascular mortality). Secondary outcomes included the individual components of MACE, all-cause mortality and heart failure. Average treatment effects were estimated using longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation.
RESULTS: Among 96 731 individuals identified, 44 890 met the study eligibility criteria and were included in the analyses. In the trial-eligible cohort, degludec was associated with a similar risk of MACE compared with glargine (risk ratio: 1.10; 95% CI: 0.91-1.34; p = 0.34), but a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.62-0.92; p = 0.002). In the trial-ineligible emulation cohort, degludec was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.67-0.95; p = 0.004) as well as reduced risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal stroke and heart failure.
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study, degludec was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with glargine, consistently observed in both trial-eligible and trial-ineligible populations, despite similar cardiovascular risk in the trial-eligible cohort.

Title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve across cohorts with different prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFRAI) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Diagnostic performance of CT-FFRAI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR.
RESULTS: In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFRAI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFRAI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P < 0.001 and P = 0.034). Net reclassification improvement for CT-FFRAI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: CT-FFRAI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.

Title: Diagnostic performance of aortic valve calcium and CT-derived aortic valve area in low-gradient aortic stenosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Practice guidelines recommend the use of computed tomography (CT) aortic valve calcium (AVC) scores for patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis (LG-AS). AVC has not been studied in comparison to invasive aortic valve study (IAVS).
OBJECTIVES: To determine the diagnostic performance of AVC and CT-derived aortic valve area (CT-AVA) compared to IAVS as a reference standard.
METHODS: We included consecutive patients with LG-AS with echocardiography, CT and IAVS performed within 1 year at a single tertiary center. Severe AS was defined by aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm2 measured by IAVS. CT-AVA was retrospectively measured by a blinded reader. CT-AVA and sex-based AVC were compared to AS defined by IAVS. Diagnostic performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. AVC and CT-AVA were compared to cardiac events consisting of death, aortic valve replacement and cardiovascular hospitalization.
RESULTS: Out of 294 patients in the overall cohort, 206 patients with definite AS severity by IAVS were included as the primary diagnostic cohort. Severe AS according to invasive AVA (≤1.0 cm2) was present in 72 patients (35.0%). Sex-based AVC scores had relatively poor diagnostic performance compared to the reference IAVS with AUCs of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.70) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.45-0.71) for men and women, respectively. CT-AVA had better diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.77-0.87).
CONCLUSIONS: In our study population, CT-AVA had significantly better diagnostic performance than AVC compared to the reference standard, IAVS.

Title: Time-matched Secondary Fracture Prevention in Older Adults: A Narrative Review of Imminent Risk, Time-to-Benefit, and Treatment Sequencing.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: After a fragility fracture, subsequent fracture risk is highest during the first 6 to 12 months and remains elevated for 1 to 2 years. Anti-osteoporosis therapies differ in onset, persistence, discontinuation kinetics, and safety constraints, yet guidelines rarely operationalize treatment timing within this imminent-risk period. This narrative review examines temporal mismatch between post-fracture risk and treatment effect and proposes a time-matched secondary fracture prevention framework.
METHODS: We conducted an argument-driven narrative review using a structured, non-systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar from January 2000 through July 26, 2026. English-language guidelines, pivotal randomized trials, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and implementation or health-services studies relevant to secondary fracture prevention were included, with priority given to 2024 to 2026 publications. Selection was purposive; no formal risk-of-bias assessment or pooled statistical analysis was performed.
FINDINGS: The evidence base comprised 103 publications and one trial-registry record. Subsequent fractures consistently clustered within the first 12 to 24 months after an index fracture. A pooled meta-analysis of bisphosphonate trials in postmenopausal osteoporosis estimated 12.4 months (95% CI, 6.3 to 18.4 months) to prevent one nonvertebral fracture per 100 treated women; this population-level estimate is not a drug-specific onset threshold and was not derived specifically from recent-fracture patients. Several injectable antiresorptive and bone-forming therapies show early fracture-risk reduction in pivotal trials, but treatment choice must remain safety qualified. In particular, romosozumab requires cardiovascular risk assessment because of the imbalance in serious cardiovascular events observed in ARCH and current labeling restrictions. Rare medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw and denosumab-associated hypocalcemia in advanced chronic kidney disease are additional counseling and monitoring considerations. Treatment cessation is also time-sensitive, especially for denosumab because delayed dosing or discontinuation without follow-on therapy can lead to rebound bone turnover and vertebral fractures.
IMPLICATIONS: Secondary fracture prevention may be improved by initiating appropriate therapy promptly after the index fracture, matching treatment characteristics to the period of highest risk, planning sequential therapy from the outset, and minimizing delivery delays. The framework is hypothesis-generating and should not override drug-specific contraindications, local labeling, or individualized benefit-risk assessment. Prospective studies should test whether explicitly time-matched care reduces early re-fracture compared with conventional risk-stratified treatment.

Title: Evaluation of Inpatient Epoetin Alfa Dosing in Patients With Anemia of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Epoetin alfa labeling and clinical guidelines recommend weight-based dosing for the management of patients with anemia and chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, fixed dosing continues to be used in inpatient practice, and comparative data in hospitalized populations are limited. This study aimed to compare fixed versus weight-based dosing in hospitalized patients with CKD.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included hospitalized adult patients with anemia of CKD who were initiated on epoetin alfa at a large academic medical center between January 2014 and August 2024. The primary outcome was hemoglobin exceeding targets (>10 g/dL for non-dialysis-dependent CKD and >11 g/dL for dialysis-dependent CKD). Secondary outcomes included 90-day all-cause mortality, rehospitalization, major adverse cardiovascular events, packed red blood cell transfusion, new or worsening hypertension, and iron deficiency.
FINDINGS: Among 100 patients (50 in the fixed-dose group and 50 in the weight-based dose group), hemoglobin exceeded targets in 8% and 4% of patients, respectively (P = 0.678). Ninety-day all-cause mortality occurred in 18% and 4% of patients, respectively (P = 0.160); no statistically significant differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Fixed-dose regimens resulted in higher weight-normalized epoetin alfa doses than weight-based dosing (119.8 vs 67.1 units/kg; P < 0.001).
IMPLICATIONS: Among hospitalized patients with CKD, fixed-dose epoetin alfa was associated with substantially higher weight-normalized doses and numerically higher rates of hemoglobin exceeding targets and mortality, though differences in clinical outcomes were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that adherence to guideline-recommended weight-based dosing may minimize excessive epoetin alfa dosing. Larger prospective studies are needed to clarify optimal inpatient erythropoiesis-stimulating agent dosing.

Title: Perioperative Management for Placement of Patent Ductus Arteriosus Stents in Infants With Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Circulation.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Stenting of the patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) offers a minimally invasive alternative to the modified Blalock-Thomas-Taussig shunt in infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow. This study reviews the periprocedural management of infants undergoing ductal stenting in the cardiac catheterization laboratory.
DESIGN: A retrospective single-center review.
SETTING: Quaternary children's hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: Infants receiving PDA stents in the cardiac catheterization laboratory from 2018 to 2021 were included.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included; median age was 5 days [1-62]; 95.6% (65/68) were neonates and 23.5% (16/68) premature. Pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum was the most common cardiac diagnosis (n = 23, 33.8%); 22.1% (15/68) presented with a syndrome and 35.3% (24/68) with noncardiac comorbidities. In total, 39.7% (27/68) developed intraoperative events. Median time to extubation was 19.4 hours [3.2-372.5].
CONCLUSIONS: Infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow undergoing ductal stenting may present with a wide range of challenges in the perioperative period. Meticulous care and interdisciplinary coordination are required to optimize the outcomes for this particularly vulnerable patient group.

Title: Visualization of post-STEMI myocardial infarction and microvascular obstruction with non-contrast, free-breathing whole- heart iT2prep-IR BOOST.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical adoption of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for risk stratification in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is often limited by long scan times and the requirement for breath-holding and contrast agents.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to validate a non-contrast, free-breathing 3D whole-heart T1/T2 CMR method (iT2prep-IR BOOST) for rapid assessment of myocardial injury in STEMI patients, hypothesizing that this technique provides promising diagnostic accuracy and quantitative assessment to conventional contrast-enhanced CMR.
METHODS: A free-breathing 3D isotropic whole-heart iT2prep-IR BOOST sequence was performed with a scan time of <8minutes. Sixty-four STEMI patients underwent CMR, including iT2prep-IR BOOST, clinical T2-STIR, late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and T1/T2 mapping. The diagnostic performance of iT2prep-IR BOOST was evaluated against LGE and T2-STIR to assess myocardial infarction (MI), microvascular obstruction (MVO), and edema. Subgroup analyses further investigated the association between MVO detected by iT2prep-IR BOOST and left ventricular (LV) remodeling at 1-year follow-up.
RESULTS: In 60 STEMI patients, the acquisition was completed in 7.2 ± 0.6min as a single free-breathing 3D whole-heart scan. Patient-level analysis showed high sensitivity and specificity for MVO (100.0% / 87.5%) and segmental MVO detection (95.8% / 97.8%). T2prep-IR BOOST yielded robust image contrast for MI comparable to LGE, while offering comparable edema visualization to T2-STIR. Volumetric and transmurality quantifications of MVO, MI, and edema showed excellent agreement with reference standards (all r > 0.90, p < 0.001), supported by significant biophysical correlations with native T1/T2 values (p < 0.001). Furthermore, in a 1-year follow-up cohort (n=51), baseline T2prep-IR BOOST-derived MVO volume was associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling, showing significant correlations with both ΔLVEDVI (r = 0.305, p = 0.029) and ΔLVESVI (r = 0.293, p = 0.037).
CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary single-center study, iT2prep-IR BOOST showed promising diagnostic performance and close quantitative agreement with conventional LGE and T2-STIR in stable STEMI patients. Further prospective validation in larger, independent, and more heterogeneous cohorts, including patients unable to undergo contrast-enhanced CMR, is required before this technique can be considered an alternative to standard LGE and T2-weighted sequences.

Title: Design of Screening Cardiometabolic Opportunities Using Transformative Echocardiography Artificial Intelligence (SCOUT-Echo-AI).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent among individuals with cardiovascular disease, but often remains undiagnosed until advanced sequelae such as fibrotic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma develop. ​​Transthoracic echocardiography routinely captures incidental subcostal views of the liver that are not used clinically. The EchoNet-Liver algorithm uses artificial intelligence (AI) to predict the presence of liver disease based on routine clinical echocardiograms. Prospective evaluation in real-world practice is needed to understand the clinical utility and impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening.
METHODS: The SCOUT-Echo-AI study is a single-arm, prospective, multicenter, open-label pragmatic interventional trial that will be conducted across six diverse U.S. healthcare systems (Kaiser Permanente Northern California, Stanford Healthcare, Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, University of California Los Angeles, Northwestern Medicine, and Massachusetts General Brigham). Routine echocardiograms will be analyzed by the EchoNet-Liver AI algorithm with an estimated enrollment of ∼3,000 patients. Treating clinicians or participants themselves will be notified of potential undiagnosed liver disease with site-specific workflows in place to ensure routine clinical care for definitive case confirmation. Primary outcomes will be SLD and fibrotic liver disease detection rates and positive predictive values within 12 months of AI identification. Pre-specified secondary outcomes will assess diagnostic accuracy against other gold-standard modalities, treatment initiation, time to diagnosis, and impact on other clinical events. Outcomes will be compared against historical usual-care and contemporary below-threshold cohorts.
CONCLUSION: SCOUT-Echo-AI is a prospective multicenter study evaluating the real-world impact of AI-enabled opportunistic liver disease screening using routine echocardiography.

Title: Independent and Joint Associations of Long-Term Ambient Meteorological Exposures and Socioeconomic Deprivation with Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Although acute meteorological events are recognized cardiovascular hazards, the combined cardiovascular impacts of long-term meteorological exposures and socioeconomic deprivation remain poorly characterized. Among 469,347 UK Biobank participants, we evaluated independent and interactive associations of 1-year average ambient temperature, relative humidity, and the Townsend deprivation index (TDI) with incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and cardiovascular death. Over median 13.7-year follow-up, 31,626 MACE, 12,565 strokes, 17,062 MIs, and 7,161 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In Cox models, the highest versus lowest temperature category was associated with lower MACE risk (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.84-0.91), whereas high humidity (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.05-1.14) and high deprivation (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.34-1.44) were independently associated with elevated risk. Under a counterfactual assigning the least deprived category's risk to both more deprived categories, 11.75% (95% CI, 9.68-13.77%) of incident MACE and 17.15% (12.68-21.39%) of cardiovascular deaths over 10 years would be attributable to deprivation (total-effect specification, omitting smoking, body mass index, hypertension and diabetes; fully adjusted, 6.67% and 11.09%). Temperature and humidity showed multiplicative interactions with TDI: versus the joint low-risk reference, low temperature with high deprivation had HR 1.55 (95% CI, 1.40-1.71) for MACE and high humidity with high deprivation HR 1.51 (1.34-1.71); additive interactions were significant only at intermediate temperature or intermediate humidity (RERI, 0.20 and 0.16). The deprivation gradient was stable in every sensitivity analysis; the temperature association did not persist within assessment centres, nor the humidity association under a time-varying specification, although both persisted across exposure windows and air-pollution adjustment. These findings indicate that long-term lower temperatures and higher humidity, together with socioeconomic deprivation, are independently and jointly associated with elevated cardiovascular risk, underscoring the need for integrated climate and social welfare policies to mitigate health disparities in vulnerable populations.

Title: Ultra-portable ultrasound for third-trimester care: diagnostic performance of the echOpen O1 operated by midwives in rural Senegal.
Journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstetric ultrasound is central to antenatal care, but access remains limited in many low- and middle-income settings. Ultra-portable devices may extend access to basic obstetric imaging and support midwife-led care.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the diagnostic performance of the echOpen O1 ultra-portable ultrasound probe for selected obstetric targets during antenatal follow-up in Senegal.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multicentre pilot diagnostic agreement study in two health facilities in the Sokone health district, Fatick region, from November 2023 to August 2024. Pregnant women at 37 weeks of gestation or more were included. Each participant underwent three ultrasound examinations: two performed by the same midwife using echOpen O1 and a standard ultrasound device in a randomly assigned order, and one blinded echOpen O1 examination performed by a second midwife. Images and short video clips were reviewed by a reference radiologist. Agreement was assessed for foetal number, foetal presentation, foetal cardiac activity and placental location.
RESULTS: Among 221 included women, 214 were analysed. Overall agreement for the core targets between echOpen O1 and standard ultrasound (intra-operator) was 99.5% (95% CI, 98.6-100). Intra-operator agreement was 99.5% (95% CI, 98.6-100) for foetal presentation, 100% (95% CI, 100-100) for foetal number, placental location and foetal cardiac activity. Expert review confirmed intra-operator agreement above 95% for all targets.
CONCLUSION: The echOpen O1 probe showed performance comparable with standard ultrasound for basic third-trimester obstetric assessments, supporting its potential to strengthen antenatal care in resource-limited settings.

Title: Standardized Diagnosis of Lymphocytic Myocarditis at Autopsy: Application of the Seaport Criteria.
Journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The histological diagnosis of lymphocytic myocarditis at autopsy is challenged by limited reproducibility and the lack of standardized criteria applicable to non-biopsy specimens. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and diagnostic performance of the new Seaport criteria for autopsy in a heterogeneous cohort of clinical autopsies.
METHODS: An autopsy cohort of 50 consecutive cases was retrospectively revaluated, including 10 sudden death cases originally diagnosed as lymphocytic myocarditis and 40 controls (ischemic heart disease, brain diseases, liver diseases, and metastatic neoplasms). Each case was reclassified according to Seaport criteria as myocarditis (focal, multifocal, or diffuse), lymphocytic infiltrate of uncertain significance (LIUS), or no inflammation. Immunohistochemistry (CD3, CD68, C4d) and molecular testing for viral genome were carried out in myocarditis/LIUS cases.
RESULTS: By applying the Seaport criteria for autopsy, active lymphocytic myocarditis was confirmed in 9 of 10 originally diagnosed cases, either focal (33%) or multifocal (67%) and never diffuse; one case was reclassified as LIUS. Three additional cases among controls showed LIUS, yielding an overall LIUS prevalence of 8% in the entire series. A subepicardial confluent topography was observed in four myocarditis cases. Temporal assessment revealed subacute forms in 55.6% and acute in 44.4%. Immunohistochemistry confirmed the lymphocytic type, and viral genome was identified in 3/9 myocarditis cases.
CONCLUSIONS: The Seaport criteria are a useful tool in the autopsy setting, supporting a standardized approach to the diagnosis of lymphocytic myocarditis. Refinement of these criteria including topographic distribution of inflammation is warranted. The clinical significance of LIUS remains to be assessed in larger series with clinicopathological correlations.

Title: Long-Term Performance of Bilateral Internal Thoracic Artery Grafts in Young Adults.
Abstract: OBJECTIVE Coronary artery disease (CAD) in young adults is uncommon but associated with substantial long-term morbidity. Limited evidence exists regarding the long-term outcomes of bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) grafting in this population. This study evaluates perioperative and long-term outcomes of BITA revascularization in young adults undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and compares survival outcomes with those of the general population. METHODS A retrospective single-center observational study was conducted in 67 young patients (39 ± 3 years) who underwent BITA grafting for multivessel CAD. Perioperative outcomes, long-term overall survival, major adverse cardio-cerebral events (MACEs), and repeat revascularization were assessed. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Further survival analysis was conducted using an age- and sex-adjusted general population matched for age, sex, and calendar year. RESULTS BITA grafting was associated with very low perioperative morbidity. The median follow-up was 17 years, with an estimated overall survival at 20 years of 74% [0.74 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.52-0.87)] and freedom from MACEs at 20 years of 70% [0.70 (95% CI, 0.49-0.84)]. Sternal wound complications were infrequent (1.5%). CONCLUSIONS BITA revascularization in young adults demonstrates excellent long-term survival, with survival comparable to that of the age- and sex-matched general population during the first 15 years after surgery, along with durable event-free outcomes, supporting its use as a durable revascularization strategy in this population.

Title: Imaging-derived coronary fractional flow reserve: advances in physics-based, machine learning, and physics-informed methods.
Abstract: Purpose of Review Imaging-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) is rapidly evolving beyond conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based pipelines toward machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and physics-informed approaches that enable fast, wire-free, and scalable functional assessment of coronary artery stenosis. This review synthesizes recent advances in computed tomography (CT)-and angiography-based FFR measurement, with particular emphasis on emerging physics-informed neural networks and neural operators (PINNs and PINOs), as well as key considerations for their clinical translation.Recent Findings ML/DL approaches have markedly improved automation and computational speed, enabling prediction of pressure and FFR from anatomical descriptors or angiographic contrast dynamics. However, their real-world performance and generalizability can remain variable and sensitive to domain shift, due to multi-center heterogeneity, interpretability challenges, and differences in acquisition protocols and image quality. Physics-informed learning introduces conservation structure and boundary-condition consistency into model training, improving generalizability and reducing dependence on dense supervision while maintaining rapid inference. Recent evaluation trends increasingly highlight deployment-oriented metrics, including calibration, uncertainty quantification, and quality-control gatekeeping, as essential for safe clinical use.SummaryThe field is converging toward imaging-derived FFR methods that are faster, more automated, and more reliable. While ML/DL offers substantial efficiency gains, physics-informed frameworks such as PINNs and PINOs may provide a more robust balance between speed and physical consistency. Prospective multi-center validation and standardized evaluation will be critical to support broad and safe clinical adoption.

Title: Individualized Cardiac Index-Guided Hemodynamic Therapy in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Elective Major Abdominal Surgery: The PELICAN Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.
RESULTS: Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279.

Title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes as early indicators of long-term maternal atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) - including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), preterm birth, and fetal growth deviations - are emerging female-specific cardiovascular risk factors, but their association with long-term maternal atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between APOs and subsequent AF.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Scopus. We included population-based cohort studies comparing women with and without APOs and reporting incident maternal AF during follow-up. Time-to-event associations were synthesized, pooling hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95 % confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: 12 population-based cohort studies including over 11 million women were analyzed. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were associated with higher long-term risk of AF (HR 1.50; 95 % CI 1.38-1.62), as was preeclampsia (HR 1.45; 95 % CI 1.23-1.71). Preterm birth was also associated with increased AF risk (HR 1.29; 95 % CI 1.13-1.48). Delivery of a large for gestational age infant was associated with higher AF risk (HR 1.23; 95 % CI 1.13-1.34), whereas small for gestational age delivery showed an inverse association (HR 0.88; 95 % CI 0.80-0.97). For GDM, the association was more uncertain, with wide CIs and effect estimates suggesting an increased risk (HR 1.20; 95 % CI 0.84-1.72).
CONCLUSION: Hypertensive and vascular pregnancy complications are associated with elevated long-term maternal AF risk. Associations for gestational diabetes and fetal growth phenotypes were heterogeneous and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings support APOs as markers of later arrhythmic vulnerability.

Title: Identifying the electrically unstable NSTEMI patient: Comparative performance of four scores for short-term risk stratification of major cardiac arrhythmias.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major cardiac arrhythmias after NSTEMI are associated with increased mortality and adverse clinical outcomes. However, evidence comparing the ability of established acute coronary syndrome risk scores to predict in-hospital arrhythmic events remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive NSTEMI patients who underwent coronary angiography at Taipei Medical University Hospital between January 2017 and August 2022. Major cardiac arrhythmias were defined as ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, new-onset atrial fibrillation, and high-degree atrioventricular block occurring during hospitalization. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, electrocardiographic features, and angiographic data were analyzed. The discriminatory performance of TIMI, HEART, GRACE 2.0, T-MACS, and an integrated multivariable model was evaluated using ROC analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 485 patients were included, among whom 55 (11.3%) developed major cardiac arrhythmias during hospitalization. Patients with arrhythmias had significantly higher rates of prior heart failure, AKI, and RBBB. Multivariable logistic regression identified heart failure (OR 3.663, p < 0.001), RBBB (OR 2.611, p = 0.030), AKI (OR 2.102, p = 0.045), and higher serum sodium levels (OR 1.079, p = 0.012) as independent predictors of arrhythmic events. The integrated prediction model demonstrated higher observed discrimination for major cardiac arrhythmias (AUC 0.733, p < 0.001) compared with conventional ACS scoring systems. In contrast, the GRACE 2.0 score showed the most consistent performance for predicting in-hospital mortality.
CONCLUSION: In NSTEMI patients, an exploratory model incorporating heart failure, AKI, RBBB, and serum sodium showed discriminatory ability for major cardiac arrhythmias. Meanwhile, the GRACE 2.0 score remained the most reliable tool for mortality prediction, supporting its continued role in global prognostic assessment of NSTEMI patients.

Title: Fluid dynamic characteristics and quantitative indicators of aortic valve calcification: A fluid-structure interaction study.
Journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Aortic valve calcification is a common valvular disorder. Current fluid-structure interaction studies specifically focused on calcified aortic valves remain limited, leading to an incomplete understanding of valvular motion and hemodynamic behaviors under calcified pathological conditions.
METHODS: Multi-component arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian formulation is utilized to perform fluid-structure interaction simulations for the aortic valve. Numerical predictions of the native valve achieve reasonable consistency with reported in vivo and in vitro experimental measurements. A series of idealized aortic valve calcification models are constructed to quantify how calcification patterns and material properties alter valvular dynamic behavior, together with the overall hemodynamic performance modulated by calcification morphology.
RESULTS: Within the idealized numerical framework, calcified aortic valves consistently present incomplete leaflet opening and elevated flow shear stress. This study proposed a preliminary dimensionless parameter to characterize calcification-induced alterations in valve dynamics. Numerical classification of calcification severity is implemented based on this parameter within the present model, which may correspond to the developmental stages of calcification to a certain extent.
CONCLUSIONS: This study established an idealized numerical model of calcified aortic valves to quantitatively evaluate calcification-related dynamic alterations. A preliminary dimensionless parameter is explored to potentially characterize aortic valve calcification severity, providing a prospective reference for evaluating the developmental stages of calcification. The findings may provide tentative theoretical insights for future clinical recognition of aortic valve calcification.

Title: Human-in-the-loop Reinforcement Learning for personalized and adaptive interventions in wellness and healthcare: A systematic literature review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is emerging as a promising technique to support personalized and adaptive clinical interventions. This is thanks to its ability to model sequential decision making and to learn from longitudinal data. The deployment of RL raises challenges regarding interpretability and integration into clinical workflows. These concerns have motivated interest in human-in-the-loop approaches, in which individuals retain an actual or intended role before an RL-supported decision affects care. However, the use of RL in healthcare remains fragmented and poorly standardized. A systematic review of the literature is therefore timely, to identify current state, directions, challenges and research gaps.
METHODS: A systematic review was reported in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. ScienceDirect, Scopus, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science databases were searched for all records available up to 21 January 2026, encompassing studies applying RL to personalized interventions in healthcare and wellness fields and including the concept of "human-in-the-loop". Extracted information contained diseases, applications, RL-methods, dataset dimensions, integration with other techniques, and performance evaluation strategies.
RESULTS: Forty-one papers met the inclusion criteria and were examined in detail. RL was mainly found in the healthcare rather than in the wellness field, especially in type 2 diabetes and other chronic diseases, and intensive care settings, where the sequential nature of decision-making processes plays a significant role. Data structure and information vary extensively, creating significant comparability challenges. The methodologies show strong heterogeneity in algorithms and evaluation metrics, limiting reproducibility and generalizability. From the disease-focus point of view, cardiovascular applications are underrepresented, despite cardiovascular diseases being the leading cause of death globally and the potential value of adaptive decision-making in cardiovascular disease management.
CONCLUSIONS: RL offers an opportunity to personalize treatments and optimize clinical decision-making processes employing sequential data. However, the lack of shared methodological standards, transparency in model descriptions, and limited number of prospective studies constitute significant barriers to its adoption. In conclusion, better documented datasets, comparable metrics, and prospective evaluations are required to establish clinical effectiveness and support future implementation.

Title: Integrating emerging preservation strategies in cardiac transplantation: From nanotherapeutic frontiers to clinical translation.
Abstract: Hypothermic preservation remains a critical bottleneck in heart transplantation, primarily due to the exacerbation of ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and tightly restricted organ viability windows. Addressing this global clinical crisis requires a departure from traditional monotherapies. This review critically appraises-rather than merely synthesizes-three multidisciplinary advancements: (1) preservation solutions supplemented with nanotherapeutics, with explicit distinction between proof-of-concept, small-animal, and clinically translatable evidence; (2) technological transitions from static cold storage (SCS) to ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) and nanowarming-assisted cryopreservation; and (3) bioactive compounds derived from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), evaluated through a SWOT framework that acknowledges phytochemical variability and the paucity of clinical transplantation data. We further examine the emerging-but currently nascent and largely speculative---role of artificial intelligence in perfusion decision support. We emphasize that these three domains are not evidentially equivalent: perfusion technology is clinically implemented, pharmacological and nanotherapeutic adjuncts remain predominantly preclinical, and AI applications in cardiac preservation are currently confined to retrospective outcome modelling, with no published closed-loop perfusion control in clinical practice.

Title: Sclerotherapy for slow-flow vascular malformations: An international survey of practice patterns and periprocedural management.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Slow-flow vascular malformations (SFVMs) are rare congenital anomalies that cause significant morbidity. Currently, no evidence-based therapy exists to improve SFVM symptoms and reduce its relapse in the long-term. Sclerotherapy is central to management and widely practiced, yet comprehensive international data are limited and no standardized guidelines exist. We aimed to evaluate current practice patterns, focusing on sclerotherapy and multidisciplinary care.
METHODS: An international cross-sectional survey was distributed to experts in the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) network. The questionnaire addressed treatment indications, sclerosant use and availability, anesthesia, coagulation management, risk communication, and case-based decision-making. Responses were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Fifty-two physicians from 16 countries completed the survey. Respondents included interventional radiologists (69%), vascular medicine specialists (15%), and pediatric surgeons (8%) in academic centers (90%). Multidisciplinary consultation was reported by 92% of participants. Ethanol (67%), bleomycin (58%), and polidocanol (52%) were the most accessible, although ethanol was consistently rated as the most dangerous. Sclerosant choice varied by lesion type and scenario. The risks most frequently communicated were skin necrosis (92% for lymphatic malformations and 94% for venous malformations, respectively), pigmentary changes (70% and 75%), and nerve injury (68% and 75%), whereas systemic complications such as cardiovascular collapse (16% and 22%) or death (14% and 22%) were less often discussed. In children, general anesthesia was preferred (90% and 86%), whereas adults received local (49% and 41%) or general anesthesia (47% and 43%). Preprocedural coagulation testing and anticoagulation strategies showed marked heterogeneity, especially for venous malformations.
CONCLUSIONS: This survey demonstrates substantial variability in SFVM management, particularly regarding sclerosant selection, anesthesia, coagulation, periprocedural care, and risk communication, and identifies areas where future prospective and collaborative research will be needed before evidence-based recommendations can be developed.

Title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiovascular Conditions in Medicare Advantage In-Home Health Risk Assessments.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medicare Advantage insurers conduct in-home health risk assessments (HRAs) to identify high-risk patients and facilitate appropriate care. Critics argue this practice increases risk-adjusted payments without improving quality. Comprehensive data on use of in-home HRAs and downstream treatment are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To examine trends in cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs, characteristics associated with HRA-based diagnoses, and treatment rates after diagnoses.
DESIGN: Cohort study.
SETTING: Population-based.
PARTICIPANTS: Medicare Advantage beneficiaries.
MEASUREMENTS: Using 100% Medicare claims, trends in the proportion of cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs (vs. facility-based visits) were examined. Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to estimate the association between beneficiary- and plan-level characteristics and HRA-based diagnoses and compare treatment rates across settings.
RESULTS: Among 21 496 506 Medicare Advantage beneficiaries diagnosed with a cardiovascular risk factor or disease, the proportion diagnosed during in-home HRAs increased between 2018 and 2022 for hypertension (45.9% to 47.7%), hyperlipidemia (57.8% to 66.7%), diabetes (47.8% to 51.6%), atrial fibrillation (30.0% to 36.0%), ischemic heart disease (37.2% to 41.6%), peripheral vascular disease (64.5% to 73.9%), and heart failure (34.7% to 42.6%). Racial and ethnic minority beneficiaries and those enrolled in lower-rated plans were more likely to receive HRA-based diagnoses. Treatment rates were substantially lower after HRA-based diagnoses across all conditions.
LIMITATIONS: Differences in the severity of conditions between groups could not be assessed. Prescription fills were used as a proxy for management. Observed differences in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions across encounter settings may be susceptible to unmeasured confounding.
CONCLUSION: Among Medicare Advantage beneficiaries, an increasingly large share of cardiovascular conditions are being diagnosed through in-home HRAs, but treatment rates after these diagnoses are consistently lower than after facility-based encounters.
PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

Title: Hypofractionated Versus Conventionally Fractionated Postmastectomy Radiotherapy With Internal Mammary Node Irradiation for High-Risk Breast Cancer (HypoMast-IMNI): A Randomized Phase III Trial.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
Abstract:
PURPOSE: When coverage of internal mammary nodes (IMN) is required, the efficacy and safety of hypofractionated regimens within postmastectomy radiotherapy (PMRT) remain to be established. This study evaluated hypofractionated radiotherapy (HypoRT) in patients with high-risk, operable breast cancer undergoing PMRT with IMN irradiation (IMNI).
METHODS: In this phase III noninferiority trial, eligible patients with high-risk disease after mastectomy (including pT1-4N2-3, pT3-4N1, or pT1-2N1 disease with additional high-risk factors) were randomly assigned (1:1) to HypoRT (42.56 Gy in 16 fractions) or conventionally fractionated radiotherapy (ConvRT; 50 Gy in 25 fractions), both targeting the chest wall and regional lymph nodes, including the IMN. The primary end point was locoregional recurrence (LRR). Secondary end points were distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), breast cancer recurrence-free survival (BCRFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment-related toxicity. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov (identifier: NCT03856372).
RESULTS: Between September 2018 and July 2022, 1,494 patients were randomly assigned. After a median follow-up of 58.1 months in the modified intention-to-treat population (n = 1,429), the 5-year cumulative incidence of LRR was 1.7% (95% CI, 0.9 to 2.9) with HypoRT and 2.2% (95% CI, 1.3 to 3.5) with ConvRT (hazard ratio, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.32 to 1.51]), meeting the noninferiority criterion (P = .017). No significant differences were observed in 5-year DMFS, BCRFS, DFS, or OS. Grade 3 acute skin toxicity was significantly lower with HypoRT (1.7% v 12.2%, P < .001). The incidence of grade ≥2 radiation pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis was low and comparable between arms, with no ischemic cardiac events recorded.
CONCLUSION: For patients with high-risk, operable breast cancer requiring PMRT with IMNI, the 16-fraction HypoRT regimen is noninferior to ConvRT for locoregional control, offers a superior acute toxicity profile, and demonstrates excellent cardiopulmonary safety.

Title: Safety profile of IL-23 inhibitors from the perspective of physicians and pharmacists: A retrospective real-world pharmacovigilance observational study based on the FAERS database.
Abstract: ObjectiveInterleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitors are widely used for psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease, yet their long-term safety profiles require continual monitoring. This retrospective observational real-world study aimed to detect potential disproportionate reporting signals associated with tildrakizumab, risankizumab, and guselkumab using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).MethodsAE reports for tildrakizumab, risankizumab, and guselkumab from Q3 2017 to Q3 2025 were retrieved from FAERS. Disproportionality analysis using reporting odds ratios (RORs) was performed, and reported adverse events were classified by system organ classes (SOCs).ResultsA total of 1124, 8574, and 14597 AEs were retrieved for the three IL-23 inhibitors, generating 42, 286, and 348 disproportionate reporting signals, and accumulating 23, 24, and 24 SOCs. Frequently reported AEs included drug ineffectiveness, psoriasis, injection-site reactions, and infections. Disproportionate reporting signals not listed in the current FDA-approved product label comprised cardiovascular events (e.g., myocardial infarction; tildrakizumab ROR = 6.45), malignancies (e.g., malignant melanoma; risankizumab ROR = 8.57), hepatobiliary disorders, and renal complications.ConclusionThese exploratory, hypothesis-generating disproportionate reporting signals may inform routine pharmacovigilance practice for IL-23 inhibitors, alongside well-established common reported events such as infections and systemic reactions. Further pharmacoepidemiologic studies are needed to validate these observations.

Title: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Is Associated With Greater Cardiovascular Risk Following Lumbar Interbody Fusion.
Abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare perioperative cardiovascular outcomes between patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) following transforaminal or posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF/PLIF).MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients undergoing elective TLIF or PLIF between 2011 and 2025. Cohorts were defined by heart failure phenotype and propensity score-matched (PSM) 1:1 for baseline demographics and comorbidities. Outcomes included postoperative atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/AFL), myocardial infarction (MI), and secondary complications within 90 days. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated. Significance was defined as p < 0.05.ResultsOf 46,431 patients, 1,253 (2.7%) had HFrEF, 1,920 (4.1%) had HFpEF, and 43,258 (93.2%) had no heart failure. After PSM, both phenotypes carried elevated risk relative to non-HF controls across measured complications, including acute respiratory failure, pneumonia, AF/AFL, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and 90-day emergency department visits (all p<0.05). In the direct phenotype comparison (1,217 matched pairs), acute MI occurred more frequently in HFrEF than HFpEF patients (14.4% vs. 8.7%, p<0.001). HFrEF was associated with greater odds of acute MI (OR 1.760 [95% CI: 1.363, 2.273], p<0.001) and AF/AFL (OR 1.278 [95% CI: 1.079, 1.513], p=0.005) compared with HFpEF.ConclusionAmong patients with heart failure undergoing TLIF or PLIF, those with HFrEF are at increased risk of postoperative AF/AFL and MI compared with HFpEF patients. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing heart failure phenotype during preoperative risk stratification and may support enhanced perioperative precautions.

Title: Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review.
Abstract: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.

Title: Cardiac Effects of Combined Versus Individual Interventions of Mediterranean Diet and Exercise in Adults with the Hypertriglyceridemic Waist Phenotype: A Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype, combining abdominal obesity and elevated serum triglycerides, is associated with adverse cardiovascular prognosis. The combination of dietary and exercise programs has the potential to improve outcomes with regard to adverse cardiac remodeling and dysfunction associated with poor metabolic health. We tested the hypothesis that the combination of a Mediterranean Diet (MedDiet) and exercise interventions improves cardiac structure and function more than the sum of each individual intervention.
METHODS: We performed a randomized 2 × 2 factorial design trial that included adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype (triglycerides ≥1.50 mmol/L, waist circumference ≥80 cm in women or ≥94 cm in men). Participants were randomly assigned to one of four 16-week interventions: (1) MedDiet alone, (2) exercise alone, (3) MedDiet + exercise, or (4) control group. The MedDiet groups received education, counseling, and key food items from the MedDiet. The exercise groups participated in a structured exercise program designed to achieve 150 min of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week. Data were collected during the screening, baseline, and post-intervention visits. In mixed-effects models, we compared the post-intervention echocardiographic measurements of left ventricular (LV) structure and function per intervention group after adjusting for age, sex, and baseline values. We calculated an interaction ratio between MedDiet and exercise to assess their combined effect.
RESULTS: Of the 200 recruited, 185 participants (76% women) had available echocardiographic data. LV measurements were within normal range for most participants. After the intervention, the posterior wall thickness (LV structure) was higher in the MedDiet groups (0.04 [95% CI: 0.01-0.07] cm), and the septal mitral annular tissue Doppler e' velocity (diastolic function) was higher in the exercise groups (0.4 [95% CI: 0.0-0.8] cm/s). No significant interactions between interventions were identified with respect to LV measurements.
CONCLUSION: No interaction between the MedDiet and exercise interventions on LV structure and function was observed among adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype. Further research is needed to ascertain whether the combination of these interventions can prevent the development of adverse LV remodeling over the long term or in participants with more advanced cardiac alterations.

Title: Integrating Non-Invasive Liver Assessment into Screening Colonoscopy: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Steatotic liver disease is underdiagnosed despite guideline recommendations for risk-based case-finding. Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening colonoscopy engages a prevention-oriented, healthcare-seeking population in whom liver disease may go undetected. We assessed the feasibility, acceptance, and yield of non-invasive liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy visits.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled adults aged ≥50 years attending screening colonoscopy. Individuals with known chronic liver disease were excluded. Participants underwent hepatic ultrasound and point shear wave elastography. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds.
RESULTS: Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds.
DISCUSSION: Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

Title: Clinical Effectiveness of AI-Based Cardiac Arrest Prediction System for General Ward Patients (VITAL-MD): Protocol for a Multicenter Pragmatic Stepped Wedge Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) remains a frequent and devastating event, and conventional early warning scores (EWSs) coupled with rapid response systems (RRSs) have shown inconsistent effects on patient-centered outcomes, largely owing to limited predictive accuracy and high false-alarm burden. AI-based EWSs (AI-EWSs) have demonstrated superior discrimination retrospectively, but high-quality prospective evidence in true external validation environments remains scarce. Existing AI-EWS trials have either been confined to internal-development settings or bundled the algorithm with specific implementation infrastructure, leaving the stand-alone effect of AI-based software as a medical device (AI-SaMD) on patient outcomes uncharacterized.
OBJECTIVE: This trial will evaluate whether implementation of AI-SaMD (VUNO Med-DeepCARS) as a stand-alone clinical decision-support tool in routine general-ward care reduces IHCA compared with usual care based on conventional EWSs.
METHODS: The VITAL-MD trial (validation of an AI-based clinical deterioration prediction model on patient outcomes through a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial [SW-CRT] multicenter evaluation of DeepCARS) is a pragmatic, multicenter, SW-CRT conducted at 4 tertiary academic hospitals in the Republic of Korea. Six tertiary academic hospitals were assessed for eligibility based on inpatient capacity, RRS operating hours aligned with the national RRS pilot program, and no prior AI-SaMD use. All adult patients aged 19 years or older admitted to general wards during the 12-month trial period are included; patients younger than 19 years, or with no documented vital signs throughout hospitalization, are excluded. The 4 sites are randomized to sequentially transition from preimplementation (usual care) to postimplementation (AI-SaMD-guided care) in 4 steps separated by 7-day washout periods. DeepCARS generates real-time risk scores from 4 vital signs and integrates into the existing electronic medical record interface without altering RRS workflows. The primary outcome is the incidence of general-ward IHCA, defined per the Utstein guidelines, among the target cohort (defined as patients exceeding the alert threshold at least once). Assuming a baseline IHCA incidence of 6.70%, a 40% relative risk reduction, an intracluster correlation coefficient of 0.01, and 350 patients per cluster-period, 7002 target-cohort patients (total enrollment approximately 72,695) provide 80% power. Analyses follow the intention-to-treat principle using generalized linear mixed models adjusting for prespecified covariates, with prespecified sensitivity, subgroup, and compliance analyses.
RESULTS: The trial was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service (KCT0010243) on February 28, 2025. Recruitment was conducted from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. All 4 sites completed transition to the postimplementation period, and data cleaning is currently underway before the final database lock, with primary results expected in 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: VITAL-MD will provide the first large-scale, multicenter randomized evidence evaluating whether an AI-EWS, deployed as a stand-alone device in external validation environments and benchmarked against real-world standard-of-care practice, improves patient-centered outcomes for general-ward patients, advancing the evaluation of AI-SaMD from retrospective diagnostic accuracy toward prospective, action-anchored clinical utility.

Title: Greenspace visitation and risk of major adverse cardiovascular events: evidence from the Houston methodist cardiovascular learning health system registry.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate whether mobility-derived greenspace visitation, as a behavioural measure of environmental exposure, is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) independent of individual and neighbourhood factors.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults in the Houston Methodist Cardiovascular Disease Learning Health System Registry (2016-2023). Greenspace visitation was defined at the census-tract level using mobility-derived foot-traffic data and modelled as annual visits per resident device. The primary outcome was incident MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, and all-cause mortality). The Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and Kaplan-Meier curves assessed associations with sequential adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, smoking, and neighbourhood social vulnerability. Among 1 088 866 adults without baseline atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, median (SD) age was 49 (17.6) years, and 59.9% were female. Greenspace visitation varied across neighbourhoods and by demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Each additional 10 annual visits was associated with lower MACE risk in unadjusted models [hazard ratio (HR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.81-0.83] and after adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and smoking (HR 0.89; 95% CI: 0.88-0.91). A non-linear relationship showed risk reductions at low-to-moderate visitation, plateauing at 10-15 visits annually. After adjusting for social vulnerability, associations were attenuated and no longer significant. The Kaplan-Meier curves showed higher event-free survival in high-visitation areas, consistent across MACE components.
