CONCLUSION: Mobility-derived greenspace visitation is associated with lower cardiovascular risk. These findings highlight greenspace engagement as a potentially modifiable behavioural exposure and support strategies to enhance access and utilization of greenspaces for cardiovascular prevention.

Title: Vascular Risk Factors and Late-Onset Epilepsy.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Late-onset epilepsy (LOE; onset at age ≥65 years) is increasingly recognized in older adults and may be associated with vascular risk.
OBJECTIVE: To identify vascular risk factors (VRFs) associated with incident LOE in older adults.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This study is an individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 US population-based prospective cohort studies (the Epilepsy-Cog Study). In 5 cohorts linked to Medicare for epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began when a participant had accrued 2 years of continuous fee-for-service enrollment and was 65 years of age or older and extended to the end of continuous enrollment. Claims linkage covered 1991-2018 in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC), 1992-2019 in the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), 2000-2019 in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), 2000-2020 in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS), and 1999-2019 in the Washington Heights/Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP). In the Northern Manhattan Study (NOMAS), which was not Medicare linked and used cohort-based epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began at cohort entry in 1993-2008 and extended to 2024. Data analysis was completed in January 2026.
EXPOSURES: Sociodemographic characteristics and VRFs assessed by self-report, examinations, laboratory measures, and medication use.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident LOE. Associations between risk factors and incident LOE were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios.
RESULTS: From 43 753 participants in Epilepsy-Cog, 551 participants with prevalent epilepsy and 945 with no follow-up after Epilepsy-Cog baseline were excluded. Among 42 257 participants (mean [SD] age, 71.4 [6.9] years; 23 383 [56.0%] female) followed up for a mean (SD) of 9.3 (6.2) years, 1500 participants (3.5%) developed LOE (3.8 per 1000 person-years). In fully adjusted models, LOE risk was higher with current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), hypertension (HR = 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.31), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), chronic kidney disease (HR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.48), history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), and apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (1 ε4 allele: HR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07-1.39; 2 ε4 alleles: HR = 1.84; 95% CI, 1.36-2.50). Associations of VRFs with LOE were similar across age, sex, and race and ethnicity subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this pooled analysis of 6 US cohorts, multiple VRFs and a history of stroke were associated with incident LOE. These findings suggest that LOE may reflect the underlying burden of brain vascular disease.

Title: A study on the dose-response relationship between glycemic variability and in-dialysis hypotension in patients with diabetes undergoing hemodialysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the dose-response relationship between Glycemic variability (GV) and Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) in diabetic hemodialysis (MHD) patients, identify the critical Coefficient of variation (CV) threshold, and inform precision glucose management.
METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 240 diabetic MHD patients (2023-2024). Continuous glucose monitoring provided GV parameters (CV, MAGE, SD). Patients were divided into IDH (n = 98) and non-IDH (n = 142) groups. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyzed dose-response; multivariate logistic regression assessed independent effects, with Subgroup analysis and interaction tests.
RESULTS: CV was significantly higher in the IDH group (42.3% vs. 26.5%, P<0.001). RCS revealed a nonlinear positive correlation (P<0.001). When CV>36%, IDH risk increased sharply (threshold effect). Each 10% CV rise increased IDH risk by 98.4% (OR 1.984). Compared to Q1, Q3 (OR 3.512) and Q4 (OR 8.637) showed significantly higher risk. Associations were stronger in patients aged ≥60 years, dialysis duration ≥36 months, or with cardiovascular disease (interaction P<0.05). CV predicted IDH with AUC=0.856; optimal cutoff 36.5% (sensitivity 78.6%, specificity 82.4%).
CONCLUSION: A significant dose-response relationship exists between GV and IDH. CV>36% is an independent risk factor. Maintaining CV below 36% may reduce IDH risk and improve outcomes.

Title: Personalized Remote Patient Management in Heart Failure : From Implanted Hemodynamic Monitoring Toward an Artificial Intelligence-Supported Adaptive Care Cycle.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Implanted pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) monitoring provides an early window on imminent worsening heart failure (HF). Randomized trials demonstrated that PAP-guided management significantly reduces HF hospitalizations, but substantial residual risk persists despite recent major advances in HF pharmacotherapy. We review lessons from PAP-guided remote patient management and examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could support more individualized eligibility assessment and multimodal longitudinal surveillance within a patient-centered adaptive care cycle to further improve clinical outcomes.
RECENT FINDINGS: HF is increasingly recognized as a systemic disease characterized, across HF phenotypes, by multiple cardiac and non-cardiac comorbidities. CHAMPION, GUIDE-HF, and MONITOR-HF did not systematically incorporate comorbidity-related risk into patient selection, while PAP-guided treatment focused predominantly on diuretic adjustment, and monitoring strategies were not adapted to individual disease trajectories. AI could help integrate multidimensional phenotyping to estimate individual risk and expected benefit pre-implant, use comprehensive longitudinal monitoring data to support personalized, actionable clinical decision-making, and enable dynamic adaptation of monitoring intensity tailored to the disease trajectory. This may improve clinical outcomes, reduce healthcare professional workload, enhance patient experience and treatment adherence, and increase cost-effectiveness.

Title: Family screening for genetic cardiomyopathies in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents: a joint clinical and genetic approach.
Abstract: Adolescents may present with abnormal ECG findings despite having no structural or electrical evidence of cardiomyopathy. The value of extending family screening to this subgroup remains uncertain. To evaluate the impact of family screening in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents, and determine whether a joint clinical-genetic approach improves the diagnostic yield. In this prospective cohort study, adolescents with an abnormal ECG identified through a nationwide screening program underwent comprehensive clinical/genetic evaluation. Phenotype-negative individuals were included. Relatives underwent clinical screening, with cascade genetic testing offered when probands carried a likely/definite pathogenic (LP/P) cardiomyopathy variant. Abnormal screening outcomes included relatives with (i) de novo cardiomyopathy diagnosis, (ii) early cardiomyopathic traits, or (iii) gene-positive/phenotype-negative (G + P -) status. Sixteen adolescents (0.6%) met inclusion criteria, and 3 (18.8%) were G + (MYBPC3, MYH7, ACTC1). One in five relatives (n = 13/71, 18.3%; 95% CI 11.0-28.9%) were referred, most having an abnormal ECG (12.7%). Nine relatives (12.7%; 95% CI 4.9-20.4%) exhibited early cardiomyopathy traits at baseline. One (1.4%) relative was G + /P - . Cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 3 (4.2%, 95% CI 0.9-11.8%) relatives at baseline (n = 2 HCM, n = 1 DCM). One relative with early cardiomyopathy traits underwent phenoconversion (NDLVC) during follow-up at 77 months, yielding an overall diagnostic rate of 5.6% (95% CI 2.0-13.8%) in 4 unrelated families. A joint clinical-genetic approach enabled personalized surveillance in 6 relatives (8.5%), including 2 (2.8%) diagnoses that would otherwise have been missed with conventional clinical screening.Conclusion: One in five relatives of ECG‑positive phenotype‑negative adolescents received a cardiomyopathy diagnosis or had early cardiomyopathy traits. A joint clinical-genetic approach in this subgroup may aid early cardiomyopathy detection in selected families, though findings remain exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts. What is Known - What is New: •Resting ECG can identify individuals harboring conditions linked to sudden cardiac death •The penetrance of cardiomyopathy is age dependent, which explains why screened adolescents may exhibit abnormal ECG patterns in the absence of a cardiomyopathy diagnosis •Our data indicate that extending screening to relatives of ECG-positive, phenotype-negative adolescents is justified, with one in five relatives receiving a new cardiomyopathy diagnosis (5.6%) or exhibiting early cardiomyopathy traits (11.3%) •A joint clinical/genetic evaluation in this context may help personalize screening strategies.

Title: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) as a prognostic marker in polytrauma: predicting 30-day mortality and coagulation support needs.
Abstract: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS), derived from a simple formula based on haematocrit and haemoglobin values, has been associated with an unfavourable prognosis in many cardiovascular conditions, demonstrating a correlation with volume overload and the haemodynamic status of the patient. Indeed, ePVS was demonstrated to estimate the degree of congestion and was independently associated with cardiovascular outcomes, rehospitalization, and death in patients with heart failure (HF), confirming its prognostic value also in inflammatory pathologies. Due to its easy and immediate availability even in the emergency department (ED), ePVS may be useful in trauma patients to improve their initial evaluation and management. The aim of this retrospective observational study was to evaluate the role of ePVS at ED admission in predicting mortality and blood products use, red blood cells (RBC) and fresh frozen plasma (FFP), in trauma. We included 790 patients, of whom 67.7% were male; mean age 43.9 years; median Injury Severity Score (ISS) 7.5. The 30-day mortality rate was 2.8% (22/790). The median ePVS was significantly increased in deceased as compared to survivors (5.76; 4.79-8.36 versus 4.41; 3.92-5.05; p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS is an independent risk factor even after adjusting for other variables associated with 30-day mortality (odds radio, OR of 1.23; 95% confidence interval, CI 1.016-1.478, p = 0.034). Prediction of 30-day mortality for ePVS showed an AUROC of 0.776 (95% CI 0.666-0.887). Moreover, ePVS showed a positive correlation with the number of packed RBC and FFP units transfused, both during ED management, within the first 24 h, and over the entire hospital stay. The present findings suggest ePVS as a quick and easy tool to predict 30-day mortality and the need for blood resuscitation in trauma patients. Future studies may validate ePVS as a quick and easy tool for trauma victims' stratification and for predicting resource needs and mortality.

Title: Computed tomography-derived cardiac parameters versus biochemical inflammatory indices for discriminating disease severity and identifying cardiovascular comorbidity in obstructive sleep apnoea: A cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: It is unclear whether haematological inflammatory indices or CT-derived cardiac parameters add discriminative information beyond standard clinical variables in obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome (OSAS). We compared both modalities, alone and combined, against age, sex and body mass index (BMI) for identifying severe OSAS and associated cardiovascular comorbidity.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cross-sectional study of 401 participants (240 OSAS, 161 controls). Four nested logistic regression models were fitted in the OSAS cohort: M0 (age, sex, BMI); M1 (M0 plus biochemical indices CAR, NLR, PLR, SII); M2 (M0 plus CT-derived cardiac parameters: pulmonary artery [PA] diameter, PA/aorta ratio, RV/LV ratio, ventricular wall thicknesses); and M3 (M0 plus CT plus biochemical). We compared discrimination (AUC, DeLong), reclassification (continuous NRI, IDI) and model fit (likelihood ratio tests), with internal validation by 500-iteration bootstrap optimism correction and repeated tenfold cross-validation. Missing predictor data were handled by multiple imputation (MICE, m = 20) as the primary approach. Cardiovascular outcomes were defined from echocardiography to avoid predictor-outcome overlap.
RESULTS: For severe OSAS, M2 improved on M0 (AUC 0.755 vs 0.716; LR p = 0.005; NRI + 0.60 [95% CI 0.35-0.83]; IDI + 0.055 [0.027-0.083]), whereas M1 did not (LR p = 0.62). M3 added nothing over M2 (ΔAUC = 0.007; LR p = 0.63). Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.705, 0.695, 0.721 and 0.716 for M0-M3, so the incremental gain was modest. Nocturnal hypoxaemia indices discriminated severe OSAS far better than CT (ODI AUC 0.888 vs PA diameter 0.699), and once ODI and T90 were available CT added little (ΔAUC < 0.01). CT parameters gave modest reclassification for hypertension, coronary artery disease and the composite cardiovascular outcome; biochemical indices did not.
CONCLUSIONS: CT-derived cardiac parameters, particularly PA diameter, added discrimination over age, sex and BMI for severe OSAS; haematological indices did not. When thoracic CT is already available for another indication, opportunistic measurement of PA dimensions may complement clinical risk stratification. These findings are exploratory and require prospective external validation.

Title: Treatment selection and long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years undergoing valve reintervention for failed surgical aortic bioprostheses: insights from the Netherlands Heart Registration.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe real-world treatment allocation and observed long-term survival in patients aged 50 to < 75 years with failed surgical aortic bioprostheses who underwent reintervention through valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation (ViV-TAVI) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (redo-SAVR) in the Netherlands.
METHODS: Patients aged 50 to < 75 years who underwent ViV-TAVI or redo-SAVR for a failing surgical bioprosthesis between 2015 and 2020 were identified from the Netherlands Heart Registration. Baseline characteristics and Dutch surgical-risk categories were compared by treatment strategy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with ViV-TAVI selection. Kaplan-Meier analysis described survival, and treatment-specific Cox models explored factors associated with all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Of 345 patients, 41% underwent ViV-TAVI and 59% redo-SAVR. Patients selected for ViV-TAVI were older (median 71 vs. 67 years, p < 0.001), had higher surgical risk (EuroSCORE II: 6.2% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.014), and had a greater comorbidity burden than redo-SAVR patients. Despite these baseline risk differences, estimated survival within the ViV-TAVI cohort was 94.2% at 30 days, 89.6% at 2 years, and 74.4% at 4 years; corresponding redo-SAVR estimates were 96.1%, 89.8%, and 88.4%. Left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30% and chronic lung disease were associated both with ViV-TAVI selection (OR: 8.04, 95% CI: 2.16-29.92 and OR: 3.25, 95% CI: 1.53-6.92, respectively) and with all-cause mortality after redo-SAVR (HR: 15.70, 95% CI: 2.49-67.14 and HR: 4.23, 95% CI: 1.53-13.14, respectively).
CONCLUSION: In this Dutch observational registry, ViV-TAVI was predominantly selected for patients with a higher-risk clinical phenotype, while redo-SAVR was more often used in lower-risk reintervention candidates and showed higher observed long-term survival. These data describe contemporary treatment selection and prognosis but do not establish comparative superiority of either strategy.

Title: Cardio-hepatic injury phenotypes and short-term outcomes in acute decompensated heart failure.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal liver biochemistry is common in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF), yet most studies evaluate individual markers rather than clinically meaningful patterns of hepatic involvement. We examined whether cardiohepatic injury phenotypes derived from routine liver tests identify distinct short-term prognostic profiles in patients hospitalized with ADHF.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included consecutive adults hospitalized with ADHF between December 2006 and 2017. Using peak in-hospital values of aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and total bilirubin, patients were classified into four phenotypes: no hepatic injury, hepatocellular injury, cholestatic injury, or combined injury. Associations with in-hospital mortality were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Post-discharge outcomes (30-day mortality, readmission, and their composite) were analyzed using Cox and Fine-Gray models.
RESULTS: Among 8332 ADHF admissions, 6792 (81.5%) had sufficient data for phenotype classification: 58.1% had no hepatic injury, 22.1% hepatocellular injury, 13.1% cholestatic injury, and 6.7% combined injury. In-hospital mortality differed markedly across phenotypes (3.5%, 16.3%, 9.0%, and 24.3%, respectively; p < 0.001). After adjustment, all injury phenotypes independently predicted in-hospital death compared with no injury. Among 6128 patients included in adjusted post-discharge analyses, hepatocellular and combined injury were independently associated with higher 30-day mortality and the composite outcome, whereas isolated cholestatic injury was not. Hepatocellular and combined injury independently predicted 30-day readmission.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine liver test patterns identify clinically meaningful cardiohepatic phenotypes in ADHF. While all hepatic injury phenotypes are associated with increased in-hospital mortality, only phenotypes with hepatocellular involvement predict adverse early post-discharge outcomes. Pattern-based interpretation of liver tests may improve early risk stratification in patients hospitalized with ADHF.

Title: New insights into takotsubo syndrome: results from a multicenter cohort.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Takotsubo syndrome has long been deemed a benign condition following sudden emotional stress. While current mechanisms explaining the acute cardiac dysfunction are not fully understood, current evidence suggests certain takotsubo populations are at higher risk of adverse course. Acute neurologic emergencies commonly precede the takotsubo syndrome and new insights into the role of the brain-heart axis and central autonomic regions driving excess sympathetic activation have come about.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This multicenter analysis included 595 patients admitted between January 2013 and December 2024 with takotsubo syndrome across 13 German tertiary care centers. The aim of this study was to (I) assess whether acute brain pathology influences severity of cardiac dysfunction differently in comparison to other nonneurologic forms of physical or emotional stress, (II) investigate short-term recovery of cardiac function, and (III) improve identification of vulnerable patients susceptible to critical in-hospital course. Marginal odds ratios were estimated for cardiac complications of takotsubo syndrome across trigger groups using generalized estimating equations. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models were fit to analyze the association between prespecified variables for short-term recovery of wall motion and systolic abnormalities as well as critical in-hospital course. Acute neurologic emergencies (47.5%) and common physical triggers (37.9%) were associated with higher risk of cardiac complications in takotsubo syndrome compared to emotional triggers (12.5%). Nonapical forms of takotsubo syndrome showed improved recovery of wall motion abnormalities (OR 2.70, 95% CI 1.34-5.45), while older patients had worse recovery of systolic function to discharge (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.93). Conversely, younger male patients in which disease was triggered by neurologic emergencies or physical triggers presented with higher odds of critical in-hospital course.
CONCLUSION: Results of this study challenge the assumption of uniform reversibility of cardiac dysfunction and emphasize the need for early risk stratification and awareness of high-risk features as well as varying clinical presentations.

Title: Association of lipoprotein(a) with ischemia-reperfusion injury in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia adversely affects ischemia-reperfusion injury in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is an independent cardiovascular risk factor beyond traditional lipid markers; however, its impact on ischemic myocardial injury remains unclear. We therefore investigated the association of Lp(a) with myocardial and microvascular damage assessed by multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), as well as clinical outcomes in STEMI patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective MARINA-STEMI (NCT04113356) cohort study, 518 STEMI patients (median age 59 years, 19% female) treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were included. Lp(a) and lipid parameters, including low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, were measured at hospital admission. CMR was performed at a median of 4 days (interquartile range (IQR) 3-5) and 4 months (IQR 4-5) after PCI. The primary objective was to assess the association of Lp(a) with infarct size (IS) and severe microvascular injury, defined as intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) on baseline CMR. The clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: all-cause death, re-infarction, or new congestive heart failure). Median Lp(a) and LDL cholesterol levels were 27 nmol/l (IQR 20-90) and 141 mg/dl (IQR 117-166), respectively. LDL cholesterol correlated with IS at baseline (ρ = 0.114, p = 0.010) and was higher in patients with IMH (145 vs. 140 mg/dl, p = 0.031). In contrast, Lp(a) showed no correlation with IS (ρ = 0.051, p = 0.246) and no association with IMH (25 vs. 28 nmol/l, p = 0.632). Elevated Lp(a) (≥ 105 nmol/l) was not associated with MACE (8.7% vs. 8.8%, p = 0.966).
CONCLUSIONS: While LDL cholesterol was significantly associated with IS and IMH, Lp(a) was not related to ischemia-reperfusion injury patterns or clinical outcomes in patients with STEMI treated with primary PCI.

Title: Autonomic dysfunction in patients with Huntington's disease: Evidence from standardized cardiovascular reflex testing.
Abstract: BackgroundAutonomic dysfunction has been reported in Huntington's disease (HD), but its extent and mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate autonomic function using standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests (CRTs) in a cohort of genetically confirmed HD patients.MethodsIn this single-center, cross-sectional study, we assessed 16 patients with manifest HD using head-up tilt test (HUTT), Valsalva maneuver (VM), deep breathing test, cold face test, and handgrip test, all performed under continuous blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) monitoring. Age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HC) were included for comparison.ResultsBased on medical history, 56% of HD patients reported symptoms of orthostatic intolerance while standing. During HUTT, they showed a significant reduction in ΔBP. BP overshoot during VM was also significantly reduced. HR responses and BP changes did not differ significantly between groups across all other maneuvers. When stratified by disease stage, parasympathetic indices were lower in later-stage patients.ConclusionsHD patients exhibited subclinical adrenergic abnormalities on CRTs, with initially preserved cardiovagal control, a pattern compatible with central autonomic involvement and possible progressive impairment of both sympathetic and parasympathetic systems over time.

Title: Clinical characteristics, risk factors, and outcomes of pediatric thrombosis: a prospective single-center study.
Journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
Abstract: The incidence of pediatric thrombosis is increasing due to multiple causes and risk factors, including genetic and acquired factors. This study aimed to evaluate clinical characteristics, risk factors, genetic mutations, and clinical outcomes of children with thrombosis. This prospective observational study included 40 children with thrombotic events. Detailed demographic, clinical, laboratory, and imaging data, as well as clinical outcomes, were collected. Thrombophilia gene testing included MTHFR C677T and A1298C, Factor XIII V34L, and factor V Leiden mutations. Statistical analyses included univariate comparisons and multivariate logistic regression to identify predictors of poor outcomes. Twenty percentage of the study population had genetic thrombophilia, while 80% had acquired risk factors. Acquired risk factors mainly included hematological (22.5%) and cardiac disorders (20%). Venous thrombosis was the most common site (80%), followed by arterial (10%) and cardiac (10%) thrombi. MTHFR C677T and factor XIII V34L mutations were detected with genetic thrombophilia only (P < 0.01), while factor V Leiden was present in both groups (P = 0.11). Overall, 67.5% of patients improved, 20% died, and 12.5% developed permanent disabilities. Multivariate analysis identified thrombocytopenia as an independent predictor of poor outcomes [odds ratio (OR) 18.44; 95% CI: 1.76-192.49; P = 0.02]. Positive blood cultures were associated with a fourfold increased risk of adverse outcomes (OR 4.0; 95% CI: 0.75-21.23; P = 0.1). Pediatric thrombosis was predominantly caused by acquired risk factors, though genetic mutations were significantly evident in this study. Screening and early diagnosis are essential for high-risk profiles. Identifying and managing sepsis and thrombocytopenia are critical to improving outcomes.

Title: Amlodipine and Nifedipine Associations with B-Type Natriuretic Peptide in Women with Hypertension and Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) are frequently prescribed to manage hypertension in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). However, whether individual dihydropyridine agents exert uniform class effects on myocardial wall stress remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study analyzed 465 consecutive patients with hypertension and HFpEF (354 women and 111 men) evaluated at Kumamoto Kinoh Hospital between May 2012 and July 2018. Multivariable linear regression models assessed associations between individual dihydropyridine CCBs (amlodipine vs. nifedipine) and plasma log-transformed B-type natriuretic peptide (lnBNP) levels.
RESULTS: In multiple imputation models among women, adjusted differences in lnBNP relative to no-CCB were 0.236 (95% CI, 0.031 to 0.441) for nifedipine and -0.118 (95% CI, -0.273 to 0.037) for amlodipine. Direct linear contrasts in women confirmed lower lnBNP levels with amlodipine than with nifedipine (adjusted difference, -0.355; 95% CI, -0.562 to - 0.147). In men, the corresponding amlodipine-versus-nifedipine difference was -0.051 (95% CI, -0.697 to 0.595; P=0.876). The formal sex-by-drug interaction contrast in complete-case analysis yielded an adjusted difference of - 0.424 (95% CI, -1.055 to 0.208; P = 0.188), with male precision constrained by sample size (7 male nifedipine users).
CONCLUSION: In women with hypertension and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, amlodipine use was associated with lower adjusted ln(BNP) levels than nifedipine use. These observational findings challenge the assumption of an interchangeable dihydropyridine class effect on myocardial wall stress, suggesting that individual pharmacological profiles-rather than uniform class-level equivalence-warrant attention in clinical evaluations.

Title: Prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in rural India: a cross-sectional study in the APCAPS cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia poses a growing public health challenge in India. Despite this, epidemiological data on the condition remain largely restricted to adults >60 years of age, despite the convergence of urbanisation-driven cardiometabolic risks and socioeconomic disadvantage in rural India potentially accelerating dementia onset. We investigated the prevalence and determinants of probable dementia in a transitional rural Indian cohort of adults aged ≥45 years.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we utilised data from the Andhra Pradesh Children and Parents Study cohort from 29 villages near Hyderabad, South India (2021-2023). We collected sociodemographic, occupational, and household asset data through face-to-face, questionnaire-based interviews. Cardiometabolic diseases (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and stroke) were assessed using validated methods. Dementia screening was performed using the Brief Community Screening Instrument for Dementia. We calculated prevalence estimates for dementia and used multivariable logistic regression to identify independent associations of probable dementia with sociodemographic, socioeconomic (education, occupation, household assets), and cardiometabolic factors (diabetes, hypertension, cardiac disease, and stroke).
RESULTS: The final sample included 2,163 adults aged ≥45 years. The prevalence of probable dementia (a positive screen on the BCSI-D) was 3.4% (95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.6-4.6) in the 45-59 age group and 7.4% (95% CI = 6.0-9.4) in the ≥60 age group. In the multivariable model, the odds of probable dementia were 2.2 times higher among unemployed or retired participants than among those working in agriculture or animal rearing (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 2.23; 95% CI = 1.26-3.95). The odds of probable dementia among literate participants were 0.5 times those among illiterate participants (aOR = 0.54; 95% CI = 0.31-0.89). The odds of probable dementia were 3.8 times higher among participants with a history of stroke than among those without (aOR = 3.77; 95% CI = 1.67-7.94).
CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that the burden of probable dementia in rural India extends into middle age, and that the condition itself is independently associated with a history of stroke and socioeconomic disadvantages. This suggests a need to extend cognitive and vascular risk assessment to adults aged ≥45 years in rural India. However, as all findings reflect positive screening results rather than confirmed diagnoses, longitudinal studies with diagnostic confirmation are needed before population-level screening recommendations can be made.

Title: Large-scale plasma proteomic profiling enhances prediction of heart failure among hypertensive individuals: prospective insights from the UK Biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for heart failure (HF), but current clinical models have limited ability to identify high-risk individuals before overt disease. Plasma proteomics may capture early molecular changes and improve risk prediction.
METHODS: We analysed 16,128 hypertensive UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants without baseline HF. Plasma levels of 2,911 proteins were measured using the Olink Explore platform. Participants were randomly split 1:1 into training and validation sets. HF-associated proteins were identified using Cox models in the training set, followed by LASSO regression to construct a protein risk score (PRS). Model performance was assessed in the validation set using Harrell's C-index, time-dependent ROC analysis, Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI), Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI), calibration, and bootstrap validation. A parsimonious panel was derived using LightGBM and sequential forward feature selection.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.1 years, 1,074 participants developed HF. In the training set, 534 proteins were associated with HF after adjustment for demographic and clinical risk factors and were enriched in cytokine signalling, extracellular matrix organisation, and immune-cell migration pathways. The 101-protein PRS was independently associated with incident HF. In the validation set, adding the PRS increased the C-index from 0.670 to 0.786 beyond age and sex, and from 0.727 to 0.787 beyond the Pooled Cohort Equations to Prevent Heart Failure (PCP-HF) model, with improved reclassification and discrimination. PRS levels were elevated years before HF diagnosis. A six-protein panel comprising NT-proBNP, GDF15, BCAN, WFDC2, CTHRC1, and CNTN5 achieved an AUC of 0.775, outperforming NT-proBNP alone.
CONCLUSIONS: Plasma proteomic profiling improves HF risk prediction among hypertensive individuals beyond conventional clinical factors and may support earlier risk stratification and precision prevention.

Title: Coronary Artery Calcium Screening: A Narrative Review and Guide to Preventive Strategies.
Abstract: Coronary Artery Calcium (CAC) scoring has become a central tool for detecting subclinical atherosclerosis and refining cardiovascular risk assessment, particularly in individuals with intermediate or atypical risk profiles. Traditional risk models such as the ASCVD Pooled Cohort Equations remain foundational but have important limitations, especially in younger adults and those with nontraditional risk patterns. CAC scoring provides direct visualization of atherosclerotic burden and can outperform serum biomarkers in predicting cardiovascular events. Recent cohort data suggest that CAC can be detected decades earlier than current guideline thresholds imply, and that early CAC presence and progression carry significant prognostic value, although evidence to support routine screening below current guideline-recommended age thresholds remains investigational rather than established practice. With advances in imaging technology and expanding population-based evidence, CAC scoring is evolving from a decision aid into an increasingly central tool in preventive cardiology, one whose benefits must be weighed against radiation exposure, incidental findings, overdiagnosis, and cost. This review summarizes current evidence on the biology of coronary calcification, available imaging techniques, CAC scoring systems, and the clinical application and limitations of CAC in primary prevention of cardiovascular diseases and situates guideline-endorsed uses of CAC alongside areas that remain hypothesis-generating.

Title: Cost-effectiveness of Empagliflozin in Chronic Heart Failure: A Markov Model-based Analysis in Uzbekistan.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic Heart Failure (CHF) is a major public health challenge associated with high morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Empagliflozin has demonstrated clinical benefits across the spectrum of heart failure; however, evidence on its economic value in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of adding empagliflozin to standard therapy for patients with chronic heart failure from the perspective of the healthcare payer.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cohort-based Markov model with a 3-month cycle length and a 20- year time horizon was developed to simulate disease progression in CHF. Health states included no complications, cardiovascular complications, renal complications, and death. Outcomes were measured in Life Years (LYs), Quality-Adjusted Life Years (QALYs), total costs, and Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratios (ICERs). Both deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: Quality-adjusted life expectancy increased from 11.595 to 12.224 QALYs. Total discounted costs were 48,133,588 UZS for empagliflozin versus 43,261,361 UZS for standard therapy. The Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) was 7,738,951 UZS per QALY gained, which was substantially below the national willingness-to-pay threshold of 141.6 million UZS.
DISCUSSIONS: Since the ICER for empagliflozin compared with placebo is substantially lower than the calculated willingness-to-pay threshold, empagliflozin can be considered a costeffective treatment option.
CONCLUSIONS: Adding empagliflozin to standard therapy for CHF is a cost-effective intervention in the Republic of Uzbekistan and provides meaningful clinical and economic benefits.

Title: Mechanistic Evaluation of Psilocybin in Neurodegenerative Disorders: Relevance of 5-HT2A Receptors and Downstream Pathways.
Abstract: More than fifty million individuals worldwide are experiencing neurodegenerative disorders, which include Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, multiple sclerosis, and frontotemporal dementia. These disorders have a significant role in the gradual degradation of cognition and motor skills. Most current treatment approaches have little effect on changing the course of the disease and are largely symptomatic. Psilocybin, a naturally occurring tryptamine alkaloid from psilocybin mushrooms, has become a promising medicinal agent because of its hallucinogenic, neuroprotective, and neuroplastic properties. After being metabolically transformed into its active form, psilocin, it primarily activates serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. This modulates glutamatergic neurotransmission and neurotrophic signaling pathways such as BDNF/TrkB and mTOR, which regulate synaptic remodeling, dendritic complexity, neurogenesis, neuroinflammatory response, and default mode network connectivity, all of which are linked to depression and dementia. Preclinical research studies demonstrate that psilocybin increases hippocampal plasticity, restores dendritic complexity, lowers proinflammatory cytokine levels, and promotes fear extinction in experimental models of stress, ischemic stroke, and neurodegeneration. Emerging clinical studies also indicate that individuals with moderate cognitive impairment, early-onset Alzheimer's disease, and Parkinson's disease may see long-term decreases in anxiety and depression as well as improvements in cognitive function, frequently after a single dose administration. Additionally, psilocybin has demonstrated promise in treating mental comorbidities that often accompany neurodegenerative illness, such as treatment-resistant depression, drug use disorders, and obsessive-compulsive disorder. However, there are still significant obstacles to overcome, such as optimizing dosing schedules, assessing safety issues such as temporary perceptual abnormalities and cardiovascular consequences, and translating preclinical results into extensive phase -III clinical studies. This review incorporates the most recent data on psilocybin's chemistry, pharmacology, metabolism, and mechanistic actions; it highlights the drug's therapeutic potential across a variety of neurodegenerative diseases and emphasizes the necessity of carefully planned randomized controlled trials to determine clinical efficacy, long-term safety, and its place in multimodal treatment approaches.

Title: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
Abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice-including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care-are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.

Title: Intravascular imaging improves outcomes in left main PCI: insights from acute and chronic presentations.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an established revascularization strategy for selected patients with left main coronary artery (LMCA) disease. However, data regarding outcomes in unselected real-world populations and the impact of intravascular imaging remain limited. We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes following LMCA PCI according to clinical presentation and to assess the prognostic impact of intravascular imaging guidance.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-centre study including consecutive patients undergoing LMCA PCI between 2019 and 2022. Patients were classified as having chronic (CCS) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) were assessed during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression and stabilised inverse probability of treatment weighting (SIPTW) analyses were performed.
RESULTS: A total of 107 patients were included (19 CCS and 88 ACS; mean age 68.6 ± 11.3 years; 80.4% male). During a mean follow-up of 1121 ± 574 days, ACS patients experienced higher rates of MACCE (40.9% vs. 15.8%; p = 0.039) and all-cause mortality (29.5% vs. 5.3%; p = 0.027) compared with CCS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with a significantly lower risk of MACCE in multivariable analysis (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.75; p = 0.009). In a SIPTW-adjusted analysis, the association remained directionally favourable, although statistical significance was not maintained (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.26-1.29; p = 0.178).
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical presentation significantly influences outcomes after LMCA PCI, with worse long-term prognosis among ACS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with lower rates of MACCE and remained directionally favourable after weighting analyses, supporting its role in optimising LMCA interventions.

Title: Life-Course Blood Pressure Trajectories and Focal Myocardial Fibrosis in Older Age in MyoFit46.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of life-course blood pressure (BP) trajectories on later-life focal left ventricular (LV) fibrosis by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) remains elusive.
METHODS: MyoFit46 prospectively recruited ≈500 participants from a 1946 birth cohort for a cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan at 77 years, assessing LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method or 5-SD method. Systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP were recorded at 36, 43, 53, 63, 69, and 77 years. For each participant, annual rates of BP change (steepness) and area under the BP trajectory (cumulative burden) for each age interval were calculated using mixed-effects models. Associations between life-course BPs and LGE were tested using generalized linear models, adjusted for antihypertensives, demographics, lifestyle, and comorbidities. Time-to-event associations between LGE and incident major adverse cardiovascular event (hospitalizations for coronary artery disease, stroke, heart failure, and atrial/ventricular arrhythmias; n=29) were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 472 participants (54% male), each 10 mm Hg greater individual SBPs at 36 to 69 years were associated with 6% to 11% greater LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method (all P≤0.033), whereas each 10 mm Hg sustained greater SBPs on any age interval from 36 to 69 associated with 16% to 24% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77(all P≤0.005), independent of SBP at 77 years. Each 1 mm Hg/y steeper SBP rise during age intervals 36 to 43, 43 to 53, and 53 to 63 was associated with 6% to 12% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77 years. LGE presence was associated with greater major adverse cardiovascular event rates (hazard ratio, 2.5 [95% CI, 1.2-5.2]).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher life-course BPs, cumulative burden, and steeper increases were associated with greater older-age LV LGE, which was linked to incident major adverse cardiovascular events. BP trajectories, beyond single-point BP measurements, warrant further investigation as tools to guide BP management strategies.

Title: Pyrophosphatase 2 Deficiency: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis and Management.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: PPA2 (pyrophosphatase 2) deficiency is a relatively newly recognized condition caused by biallelic variants in the PPA2 gene. The gene encodes the mitochondrial enzyme PPA2, involved in the production of orthophosphate in the mitochondrial matrix. Affected individuals typically present with sudden cardiac death or acute heart failure following common viral illnesses in infants and toddlers, or following exposure to small amounts of alcohol as teenagers. The condition has a high mortality rate in these situations. Here, we explore the clinical presentations and current management of these patients with a view to guiding future emergency clinical management of cases.
METHODS: Case records from published and unpublished affected individuals diagnosed with PPA2 deficiency were compiled in a retrospective cohort study of genotypes, phenotypes and clinical management protocols in individuals with biallelic (likely) pathogenic PPA2 variants.
RESULTS: We collated 93 affected individuals from 53 families, 14 of which have not previously been reported. Patient presentation is invariably acute, often associated with fatigue, vomiting, seizures and collapse. Generally, presenting individuals received standard emergency management with cardiopulmonary resuscitation and appropriate management of arrhythmia, and here we present compiled clinical management protocols for emergency and ongoing treatment of PPA2-deficient patients. A pronounced inheritance rate of pathogenic alleles from carrier parents is noted, and further research is warranted to confirm and investigate any selective advantage for gametes carrying pathogenic PPA2 variants.
CONCLUSIONS: PPA2 deficiency has a high mortality rate following exposure to common childhood viruses in children around and under the age of 3 and in teenagers exposed to ethanol. We have presented current therapeutic approaches gathered from a worldwide survey of clinicians treating their patients, possible pathogenic mechanisms and inheritance peculiarities of the condition and provide a comprehensive review of the current recommendations surrounding patients' clinical management.

Title: Standardization of Collected Biobank Data to Facilitate Cardiovascular Research: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease has been the focus of extensive biomedical research, yet it remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. One recent approach to support scientific discovery has been the development of large-scale population-based prospective studies that couple phenotypic data, including outcomes, to collection and analysis of biological samples. Large, data-dense biobanks, particularly those linked to electronic health records (including laboratory, electrocardiographic, imaging, and therapeutic data) and genomic data, have demonstrated value for interdisciplinary research into the epidemiology, cause, treatment, and prevention of disease and yield increasingly refined insights into monogenic and complex traits. One limitation to wider use of these resources is that they may collect phenotypic and biological data in a nonuniform fashion, limiting data harmonization, analysis, and validation. The purpose of this scientific statement is to discuss the current state of available biobanks, endorse biobanks for discovery and implementation science, and propose opportunities for future harmonization to increase the potential for novel studies aimed at understanding mechanisms and developing novel therapies for cardiovascular disease treatment and prevention.

Title: Racial Disparities in Longitudinal Functional Outcome After Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The burden of stroke is unequally distributed in the United States, with Black individuals experiencing more incident stroke. It remains unclear whether Black individuals also experience worse stroke recovery. We sought to study disparities in longitudinal functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke in a population-based study.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study in the Greater Cincinnati Northern Kentucky region over an 18-month period (July 2019 to December 2020). All acute ischemic stroke events were captured. The modified Rankin Scale scores were determined at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months for patients who survived the index event. We studied the association between Black race and longitudinal modified Rankin Scale (across all time points) with mixed-effects ordinal regression, initially adjusting for age, sex, and time since stroke. Hierarchical regression was used to sequentially adjust for stroke severity and management, premorbid health, and social determinants.
RESULTS: Among 2796 patients with acute ischemic stroke (mean age, 69.0; 31% Black; 52% female), 2537 survived and were included (mean age, 68.4; 32% Black; 52% female). Black race was associated with a worse longitudinal modified Rankin Scale score (cOR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.89-3.60]). Excluding patients with recurrent events did not change this association (cOR, 2.69 [95% CI, 1.92-3.78]). Adding variables reflecting initial stroke severity and management partly attenuated the association (cOR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.43-2.60]). Adding variables reflecting premorbid health further attenuated the association (cOR decreased to 1.43 [95% CI, 1.09-1.87]). The remaining association between Black race and the modified Rankin Scale score was fully attenuated by social determinants, with cOR, 1.09 (95% CI, 0.80-1.47). There was no interaction between race and time since stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: Starting at discharge and persisting out to 12 months, acute ischemic stroke functional outcomes are worse among Black individuals. These disparities are significantly attenuated by clinical factors and social determinants; future studies should explore whether the social determinants can be intervened upon in the recovery period.

Title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED.
METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days.
RESULTS: Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54).
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

Title: Multidimensional Echocardiographic Parameters Predict Left Ventricular Functional Recovery After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
Abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of preoperative and early postoperative echocardiographic parameters for left ventricular function recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and to evaluate the relationship between functional recovery and 1-year clinical prognosis.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 214 patients undergoing first-time elective CABG at The First Affiliated Hospital of Yangtze University between January 2022 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, 3-7 days postoperatively, and at 6 months to evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial volume index (LAVI), and ratio of early mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e'). Based on 6‑month LVEF change, patients were divided into recovery (ΔLVEF ≥5%) and non‑recovery (ΔLVEF <5%) groups. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors, and the corresponding models were established and validated. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were recorded at 1‑year follow‑up.
RESULTS: Of the 214 patients enrolled in the study, functional recovery of the left ventricle was observed in 128 individuals, corresponding to 59.8% of the cohort. Multivariate analysis identified several preoperative and procedural variables as independent predictors of functional recovery, including left atrial volume index (LAVI), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD), left atrial diameter (LAD), Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score, and the number of graft vessels. Age, preoperative LVEF, and e' velocity were independently associated with lower odds of functional recovery. Global longitudinal strain (GLS) and diabetes history showed no independent predictive value. The clinical-echocardiographic combined model demonstrated excellent discrimination and showed higher discriminative performance than the basic clinical model and conventional echocardiographic model. Subgroup analysis revealed that GLS showed no independent predictive value across all LVEF subgroups (p > 0.05), whereas LAVI and LAD were significant predictors in patients with LVEF ≥40% (including the 40%-49% subgroup), but showed no predictive relevance in those with LVEF <40%. Early postoperative ΔLVEF predicted 6-month functional recovery with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.846. After one year of follow‑up, the recovery group exhibited a markedly lower rate of MACE than the non‑recovery group, with left ventricular functional recovery serving as an independent protective factor against MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative structural parameters, including LAVI, LVEDD, LVESD, and LAD, are independent imaging biomarkers for predicting left ventricular functional recovery after CABG. GLS and E/e' ratio show no independent predictive value in this study. The integrated model combining clinical factors with multi-dimensional echocardiographic parameters demonstrates excellent discriminative ability. Early postoperative LVEF improvement strongly predicts 6-month functional recovery, while postoperative recovery of left ventricular function is associated with a significantly lower 1-year MACE risk.

Title: Long-term outcomes in adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot: a single-centre retrospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot represent a growing clinical population at risk for long-term cardiovascular complications. Characterising their postoperative course and late outcomes is essential to guide surveillance and management.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical characteristics and long-term outcomes of adult patients (≥18 years) with repaired tetralogy of Fallot who received care at a quaternary-care institution between January 2000 and December 2024.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study. Adult patients with a diagnosis of repaired tetralogy of Fallot who had undergone complete surgical repair either during the study period or before it were included. Clinical and sociodemographic data were obtained.Variables related to prior palliative procedures, type of surgical repair, reinterventions (surgical or catheter-based), and long-term outcomes were analysed.
RESULTS: A total of 56 patients were included; 31 (55.4%) were women. The median duration of follow-up after repair was 23 years; twenty patients (35.7%) had undergone a palliative or prior intervention before complete repair. The most common type of outflow tract reconstruction was a transannular patch (37.5%), followed by homograft implantation (25.0%). Reinterventions occurred in 29 patients (51.8%), most commonly pulmonary valve replacement (23 patients, 41.0%), mainly due to progressive pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular dilation. Arrhythmic complications included premature ventricular contractions in 35.7% of patients. Long-term mortality was 3.6%.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot demonstrate high long-term survival; however, late complications are common and frequently require surgical or catheter-based reintervention. These findings underscore the need for lifelong specialised follow-up in adult CHD programmes.

Title: Dynamic change in soluble suppressor of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) during acute decompensated heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction, and its mortality implications.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) concentrations measured at clinician-determined decompensation and recompensation, and their change between these states, with one-year mortality in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF).
METHODS: Paired sST2 samples were obtained at decompensation and recompensation from 168 patients hospitalized with ADHF and a left ventricular ejection fraction of <50%. Associations with one-year all-cause mortality were assessed using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis. Discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, with exploratory cut-offs derived using Youden's index.
RESULTS: The median age was 71.5 years (IQR 62-80.8), 39 (23.2%) were women, median LVEF was 26% (IQR 17.5-32.5), and 158 (94.1%) had NYHA class III or IV symptoms. During one-year follow-up, 34 patients (20.2%) died. Each doubling of decompensation sST2 was associated with higher mortality after adjustment for creatinine (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.23-2.25). Recompensation sST2 remained associated with mortality after adjustment for creatinine and NT-proBNP (HR per doubling 1.71, 95% CI 1.18-2.48). The respective areas under the curve were 0.686 and 0.688, with exploratory cut-offs of 66.5 and 57 ng/mL. Unchanged or increased sST2 was associated with higher mortality than decreased sST2 in unadjusted analysis (HR 2.76, 95% CI 1.37-5.59, p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: Elevated sST2 at decompensation and unchanged or increased concentrations during recompensation were associated with one-year mortality in patients with ADHF. These findings support further evaluation of sST2 as an adjunctive prognostic biomarker in this setting; the cohort-derived cut-offs require validation.

Title: Real-world impact of coronary artery calcium scoring on primary prevention management in a community cardiology practice.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring on lipid-lowering therapy intensification, aspirin initiation, and downstream cardiac testing in primary prevention patients in a community cardiology setting.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
SETTING: Single community cardiology practice.
PARTICIPANTS: Four hundred consecutive patients undergoing CAC scoring in 2022.
INTERVENTIONS: CAC scoring used for risk stratification and clinical decision-making.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Changes in lipid-lowering therapy, aspirin initiation, and downstream cardiac testing across CAC categories (0, 1-99, 100-399, ≥400); risk reclassification using Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) and Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) risk scores.
RESULTS: Among 400 patients (mean age 60.2 ± 10.6 years; 46.5% male), 30% had CAC = 0, 37% CAC 1-99, 18% CAC 100-399, and 16% CAC ≥400. Lipid therapy modification increased across categories (7.7%, 33.3%, 69.0%, 81.7%; p < 0.001), as did aspirin initiation among aspirin-naive patients (1.0%, 8.0%, 51.9%, 52.5%; p < 0.001) and stress testing (2.7%, 6.5%, 29.0%, 68.6%; p < 0.001). Each one-category CAC increment was independently associated with lipid therapy modification (adjusted OR 4.36, 95% CI 3.13-6.06), aspirin initiation (OR 4.48, 95% CI 2.85-7.03), and stress testing (OR 5.11, 95% CI 3.33-7.84; all p < 0.001). CAC changed MESA risk category in 192/348 patients (55.2%): 87 upward and 105 downward.
CONCLUSIONS: CAC burden was independently associated with graded intensification of lipid-lowering therapy, aspirin initiation, and downstream testing after multivariable adjustment, extending prior descriptive literature with persistent, quantified associations in real-world community practice. Improvement in clinical outcomes cannot be assessed from this retrospective, six-month implementation study.

Title: Epimeric Vitamin D is Not Associated With Arterial Stiffness or Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Advanced CKD.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: 3-epi-25(OH)D3, an epimeric form of 25(OH)D3 generated by C-3 epimerization, declines with advancing chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its role in vascular health and related outcomes remains largely unknown. We aimed to determine whether circulating 3-epi-25(OH)D3 levels are associated with arterial stiffness and longitudinal cardiovascular (CV) outcomes in advanced CKD (stages 5 and 5D).
STUDY DESIGN: A prospective observational study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: A total of 270 patients with advanced CKD using the Cambridge Coventry Vascular cohort.
EXPOSURE S OR PREDICTOR S: Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D3 measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.
OUTCOME S: Arterial stiffness was assessed by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV) and augmentation index (AIx75). Longitudinal outcomes included a composite of major CV events and all-cause mortality.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D3 was categorized into quartiles. Associations were assessed using multivariable regression adjusted for age, race, and dialysis status. Kaplan-Meier and Cox models assessed longitudinal outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 270 participants, quartiles were Q1 < 0.30 ng/mL (n = 64), Q2: 0.30-0.456 ng/mL (n = 71), Q3: 0.457-0.729 ng/mL (n = 68), and Q4 ≥ 0.73 ng/mL (n = 67). Strata were similar in age (44.9 years), sex, and BMI (all P > 0.05). Race differed by quartile (P < 0.001); 87.4% were White. 24.8% were pre-dialytic, 61.1% treated with hemodialysis, and 14.1% treated with peritoneal dialysis. Arterial stiffness was similar across quartiles (AIx75 ∼20-21%, P = 0.99; PWV: 7.8-8.0 m/s, P = 0.94). 3-epi-25(OH)D3 showed no association with AIx75 or PWV before or after adjustment using multiple regression modeling. Over 9.3 years, 115 composite events occurred (97 CV events, 18 deaths). Kaplan-Meier analysis did not discriminate risk across 3-epi-25(OH)D3 quartiles for the composite outcome (log-rank P = 0.23), and adjusted Cox models showed no association.
LIMITATIONS: Observational design with possible residual confounding.
CONCLUSION: In advanced CKD, 3-epi-25(OH)D3 showed no independent association with arterial stiffness or CV events and mortality. Further studies are needed to determine the role of epimeric vitamin D in patients with CKD.

Title: Acute and Chronic Resistance Training Differentially Modulate Myocardial Angiogenesis-Related Gene Expression in Wistar Rats.
Abstract: Myocardial angiogenesis contributes to the maintenance of myocardial perfusion and cardiac function. Resistance training (RT) induces cardiovascular adaptations, but the myocardial transcriptional responses to acute RT (ART) and chronic RT (CRT) remain incompletely understood. This study compared the expression of angiogenesis- and metabolic adaptation-related genes in the left ventricle following a single RT bout and 8 weeks of repeated RT in healthy male Wistar rats. Twenty-four rats were randomized to three groups: sedentary control (CON) (n = 8), ART (one ladder-climbing session), or CRT (ladder-climbing 5 days/week for 8 weeks). RT was performed on a 1-m ladder inclined at 80° using progressive loads attached to the tail. Left-ventricular tissue was collected 1 h after the exercise bout in ART and 1 h after the final training session in CRT. Compared to CON, ART showed significantly higher HIF-1α and FSTL1 expression, whereas PGC-1α and VEGF did not differ significantly. CRT also showed significantly higher HIF-1α and FSTL1 expression than CON, together with significantly higher PGC-1α and VEGF expression. No significant differences were observed between ART and CRT for any of the genes examined. These findings demonstrate distinct myocardial transcriptional profiles following ART versus CRT, characterized by an HIF-1α- and FSTL1-associated response after a single bout and a PGC-1α- and VEGF-associated response following CRT.

Title: Prehospital predictors of clinical outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity: a JCS-ReSS report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with pulseless electrical activity (PEA) has a poor prognosis and is aetiologically heterogeneous. We aimed to identify prehospital predictors of a favourable outcome, overall and by presumed aetiology.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study analysed 442,630 adults with OHCA and an initial rhythm of PEA from the All-Japan Utstein Registry between 2005 and 2024. The primary outcome was a favourable neurological outcome at 1 month. Two models were fitted, at the scene and at hospital arrival, each also within each aetiology. Epinephrine and advanced airway management (AAM) were assessed by time-dependent propensity score sequential matching.
RESULTS: At the scene, a witnessed arrest (risk ratio [RR], 1.65) predicted a favourable neurological outcome, and a longer response time predicted a worse one (RR, 0.66; 10 versus 5 min). The gradient with age was steeper in cardiac than non-cardiac PEA (RR, 0.38 versus 0.78). At hospital arrival, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (RR, 23.31) was the strongest predictor, but conversion to a shockable rhythm predicted a favourable outcome only in cardiac PEA and a worse outcome in non-cardiac PEA (RR, 1.37 versus 0.73). Standardised to a common covariate distribution, 1-month survival was higher in non-cardiac PEA, whereas a favourable neurological outcome was more likely in cardiac PEA. After time-dependent adjustment, the apparent harm from epinephrine and AAM was attenuated.
CONCLUSIONS: Prehospital information available before hospital arrival predicted a favourable neurological outcome, but its prognostic meaning depended on the presumed aetiology. These independent prehospital predictors could inform future risk stratification.

Title: Comment on "Real-world long-term outcomes of clopidogrel-based dual antiplatelet therapy post-drug-eluting stent implantation in all comers patients: A retrospective evaluation".
