Title: The effect of time-varying left ventricular ejection fraction on clinical outcome in critically ill COVID-19 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and acute cor pulmonale are associated with adverse outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19, the prognostic significance of left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction remains insufficiently characterized. In particular, dynamic changes in cardiac function during intensive care has seldom been studied. We therefore investigated the association between time-varying LV systolic function, assessed by LV ejection fraction (LVEF) and intensive care unit (ICU) mortality in patients with COVID-19, taking into account right ventricular function and forward flow.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study combined three ICU data repositories comprising 808 patients with 1614 echocardiographic examinations. Time-varying LV systolic function (LVEF ≤ 50%, 51-70%, >70%) was the primary exposure, and ICU mortality was the outcome. Multivariable Cox models with time-varying covariates, including, acute cor pulmonale, left ventricular outflow tract velocity time integral and key clinical characteristics were used to assess associations between LV systolic function phenotypes and outcome.
RESULTS: At baseline, 27% of patients had abnormal LV systolic function (LVEF ≤ 50%) and 17% had hyperdynamic LV function (LVEF > 70%). The proportion of patients with normal LV systolic function increased over time. Abnormal LV systolic function was most prevalent at the first echocardiographic examination (27%) and least prevalent at the fifth examination (17%), whereas hyperdynamic LV function became more frequent during ICU stay, peaking at the 4th echocardiographic examination. Abnormal (aHR; 1.174, 95% CI: 0.901-1.531) or hyperdynamic (aHR: 1.041, 95% CI: 0.785-1.379) LV systolic dysfunction was not independently associated with ICU mortality.
CONCLUSION: In critically ill patients with COVID-19, LV systolic dysfunction, including both abnormal and hyperdynamic LV phenotypes, were common and dynamic during ICU stay. LV systolic dysfunction was not independently associated with ICU mortality when modelled longitudinally and adjusted for RV dysfunction, forward flow and other clinical covariates. These findings suggest that the prognostic value LVEF phenotypes in severe COVID-19 may be limited. Further studies incorporating more sensitive measures of LV function and biomarkers of myocardial injury may be required to delineate subtle changes not captured by LVEF.

Title: Timing of Cardiac Rehabilitation After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a cornerstone of post-acute care for patients experiencing cardiovascular events or interventions. It aims to improve cardiorespiratory capacity, enhance quality of life, and maximize physical function, facilitating a return to daily activities. However, the optimal timing for initiating CR following acute coronary events or procedures remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, 40 patients diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction and treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were randomly assigned to two groups. Group A commenced cardiac rehabilitation one month after PCI, while Group B initiated rehabilitation two months post-PCI. Both groups completed a supervised 12-session rehabilitation program under the guidance of a physical medicine specialist. Functional outcomes were assessed before and after rehabilitation using the SF-36 quality of life questionnaire and echocardiographic parameters. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25. Within-group changes were evaluated with paired t-tests, and between-group comparisons of change scores were conducted using independent samples t-tests. A P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Post-rehabilitation, the mean SF-36 score was 65.85±6.67 in Group A and 67.05±5.96 in Group B (P=0.192). The mean change in Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) was 2.25% in Group A and 0.15% in Group B (P=0.305). After rehabilitation, grade 1-2 diastolic dysfunction remained present in 85% of patients in both groups, while 15% of patients in each group showed no evidence of diastolic dysfunction (P=0.506).No significant differences were found between groups in heart rate (HR) Max (107.45±15.04 vs. 115.20±13.12; P=0.091), HR Recovery (22.50±7.05 vs. 23.10±7.78; P=0.800), or MET change (6.60±1.83 vs. 6.20±2.39; P=0.556).
CONCLUSION: Initiating cardiac rehabilitation one month as opposed to two months after primary PCI did not yield significant differences in quality of life or cardiac functional parameters. These findings indicate that there may be flexibility in the timing of CR initiation without compromising short-term functional outcomes.

Title: Hematological inflammatory markers as predictors of atherosclerotic progression in patients with psoriasis: A retrospective case-control study from the SH-YIMED database.
Journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health
Abstract: Chronic inflammation drives cardiovascular comorbidity in psoriasis. Clinical-only risk models have limited utility, whereas the predictive value of blood inflammatory markers for psoriatic atherosclerosis is unconfirmed. This hospital-based case-control study enrolled 636 patients with psoriasis who underwent vascular ultrasonography, and 134 matched pairs were obtained through 1:1 propensity score matching. We analyzed primary and exploratory hematological inflammatory markers, examined their links to atherosclerosis using logistic regression and supplementary stratified and nonlinear analyses, and constructed risk prediction models that were assessed by area under the curve, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (OR = 16.33, 95% confidence interval = 7.54-35.35, P < .001) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) (OR = 20.78, 95% confidence interval = 7.92-54.53, P < .001) were stronger independent predictors of atherosclerosis than C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, with significant age interactions for NLR (interaction OR = 7.45, P = .018) and SII (interaction OR = 28.03, P = .008). Models incorporating NLR (area under the curve = 0 .894, integrated discrimination improvement = 0.439, net reclassification improvement = 1.339) or SII (area under the curve = 0.891, integrated discrimination improvement = 0.413, net reclassification improvement = 1.281) exhibited favorable calibration and a higher clinical net benefit across decision curve analysis thresholds of 0.05-0.75. The combined C-reactive protein + NLR + SII model attained the highest area under the curve of 0.906. NLR and SII improved cardiovascular risk prediction for patients with psoriasis with atherosclerosis, enabling effective risk stratification.

Title: Proteomic markers associated with blood pressure, hypertension, and treatment-resistant hypertension.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to investigate associations between 92 proteins and blood pressure (BP), prevalent hypertension (HT) and apparent treatment-resistant HT (aTRH) in a population-derived sub cohort.
METHODS: Excluding subjects with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) (n = 189), linear regression models assessed associations between proteins and systolic BP. Proteins showing significant associations (false discovery rate 5%) with systolic BP were analysed adjusting for clinically relevant covariates. Associated proteins were further analysed for associations with diastolic BP, prevalent HT, and aTRH, in multivariable regression models.
RESULTS: Complete data was available in 1527 individuals (mean age 67.1 ± 6.0 years; 30.5% women). Interleukin-1 receptor type 2 (IL1R2) associated with systolic BP (β 2.79, p 0.008), diastolic BP (β 1.78, p < 0.001), HT (odds ratio (OR), 1.34 [95% CI, 1.01-1.78]) and aTRH (OR, 1.94 [1.11-3.39]) while chitinase-3-like-protein 1 (CHI3L1) associated with systolic BP (β 1.53, p 0.004) and prevalent HT (OR 1.20, [1.04-1.38]). Pathway analysis suggested "metabolism of angiotensinogen to angiotensins", "neutrophil degranulation" and "peptide hormone metabolism" as significantly enriched, in relation to blood pressure.
CONCLUSIONS: Among 1527 individuals without established ASCVD, IL1R2 was associated with systolic and diastolic blood pressure, as well as with both HT and aTRH, while CHI3L1 associated with systolic blood pressure and prevalent HT. These findings may offer novel insights and inspire future research on HT and inflammation.

Title: The Impact of Age and Physical Assessment Measures on Performance Among Non-Weightbearing Walking Aids: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Walking aids for non-weightbearing (NWB) ambulation are often arbitrarily provided with no evidence that physical assessment predicts ambulatory performance.
PURPOSE: We sought to determine if convenient physical assessment measures could guide NWB walking aid prescription and to determine how age impacts ambulatory performance.
METHODS: This prospective randomized crossover study examined 22 healthy adults, recruited from Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, and surrounding area through flyers and word of mouth. Inclusion criteria were independent unrestricted community dwellers with no self-reported neuromusculoskeletal or cardiovascular conditions who were age 18 years or older. Participants were stratified into 2 age cohorts: younger (age <50 years) and older (age ≥50 years). Physical assessment measures included triceps and latissimus dorsi strength, single lower-limb balance, and arm endurance. Performance measures included distance traversed, rate of perceived exertion, and peak stance limb plantar force (SLPF) evaluated among 4 walking conditions: unaided, NWB with crutches, standard walker, and wheeled knee walker. Two analyses were performed, one using the entire sample population and another split by age.
RESULTS: There were no differences in physical assessment measures between the younger and older cohort, yet distance traversed in the older cohort was highly dependent on all physical assessment measures when using crutches or a standard walker. Peak SLPF was reduced in the younger cohort when using the wheeled knee walker, but not in the older cohort. In the younger participants, reducing peak SLPF was highly dependent on arm endurance when using a standard walker or crutches and latissimus dorsi strength when using the wheeled knee walker. Surprisingly, older participants with stronger latissimus dorsi strength reported a higher rate of perceived exertion when using the wheeled knee walker compared to other devices.
CONCLUSION: Arm strength, single lower-limb balance, and arm endurance should be considered when prescribing walking aids in older adults, and the wheeled knee walker should be considered in younger adults in need of reduced peak SLPF.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prospective randomized comparative study.

Title: Associations of Traditional Chinese Medicine Therapy with Risks of Lower-Limb Amputation, Cardiovascular Mortality and All-Cause Mortality in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Occlusive Disease-A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This is a retrospective cohort study assessing the association between the use of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and the risk of lower-limb amputation, cardiovascular (CV) mortality, and all-cause mortality among people with peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD).
METHODS: The study utilized data from the National Health Insurance Research Database of the Ministry of Health and Welfare of Taiwan. A 1:1 propensity score matching ratio based on gender, age (5-year interval), comorbidities, medications, and year of index date.The risk of outcomes among PAOD patients with and without TCM use was estimated by a Cox proportional hazards model.
RESULTS: The study findings showed that TCM treatment was associated with a significant decreased risk of lower-limb loss (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 0.55, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.50-0.61), CV death (aHR = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.31-0.34), and all-cause mortality (aHR = 0.34, 95% CI = 0.34-0.35) among people with PAOD, especially for CV death and all-cause death.
CONCLUSION: We found that patients with PAOD treated with TCM have a decreased risk of endpoints, especially for CV death and all-cause death.

Title: Complex relationship between iron status and outcomes of STEMI: hypothesis-generating study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Iron deficiency (ID) is common amongst patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Its impact on outcomes remains contested. Previous studies reported favourable or adverse impacts depending on outcome measures, sampling timepoints, ID definition and follow-up duration. This study systematically characterises the prognostic impact of iron status on short-term, mid-term and long-term outcomes, and evaluates the effect of sampling timepoint and ID definition on these prognostic relationships.
METHODS & RESULTS: We performed an observational cohort study in patients with acute STEMI (n = 167) and no prior heart failure (HF). Iron markers were sampled at presentation, and successive timepoints thereafter. Cardiac Magnetic Resonance was performed at 2 days and 6 months. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), consisting of new-onset HF, recurrent MI or cardiac death were recorded over 4.5 years. Mechanisms were evaluated in a preclinical model of MI.ID was common at presentation, affecting between 44.9% and 67%, depending on ID definition. Tsat <20%, serum iron<13μM, or European Society of Cardiology's definition, but not ferritin<100μg/L, independently predicted lower risk of MACE. Lower Tsat at presentation predicted attenuated infarct and non-infarct T1, and smaller left ventricular volumes at 2 days. This prognostic effect was weakened by delayed sampling. Lower Tsat and serum iron in the post-acute timepoints, but not at presentation, predicted lower myocardial salvage at 6 months. In mice, MI triggered an acute myocardial labile iron storm and early LV remodelling, progressing to HF. Baseline ID and acute iron chelation averted these effects.
CONCLUSIONS: This study gives rise to the hypothesis that ID at presentation with STEMI improves long-term outcomes by attenuating myocardial injury. It reconciles previous conflicting reports by revealing the confounding effects of delayed sampling, and non-interchangeability of different ID definitions. It suggests iron chelation in the acute stage, followed by post-acute iron repletion might improve long-term outcomes.

Title: Additive Value of Acetylcholine Testing in ANOCA: A US-Based Multicenter FlowLab Study.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA) is an underrecognized cause of angina with non-universal diagnostic techniques and patient management strategies. Among ANOCA testing, vasospasm provocation is not always performed mainly due to differences in institutional availability.
AIMS: Using the FlowLab Study, we quantified vasospasm prevalence among patients with ANOCA at US centers and compared physician decision-making, endotype distribution, and management between sites that did and did not include vasospasm testing in their workup.
METHODS: The FlowLab Study was a prospective, multicenter, US-based study of patients who were referred for coronary angiography and underwent ANOCA testing using the bolus thermodilution method. Presumed diagnosis before cardiac catheterization and final diagnosis after ANOCA testing were compared between participating sites with or without acetylcholine testing availability.
RESULTS: A total of 253 procedures at 14 US sites were included in this study. There were 155 procedures among sites performing spasm provocation testing and 98 procedures among sites not performing spasm provocation testing. Prior to cardiac catheterization, sites with spasm provocation testing were less likely to suspect epicardial coronary artery disease as the cause of angina compared to sites without (27% vs. 59.2%, p < 0.0001). A diagnosis of CMD was made more frequently at sites performing spasm testing compared to sites not performing spasm testing (68% vs. 29.6%, p < 0.0001). Similarly, among 125 patients who underwent spasm provocation testing, diagnostic yield increased from 34.4% with bolus thermodilution alone to 84.8% after the addition of spasm provocation testing (p < 0.001). In these patients, intensification involving calcium channel blockers was more frequent with epicardial (67%) and microvascular spasm (41%) than without spasm (24%, p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary US practice, adding spasm provocation testing to bolus thermodilution more than doubled diagnostic yield and was followed by medication changes directed toward the diagnosed endotype. Differences between sites with and without spasm testing also reflected variation in procedural practice.

Title: Calibrating Machine Learning Approaches for Probability Estimation Without Calibration Data.
Abstract: Statistical prediction models for binary outcomes are becoming increasingly popular. One significant challenge is calibrating these models to suit the characteristics of a target population that is structurally different from the original population. Calibration is especially challenging when there is no training data available from the target population. To address this problem, we propose a novel calibration method, SimCal, which uses synthetic data generated from the model development data in conjunction with marginal statistics from the calibration cohort. We show that expert judgment modeling (EJM) may be used for calibration if cross-sectional data from the target population are available comprising expert judgments about the potential outcome and the covariates. We describe three alternative calibration approaches when calibration data are lacking: similarity-binning averaging (SBA), adaptive calibration of predictions (ACP), and Elkan calibration. In a simulation study, we compare SBA, ACP, Elkan calibration, and SimCal. R code for applying these methods is provided from the re-analysis of data on coronary artery disease. We illustrate all 5 calibration approaches with a real data set for predicting functional outcome after stroke and all approaches but EJM in the re-analysis of the Cleveland Clinic data. None of the approaches performed convincingly well in all situations. SimCal performed well when model parameters were correctly specified. EJM failed on the stroke data. Further research is urgently required for calibration in the absence of calibration data.

Title: Associations of Social Determinants of Health and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality: UK Biobank Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIM: Social determinants of health (SDHs) play an important role in addressing inequitable and avoidable disparities in health status within countries but lack systematic assessment in broad populations. The aim of this study was to determine the association of SDHs, individually, in combination and cumulatively, with all-cause mortality risk, cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality, and cancer mortality.
METHODS: Data were obtained from 190,239 adults in the UK Biobank. Exposure variables were SDHs assessed by self-reported sociodemographic characteristics using standardized questionnaires. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate the associations of combined SDHs and cumulative number of SDHs with all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality.
RESULTS: Over a median 12-year follow-up, 9,871 deaths occurred, including 1,673 from CVD and 5,199 from cancer. Compared to favorable SDHs, medium SDHs (HR 1.143; 95% CI 1.090-1.198) and unfavorable SDHs (HR 1.642; 95% CI 1.559-1.729) were associated with higher all-cause mortality risks. Medium and unfavorable SDHs were associated with increased risks of CVD mortality (by 16.3% and 81.5%) and cancer mortality (by 7.7% and 26.1%). Having ≥8 cumulative adverse SDHs significantly heightened all-cause mortality risk. In exploratory analyses, baseline hypertension and diabetes statistically accounted for a portion of the associations between combined SDHs and mortality outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Unfavorable SDHs are substantially associated with increased risks of all-cause, CVD, and cancer mortality. Exploratory findings suggest that baseline hypertension and diabetes substantially explain these associations, highlighting existing disease burden as a key driver of health inequalities.

Title: The higher adherence to the DASH diet the lower incidence and mortality from cardiovascular disease and all causes: ELSA-Brasil study.
Journal: International journal of food sciences and nutrition
Abstract: To investigate the association between adherence to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality and all-cause mortality. The study included 14,621 participants from the ELSA-Brasil cohort. DASH adherence was assessed at baseline using a continuous score. Fine-Gray competing risk models were for MACE and CVD mortality, and Cox models for all-cause mortality. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic factors, behaviours, comorbidities, weight change, and total energy intake. Mean age was 52 years (SD 9), and mean DASH score was 23.9 (SD 4.4). Each one-point increase in the DASH score was associated with lowerrisk of MACE (sHR 0.96; 95% CI 0.92-0.99), CVD mortality (sHR 0.95; 95% CI 0.92-1.00), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Greater DASH adherence was associated with lower incidence of MACE and reduced CVD and all-cause mortality in Brazilian adults.

Title: Preoperative natremia and AKI after cardiac surgery: an international multicenter prospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND GOAL OF STUDY: Whether preoperative natremia levels may play a role in the development of acute kidney injury (AKI) after cardiac surgery is uncertain. We conducted a cohort study to evaluate the influence of preoperative natremia on AKI in high-risk patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort study involved 14 British and Spanish hospitals, each under local ethics committee approval. The study population comprised all consecutive patients aged 18 years or older, with a Cleveland Clinic score ≥ 4, undergoing cardiac surgery from July to December 2017. The resultant 241 consecutive patients were classified according to tertiles of preoperative natremia levels (< 139, > 139-141, and > 141 mmol/L).
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The AKIN criteria were used to define AKI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate the adjusted association between preoperative natremia and AKI. A potential link was observed between sodium levels ≤ 139 mmol/L and an increased risk of moderate-to-severe AKI relative to levels above 141 mmol/L (OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.02-3.95, p = 0.03), after multivariable adjustment for age and preoperative serum creatinine. No significant associations were observed between sodium levels and RRT or in-hospital mortality. Conclusions The results from this cohort of high-risk cardiac surgery patients lend tentative support to the hypothesis that preoperative natremia levels ≤ 139 mmol/L might be linked to a higher risk of moderate-to-severe AKI compared with levels above 141 mmol/L. These findings warrant further evaluation in a larger cohort.

Title: Effectiveness of a voice-guided tap-and-talk educational tool in enhancing cardiovascular knowledge and self-management in aged patients following percutaneous coronary intervention.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a voice-guided, tap-and-talk educational tool and assess its effectiveness in improving disease-related knowledge and self-management behaviors among older adults following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS: A voice-guided tap-and-talk educational tool was designed to address the specific needs of older adults post-PCI. A cluster randomized controlled trial was conducted in cardiovascular wards. The control group received conventional health education using printed manuals, whereas the intervention group received education via the tap-and-talk interactive tool. Outcomes included the level of knowledge regarding coronary heart disease and engagement in self-management behaviors. Chi-squared test and independent-sample t-test, chi-square test and paired t-test, and univariate repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) were conducted accordingly.
RESULTS: A total of 96 patients completed the study, including 49 in the experimental group and 47 in the control group.No statistically significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the groups (p > 0.05). A significant group × time interaction effect was detected for coronary heart disease (CHD)-related knowledge (F = 9.026, P < 0.001). At 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher self-management behavior scores than the control group (F = 11.607, P < 0.001). Additionally, CHD-related knowledge scores showed a mild downward trend over time in both groups (F = 124.067, P < 0.001). Consistent with the interaction effect mentioned above, the intervention group achieved significantly higher CHD-related knowledge scores than the control group at all three follow-up time points (1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-intervention) (F = 195.188, P < 0.001). Scores in the intervention group remained consistently higher across all domains. The tool received high acceptance ratings from participants (mean score 96.04 ± 2.61).
CONCLUSION: The tap-and-talk voice-guided educational tool was effective in enhancing knowledge and promoting self-management behaviors among older adults following PCI. The tool demonstrated a high level of user acceptability within the target population.

Title: Gut Regulated Associations of Neuronal Signalling in High Blood Pressure (GRAINS-BP): a double-blinded randomised crossover placebo-controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension affects 1 in 3 Australian adults and is a major contributor to stroke and myocardial infarction. Despite the availability of various medications, over 50% of patients struggle to control their blood pressure (BP) due to nonadherence, difficulty finding the right treatment, or avoidance of medication. Diet plays a key role in cardiovascular health, with high-fiber intake shown to lower BP through the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites formed during fiber fermentation. A previous clinical trial found that incorporating a specific type of resistant starch - high amylose maize starch enriched with acetate and butyrate (HAMSA/B) - significantly reduced blood pressure in hypertensive patients. While the exact mechanism remains unclear, SCFAs may influence BP via the gut-brain axis by reducing muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA), which has vasoconstrictor function and is elevated in hypertensive individuals.
METHODS: The GRAINS-BP clinical trial will recruit 29 adults with untreated hypertension (≥ 140/90 mmHg) for a double-blind, cross-over study using HAMSA/B administered as a shake delivered twice daily. The assessment period will span 48 days and include four visits at the Alfred Hospital, Melbourne, Australia. At visit 1, baseline measurement will be taken, including muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) and electrocardiogram (ECG). Participants will be randomised to the order in which they receive the placebo and HAMSA/B shake. Each intervention period will last 14 days, separated by a 20-day washout before participants cross over to the alternate treatment. At each visit, faecal, urine, and blood samples will be collected to investigate microbiome, cardiometabolic, renal, and immune profiles, respectively. Univariate and multivariate statistical analyses will be conducted to examine treatment effects and to identify correlations among microbiome, cardiometabolic, renal, and immune outcomes.
DISCUSSION: This project's primary outcome is change in autonomic nervous system activity. Secondary outcomes include 24-h BP, gut microbiome composition, SCFA levels, immune cell profiles gastrointestinal transit time, quality of life, anxiety and depression symptoms, cognitive function, gut barrier integrity, and circulating micro- and nanoplastics. Findings from this study will reveal whether SCFAs reduce blood pressure by their influence on the autonomic nervous system.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12625000557437).

Title: Distinct hemodynamic implications of junctional rhythm versus sinus rhythm on cardiac reverse remodeling after the Maze procedure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical success after the Maze procedure is conventionally defined as "freedom from atrial fibrillation (AF)," often grouping junctional rhythm (JR) with normal sinus rhythm (NSR). However, the specific hemodynamic impact of JR remains poorly understood. This study investigated whether JR truly represents a successful outcome compared to NSR and AF.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing the Maze procedure (2012-2024). After designating the first postoperative month as a blanking period for rhythm instability, we included only patients maintaining a consistent rhythm without crossover from 1 to 12 months postoperatively: AF (n = 71), NSR (n = 213), and JR (n = 35). Outcomes included cardiac reverse remodeling-assessed by left atrial contractile strain (LASct) and chamber dimensions-and permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation.
RESULTS: In the IPTW-adjusted cohort, the NSR group achieved significant cardiac reverse remodeling, characterized by improved LVEF (58.5%), reduced LA volume index (75.1 mL/m²), and notable recovery of LASct. In stark contrast, the JR group failed to show any reverse remodeling or mechanical recovery, exhibiting hemodynamic stagnation indistinguishable from the AF group. Consequently, no significant difference in cardiac function was observed between the JR and AF groups. Furthermore, the JR group faced a drastically elevated risk of PPM implantation compared to both the NSR and AF groups (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: JR is not a benign alternative to sinus rhythm; it mimics AF in preventing cardiac reverse remodeling and carries a high risk of pacemaker dependency. Therefore, JR should be clinically differentiated from NSR and recognized as a suboptimal hemodynamic outcome similar to AF.

Title: Determinants of outcome in atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial functional tricuspid regurgitation (AFTR) is increasingly recognized as a result of atrial remodelling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, prognostic predictors in this population remain incompletely defined.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate echocardiographic characteristics and identify predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with AFTR.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied consecutive patients with AF who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2017 and 2025. Inclusion required significant right atrial remodelling, defined as a right atrial area > 25 cm2. Patients with at least moderate functional tricuspid regurgitation comprised the AFTR cohort, while patients with mild/trivial/no tricuspid regurgitation served as controls. Patients with primary valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, device-related valve disease, RV dilatation, or more than mild RV systolic dysfunction were excluded. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify predictors of mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 152 patients were included, comprising 120 patients with AFTR and 32 controls. Compared with controls, patients with AFTR demonstrated larger atrial dimensions, higher right-sided hemodynamic-burden, impaired RV longitudinal strain, and reduced reservoir RA strain. During a median follow-up of 6.3 years, 53 deaths (45%) occurred among patients with AFTR. In univariable Cox analysis, age (HR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.04; p = 0.016), TR Vmax (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.35; p = 0.020), and lower reservoir RA strain (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.96; p = 0.003) were associated with mortality. In multivariable analysis, reservoir RA strain remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.81-0.95; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: AFTR is characterized by marked biatrial remodelling and impaired right atrial function. Reduced RA reservoir strain was independently associated with mortality, supporting a potential role for RA deformation imaging in risk stratification in AFTR.

Title: Preoperative platelet-related inflammatory burden is associated with delayed early hemodynamic recovery following minimally invasive cardiac surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MICS) is associated with reduced surgical trauma and improved postoperative recovery; however, early hemodynamic recovery remains variable and may be influenced by patient-related biological factors. This study evaluated the association between preoperative inflammatory biomarkers and delayed early postoperative recovery following MICS.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 166 consecutive patients undergoing thoracotomy-based MICS at a single tertiary center between January 2020 and January 2026. Preoperative inflammatory indices, including platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), were calculated from routine laboratory parameters. The primary endpoint was prolonged postoperative inotropic support (> 24 h); vasopressor-only therapy administered for vasoplegia or isolated blood pressure support was not counted. Multivariable complete-case logistic regression (n = 154), receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Prolonged inotropic support was needed in 41 patients (24.7%). Patients requiring prolonged support were older, had a higher prevalence of hypertension, and had longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration in univariable comparisons. LVEF was numerically lower but did not reach conventional statistical significance. PLR and SII were significantly higher in these patients (p = 0.003 and p = 0.010, respectively). In separate adjusted models, both PLR > = 142 and SII > = 462 were associated with prolonged support. In the combined complete-case model including both biomarkers, PLR > = 142 remained independently associated with prolonged support (OR 4.18, 95% CI 1.30-13.40, p = 0.016), whereas SII > = 462 did not (OR 1.66, 95% CI 0.52-5.31, p = 0.391). ROC analysis showed modest discrimination (PLR AUC 0.655, 95% CI 0.564-0.753, p = 0.003; SII AUC 0.634, 95% CI 0.538-0.729, p = 0.010). No significant associations were observed between inflammatory biomarkers and early mortality, acute kidney injury, or postoperative atrial fibrillation.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative platelet-related inflammatory burden, as reflected by PLR, was associated with delayed early postoperative hemodynamic recovery following MICS. However, the discriminatory performance of PLR was modest, and this biomarker should be interpreted as a complementary risk indicator rather than a stand-alone decision-making tool. These findings are exploratory and require prospective validation in independent cohorts.

Title: Analysis of myocardial work in different obesity phenotypes and its association with epicardial adipose tissue.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate subclinical cardiac dysfunction across distinct obesity phenotypes using myocardial work (MW) indices, and to investigate the moderating role of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) on MW impairment.
METHODS: One hundred ninety-two participants were categorized by BMI and metabolic status into four groups: metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically healthy obesity (MHO), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), and metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). MW indices were measured using speckle-tracking echocardiography. EAT volume was quantified from ECG-gated CT scans. Associations were analyzed using ANCOVA and regression models.
RESULTS: Despite no significant differences in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) among the groups, MUNW and MUO individuals exhibited significantly impaired MW, characterized by lower global work index (GWI), global constructive work (GCW), and global work efficiency (GWE), alongside higher global waste work (GWW), compared with MHNW controls. MHO patients showed significantly better MW profiles than MUNW and MUO groups. EAT volume was increased in all obesity phenotype groups. Although no direct association was found between EAT volume and MW indices, EAT volume significantly moderated the relationship between Metabolically Unhealthy (MUH) and both GWE and GWW.
CONCLUSIONS: MW detects subclinical dysfunction earlier than LVEF across obesity phenotypes, with impairment progressively worsening from MHO to MUNW to MUO. In metabolically unhealthy individuals with increased EAT volume, more pronounced reductions in GWE and elevations in GWW were observed.
TRIAL RRGISTRATION: This study has been registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry under the registration number ChiCTR2500100754 (registration date: April 15, 2025).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Immature neutrophil response is associated with cardiac complications after non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage.
Abstract: Acute non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is complicated by systemic inflammation and cardiac dysfunction that contribute to the high rates of morbidity and mortality. To better define the mechanistic relationship between immune response and cardiac complications, we evaluated subpopulations of circulating immune cells and their associations with abnormalities of cardiac rhythm, injury biomarkers, and mechanical function after hemorrhage. In this single-site prospective observational study, we screened all adult patients presenting to our neurocritical care unit with non-traumatic SAH who required external ventricular drain (EVD) placement for treatment of hydrocephalus. Following informed consent, peripheral blood samples were obtained at post-bleed days (PBDs) 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10. Subjects were separated into groups based on evidence of cardiac abnormalities (cAbn(+))" versus "no cardiac abnormalities (cAbn(-))," and flow cytometric analysis was used to identify and quantify immune cell subpopulations. Circulating neutrophil-secreted factors, including myeloperoxidase (MPO), were measured in plasma using ELISA. We measured associations between these immune factors and cardiac abnormalities. Sixty patients were enrolled between January 2018 and August 2023. Our patient cohort was 65% female with a median age of 58 (IQR 51-68). Poor grade SAH (Hunt Hess = 4-5) occurred in 52% (n = 31) of patients. In the overall cohort 47 (78%) required prolonged mechanical ventilation (> 24-hours), and 52 (87%) underwent coil embolization/clipping of their aneurysm. The average ICU and hospital lengths of stay (LOS) were 18.5 (IQR 12.2-22) and 23 (IQR 18.2-33.8) days, respectively. In-hospital mortality for enrolled patients was 11.8% and overall mortality 6 months after discharge was 25% (n = 15). 40% (n = 24) of patients were discharged home, 37% (n = 22) to acute rehabilitation, 8% (n = 5) to SNF, and 3% (n = 2) to hospice. Cardiac abnormalities after SAH were associated with increased circulating neutrophil counts but not monocyte or lymphocyte levels. Circulating neutrophils in patients with cardiac abnormalities also had reduced cell-surface expression of maturation markers CD10, CD14, and CD16 in patients with cardiac abnormalities. Elevated levels of immature neutrophils and circulating levels of lipocalin-2, and myeloperoxidase (MPO) correlated with increased Hunt-Hess score, ICU, and hospital length of stay. Higher grade SAH was associated with increased immature neutrophil response, which was associated with cardiac abnormalities. These cardiac abnormalities tracked with increased levels of pro-inflammatory lipocalin-2 and MPO, and worse outcomes.

Title: Late cardiopulmonary morbidity in patients with Hodgkin lymphoma: a retrospective nationwide registry study.
Abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a B-cell neoplasm with a cure rate of 90%. Previous data on late morbidity in patients with HL cover the era of older treatment modalities. This real-world study consisted of 2912 patients diagnosed with HL between 2000 and 2019 in Finland and aimed to clarify the incidence of late-onset cardiopulmonary morbidity compared to matched controls. Patient data were collected from four nationwide Finnish healthcare registries. We reported a higher occurrence of coronary artery disease in patients aged < 50 years at diagnosis than in controls (RR 3.80 (2.16-6.74), p < 0001). Additionally, a higher incidence of both heart failure (RR 1.68 (1.28-2.21), p < 0.001) and valvular heart disease (RR 1.80 (1.17-2.78), p = 0.006) was detected in patients aged ≥ 50 years at diagnosis than in the controls. Remarkably, in the < 50 years age group, the incidences of pneumonia (RR 4.89 (3.58-6.71), p < 0.001) and pulmonary embolism (RR 7.78 (2.75-21.95), p < 0.001) were higher than those in the control group. In conclusion, with the current treatment modalities, late cardiopulmonary morbidity in long-term survivors remains a great challenge. A strategy for primary prevention and early detection of late toxicity remains crucial and a critical evaluation of current treatment practices is warranted.

Title: Longitudinal association between body weight change and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity in patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus: A post hoc analysis of the FMD-J study B.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Abstract: We investigated cross-sectional associations between body mass index (BMI) and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and longitudinal associations between body weight change and baPWV over 3 years in 874 patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus without coronary artery disease (475 men; mean age, 61.9 ± 9.5 years). baPWV was measured at baseline, 1.5 years, and 3 years. At baseline, BMI was inversely correlated with baPWV (r = -0.14, P < 0.001), and multivariate analysis confirmed this association (β = -12.5, P < 0.001). In generalized linear mixed-effects models adjusted for concurrent systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and other covariates, neither continuous percentage change in body weight (β = -1.2, P = 0.08) nor categorical body weight change (≥5% increase: β = -10.6, P = 0.45; ≥5% decrease: β = 18.0, P = 0.15) was associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV, with no interaction across baseline BMI categories. The modest body weight changes observed in this cohort were not significantly associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV.

Title: Sustained improvement in sickle cell cardiomyopathy after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is superior to that with disease-modifying therapy.
Abstract: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative for sickle cell disease (SCD) - a group of inherited haemoglobin disorders encompassing homozygous haemoglobin S (HbSS) and compound heterozygous sickling disorders, including haemoglobin SC disease (HbSC), haemoglobin S/β0-thalassaemia (HbSβ0), haemoglobin S/β+-thalassaemia (HbSβ+), etc., but its long-term impact on SCD myocardial remodelling is incompletely characterized. We performed serial cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography in children and young adults with SCD undergoing matched-sibling or haploidentical HSCT in a prospective clinical trial with up to 36 months of post-HSCT follow-up. CMR assessments were conducted before HSCT and through the post-HSCT period. Echocardiographic parameters at 12 months post HSCT were compared with those of age-matched participants receiving disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Among 20 HSCT recipients (mean age 14.8 years), CMR demonstrated progressive reductions in biventricular volumes and left atrial volume over 36 months, with preservation of ejection fraction. Extra-cellular volume, a surrogate marker of myocardial fibrosis, showed significant improvement from baseline, having normalized in nearly all participants assessed at 36 months. Compared with age-matched DMT recipients, HSCT recipients had lower tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity and improved diastolic parameters at 12 months post-HSCT, with normalization of cardiac output on echocardiography. These findings demonstrate sustained reversal of myocardial fibrosis and structural cardiac remodelling after HSCT for SCD. HSCT may, therefore, modify the trajectory of SCD cardiomyopathy beyond the improvements achieved with current DMTs.

Title: Reduced Adverse Events Without Survival Benefit With HeartMate 3 vs. HeartMate II in Japan.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: HeartMate 3 (Abbott Laboratories), a fully magnetically levitated left ventricular assist device (LVAD), has shown improved hemocompatibility vs. previous devices, but nationwide real-world data in Japan remain limited.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Using the Japanese nationwide registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed patients who underwent de novo implantation of HeartMate 3 or HeartMate II between 2013 and 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, and device dysfunction requiring exchange or explantation within 2 years. In all, 978 patients were included in the study (HeartMate 3, n=486; HeartMate II, n=492). The 2-year cumulative incidence of the primary outcome was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group than in the HeartMate II group (9% vs. 23%; P<0.001). HeartMate 3 was independently associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.35; 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.51; P<0.001), which remained consistent in competing-risk and several statistically matched analyses. The incidence of hemocompatibility-related adverse events, including major bleeding, stroke, and device dysfunction, was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group. In contrast, 2- and 5-year overall mortality did not differ significantly between groups (<10% for both devices).
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide Japanese registry, HeartMate 3 reduced major LVAD-related complications without improving survival, supporting its clinical advantages in contemporary LVAD management.

Title: High Lipoprotein(a) Is a Predictor of Adverse Events and Heart Failure in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a well-established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but its prognostic role after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. This study investigated the association between Lp(a) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), in patients with AMI.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 1,235 patients with AMI from the NARA-MI registry who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention and had serum Lp(a) measured at admission. Based on receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, patients were categorized into high (≥24 mg/dL) and low (<24 mg/dL) Lp(a) groups. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause death, recurrent AMI, HF hospitalization, or unplanned coronary revascularization. During a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 497 MACE events occurred. The incidence of MACE (48.0% vs. 38.3%; P=0.004) and HF hospitalization (9.3% vs. 5.0%; P=0.008) was significantly higher in the high Lp(a) group. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, high-Lp(a) independently predicted MACE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-1.73; P=0.001) and HF hospitalization (HR 1.87; 95% CI 1.15-3.04; P=0.016). Among patients with HF, 39.7% were classified as HFpEF.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes after AMI, particularly HF. Measurement of Lp(a) may improve risk stratification after AMI and help identify patients at high risk of developing HF, including HFpEF.

Title: Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity in Dogs: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Doxorubicin, an anthracycline widely used in both human and veterinary oncology, is highly effective against a variety of malignancies in dogs, including lymphomas, sarcomas and carcinomas. Despite its efficacy, doxorubicin exposure can be associated with cardiotoxicity, which may present acutely or chronically, potentially leading to severe cardiac arrhythmia and congestive heart failure. Mechanisms underlying cardiotoxicity are multifactorial, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage via topoisomerase IIβ, inflammation and dysregulated cell death pathways such as apoptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis. In dogs, known risk factors include higher cumulative dose, breed predisposition to idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and higher body weight. Cardiac biomarkers, electrocardiography, echocardiography and other advanced imaging techniques have been employed to detect cardiac changes that can be seen also in the absence of clinical signs. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from experimental and retrospective research, highlighting the need for large prospective clinical studies to strengthen recommendations for monitoring and prevention. A deeper understanding of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in dogs is needed to identify factors influencing individual susceptibility, clarify the progression from subclinical damage to clinical cardiac dysfunction, and guide future research. Emerging approaches, including advanced echocardiography, microRNAs, proteomic biomarkers and pharmacokinetic modelling, may help improve early detection and guide more individualised dosing to minimise toxicity.

Title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture : protocol for a multicentre, randomized controlled trial of two blood transfusion strategies.
Abstract:
AIMS: Hip fracture is a global health issue. Complications are common, leading to reduced quality of life or death. These occur more frequently if anaemia is present. We hypothesize that correcting anaemia in the perioperative period may decrease major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and death after hip fracture.
METHODS: This multicentre prospective randomized trial compares transfusion strategies after hip fracture in patients aged ≥ 60 years. We initially planned to randomize 1,984 participants with anaemia, defined as haemoglobin ≤ 90 g l-1, to one of two transfusion strategies: liberal transfusion (aim haemoglobin 90 g l-1 to 110 g l-1), or restrictive transfusion (aim 75 g l-1 to 90 g l-1). The intervention lasts from randomization to hospital discharge or 30 days post randomization, whichever is soonest. The primary outcome measure was a composite of death or MACE adjudicated by blinded clinical experts. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and quality of life, evaluated at 120 days. Cost-effectiveness and health economic evaluation will also be reported.
RESULTS: This trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, HTA award (National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) 130875) and registered at ISRCTN 28818784. Ethical approval was obtained to recruit patients in the UK. As recruitment fell short of the initial target, and following consultation with the funder, we refined our primary outcome to include myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS), and reduced the required sample size to 842.
CONCLUSION: Recruitment commenced on 10 June 2022. The first participant was recruited on 16 June 2022. We will engage clinicians and healthcare planners to implement the findings. We plan to recruit until 31 October 2026. Results will be disseminated to clinicians, policymakers, patients, and the public.

Title: Multi-center study of CMR versus cardiac catheterization with endomyocardial biopsy for pediatric transplant surveillance: study protocol.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract: Notwithstanding advances in post-transplant care, acute allograft rejection (AR) remains the leading cause of mortality in pediatric heart transplant recipients (PHTX). Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) continues to be the standard of care for AR detection, despite being invasive, costly, and associated with patient discomfort and potential complications. Non-invasive alternatives, including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) with T1 and T2 parametric mapping and blood biomarkers (BB) such as cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and microRNA (miRNA), have shown promise in the adult transplant population, but their validation in the pediatric transplant population is lacking. The "Predictive Modeling of Acute Rejection in Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients" (PEACE) study is a prospective, multicenter trial aiming to assess the diagnostic accuracy of CMR and BB in comparison to EMB. The goal of this manuscript is to describe the purpose and experimental protocol of the PEACE study. The PEACE study's overarching hypothesis is that CMR and BB can consistently and accurately detect myocardial abnormalities, potentially guiding the need for EMB. Secondary objectives include cost-analyses of CMR and BB, as well as a biomarker performance evaluation in biopsy-negative, but symptomatic and suspected AR cases. PEACE will enroll PHTX ages 6-25 years, across approximately 20 U.S. pediatric hospitals. All subjects will undergo EMB for surveillance or suspected AR as standard of care. As part of the research protocol, subjects will undergo blood collection for BB prior to the EMB and CMR within 5 days of EMB. Central core labs will conduct blinded analysis for imaging, pathology, and biomarkers to ensure consistent data interpretation. PEACE represents a critical step in reducing reliance on invasive biopsies in the clinical care of PHTX. By validating non-invasive tools in a large, diverse population, the PEACE study could transform AR detection, resulting in improvement of the patient experience and outcomes in this vulnerable population. (Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07770659, Non-invasive Prediction of EArly Cardiac rEjection (PEACE)).

Title: A randomized controlled trial of a novel AI-based prognostic decision support tool integrated into the electronic health record for ischemic heart disease: Rationale and design of the PM Heart trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading global cause of years of life lost. Although the clinical presentation and progression of IHD differ widely, clinical management is relatively uniform. To improve risk stratification and clinical management, we developed a decision support tool - the PMHeartIHD Algorithm (also named PMHNet) - based on extensive clinical, registry and biochemical data. This algorithm automatically calculates one-year survival following an IHD event. We hypothesize that presenting the prognoses calculated by the PMHeartIHD Algorithm to the treating physicians will improve both the clinical management and outcome of the individual patient.
OBJECTIVE: The objectives of the PM Heart trial include clinical and technical aspects. First, the primary aim is to investigate if the clinical use of the prognosis calculated by the algorithm improves patient prognosis and minimizes the risk of re-hospitalization, compared to standard of care. A secondary objective is to generate knowledge on how decision support tools in cardiology may be implemented, received, and used directly in clinical practice.
METHODS: The PMHeartIHD Aalgorithm has been integrated into the electronic health record (EHR) system (Sundhedsplatformen (SP), EPIC) for clinical use. The PM Heart trial is designed as a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, clinical trial, automatically enrolling and randomizing hospitalized patients with coronary artery disease at the cardiology departments in The Capital Region and Region Zealand in Denmark. Patients are randomized (1:1 ratio) immediately after coronary angiography, to either show or hide the calculated PMHeartIHD-prognosis or not in the electronic health record.
RESULTS: The primary outcome is a composite outcome consisting of re-admissions within 30 days and one-year survival rates after randomization. Inclusion began September 2023, and follow-up is expected to finish in 2026.
CONCLUSIONS: We present the design of and rationale for the PM Heart trial. Our aim is to assess the clinical value of implementing an artificial intelligence-based decision support tool in clinical practice.

Title: Trends in cardiovascular disease and risk factors between 2004 and 2021: Findings from the U.S. Millennium Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in the United States (U.S.). Military veterans have notably high prevalences of CVD. The study aimed to report the prevalence of self-reported CVD and risk factors among post-9/11 veterans from 2004 to 2021.
METHODS: The U.S. Millennium Cohort Study prospectively follows service members and veterans. Eligible participants enrolled in 2001, separated from the military by 2021, and provided CVD information post-separation. Data from cross-sectional snapshots were used to examine unadjusted and standardized prevalences of CVD and risk factors. Linear trends in prevalence tested for significant changes.
RESULTS: Among 43,769 participants (average baseline age 37.2) between 2004-2006 and 2019-2021, results show current smoking decreased from 23.7 to 8.2 per 100. Prevalence estimates for all other examined factors increased; obesity from 22.2 to 47.7 per 100, hypertension from 9.0 to 23.5 per 100, diabetes from 1.6 to 7.0 per 100. CVD outcomes were less common and increased from <0.8 to <3.0 per 100.
CONCLUSIONS: Among a population of post-9/11 veterans, most CVD factors increased between 2004 and 2021. Treatment and intervention programs targeted toward veterans transitioning to civilian life should consider weight management and healthy lifestyle factors related to CVD prevention.

Title: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome. Current concepts, dilemmas, and challenges.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome (PAES) results from extrinsic compression of the popliteal artery as it passes through the popliteal fossa due to congenital musculotendinous anomalies or acquired muscle hypertrophy. The consequence of this compression is a progressive damage to the arterial wall, which can ultimately cause irreversible injury. This damage initially manifests as intermittent claudication, which usually occurs in young, athletic individuals with no cardiovascular risk factors. There may be an overlap of symptoms with other conditions, making diagnosis challenging. Beyond clinical suspicion, dynamic tests with provocation manoeuvres are essential. Early decompression treatment of symptomatic cases can prevent the onset of potentially serious complications, including amputation.
SOURCES OF DATA: This review integrates evidence from peer-reviewed literature focusing on popliteal entrapment syndrome.
AREAS OF AGREEMENT: Shortening the timeline from diagnosis to referral can help prevent irreversible damage to the arteries.There are a significant number of publications on PAES, based on retrospective single-centre experiences, short series or case reports, and limited scientific evidence. All publications repeatedly conclude that prospective multicentre studies are needed to standardize diagnostic and therapeutic protocols and develop guidelines for PAES.
AREAS OF CONTROVERSY: There are many points of disagreement regarding the management of PAES, and this does not help in addressing two key issues: avoiding misdiagnosis and unnecessary surgeries, which promote delayed diagnosis in worse clinical conditions.
GROWING POINTS: The creation of multicentre working groups seems necessary due to the limited number of cases at individual centres for conducting prospective studies.
AREAS TIMELY FOR DEVELOPING RESEARCH: Creation of international consensus protocols on definition, diagnosis, and treatment of PAES.

Title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen.
SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

Title: β3-Adrenergic Receptor Agonism Reduces Right Ventricular Systolic Pressure in a Preclinical Model of Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular pharmacology and therapeutics
Abstract: PurposePulmonary hypertension (PH) commonly complicates heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), driving morbidity and mortality, yet no therapies exist for HFpEF-PH. β3-adrenergic receptor (ADRB3) agonists may provide cardiometabolic and anti-inflammatory benefits. We evaluated pharmacological ADRB3 modulation in a preclinical HFpEF-PH model.MethodsHFpEF-PH was induced in male and female AKR/J mice via high-fat diet feeding for 16-20 weeks. At 12-16 weeks of feeding, mice were randomized to low-dose mirabegron (LDM, 3.6 mg/kg/day), high-dose mirabegron (HDM, 14.4 mg/kg/day), nebivolol (1.0 mg/kg/day), or vehicle for 4 weeks. A separate cohort received the ADRB3 antagonist SR59230A (0.5 mg/kg/day) or vehicle. Right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP), body weight change, and gene expression of nitric oxide synthases (Nos1, Nos2, Nos3), thermogenic markers (Ucp1, Ppargc1a), and inflammatory cytokines (Il1b, Il6, Tnf) were assessed.ResultsHDM and nebivolol significantly reduced RVSP compared to controls (P=0.010 and P=1.0×10-4), whereas SR59230A increased RVSP (P=0.006). LDM did not significantly affect RVSP, and LVEDP was unchanged across all treatment groups. HDM also reduced weight gain vs. control (P=0.023). HDM increased Ucp1 and Ppargc1a expression in adipose tissue, and nebivolol increased Ppargc1a expression in adipose tissue. These molecular findings remained significant in sensitivity analyses.ConclusionHDM and nebivolol reduced RVSP in a preclinical model of HFpEF-PH, whereas ADRB3 antagonism increased RVSP. These findings provide pharmacological evidence consistent with involvement of ADRB3 signaling and support further investigation of ADRB3-targeted approaches; the molecular pathways underlying these hemodynamic effects remain to be established.

Title: Endothelial dysfunction and long-term survival in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: An EASIX-based national cohort study.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the association of the endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in adults at cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.MethodsThis retrospective analysis of a population-based cohort included 10,885 adults aged ≥30 years from NHANES 1999-2018, with mortality follow-up through 2019. EASIX was calculated as lactate dehydrogenase × creatinine/platelet count. Survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses evaluated mortality associations.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 97 months, 1,122 participants died, including 295 from cardiovascular causes. Each one-unit increase in EASIX was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.24-1.61) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.13-1.49). There was no evidence of non-linearity for all-cause mortality (P = 0.466), while the cardiovascular association was non-linear (P = 0.008). Associations persisted after additional lifestyle adjustment. CKM-stage interactions were not significant in the full cohort.ConclusionsHigher EASIX was associated with greater all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in CKM stages 0-3. Its potential role in clinical risk assessment warrants further validation.

Title: Cardiology Support Utilization Patterns and Associated Barriers Across Northwestern Ontario.
Abstract: The Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre On-Call Cardiology Support Service serves a geographically vast region across Northwestern Ontario where cardiovascular disease is a major burden. The objective is to analyze service utilization patterns including locations, indications, interventions, and barriers. In this 6-month prospective study, cardiologists collected data via survey on calls from rural and remote providers. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test were used. The Canadian Institute for Health Information's Rural Health Systems Model was used for interpretation. Two hundred and six responses across 19 locations identified: common consultations-chest pain, dyspnea, and atrial fibrillation; frequent interventions-medical recommendations, education, and transfer decisions; key barriers-limited personnel knowledge and infrastructure. Significant associations were identified. This study characterized cardiology support service utilization across Northwestern Ontario, identifying key barriers and opportunities to strengthen rural health systems planning and cardiovascular care. These findings can inform targeted initiatives and support future evaluations.

Title: The "living well with lupus" lifestyle intervention: Effects on gut microbiota in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and high cardiovascular risk.
Abstract: BackgroundSystemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease associated with increased cardiovascular risk and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Although lifestyle can modulate the microbiome, the impact of multidisciplinary interventions in SLE remains unclear. Thus, the aim of the present study was to investigate the effects of a multidisciplinary lifestyle intervention on gut microbiota diversity and composition in women with SLE and high cardiovascular risk.Materials and methodsThis study analyzed a subsample (n = 31) from the "Living Well with Lupus" (LWWL) study, a 6-month randomized controlled trial. Patients were assigned to a lifestyle intervention + standard care (LWWL) or a standard care control group (CG). Gut microbiota (16S rRNA sequencing), fecal short-chainfatty acids (SCFAs), selected cardiovascular risk factors, dietary intake, and physical activity levels were assessed before and after the intervention.ResultsNo significant changes were observed in cardiovascular risk factors, food intake, or physical activity levels. Fecal SCFA concentrations and alpha/beta diversity also remained stable. Exploratory taxonomic analyses nevertheless identified distinct relative-abundance patterns across groups and time, including a numerical increase in the Firmicutes-to-Bacteroidota (F/B) ratio in LWWL and different trajectories of several SCFA-associated genera. Among these, Blautia and Parasutterella increased, whereas Butyricimonas, Coprococcus, and Odoribacter decreased from pre- to post-intervention in LWWL, with different trajectories observed in CG across these genera.ConclusionsThese findings suggest that taxonomic features of the gut microbiota may show compositional variation following a lifestyle intervention even in the absence of detectable changes in the measured cardiometabolic or behavioral outcomes. However, the functional and clinical significance of these exploratory taxonomic patterns remains uncertain and warrants further investigation.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Etomidate Versus Ketamine for Endotracheal Intubation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is a commonly used technique for critically ill patients requiring emergency intubation, and the choice of induction agent is crucial for minimizing peri-intubation morbidity and maintaining hemodynamic stability. The most commonly used induction agents are etomidate and ketamine, although controversy remains about their effectiveness and safety. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis compared the efficacy and safety of etomidate versus ketamine for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2000 and May 2026 were systematically searched in PubMed, The Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect. The included studies compared etomidate with ketamine for emergency endotracheal intubation in critically ill adults. We analyzed data with RevMan 5.4 and Mantel-Haenszel random-effects models and calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Seven RCTs involving 5234 patients were included in the final analysis. No significant difference was observed between etomidate and ketamine regarding 28-day mortality (RR 1.01; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93-1.10; p=0.84), cardiac arrest (RR 0.91; 95% CI 0.62-1.34; p = 0.64), failed intubation (RR 1.09; 95% CI 0.68-1.76; p=0.71), or vasopressor requirement (RR 1.27; 95% CI 0.94-1.72; p=0.13). Sensitivity analyses suggested possible hemodynamic differences between the two agents, which should be interpreted cautiously, and etomidate was relatively cardiovascularly stable in some analyses. Overall, etomidate and ketamine showed similar efficacy and safety for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two agents in mortality, cardiac arrest, failed intubation, or vasopressor use. Thus, clinicians should choose the induction agent on a case-by-case basis, based on patient, hemodynamic, and clinician-specific factors. Randomized trials in selected critically ill patient populations should be conducted on a larger scale.

Title: Cardiovascular exercise mitigates inflammation in the early subacute phase of stroke recovery: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive inflammation in early phases post-ischemic stroke is associated with poor long-term outcome and increased stroke recurrence. Interventions capable of downregulating persistent states of inflammation could improve recovery and prevent secondary stroke. Cardiovascular exercise (CE) has well-established anti-inflammatory effects but its capacity to attenuate the exaggerated inflammatory response triggered by ischemic stroke is unclear.
METHODS: We investigated the impact of eight weeks of CE on the serum concentration of inflammatory mediators in the early subacute phase post-stroke. Seventy-one patients with first-ever ischemic stroke were randomly assigned to moderate-to-vigorous CE (n = 45) or standard care (SC) (n = 26). Concentrations of CRP, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α and IL-1β were measured at baseline and after the interventions. Differences between groups were analyzed with linear mixed models adjusted for age and sex.
RESULTS: Compared with the CE group, the SC group showed significant increases in IL-6 (β = 0.585, 95% CI = 0.164-1.006, p = 0.0073), IL-8 (β = 0.160, 95% CI = 0.004-0.317, p = 0.0447), and TNF-α (β = 0.0845, 95% CI = 0.0137-0.1553, p = 0.0206). The SC group also showed greater increases in CRP (β = 0.250, 95% CI = -0.407, 0.906, p = 0.4499) and IL-10 (β = 0.251, 95% CI = -0.024, 0.527, p = 0.0729) but group differences were not significant. IL-1β levels remained stable and differences between groups were not significant (β = -0.008, 95% CI = -0.058, 0.042, p = 0.7618).
CONCLUSIONS: When introduced in the early subacute phase of stroke recovery, moderate-to-vigorous CE mitigates increases in inflammation, but the effect differs across mediators. To what extent reducing the inflammatory response in the early stages post-stroke with CE can impact long-term recovery and stroke recurrence needs to be determined.

Title: Baseline Serum HMGB1 and the Composite of All-Cause Mortality or First Heart Failure Rehospitalization in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between baseline serum high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) and the composite of all-cause mortality or first heart failure rehospitalization in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort included 224 patients with HFpEF. The primary endpoint was the first occurrence of all-cause mortality or heart failure rehospitalization.
RESULTS: During a median observation time of 58 months, 37 of 224 patients (16.5%) experienced the composite endpoint. Baseline HMGB1 was higher in patients with events than in those without events (8.76 ± 3.18 vs 5.99 ± 1.86 µg/L; P<0.001). After adjustment for NT-proBNP, age, and sex, each 1 µg/L increase in HMGB1 was associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint (hazard ratio, 1.399; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.242-1.576; P<0.001). Apparent areas under the curve were 0.753 (95% CI, 0.653-0.853) for HMGB1, 0.790 (95% CI, 0.708-0.872) for NT-proBNP, and 0.870 (95% CI, 0.793-0.947) for their combination. The combination did not significantly outperform NT-proBNP alone (ΔAUC, 0.080; 95% CI, -0.012 to 0.171; nominal P=0.088; Holm-adjusted P=0.176). The optimism-corrected Cox concordance index was 0.828, and sensitivity analyses showed associations in the same direction.
CONCLUSION: Higher baseline serum HMGB1 was associated with the composite of all-cause mortality or first heart failure rehospitalization in this exploratory HFpEF cohort. Incremental discrimination beyond NT-proBNP and clinical utility remain unestablished. Independent prospective multicenter validation is required.

Title: Pro-inflammatory cytokines moderated by visceral adiposity from a pragmatic randomized crossover trial of portable HEPA air purifiers.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airborne particulate matter (PM) increases the risk of cardiovascular disease. High efficiency particulate arrestance (HEPA) filtration can reduce indoor PM, but evidence is lacking as to whether HEPA filtration has an effect on pro-inflammatory cytokines.
METHODS: This pragmatic crossover trial randomly assigned participants to 30 days of HEPA or sham filtration, followed by a 30-day washout, and then 30 days of the alternative. Concentrations of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) were measured in quality-controlled peripheral blood plasma samples using ultra-sensitive assays. Linear mixed models compared HEPA to sham filtration. The moderating effect of visceral adipose tissue (VAT) was assessed using a dichotomized A Body Shape Index (ABSI) z-score and other measures of adiposity.
RESULTS: Among 116 participants, mean age was 41.5 years, 58.6% were female, and 72.4% were non-Hispanic White. No overall difference in mean IL-1β concentration was observed between HEPA and sham filtration. However, VAT significantly moderated the results (test for interaction p = 0.001). Among participants with excessive VAT (ABSI z-score ≥ +0.229, N = 12), HEPA filtration significantly reduced mean IL-1β concentration by 22.8% compared with sham filtration (0.138 versus 0.179 pg/mL, p < 0.001). No reduction was observed among participants with healthy VAT. Similar non-significant patterns were observed for IL-6, but little effect for hsCRP. Other measures of adiposity, including BMI, were less effective or did not moderate the results.
CONCLUSIONS: VAT moderated inflammatory responses to HEPA filtration, with a significant reduction in IL-1β among participants with excessive VAT.

Title: Association of adverse pregnancy outcomes with coronary microvascular dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
