BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) are recognized cardiovascular risk enhancers, yet their association with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) has not been systematically quantified.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between APOs and CMD and to provide pooled estimates of CMD prevalence and severity in women with APO history.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched through December 2025. Observational studies evaluating coronary microvascular function using PET, Doppler echocardiography, stress CMR, or invasive physiology in women with APOs versus controls were included. Multivariate random-effects meta-analysis was performed to account for non-independent effect estimates arising from shared control groups. Risk of bias was assessed using NOS; certainty of evidence using GRADE.
RESULTS: Five studies (1,183 participants; 583 APO, 600 controls) were included. Women with APO history demonstrated significantly reduced CFR (SMD -0.94; 95% CI, -1.43 to -0.45; p<0.0001; I²=88.2%) and elevated CMD prevalence (OR 6.74; 95% CI, 1.55-29.42; p0.011; I²=92.2%). An exploratory graded pattern was observed, with combined preeclampsia and gestational diabetes associated with the largest CFR reduction (SMD -1.27); however, this was driven primarily by a single study with shared controls. Publication bias assessment was non-significant for CFR (p0.312) but borderline for CMD prevalence (p0.078).
CONCLUSIONS: APOs are associated with reduced CFR and elevated CMD prevalence, suggesting CMD may represent a plausible intermediate phenotype linking pregnancy complications to long-term cardiovascular disease. Given low to very low certainty evidence and substantial heterogeneity, these findings are hypothesis-generating and support further prospective research.

Title: Effectiveness of Yoga-based guided meditation In Improving the quality of sleep in patients with coronary artery disease: The Yoga Nidra Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor sleep quality has emerged as a risk for coronary artery disease (CAD) and is also associated with poor prognosis and increased mortality. Sleep aids, among CAD patients, lead to increased heart failure, hospitalisation, and mortality. Yoga Nidra, a form of guided meditation, has been shown to improve sleep quality and duration. The aim of the study is to evaluate the adjunctive effect of Yoga Nidra on actigraphy-measured sleep quality parameters, psychological outcomes, and health-related quality of life in patients with CAD.
METHODS: This is a two-arm,1:1 allocation, randomised, controlled, open-label, blinded-endpoint, single-centre trial conducted in a tertiary care hospital between 22-9-2021 and 30-03-2024.144 out of 678 consecutively screened patients with stable CAD and poor sleep quality met the eligibility criteria and were enrolled. Participants were randomised to either a 35-minute, 12-week Yoga Nidra intervention group (n = 72) or a standard care group (n = 72) with sleep hygiene counselling imparted to all patients.The primary outcome was to assess actigraphy-measured sleep efficiency. Secondary outcomes included assessments of actigraphy-derived sleep parameters, ambulatory blood pressure (BP), echocardiographic diastolic function (E/E'), psychological health, and quality-of-life evaluations using validated scales.
RESULTS: The Yoga Nidra group exhibited significant improvements in sleep efficiency (82% [76-86] vs. 64% [57-74]; p < 0.05), total sleep time (357 ± 99 min vs. 298 ± 83 min; p < 0.05), reduced sleep latency (15 [11-24] vs. 30 [14-70] min; p < 0.05), and lower wake after sleep onset (48 [28-67] vs. 67 [37-119] min; p < 0.05). Significant improvements were also observed in perceived stress, depression levels, and quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Yoga Nidra is effective in improving sleep quality inpatients with coronary artery disease.Stress, depression, and health-related quality of life also improved with Yoga Nidra.

Title: Prehospital extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a protocol for the Rapid prehospital ACcess to ECPR in Prague (RACE Prague) single-arm pilot feasibility study.
Abstract:
AIM: The benefit of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is strongly time dependent, yet in established in-hospital ECPR systems, including Prague, the median collapse-to-flow time has remained around 60 min or more, dominated by intra-arrest transport. Evidence for prehospital ECPR remains limited, particularly its comparison with in-hospital ECPR. RACE Prague evaluates whether dispatching a mobile cannulation team to the scene shortens this interval within the same ECPR system.
METHODS: Single-centre, prospective, interventional, single-arm pilot feasibility study. Twenty adults aged 18-70 years with witnessed refractory OHCA (three unsuccessful defibrillations and/or ≥10 min of resuscitation in pulseless electrical activity), receive prehospital percutaneous femoro-femoral veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) from a mobile ECPR team. The primary endpoint (time from estimated collapse to ECMO flow ≥2.0 L/min) is tested hierarchically against the historical Prague OHCA in-hospital ECPR cohort (target shortening ≥15 min) and a contemporaneous in-hospital ECPR cohort at the same centre. Secondary endpoints include 30-day survival with favourable neurological outcome assessed blind, decomposition of prehospital pathway intervals, cannulation success, and pre-specified safety endpoints. Enrolment proceeds without prior consent under ethics-approved emergency-research provisions, with deferred consent thereafter.
CONCLUSION: RACE Prague is testing the effect of cannulation location on the time to extracorporeal support and will provide essential evidence on the feasibility of prehospital ECPR.Trial registration:ClinicalTrials.govNCT06789978; Ethics Committee of the General University Hospital in Prague, reference 134/23 S-IV.

Title: ICD-Coded Versus Undiagnosed Acute Kidney Injury in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common among older adults and associated with adverse outcomes, yet it often goes undiagnosed. We aimed to compare the prevalence of undiagnosed versus International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-coded AKI as well as their clinical and molecular characteristics and evaluate their associations with clinical outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: A total of 5,692 adults with proteomic and metabolomic profiling from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study, excluding individuals with end-stage kidney disease at baseline (2011-2013).
EXPOSURES: AKI, defined as either ICD-coded or undiagnosed based on 3 abstracted levels of serum creatinine measured during hospitalizations.
OUTCOMES: Incident coronary heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and all-cause mortality.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: ICD-coded AKI was compared with undiagnosed AKI across all hospitalizations. Risk factors for ICD-coded and undiagnosed AKI were assessed separately using Cox proportional hazards models from study visit to the first AKI encounter. Time-varying Cox models were used to evaluate the associations of ICD-coded and undiagnosed AKI with adverse outcomes.
RESULTS: ICD codes identified 51.4% of AKI defined based on changes in serum creatinine, with higher sensitivity for more severe stages and a specificity of 87.0%. Undiagnosed AKI was more common in women; otherwise, clinical risk factors for undiagnosed AKI were similar to those for ICD-coded AKI, as were proteomic and metabolomic risk factors. Both AKI groups were strongly associated with coronary heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and mortality.
LIMITATIONS: AKI was estimated using 3 values of serum creatinine only and not urinary output. Diagnosed AKI was identified using billing codes, which may underestimate clinical diagnosis of AKI.
CONCLUSIONS: Undiagnosed AKI is prevalent, especially among women, and is biologically and prognostically similar to ICD-coded AKI, motivating efforts to improve AKI recognition and diagnosis.

Title: Epicardial adipose tissue radiomics complement calcium scoring in black adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional markers of risk such as coronary artery calcium (CAC) scores are lower and less predictive in Black adults, despite a high prevalence of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Metabolic Syndrome We evaluated whether incorporation of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) features capture prognostic signal beyond CAC and social deprivation index, in predicting major adverse cardiovascular events.
METHODS: Adults with T2DM undergoing non-contrast CT calcium scoring from the CLARIFY registry (NCT04075162), including 1024 non-Hispanic Black participants and 3072 propensity-matched non-Hispanic White participants were included. EAT was automatically segmented and radiomic features were extracted and selected using survival-based machine learning. Cox proportional hazards models were constructed using CAC, Social Deprivation Index (SDI), and EAT features alone and in combination. The primary endpoint was 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-3P), defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke. Model discrimination, reclassification, and calibration were assessed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of approximately 5 years, 206 (20%) Black participants and 422 (14%) matched White participants experienced MACE-3P In Black participants, the SDI+CAC+EAT model demonstrated the highest discrimination (C-index 0.62) and significantly improved reclassification compared with CAC alone (NRI) of 0.29 (95% CI 0.15-0.56; p < 0.0007). In contrast, the SDI+CAC+EAT model showed no improvement in discrimination when compared to CAC alone (C-index 0.67 v. 0.67) in the White cohort.
CONCLUSION: In adults with T2DM, EAT may serve as a complimentary imaging marker when combined with CAC scores to provide incremental prognostic information or refine risk characterization.

Title: Temporal changes in lipoprotein(a) after acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and is traditionally considered stable. Its behavior following acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and clinical implications remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize the temporal trajectory of Lp(a) following ACS, evaluate whether baseline levels predict longitudinal changes, and assess the stability of clinically relevant Lp(a) risk categories.
METHODS: In this prospective study, 225 patients with ACS underwent serial Lp(a) measurements during hospitalization and at follow-up (≥6 months). Longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. Associations between baseline Lp(a) and changes over time were evaluated using Spearman correlation. Stability of Lp(a) threshold risk categories (<50, 50-105, ≥105 nmol/L) was assessed by examining transitions across categories.
RESULTS: Lp(a) increased following ACS (p < 0.001), peaking at Days 4-7 (+30.0 %, p = 0.0001) and remaining elevated at Day 30 (+15.0 %, p = 0.0042), before returning to baseline at follow-up. Among individuals with increases in Lp(a), baseline Lp(a) was the strongest determinant of trajectory, with higher levels associated with greater increases at all timepoints (ρ 0.37-0.63, all p < 0.05). Categories for those evels in the low (<50 nmol/L) and high (≥105 nmol/L) categories remained stable with minimal reclassification. Variability was confined to levels in the intermediate range (50-105 nmol/L), where 37.5 % transitioned to ≥105 nmol/L.
CONCLUSIONS: Lp(a) rises transiently after ACS and returns to baseline over time. Levels in the high and low risk categories remain in those categories, while variability is limited to the intermediate range. A single Lp(a) measurement obtained during ACS may be sufficient for individuals with clearly low or markedly elevated Lp(a) levels, whereas repeat testing after clinical stabilization may be considered for patients with intermediate or borderline baseline levels.

Title: De-escalating Therapy in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea After Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist-Induced Weight Loss: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Incretin-based therapies now achieve weight reduction of a magnitude previously attainable only through bariatric surgery and have demonstrated substantial reductions in the apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) in adults with obesity-related obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). Sleep services are consequently managing growing numbers of patients who undergo rapid, substantial weight loss while established on positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy, and who ask whether that therapy can be stopped. No guideline addresses this question. This narrative review synthesises three literatures that have developed largely in isolation: the relationship between weight change and OSA severity, the efficacy data for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual incretin agonists in OSA, and the experimental PAP withdrawal literature. Across randomised trials and meta-analyses, there is consistent agreement that incretin therapy reduces AHI, body weight and blood pressure, with effect magnitude varying by agent, dose and baseline adiposity. There is, however, material disagreement on three questions directly relevant to de-escalation: whether the effect is wholly weight-mediated, whether AHI reduction translates into reduction in cardiovascular risk, and what proportion of patients achieve genuine disease remission as opposed to severity reduction. Approximately half of participants in the largest trial did not reach a severity threshold at which PAP would ordinarily be considered unnecessary, and withdrawal studies demonstrate recurrence of obstructive events and adverse haemodynamic change within days of stopping therapy. This review proposes a structured, reversible and documented framework for reassessment rather than ad hoc discontinuation and identifies the evidence gaps that must be closed before de-escalation can be considered evidence-based practice.

Title: External validation of artificial intelligence-guided electrocardiogram (AI-ECG) in detecting asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIM: Asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction (LVD) represents a key and frequently under-recognized stage in the heart failure (HF) continuum. Early identification enables targeted prevention and timely initiation of evidence-based therapies. Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) may provide a scalable alternative to imaging for LVD detection. This systematic review synthesized evidence from exclusively externally validated AI-ECG studies evaluating the detection of asymptomatic LVD, with symptomatic HF cohorts included to contextualize the evidence base across the HF continuum.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted on 8th September 2025. The main output was the pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).
RESULTS: From 3,587 records, 12 asymptomatic and 30 symptomatic studies were identified (538,735 participants). In asymptomatic cohorts evaluating left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD), AI-ECG demonstrated promising but heterogeneous discriminatory performance (I²>85%) with pooled AUROCs of 0.87 (95% CI 0.75-0.99) for LVEF ≤35%, 0.93 (95% CI 0.88-0.97) for LVEF ≤40%, and 0.89 (95% CI 0.85-0.97) for LVEF ≤50%. Symptomatic cohorts showed AUROCs of 0.89 (95% CI 0.86-0.92), 0.90 (95% CI 0.88-0.92), and 0.85 (95% CI 0.83-0.86) respectively. Asymptomatic left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD) demonstrated moderate performance (AUROC 0.76, 95% CI 0.66-0.86) with no externally validated symptomatic LVDD studies identified. Small-study effects were detected exclusively in asymptomatic cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Discriminatory performance of AI-ECG in asymptomatic LVSD is broadly comparable to symptomatic populations. High risk of bias driven by prolonged ECG-to-echocardiogram intervals reflecting real-world logistical constraints necessitate cautious interpretation of results and further prospective validation.

Title: Utility of a coronary artery disease polygenic risk score in a low-risk primary prevention cohort.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate whether a coronary artery disease (CAD) polygenic risk score (PRS) identifies clinically low-risk individuals at elevated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk.
METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study within the UK Biobank including adults aged 40-74 years, free of ASCVD and diabetes, not on lipid-lowering therapy, and with baseline LDL <190 mg/dL. Participants were enrolled from 2006 to 2010 and followed through 2021. Ten-year ASCVD risk was estimated using pooled cohort equations. A CAD PRS derived from 2.3 million genome-wide variants was categorized as top 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, and bottom 50%. Lipoprotein(a) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein were similarly stratified. The primary endpoint was a composite of myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or cardiovascular death. Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for 10-year ASCVD events, and net reclassification improvement (NRI) was assessed at 5% and 7.5% risk thresholds.
RESULTS: Among 266,917 low-risk individuals (median age 54; 38% male), ASCVD risk increased substantially across higher PRS strata. Compared with the bottom 50%, individuals in the top 50% had more than double the risk (aHR 2.48), the top 20% had over triple the risk (aHR 3.71), and the top 5% and 1% had 6-fold (aHR 6.31) and 9-fold (aHR 9.73) higher risks, respectively (all p < 0.0001). Adding PRS improved model discrimination (AUC 0.76 vs 0.72) and reclassified 12% of low-risk individuals upward-over tenfold more than Lp(a) or hs-CRP.
CONCLUSION: In primary prevention, a CAD PRS identifies individuals with markedly higher ASCVD risk despite low clinical risk estimates and may merit consideration among ASCVD risk enhancers.

Title: Genetically determined very low lipoprotein(a) is not associated with type 2 diabetes and glycemic traits.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein (a) [Lp(a)] is an independent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factor, with levels largely determined by variation in the LPA gene. Despite interests in therapeutic Lp(a) lowering, the phenotypic effects of very low Lp(a) are incompletely characterized, with some studies suggesting increased type 2 diabetes risk.
OBJECTIVES: Estimate associations between very low Lp(a), inferred by LPA loss of function variant rs41272114, with type 2 diabetes and glycemic biomarkers.
METHODS: A multi-population study of European, Hispanic/Latino, and South Asian populations from five cohort studies was assembled. Effects of the null allele rs41272114 (CC, wild-type; T, null allele) on type 2 diabetes and glycemic biomarkers (fasting glucose, fasting insulin, glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein ratio, and HOMA-IR) were estimated using multivariable-adjusted and cohort-specific linear or logistic regression models that were combined using inverse variance meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Of n=519,892 participants, the T null allele was common (n=49,841 CT and n=2,039 TT) and n=38,320 participants had type 2 diabetes (prevalence range: 4.7, 29.5%). Participants with the TT genotype had a median Lp(a) ranging 1.5-1.9 nmol/L compared to median Lp(a) ranging 15.8-30.0 nmol/L in participants with the CC genotype. We did not observe increased odds of type 2 diabetes by rs412722114 genotype (ORCTvs.CC = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.94, 1.00; ORTTvs.CC = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.89, 1.15). Mean levels of glycemic biomarkers also did not differ by rs41272114 genotype.
CONCLUSIONS: In a large multi-population study with high burdens of type 2 diabetes, life-long very low Lp(a) did not increase type 2 diabetes risk.

Title: Whole heart atherosclerosis volume and risk for major adverse cardiovascular events across the clinical likelihood for obstructive CAD; the CONFIRM2 study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The totality of atherosclerosis from the coronary tree can be measured with quantitative coronary CT and is increasingly being recognized as important marker for future cardiovascular events. We evaluated the risk and absolute event rates of plaque volume staging systems and provided analyses according to the clinical likelihood of obstructive CAD.
METHODS: CONFIRM2 is an ongoing, global, multicenter, observational registry that included patients with clinically indicated coronary CT angiography and follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Patients without cardiac symptoms and prior CAD were excluded. Atherosclerosis was quantified across all coronary segments by AI-QCT. Total plaque volume (TPV) was categorized into non-calcified plaque (NCPV, HU <350) and calcified (HU>350). The primary end point was the incidence rate of MACE over at 4 years and included all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, congestive heart failure, late revascularizations (occurring >90 days post index CCTA), and hospitalization for unstable angina. Secondary endpoint included Death, MI, and stroke. The prognostic value of TPV and NCPV was evaluated across the pretest likelihood according to the ESC Risk Factor Weighted Likelihood (ESC RF-CL).
RESULTS: A total of 6061 patients (mean age 58.6 ± 12.1 years, 48.6% male) were included and the mean follow-up duration was: 4.4 ± 1.8 years. According to the ESC RF-CL for obstructive CAD, patients were classified as very-low, low, and moderate risk in 36.0%, 43.0%, and 22.0%, and obstructive CAD rates were 6.8%, 15.7%. and 28.2, respectively. Within the total cohort, TPV >0-250, 250-750, and >750 mm3 were associated with MACE: HR 2.5 (95% CI 1.1, 5.6), HR 10.1 (95% CI 4.4, 22.9), and HR 15.9 (95% CI 6.7, 38.0) compared with TPV=0. According to RF-CL very-low, low, and moderate, the MACE rates were: 0.7, 2.9, 0.0% for TPV=0 mm3; 2.3%, 3.6%, 4.6% for TPV >0-250 mm3; 10.3%, 12.3%, 13.5% for TPV 250-750 mm3; and 18.8%, 16.7%, and 19.8% for TPV>750 mm3. Findings were consistent for the secondary endpoint.
CONCLUSION: Among a large cohort of symptomatic patients evaluated by coronary CT angiography, the burden of atherosclerosis by AI-QCT was the main driver for cardiovascular events. Absolute event rates were consistently higher by each plaque volume stage, and consistent across the clinical likelihood subgroups for obstructive CAD. While quantitative atherosclerosis was present in the majority of patients, risk increased significantly from 250 mm3 of TPV during intermediate term follow-up.

Title: Association of reproductive factors with acute myocardial infarction in young women: A VIRGO and NHANES case-control study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Young women with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) often present with distinct risk profiles compared with older women and men, but the role of reproductive factors remains poorly understood. This study examines associations of reproductive factors with AMI in young women.
METHODS: We conducted a case-control study of 1561 women aged 18-55 years with AMI from VIRGO and age-matched controls from NHANES. A wide range of reproductive factors were evaluated. Conditional logistic regression estimated odds ratios for AMI, sequentially adjusted for race/ethnicity, socioeconomic variables, and traditional risk factors. Stratified analyses were performed by menopausal status.
RESULTS: Early menarche (<11 years; OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.56-2.73), menopause (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.50-2.22), gestational diabetes (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.23-2.19), birth control pills use for 1-5 years (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.36-2.05), and ever use of female hormones (OR 1.99, 95% CI 1.62-2.46) were associated with higher odds of AMI, while first live birth at ≥30 years (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.36-0.69), breastfeeding ≥1 month (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.38-0.56), and current contraceptive use (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.32-0.76) were associated with lower odds. After adjustment for traditional risk factors, birth control pills use for 1-5 years (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.25-2.34) and female hormone use (OR 1.75, 95% CI 1.28-2.38) remained significantly associated. Associations varied by menopausal status.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive factors are associated with early-onset AMI in young women. Recognition of reproductive history may inform prevention strategies in young women.

Title: Inverse Association of the Life's Crucial 9 Score With MAFLD: An Exploratory Mediation Analysis of the C-Reactive Protein-Albumin-Lymphocyte (CALLY) Index.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is strongly associated with cardiovascular disease. Life's Crucial 9 (LC9), an expanded cardiovascular health metric incorporating psychological health, may provide a multidimensional measure of cardiometabolic health. The CALLY index integrates inflammatory, immune, and nutritional information and has been associated with MAFLD. However, whether ln(CALLY) statistically accounts for part of the association between LC9 and MAFLD remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between LC9 and MAFLD and to explore the statistical indirect association through ln(CALLY).
METHODS: Data were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) conducted between 2005 and 2016. Weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling, subgroup analysis, and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression were used to assess the relationship between LC9 and MAFLD. Exploratory mediation analysis was performed to evaluate the statistical indirect association through ln(CALLY). Sensitivity and supplementary analyses were conducted to assess the robustness of the findings with respect to missing data, alternative disease definitions, definitional overlap, alternative cardiovascular health metrics, individual LC9 components, and mediator choice.
RESULTS: This study included 3841 participants. Higher LC9 scores were significantly associated with lower odds of prevalent MAFLD. Specifically, every 10-point increase in the LC9 score was associated with lower odds of MAFLD (OR = 0.51, 95% CI: 0.47-0.56, p < 0.001). Participants in the highest tertile of the LC9 score had lower odds of MAFLD (OR = 0.16, 95% CI: 0.12-0.22, p < 0.001) compared with those in the lowest tertile. Similarly, ln(CALLY) was inversely associated with MAFLD (OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.52-0.64, p < 0.001). Exploratory mediation analysis indicated that ln(CALLY) statistically accounted for approximately 17.7% of the LC9-MAFLD association (p < 0.001). Sensitivity and supplementary analyses showed that the association was attenuated but remained statistically significant after exclusion of overlapping metabolic components from LC9 (OR per 10-point increase in modified LC9 = 0.891, 95% CI: 0.832-0.955, p = 0.002) and remained materially consistent when MASLD was used as an alternative outcome (OR = 0.545, 95% CI: 0.494-0.602, p < 0.001). No significant indirect association was observed using PNI as an alternative mediator (p = 0.988). WQS analysis assigned relatively larger weights to BMI, blood glucose, and psychological health.
CONCLUSION: Higher LC9 scores were associated with lower odds of prevalent MAFLD. Exploratory mediation analysis suggested a statistical indirect association through ln(CALLY), although causal or temporal mediation cannot be inferred. Further prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Use of an AI metabolomics score to predict cardiovascular risk among patients with Psoriasis in the MGB and UK Biobanks.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic inflammation in psoriasis accelerates atherosclerosis and confers excess cardiovascular risk that is not fully captured by traditional clinical predictors. Metabolomic profiling may identify disease-specific metabolic signatures associated with cardiovascular events and enhance risk prediction beyond conventional factors.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether plasma metabolomic profiling improves cardiovascular risk prediction in patients with psoriasis and to develop and externally validate an artificial intelligence-driven metabolomic risk score (MetaPsoAI) for incident cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We analyzed 1086 individuals with psoriasis and no prior coronary artery disease from the Mass General Brigham (MGB) Biobank who underwent nuclear magnetic resonance-based quantification of 168 circulating metabolites. Associations between metabolites and incident all-cause death or myocardial infarction were assessed. An extreme gradient boosting algorithm was used to develop MetaPsoAI for prediction of myocardial infarction or stroke. External validation was performed in the UK Biobank (n = 274,000), stratified by psoriasis status.
RESULTS: Multiple metabolites, particularly HDL subfractions and amino acid metabolites, were associated with cardiovascular outcomes. MetaPsoAI stratified risk across quartiles, with individuals in the highest quartile demonstrating a 3.6-fold higher risk of myocardial infarction or stroke in the MGB cohort. In the UK Biobank, the highest quartile was associated with a 1.9-fold increased risk among psoriasis patients, with stronger effect sizes compared with non-psoriasis controls.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the potential of AI-driven metabolomics to refine cardiovascular risk prediction in immune-mediated diseases and enable precision prevention strategies for patients with psoriasis.

Title: Proteomic and metabolomic correlates of sociodemographic factors and their associations with kidney and cardiovascular outcomes: findings from the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort.
Ticagrelor versus prasugrel following PCI in acute coronary syndromes and high-risk coronary artery disease: A meta-analysis of one-year randomized trial outcomes.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend potent P2Y12 inhibitors over clopidogrel following percutaneous coronary intervention. Whether ticagrelor- or prasugrel-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) provides superior clinical outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain, particularly across acute coronary syndromes (ACS) and high-risk coronary artery disease (CAD) populations.
METHODS: We searched databases for randomized controlled trials comparing ticagrelor- and prasugrel-based DAPT in patients with CAD undergoing PCI with 1-year follow-up. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, stent thrombosis, and major bleeding. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses were performed in ACS populations.
RESULTS: Three trials randomized a total of 7048 patients. In the primary analysis, prasugrel-based therapy was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in MACE compared with ticagrelor-based therapy (HR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.67-1.03; p = 0.09). All-cause mortality (HR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.68-1.08; p = 0.20), cardiovascular death (HR = 0.93; 95% CI: 0.72-1.21; p = 0.60), myocardial infarction (HR = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.56-1.14; p = 0.22), stroke (HR = 1.04; 95% CI: 0.63-1.73; p = 0.87), stent thrombosis (HR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.45-1.11; p = 0.13), and major bleeding (HR = 0.89; 95% CI: 0.68-1.17; p = 0.41) were comparable between strategies. ACS-restricted sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent findings across all outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ACS and high-risk CAD undergoing PCI, current randomized evidence does not establish conclusive superiority between ticagrelor- and prasugrel-based DAPT for 1-year ischemic or bleeding endpoints.

Title: Cardiometabolic Risk Factors, Obesity Phenotypes, and Novel Anthropometric Indices in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Hospital-Based Case-Control Study in Central India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is the most severe manifestation of cardiovascular disease and disproportionately affects South Asians at a younger age than Western populations. Body mass index (BMI) inadequately reflects visceral adiposity, particularly in Indian populations. Obesity phenotypes, which combine BMI with metabolic status, and novel anthropometric indices may improve cardiovascular risk assessment, but data from Indian ACS patients remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between cardiometabolic risk factors, obesity phenotypes, and novel anthropometric indices with ACS, and to quantify these associations using odds ratios (ORs).
METHODS: This case-control study enrolled 50 patients with confirmed ACS (unstable angina, Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), or ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)) and 50 age-, sex-, and weight-matched healthy controls at a tertiary care hospital. Sociodemographic, clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical data were recorded. Participants were classified into four obesity phenotypes - metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), metabolically healthy overweight/obese (MHO), and metabolically unhealthy overweight/obese (MUO) - based on BMI and presence of hypertension, diabetes, and/or dyslipidemia. Five novel indices were calculated: A body shape index (ABSI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and abdominal volume index (AVI). Continuous variables were compared using t-tests and categorical variables using chi-square/Fisher's exact test; unadjusted ORs with 95% CIs were calculated. p<0.05 was significant. ST-elevation myocardial infarction Results: Cases and controls were comparable for age and sex (p>0.05). Hypertension (60% vs 36%), diabetes (52% vs 28%), dyslipidemia (56% vs 32%), and smoking (44% vs 24%) were more common among cases (all p<0.05). Per 1-SD increase, BMI was not significantly associated with ACS (Exp(B) 1.208, 95% CI 0.816-1.790, Wald 0.89, p=0.345), whereas waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and neck circumference were each significantly associated with ACS. Each of the five novel indices was significantly associated with ACS per 1-SD increase (all p<0.001; e.g., WHtR Exp(B) 2.473, 95% CI 1.638-3.732, Wald 18.59); because each index reflects a different geometric construct even when expressed per 1-SD, indices are not ranked by strength of association. Using MHNW as reference, MUO showed significantly increased odds of ACS (OR 3.33, 95% CI 1.10-10.12); MUNW showed a similar point estimate (OR 3.33, 95% CI 0.89-12.49) that did not reach significance (p=0.074), and MHO was not significantly associated with ACS (OR 1.50, 95% CI 0.48-4.65). All ORs are unadjusted.
CONCLUSION: In this unadjusted, cross-sectional comparison, metabolic health and central fat distribution were associated with ACS, whereas BMI was not. Obesity phenotyping and novel anthropometric indices warrant further evaluation in larger, multivariable-adjusted, prospective studies as potential adjuncts to cardiovascular risk stratification in South Asian populations.

Title: Indications and outcomes of ventricular assist devices in children and young adults with neuromuscular diseases: A systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) are frequently complicated by progressive cardiomyopathy leading to advanced heart failure. Ventricular assist device (VAD) implantation has emerged as a potential option in selected pediatric and young adult patients, but evidence on indications and outcomes is limited. We aimed to systematically review evidence on VAD implantation in children and young adults with NMDs, focusing on device strategies and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Systematic review following Cochrane methodology and reported per the PRISMA guidelines. Six major biomedical databases were searched from inception to October 1, 2025. Studies including patients aged ≤25 years with NMDs undergoing VAD implantation were eligible. The primary outcome was clinical status at last reported follow-up, classified as alive on device support, alive after heart transplantation (HT), or deceased.
RESULTS: Six retrospective studies comprising 37 patients were included. Duchenne muscular dystrophy was the most common diagnosis (48.6%). Destination therapy was the most frequently reported strategy (45.9%), followed by bridge-to-transplant (37.8%) and bridge-to-decision (16.2%). At last follow-up, 75.7% were alive: 43.2% on device support and 32.4% after undergoing HT; 24.3% had died. Complications were common, most frequently bleeding and infection, whereas neurologic events were the leading cause of death. Reporting of functional outcomes and quality of life was sparse and heterogeneous.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence on VAD use in this population is limited to small retrospective cohorts. Although most patients were alive at last reported follow-up, morbidity remains substantial and patient-centered outcomes are poorly characterized. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized outcome definitions are needed.

Title: Telerehabilitation vs. centre-based cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome: results of the pragmatic TELECOR randomized trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves cardiovascular outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but access remains suboptimal. Telerehabilitation may overcome barriers, yet evidence from real-world, public health systems is limited. This randomized controlled trial study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured telerehabilitation programme compared with standard centre-based CR in patients after ACS, focussing on cardiovascular risk factor control and lifestyle adherence.
METHODS AND RESULTS: TELECOR is a pragmatic, open-label, randomized trial conducted at a tertiary public hospital. Adults with recent ACS were randomized 1:1 to an 8 week structured telerehabilitation or a centre-based CR programme. The primary outcome was achievement of a composite target (≥4 of 7 predefined cardiovascular and lifestyle goals) at 8 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in functional capacity, medication adherence, quality of life, psychological status, satisfaction, and cardiovascular events at 6 months. A total of 129 patients were randomized (65 telerehabilitation, 64 centre-based). At 8 weeks, 86% of telerehabilitation vs. 79.7% of centre-based participants met the composite target (P = 0.37). At 6 months, this was 87% vs. 80.4% (P = 0.34). Both groups showed similar improvements in functional capacity (≈+1 metabolic equivalent of tasks), adherence (>84%), and satisfaction (>91/100). No between-group differences were observed in clinical events or psychological outcomes.
CONCLUSION: In a real-world public hospital setting, telerehabilitation was non-inferior to conventional CR in achieving cardiovascular risk factor control and improving functional capacity. These results support the broader integration of digital CR models into routine secondary prevention care.

Title: Differences in Office and Ambulatory Pulse Wave Analysis in Patients with White Coat Hypertension and Other Hypertension Phenotypes.
Journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Increased arterial stiffness is a sign of vascular damage; therefore, assessing it is crucial for evaluating cardiovascular risk. Arterial stiffness parameters such as pulse wave velocity (PWV) and augmentation index (at heart rate 75 bpm, AIX@75) were shown to correlate directly with blood pressure (BP).
AIM: Since these parameters may consequently be altered in patients with white coat effect (WCE), this study examined differences in office and 24h measurements of these parameters across various BP phenotypes.
METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, conducted between 2018 and 2023 at three nephrology clinics, office and 24h BP measurements and pulse wave analysis (PWA) of 208 patients were examined.
RESULTS: 189 patients were included; 48 were diagnosed with controlled hypertension (HTN), 63 with uncontrolled HTN, 22 with a masked HTN phenotype, 30 with WCE, of whom 11 had white coat HTN (WCH) and 19 had white coat uncontrolled HTN (WCUH), and 26 had normal BP. By definition, patients with WCE had significantly higher office peripheral and aortic BP than the respective 24h values (p<0.0001 each). Their AIX@75 was significantly higher on office (32.7±11.4%) than on 24h measurement (27.4±7.2%, p=0.0354), and they showed a significantly greater reduction in PWV between office and 24h measurement than normotensives and all other BP phenotypes (padj <0.0001 each).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with WCE, there are significant differences in arterial stiffness parameters between office and 24h measurements, suggesting that both measurement methods provide complementary hemodynamic information. Prospective studies are needed to determine the prognostic significance of these differences.

Title: Metabolic health is a stronger determinant than obesity for cardiovascular disease incidence: a meta-analysis of longitudinal cohort studies.
Abstract: Overweight and obesity are established risk factors for cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), yet heterogeneity in metabolic health among individuals with varied body mass index (BMI) complicates risk assessment. This systematic-review and meta-analysis of cohort studies investigated the risk of combined BMI-metabolic health phenotypes in relation to CVDs. PubMed and Scopus were searched up to January 2025. Metabolic phenotypes were defined as individuals with metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically healthy overweight (MHOW), metabolically healthy obesity (MHO), and their metabolically unhealthy counterparts, were analyzed for associations with CVD, coronary heart disease (CHD), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and heart failure (HF). Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95%confidence intervals (95% CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Fifty-one publications (44 studies) were included. Compared with MHNW individuals, individuals with metabolically unhealthy obesity exhibited significantly higher risks across all cardiovascular outcomes with HRs of 2.10 (1.85-2.40) for CVD, 1.97 (1.71-2.27) for CHD, 2.20 (1.75-2.76) for MI, 1.55 (1.38-1.78) for stroke, and 2.05 (1.65-2.54) for HF. There was a positive dose-response relationship between both higher BMI and poor metabolic health and risk of CVD, CHD, MI, and HF incidence, however, associations for metabolically unhealthy normal weight subjects often exceeded that of metabolically healthy obese subjects. For stroke, poor metabolic health appears to be a primary determinant of risk. In conclusion, worsening metabolic health and higher BMI independently associated with increased CVD, CHD, MI, and HF risk, with their combination posing the greatest risk, while stroke risk was mainly associated with metabolic health.

Title: Comparison of cardiovascular events in patients with metastatic hormone sensitive prostate cancer treated with LHRH agonists to LHRH antagonists in the US: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is standard treatment for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSCaP). Patients receive LHRH-agonists (LHRH-AG: leuprolide, goserelin or triptorelin) or LHRH-antagonists (LHRH-AN: degarelix or relugolix) with intensification with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors, with or without chemotherapy. Given ongoing concerns about cardiovascular risk, we used real-world data from TriNetX to compare the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) between patients receiving LHRH-AG vs. LHRH-AN.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included adult patients with mHSCaP who received either an LHRH-AG or LHRH-AN. The composite primary outcome was MACE (defined as myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, or all-cause mortality). Secondary outcomes were MI, stroke, and all-cause mortality. Patients were 1:1 propensity-score matched (PSM). Kaplan-Meier analysis reporting hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the outcomes was conducted. We conducted a subgroup analysis to assess the effect of intensification of therapy. Exploratory analyses were conducted to assess HR of outcomes and new-onset metabolic comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, insulin use, hypertension, and dyslipidemia) amongst patients without cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: Before PSM, there were 27,051 in LHRH-AG and 3,339 in LHRH-AN cohorts. After PSM, 3,329 patients in each cohort were compared. Compared to LHRH-AN, LHRH-AG was associated with a decreased risk of MACE (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.93), MI (HR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.66-0.97), and any-cause mortality (HR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.78-0.93). Treatment intensification did not modify the association between MACE outcomes and LHRH-AG vs. LHRH-AN.
CONCLUSIONS: Using real-world data, LHRH-AG was associated with a decreased risk of experiencing MACE. Among those undergoing intensification of therapy, there was no difference in MACE risk associated with LHRH-AG vs. LHRH-AN.

Title: The Association of the Systemic Oxygen Delivery to Oxygen Consumption Ratio With Mortality, Heart Transplantation, and Mechanical Circulatory Support.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify if the delivery of oxygen over consumption of oxygen (DO2/VO2) ratio is significantly associated with clinical outcomes such as mortality, need for heart transplantation, or need for a mechanical circulatory support device.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Medical and surgical cardiac intensive care units of the Mayo Clinic.
PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients (≥18 years old) admitted to the cardiothoracic surgical or cardiac intensive care units between January 2012 and December 2025 were included if they underwent invasive hemodynamic assessment with simultaneous arterial blood gas, mixed venous blood gas, hemoglobin, and mean arterial pressure. Patients were excluded if they had their venous oxygen saturations drawn from a central line or a peripherally inserted central catheter, as well as those admitted for sepsis/septic shock.
INTERVENTIONS: No interventions were performed on patients.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: DO2/VO2 demonstrated a nonlinear association with mortality. Using the median value of 4.73 as a reference point, patients with a DO2/VO2 value of ∼2 had the highest likelihood of mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis using a prespecified cut-point of 5 did not demonstrate any significant relationship with mortality, likely because of the underlying nonlinear relationship. There was no significant association between DO2/VO2 ratio and the need for mechanical circulatory support or heart transplantation.
CONCLUSIONS: DO₂/VO₂ is a marker of systemic oxygen balance that complements conventional hemodynamic indices. A categorical threshold of 5 did not show an association with clinical outcomes, but continuous analyses did suggest that a low DO₂/VO₂ may identify a high-risk phenotype.

Title: Continuous Bilateral Lower-Limb Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Monitoring in Patients on Intra-aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Prospective Feasibility and Physiology Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of continuous bilateral lower-limb near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitoring as an adjunct to standard hourly neurovascular assessment (NVA) in patients receiving intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, and to characterize the relationship between regional oxygen saturation (rSO₂) and in-hospital mortality.
DESIGN: Prospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: Cardiac care unit of a tertiary cardiac center (Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Singapore).
PARTICIPANTS: Fifty consecutive adult patients receiving IABP support via femoral arterial access.
INTERVENTIONS: Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring using NIRS was performed throughout IABP support, alongside standardized hourly NVA of both limbs (capillary refill time, skin color, temperature, pulse quality, and Doppler signal).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Right femoral access was used in 94% of patients (47 of 50). Minimum contralateral (left) rSO₂ was significantly lower in nonsurvivors than survivors (29.3% ± 17.6% v 43.3% ± 14.4%, p = 0.024), with a directionally similar but nonsignificant trend on the ipsilateral (right) side (p = 0.083). Regional oxygen saturation correlated moderately with capillary refill time (Spearman rank correlation [rs] ≈ 0.50) and pulse quality (rs ≈ 0.38) bilaterally but not with temperature change, which deteriorated in >92% of limbs. Low rSO₂ (<40%) in either limb was associated with a nonsignificant 3.16-fold increase in mortality odds (95% confidence interval, 0.55-18.11; p = 0.197). No patient developed acute limb ischemia. Sepsis (odds ratio [OR], 13.0) and renal replacement therapy (OR, 7.1) were the only statistically significant predictors of mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring is feasible throughout IABP support and produces a physiologically coherent signal that correlates moderately with objective NVA parameters and is lower in patients who do not survive to discharge. No limb ischemic events occurred; these findings are best regarded as feasibility and physiology data rather than evidence that continuous monitoring improves limb outcomes, and they warrant confirmation in a larger, multicenter study.

Title: Associations of multi-trajectories of smoking, alcohol use, and physical activity with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease risk in Korean adults: A nationwide matched case-control study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify multi-trajectories of smoking, alcohol use, and physical activity before diagnosis and examine their associations with overall and subtype-specific cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease risk.
METHODS: This matched case-control study used National Health Insurance Service data from South Korea for adults aged 30-69 years screened in 2015-2016. Cases had a first cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease admission during 2017-2022; controls were matched on sex, age, and insurance premium quantile. Six-year preindex trajectories of smoking, alcohol use, and physical activity were identified using group-based multi-trajectory modeling, with associations estimated by conditional logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 241,163 cases and 865,065 controls, five groups were identified. Compared with the Low-smoking inactive group, the Smoking-dominant and Heavy-smoking low-activity groups had higher odds of acute myocardial infarction (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.73, 1.88; OR 2.58, 95% CI 2.46, 2.70, respectively). The Alcohol-prominent group had higher odds of intracranial hemorrhage (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.12, 1.27), whereas the Low-smoking active group had lower odds of cerebral infarction (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.84, 0.92).
CONCLUSIONS: Multi-trajectory patterns of health behaviors identified a high-risk minority before diagnosis and revealed subtype-specific risk patterns. Screening-based behavioral information may support population-level risk stratification and targeted prevention.

Title: C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index and coronary microvascular dysfunction after primary percutaneous coronary intervention: The mediating role of insulin resistance.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index integrates systemic inflammation, nutritional status, and immune function. We investigated its association with angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR)-defined coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and performed an exploratory statistical mediation analysis involving estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR).
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study included 456 consecutive patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. AMR-defined CMD was prespecified as AMR ≥250 mmHg·s/m. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), and prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. Sensitivity and exploratory mediation analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: AMR-defined CMD was present in 228 patients (50.0%). In Model 3, each doubling of CALLY was associated with lower odds of AMR-defined CMD (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.80-0.94; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, Q3 and Q4 were associated with 44% (OR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97; P = 0.037) and 52% (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.28-0.84; P = 0.010) lower odds, respectively (P for trend = 0.018). RCS analysis showed an overall association (P = 0.001) without evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.310). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. Exploratory mediation analysis estimated that eGDR statistically accounted for 15.47% of the observed association.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher CALLY values were inversely associated with AMR-defined CMD after primary PCI for STEMI. eGDR may account for part of this association. CALLY may serve as an auxiliary marker for AMR-defined CMD risk stratification, pending prospective multicenter validation.

Title: Associations of PM2.5 components with dynamic and accelerated progression of different kidney function states and subsequent cardiovascular events: The GOLD-Health cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been associated with an increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, the relationships between specific PM2.5 components and the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory remain uncertain.
METHODS: Employing multistate and accelerated failure time (AFT) modeling in a prospective cohort of 307,639 participants, we examined the associations of 2-year exposure to PM2.5 and its components (sulfate [SO42-], nitrate [NO3-], ammonium [NH4+], organic matter [OM], and black carbon [BC]) with dynamic and accelerated progression from different kidney function categories (1-4, according to estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] and self-reported CKD) to CVD, and ultimately to cardiovascular death.
RESULTS: Over 1,058,210 person-years of follow-up, we documented 23,948 CVD cases and 7763 cardiovascular death cases. We observed that PM2.5 and its components were significantly associated with the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory, with SO42-, NO3-, and NH4+ exhibiting larger hazard ratios (HRs). Per-interquartile range (IQR) increments in SO42-, NO3-, and NH4+ were positively correlated with the transition from kidney function category 2 to 3, and the HRs were 1.273 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.257-1.289), 1.304 (95% CI: 1.290-1.317), and 1.280 (95% CI: 1.267-1.294), respectively. The AFT model indicated that higher levels of PM2.5 and its constituents significantly accelerated the dynamic cardiorenal trajectory. The predictive transition times from kidney function category 2 to 3 for 2-year NO3- exposure were 1727.43 days at 4.2 μg/m3 and 868.56 days at 7.0 μg/m3.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings revealed that PM2.5 components (2-year exposure) may be important risk factors for adverse cardiorenal outcomes.

Title: Nifedipine-modulated gut microbiota attenuates hypertensive vascular injury through Bifidobacterium-associated inosine-Adora2b signaling.
Abstract: Although antihypertensive drugs mitigate hypertensive vascular injury, their vascular benefits are not fully explained by blood pressure reduction alone. Many cardiovascular drugs reshape the gut microbiota, which in turn influences their vascular pharmacology. We therefore investigated whether gut microbiota remodeling contributes to nifedipine-mediated vascular protection in high-salt hypertensive rats and a pilot patient cohort. Combining 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, fecal microbiota transplantation, microbiota depletion, supplementation, and selective receptor antagonism, we found that nifedipine ameliorated gut dysbiosis. Transplantation of nifedipine-modulated microbiota improved intestinal barrier integrity and reduced vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, collagen deposition, and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching, while only marginally lowering blood pressure. Conversely, microbiota depletion markedly attenuated these vascular benefits despite preserving nifedipine-induced blood pressure lowering. These vascular benefits were associated with nifedipine-restored Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis 420 (B420) and increased inosine availability. Supplementation with either recapitulated major vascular protective effects of nifedipine without statistically significant changes in blood pressure. In hypertensive patients, nifedipine treatment was associated with higher intestinal B420 abundance and inosine levels. In vitro, inosine modulated macrophages in an Adora2b- and Rap1-dependent manner, with accompanying changes in cAMP and KLF4, ameliorating VSMC dysfunction via paracrine signaling. In vivo, systemic Adora2b antagonism attenuated the vascular protective effects of both inosine and B420. Together, our findings support a gut microbiota-dependent component of nifedipine-mediated vascular protection that extends beyond blood pressure lowering, involving B420, increased inosine availability, and Adora2b signaling. We also nominate B420 and inosine as candidate adjuncts to calcium channel blocker therapy.

Title: ECMO Weaning Blood Processing: A Scoping Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has been widely used for life support in severe refractory cardiac and respiratory failure. During ECMO weaning, the circuit usually retains 500-800 mL of residual blood. Direct discarding leads to blood loss, increased anemia, and higher allogeneic transfusion requirements, while appropriate autologous blood reinfusion can reduce transfusion risks and medical costs. However, evidence on blood processing strategies during ECMO weaning remains scattered, and no unified clinical guidelines exist.
METHODS: This scoping review strictly followed the PRISMA‑ScR 2018 checklist and JBI methodology. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang from inception to March 28, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed quality. Descriptive synthesis and qualitative analysis were performed due to high heterogeneity and lack of randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
RESULTS: A total of 68 articles were retrieved, and 9 studies were finally included. The identified blood processing strategies were classified into four categories: blood cell salvage system (BCS) autologous reinfusion, pump-controlled blood reinfusion, modified CPD blood bag storage reinfusion, and direct discard.
CONCLUSION: Based on current observational evidence, autologous blood reinfusion during ECMO weaning appears feasible and is associated with favorable surrogate hematological outcomes compared with direct discard. Identified strategies differ in indications, operation, and costs, and may be selected individually according to ECMO mode, hemodynamic status, and institutional conditions. Given the limited number, low quality, and high heterogeneity of included studies, no conclusions regarding hard clinical outcomes can be drawn. This review highlights the urgency of high‑quality studies with long‑term clinical endpoints to further verify efficacy and safety.

Title: Changing global prevalence of diuretic resistance amongst patients with heart failure: a systematic review and cumulative meta-analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diuretic resistance (DR) is a major challenge in the management of heart failure, contributing to persistent congestion, prolonged hospitalization, and adverse outcomes. However, inconsistent DR definitions and study designs have resulted in uncertain prevalence estimates and limited guideline development.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the pooled prevalence of DR in heart failure using studies with valid heart-failure denominators and extractable binary DR events, and to evaluate the stability and heterogeneity of prevalence estimates over time.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, Science Citation Index, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and the Database of Abstracts of Reviews of Effects were searched from 2000 through the final updated search in 2026, supplemented by reference screening.
STUDY SELECTION: Observational studies and randomized studies relevant to DR in adults with heart failure were considered for the systematic review. For the quantitative prevalence analysis, studies were required to include an unselected or consecutively assembled heart-failure denominator and an extractable binary DR event count based on a prespecified or study-defined criterion arising after cohort entry. Studies enrolling only patients with established DR, reporting only continuous diuretic-response measures, or lacking a valid binary DR numerator were excluded from prevalence pooling but could remain relevant to the qualitative systematic review. Two reviewers independently extracted data. Prevalence was pooled on the logit scale using an inverse-variance random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of between-study variance and Hartung-Knapp inference. Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, cumulative meta-analysis, influence and sensitivity analyses, a generalized linear mixed-model robustness analysis, and exploratory funnel-plot asymmetry testing were undertaken.
RESULTS: Twelve prevalence-eligible studies involving 24,904 patients were included in the quantitative prevalence analysis, of whom 4,861 met study-defined criteria for DR. The pooled prevalence was 23.0% (95% CI, 13.6%-36.2%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=98.5%; τ²=0.851; Q = 757.17, df=11; p < 0.001). The 95% prediction interval was 3.4%-71.6%. A generalized linear mixed model yielded a similar pooled prevalence of 22.5% (95% CI, 14.5%-33.2%). Cumulative analysis showed that the estimate changed as new eligible studies accrued, reaching 23.0% after inclusion of the most recent studies. Exploratory regression analysis did not demonstrate statistically significant funnel-plot asymmetry (p = 0.072).
CONCLUSION: Approximately one in four patients with heart failure meets a study-defined criterion for DR in prevalence-eligible cohorts. However, the very wide prediction interval and extreme heterogeneity show that DR frequency is strongly dependent on population, setting, timing of assessment, and operational definition. Standardized diagnostic criteria and prospectively assembled prevalence cohorts are required to improve comparability and guide clinical practice.

Title: Comparative effectiveness of turmeric and curcumin formulations on glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory markers in people with prediabetes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
Abstract: Prediabetes is a growing global health concern associated with higher risk of diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Curcumin has been studied for glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory effects, but comparative data across formulations remain limited. This network meta-analysis (NMA) evaluated turmeric and curcumin formulations in adults with prediabetes. Seven databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing turmeric/curcumin formulations with placebo. Primary outcomes included glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory markers. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. NMAs with surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) were performed. Twenty-four RCTs (25 publications, 1952 participants; mean baseline fasting blood sugar (FBS): 110.3 mg/dL) evaluating eight curcumin-based formulations were included. Turmeric extract combined with other compounds (EC) and turmeric extract (E) were associated with significant reductions in FBS with WMD -10.73 (95%CI: -14.22, -7.25;SUCRA 92.2%), and -10.57 (95%CI: -14.35, -6.79;91.5%;SUCRA 91.5%), respectively. E was associated with a significant reduction in HbA1c, while EC was associated with lower HOMA-IR with MWD -0.73 (95%CI: -1.41, -0.05; SUCRA 79.8%). Whole turmeric with other compounds (WC) was associated with a significant reduction in LDL-C (WMD: -37.19, 95%CI: -56.97, -17.42; SUCRA: 97.3%). E was associated with a lower risk of incident type 2 diabetes (RR= 0.05; 95%CI:0.00,0.78), although this estimate was based on low-certainty of evidence. No significant effects were observed for inflammatory markers. Overall certainty of evidence was low due to heterogeneity and short trial durations, and variability among combination formulations. In prediabetes, formulation-specific metabolic effects were observed. However, given the low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger, longer-term trials before clinical recommendation can be made.

Title: Plasma Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin levels and risk of future incident venous thromboembolism.
Journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although neutrophils are suggested to play a role in the pathogenesis of venous thromboembolism (VTE), no study has investigated whether neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a marker of neutrophil activation, is associated with future VTE risk in the general population.
AIM: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE.
METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007). Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for VTE according to quartiles of plasma NGAL adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, arterial cardiovascular disease, cancer, and C-reactive protein. Separate analyses with follow-up restricted to the first 2- and 5 years after cohort inclusion were conducted to investigate potential short-term associations.
RESULTS: We found no association between NGAL levels and risk of future VTE when analyzing the entire study period (OR for highest vs. lowest quartile of NGAL: 1.02, 95% CI: 0.70-1.51). However, when follow-up was restricted to 2 years, higher NGAL levels were associated with increased risk of future VTE (OR 3.87, 95% CI 1.15-13.03). The association was attenuated when follow-up was extended to 5 years (OR: 1.51, 95% CI: 0.82-2.80).
CONCLUSION: Higher plasma NGAL levels were associated with a transiently increased risk of future VTE.

Title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies.
AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE.
RESULTS: Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I2 = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I2 = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

Title: Prospective associations between empirical dietary inflammatory pattern score and cardiovascular diseases and cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Inflammation plays an important role in cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and cancer development, and dietary factors can modulate inflammation. Several studies have shown an association between Empirical Dietary Inflammatory Pattern (EDIP) and CVDs and cancer, but there are limited prospective studies in Asian populations. We aimed to prospectively investigate the association between the inflammatory potential of the diet, as measured by an EDIP score adapted to an Asian population (EDIP-A) and the risks of CVDs, cancer, and mortality from CVDs and cancer in a large multi-ethnic Asian cohort.
METHODS: We used data from the Multi-Ethnic Cohort (n = 10,640), a prospective study comprising ethnic Chinese, Malay, and Indian adults aged 21-65 years, recruited between 2004 and 2010. The EDIP-A score was calculated using a validated food-frequency questionnaire. Outcomes including incidence of nonfatal stroke, nonfatal acute myocardial infarction (AMI), CVDs mortality, cancer incidence and cancer mortality were ascertained through data linkage with national registries. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between the EDIP-A score and these outcomes.
RESULTS: During 887,505 person-years of follow-up, 435 nonfatal AMI cases, 317 nonfatal strokes, and 188 CVD deaths were documented. For cancer outcomes, 653 incident cases and 176 cancer deaths were recorded. Participants in the highest quintile of EDIP-A score had a higher risk of nonfatal stroke [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.64, 95 % CI 1.06, 2.55, P-trend = 0.01] than participants in the lowest quintile. These associations remained significant after further adjustment for body mass index. These associations were modified by smoking status (P-interaction <0.05). No significant associations were observed between EDIP-A score and risk of nonfatal AMI, CVD mortality, cancer incidence and cancer mortality.
CONCLUSION: Dietary patterns with a higher proinflammatory potential were associated with higher stroke risk, particularly among smokers. These findings suggest that reducing the inflammatory potential of the diet may be a promising strategy for prevention of CVDs.

Title: Supraclavicular artery island flap for head and neck reconstruction: Our experience and exploratory analysis of risk factors.
Journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The supraclavicular artery island flap (SCAIF) is being increasingly used for reconstruction of complex head and neck defects as an alternative to the traditional free flap or pedicled pectoralis flap. Here, we describe our experience with SCAIF for oncologic head and neck reconstruction and aim to identify patient factors associated with flap complications.
METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who underwent SCAIF reconstruction at a tertiary academic center was conducted between 2015 and 2023 (n=23). Collected variables included patient characteristics, operative parameters, and postoperative outcomes.
RESULTS: The mean patient age was 70.2 years. Six patients had a history of prior radiation, and 6 underwent ipsilateral neck dissection. Twelve patients received adjuvant radiation following flap transfer. Minor flap-related complications included delayed wound healing (n = 3) and partial flap necrosis (n = 6). One patient experienced total flap necrosis. Systemic complications included myocardial infarction (n = 2), pulmonary embolism (n = 1), atrial fibrillation (n = 1), and deep vein thrombosis (n = 1). Advanced age was associated with recipient-site complications (p = 0.018). Elevated body mass index was associated with systemic complications, longer ICU stays, and increased total hospital length of stay (p=0.036, p = 0.008, and p = 0.001, respectively). History of vascular disease and diabetes mellitus were associated with flap necrosis and delayed wound healing, respectively (p=0.025 and p=0.004). Longer operative time was associated with flap dehiscence (p=0.002).
CONCLUSION: SCAIF is a reliable and versatile reconstructive option for oncologic head and neck defects, including in previously operated or irradiated necks. Caution is warranted particularly in patients with diabetes or vascular disease, as vascular comorbidities appear to be more clinically precise risk factors than chronological age alone. Elevated body mass index also warrants consideration.

Title: Impact of clozapine on the proteome: A systematic review and functional analyses.
Abstract: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), yet its use is limited by potentially life-threatening adverse effects including myocarditis, agranulocytosis and pneumonia. Improved mechanistic understanding may facilitate safer prescribing. We conducted the first systematic review integrating proteomic findings associated with clozapine exposure. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase and Scopus were searched for clozapine-associated proteomic studies in animal, human and cell-based models. Differentially expressed proteins were mapped to Reactome pathways using the Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING). Using the same approach, analyses stratified all proteins by model type and replicated proteins by exposure duration and biological system. Replicated proteins were further analysed using QIAGEN Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA). Across studies, 1070 unique proteins changed following clozapine exposure (603 increased, 394 decreased, 73 discordant). Of these, 152 were identified in ≥2 studies, with 79 showing concordant directionality. Nine were replicated in ≥3 studies with consistent direction. Overall STRING analysis identified recurrent immune/inflammatory, cellular-stress and neuronal pathway enrichment, with stratified analyses providing partial support for these and related metabolic processes across model types, exposure duration and biological system. IPA highlighted necrosis-related processes and downstream disease effects involving cardiovascular, hepatic and renal systems. These findings suggest that immune, inflammatory and regulated cell-death pathways may contribute to clozapine-associated adverse effects, although their relationship to treatment response remains unknown. Limited time series data directly compare brain and peripheral blood changes. Prospective longitudinal proteomic studies during clozapine initiation are warranted to identify early biomarkers and intervention windows.

Title: Sleep-state transition instability with recurrent multisystem activation: A case-based phenotypic framework.
Abstract: The wake-to-sleep transition is a physiologically vulnerable period during which benign and pathologic motor phenomena may emerge. Current sleep nosology recognizes isolated hypnic jerks, propriospinal myoclonus at sleep onset, sleep-related rhythmic movement disorder, and other minor sleep-related motor activities, but these entities may not fully explain patients with persistent, repetitive motor activation recurring across successive attempts to fall asleep. We describe eight representative cases characterized by recurrent motor events centered on sleep onset or early sleep-state transitions, associated sensory and autonomic symptoms, clinically meaningful sleep fragmentation, and absence of a more satisfactory alternative diagnosis. On the basis of these observations, we introduce sleep-state transition instability with recurrent multisystem activation (SSTI-RMA) as a provisional, hypothesis-generating phenotypic construct rather than an established diagnostic entity. The recurring clinical pattern comprises recurrent motor activation during wake-to-sleep or early sleep transitions together with variable sensory, autonomic, cardiovascular, respiratory, or other non-motor manifestations, repetition or clustering of events, difficulty initiating or stabilizing sleep, clinically significant distress or impairment, and absence of a more satisfactory alternative explanation. We conceptualize the SSTI-RMA phenotype as a possible disorder of sleep-state instability rather than as an isolated motor phenomenon, potentially involving impaired coordination among neural, autonomic, and vascular processes during sleep entry. No validated polysomnographic signature, frequency threshold, biomarker, or prevalence estimate is currently available, and the relationship of this phenotype to severe or recurrent sleep starts remains unresolved. SSTI-RMA should therefore be regarded as a descriptive research framework intended to facilitate standardized phenotyping and prospective studies capable of determining whether it represents a distinct entity, part of a continuum of established sleep-onset phenomena, or a heterogeneous phenotype with multiple causes.

Title: From SCORE-Belgium to SCORE2: impact of successive guideline updates on cardiovascular risk categorization.
Abstract: Background: Successive European guideline updates have modified the estimation and categorisation of cardiovascular risk. The transition from the Belgian SCORE calibration to SCORE2 in 2021, followed by revision of SCORE2 thresholds in 2025, may substantially alter clinical interpretation without changes in individual patient characteristics.Methods: Adults aged 40-69 years in primary prevention were retrospectively included from two Belgian centres. Both cohorts were pooled into a single analytical population. Cardiovascular risk was assessed using the HDL-corrected SCORE-Belgium model (2019), SCORE2 (2021), and the updated SCORE2 thresholds (2025), applied to identical baseline data. Low and moderate categories were harmonised. Reclassification was analysed descriptively.Results: Among 413 individuals, 84.3% were classified as low-moderate risk with SCORE-Belgium, 11.6% as high risk, and 4.1% as very high risk. With SCORE2 (2021), 58.8% were categorised as high risk and 7.3% as very high risk. Application of the 2025 thresholds reversed this distribution: 93.5% were classified as low-moderate risk, 6.5% as high risk, and none as very high risk. These variations affected largely the same individuals and occurred despite identical underlying risk estimates.Conclusion: Guideline updates markedly influence cardiovascular risk categorisation in primary prevention.
