CONCLUSION: CagriSema produces clinically meaningful additional weight loss and modest improvements in surrogate cardiometabolic measures compared with semaglutide 2.4 mg alone, at the cost of more frequent injection-site reactions and, at most, modestly more frequent gastrointestinal events. The evidence is insufficient to determine whether serious adverse events or neoplasms differ between treatments, and long-term durability, cardiovascular outcomes and body composition remain undetermined.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261380458.

Title: Sex-specific clinical profiles in patients with acute ischemic stroke and chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common among patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and is associated with worse outcomes. Although sex-related differences in stroke are well recognized, it remains unclear whether clinical characteristics associated with sex differ according to CKD status. We characterized sex-associated clinical profiles among patients with AIS with and without documented CKD.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the PRISMA Health Stroke Registry. Baseline characteristics were compared between patients with and without documented CKD in the overall cohort and after stratification by sex. Multivariable logistic regression with backward likelihood-ratio selection was used to identify independent clinical characteristics associated with documented CKD in the overall cohort and with male sex within the CKD and non-CKD subgroups. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Internal stability was assessed using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Among 5,469 patients with AIS, 447 (8.2%) had documented CKD. Independent characteristics associated with CKD included prosthetic heart valve (OR, 3.73), elevated serum creatinine (OR, 2.79), obesity (OR, 2.51), heart failure (OR, 2.21), hypertension (OR, 2.20), African American race (OR, 2.11), and depression (OR, 1.97). In stratified analyses, associations of male sex with sleep apnea, smoking, and diastolic blood pressure ≥80 mmHg were numerically stronger in the CKD group than in the non-CKD group: sleep apnea, OR 4.62 vs. 2.38; smoking, OR 3.19 vs. 1.31; and diastolic blood pressure ≥80 mmHg, OR 2.58 vs. 1.43. However, formal interaction testing did not demonstrate statistically significant effect modification by CKD status. The sex-association model among patients with CKD demonstrated greater apparent discrimination than the corresponding non-CKD model (AUC, 0.785 vs. 0.630).
CONCLUSION: Patients with AIS demonstrated distinct sex-associated clinical profiles according to CKD status. Although several associations were numerically stronger among patients with CKD, formal interaction testing did not establish statistically significant effect modification. These findings characterize clinical heterogeneity among men and women with established AIS and warrant further investigation to determine whether these profiles have implications for treatment or outcomes.

Title: Association of Sex and Other Demographic Characteristics With Hemoglobin A1c in Older Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Cross-Sectional Analysis of the U.S. Premier Healthcare Database.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In type 1 diabetes, results for hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) sex-based differences are mixed, with limited data in later ages. The study objective was to determine whether female sex is independently associated with higher HbA1c in the U.S. older adult population.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was performed on real-world data from the Premier Healthcare Database from January 2020 to December 2022 examining adults with type 1 diabetes, ages 55-75 years. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were used to determine demographic variables independently associated with HbA1c. Predictor variables included age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance payor, testing location, marital status, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
RESULTS: Of 12,088 individuals with HbA1c data (52.4% women, mean age 64.7 ± 5.8 years), HbA1c was 0.13% (95% CI 0.08, 0.18; P < 0.001) higher on average in women and 0.81-0.97% higher in Black patients, adjusting for all other variables. Female sex (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.13; 95% CI 1.05, 1.21; P < 0.001; adjusted OR [aOR] 1.16; 95% CI 1.07, 1.26; P < 0.001), Black compared with White race (aOR 1.78; 95% CI 1.49, 2.12; P < 0.001), and Medicaid compared with Managed Care payor (aOR 1.63; 95% CI 1.28, 2.07; P < 0.001) were independently associated with increased odds of HbA1c above target, ≥7% for ages 55-64 years and ≥8.5% for ages ≥65 years.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort with type 1 diabetes, women experienced slightly higher HbA1c and higher odds of HbA1c above recommendations. Individuals with Black race and Medicaid insurance payor experienced clinically significantly higher HbA1c levels. Further interventions to address HbA1c disparities are needed.

Title: Effectiveness of Nursing Interventions on Stress and Functional Capacity Among Patients After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) frequently experience psychological stress and reduced functional capacity during the postoperative period. This randomized controlled trial assessed the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions on stress and functional capacity in post-CABG patients.
METHODS: A prospective parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in North India. Two hundred adult CABG patients were randomized to receive either nurse-led interventions (educational booklet, visual CD, and face-to-face counseling) or routine postoperative care. Stress was assessed using the Depression Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21) stress subscale, and functional capacity using the Duke Activity Status Index (DASI) and metabolic equivalents (METs). Assessments were performed at baseline, one week, one month, and three months. Data were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U test, chi-square test, effect sizes, and linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Baseline stress and functional scores were comparable between the two groups. At one week, one month, and three months, patients in the intervention group demonstrated significantly lower stress, depression, and anxiety scores than those in the control group (p ≤ 0.001). However, at three months, the intervention group demonstrated significantly greater functional capacity than the control group (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The nurse-led interventions significantly improved psychological outcomes and functional recovery during the postoperative period in the post-CABG patients.

Title: Association of the Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet Score with Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Mortality in Patients Underwent Coronary Angiography: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a frequent complication in patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG), which can cause deterioration of renal function and adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to explore the relationships between the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score and CA-AKI risk, as well as all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients undergoing CAG.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing CAG, including those receiving concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and stratified them according to the quartiles of the HALP score. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between HALP score and CA-AKI, and the Cox regression model was adopted to evaluate the relationship between HALP score and mortality.
RESULTS: This study included 42554 patients undergoing CAG. Among these, 5130 patients (12.1%) experienced CA-AKI. HALP score showed a significant inverse association with CA-AKI, with lower HALP score linked to higher CA-AKI risk. After adjusting for all the potential confounding variables, participants in the highest quartile of HALP score had the lowest risk of CA-AKI (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.73-0.90, p < 0.001). In Cox regression models, patients undergoing CAG with the highest HALP score exhibited the lowest risks of all-cause mortality (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.60-0.70, p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality. (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.58-0.73, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The HALP score was independently associated with CA-AKI, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality among patients undergoing CAG.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Inter-vessel heterogeneity in coronary microvascular dysfunction: A three-vessel physiological assessment.
Journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is typically assessed in the left anterior descending artery (LAD); however, inter-vessel differences involving the left circumflex (LCX) and right coronary arteries (RCA) remain unclear. We investigated inter-vessel variations in CMD and their associations with patient characteristics.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 91 patients (overall cohort) to evaluate patient characteristics across different coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) phenotypes based on physiological cutoffs: isolated CFR impairment, isolated IMR impairment, and combined impairment. Additionally, in a subgroup of 34 patients who successfully underwent physiological assessments in all three major coronary arteries (three-vessel cohort), we compared the CMD diagnostic rates between LAD-only and three-vessel assessments and evaluated vessel-specific correlations between CFR and IMR. In the Overall cohort, analysis of vessel-specific phenotypes revealed that patients with isolated IMR impairment in the LAD had a significantly higher body mass index (26.4 ± 4.90 kg/m2, p = 0.038). In the RCA, patients with isolated CFR impairment were significantly older (77.0 ± 9.18 years, p = 0.044). In the three-vessel cohort, the CMD diagnostic rate was significantly higher with a three-vessel assessment than with an LAD-only assessment (52.9% vs. 23.5%, p = 0.044). Furthermore, a significant inverse correlation between CFR and IMR was observed only in the LCX (r = -0.326, p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary microvascular physiology varies across the LAD, LCX, and RCA, indicating that conventional LAD-only assessments may underestimate CMD burden. These preliminary retrospective findings require validation in prospective, multicenter studies before routine clinical adoption.

Title: Beyond Prognosis: A Systematic Review of the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Modifiable Cardiovascular Biomarker.
Abstract: The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an accessible marker of systemic inflammatory activity associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but whether it is modifiable through intervention and whether its reduction corresponds to cardiovascular benefit remain uncertain. This systematic review evaluated randomized evidence concerning the effects of pharmacological, nutritional, lifestyle, and procedural interventions on NLR among adults with established cardiovascular disease or elevated cardiovascular risk. MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched for studies published from January 1, 2021, through July 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, randomized crossover trials, and secondary analyses of randomized trials reporting treatment-related changes in NLR. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidance. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, its crossover adaptation, and the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool, where appropriate. Twelve studies involving 1,741 participants were included and synthesized narratively. Direct interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibition produced the clearest dose-dependent reduction in NLR, while glutathione, cardiac rehabilitation, time-restricted eating, curcumin, normobaric hyperoxia, and selected nutritional strategies also demonstrated potentially favorable effects. Findings for sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors were inconsistent, with early empagliflozin initiation modulating inflammatory activity in one trial but producing no treatment-specific reduction in NLR during post-infarction recovery in another. Several studies associated lower inflammatory activity with improved ventricular function, global longitudinal strain (GLS), coronary plaque behavior, infarct volume, or neurological severity; however, few formally examined whether NLR independently predicted or mediated these effects. Clinical cardiovascular outcomes were infrequently reported and generally underpowered. Methodological limitations included small sample sizes, heterogeneous measurement schedules, post hoc analyses, multiple biomarker comparisons, and incomplete reporting of NLR outcomes. NLR appears to be a modifiable, context-dependent inflammatory marker, but current randomized evidence does not establish it as a therapeutic target or validated surrogate for cardiovascular benefit. Future trials should prespecify serial NLR assessments and determine whether phenotype-specific changes provide incremental prognostic or treatment monitoring value.

Title: Mast cell activation syndromes in clinical practice: diagnostic challenges, phenotypes, and real-life management.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) is characterized by recurrent, systemic episodes of mast cell mediator release, often resembling anaphylaxis and involving multiple organ systems.
AIM: To describe clinical, laboratory, and therapeutic characteristics of patients with non-clonal mast cell activation syndromes in a real-life cohort.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 21 adult patients fulfilling criteria for non-clonal mast cell activation syndromes, evaluated between 2015 and 2025 at a tertiary allergy and immunology centre in Istanbul, Türkiye. Demographic features, clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, and treatment responses were analysed.
RESULTS: Eighteen (85.7%) patients were female, with a mean age of 50.1 years. All experienced recurrent acute cutaneous symptoms, with gastrointestinal (42.9%), cardiovascular (61.9%), and respiratory (76.2%) involvement. Baseline serum tryptase levels were normal or mildly elevated, and all patients demonstrated an event-related "20% + 2 ng/ml" increase during follow-up. KIT D816V mutation was negative in peripheral blood in all patients and in bone marrow in 6 evaluated cases. No aberrant mast cell immunophenotype was detected in those undergoing bone marrow assessment. Based on available evaluation, 6 patients were classified as consistent with idiopathic (non-clonal) MCAS, whereas the remaining patients had comorbidities suggestive of secondary MCAS.
CONCLUSIONS: Non-clonal mast cell activation syndromes remain diagnostically challenging and often require longitudinal evaluation. Omalizumab may serve as an effective adjunct therapy in patients with persistent symptoms. A phenotype-based approach is warranted.

Title: Immune and inflammatory features associated with pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related genes in HFpEF: a machine learning study.
Abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and myocardial fibrosis. Whether pyroptosis intersects with fibrotic remodeling in HFpEF remains uncertain. Two murine cardiac transcriptomic datasets were integrated after batch correction and intersected with curated pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related gene sets. Functional enrichment, univariate logistic regression, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used for feature selection. Complete separation in the ordinary three-gene logistic fit prompted refitting with Firth bias-reduced logistic regression. Performance was assessed by apparent area under the curve (AUC), stratified bootstrap optimism correction, and repeated nested cross-validation; the panel was re-estimated in a human left-ventricular dataset for exploratory replication. Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT) estimated immune-cell fractions, and expression was examined in a high-fat diet (HFD)/Nω-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester hydrochloride (L-NAME) murine model and whole blood from patients with HFpEF. Six candidates-Pparg, Ace2, Smad2, Lcn2, Ptpn11, and Sqstm1-were identified. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses linked them to SMAD binding, autolysosome/amphisome activity, cellular senescence, efferocytosis, and renin-angiotensin signaling. In the 45-sample discovery cohort, the fixed Pparg-Ptpn11-Ace2 Firth model had an apparent AUC of 1.0000; bootstrap correction yielded an AUC of 0.9971 (95% percentile interval, 0.9780-1.0000). Repeated nested cross-validation produced a mean out-of-fold AUC of 0.9286 (2.5%-97.5% percentile interval, 0.8726-0.9700), revealing additional feature-selection uncertainty. Re-estimation in the human dataset represented panel-level replication rather than validation of a locked cross-species model. No inferred immune-cell fraction differed between HFpEF and control after false-discovery-rate correction, although exploratory correlations were observed among deconvolved fractions and with Ptpn11 expression. HFD/L-NAME-treated mice developed diastolic dysfunction, reduced exercise capacity, pulmonary congestion, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and myocardial fibrosis despite preserved systolic function; myocardial Ptpn11, Pparg, and Ace2 transcripts and their proteins were reduced. In patients with HFpEF, whole-blood PTPN11 mRNA was lower than in controls and inversely associated with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and C-reactive protein; these unadjusted findings remain exploratory. The three-gene panel is hypothesis-generating rather than a stable diagnostic model; its transportability, selection stability, and clinical relevance require prospective validation.

Title: Comment on "Seasonal variation in outcomes of diabetic patients with acute myocardial infarction: A retrospective cohort study".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: Retinal Arterial Wall Reflectivity and Incident Cardiovascular Disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether retinal arterial wall reflectivity is associated with future cardiovascular disease (CVD) in a large community-based Japanese cohort.
DESIGN: Community-based cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 6264 adults from the Nagahama Study (baseline 2012-2016) without a history of CVD.
METHODS: Retinal arterial wall reflectivity was measured on peripapillary OCT images at baseline. Participants were followed for approximately 7 years, and incident CVD events, including stroke and coronary artery disease (CAD), were identified through medical records. Associations were evaluated using Fine-Gray competing risk models and expressed as subdistribution hazard ratios (SHRs). Retinal arterial caliber was included in multivariable analyses.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident CVD events, including stroke and CAD.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 6.7 years, 125 incident CVD events occurred. In the full cohort, retinal arterial wall reflectivity was not independently associated with CVD (SHR per 10 arbitrary units, 1.026; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.920-1.145). A continuous age-by-reflectivity interaction was observed (P = 0.029). In post hoc exploratory analyses among participants younger than 70 years, parsimonious models suggested possible associations with CVD (SHR, 1.173; 95% CI, 1.031-1.334) and stroke (SHR, 1.280; 95% CI, 1.088-1.506).
CONCLUSIONS: Retinal arterial wall reflectivity was not independently associated with incident CVD in the full cohort. Post hoc exploratory analyses among participants younger than 70 years suggested possible modest associations with CVD, particularly stroke-related outcomes. These findings suggest that retinal arterial wall reflectivity may reflect subclinical vascular alterations, but require external validation.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

Title: Case-control study on the association of angiotensin-converting enzyme gene I/D rs4646944 single nucleotide polymorphism and young-onset cryptogenic ischemic stroke in an Algerian cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Numerous studies have shown a link between the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and ischemic stroke. Cryptogenic ischemic stroke is the most commonly recorded form of ischemic stroke among young adults. The insertion/deletion (I/D) variant of ACE (rs4646994) has been linked to ischemic stroke.
OBJECTIVES: We examined the potential correlation between this single nucleotide polymorphism and cryptogenic ischemic stroke in young adults.
METHODS: This case-control study included 42 young adults (< 50 years of age) diagnosed with cryptogenic ischemic stroke according to the TOAST classification, along with 42 healthy controls from the general population. The vascular risk factors included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, smoking, and cardiovascular diseases. Genomic deoxyribonucleic acid was extracted, and the ACE rs4646994 polymorphism was examined using polymerase chain reaction.
RESULTS: Younger age (p = 0.004) and female sex (p = 0.007) were significantly connected to an increased risk of stroke, contrasting with typical stroke demographics. Hypertension (p = 0.002) and smoking (p = 0.04) emerged as important, modifiable risk factors. There was no notable distinction between patients and controls regarding the frequencies of alleles and genotypes of the ACE I/D single nucleotide polymorphism (p > 0.05). These results were not associated with cryptogenic ischemic stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: While aligning with the current literature, our results are constrained by the limited sample size, the case-control design, and the dependence on self-reported data, which could have led to bias. This genetic study of a population from eastern Algeria did not show a link between the ACEI/D single nucleotide polymorphism and cryptogenic ischemic stroke.

Title: Sinus arrest during right pulmonary vein isolation related to right sinus node artery injury: a case report.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: A 50-year-old man with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation received radiofrequency catheter ablation after electrical cardioversion. The second radiofrequency application on anterior antrum of the right superior pulmonary vein induced sinus arrest following a sinus cycle length prolongation. Sinus arrest persisted. Right ventricular pacing was required for 3 min until a sinus rhythm was restored. Preprocedural contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed that the ablation site was near the right sinus node artery (SNA). Retrospective analysis during catheter ablation confirmed a direct anatomical relationship between the ablation site and the right SNA. In the present case, rapid recovery without coronary intervention suggests a transient and reversible mechanism, such as SNA spasm. This case highlights the importance of preprocedural anatomical assessment of the SNA and performing ablation under sinus rhythm, which may facilitate early recognition of sinus node dysfunction and help prevent irreversible injury.
LEARNING OBJECTIVE: A right sinus node artery might be close to the right superior pulmonary vein and can be affected by right pulmonary vein isolation. In cases of persistent atrial fibrillation, performing ablation under sinus rhythm allows immediate recognition of sinus node dysfunction and may help prevent irreversible sinus node injury.

Title: Unrestricted drinking before procedural sedation using fasting cards: a prospective observational quality improvement study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: International guidelines recommend clear-liquid fasting for 2 hours before procedural sedation-but in practice, this fasting time is usually exceeded, often significantly. We aimed to align actual liquid fasting times with these guidelines by implementing ‟unrestricted drinking using fasting cards" for patients undergoing procedural sedation.
METHODS: In a prospective, observational, quality improvement study, we implemented ‟unrestricted drinking before procedural sedation using fasting cards" in 2 ‟Plan-Do-Study-Act" cycles. Our patient population included those scheduled for elective procedures with sedation in gastroenterology, pulmonary, and cardiology.
RESULTS: The introduction of ‟drink until called" and subsequent education, including fasting cards, increased the proportion of patients who were aware they could drink before sedation to 81%. The awareness about permission to drink before procedural sedation correlated with significantly shorter median (interquartile range) clear-liquid fasting times of 1.2 (0.7-2.5) hours than those who were not informed (11.3 [4.1-12.7] hours; P < .00001) and a greater median cumulative preoperative drinking volume on the day of sedation (300 [200-500] mL vs 50 [50-100] mL; P < .00001). In addition, patients informed about their drinking permission experienced less thirst (71.6% vs 42.1%; P < .05) and were more likely to take morning medication (72.8% vs 52.6%; P < .05).
CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate the importance of aligning clinical practice with established guidelines to improve patient safety and comfort. Future efforts should focus on overcoming institutional and cultural barriers to enable widespread adoption of such quality improvement measures.

Title: Cardiovascular risk factors at 24 months after risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy: a prospective controlled study from WHAM.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women at risk of ovarian cancer due to BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants are advised to undergo bilateral risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) prior to natural menopause. Epidemiologic evidence suggests that surgical menopause increases cardiovascular disease risk, but prospective data are limited. It is also unknown how timing of RRSO impacts cardiovascular risk and whether this risk is mitigated by menopausal hormone therapy (MHT). We aimed to prospectively measure cardiometabolic risk factors 24 months after premenopausal RRSO compared to age-matched women who retained their ovaries.
METHODS: Prospective observational study from baseline to 24 months in 104 RRSO women and 102 controls who retained their ovaries. At baseline and 24 months, blood pressure, body mass index (BMI), waist and hip circumference, fasting lipids, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), glucose, and insulin were measured, and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance was calculated. Analyses were performed using generalized estimating equations, adjusting for baseline age, smoking status, vasomotor symptoms, and height (for BMI).
FINDINGS: Baseline cardiometabolic phenotypes were similar between groups. At 24 months, there was no difference between groups in the rise in diastolic blood pressure of ≥5 mm Hg (adjusted odds ratio, 1.03; 95% confidence interval, 0.48 to 2.18). There was no evidence of a difference between groups in changes in BMI, waist circumference, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), non-HDL-C, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, hs-CRP, or markers of glucose metabolism at 24 months. After RRSO, 62% of women used MHT, but there was no difference in any measured cardiometabolic marker between MHT users and nonusers.
INTERPRETATION: Surgical menopause did not clearly impact cardiometabolic status at 24 months. Cardiometabolic risk markers did not appreciably differ between MHT users and nonusers.

Title: Modern Obesity Treatment: Efficacy, Safety, and Future Directions of GLP-1 (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1) and GIP (Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide) Receptor Agonists.
Abstract: Obesity is a chronic and heterogeneous disease associated with a substantial burden of metabolic, cardiovascular, hepatic, and renal complications. In recent years, incretin-based therapies have changed the pharmacological management of obesity by providing levels of weight reduction that were previously difficult to achieve with medical treatment alone. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the efficacy, safety, and broader clinical effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults with overweight or obesity. Relevant literature was identified through searches of major medical databases, with emphasis on randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, and pivotal phase 2 and phase 3 trials. Liraglutide established the role of GLP-1 receptor agonism in weight management, while semaglutide provided greater and more sustained weight reduction. Tirzepatide, a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, produced greater weight loss than semaglutide in direct comparative studies. Beyond weight reduction, incretin-based therapies have demonstrated favorable effects on glycemic control, cardiovascular risk, kidney outcomes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and quality of life. Gastrointestinal adverse effects, particularly nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, remain the most common limitations and are most prominent during dose escalation. Emerging multi-receptor and combination therapies, including retatrutide, CagriSema, MariTide, and amycretin, may further expand treatment options, although long-term efficacy and safety data remain limited. Overall, incretin-based therapies support a shift from weight-centered obesity treatment toward individualized, complication-oriented long-term care.

Title: Dietary intake and circulating levels of vitamins, antioxidants, and fatty acids in relation to coronary heart disease risk: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between vitamin, antioxidant, and fatty acid exposure and coronary heart disease (CHD) risk remain uncertain, and dose-response relationships are poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the overall and dose-response associations between dietary and circulating vitamin, antioxidant, and fatty acid levels and CHD risk from observational evidence.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published up to February 2, 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD420261380823). Eligible observational studies (case-control, cohort, cross-sectional) reporting associations between vitamin, antioxidant, or fatty acid levels and CHD risk were included. A total of 27 studies were analyzed. Categorical (highest vs. lowest) and dose-response analyses were performed, estimating pooled odds ratios (ORs), relative risks (RRs), and hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Twenty-seven observational studies were included. In categorical analyses, higher circulating 25(OH)D (pooled HR = 0.79, 95% CI = 0.74-0.85; I 2 = 1.4%, τ 2 = 0.0000) and carotenoids (pooled OR = 0.64, 95% CI = 0.46-0.91; I 2 = 0.0%, τ 2 = 0.0000) were inversely associated with CHD risk. In analyses per 1-SD increase in circulating fatty acid levels, linoleic acid was inversely associated with CHD risk (pooled OR = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.57-0.84; I 2 = 0.0%, τ 2 = 0.0000), whereas palmitic acid (pooled OR = 1.52, 95% CI = 1.23-1.89; I 2 = 0.0%, τ 2 = 0.0000) and dihomo-γ-linolenic acid (DGLA; pooled OR = 1.26, 95% CI = 1.05-1.52; I 2 = 0.0%, τ 2 = 0.0000) were positively associated with CHD risk. Several other exposure-specific estimates and most dose-response analyses were supported by only one or two studies and should therefore be interpreted cautiously.
CONCLUSION: In observational studies, selected dietary and circulating vitamin, antioxidant, and fatty acid exposures were associated with CHD risk. These associations do not establish causality or justify specific supplementation recommendations, and findings based on sparse data require confirmation in additional prospective studies.

Title: Probiotics and synbiotics as adjunctive therapies for heart failure: a systematic review with network and pairwise meta-analyses.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the use of probiotics and synbiotics as microbiome-directed adjunctive therapies for heart failure (HF), while explicitly determining whether any eligible prebiotic-only trials existed.
METHODS: We searched eight English- and Chinese-language databases from inception to 1 May 2026 and conducted expanded sensitivity searches in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science on 15 July 2026. Random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA) was used only for connected multi-node evidence; two-node evidence was analyzed pairwise. As placebo, usual care, and food comparators were not clinically exchangeable, comparator-stratified sensitivity analyses of direct evidence were conducted using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and Hartung-Knapp (HK) confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 12 randomized studies were included in the systematic review (14 reports); 11 contributed to at least one primary or sensitivity quantitative analysis, and 10 contributed to the primary analyses. The revision-stage search audit identified no additional eligible randomized trials and no eligible prebiotic-only trials. Across all the trial populations, 1,021 participants were randomized, 973 of whom were allocated to review-eligible arms. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) network included 7 studies and 539 participants in the analysis set; however, this network was star-shaped, had no closed loops, and depended on a combined comparator node. The exploratory NMA estimate for multi-strain bacterial probiotics versus the combined comparator was a mean difference (MD) of 2.13 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI] -0.10 to 4.35). The comparator-stratified sensitivity analysis for usual care yielded an MD of 1.83 percentage points (95% CI -2.33 to 5.98). All synthesized results were assessed as having either some concern or a high risk of bias. The effect estimates were generally imprecise, and the certainty of evidence was low or very low. Adverse event definitions and denominators were inconsistent.
CONCLUSION: The available evidence is sparse and affected by significant non-transitivity, risk of bias, and imprecision. Network comparisons and rankings should be considered hypothesis-generating; therefore, no probiotic or synbiotic adjunct can be recommended for routine HF management.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: CRD420261413595. Public URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261413595.

Title: Soluble guanylate cyclase modulation in heart failure and chronic kidney disease: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational boundaries.
Abstract: Heart failure (HF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) frequently coexist and amplify one another through hemodynamic, neurohormonal, inflammatory, oxidative, and microvascular mechanisms. Impaired nitric oxide (NO)-soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC)-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)-protein kinase G (PKG) signaling represents a biologically plausible component of this cardiorenal interaction. However, clinical translation of sGC modulation requires careful interpretation because sGC stimulators and activators preferentially engage distinct biochemical states of the enzyme, and available evidence remains heterogeneous across compounds, phenotypes, and endpoint domains. This narrative review integrates mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence for clinically evaluated sGC modulators, including vericiguat, riociguat, praliciguat, runcaciguat, avenciguat, and cinaciguat, with emphasis on HF-CKD translational relevance. Vericiguat demonstrated benefit in a specific population of clinically stabilized patients with symptomatic chronic HF, LVEF below 45%, and a recent worsening-HF event. In VICTORIA, the reduction in the composite endpoint of cardiovascular death or first HF hospitalization was primarily driven by fewer HF hospitalizations, with no statistically significant reduction in cardiovascular death alone. Conversely, the VICTOR trial was neutral for its primary endpoint in stable ambulatory HFrEF, and HFpEF studies of vericiguat or praliciguat did not improve their prespecified biomarker, health-status, or exercise endpoints. In CKD populations, runcaciguat and avenciguat have shown short-term albuminuria reductions, but these surrogate signals have not established durable kidney protection, including long-term preservation of eGFR or prevention of kidney failure. To contextualize heterogeneous evidence, we propose an evidence-interpretation framework incorporating HF phenotype and clinical state, CKD phenotype, putative sGC redox biology, and endpoint domain. This framework is intended for evidence interpretation and hypothesis generation rather than patient-level treatment selection; no validated clinical assay defines tissue sGC redox state, and no prospective treatment-by-biomarker interaction has established redox-guided selection. Future studies should prioritize phenotype-enriched HF-CKD populations, contemporary background therapy, and prespecified cardiovascular and kidney outcomes to define the clinical role of sGC modulation.

Title: The association of triglyceride-glucose body roundness index with carotid atherosclerosis in type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose body roundness index (TyG-BRI) has emerged as a promising biomarker correlated with elevated risks of adverse cardiovascular events. Notably, the potential linkage between TyG-BRI and carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) has not been formally evaluated in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study consecutively enrolled 1060 adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Fujian, China. Anthropometric measurements and fasting venous blood biochemical data were collected to calculate TyG-BRI. CAS was ascertained using high-resolution B-mode ultrasound. Spearman correlation analysis was performed to examine the correlations between TyG-BRI and metabolic indicators. Following stepwise adjustment for confounding variables, hierarchical binary logistic regression and restricted cubic spline curves were applied to evaluate the association of TyG-BRI with CAS risk as well as potential effect modifiers. Finally, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was conducted to evaluate the identification capability of TyG-BRI for CAS.
RESULTS: Patients with CAS had significantly higher TyG-BRI levels than non-CAS controls. TyG-BRI was positively correlated with carotid intima-media thickness, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), blood pressure, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and uric acid. In fully adjusted models, elevated TyG-BRI was non-linearly associated with higher CAS risk (P for overall association < 0.001, P for non-linearity < 0.01). Per 1-standard-deviation increment in TyG-BRI, the ORs were 1.503 (95% CI 1.281-1.763, P < 0.001) for carotid intima-media thickening, 1.453 (95% CI 1.236-1.709, P < 0.001) for carotid plaque, and 2.247 (95% CI 1.820-2.773, P < 0.001) for CAS. Associations remained consistent across subgroups stratified by age, sex, body mass index (BMI), HbA1c and hypertension, with a stronger effect in participants with BMI < 24 kg/m² (OR 4.838, 95% CI 3.007-7.784, P < 0.001). ROC analysis showed TyG-BRI significantly identified CAS (AUC = 0.698, 95% CI 0.664-0.731, P < 0.001), outperforming TyG and TyG-BMI while matching the performance of the composite indices of TyG combined with waist circumference or waist-to-height ratio.
CONCLUSION: TyG-BRI demonstrated an independent, non-linear dose-response association with CAS risk in type 2 diabetes. Its integration into cardiovascular risk stratification holds promise for enabling earlier identification of CAS.

Title: Joint Control of Inflammation, Cholesterol, and Lipoprotein(a) With Incident Cardiovascular Events in People With Type 2 Diabetes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to investigate the joint associations of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), LDL cholesterol (LDL-C), and lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] with cardiovascular disease (CVD) among patients with type 2 diabetes.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study identified patients with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank. Baseline hsCRP, LDL-C, and Lp(a) were dichotomized according to guideline-recommended target levels. Patients were followed for incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), total CVD (ASCVD plus heart failure), death, or study end. Competing risk models adjusted for important covariates were used.
RESULTS: There were 29,658 patients with type 2 diabetes who were followed for a median of 15 years. Those with all three biomarkers above target had significantly increased risks compared with those with all at target: fatal and nonfatal ASCVD (adjusted hazard ratio 1.59; 95% CI 1.24, 2.03) and total CVD (adjusted hazard ratio 1.44; 95% CI 1.13, 1.83). Cardiovascular risk increased progressively as fewer biomarkers achieved target levels (all P trend < 0.001), with stronger associations in patients with shorter diabetes duration (<2 years vs. ≥2 years).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated hsCRP, LDL-C, and Lp(a) showed dose-dependent associations with cardiovascular risk in patients with type 2 diabetes, supporting their control in cardiovascular risk prevention.

Title: Prasugrel Outperforms Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Real-World Analysis.
Abstract: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor is standard for patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet real-world comparisons of ticagrelor and prasugrel remain limited. We evaluated their relative effectiveness and safety using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (2010-2024). Adult ACS patients receiving prasugrel or ticagrelor within 24 h post-PCI were included. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and cerebral infarction; secondary endpoints included individual components, major bleeding, and repeat revascularization. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses assessing robustness. Among 14,895 matched pairs (n = 29,790) from 126,273 patients, prasugrel was associated with lower risk of the composite endpoint (HR 0.641; 95% CI 0.613-0.671), all-cause mortality (HR 0.557; 95% CI 0.487-0.637), and MI (HR 0.648; 95% CI 0.616-0.680), without increased bleeding (HR 0.945; 95% CI 0.824-1.084). Repeat revascularization was higher with prasugrel (HR 1.791; 95% CI 1.639-1.957). Effects were consistent across subgroups. In this real-world setting, prasugrel demonstrated superior effectiveness over ticagrelor in reducing mortality and ischemic events without increasing the risk of bleeding, although higher rates of repeat revascularization warrant further study. These findings support prasugrel as a potentially preferred P2Y12 inhibitor in selected ACS patients undergoing PCI.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Observational Study

Title: Dapagliflozin in phenotypically stratified HFpEF without myocardial fibrosis: the STADIA-HFpEF randomized crossover trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction(HFpEF) is characterized by increased diastolic left ventricular(LV) stiffness resulting from variable contributions of myocardial extracellular matrix(ECM) remodeling and titin-based cardiomyocyte stiffness. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors(SGLT2i) improved cardiomyocyte distensibility, inflammation, and oxidative stress in experimental and human HFpEF myocardium. We investigated whether dapagliflozin improves LV distensibility in phenotypically stratified HFpEF patients without significant myocardial fibrosis.
METHODS: STADIA-HFpEF was a 34-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. HFpEF patients underwent multi-level phenotypic stratification including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging to exclude structural cardiomyopathies and significant myocardial ECM remodeling. Participants were randomized to dapagliflozin 10 mg or placebo for two 13-week treatment periods separated by an 8-week washout.The co-primary endpoints were changes in E/e'/LV end-diastolic volume index(LVEDVi) and mean LV e', reflecting LV distensibility and relaxation. Secondary endpoints included echocardiographic variables, quality of life, 6-minute walk distance, and inflammatory biomarkers.
RESULTS: Between February 2020 and October 2022, 32 patients were randomized and 29 completed the study protocol. Median age was 73(68-76) years including 28 women(88%). Dapagliflozin did not significantly modify E/e'/LVEDVi compared with placebo 0.24 (0.20-0.32) to 0.26 (0.22-0.34) vs. 0.23 (0.22-0.29) to 0.25 (0.21-0.31); p=0.370 nor did it change mean LV e' 6.2 (5.6-7.5) to 6.2 (5.7-7.1) vs. 6.6 (5.6-7.4) to 6.7 (5.4-7.5); p=0.448. Most secondary outcomes were neutral. However, an isolated improvement in LA conduit strain and numerical reductions in inflammatory biomarkers were observed during dapagliflozin treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: In phenotypically stratified HFpEF patients without significant myocardial fibrosis, dapagliflozin did not improve LV distensibility or relaxation. An isolated improvement in LA conduit strain and numerical reductions in inflammatory biomarkers were observed; however, these exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.

Title: Post-Operative Acute Kidney Injury After Pediatric Heart Transplantation and Longitudinal Invasive Assessment of Cardiac Filling Pressures.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) has been associated with diastolic dysfunction in pre-clinical studies, but with limited evaluation in clinical settings. We sought to examine the association between post-operative AKI and diastolic function after pediatric heart transplantation.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective review of patients ≤ 21years undergoing first-time heart transplantation between May 2010-July 2023. AKI was defined and staged per the KDIGO creatinine criteria, with Stage 2 or 3 classified as severe. Right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) obtained from surveillance cardiac catheterizations in the first two years post-transplant were used to assess diastolic function. Linear mixed-effects models were used to compare hemodynamics between groups.
RESULTS: We included 101 patients, aged 0-20 years, median 4 years (IQR 0-13). Pre-transplant diagnosis was congenital heart disease (CHD) in 51 (50%) and cardiomyopathy in 50 (50%) patients. Post-operative AKI occurred in 29 (29%) patients; 16/29 had severe AKI. AKI was more common in patients with CHD than cardiomyopathy [20/29 (69%) vs. 9/29 (31%), p = 0.02]. On mixed-effects model analysis adjusting for pre-transplant diagnosis, ischemia time > 4 h, and time since transplantation, severe AKI was associated with higher filling pressures over the first 2 years post-transplant, including a 2.2 mmHg increase in RVEDP (95% CI 1.3-3.1; p < 0.0001) and a 1.8 mmHg increase in PCWP (95% CI 0.8-2.8; p = 0.0005).
CONCLUSIONS: Severe post-transplant AKI was independently associated with higher biventricular filling pressures, suggesting a clinically relevant kidney-heart interaction. Larger studies are needed to further define its mechanistic and clinical implications.

Title: Urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and clinical outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome: a focus on patients with impaired ejection fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the prognostic value of urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) normalized to creatinine in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), focusing on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 144 patients emergently admitted for ACS, with urinary NGAL measured 4-48 h postadmission. Primary and secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs), respectively. Optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoffs were determined using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Associations between urinary NGAL/creatinine and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: During a median 734.5-day follow-up, 8 deaths and 44 MACCE occurred. The optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoff for predicting MACCE was 20.85 ng/mg creatinine. All deaths occurred in the high NGAL/creatinine group (≥20.85), but mortality analyses were limited by statistical separation. High NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with MACCE (hazard ratio = 3.47, 95% confidence interval = 1.61-7.47) and remained associated with a higher event hazard after adjustment for age, brain natriuretic peptide, LVEF, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (adjusted hazard ratio = 2.75; P = 0.017). In subgroup analyses, the area under the curve for MACCE was numerically higher in patients with LVEF <50% than in those with LVEF ≥50% (0.753 vs. 0.581). Formal interaction testing in the Cox model, however, did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF category (P for interaction = 0.100).
CONCLUSION: Urinary NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with long-term MACCE in patients with ACS. Although subgroup analyses showed numerically different associations according to LVEF, formal interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF.

Title: Postpartum Blood Pressure After Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Subsequent Cardiovascular Disease: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
Journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between blood pressure values at 6 weeks postpartum and subsequent cardiovascular disease (CVD) over a 20-year period among women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.
SETTING: English primary and secondary care data, linked to cause-specific mortality records from 2000 to 2020.
POPULATION: A cohort of 39 934 women between 15 and 49 years of age at birth who had HDP, were registered with a general practitioner (GP) contributing to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), and eligible for linkage to hospital episode statistics (HES) data were included. We excluded 22 100 (55.3%) women with no blood pressure values recorded at 6 weeks postpartum.
METHODS: Primary analysis included multivariable Cox regression modelling (weighted by the inverse probability of having a severe HDP).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Validated composite outcome of 12 cardiovascular diseases.
RESULTS: The rate for incident cardiovascular events was 109 per 10 000 person-years; 794 (68%) of them occurred in women aged < 40 years. Women with abnormal blood pressure at 6 weeks postpartum had a higher risk of subsequent CVD than women with normal blood pressure: 10.9% vs. 5.4% - adjusted hazard ratio 1.96 (95% CI 1.51-2.54).
CONCLUSIONS: Less than half of women with HDP had a blood pressure record in their GP notes at 6 weeks postpartum. The absence of a record of normal blood pressure at this time point was associated with an increased risk for subsequent CVD The immediate postpartum period may be a crucial window in preventive care to improve women's health.

Title: Acute ischemic stroke despite NOAC therapy in atrial fibrillation: Clinical factors associated with AIS in a 2-center observational case-control study.
Abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) can occur in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF) despite treatment with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs). This study evaluated clinical, treatment-related, inflammatory, and echocardiographic factors associated with AIS in NOAC-treated patients with AF. This retrospective, 2-center case-control study included 322 patients with non-valvular AF who had received NOAC therapy for at least 3 months. Of these, 112 were hospitalized with AIS and 210 were outpatient controls without AIS at the study assessment. Group differences and factors associated with AIS were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. ROC analyses were exploratory. Patients with AIS were older than controls and more often had hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, prior stroke, and prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use. In the adjusted analysis, prior stroke (OR = 32.79), coronary artery disease (OR = 3.47), prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use (OR = 2.55), female sex (OR = 2.26), diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.99), and C-reactive protein (OR per mg/L = 1.10) were associated with AIS. HAS-BLED (area under the curve = 0.881, 95% CI = 0.844-0.918) and CHA2DS2-VASc (area under the curve = 0.840, 95% CI = 0.795-0.885) distinguished AIS cases from controls in exploratory ROC analyses. Among NOAC-treated patients with AF, prior stroke and cardiovascular comorbidities were strongly associated with AIS. Prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use was also associated with AIS. Inflammatory markers measured during acute stroke had limited additional value. Because this was a case-control study, the findings do not estimate stroke incidence or future stroke risk and require prospective validation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy: A comprehensive review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management.
Abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM) is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized cardiac complication of liver cirrhosis, characterized by impaired myocardial contractile reserve, diastolic dysfunction, and electrophysiological abnormalities. Despite its clinical significance, particularly in the setting of liver transplantation, CCM remains largely overlooked. We performed a narrative review of the literature on CCM published up to December 2025, covering pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, imaging modalities, biomarkers, and management strategies. Depending on the diagnostic criteria used, the prevalence of CCM ranges from 29% to 67.2%. Advanced imaging techniques, particularly global longitudinal strain and cardiac magnetic resonance, enable early detection of subclinical systolic dysfunction. A "toxic triangle" comprising systemic inflammation, metabolic derangements, and neurohormonal activation represents an integrated pathophysiological model that drives myocardial fibrosis and dysfunction. Beta-blockers and aldosterone antagonists remain mainstays of pharmacological management, while liver transplantation is currently the only definitive therapy. CCM is an underrecognized condition with substantial clinical implications. Standardized diagnostic criteria, validated biomarkers, and large-scale prospective studies are urgently needed to improve patient outcomes.

Title: Comparison analysis of the triglyceride-glucose index, triglyceride-glucose and frailty index in cardiovascular disease and mortality association among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based cohort study.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of excess mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Conventional risk assessment may not fully capture the metabolic abnormalities and physiological vulnerability associated with RA. We investigated whether the triglyceride-glucose-frailty index (TyG-FI), which combines a surrogate marker of insulin resistance with accumulated health deficits, was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among adults with RA. We analyzed 1090 adults with self-reported RA from 10 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 1999 and 2018. TyG-FI was calculated as the product of the triglyceride-glucose index and a 49-item deficit-accumulation frailty index. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association with prevalent CVD, whereas Cox proportional hazards regression was used to examine cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and discrimination analyses were conducted as secondary analyses. In the fully adjusted models, each 1-unit higher TyG-FI was associated with higher odds of prevalent CVD (odds ratio, 4.50; 95% confidence interval, 3.20-6.33) and a higher hazard of cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.77; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-2.70). The reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.80 for prevalent CVD and 0.81 for cardiovascular mortality in models incorporating TyG-FI, compared with 0.73 and 0.80, respectively, in models incorporating TyG. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a stronger association between TyG-FI and prevalent CVD among participants aged ≤65 years (P for interaction = .044). Higher TyG-FI was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among US adults with self-reported RA. TyG-FI may capture complementary metabolic and frailty-related information; however, its incremental predictive value, calibration, clinical utility, and external validity require further evaluation before clinical implementation.

Title: The effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on heart rate and physiological parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased sympathetic activity and an elevated cardiovascular risk. Noninvasive interventions targeting autonomic regulation may offer complementary therapeutic strategies.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial aimed to investigate the acute effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters of patients with OSA. Patients with polysomnography-confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 15 events/hour) were randomly assigned to an intervention group that received a standardized 16-minute multiregional fascial mobilization protocol or a control group that rested quietly in the supine position for the corresponding period without receiving manual or tactile intervention. The intervention targeted the cervical, thoracic, and abdominal regions, under controlled conditions. The primary outcomes included heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and peripheral oxygen saturation. Measurements were obtained at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and 5 and 15 minutes post-intervention.
RESULTS: A total of 95 male patients (mean age: 48.12 ± 10.21 years) completed the study. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups, except for heart rate. After adjustment for baseline heart rate using mixed analysis of covariance, no significant group × time interaction was observed for heart rate (P = .476, partial ηp2 = .008). Similarly, no significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, or peripheral oxygen saturation (all P > .05). Although significant time effects were observed for some physiological parameters, the magnitude of these effects varied across outcomes, and none was accompanied by a significant group × time interaction. Therefore, these temporal changes were not interpreted as intervention-specific effects. No adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSION: Heart rate changed significantly over time following the interventions; however, after adjustment for baseline heart rate, the pattern of change did not differ significantly between the fascial mobilization and control groups. Similarly, no significant between-group differences in changes over time were observed for blood pressure or oxygen saturation. These findings do not demonstrate a specific acute effect of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters assessed. Further studies using advanced measures of autonomic function and longer follow-up periods are warranted.

Title: Deaths involving chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and cardiac arrest in older US adults, 1999-2023: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract: National long-term trends and disparities in deaths in which both chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and cardiac arrest are recorded on death certificates are not well characterized. We used CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data (1999-2023) to identify US adults aged ≥ 65 years whose death certificates listed both COPD (ICD-10 J41-J44) and cardiac arrest (I46) as underlying or contributing causes. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization; the urbanization analysis was limited to 1999 to 2020 because those data were not available after 2020. Trends were analyzed using annual percentage changes (APCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); P < .05 was considered statistically significant. Among 7,18,280 deaths involving concurrent coding of COPD and cardiac arrest, AAMRs declined from 86.4 in 1999 to 52.5 in 2023. A significant decrease occurred from 1999 to 2006 (APC: -2.87; P = .01), followed by a plateau and a further decline from 2021 to 2023 (APC: -4.77; P < .001). Older men exhibited higher AAMRs than older women (86.8 vs 55.2). Non-Hispanic (NH) White individuals had the highest mortality (69.7), followed by NH Black/African American (64.3) and Hispanic/Latino (60.7) populations. The West region reported the highest AAMR (98.9). During 1999 to 2020, nonmetropolitan residents had higher AAMRs than metropolitan residents (70.8 vs 67.9). Population-level mortality records involving both COPD and cardiac arrest declined overall but remained heterogeneous across demographic and geographic strata. These findings describe concurrent coding on death certificates and do not establish that COPD increases the risk of cardiac arrest or causes the observed deaths.

Title: Association of Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) with long-term mortality in type 2 diabetes patients with coronary heart disease: A prospective national cohort study.
Abstract: Endothelial dysfunction is prevalent in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) with coronary heart disease (CHD), increasing cardiovascular risk. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) is a novel composite biomarker, yet its prognostic value in this comorbid population remains unclear. In this prospective cohort study, we analyzed 909 participants with T2DM and CHD from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999 to 2010, followed until 2019. EASIX was calculated using lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and platelet count. Multivariable Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing-risk models assessed associations between EASIX and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, respectively. Time-dependent C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement evaluated the incremental prognostic value of EASIX beyond established risk factors. During a median follow-up of 111 months, 617 all-cause and 251 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Higher EASIX levels were significantly associated with increased mortality risks. In fully adjusted models, the highest quartile had a hazard ratio of 1.93 (95% confidence interval = 1.48-2.50) for all-cause mortality and a subdistribution hazard ratio of 1.56 (95% confidence interval = 1.05-2.33) for cardiovascular mortality compared with the lowest quartile. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant nonlinear positive relationship. Adding EASIX to a base model (age, HbA1c, and estimated glomerular filtration rate) significantly improved the C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement for both outcomes (all P < .001). Elevated EASIX levels are independently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with T2DM and CHD. In this population, its inclusion in risk assessment protocols enhances the predictive value for long-term clinical outcomes.

Title: Causal effects of antihypertensive drugs on thyroid diseases: A trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization study.
Abstract: Thyroid disorders frequently coexist with cardiovascular disease, including hypertension, but whether long-term modulation of antihypertensive drug targets influences thyroid disease risk remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the associations of 7 antihypertensive drug-target classes with thyroid diseases in European and East Asian populations using a trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) framework. We performed a two-sample, trans-ancestry drug-target MR analysis of 7 antihypertensive target classes. Target-proximal single-nucleotide polymorphisms associated with systolic blood pressure (SBP) were used as genetic proxies. Estimates were scaled per 1-mm Hg genetically predicted increase in SBP; the putative effect of target inhibition that lowers SBP was therefore interpreted in the opposite direction. Summary statistics were obtained for 4 primary thyroid diseases, benign thyroid tumors where available, and 3 thyroid-related proteins in European and East Asian datasets. Hypertension was used as a positive-control outcome. Random-effects inverse-variance weighting was the primary method, with Wald ratio estimation for single-nucleotide polymorphism instruments and weighted-median, Cochran's Q, MR-Egger, and Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy RESidual Sum and Outlier analyses as sensitivity assessments. Within the European populace, genetic surrogates for β-blockers exhibit (odds ratio = 0.93; 95% confidence interval = 0.87-0.99) a close association with heightened susceptibility to thyroid carcinoma, whereas KCNH2 (1.15; 1.01-1.32) demonstrates an inverse correlation with thyroid cancer risk. Moreover, calcium channel blockers exhibit a conspicuous linkage with an elevated incidence of hyperthyroidism (0.97; 0.96-0.99) alongside a diminished likelihood of thyroid cancer (1.07; 1.03-1.10). CYP17A1 exerts a protective influence against hyperthyroidism (1.04; 10.1-1.07) and Graves disease (1.10; 1.05-1.16) but manifests a pathogenic effect concerning hypothyroidism (0.99; 0.97-1.00) and thyroid cancer (0.92; 0.86-0.98). Conversely, KCNJ11 demonstrates a proximate correlation between diminished hypothyroidism risk and augmented thyroid cancer susceptibility (0.83; 0.73-0.95). Analogous estimations were noted for CYP17A1 within the East Asian cohort. Genetically proxied perturbation of several antihypertensive drug targets was associated with thyroid disease risk, with CYP17A1 showing the broadest cross-ancestry pattern. These estimates reflect lifelong target-proximal genetic effects rather than the clinical effects of prescribed drugs and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending replication, pharmacoepidemiological studies, and randomized clinical trials.

Title: TyG-ABSI and TyG-WWI as insulin-resistance body shape markers of mortality in middle-aged and older adults within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework: A multi-cohort observational study with external survival-model validation.
Abstract: Insulin resistance, adiposity, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease are closely interconnected in middle-aged and older adults and are central to the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. Triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-related indices combine routine lipid, glucose, and anthropometric information, but their cross-population consistency and incremental prognostic value for mortality-risk assessment remain uncertain. We analyzed harmonized participant-level data from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), and Health and Retirement Study (HRS), with HRS used as a sensitivity cohort. Eligible participants were aged ≥ 50 years, had follow-up beyond baseline, available mortality status, and complete data for 7 TyG-related indices. Cohort-specific Cox models estimated associations of standardized TyG, TyG-body mass index, TyG-waist circumference, TyG-waist-to-height ratio, TyG-weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), TyG-a body shape index (ABSI), and TyG-body roundness index with all-cause mortality. Nonlinearity, proportional-hazards assumptions, sensitivity analyses, NHANES heart disease mortality, incremental prediction, and survival machine learning with external validation were further assessed. The primary analytic sample included 21,044 NHANES participants, 5454 ELSA participants, and 11,157 CHARLS participants, among whom 5566, 116, and 1393 deaths occurred during follow-up, respectively. The HRS sensitivity cohort included 4103 participants and 484 deaths. In fully adjusted Cox models, all 7 TyG-related indices were associated with higher all-cause mortality in NHANES, with the strongest associations observed for TyG-ABSI (hazard ratio [HR] 1.159, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.115-1.205) and TyG-WWI (HR 1.155, 95% CI 1.113-1.199). In CHARLS, TyG-ABSI was positively associated with mortality (HR 1.088, 95% CI 1.029-1.151), whereas estimates in ELSA were imprecise. In HRS sensitivity analyses, TyG-WWI and TyG-ABSI remained positively associated with mortality. Adding TyG-related indices to a clinical Cox prediction framework produced only minimal absolute gains in discrimination. The final TyG-ABSI extreme gradient boosting survival model yielded 5-year time-dependent area under the curves of 0.808 in the NHANES internal test set and 0.760 in CHARLS. A research-use web calculator was developed for 5-year and 8-year mortality-risk estimation. TyG-ABSI and TyG-WWI were the most consistent TyG-related body shape markers of all-cause mortality across international aging cohorts. Although TyG-ABSI supported externally validated survival prediction, its incremental predictive value beyond established clinical and CKM variables was limited. These findings suggest that TyG-related body shape indices may serve primarily as interpretable, low-cost CKM risk markers rather than standalone prediction tools.

Title: Online clinical readiness course enhanced knowledge and perceived confidence of trainees during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted medical education globally. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the International Emergency Medicine Education Project's online COVID-19 Clinical Readiness Course in enhancing participants' knowledge and perceived confidence in managing COVID-19.
METHODS: This is a prospective, mixed-methods study. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and post-course assessments and surveys, while qualitative feedback was gathered via open-ended responses at the end of the course. Non-parametric tests were used for statistical comparisons, and thematic analysis of qualitative data was performed using customized large language model tools with human review and triangulation.
RESULTS: A total of 703 participants from 72 countries enrolled, 644 (91.6%) completed the knowledge assessments, and 510 (72.5%) completed the exit surveys. The majority (77.2%) were medical trainees, and 51.4% were from low- and lower-middle-income countries. The median score increased from 60 to 92 (p < 0.001) post-course. Perceived confidence in managing key clinical scenarios, including hypoxia, early symptoms, airway problems, sepsis, and cardiac arrest, also increased significantly (p < 0.001). Participants reported that the course met their expectations, with a median (IQR) score of 9 (8-10). Qualitative feedback revealed high satisfaction and highlighted areas for improvement.
CONCLUSION: The online Clinical Readiness Course significantly improved knowledge and perceived confidence in COVID-19 management among medical trainees worldwide. Scalable online education may help address training gaps during public health emergencies and support global medical education.

Title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Cardiovascular and All-Cause Mortality Among U.S. Women with Breast Cancer: a National NHANES Analysis.
Journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular complications are an important and increasingly recognized concern among women with breast cancer. Racial and ethnic differences in cardiovascular disease burden suggest that certain populations may be at heightened risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This study examined racial differences in cardiovascular outcomes and mortality among women with breast cancer using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of 669 women with self-reported breast cancer identified in NHANES and linked to the National Death Index. Participants were categorized by race and ethnicity as Non-Hispanic White, Non-Hispanic Black, Mexican American, Other Hispanic, or Other Race. Heart failure prevalence was evaluated as a clinically relevant cardiovascular outcome. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause and cardiovascular-specific mortality, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and forest plots were generated to visualize differences across groups.
RESULTS: Non-Hispanic Black women demonstrated the highest prevalence of cardiovascular disease, including heart failure (8.2%), compared with Non-Hispanic White (7.4%), Other Race (6.1%), Other Hispanic (2.2%), and Mexican American women (1.7%). Non-Hispanic Black women showed a trend toward poorer survival outcomes, with an elevated risk of all-cause mortality (HR 1.80; 95% CI: 0.96-3.36) compared with Mexican American women. After multivariable adjustment, this association persisted (HR 1.81; 95% CI: 0.96-3.41). Cardiovascular-specific mortality was higher among Non-Hispanic Black women, reaching statistical significance in the fully adjusted model (adjusted HR 3.46; 95% CI: 1.66-7.24).
CONCLUSION: Racial differences in cardiovascular outcomes and mortality were observed among women with breast cancer, with Non-Hispanic Black women experiencing a higher burden. These findings highlight the need for targeted, evidence-based strategies to address cardiovascular risk and improve equitable outcomes in this population.

Title: Planned Antihypertensive Deprescribing in Long-Term Care Residents: A Systematic Review of Randomized Evidence.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence supporting antihypertensive treatment in older adults is derived largely from populations that differ from long-term care residents, in whom frailty, dementia, multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and competing clinical priorities may alter the balance between preventive benefit and treatment burden.
OBJECTIVES: The aim was to synthesize randomized evidence on planned antihypertensive deprescribing in institutional long-term care and determine whether clinically and methodologically comparable effects support a common treatment-effect estimate.
METHODS: Randomized or cluster-randomized studies of planned antihypertensive deprescribing in long-term care were systematically reviewed. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, CINAHL Complete, Web of Science Core Collection, trial registries, and PROSPERO were searched from inception and updated to 20 August 2026. Meta-analysis was reserved for outcomes with at least two clinically and methodologically compatible estimates of a common, interpretable effect; otherwise, structured study-level synthesis was used. Result-specific risk of bias was assessed with the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2), and certainty with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) tool.
RESULTS: Three randomized long-term care studies involving 1548 residents were included. Their populations, deprescribing strategies, monitoring, restart criteria, and follow-up differed substantially, and no outcome was considered sufficiently clinically and methodologically comparable for meta-analysis. RETREAT-FRAIL reported an adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause mortality of 1.02 (95% confidence interval 0.86-1.21) over a median potential follow-up of 38.4 months, whereas DANTON reported an HR of 1.65 (0.95-2.85) to 32 weeks; Gulla/COSMOS had no cluster-adjusted comparative mortality estimate. At 16 weeks in DANTON, deprescribing increased systolic blood pressure by 11.0 mmHg (5.6-16.4), increased diastolic blood pressure by 4.6 mmHg (1.1-8.1), and reduced the number of antihypertensive drugs by 1.2 (1.0-1.4). Evidence for hospitalization, falls, cardiovascular events, cognition, function, and quality of life remained sparse, outcome-specific, or at risk of bias.
CONCLUSIONS: Randomized evidence for antihypertensive deprescribing in long-term care remains sparse and clinically heterogeneous. Within individual trials, supervised deprescribing reduced antihypertensive exposure and raised blood pressure, but the magnitude and clinical consequences varied by strategy and follow-up. Current evidence does not establish a common effect on mortality, hospitalization, or other resident-important outcomes, making trial-specific estimates and deprescribing protocols more informative than a single pooled treatment effect.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261370802.

Title: Impact of matched samples on domain harmonization in cross-cohort NMR metabolomics.
Journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Machine learning models trained on metabolomics data frequently show reduced performance when applied to independent cohorts because of domain shifts introduced by differences in analytical platforms, sample handling, storage conditions, and metabolite quantification procedures. Robust approaches for harmonizing metabolomics datasets across cohorts are therefore needed to improve model transferability and reproducibility.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of matched samples on domain harmonization and cross-cohort prediction performance in NMR metabolomics data, and to compare multiple harmonization strategies for improving model generalization across independently acquired datasets.
METHODS: A machine-learning framework was developed to classify ICD-10 code I50.9 (unspecified heart failure) using plasma NMR metabolomics data from the Estonian Biobank. Models were trained on a source dataset comprising 12,000 samples measured at Nightingale Health and evaluated on an independently measured destination dataset of 295 samples acquired on a different NMR platform. Harmonization approaches included within-domain normalization, Optimal Transport, Bridge mapping, and Empirical Bayes correction.
