Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.
METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.
RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).
CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

Title: Arrhythmias in patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and the impact of contemporary disease-modifying therapies.
Abstract: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is an increasingly recognized infiltrative cardiomyopathy characterized by extracellular deposition of misfolded transthyretin fibrils, leading to progressive myocardial stiffening, electrical remodeling, and conduction-system disease. These pathophysiological changes create a complex arrhythmic substrate, resulting in a high burden of atrial, bradyarrhythmia, and ventricular arrhythmias that significantly contribute to morbidity and mortality. Despite advances in disease recognition, the optimal management of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM remains challenging, with limited evidence guiding antiarrhythmic strategies and device therapy. In particular, the prognostic significance of ventricular arrhythmias and the role of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) remain controversial. Recent disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), including transthyretin stabilizers (tafamidis, diflunisal) and gene-silencing agents (patisiran, vutrisiran), have transformed the therapeutic landscape and may modify disease progression and arrhythmic burden, although their direct antiarrhythmic impact is not yet fully defined. This narrative review provides a structured overview of the mechanisms, epidemiology, and clinical management of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM, with a focus on clinically relevant decision-making and the potential influence of contemporary DMTs. Finally, it highlights key unresolved questions and areas requiring further prospective research.

Title: Polyvascular disease by systematic vascular screening and adverse outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic significance of systematically screened extra-coronary vascular disease in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains incompletely understood. We investigated the prevalence and prognostic impact of polyvascular disease (PVD) identified using a routine vascular screening strategy in patients with AMI.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center observational study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement and carotid ultrasonography were routinely performed during index hospitalization. PVD was defined as the presence of peripheral artery disease (ABI ≤ 0.90) and/or carotid artery disease, defined as carotid plaque according to the Mannheim consensus (maximal wall thickness ≥ 1.5 mm) or ≥50% carotid stenosis. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and unplanned coronary revascularization after discharge.
RESULTS: Among 233 eligible patients, PVD was identified in 73 patients (31.3%), including 55 (23.6%) with single-territory PVD and 18 (7.7%) with multiterritory PVD. During a median follow-up of 419 days, the primary endpoint occurred in 43 patients. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a graded decrease in event-free survival according to increasing PVD burden (log-rank P = 0.014; P for trend = 0.007). In Cox proportional hazards analysis, the presence of PVD was significantly associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, and renal dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: PVD is common in patients with AMI and is associated with poor long-term clinical outcomes. Routine systematic assessment of extra-coronary vascular disease may improve cardiovascular risk stratification.

Title: Prevalence and prognostic role of left atrial reverse remodeling in patients undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: insights from the Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
Abstract:
AIMS: Atrial enlargement is a complex maladaptive process related to pressure and volume overload. Left atrial reverse remodeling (LARR) has been described as a result of medical and interventional therapies. We sought to explore LARR prevalence and its prognostic implications following mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER).
METHODS AND RESULTS: Four-hundred and twenty-five patients from the MERIT-TEER (Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing M-TEER) who received a successful procedure from 2012 to 2024 with available left atrial volume (LAV) have been analyzed. LARR was defined as a reduction in LAV of at least 15%. LARR prevalence and its association with the risk of heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality at 4 years' follow-up were evaluated in the overall population and according to mitral regurgitation etiology.At short-term follow-up, LARR was observed in 124 patients (29.20%). LARR was more prevalent among primary mitral regurgitation (PMR) patients compared with those with ventricular secondary (vSMR) and atrial secondary mitral regurgitation (aSMR) (37.23, 27.19, and 18.33%; P = 0.017). At long-term follow-up, the composite outcome occurred in 153 patients (36.2%). LARR was independently associated with lower risk of events in the overall population [adjusted hazard ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.85, P = 0.005] and among vSMR patients (adjusted hazard ratio 0.43, 95% CI 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), but not in aSMR or PMR.
CONCLUSION: LARR was observed in less than one-third of patients undergoing M-TEER (29.2%), occurring more frequently in PMR. LARR was independently associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization in the overall population and particularly in patients with vSMR.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for predicting mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events: A systematic review and narrative synthesis.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide. While clinical scores provide modest predictive accuracy, the electrocardiogram (ECG) is rarely leveraged for prognosis. Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning now enable extraction of high-dimensional features from ECG waveforms for predicting cardiovascular outcomes. Our objective was to systematically evaluate the prognostic performance of AI-enabled ECG models for predicting all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). We searched PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar through November 2025 for studies using AI/ML models with 12-lead or single-lead ECGs to predict all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, or MACE in adults (≥18 years old). Eligible studies included adults (≥18 years) using ECG as primary input. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Narrative synthesis was conducted due to heterogeneity. Thirteen studies were included (~5.9 million patients). Eleven reported all-cause mortality (8 short-term: 30-day to 1-year), four reported cardiovascular mortality, and eight assessed MACE (4 composite MACE, 4 individual components). Models predominantly used convolutional neural networks [CNNs] on raw ECG waveforms. C-statistics ranged 0.70-0.89 for mortality prediction. Definitions and follow-up durations varied, limiting direct comparison. AI-ECG models demonstrate strong potential for predicting mortality and cardiovascular events with consistent performance and scalability. However, prospective validation and standardization are essential before clinical implementation.

Title: Prenatal echocardiographic predictors that increase the risk of urgent Ballon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) after birth in patients with Dextro-Transposition of the Great Arteries- Retrospective Study from Tertiary Center Lodz- Poland ICZMP (2014-2024).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Dextro-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) is a critical congenital heart disease (CHD) requiring prompt postnatal intervention, primarily: a line for Prostin infusion, hospitalization in an Intensive Care Unit, and in some cases, Balloon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) as a rescue procedure before planned Arterial Switch Operation (ASO). In this part, we focus on prenatal prediction of postnatal BAS.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at the Department of Prenatal Cardiology, Polish Mother's Memorial Hospital in Lodz, covering the years 2014-2024. From a total of 112 prenatally diagnosed d-TGA cases, 70 fetuses (46 with isolated d-TGA and 24 with d-TGA and VSD) met the inclusion criteria; follow-up of four pregnancies ended up in other hospitals, so the final series was 66 cases. Statistical analyses were performed using Statistica software.
RESULTS: Out of 66 analyzed cases, 32 newborns (48%) required postnatal BAS, with 87.5% of these procedures performed within the first 24-48 hours of life. Prenatal echocardiography correctly predicted the postnatal management pathway in 90.9% of cases (60/66), identifying all 26 neonates requiring urgent balloon atrial septostomy (100% positive predictive value), while 6 neonates in the planned group required unexpected postnatal septostomy. We noted that the 18% (n=6) of cases not identified prenatally occurred when the last scan was performed > 14 days before birth, suggesting that the time interval significantly impacts the reliability of late-gestation FO assessment. The study identified 10 prenatal "red flags," including FO size < 3 mm, bi-directional FO flow, and pulmonary vein velocity ≥ 45 cm/s and other features, as high-reliability indicators for urgent postnatal intervention.
CONCLUSION: Prenatal functional assessment of the foramen ovale in the late third trimester was highly effective in predicting the need for postnatal urgent BAS in d-TGA cases. The accuracy of these "red flags" was significantly higher when the last fetal echocardiogram was performed within 14 days to delivery.

Title: Urinary biomarkers at hospital admission and community-acquired acute kidney injury: A prospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to determine the sensitivity and specificity of a 13-urinary biomarker (uBM) panel for identifying community-acquired acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) and to assess whether these biomarkers were independently associated with CA-AKI.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital. Adults admitted through the emergency department were included. CA-AKI was defined as a ≥0.3 mg/dl decrease in serum creatinine (SCr) within 48 hours or a ≥50% decrease within 7 days. Blood samples were collected daily for SCr measurement, and urine samples were obtained at admission for uBM assessment. All the uBM were classified as abnormal when they exceeded the 75th percentile of the distribution.
RESULTS: 731 patients were included (55% male, median age of 61 years; 48% had hypertension, 28% had diabetes mellitus, and 23% had heart failure). The main reasons for hospitalization were respiratory (32%), genitourinary (15%), and cardiovascular (11%) diseases. CA-AKI was diagnosed in 26% of the patients. Compared with patients without CA-AKI, those with CA-AKI showed higher rates of elevation in four uBM: KIM-1 (31% vs. 23%; p=0.032), TIMP-2*IGFBP-7 (30% vs. 23%; p=0.045), clusterin (32% vs. 22%; p=0.011), and MCP-1 (33% vs. 22%; p=0.003). The sensitivity and specificity of uBM for detecting CA-AKI ranged from 23% to 33% and from 74% to 78%, respectively, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ranged from 0.485 to 0.554. Logistic regression analyses identified conditions independently associated with CA-AKI, including: hypotension [OR (95% CI): 2.07 (1.33-3.23); p=0.001], dehydration [OR (95% CI): 2.01 (1.40-2.91); p<0.001], chronic kidney disease [OR (95% CI): 2.00 (1.19-3.35); p=0.009], genitourinary tract disease [OR (95% CI): 2.00 (1.26-3.10); p=0.003], chronic liver disease [OR (95% CI): 1.69 (1.09-2.61); p=0.018], and elevation of one or more of the following uBM: KIM-1, TIMP-2*IGFBP-7, clusterin, and MCP-1 [OR (95% CI): 1.51 (1.06-2.14); p=0.022].
CONCLUSION: The expression of one or more of four uBM at emergency department admission (KIM-1, TIMP-2*IGFBP-7, clusterin, and MCP-1) may help identify patients with a higher probability of having CA-AKI, even with modest AUC results.

Title: Patient Blood Management Adoption and Transfusion-Threshold Concordance Among Romanian Anesthesiologists: National Survey Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Romania issued national patient blood management (PBM) guidelines in 2018. A 2023 national survey described the overall uptake of PBM among anesthesiologists but did not examine which clinicians and institutions adopted PBM, nor whether stated transfusion thresholds aligned with a study-defined restrictive reference.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify determinants of PBM adoption and to quantify transfusion-trigger concordance, using a planned, exploratory, cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2023 survey.
METHODS: We analyzed 511 responses to the 38-item Romanian Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care (SRATI) PBM survey. Three adoption outcomes (applying PBM, a formal hospital PBM group, and routine preoperative anemia treatment) were modeled by multivariable logistic regression against physician grade, hospital category, and local PBM educational events. Eight standardized clinical vignettes (age×cardiac disease×bleeding state) were scored against a restrictive hemoglobin reference (7 g/dL general; 8 g/dL with cardiac disease). The reported timing of the preanesthetic consultation (4 frequency items) was additionally examined as a determinant of preoperative anemia treatment. This was a planned, exploratory secondary analysis; the robustness of the main findings was examined in sensitivity analyses that accounted for survey attrition and for alternative transfusion-threshold scoring rules.
RESULTS: Overall, 73.7% (373/506) reported applying PBM, 33.1% (158/477) reported a formal PBM group, and 33.5% (117/349) reported routine preoperative anemia treatment. Local PBM educational events were the strongest adjusted correlate of reported adoption (applying PBM: adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 9.78, 95% CI 4.33-22.07; P<.001; formal group: aOR 7.72, 95% CI 4.30-13.88; P<.001). Earlier preanesthetic consultation was associated with routine preoperative anemia treatment (aOR 1.79 per frequency level for consultation more than 7 days before surgery, 95% CI 1.36-2.35; P<.001). Transfusion-trigger concordance was lower for older than younger patients in otherwise identical scenarios (eg, active bleeding without cardiac disease: 195/345, 56.5% at ≥65 years vs 288/347, 83% at <65 years), and 56.5% (196/347) endorsed a liberal trigger (hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL) in at least one noncardiac scenario. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with a restrictive transfusion pattern (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 0.69-1.98; P=.56). Findings were unchanged across scoring rules, and reported PBM application was similar among respondents who did and did not complete the demographic block (246/329, 74.8% vs 127/177, 71.8%; P=.53).
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cross-sectional analysis, reported PBM adoption was associated more strongly with local educational activity than with hospital category or physician seniority. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with restrictive stated thresholds in hypothetical scenarios, and respondents selected more liberal thresholds for older patients. Standardized multidisciplinary pathways, earlier anemia screening shared with the surgical team, and education focused on transfusion decisions may help address these gaps. Prospective studies using observed process measures, transfusion practice, and clinical outcomes are needed.

Title: Prehospital Risk Stratification for Early Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric criteria remain limited for identifying injured children who may benefit from early blood transfusion for hemorrhagic shock. This study evaluated whether emergency medical services (EMS)-observable variables in a national trauma registry could identify children at risk for early hospital blood transfusion.
METHODS: We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study using the National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2020). Among 391,126 records for patients aged 1-15 years, we included children transported by EMS directly from the scene to a participating trauma center after excluding burn injuries, interfacility transfers, and missing pre-identified EMS variables (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, or Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS]). The primary outcome was any blood product administered within 4 h of emergency department arrival. Five prespecified EMS-observable predictors composed the model: age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest. We fit a multivariable logistic regression and a classification and regression tree (CART) using an 80/20 stratified train-validation split. Missing data sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and CART refitting in the broader eligible cohort.
RESULTS: Among 79,764 children, 2,634 (3.3%) received early transfusion in the hospital. All five predictors were independently associated with early transfusion, led by GCS ≤ 14 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.61-9.22), penetrating mechanism (aOR 5.87; 95% CI, 5.28-6.51), and age-adjusted hypotension (aOR 5.39; 95% CI, 4.74-6.13). In the validation cohort, CART analysis stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk tiers comprising 77.0%, 19.7%, and 3.3% of patients, respectively. Early-transfusion rates were 1.2%, 6.1%, and 36.7% across these tiers. The high-risk tier accounted for 36.8% of all early transfusion events. Using the high-risk tier as a decision threshold, sensitivity was 36.8%, specificity 97.8%, positive predictive value 36.7%, and negative predictive value 97.8%.
CONCLUSIONS: Five EMS-observable features, including age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest, identified a small subgroup of pediatric trauma patients with substantially elevated risk of early hospital transfusion. This parsimonious framework may inform prospective validation of prehospital transfusion criteria.

Title: Influence of Perioperative Variables on Surgical Site Infection in Patients With Frailty and Prefrailty Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection (SSI) in patients with frailty undergoing myocardial revascularization is a major clinical challenge, and there is a gap in the literature related to this topic.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify perioperative variables associated with SSI in patients with frailty and prefrailty undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting within 30 days of the procedure.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 467 patients with frailty or prefrailty aged 60 years and older who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting in 6 Brazilian centers between January 2018 and December 2024. Frailty was defined using the Fried criteria. SSI was defined as a wound with exposed tissue with positive culture requiring antibiotic treatment. Univariate and multivariate analyses were carried out.
RESULTS: The rate of SSI was 5.6% (26/467). The New York Heart Association classification (P=.02), Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI; P=.01), use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB; P=.003), CPB time (P=.02), total surgery time (P<.001), occurrence of bleeding (P=.04), mechanical ventilation time (P=.001), length of hospital stay (P<.001), intensive care unit stay (P<.001), and need for reoperation (P<.001) variables were associated with SSI in unadjusted comparisons. In the multivariate model, the CCI (odds ratio 1.58, 95% CI 1.25-1.99; P<.001) and use of CPB (odds ratio 4.89, 95% CI 1.71-13.94; P=.003) were independently associated with SSI.
CONCLUSIONS: The CCI and the use of CPB were independently associated with SSI.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of immune-inflammatory biomarkers for predicting no-reflow in patients with acute myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether routine immune-inflammatory biomarkers predict no-reflow (NR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients, quantify their incremental predictive value over clinical variables, and build an interpretable peri-procedural prediction model.
METHODS: This prospective cohort recruited 382 AMI patients undergoing PCI. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent correlates; confounder-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed nonlinear associations. LASSO regression selected core predictors with variance inflation factor (VIF) assessing multicollinearity. Four machine-learning models underwent 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation and SHAP interpretation. Incremental value was tested via ΔAUC (DeLong test), continuous NRI, and IDI. Stratified regression and interaction tests evaluated AMI-subtype effect modification.
RESULTS: NR occurred in 91 patients (23.8%). Multiple neutrophil-centred indices independently correlated with NR after adjustment. Seven predictors constituted the final model (all VIF < 2.5). LightGBM yielded optimal discrimination and modest net clinical benefit (AUC 0.799, 95% CI 0.699-0.899); AMI subtype and neutrophil-related markers dominated SHAP outputs. Neutrophil count, NAR, NHR, SII, and PIV significantly improved discrimination. Seven of the 16 tested markers yielded significant continuous NRI, and ten demonstrated significant IDI gains. In stratified analyses, neutrophil count, NLR, and MHR were associated with NR in STEMI but not NSTEMI patients; interaction tests found no significant AMI-subtype effect modification.
CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural neutrophil-centred inflammatory biomarkers are independent correlates of post-PCI NR and offer incremental predictive value over conventional clinical variables. The interpretable LightGBM model supports peri-procedural NR risk stratification, though external validation and recalibration are mandatory before clinical application.

Title: Cardiovascular risk associated with first-line Janus kinase inhibitors versus TNF inhibitors in patients with RA: a nationwide cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) between TNF inhibitors (TNFi) and Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) when initiated as first-line advanced therapy in patients with RA.
METHODS: Using the Korean nationwide claims database, we identified patients newly diagnosed with RA between 2010 and 2015. Patients who initiated TNFi or JAKi as first-line advanced therapy were selected for analysis. Patients were followed from initiation of TNFi or JAKi through June 2024. The primary outcome was incident MACE, defined as myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke or coronary revascularization. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied in the total cohort. We additionally performed propensity score (PS)-matched analyses to address confounding by indication. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to baseline cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: The study included 6174 patients (TNFi = 5152; JAKi = 1022). The incidence rates of MACE were 4.1 and 3.6 per 1000 person-years in the TNFi and JAKi groups, respectively. MACE risk did not differ significantly between JAKi and TNFi in the total study cohort (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.636, 95% CI 0.283-1.429) or in the PS-matched population (adjusted HR 0.715, 95% CI 0.187-2.739). Results were consistent across all prespecified subgroups, including patients with baseline cardiovascular risk factors.
CONCLUSION: First-line use of JAKi was not associated with an increased risk of MACE compared with TNFi. These findings provide real-world evidence supporting the cardiovascular safety of JAKi as first-line advanced therapy in patients with RA.

Title: Outcomes of systemic sclerosis with overlapping myositis: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest disease-specific mortality among rheumatic diseases, with cardiac involvement and interstitial lung disease (ILD) as leading causes of death. We aimed to determine whether overlapping myositis independently contributes to cardiac involvement and mortality in SSc.
METHODS: We did a 1:1 propensity score matched retrospective cohort study of 880 SSc patients (2013 ACR/EULAR criteria) at a single centre. SSc myositis required proximal weakness and elevated muscle enzymes without alternative causes. Cardiac involvement used SCTC criteria (pericardial effusion, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, conduction disease). We used standard and Firth penalised logistic regression for cardiac predictors, Cox regression for survival, and Fisher's exact test for cause specific mortality. All p values were Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted.
RESULTS: Of 880 patients, 92 (10.4%) had myositis. After matching, 92 pairs (n = 184) were analysed. Myositis independently predicted cardiac involvement (standard aOR=19.99, 95%CI 2.19-182.26, p = 0.008; Firth OR = 12.84, 95%CI 2.31-98.47, p = 0.006). Higher mRSS also predicted cardiac involvement (aOR=2.34 per 10 points, p = 0.006). Anti-Scl70 was less common in myositis (25.0% vs. 50.0%, p = 0.009). Overall mortality did not differ (13.0% vs. 9.8%, p = 0.620). In non-myositis deaths, ILD caused 33.3%; in myositis deaths, cardiac failure caused 25% and no ILD-related deaths (Fisher's p = 0.229). Cardiac involvement was significantly associated with mortality (aHR=8.09 (1.36-48.26), p = 0.022), independent of myositis.
CONCLUSION: Overlapping myositis in SSc is associated with an increased risk of cardiac involvement and a shift in the cause-of-death profile away from ILD, without a detectable difference in overall survival over the observed median 21-month follow-up. Systematic cardiac surveillance is needed in these patients.

Title: Cost-utility of expanded hypertension screening and treatment among adults covered by Peru's Seguro Integral de Salud: a Markov model using national data.
Journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We assessed the cost-utility of expanding hypertension screening, diagnosis, and treatment among adults covered by Peru's Seguro Integral de Salud (SIS).
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Analyses assembled in May 2026 used a 10-year cohort Markov model parameterized with the 2024 Peruvian Demographic and Family Health Survey (ENDES), SIS administrative data for 2022-2024, and published parameters. Universal and risk-targeted scenarios were compared with population-specific usual care, using S/ 25,007 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY).
RESULTS: The baseline sample included 6,098 adults aged 40-74 years; hypertension prevalence was 28.9%. Universal 80-80-80 expansion averted 60.7 cardiovascular events and 6.1 cardiovascular deaths and gained 51.3 QALYs per 100,000 eligible adults. Incremental cost was S/ 7,784,979, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of S/ 151,686/QALY. The scenario targeting 10-year cardiovascular risk ≥10% had an ICER of S/ 60,171/QALY in its eligible subgroup.
CONCLUSIONS: All scenarios exceeded the threshold. Lower targeted-scenario ICERs concern different eligible populations. Estimates depend on modeled effects, the 10-year horizon, and exclusion of event-related savings.

Title: Anticoagulation in Mechanical Circulatory Support: Contemporary Challenges and Future Directions in Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy.
Abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is increasingly used in patients with cardiogenic shock, advanced heart failure, and severe respiratory failure; however, anticoagulation management remains challenging due to the competing risks of thrombosis, bleeding, hemolysis, and device dysfunction. In this review, we synthesize contemporary evidence on anticoagulant selection, monitoring strategies, and device-specific management across major MCS platforms, including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, temporary ventricular assist devices, Impella devices, and durable left ventricular assist devices. Unfractionated heparin remains the cornerstone anticoagulant across most MCS platforms, while anti-factor Xa-guided monitoring is increasingly incorporated into clinical practice in many centers alongside activated partial thromboplastin time and other monitoring modalities. Direct thrombin inhibitors represent important alternatives, particularly for patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or heparin resistance. Recent advances include bicarbonate-based purge strategies for Impella support and evolving antithrombotic approaches in HeartMate 3 recipients, introduced by the ARIES-HM3 trial. Emerging investigational strategies, including direct oral anticoagulants, factor XI/XII inhibition, and precision anticoagulation approaches, show promise for improving hemocompatibility; however, current evidence remains limited, and further prospective studies are required before these strategies can be routinely adopted. Overall, contemporary evidence supports an individualized approach to anticoagulation based on device characteristics, patient-specific risk profiles, and current guideline recommendations, while highlighting important knowledge gaps that warrant further high-quality prospective investigation.

Title: Joint association of physical activity and sedentary time with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among advanced CKM syndrome participants, insights from NHANES 2007-2018.
Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents the interconnection of metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease, with advanced stages associated with high mortality. However, the associations of leisure-time physical activity (PA) and sedentary time with mortality in participants with advanced CKM syndrome remain unclear. This study conducted a prospective cohort study using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2018. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses, and subgroup analyses were applied to examine the independent and joint associations of leisure-time PA and sedentary time with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among participants with advanced CKM syndrome. Among advanced CKM participants, physical inactivity was associated with higher risks of all-cause (HR = 2.43, 95% CI: 1.98-2.97, P < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR = 2.62, 95% CI: 1.79-3.82, P < 0.001). Compared with < 4 h/day, sedentary time > 8 h/day was independently linked to elevated risks of all-cause (HR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.33-2.19, P < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.34-3.38, P = 0.005). Joint analyses showed that the group characterized by physical inactivity combined with ≥ 6 h/day sedentary time was associated with the highest risk of all-cause (HR = 2.77, 95% CI: 2.16-3.56, P < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR = 3.39, 95% CI: 2.13-5.40, P < 0.001). These associations were further supported by RCS analyses and sensitivity analyses. The findings underscore the potential survival advantages associated with enhancing physical activity and reducing sedentary behavior in this high-risk population.

Title: Are we Adhering to Guidelines for Follow-up Imaging in Neonates with Simple Congenital Heart Defects? What are the Healthcare Costs of Non-adherence?
Abstract: Simple congenital heart defects (CHDs) are frequently identified via neonatal echocardiograms ("echos"). In 2020, the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology issued guidelines for follow-up imaging of CHDs. In this retrospective study, we evaluated adherence to these guidelines at an academic health center in Southeastern Ontario. The cohort included neonates who had one or more simple CHDs diagnosed in the first 30 days of life between April 1, 2020, and March 31, 2024. We reviewed electronic medical records up to September 30, 2025 to examine (a) rates of non-adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up imaging; (b) factors that may contribute to non-adherence; and (c) the costs of excessive imaging. Among 248 patients, 376 echos were performed over the study period. Adherence status could be determined for 320. Follow-up for 39.7% of echos did not adhere to the guidelines, primarily because repeat echos were performed earlier than recommended. Non-adherence was substantially higher for lesions requiring surveillance imaging, as per guidelines, compared with lesions where follow-up imaging is not recommended or findings were normal (91.9% vs. 12.0%; OR = 83.4, 95% CI: 37.5-185.5). The pediatric cardiologist's recommendation was documented for 74.5% of echos, but only 48.9% of recommendations aligned with the guidelines. Non-adherence was higher when recommendations were not documented or deviated from the guidelines. Sixty-two echos were deemed excessive, corresponding to $13,339 in extra imaging costs. The high rate of non-adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up imaging for simple CHDs highlights an opportunity to reduce unnecessary healthcare costs through consistent documentation of guideline-aligned follow-up recommendations by pediatric cardiologists.

Title: Comparison of Feeding, Nutritional, and Procedural Outcomes in Infants with Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Blood Flow Undergoing Surgical Systemic-to-Pulmonary Artery Shunt Versus Ductal Stenting.
Abstract: Ductal stenting and surgical systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunting (surgical shunt) are alternative strategies to establish pulmonary blood flow in infants with ductal-dependent circulation. The impact of palliation strategy on feeding, nutrition, and neurodevelopment remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 100 infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow (2017-2024) undergoing surgical shunt (n = 57) or ductal stenting (n = 43). Outcomes included feeding, nutrition, hospital course, and neurodevelopment. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors associated with gastrostomy tube (GT) placement. Baseline demographics were similar except for cardiac anatomy. Ductal stent patients reached target enteral feeds post-procedurally sooner (3 vs. 6 days, p < 0.001), had higher discharge weight-for-age z-scores (- 1.30 vs. -1.98, p = 0.02), and smaller declines in growth during hospitalization (p = 0.007). GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting (26% vs. 51%, p = 0.011), but palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.14-1.24, p = 0.12). Oral feeding or breastfeeding within 5 days following palliation was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement (OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.06-0.81, p = 0.03). Ductal stent patients also had shorter mechanical ventilation and ICU stays and required less vasoactive-inotropic support. Total hospital length of stay, need for reintervention, suspected or diagnosed necrotizing enterocolitis, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups. Ductal stenting was associated with improved early post-procedural recovery, faster feeding progression, and better preservation of growth compared with surgical shunt palliation. Although GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting in unadjusted analysis, palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment. Early post-procedural oral feeding was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement but may also reflect feeding readiness and clinical recovery.

Title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favorable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and cardiopulmonary bypass, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown.
METHODS: Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic cardiopulmonary bypass with 80 minutes of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 minutes. Results: Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions: Disconnection of the ventilator during cardiopulmonary bypass and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

Title: Vitamin D Supplementation in Community-Dwelling Adults.
Abstract: Vitamin D testing is commonly performed in adults. Evidence is lacking to support vitamin D screening or supplementation in the general population, regardless of baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. The National Academy of Medicine recommends that individuals 70 years and younger consume 600 IU of vitamin D daily and that individuals older than 70 years consume 800 IU daily. This can be achieved through dietary sources, supplements, or both. Achieving the recommended intake prevents serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels from decreasing to less than 12 ng/mL in 97.5% of the general population. Randomized controlled trials of vitamin D supplementation in the general population, including patients with low baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels, do not demonstrate reduced all-cause mortality or improvement in cardiovascular health. Some patients with prediabetes may benefit from taking at least 3 years of vitamin D supplementation that exceeds the recommended dietary intake to reduce the risk of progression to type 2 diabetes. Randomized controlled trials of vitamin D supplementation for reducing the risk of falls and fractures, cancer, dementia, respiratory infections, and depression; for symptoms of fatigue, hair loss, and chronic pain; and during pregnancy and menopause do not show consistent benefit, including in patients with low baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels.

Title: H2FPEF Score and Charlson Comorbidity Index as Independent Predictors of Cardiovascular Outcomes in Elderly Patients Undergoing Geriatric Rehabilitation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is difficult to diagnose in older adults. The H2FPEF score estimates the likelihood of HFpEF and has been associated with adverse prognosis, but its performance has not been evaluated in geriatric inpatients with a high comorbidity burden.
HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that the H2FPEF score predicts adverse outcomes in geriatric inpatients independently of comorbidity burden.
METHODS: This prospective cohort included consecutive patients admitted to a geriatric rehabilitation unit. All patients underwent functional and echocardiographic assessment at admission. The ability of the H2FPEF score, the Charlson comorbidity index (CCI), and their combination to predict 1-year all-cause mortality (ACM) or cardiovascular rehospitalization (CR) was evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 302 patients (median age 83 years, 40% men), 24% had a H2FPEF score ≥ 6 indicating high HFpEF probability and 42% had a CCI > 3 indicating high comorbidity burden. The H2FPEF score correlated with CCI (β = 0.27, p < 0.01) and functional disability (lower Instrumental Activities of Daily Living score; β = -0.17, p = 0.003), but not with cognitive impairment. Both a high H2FPEF score and high CCI were associated with a higher risk of the combined outcome of 1-year ACM or CR (adjusted HR 2.89 [95% CI 1.63-5.10], p < 0.001 and adjusted HR 2.66 [95% CI 1.67-4.21], p < 0.001, respectively), with no interaction between them (p = 0.63). Patients with both high-risk scores had the highest risk (adjusted HR 4.66 [95% CI 2.54-8.57], p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In geriatric inpatients, a high H2FPEF score is common and independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes at 1 year.

Title: Calcium Density as a Marker of Coronary Plaque Stabilization in Primary Prevention: The CAUGHT-CAD Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite primary prevention statin treatment, a substantial proportion of individuals remain at residual risk for cardiovascular events. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CTA) enables the quantification of compositional changes in calcified plaque.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine whether increases in coronary calcified plaque volume and density associated with statin therapy could be used as a marker of plaque stabilization in asymptomatic individuals undergoing serial coronary CTA.
METHODS: In the CAUGHT-CAD trial, asymptomatic, statin-naive, intermediate-risk individuals were randomized to a primary prevention strategy (including statin treatment) vs usual care. Participants underwent coronary CTA at baseline and 3 years. In this post hoc analysis, volumes of 5 plaque subtypes were quantified: noncalcified (≤350 HU), low-density calcium (351-500 HU), intermediate-density calcium (501-700 HU), high-density calcium (701-1000 HU), and very high density calcium (>1,000 HU). The primary outcome was the per-lesion level change in volumes of calcified plaque subtypes.
RESULTS: Eight hundred forty lesions were included from 338 participants (mean age: 58.3 ± 6.9 years, 57.1% men, 161 [47.6%] statin treated). Statin treatment was associated with greater progression in intermediate-density (β = 0.89, SE = 0.39; P = 0.02) and high-density (β = 0.79, SE = 0.24; P = 0.001) calcium, alongside regression of noncalcified plaque (β = -9.83, SE = 1.64; P < 0.001), following adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) level, and baseline plaque volume. Among statin-treated participants, LDL-C reduction ≥30% was associated with greater progression of high-density (β = 1.11, SE = 0.49; P = 0.03) and very high density (β = 1.68, SE = 0.85; P = 0.04) calcium.
CONCLUSIONS: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C. (Coronary Artery Calcium Score: Use to Guide Management of Hereditary Coronary Artery Disease [CAUGHT-CAD]; ACTRN12614001294640).

Title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment.
METHODS: In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method.
RESULTS: The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency.
CONCLUSIONS: Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

Title: Coronary Visual Intelligence System (CorVIS) Guided Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is usually displayed in 2-dimensional planes with few fixed 3-dimensional (3D) views, which may limit appreciation of the spatial relationship between plaques and vessel. We describe initial clinical experience with CorVIS, an artificial intelligence-based coronary visualization system, in complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 cases-2 chronic total occlusions and 1 heavily calcified lesion-in which CorVIS provided freely rotatable 3D reconstructions with plaque characterization. In each case, the CorVIS corresponded to specific procedural decisions, including the chosen crossing approach and calcium-modification strategy. All 3 procedures were completed successfully.
DISCUSSION: These cases suggest that artificial intelligence-based 3D CCTA reconstruction may complement conventional imaging for preprocedural planning of complex PCI. The efficacy of CorVIS in facilitating complex PCI remains to be verified in further prospective studies.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In this initial case series, CorVIS delivered freely rotatable 3D CCTA reconstructions and plaque characterization, informing key procedural decisions for complex PCI.

Title: PCWP Characterizes Responders of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing in HFpEF Population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hemodynamic and mechanical benefit of left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remained underexplored.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to evaluate the hemodynamic and mechanical response of LBBAP in HFpEF population.
METHODS: This cohort study includes patients with pacemaker-indicated symptomatic bradycardia and right heart catheterization (RHC) diagnosed HFpEF. Patients are consecutively enrolled from 2 treatment groups: 1 group receives LBBAP only, and the other receives right ventricular pacing (RVP) only. Periprocedural right heart catheterization and echocardiography were evaluated and compared. Primary endpoint was the composite of heart failure hospitalization (HFH) and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Two hundred one patients with HFpEF were included, 100 patients from RVP group and 101 patients from LBBAP group. Baseline characteristics were similar. Compared with RVP, LBBAP achieved better electrical synchrony with preserved hemodynamics and cardiac mechanics. With a median of 17.6 (13.5, 22.5) months, LBBAP also presented better survival for the primary endpoint (21.5% for RVP vs 9.5% for LBBAP; log-rank P = 0.024), contributed by reduced HFH incidence. Distinctively, LBBAP resulted in a more significant reduction of mean PCWP (-2.3 [-3.0, 0] mm Hg for RVP vs -4.0 [-4.9, -1.0] mm Hg for LBBAP; P < 0.001). Multivariate Cox model revealed that in the LBBAP group, Δmean PCWP predicted primary endpoint incidence (HR [95% CI]: 1.525 [1.118, 2.080]; P = 0.011).
CONCLUSIONS: In HFpEF population, LBBAP better preserved cardiac function and presented better survival for HFH compared with RVP. Reduction of PCWP might characterize the responders of LBBAP in HFpEF population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05575557.

Title: Strategy and Outcomes of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Total Occlusion With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) are at high-risk, and retrograde CTO percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is often avoided because of hemodynamic and safety concerns.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated CTO-PCI strategy selection and outcomes according to LVEF, focusing on patients selected for a primary retrograde approach.
METHODS: We analyzed 11,458 patients from the Japanese CTO-PCI Expert Registry (2014-2022), including 1,692 with LVEF <40% and 9,766 with LVEF ≥40%. Core laboratory-adjudicated angiographic findings, procedural strategies, and in-hospital outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Patients with LVEF <40% had more complex coronary anatomy. A primary retrograde approach was selected in 489 of 1,692 procedures (28.9%) in the LVEF <40% group and 2,500 of 9,766 procedures (25.6%) in the LVEF ≥40% group (OR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.05-1.33; P = 0.005). Overall technical and procedural success rates were comparable between groups. In the primary retrograde cohort, technical success was achieved in 450 of 489 procedures (92.0%) with LVEF <40% and 2,186 of 2,494 procedures (87.7%) with LVEF ≥40% (OR: 1.63; 95% CI: 1.14-2.37; P = 0.005). In-hospital mortality, stroke, contrast-induced nephropathy, and preprocedural mechanical circulatory support were more frequent in patients with LVEF <40%, whereas other in-hospital adverse events were generally similar.
CONCLUSIONS: Reduced LVEF was associated with more frequent selection of a primary retrograde approach. Among selected patients undergoing primary retrograde CTO-PCI, technical success remained high despite greater anatomical complexity.

Title: P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy vs Dual Antiplatelet Therapy by Age After PCI: A SHARE Substudy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abbreviated dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy is increasingly used after percutaneous coronary intervention, but whether its effects are consistent across age is uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: The authors examined age-related differences in outcomes with P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy vs 12-month DAPT after percutaneous coronary intervention.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the Short-Term DAPT After Deployment of Bioabsorbable Polymer Everolimus-Eluting Stent randomized trial stratified 1,387 patients at age 75 years. The primary endpoint was net adverse clinical events (NACE)-major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5) plus major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events-through 12 months.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 365 days (Q1-Q3: 353-365); 210 patients (15.1%) were ≥75 years. NACE occurred in 25 of 1,177 patients <75 years (2.4%; 95% CI: 1.4-3.3) and 7 of 210 aged ≥75 years (3.7%; 95% CI: 1.0-6.4). NACE did not differ between monotherapy and 12-month DAPT in patients <75 years (8 of 587 [1.6%; 95% CI: 0.5-2.8] vs 17 of 590 [3.1%; 95% CI: 1.6-4.6]; HR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.20-1.09) or ≥75 years (3 of 107 [3.3%; 95% CI: 0.0-6.9] vs 4 of 103 [4.2%; 95% CI: 0.1-8.1]; HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.16-3.17), with no treatment-age interaction (P = 0.637 dichotomized; P = 0.173 continuous). Major bleeding increased with age, whereas major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events remained stable.
CONCLUSIONS: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after 3-month DAPT was associated with similar net clinical outcomes to 12-month DAPT in both younger and older patients, with no significant treatment-age heterogeneity. These findings support consideration of abbreviated DAPT as a reasonable treatment option in selected older adults, although larger studies are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT03447379.

Title: Caregiver and Family Factors Related to Life's Essential 8 in Young Children.
Journal: Journal of pediatric health care : official publication of National Association of Pediatric Nurse Associates & Practitioners
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Promotion of cardiovascular health (CVH) during young childhood is critical for preventing later disease.
METHODS: This study describes the CVH of 269 young children from an observational cohort study and examines child, caregiver, and family factors related to CVH. Child anthropometrics were measured. Parents reported on child smoking exposure, sleep, physical activity, diet, and possible CVH correlates. CVH composite scores were calculated using the American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework.
RESULTS: The average LE8 score for the sample was in the moderate CVH range (74.8 ± 10.2). Most children had no smoking exposure (92%), met sleep recommendations (66%), and had a healthy weight (76%). Few children met recommendations for physical activity or diet. Caregiver (education, age, health) and family (household size, insurance) factors related to CVH.
DISCUSSION: CVH promotion efforts for young children should target physical activity, diet, and caregiver and family factors.

Title: Long-Term Safety and Procedural Performance of an Interatrial Shunt for Heart Failure According to Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term device durability and phenotype-specific safety outcomes after interatrial shunting require further characterization.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the procedural success, device durability, and heart failure (HF) phenotype-specific safety outcomes of an interatrial shunt in the RELIEVE-HF trial.
METHODS: Randomized patients were assigned 1:1 to shunt or sham control with prespecified stratification by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) into heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (LVEF ≤40%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (LVEF >40%). Procedural performance, device durability, serious adverse events (SAEs), major adverse cardiovascular or neurological events (MACNE), major bleeding, and renal outcomes were assessed through 2 years.
RESULTS: Among 605 enrolled patients (508 randomized; 97 roll-in), shunt implantation was attempted in 370 and was successful in 369 (99.7%). Among implanted patients with follow-up (n = 348), no device- or procedure-related MACNE occurred through 2 years (0%; 95% CI: 0%-0.9%), and shunt patency was 99.4% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.9%). Prespecified LVEF-stratified analyses demonstrated divergent safety profiles. In HFrEF, shunt therapy was not associated with excess all-cause MACNE, major bleeding, or renal decline and was associated with lower SAE burden. In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline.
CONCLUSIONS: Interatrial shunt implantation was mechanically reliable and durable through 2 years. Safety outcomes differed by HF phenotype, with no evidence of excess clinical safety events in HFrEF but increased adverse events in HFpEF. These findings support phenotype-specific evaluation of interatrial shunt therapy. (REducing Lung congestion symptoms using the v-wavE shunt in adVancEd Heart Failure [RELIEVE-HF]; NCT03499236).

Title: Acute Effect of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation at Two Different Sites on Blood Pressure and Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Hypertensive Individuals: A Randomized, Crossover, Double-Blind Clinical Trial.
Journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the acute effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) on blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) variability (HRV) in hypertensive individuals at two auricular sites.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty-four hypertensive adults underwent three taVNS sessions applied to the tragus, cymba conchae, and earlobe (control), with one-week intervals between sessions. Systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), HR, peripheral oxygen saturation, autonomic function, and HRV were assessed before, during, and after stimulation. HRV analysis included time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear indices.
RESULTS: Participants exhibited baseline sympathetic predominance and reduced HRV. Stimulation at the cymba conchae produced greater reductions in SBP and DBP than at the other sites (p < 0.05), without significantly affecting HRV parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: A single taVNS session did not produce clinically meaningful changes in autonomic function. However, stimulation at the cymba conchae showed greater potential for BP reduction. Further studies using longer and more robust protocols are warranted.

Title: Comparative Clinical Outcomes Across Ambulatory Cardiac Monitoring Modalities.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comparative effectiveness data across ambulatory cardiac monitoring (ACM) modalities are limited.
OBJECTIVE: To confirm and extend comparative findings across ACM modalities and vendors in commercially insured and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries without prior arrhythmia.
METHODS: Retrospective study using Optum Research Database. Adults ≥ 18 years with first ACM use between January 1, 2017 and June 30, 2022 were categorized as long-term continuous monitors (LTCM), Holter, external ambulatory event monitors (AEM), or mobile cardiac telemetry (MCT). Outcomes were arrhythmia diagnosis (90 days), repeat monitoring (180 days), cardiovascular events, hospitalization, emergency department [ED] visits, and costs (365 days). Inverse probability of treatment weighting used a specific LTCM (iRhythm Technologies, San Francisco, CA) as reference.
RESULTS: Among 352,782 patients (mean age 62.0 ± 17.1 years; 61% female), 25% received LTCM, 37% Holter, 20% AEM, and 18% MCT. Among LTCM users, 58% received iRhythm LTCM. Compared with this LTCM, Holter, MCT, and other LTCM had lower odds of arrhythmia diagnosis (IPTW-weighted ORs 0.50-0.95; p < 0.01); AEM did not differ. Repeat monitoring was higher for other LTCM, AEM, and Holter (IPTW-weighted ORs 1.99-2.77; p < 0.001); MCT did not differ. All other modalities had higher IPTW-weighted odds of cardiovascular events (ORs 1.10-1.66; p < 0.001), hospitalization (ORs 1.12-2.04; p < 0.001), ED visits (ORs 1.09-2.08; p < 0.001), and costs (IPTW-weighted cost ratios 1.03-1.28; p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes differed across ACM modalities and vendors, confirming observations in other payer populations. A specific LTCM was associated with higher claims-based arrhythmia yield and lower repeat monitoring than most alternatives, and with lower hospitalization, health care utilization, and costs.

Title: High sensitivity C-reactive protein and the risk of cardio-kidney outcomes in adults with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease: a nationwide study.
Journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: The burden and prognostic significance of inflammation in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly characterized, with prior studies yielding conflicting estimates of the association between elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and cardio-kidney outcomes.
METHODS: Observational nationwide study of 23,008 adults with CKD stages 3-5 attending nephrology care and enrolled in the Swedish Renal Registry (2008-2023). Inflammation was assessed longitudinally via 94,500 repeated hsCRP registrations. Time-varying, cause-specific Cox models accounting for competing risks estimated associations with study outcomes, which included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), heart failure (HF) hospitalization, acute kidney injury (AKI), kidney failure requiring replacement therapy (KFRT) and all-cause mortality. Pre-defined stratifiers were atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) history and CKD stage.
RESULTS: Mean age was 71 years, 65% were male, and median estimated glomerular filtration rate was 25 mL/min/1.73 m². Median hsCRP was 4.0 (IQR 1.9-7.0) mg/L, and 75% of participants had hsCRP≥2. Over median 3.9 (IQR 2.0-6.7) years, hsCRP ≥2 mg/L was associated with higher rates of all outcomes: hazard ratio 1.20 (95% confidence interval 1.12-1.28) for MACE (n=5,480 events); 1.29 (1.22-1.37) for HF hospitalization (n=8,173); 1.28 (1.18-1.38) for AKI (n=3,943); 1.09 (1.02-1.15) for KFRT (n=6,177); and 1.43 (1.37-1.50) for mortality (n=12,645). In spline analyses, associations were steeper at lower hsCRP levels and flatter thereafter for all outcomes except KFRT, where the hsCRP-response relationship was relatively flat. Associations with MACE, HF, AKI and mortality were consistent regardless of ASCVD status and CKD stage. Associations with KFRT were inconsistent across CKD stages.
CONCLUSION: In this nationwide cohort of adults with moderate to severe CKD receiving nephrology care, inflammation was common, and higher hsCRP levels were associated with adverse cardiovascular and kidney outcomes, as well as mortality. Although associations were less consistent for KFRT, these findings collectively support the utility of hsCRP monitoring in this population.

Title: Long forms of cardiac troponin T are independent of kidney function and improve the diagnosis of myocardial infarction.
Journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: A recently developed cardiac troponin T (cTnT) assay measuring intact or mildly fragmented cTnT (long cTnT) has shown promise in improving the accuracy of myocardial infarction (MI) detection compared to the commercial high sensitivity cTnT (hs-cTnT) assay. However, data on patients with kidney dysfunction are limited. We compared the performance of long and hs-cTnT in MI diagnostics across the full spectrum of kidney function.
METHODS: In this prospective study, consecutive patients presenting at the emergency department with an elevated (≥14 ng/L) hs-cTnT were recruited. Long and hs-cTnT were measured on admission and kidney function was determined with plasma creatinine (Crea), cystatin C (CysC) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) using contemporary equations with Crea, CysC or both (Crea-CysC) together. The association of eGFR with hs-cTnT and long cTnT concentrations and the discriminative ability of hs-cTnT and long cTnT for type 1 MI and any MI were evaluated.
RESULTS: In total, 1811 patients were included, 205 (11.3%) had a MI and 204 (11.3%) had a history of chronic kidney disease. The overall median (interquartile range) Crea-eGFR, CysC-eGFR and Crea-CysC-eGFR were 71 (51-87), 52 (36-69) and 63 (44-79) ml/min/1.73m2. In patients without MI, long cTnT showed no consistent association with kidney function (β=0.0008, P = 0.050; β=0.0005, P = 0.222; β=0.0006, P = 0.182 for Crea-eGFR, CysC-eGFR and Crea-CysC-eGFR, respectively), whereas hs-cTnT was inversely associated with kidney function (β=-0.0032, -0.0035 and - 0.0035; all P < 0.001). Long cTnT demonstrated superior diagnostic performance compared with hs-cTnT for the detection of MI (P < 0.001), with the advantage becoming progressively more pronounced with lower eGFR irrespective of equation used.
CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to hs-cTnT, long cTnT is unaffected by kidney function and outperforms hs-cTnT in the detection of MI, with the greatest diagnostic advantage observed in patients with lower eGFR.

Title: Effects of seven traditional Chinese sports on physiological outcomes in individuals receiving treatment for substance use disorder: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Substance use disorder is a major public health challenge, with physiological consequences, including dysregulated blood pressure, abnormal heart rate, and altered body composition, which increase the risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality. Physical exercise shows rehabilitation potential, but evidence-based guidance on optimal traditional Chinese exercise regimens is lacking.
OBJECTIVE: This network meta-analysis evaluated and ranked the comparative effects of seven traditional Chinese sports (Taiji Rouliqiu, combined Tai Chi and Qigong, 24-form Tai Chi, Baduanjin, Tai Chi rehabilitation exercise, shuttlecock, and Tai Chi Thirteen Postures Daoyin) on physiological outcomes in individuals with substance use disorder.
METHODS: Randomized controlled trials were searched from PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and VIP databases from inception to February 2026. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed, with treatment rankings assessed by surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values and consistency evaluated via node-splitting analysis.
RESULTS: Seventeen RCTs involving 1,133 participants were included. Combined Tai Chi and Qigong ranked highest for BMI (SUCRA = 92.4%), diastolic blood pressure (SUCRA = 73.8%), and resting heart rate (SUCRA = 82.9%). Tai Chi rehabilitation exercise ranked highest for systolic blood pressure (SUCRA = 66.3%), and Tai Chi Thirteen Postures Daoyin ranked highest for body fat percentage (SUCRA = 87.9%). No significant inconsistency was detected, and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness.
CONCLUSION: Combined Tai Chi and Qigong, Tai Chi rehabilitation exercise, and Tai Chi Thirteen Postures Daoyin emerged as the most promising interventions. These findings provide preliminary evidence for exercise-based rehabilitation strategies, though future head-to-head trials are needed to confirm the observed rankings.

Title: Clinical and Metabolic Correlates of Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy in Long-Standing Type 2 Diabetes: A Tertiary-Care Cross-Sectional Study from Eastern India.
Journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) is a serious and underdiagnosed complication of long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus, associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Data from Indian populations evaluating the relationship between somatic and autonomic neuropathy remain limited.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 98 patients with long-standing type 2 diabetes were evaluated at a tertiary-care center in Eastern India. Somatic neuropathy was assessed clinically and electrophysiologically, while autonomic function was evaluated using standard cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests and galvanic skin response (GSR). CAN was staged as possible, definite, or advanced. Clinical and metabolic correlates were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with CAN.
RESULTS: Distal symmetric polyneuropathy was present in 44.9% of patients, and any peripheral neuropathy was present in 59.2%. CAN was highly prevalent, with definite and advanced CAN observed in 28.6% and 46.9%, respectively. Abnormal GSR was noted in 42.9%, and overall diabetic autonomic involvement (defined as the presence of CAN and/or isolated sudomotor dysfunction) was present in 92.9%. Increasing CAN severity was associated with higher hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) ( P = 0.0055), fasting blood glucose ( P = 0.0083), and age ( P = 0.0027), while duration showed a borderline association ( P = 0.0548). HbA1c was the only variable independently associated with CAN after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio ≈ 2.10 per 1% increase). The sustained handgrip test did not demonstrate a significant association with the presence of CAN (χ 2 , P = 0.712), indicating limited discriminatory ability in this cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Autonomic neuropathy, particularly CAN, was highly prevalent in this cohort of patients with long-standing type 2 diabetes. Poorer glycemic control, reflected by higher HbA1c, showed the strongest independent association with CAN. Comprehensive autonomic assessment should be considered even in the absence of overt somatic neuropathy.

Title: Effects of testosterone on exercise capacity in postmenopausal women with stage B heart failure.
Journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Asymptomatic individuals with stage B heart failure (HF) often have reduced exercise capacity. As exogenous testosterone may have favorable skeletal muscle and vasculature effects, this study investigated whether transdermal testosterone improves exercise capacity in women with stage B HF.
METHOD: In this single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial involving women aged ≥55 years with stage B HF (defined as cardiac remodeling and/or diastolic dysfunction) and reduced exercise capacity (<100% age-predicted peak oxygen uptake V˙O2peak]), participants were randomly allocated to transdermal testosterone 5 mg/day or identical placebo for 4 months with cross-over after a 4-week washout. The primary outcome was change in V˙O2peak. Secondary outcomes included changes to cardiac structure and function assessed by echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and subjective quality of life.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight participants (median age 72 years, range 60-80 years; median body mass index 33.2 kg/m2 [P25-P75 28.7-35.9 kg/m2]) completed the study. Testosterone treatment increased circulating serum testosterone concentrations and was well tolerated, with no adverse treatment-related events. Testosterone treatment had no significant effect on V˙O2peak (β = -0.05, 95% confidence interval = -0.74, 0.65, p = 0.897), cardiac structure or indices of cardiac function, or quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Transdermal testosterone treatment did not improve exercise capacity in postmenopausal women with stage B HF.

Title: Robotic Posterior Retroperitoneoscopic Adrenalectomy: 1-Year Experience at a High-Volume Endocrine Referral Center.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence on multiplatform implementation of robotic posterior retroperitoneoscopic adrenalectomy remains limited. We assessed first-year operative performance in a high-volume endocrine referral center experienced in laparoscopic posterior retroperitoneoscopic and robotic adrenal surgery.
METHODS: All consecutive adults undergoing unilateral total robotic posterior retroperitoneoscopic adrenalectomy between July 2025 and July 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Operative times, perioperative outcomes, chronological trends, cumulative sum curves, and multivariable Gamma generalized linear models were assessed.
RESULTS: Thirty-four procedures were performed: 7 with Toumai, 25 with da Vinci Xi, and 2 with da Vinci SP. Median total operative, docking, console, and procedure times were 59.0, 6.0, 19.0, and 54.0 min, respectively. One conversion to laparoscopic posterior retroperitoneoscopic adrenalectomy occurred (2.9%). Two intraoperative complications (5.9%) and two 30-day postoperative complications (5.9%) were recorded, including one death after postdischarge acute myocardial infarction. Across the cohort, docking time decreased with consecutive case number (Spearman ρ = -0.623; p < 0.001), whereas total operative and console times did not. After adjustment for platform, body mass index, and lesion size in 32 multiport procedures, only docking time remained associated with case number (time ratio 0.980, 95% confidence interval 0.963-0.997; p = 0.021). Cumulative sum inflections occurred around Cases 7-8 but coincided with platform transition.
CONCLUSION: In this limited first-year experience in an expert adrenal surgery program, robotic posterior retroperitoneoscopic adrenalectomy implementation was feasible across three platforms, with adaptation reflected mainly by docking optimization. Platform-specific time differences were descriptive and cannot establish comparative efficiency because platform use was sequential and instrumentation differed across systems.

Title: Allometric Scaling of Left Heart Structure and Function in Elite Cyclists: Development of Sport-Specific Prediction Equations.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elite athletes frequently exceed conventional left ventricular (LV) and left atrial thresholds when guideline-recommended linear scaling for body size is applied, prompting unnecessary investigation. Few athlete-specific allometric equations yield percentage predicted values or Z scores. We aimed to develop allometric equations for LV and left atrial structure and function in elite cyclists, accounting for body size, sex, discipline, and heart rate, and to compare these with body surface area (BSA) indexing.
METHODS: We evaluated 181 elite cyclists (105 male, 76 female; age 22.7±5.5 years; 128 endurance, 53 sprint) with normal preparticipation cardiac screening. Weighted least squares allometric regression determined optimal scaling exponents for height, weight, and BSA, with models advancing in complexity only when prediction accuracy significantly improved. Equations were externally validated in 62 independent elite male endurance cyclists.
RESULTS: Men had larger BSA-scaled LV and left atrial size than women (both P<0.001). Many cyclists exceeded conventional thresholds (American Society of Echocardiography 2015: LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA 69.6%, LV end-systolic volume indexed to BSA 62.9%; British Society of Echocardiography 2020: LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA 50.8%, left atrial volume indexed to BSA 28.7%). Height provided superior allometric fit versus weight or BSA. Height, sex, discipline, and RR interval were key determinants. On external validation, only 6.5% exceeded the Z score threshold for LV end-diastolic volume indexed to BSA, compared with 90.3% classified abnormal by ASE guidelines.
CONCLUSIONS: Height-based allometric scaling outperformed weight or BSA for cardiac dimensions and function in elite cyclists. These sport-specific equations, validated in an independent cohort, provide clinically usable percentage predicted values and Z scores that permit quantitative assessment rather than binary thresholds and may reduce misclassification of physiological adaptation as disease in preparticipation cardiac screening programs.

Title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Incident Cardiovascular Events and Death in Treated Serious Mental Illness, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with serious mental illness (SMI), type 2 diabetes, and obesity have elevated cardiovascular risk. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have established cardiometabolic benefits in the general population, but their effects in SMI are unclear. We evaluated whether GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and all-cause death.
METHODS: This was a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study of 218 043 adults with SMI, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and active antipsychotic or antidepressant medications in the TriNetX database (73 health care organizations). Outcomes were incident MI, HF, and all-cause death at 1 and 3 years. The primary exposure was GLP-1RA use versus nonuse; secondary analyses examined semaglutide or tirzepatide. Exploratory analyses evaluated sex, race, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use.
RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death. Risk differences at 1 and 3 years were -0.007 and -0.010 for MI, -0.011 and -0.018 for HF, and -0.039 and -0.065 for death (all P<0.001). Semaglutide or tirzepatide use was also associated with lower risks of MI, HF, and death (all P<0.001). Findings were directionally consistent after accounting for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor use.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with treated SMI, type 2 diabetes, and obesity using GLP-1RAs, particularly semaglutide or tirzepatide, had significantly reduced 1- and 3-year risks of incident MI, HF, and all-cause death versus nonusers. These pooled associations should be interpreted in the context of SMI's clinical heterogeneity and the limitations of administrative case ascertainment.

Title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain.
