METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year.
RESULTS: Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin.
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Echocardiographic Assessment and Clinical Applications of the Left Atrial Stiffness Index in Cardiovascular Disease.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract: The left atrial stiffness index is an emerging echocardiographic marker that integrates pressure-related burden and atrial reservoir deformation to provide a composite measure of left atrial pressure-deformation coupling. This review summarizes the pathophysiological basis of left atrial stiffness, the methodological principles underlying echocardiographic left atrial stiffness index assessment, and the current evidence supporting its clinical applications across cardiovascular diseases. The strongest evidence is available in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, in which increased left atrial stiffness index has been associated with adverse hemodynamics, exercise intolerance, rhythm recurrence, and adverse clinical outcomes. In hypertension, cardiomyopathies, valvular heart disease, and congenital or aortic disorders, available data suggest potential clinical relevance, although the evidence remains more heterogeneous and less mature; by contrast, evidence in ischemic, inflammatory, and stroke-related settings is still preliminary. Despite its physiological appeal, broader clinical adoption remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, variable thresholds, limited invasive validation, and uncertain incremental value beyond its component measures. At present, left atrial stiffness index is best positioned as an adjunctive marker for phenotyping, hemodynamic assessment, and risk stratification, particularly in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, pending further methodological harmonization and prospective disease-specific validation.

Title: Association of Non-Cytochrome P450 3A4-Metabolized Statins Versus Atorvastatin With Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Cancer Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Propensity Score-Matched Target Trial Emulation.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) often undergo CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4) metabolism. Atorvastatin is a CYP3A4 substrate, whereas rosuvastatin and pitavastatin largely bypass this pathway. We evaluated whether statin choice was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events in TKI-treated patients with cancer.
METHODS: Using TriNetX, we conducted an active-comparator, new-user target trial emulation among adults with cancer receiving their first TKI. The index date was the first statin dispensation; outcome ascertainment began on Day 30 and continued up to 3 years. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons included rosuvastatin versus atorvastatin (primary; 2215 per group), pitavastatin comparisons, and a pooled non-CYP3A4 statin comparison.
RESULTS: Among 10 843 eligible patients (mean age, 66.7 years; 60.7% male), rosuvastatin was associated with a lower major adverse cardiovascular events rate than atorvastatin (624 versus 769 events; hazard ratio [HR], 0.84 [95% CI, 0.76-0.93]). The proportional-hazards assumption was violated (P=0.042), so the HR was interpreted as a time-averaged association. The pooled comparison was concordant (HR, 0.87 [95% CI, 0.78-0.96]). The early-persistence Day-180 estimate was imprecise (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.73-1.09]).
CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin use was associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events than atorvastatin in TKI-treated patients with cancer. This observational finding is compatible with, but does not establish, a CYP3A4-mediated interaction. Residual confounding, nonaligned TKI and statin timing in part of the primary cohort, and lack of individual-level event-time data require prospective confirmation.

Title: Trends in Use of Coronary Angiography, Percutaneous Coronary Intervention, and Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Over a Decade in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass graft are among the most commonly performed procedures globally. The influence of recent scientific evidence on national-level temporal trends remains poorly explored.
METHODS: The frequency, characteristics, and outcomes of elective and nonelective coronary angiography, PCI, and coronary artery bypass graft were described using the French National Hospitalization Database from 2014 to 2023 (covering a population of 67.0 million inhabitants), totaling 6 290 951 coronary interventions among 2 985 822 patients (mean age, 67.8±12.2 years; 69.9% men).
RESULTS: Over 10 years, the annual number of coronary interventions increased by 33%, driven by a rise in coronary angiography (+32%) and PCI (+40%), while coronary artery bypass graft decreased (-8%). The growth in PCI was predominantly related to an increase in elective procedures (from 53.5% to 56.9%, P<0.001), particularly among older patients (+73%), and in multivessel disease (from 16.7% in 2014-2015 to 19.0% in 2022-2023, P<0.001). Attempts to recanalize chronic total coronary occlusion doubled (from 1.9% to 3.3%, P<0.001). In-hospital death after PCI decreased (from 2.05% in 2014 to 1.58% in 2023, P for trend<0.001), with the most notable improvements observed in nonelective PCI. Similarly, in-hospital death after coronary artery bypass graft declined (from 3.5% to 2.9%, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore a significant increase in both coronary angiography and PCI over the past decade in France, particularly in procedures classified as elective among older patients. This trend raises questions about the influence of recent scientific evidence and guidelines on clinical practice in this country.

Title: Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information.
METHODS: In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed.
RESULTS: Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P<0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in patients undergoing coronary CT angiography. Circulating TMAO provides complementary prognostic information and refines risk stratification, particularly among individuals without functionally significant ischemia. Integrating systemic biomarkers with coronary physiological assessment may improve individualized risk evaluation beyond imaging alone.

Title: American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 and Heart Failure in Black Individuals: An Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-reported Black individuals have a disproportionately high prevalence of heart failure (HF) compared with other racial groups. In an effort to empower patients and health providers to combat cardiovascular disease, the American Heart Association identified Life's Essential 8 as the 8 health behaviors crucial for heart health. In this study, we evaluate the association between components of Life's Essential 8 and HF outcomes among Black individuals.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study analyzed 107 622 individuals captured in the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) from 1999 to 2020 who were categorized by self-reported race. To represent Life's Essential 8, variables of self-reported sleep duration, physical activity, smoking status, and dietary habits were used. Additionally, self-reported diagnoses of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart failure were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for the associations between Life's Essential 8 components and HF among Black individuals.
RESULTS: Black individuals were diagnosed with HF at a younger age compared with White individuals (54 years vs 65 years, P<0.001). Among Black individuals, body mass index (odds ratio [OR], 1.041 [95% CI, 1.027-1.055], P=0.02), hypertension (OR, 3.175 [95% CI, 2.14-4.69], P<0.0001), hyperlipidemia (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.76], P=0.02), and diabetes (OR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.60-2.67], P≤0.0001) were associated with increased odds of HF. Physical activity was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.564 [95% CI, 0.38-0.836], P=0.004) of HF in Black individuals.
CONCLUSIONS: Black individuals experienced HF at significantly younger ages, with traditional cardiometabolic factors (body mass index, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes) each independently being associated with HF risk. Physical activity appears protective, underscoring the importance of early, targeted prevention strategies.

Title: Associations of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 Activity With Markers of Endothelial Dysfunction and Oxidative Stress in Young Healthy Adults: The African-PREDICT Study.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone-system plays a major role in the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease through, among others, endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Circulating ACE2 (angiotensin-converting enzyme 2) is emerging as a biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk; however, its role in younger populations is not well-established. This study aimed to investigate sex differences in serum ACE2 activity and associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers in young, apparently healthy men and women.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we included 1134 young (aged 20-30 years) men (n=557) and women (n=577). Serum ACE2 activity was measured using a validated fluorometric assay. We analyzed markers of endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and antioxidant capacity. We performed a 2-sample t test and Mann-Whitney U test. We applied multivariable-adjusted Tobit regression analysis to account for left truncation.
RESULTS: Men had higher ACE2 activity than women (P<0.001). After multiple adjustments for covariates, ACE2 activity was positively associated with von Willebrand factor (P=0.006), and a disintegrin-like metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motif type 1 member 13 (P=0.019) in men. Among women, ACE2 activity was negatively associated with asymmetric dimethylarginine (P=0.043) and superoxide dismutase (P=0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Serum ACE2 activity was higher in men than women and showed sex-specific associations with endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress-related markers. Our results suggest an association between ACE2 shedding and pathophysiological processes associated with alterations in endothelial integrity and early endothelial dysfunction, which may be influenced by sex. This highlights the role of circulating ACE2 as a potential early biomarker of cardiovascular disease risk in young adults.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03292094.

Title: Mental Health Factors in Cardiothoracic Surgery Risk Prediction Models: A Systematic Review.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are associated with substantial morbidity and death in cardiovascular disease, yet their role in perioperative risk stratification remains unclear in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery. We evaluated how mental health disorders are currently incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk prediction models.
METHODS: We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systemic Reviews and Meta-Analysis-concordant systematic review of PubMed and Embase on September 11, 2025 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420251274958). We included studies that developed or validated risk models predicting postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery that either included a mental health disorder as a covariate or validated a model in patients with such disorders. Model characteristics were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systemic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+Artificial Intelligence. Findings were synthesized qualitatively.
RESULTS: Of 17 986 articles screened, 9 studies met inclusion criteria and described 17 unique models. No study validated a model specifically in patients with mental health disorders. Depression was the most frequently included mental health covariate (8 models). When incorporated, mental health disorders had associations comparable to established clinical risk factors. The most frequently modeled outcomes were hospital readmission and postoperative depression. Three studies had a high risk of bias. Covariate selection and modeled outcomes varied substantially.
CONCLUSIONS: Mental health disorders are rarely incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk models despite potentially important prognostic associations. Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.

Title: Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty.
RESULTS: We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

Title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

Title: Association of Poor Adherence to Guideline-Directed Medical Treatment With Adverse Events Including Fatal Arrhythmia in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Nationwide Cohort Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Poor adherence to guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) correlates with increased risks of mortality and hospitalization. Whether it is associated with life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias (VA) remains unclear. We assessed GDMT adherence levels and clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF.
METHODS: Using the National Health Insurance Service database, patients who underwent implantable cardioverter-defibrillator or cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator implantation between 2008 to 2020 for primary prevention were included. Those with sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation/flutter, or aborted sudden cardiac death were excluded. Adherence to renin-angiotensin system blockers (RASB), beta blockers (BB), and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA) was assessed using the weighted proportion of days covered method. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and life-threatening VA.
RESULTS: Among 3,780 patients, prescription rates were 87.5% for RASB, 89.7% for BB, and 74.2% for MRA. Poor adherence was associated with an increased risk of the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 1.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.31-1.82) and all-cause mortality (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.52-2.20) compared with optimal adherence. These associations were more pronounced in ischemic heart failure (HF). Although crude VA event rates were numerically higher with lower adherence, these associations were insignificant after covariate adjustment, regardless of HF etiology.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower GDMT adherence was independently associated with increased mortality despite device therapy, particularly in ischemic HF. Although its relationship with arrhythmic outcomes was unclear, sustained adherence remains important and supports targeted interventions to enhance treatment continuity.

Title: Etiologies and Independent Risk Architecture of 7-Day Graft Loss in Adult Liver Transplantation: A National Registry Analysis.
Journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Seven -day graft loss (first postoperative week graft failure or recipient death ) has not been systematically characterized at a national scale in adult liver transplantation. We identified etiologies and independent predictors of 7 -day graft loss, primary nonfunction, and 7 -day posttransplant death in adult deceased donor liver transplant recipients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 54 646 adult deceased donor liver transplant recipients (Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network, 2015 -2024 )and evaluated etiologies and independent predictors of 7 -day graft loss, primary nonfunction, and 7 -day posttransplant death using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 1442 events of 7 -day graft loss (2.6 % ), primary nonfunction predominated (43.6 % ), followed by graft thrombosis (10.3 % ) and infection (3.8 % ). Cardiovascular failure (42.6 % ) was the leading cause of 7 -day death. Retransplant (odds ratio 3.72; P < .001 ), Status 1 (odds ratio 2.24; P < .001 ), donation after circulatory death (odds ratio 1.82; P < .001 ), dialysis dependence (odds ratio 1.79; P <.001 ), and Black recipient race (odds ratio 1.74; P < .001 ) independently predicted 7 -day graft loss. Male recipient sex was protective (odds ratio 0.86; P = .01 ). Each additional hour of cold ischemia time increased 7 -day graft loss odds by 10 % (odds ratio 1.10; P < .001 ). The primary nonfunction model identified Hispanic (odds ratio 1.27; P = .03 ) and Asian (odds ratio 1.60; P = .02 ) recipient race as additional predictors, with 34 % lower odds from 2020 onward (odds ratio 0.66; P < .001 ), coincident with acuity circle allocation and expanded machine perfusion adoption. The 7 -day death model added recipient age ≥60 years (odds ratio 1.58; P < .001 ) and elevated Model for End -Stage Liver Disease score (odds ratio 1.01; P = .003 ) as independent contributors.
CONCLUSIONS: Every predictor is ascertainable before transplant, supporting risk stratification during organ offers, informed donor -recipient matching, and perioperative optimization to reduce early graft loss.

Title: Collaborative Technology-Assisted Depression Program for Chronic Disease Patients in Santiago, Chile.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of a collaborative, computer-assisted psycho-educational intervention for managing depression in patients with hypertension and/or diabetes in comparison with usual care in primary care clinics in Santiago, Chile.
METHODS: Adults with moderate-to-severe depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] ≥15) enrolled in the Cardiovascular Health Care Program were recruited. The active arm (n = 180) received an eight-session computer-assisted, psycho-educational program, telephone monitoring, and usual care for chronic diseases, while the control group (n = 179) received usual care for depression and chronic diseases. Outcomes were assessed at 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups, with the primary outcome being depression improvement (50% decrease in PHQ-9 score) at 6 months. Intention-to-treat analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: The active arm showed non-statistically significant reductions in depressive symptoms and improvements in mental health-related quality of life, treatment adherence, and health care utilization compared to the control arm.
CONCLUSIONS: While results did not demonstrate statistical difference within the programs to treat the health problems included in the study, the findings support the use of computer-assisted psychoeducation intervention.
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: These findings advocate for optimizing current care models by incorporating scalable, evidence-based interventions, such as technology-assisted programs, to address remaining gaps in mental health integration.

Title: Predicting prolonged mechanical ventilation in neonates after cardiac surgery: development of a nomogram for risk prediction based on preoperative and intraoperative factors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite improvements in neonatal cardiac surgery, prolonged mechanical ventilation remains a prevalent postoperative complication. This study was designed to build a prolonged mechanical ventilation prediction model based on preoperative and intraoperative factors in neonates (0-28 days) after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on perioperative data of 385 newborns undergoing cardiac surgery at Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital from 2018 to 2024. Prolonged mechanical ventilation was defined as postoperative mechanical ventilation duration >7 days.
RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors, visualised via a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by area under receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified airway anomalies (odds ratio = 2.280, 95% confidence interval 1.217-4.271, P = 0.010), preoperative mechanical ventilation (odds ratio = 2.244, 95% confidence interval 1.283-3.925, P = 0.005), radical surgery (odds ratio = 0.220, 95% confidence interval 0.091-0.533, P < 0.001), intraoperative red blood cell transfusion volumes (odds ratio = 1.529, 95% confidence interval 1.065-2.195, P = 0.021), intraoperative elevated lactate levels (odds ratio = 2.352, 95% confidence interval 1.256-4.403, P = 0.008), and higher vasoactive-inotropic score at the end of surgery (odds ratio = 1.060, 95% confidence interval 1.023-1.199, P = 0.001) as risk factors for prolonged mechanical ventilation. The nomogram achieved an area under the receiver operating curve of 0.784, with robust calibration and clinical utility. Prolonged mechanical ventilation was associated with prolonged hospital stay (median 23 vs. 16 days, P < 0.001) and increased hospital mortality (12.3% vs. 1.1%, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This model accurately stratifies the risks of prolonged mechanical ventilation in neonates after cardiac surgery, potentially guiding postoperative management.

Title: Prediction of 10-Year Incident Hypertension After Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
Journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a model including pregnancy-related factors for the prediction of incident hypertension after pregnancy and to assess the impact of pregnancy-related factors on model performance.
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Routine primary care data linked to the data from the Dutch Perinatal Registry and Statistics Netherlands.
POPULATION: Women with a first childbirth at ≥ 24 weeks' gestation between 2007 and 2019 were included and were followed for up to 10 years after childbirth.
METHODS: Two Cox proportional hazards models were developed to estimate the 10-year risk of hypertension. Model 1 included sociodemographic factors and CVD-related factors, while model 2 additionally included pregnancy-related factors.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ten-year risk of incident hypertension.
RESULTS: We included 28 234 women, of which 639 developed hypertension (cumulative 10-year incidence 3.3%). The C-index of model 1 was 0.659 (95% CI: 0.642-0.684) and increased to 0.772 (95% CI: 0.754-0.796) after the addition of pregnancy-related factors. The C-index difference was 0.113 (95% CI: 0.092-0.132), mostly driven by the inclusion of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Net reclassification improvement was 0.213 (95% CI: 0.159-0.273) for events and 0.001 (95% CI: -0.004 to 0.006) for non-events.
CONCLUSIONS: Our prediction model for hypertension showed good discrimination and calibration after the addition of pregnancy-related factors. This model may help to target cardiovascular risk management for women with a high risk of hypertension after pregnancy in order to improve women's cardiovascular health.

Title: Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT).
Abstract:
AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo.
METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers.
RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

Title: Active Helicobacter pylori Infection and Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection may promote systemic inflammation and has been proposed as a contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF), but clinical evidence is inconsistent. The aim of the study was to explore whether active H. pylori infection was associated with AF in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included adults from a two-center observational AMI cohort. Active H. pylori infection was assessed during hospitalization using a urea breath test (UBT). AF was defined as AF documented before admission or identified during the index hospitalization. Associations were estimated using logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, center, and smoking. Exploratory multivariable interaction analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: Of 310 enrolled patients, 300 had conclusive H. pylori screening results; 60 (20.0%) were positive. AF was recorded in 4 of 60 H. pylori-positive patients (6.7%) and 30 of 240 H. pylori-negative patients (12.5%). H. pylori positivity was not significantly associated with recorded AF (unadjusted OR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.17-1.41; p = 0.228; adjusted OR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.16-1.46; p = 0.235). These estimates refer to pooled AF; only four AF cases occurred among patients testing positive.
CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant association was detected between H. pylori breath-test positivity and pooled documented AF among patients hospitalized with AMI, but a clinically meaningful association cannot be excluded. Larger prospective studies with longitudinal follow-up are needed to clarify whether active H. pylori infection is associated with incident AF after AMI.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Chios Mastic in Well-Controlled Hypertension: Findings From the HYPER-MASTIC Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Residual cardiovascular risk persists in patients with adequately controlled hypertension, driven partly by inflammation, oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Chios mastic (Pistacia lentiscus var. Chia) has shown antihypertensive, antioxidant and vascular effects in experimental and clinical settings. This trial evaluated whether Chios mastic supplementation confers additional cardiovascular benefits in well-controlled hypertensive individuals. In this double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 106 adults with stable, well-controlled hypertension and variable cardiovascular risk, based on SCORE2, received low-dose Chios mastic (1500 mg/day), high-dose Chios mastic (2800 mg/day) or placebo for 3 months. Primary endpoints were changes in 24-h ambulatory systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Secondary endpoints included vascular function, oxidative stress and proteasome activity in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and red blood cells. Transcriptomic profiling was performed in a predefined high-risk subgroup. Chios mastic supplementation was well tolerated, with high adherence confirmed by dose-dependent increases in plasma masticadienonic and isomasticadienonic acids. No significant between-group differences were observed in 24-h systolic or diastolic blood pressure after the intervention. Oxidative stress markers and proteasome activity remained unchanged across groups. In high-risk participants, mastic supplementation induced distinct transcriptomic changes, particularly in pathways related to endothelial junction organization and vascular integrity. Overall, in adults with well-controlled hypertension and low baseline cardiovascular risk, Chios mastic supplementation did not lower blood pressure over 3 months, likely reflecting a ceiling effect. Transcriptomic findings suggest biologically meaningful vascular effects in individuals with higher residual cardiovascular risk, supporting future investigation in higher-risk populations.

Title: Real-World Invasive Evaluation of Myocardial Bridging: A Multicenter Italian Survey of Interventional Cardiologists' Practices.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial bridging (MB) is increasingly recognized as a potential cause of ischemia through heterogeneous mechanisms, yet real-world management remains heterogeneous. We surveyed interventional cardiologists to describe contemporary MB practice, focusing on functional assessments, perceived value, and barriers to the "full-physiology" approach, and priorities for standardization and research.
AIMS: To characterize contemporary MB management among interventional cardiologists, focusing on physiology approaches, imaging strategies, and perceived barriers to implementation and treatment.
METHODS: An anonymized online survey was conducted among interventional cardiologists from 28 Italian centers. Items covered MB-specific functional assessment strategies, therapies, implementation barriers, operational infrastructure, and research interest.
RESULTS: Ninety-three cardiologists responded (mean age 38.8 ± 8.6 years; 82.8% male). Pressure-based indices were widely used for epicardial CAD, but phenotyping in MB was uncommon: 57.0% performed physiology in < 10% of MB cases, and 19.4% never did. Epicardial MB assessment relied mainly on adenosine-FFR (33.3%) or iFR (31.2%), whereas stress-enhanced protocols were rarely used. Although intracoronary acetylcholine testing was commonly used in general practice (79.6%), only 49.5% of respondents reported using it to assess MB-related coronary spasm, and most did so in only a small proportion of cases. CMD testing in MB was rare (< 10% in 66.7%). Despite this, most respondents (87.1%) endorsed "full-physiology" as useful for mechanism identification and personalized therapy, but cited evidence uncertainty, procedural time, and limited experience as key barriers. Operational readiness was low (dedicated protocols: 26.9%; registries: 39.8%; routine capture: 34.4%). Willingness to join a randomized trial was high (93.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite the widespread availability of invasive functional assessment tools and operators' recognition of their relevance, their use in MB remains limited and heterogeneous, reflecting the lack of evidence-based guidance and underscoring the need for dedicated mechanistic studies and standardized invasive workflows.

Title: Serum vs. Dietary Magnesium and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Saudi Adolescents.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Magnesium (Mg) is an essential micronutrient that participates in more than 300 enzymatic reactions, with well-established functions in glucose and lipid metabolism and cardiovascular health. Although serum Mg is routinely used in clinical practice, circulating concentrations may not accurately represent total body Mg status because of tight physiological regulation. The present study evaluated the associations of serum Mg concentration and dietary Mg intake with cardiometabolic outcomes in a cohort of Saudi adolescents. Methods: This cross-sectional study involved 234 Saudi adolescents (166 girls, 68 boys; mean age 14.8 ± 1.7 years) who were assessed for anthropometrics, biochemical parameters and dietary intake. Hypomagnesemia was classified as serum Mg <0.75 mmol/L, while inadequate dietary Mg intake was based on age- and sex-specific cutoffs for children. Results: Hypomagnesemia was present in 87 participants (37.2%) and was more common among boys than girls (50% vs. 31.9%, p = 0.011). No significant differences in the assessed cardiometabolic measurements were observed across serum Mg tertiles. Absolute dietary Mg intake was strongly correlated with total energy and other dietary intakes and was inversely associated with body mass index. Associations based on absolute dietary Mg intake were attenuated after energy adjustment for overweight/obesity. For elevated triglycerides, the highest vs. lowest tertile of residual-adjusted Mg showed a nominal inverse association in the age- and sex-adjusted model (OR: 0.40; 95% CI: 0.17-0.96). However, the corresponding trend did not remain statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. Conclusions: Serum Mg showed limited associations with cardiometabolic outcomes, while associations between dietary Mg and cardiometabolic outcomes were sensitive to energy adjustment and multiple-comparison correction. The inverse association between residual-adjusted Mg and elevated triglycerides should therefore be considered exploratory. These findings highlight potential differences between serum and dietary Mg as indicators of Mg status and underscore the importance of accounting for total energy intake when examining dietary Mg in relation to cardiometabolic health in adolescents.

Title: Association Between Diet Quality and 20-Year Heart Failure Incidence: Findings from the ATTICA Cohort Study (2002-2022).
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Diet quality is a potentially modifiable determinant of heart failure (HF), yet evidence regarding its long-term association with HF incidence remains limited. This study examined the association between baseline diet quality and 20-year incident HF in the population-based ATTICA cohort. Methods: Among 3042 adults free of cardiovascular disease at baseline (2001-2002), HF status was available for 2159 participants in 2022, of whom 241 (11.2%) developed HF. Diet quality, including the relative contributions of healthy and unhealthy food groups, was assessed using the Global Diet Quality Score (GDQS), derived from a validated food-frequency questionnaire. Logistic regression models were sequentially adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, education, physical activity, smoking burden, hypertension, diabetes, and hypercholesterolemia. Results: HF incidence was 20.7%, 5.1%, and 6.6% among participants with low, intermediate, and high diet quality, respectively (p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted analysis (n = 1973), better overall diet quality was associated with lower odds of HF (odds ratio [OR] per 1-point increment, 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94-0.99). A greater contribution of healthy foods was also inversely associated with HF (OR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.93-0.98), whereas the unhealthy-food component was not independently associated with the outcome (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.96-1.13). Conclusions: Better diet quality, particularly greater consumption of health-promoting foods, was independently associated with lower 20-year HF incidence in a Mediterranean population.

Title: Ketogenic Dietary Therapies and β-Hydroxybutyrate as Modulators of Mitochondrial Function: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Translation.
Abstract: Ketogenic dietary therapies (KDTs) have been used for a century in drug-resistant epilepsy, and β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), the major ketone body, is recognized as a signaling metabolite. This review examines how KDTs and BHB modulate mitochondrial function and evaluates evidence supporting these mechanisms. BHB is oxidized through D-β-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase 1 and succinyl-CoA:3-oxoacid-CoA transferase and alters redox balance and oxidative phosphorylation. It also inhibits class I histone deacetylases, serves as the substrate for lysine β-hydroxybutyrylation, activates hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 2, and blocks the NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 inflammasome. These pathways influence redox defense, organelle quality, and inflammation. However, ketogenic feeding suppresses mitochondrial one-carbon metabolism and some signaling effects occur only at BHB concentrations exceeding those typically achieved through dietary ketosis. Clinical benefits are best established in drug-resistant epilepsy and appear genotype-dependent in primary mitochondrial disease, with potential benefit in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variant carriers but possible harm in DNA polymerase gamma-related disease and mtDNA deletion myopathy. Outside neurology, human evidence includes a hemodynamic response to infused 3-hydroxybutyrate in heart failure, sustained glycemic improvement in non-randomized diabetes cohorts, and small trials in psychiatric and oncological populations. Most clinical studies have not directly measured mitochondrial outcomes. Proposed mitochondrial mechanisms of KDTs and BHB remain plausible but are not established explanations for clinical benefit. Genotype-stratified trials, ketone exposure assessment, and direct measurement of mitochondrial variables in patients are needed.

Title: Longitudinal Changes in Left Ventricular Structure and Function During a Dietary Weight-Management Trial in Adults with Heart Failure, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity: A Secondary Analysis of Pro-HEART.
Abstract: Background: Obesity is associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in heart failure (HF), but changes during dietary weight management are not well described. We examined longitudinal changes in left ventricular (LV) structure and systolic function during a dietary weight-management intervention. Methods: Pro-HEART participants were randomized to high-protein or standard-protein hypocaloric diets. LV end-diastolic dimension (LVEDD), ejection fraction (LVEF), and posterior wall thickness (LVPWT) were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 15 months. Linear mixed-effects models tested time and diet effects. Results: At 15 months, LVEDD data were available for 31 of 92 participants (33.7%). Achieved protein intake was similar between randomized groups. Among 92 participants, LVEDD changed significantly over time (F(2, 51.20) = 7.45, p = 0.001), with model-estimated mean LVEDD decreasing from 59.00 mm at baseline to 54.56 mm at 15 months. LVEDD decreased from 3 to 15 months (-4.42 mm; 95% CI, -7.52 to -1.33; nominal p = 0.006; Holm-adjusted p = 0.012) and from baseline to 15 months (-4.44 mm; 95% CI, -6.86 to -2.02; nominal p < 0.001; Holm-adjusted p = 0.002). LVEF did not change significantly over time (overall p = 0.074); an exploratory baseline-to-15-month contrast was +4.11 percentage points (95% CI, 0.55-7.67; Holm-adjusted p = 0.072). LVPWT did not change significantly, and no diet group × time interactions were observed. Conclusions: LVEDD was lower at longer-term follow-up. LVEF did not change significantly over time, although an exploratory baseline-to-15-month contrast suggested an increase. Because both groups received hypocaloric diets, there was no non-dietary control group, and longitudinal HF medication data were unavailable, the observed cardiac changes cannot be attributed specifically to weight loss or the dietary intervention.

Title: Association of Nut Consumption with Dementia and Alzheimer's Disease.
Abstract: Background: Nut consumption reduces risks of cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease and depression. However, its association with dementia and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains unclear. Methods: A population-based case-control study was conducted in China, including 466 participants aged 52-100 years (233 with dementia). Data on socio-demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, comorbidities, and dietary intake over the past two years were collected through structured face-to-face interviews. Nut consumption was categorised as non-consumption or <monthly, ≥monthly but <weekly, ≥weekly but <daily, daily, and ≥twice daily. Multiple adjusted logistic regression models were employed to examine the association of nut consumption with dementia and AD. Results: Of the 466 participants, 59.0% reported consuming nuts at non-consumption or <monthly, 22.5% monthly, 11.8% weekly, 6.0% daily, and 0.6% ≥ twice daily. Compared with non-consumption or <monthly consumption, the age-adjusted odds ratio (OR) for dementia was 0.31 (95% CI 0.18-0.52) for monthly intake, 0.52 (0.28-0.97) for weekly intake, and 0.32 (0.14-0.72) for daily or higher intake. After further adjustment for gender, education, family income, marital status, smoking, stroke, chronic bronchitis, depression, and other dietary intakes, OR was 0.27 (0.13-0.55) for monthly intake and 0.47 (0.23-0.99) for ≥weekly intake. Among 133 participants with AD, similar associations were observed, with a fully adjusted OR of 0.34 (0.17-0.69) for ≥monthly nut consumption. Conclusions: Higher nut consumption was associated with reduced risks of dementia and AD. Increasing nut intake may represent a potential strategy for dementia and AD prevention. However, large-scale cohort and interventional studies are needed to further clarify the association and determine the magnitude of the effect.

Title: Iron Supplementation and Copper Homeostasis: Evidence for Potential Copper Depletion, Biomarker Challenges, and Clinical Implications.
Abstract: Iron deficiency remains a major nutritional problem, particularly among women of reproductive age, pregnant women, infants, and children. Oral iron supplementation is the principal strategy for prevention and treatment, but the biological interdependence of iron and copper metabolism raises concern that prolonged or excessive iron exposure may impair copper availability in susceptible individuals. This review summarizes human and animal evidence linking iron supplementation or high dietary iron intake to altered copper homeostasis, with emphasis on underlying mechanisms, biomarker limitations, and clinical implications. Human studies report inconsistent changes in serum copper and ceruloplasmin, suggesting that baseline mineral status, physiological demand, iron dose, treatment duration, inflammation, and biomarker selection may influence responses. Animal studies provide stronger mechanistic evidence that high iron intake can reduce intestinal copper absorption and copper-dependent ferroxidase activity, promote tissue iron sequestration, and contribute to anemia, impaired growth, cardiac enlargement, dyslipidemia, gastrointestinal alterations, and disrupted maternal-offspring copper transfer. However, the clinical relevance of these findings remains uncertain because standardized diagnostic criteria and sensitive biomarkers for marginal copper deficiency are lacking. Iron intervention should remain guided by confirmed iron status, while dose, duration, and treatment response warrant careful consideration. Evaluation of copper status may be particularly relevant when hematological recovery is inadequate despite sufficient iron stores or when additional risk factors for copper deficiency are present. Prospective human studies incorporating functional biomarkers are needed to identify susceptible populations and clinically relevant exposure conditions.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Dielectric Fingerprinting of Arrhythmogenic Substrates: A Precision Paradigm for Tissue Characterization Guided Cardiac Electrophysiology.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrical and dielectric properties of the myocardium depend on its composition, fibrosis, edema, ischemia, and heat damage, and hence may play an important role in defining the electrophysiologic substrate. Local impedance and other impedance-based methods give information about these parameters that is available to clinicians, but not direct or substitutable for intrinsic conductivity and permittivity of the tissue. The use of artificial intelligence has been thoroughly studied for the ECGs, electrograms, images, and computational data analysis, but not for dielectric or impedance measurements.
OBJECTIVE: The study aims to review the scientific basis of dielectric properties of heart muscle critically in cardiology and electrophysiology, to differentiate between existing clinical and conceptual applications of myocardial dielectrics, and to estimate current and potential contributions of artificial intelligence to their interpretation.
DATA SOURCES AND STUDY SELECTION: The current work represents a structured narrative review in PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases from inception until May 2026 based on various combinations of keywords that refer to myocardial impedance, dielectric properties, conductivity, permittivity, local impedance, dielectric imaging, cardiac electrophysiology, catheter ablation, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. This review included experimental, ex vivo, animal, computational, and human studies related to myocardial dielectric properties and their use in electrophysiology. Evidence was classified according to four categories: direct human clinical evidence; preclinical/translation evidence; indirect evidence from related techniques; and extrapolation concept. As a result of heterogeneity between studies, sensing technologies, and outcomes, the results have been analyzed narratively.
KEY FINDINGS: Evidence regarding the usage of AI algorithms, which have been primarily trained on myocardial dielectric or catheter-based local impedance data, is extremely scarce and mostly consists of preclinical or ex vivo data. On the contrary, the majority of clinically used AI algorithms in the field of electrophysiology make use of ECG data, intracardiac electrogram data, image processing, or computational modeling without any inputs related to dielectrics or local impedance.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Dielectric sensing is an attractive supplement to traditional methods of voltage mapping and imaging, although the clinical readiness of dielectric sensing greatly varies depending on the application. At the present time, the existing data provide a basis for utilizing the local impedance measurement in the ablation procedure and evaluation of the myocardium properties, while the combination of artificial intelligence and dielectric sensing is still experimental. Before being introduced into the clinical electrophysiology practice, signal acquisition standardization and prospective multicenter trials are needed.

Title: Artificial Intelligence and Sensing Technologies for Vascular Access in Hemodialysis: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Vascular access performance determines the adequacy, safety, and cost of hemodialysis. Stenosis, thrombosis, cannulation difficulty, infection, and access-related cardiac stress remain major sources of morbidity. This narrative review examines artificial intelligence and sensing technologies for vascular access care, based on PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov searches through 22 August 2026 with citation chaining. Existing reviews have examined artificial intelligence in dialysis broadly or prediction models in isolation. In this review, the vascular access itself is kept as the unit of analysis, and the evidence is followed across four connected stages: systemic risk stratification; prediction of maturation, dysfunction, and complications from clinical, ultrasound, and multimodal data; longitudinal monitoring with optical, acoustic, vibration, thermal, and pressure sensors; and procedural support with robotics and visualization technologies. Reported discrimination is high in retrospective, recording-level analyses, reaching areas under the curve of 0.99 and sample-level accuracy of 100%, but falls to approximately 0.71 in longitudinal designs that predict future events in the same patients; patient-level external validation and calibration are also rarely reported. No approach has yet been demonstrated to reduce thrombosis, prolong patency, avoid interventions, or lower cost relative to standard care in prospective multicenter studies. Deployment is further constrained by power budgets, duty cycling, and transmission bandwidth in wearable devices. Technical feasibility should not be read as clinical utility.

Title: Molecular Biomarkers Linking Psoriasis and Cardiovascular Disease: Current Evidence and Clinical Perspectives.
Abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory disease affecting the skin, nails, and joints. Its complex pathogenesis results from interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors and is accompanied by an increased risk of multiple systemic comorbidities, particularly cardiovascular disease. Growing evidence indicates that both conditions share common molecular pathways driven by chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, metabolic disturbances, and immune dysregulation. Among the emerging molecular biomarkers, chemerin, endocan, and growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) have attracted considerable attention due to their role in vascular homeostasis, adipose tissue biology, glucose metabolism, and inflammatory signaling. This review summarizes current evidence on the involvement of these biomarkers in psoriasis and cardiovascular disease, highlighting their contribution to the molecular mechanisms underlying the psoriasis-cardiovascular disease axis. Furthermore, we discussed their potential usefulness as candidate biomarkers for cardiovascular risk. However, prospective validation is strictly required to confirm their clinical utility and establish their incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors.

Title: Tracking Active Fibroblast-Mediated Tissue Remodelling in Cardiomyopathies: Translational Insights from FAPI PET Imaging.
Abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a major pathological component of cardiac remodelling and contributes to ventricular stiffness, impaired myocardial function, heart failure progression, and arrhythmic vulnerability across a broad spectrum of cardiomyopathies. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), fibrotic remodelling encompasses both diffuse interstitial matrix expansion and focal replacement fibrosis and is closely associated with disease severity and adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and quantitative parametric mapping, is central to non-invasive myocardial tissue characterization. LGE primarily identifies focal areas of replacement fibrosis and scar, whereas native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) mapping provide complementary information on diffuse myocardial and interstitial tissue abnormalities, including extracellular matrix expansion. However, these techniques characterize the structural and tissue-level consequences of myocardial injury and remodelling rather than directly visualizing the cellular processes underlying fibroblast activation. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography (FAPI PET) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging approach for assessing active fibroblast-mediated tissue remodelling. By targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a cell-surface serine protease upregulated in activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. FAPI radiotracers may provide a molecular readout of accessible FAP expression that complements structural and tissue characterization by CMR. This review examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying active myocardial remodelling, with particular emphasis on transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad signalling, fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, FAP expression, and extracellular matrix turnover. We critically evaluate the current clinical evidence for FAPI PET/CT and hybrid PET/CMR across cardiomyopathies, focusing on HCM while also considering ischemic, inflammatory, infiltrative, and other non-ischemic forms of cardiac remodelling. Particular attention is given to the relationship between myocardial FAPI uptake, CMR tissue characterization, ventricular function, circulating biomarkers, and calculated arrhythmic risk. Although initial studies support the complementary value of FAPI PET and CMR for characterizing active and established myocardial remodelling, the available evidence remains limited by small, predominantly single-centre cohorts, heterogeneous radiotracers and acquisition protocols, and the absence of validated quantitative thresholds or prospective outcome data. Larger longitudinal studies are required to determine whether FAPI PET can provide incremental prognostic information or serve as a reproducible imaging biomarker for disease progression and therapeutic response.

Title: Serum Argininosuccinic Acid Is Associated with Diabetes in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease: An Exploratory Targeted LC-MS/MS Study.
Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is associated with metabolic alterations, but amino-acid differences among patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) remain incompletely characterized. We screened 45 amino acids and related metabolites by diabetes status in an exploratory retrospective disease-restricted cohort (recorded diseased-vessel count ≥ 1; n = 33). Argininosuccinic acid was available for 26 patients. Comparisons used exact Wilcoxon tests, Cliff's delta, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Estimated argininosuccinic acid concentrations were higher in diabetes (0.28 [0.21-0.34] vs. 0.15 [0.13-0.19] µmol/L; Cliff's delta = 0.765; p < 0.001; q = 0.035), the only association surviving false-discovery-rate correction. All argininosuccinic acid estimates were extrapolated below the lowest calibrator and should be interpreted as semiquantitative. The diabetes coefficient remained positive in crude and age- and sex-adjusted HC3-robust models, but renal and influence analyses were imprecise. Argininosuccinic acid correlated inversely with eGFR (rho = -0.445; p = 0.023) and positively with creatinine (rho = 0.486; p = 0.012). The diabetes-by-CAD interaction was not significant (p = 0.183). These data suggest a hypothesis-generating association requiring validation with an appropriate calibration range and careful renal phenotyping.

Title: Integrative Transcriptomics and Machine Learning Nominate IL15- and PPP2R1A-Centered Programs in PTSD Using Pathway-Informed Autonomic-Cardiac Gene Prioritization.
Abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with immune and autonomic disturbances, but molecular programs linking PTSD-related blood transcriptional signals with autonomic-cardiac biology remain incompletely characterized. The public Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) cohorts analyzed here did not directly measure palpitations or autonomic dysfunction. Peripheral-blood transcriptomes from GSE81761 and GSE63878 were integrated with a prespecified pathway-derived autonomic-cardiac gene set constructed from Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways. Genes overlapping the curated pathway set were assessed using functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses. Multi-algorithm comparison and a separate random-forest/SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis were performed for internal model assessment and biological prioritization. GSE64813 and GSE97356 were analyzed using targeted single-gene analyses and cohort-specific multivariable logistic models. Model performance was examined using repeated nested cross-validation, a fully nested sensitivity analysis, and locked-transfer testing to GSE64813 and GSE97356. Interleukin 15 (IL15) and protein phosphatase 2 scaffold subunit Aalpha (PPP2R1A) were evaluated using external-cohort analyses, immune-cell deconvolution, and descriptive postmortem hippocampal single-nucleus data. Among 1679 nominally significant PTSD-associated candidate genes, 92 overlapped the curated pathway set and were enriched for cytokine signaling, chemotaxis, apoptosis, calcium transport, and PP2A-related functions. PPI analysis yielded 37 recurrent candidate hub genes. The original model comparison ranked support-vector machine (SVM) the highest across the merged and source-cohort summaries [mean area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC) 0.853], but these estimates represent internal discovery-stage performance. IL15 was recurrently prioritized by network-based analyses, whereas PPP2R1A was a component of an enriched phosphatase-related module. IL15 and PPP2R1A showed modest single-gene effects in GSE64813 (AUC 0.566 and 0.612) and GSE97356 (AUC 0.558 and 0.593). Cohort-specific refitted models showed apparent AUC values of 0.834 and 0.749, respectively. Repeated nested cross-validation conditional on the preselected 29-gene feature set identified L2-regularized logistic regression as the best-performing algorithm (mean AUC = 0.690). Importantly, a more stringent fully nested sensitivity analysis, in which differential-expression screening and pathway intersection were repeated within each outer training fold, yielded a mean repeated outer-cross-validated AUC of 0.593 [standard deviation (SD) = 0.033; range, 0.541-0.625], indicating limited predictive performance. Locked-transfer AUCs were 0.664 in GSE64813 and 0.534 in GSE97356. Single-nucleus summaries suggested donor- and nucleus-type-dependent expression patterns for IL15 and PPP2R1A. These findings identify IL15-related cytokine signaling and PPP2R1A-related phosphatase regulation as candidate molecular programs linking PTSD-associated transcriptional variation with pathway-derived autonomic-cardiac biology. The results should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than direct molecular evidence for unmeasured palpitation symptoms. Prospective validation in independent, clinically well-characterized cohorts with standardized autonomic and cardiac phenotyping is warranted.

Title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Iron Overload Disorders: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis of Bioenergetic Dysfunction, Oxidative Stress, and Biomarker-Guided Management.
Abstract: Iron overload associated with transfusion-dependent disorders promotes oxidative stress, mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction, and ferroptotic cell death. Although iron chelation therapy remains the cornerstone of management, the mechanistic links between iron burden, subcellular injury, and emerging biomarkers have not been comprehensively integrated within a clinically relevant framework. This systematic review aimed to synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence on the effects of iron chelation therapy on systemic iron burden, mitochondrial bioenergetics, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and biomarker-guided management. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published from January 2000 to June 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The database search yielded 465 records. After removing 120 duplicates, 345 unique records were screened by title and abstract, of which 210 did not satisfy the predefined eligibility criteria. The remaining 135 articles underwent full-text assessment; 45 were excluded because of inappropriate study design (n = 20), lack of relevant outcomes (n = 15), or unavailable full texts (n = 10). Of the 90 remaining articles, 29 studies (7 randomized controlled trials, 6 observational studies, 3 systematic reviews or guidelines, 6 experimental animal studies and 7 in vitro or cellular mechanistic studies) were included for qualitative narrative synthesis. An additional 61 review articles, guidelines, and epidemiological reports were retained for background context. Methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and SYRCLE tools. Clinical evidence indicated that deferoxamine, deferiprone, and deferasirox consistently reduce systemic iron burden, reflected by improvements in serum ferritin, liver iron concentration, and cardiac T2* magnetic resonance imaging. Circulating iron-related biomarkers, including non-transferrin-bound iron and labile plasma iron, provided additional information on redox-active iron exposure. Preclinical evidence further suggested that iron chelation may attenuate mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptotic signaling. However, mechanistic biomarkers of mitochondrial bioenergetics, oxidative injury, and ferroptosis remain insufficiently validated in prospective clinical populations. Considerable heterogeneity in study populations, interventions, biomarker methodologies, and clinical and mechanistic outcomes limited direct quantitative comparison and supported a narrative synthesis approach. Current evidence supports iron chelation as an effective strategy for reducing systemic iron burden, while emerging bioenergetic, redox, and ferroptosis-related biomarkers provide promising mechanistic insights into iron-mediated cellular injury. Nevertheless, their clinical utility remains uncertain because of limited prospective validation, methodological heterogeneity, and insufficient standardization. Future translational studies should integrate conventional iron indices with validated mitochondrial and redox biomarkers and determine whether biomarker-guided chelation strategies can improve clinically meaningful outcomes beyond conventional iron-burden monitoring.

Title: Targeting the Gut Vascular Axis in Atherosclerosis: Probiotic and Phytoantioxidant Crosstalk as a Hypothesis-Generating Framework for Residual Cardiovascular Risk.
Abstract: Despite decades of effective statin therapy, a clinically important proportion of patients with atherosclerosis continue to experience ischemic events, even when low-density-lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is at guideline-recommended levels. This shortfall is increasingly attributed to residual inflammatory, oxidative, and gut microbial pathways that lipid lowering therapy was never designed to address. This review establishes the mechanistic rationale for combining two emerging dietary intervention classes, probiotics and phytoantioxidants, as adjuncts acting on the gut vascular axis. We systematically trace the evidence for each class. For probiotics, we elucidate the restoration of gut-barrier integrity, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) signaling, bile acid metabolism, and suppression of the trimethylamine to trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMA-TMAO) axis, including strain-specific efficacy and sex-based disparities in microbial composition. For phytoantioxidants, we detail the activation of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), suppression of mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling, and sirtuin 1 (SIRT1)-dependent endothelial protection. We critically appraise the biological plausibility of their combined administration while explicitly defining where this rationale remains a testable hypothesis rather than an established strategy. To date, only one small randomized trial has evaluated a combined probiotic and phytoantioxidant formulation against an atherosclerosis relevant biomarker, and it lacked single-agent comparator arms necessary to attribute benefit to synergy rather than individual components. Furthermore, evidence for each class alone remains constrained by small sample sizes and heterogeneous dosing. Finally, we propose a novel, sex-stratified, strain-specified combination trial framework designed to rigorously evaluate this dual-target approach. This synthesis is intended to generate testable hypotheses for future research rather than to establish an evidence base for current adjunctive clinical use.

Title: Egg-Derived Lipids and Phospholipids as Emerging Functional Ingredients: Molecular Structure, Bioavailability, Metabolic Effects, and Food Applications.
Abstract: Egg yolk is often treated in the functional-food literature as a single, compositionally uniform fat depot, but this simplification obscures its actual structure: the yolk is a compartmentalized lipid system in which egg-yolk lipids are distributed between a triglyceride-dominant, low-density-lipoprotein (LDL) plasma fraction and a phospholipid-enriched, high-density-lipoprotein (HDL) granule fraction. Prior reviews of egg-yolk lipid bioactivity, extraction methodology, and flavor chemistry have generally addressed these topics as separate studies; here, molecular architecture, extraction and characterization, gastrointestinal digestion and bioaccessibility, human bioavailability and metabolic fate, health outcomes, and technological functionality are synthesized as stages of a single pathway. The compositional asymmetry between the LDL plasma fraction and the HDL granule fraction is well established, and differences in their emulsifying behavior are supported by the technological literature; divergent metabolic effects of the isolated fractions have so far been shown only in animal models, whereas differences in digestion kinetics are inferred from structure and remain a working hypothesis because direct experimental comparison of the digestion of isolated HDL and LDL fractions is still lacking. On the human evidence side, a single randomized crossover trial in 18 healthy adults found a higher plasma choline response to phospholipid-bound choline than to choline delivered as a synthetic salt, a preliminary finding that awaits replication, while two crossover studies found no significant postprandial rise in plasma cholesterol area under the curve after whole-egg intake. Because this is an indirect, postprandial measure rather than a direct assessment of intestinal absorption, it is consistent with, but does not establish, limited cholesterol absorption from the whole-egg matrix, and whether whole-egg cholesterol should be distinguished from isolated dietary cholesterol exposure in the epidemiological literature remains a hypothesis. Large prospective meta-analyses report that egg and dietary cholesterol intake associate modestly with elevated all-cause and cancer mortality, but not with cardiovascular-disease-specific mortality or events; these observational associations describe health outcomes and do not, on their own, test a mechanistic distinction between whole-egg cholesterol and isolated dietary cholesterol absorption. Extraction and delivery-system technology for egg phospholipids is more advanced than commonly assumed, with pilot-scale supercritical-fluid purification already achieved and egg-yolk phosphatidylcholine reported to show formulation-specific advantages over soybean phosphatidylcholine in individual liposome studies, although these studies differ in cargo, preparation method, and outcome measures. This delivery-system evidence, however, remains at the level of isolated liposome formulations; finished food products incorporating egg-phospholipid liposomes, with accompanying sensory or consumer-acceptance validation, have not yet been reported. The principal barriers to validated functional-ingredient status are correspondingly narrower than a general shortfall in bioactivity or functionality evidence: a direct human bioavailability comparison between whole egg and an isolated egg-phospholipid ingredient, and dedicated techno-economic and life-cycle assessment of egg-lipid extraction, remain the two outstanding gaps.

Title: Electrophysiology of the Camel Heart: A Systematic Review of Evidence from Camelus dromedarius.
Abstract: Objective: We aimed to synthesise the available evidence on dromedary-camel electrocardiographic (ECG) measurements, rhythm, and conduction while distinguishing direct electrophysiological studies from supporting cardiovascular reports. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and supplementary sources were searched from inception to 22 December 2025. During revision, the research librarian verified that the saved strategies contained the principal ECG and conduction terms. This verification did not retrieve or screen additional database records. Results: Fifteen primary studies met the eligibility criteria, all involving Camelus dromedarius. Six provided direct ECG or electrical telemetry data, whereas nine provided supporting heart rate, Doppler, echocardiographic, or haemodynamic data that were not used to derive ECG intervals or arrhythmia frequency. Direct studies reported low resting heart rates, atrioventricular conduction times (PR intervals) of approximately 180-260 ms, and drug-associated rhythm or conduction abnormalities. Lead configuration, animal position, recording duration, sampling, and outcome reporting varied substantially. Biological sex was incompletely reported, and no study compared males with females. Conclusions: The directly measured ECG findings are preliminary descriptors rather than validated reference intervals. Confidence is limited by small samples, methodological heterogeneity, the dated search, and possible loss of baseline studies through the executed exposure/context block. The conclusions apply only to Camelus dromedarius. Registration: International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), CRD420251169514.

Title: Extended Reality for Image-Guided Small Animal Surgery: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions.
Journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
Abstract: Image-guided surgery has become an integral component of modern veterinary surgery using advanced imaging modalities, such as computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasonography, and fluoroscopy. Recently, extended reality (XR) technologies have emerged as promising tools to enhance image-guided surgical procedures by improving three-dimensional anatomical understanding, surgical navigation, and intraoperative decision-making. Although XR has gained considerable attention in human surgery, its application in veterinary surgery remains at an early stage. This narrative review aimed to provide a comprehensive overview of the current evidence regarding XR technologies in small animal surgery, with particular emphasis on their integration with preoperative and intraoperative imaging modalities. The available literature was reviewed to evaluate current clinical applications, technological developments and future perspectives. A literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published up to May 2026 using combinations of terms related to extended reality and small animal veterinary surgery. Original articles, case reports, pilot studies, technical reports, and reviews addressing clinical, experimental, or simulation-based applications were considered.
