The MCP-1 correlated with BMI (r = 0.39, p = 0.0001), waist circumference (r = 0.34, p = 0.002), CRP (r = 0.33, p = 0.03), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (r = -0.28, p = 0.02), and visceral adipose tissue (VAT) (r = 0.38, p = 0.0001). Multiple stepwise regression analysis showed that VAT influenced the MCP-1 level.
CONCLUSION: Menopausal status influences MCP-1 concentrations; however, the relationship of MCP-1 with VAT favors the activation of inflammatory mechanisms, outweighing the effects of hormonal status.

Title: Clinical and cardiovascular impact of pregnancy in women with Marfan syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome (MS) is associated with mutations in the FBN1 gene, which encodes fibrillin-1, an essential protein in elastic fibers. Cardiovascular damage in MS has serious complications such as aneurysms and aortic dissection (AD), which increase during pregnancy.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cardiovascular and clinical status of women with Marfan syndrome and pregnancy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study in women with MS or other connective tissue diseases (CTD) classified according to the 2010 Ghent criteria.
RESULTS: One hundred women were included, 35 were admitted as pediatric patients, and 65 as adults. Ten women without medical records were excluded. Forty-eight non-pregnant women and 46 pregnant women were analyzed. 20 births, 26 cesarean sections, 9 preeclampsia, and 14 miscarriages. Of the total group, 14 had con-genital heart disease, 36 had AD, 47 had aortic regurgitation, 22 had mitral valve regurgitation, 15 had tricuspid valve regurgitation, 39 had valve prolapse, 67 had surgeries, and 15 had stents. 19 died, 5 due to aneurysm rupture, 4 had AD, 3 had cardiogenic shock, 5 had septic shock, and 2 had hypovolemic shock.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular damage in pregnancies of women with MS or CTD is complex. The diagnosis of MS is late in some cases; it is at the time of delivery, and genetic counseling is not timely. These are areas of opportunity to impact on prevention, timely gynecological and obstetric status, and surgery.

Title: Lipid profile in mexican women at cardiaovascular risk.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women, particularly postmenopausal. Metabolic and social gender differences influence lipid profiles and cardiovascular risk. In Mexico, factors such as obesity, diabetes, hormonal contraceptive use, and limited healthcare access exacerbate this issue.
OBJECTIVE: To describe the lipid profile of Mexican women with high and very high cardiovascular risk, and compare it to that of men.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study from the REMEXDIS (Mexican Registry of Dyslipidemia) cohort. Clinical, demographic, and biochemical variables were analyzed in 17,532 patients (9536 women). Statistical tests were applied to identify sex-related differences.
RESULTS: Women had a higher body mass index and a lower rate of suspected familial hyper-cholesterolemia. Men had significantly higher levels of total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and glucose. However, women were more frequently classified as very high cardiovascular risk (59.44% vs. 35.90%; p = 0.01). Notably, 48.36% of dyslipidemic women were previously undiagnosed.
CONCLUSIONS: Mexican women with cardiovascular risk exhibit distinct clinical and metabolic characteristics compared to men. These findings highlight the importance of gender-specific strategies for prevention, diagnosis, and management of cardiovascular disease in women.

Title: Sex differences in hospital mortality with the myocardial infarction code.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are differences in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), with a worse prognosis in women.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate sex differences in presentation, management of the myocardial infarction code and in-hospital mortality in the National Registry of Acute Coronary Syndromes.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A total of 62,118 adults (74% men and 26% women) with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or non ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) treated in 177 hospitals were included. Treatment and prognosis were compared.
RESULTS: Women had higher comorbidity and lower smoking rates. STEMI was more prevalent in men (73.0% vs. 63.6%), and Non ST Elevation-Acute Coronary Ayndrome (NSTE-ACS) was more prevalent in women (36.4% vs. 27.0%). Under the heart attack code, reperfusion rates were higher in men: percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) 28.3% vs. 27.9%, fibrinolytic therapy (FT) 36.4% vs. 31.9%, and pharmaco-invasive strategy (PIS) 7.9% vs. 7.2%, respectively; non-reperfusion rates were higher in women (27.3% vs. 33%; p < 0.0001). Complications were more frequent in women, and mortality was also higher in women (15.3% vs. 10.4%; OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.48-1.65). In logistic regression, female sex, age, diabetes, and hypertension independently predicted in-hospital death.
CONCLUSIONS: Women received less reperfusion, greater comorbidity and mortality, therefore timely and equitable care in the myocardial infarction code must be guaranteed.

Title: Evaluation of Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate Dosing for Major Bleeding Following Cardiac Surgery.
Abstract: Four-factor prothrombin concentrate complex (4F-PCC) may be used for significant bleeding following cardiac surgery but the optimal dosing has not been established. The purpose of this study was to compare two dosing strategies of 4F-PCC in cardiac surgery patients. This retrospective chart review evaluated 4F-PCC dosing of 25 units/kg compared to 12.5 units/kg in cardiac surgery patients following a protocol change for 4F-PCC dosing. The primary outcome was major bleeding, defined as the number of patients receiving ≥3 packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusions within 24 h of 4F-PCC administration. Secondary outcomes included other surrogate markers for bleeding (eg, Use of other blood products and hemostatic agents), thrombotic events within 14 days of surgery, hospital length of stay, and all-cause mortality. A total of 42 patients were included (31 patients in the 25 units/kg group and 11 patients in the 12.5 units/kg group). There was no difference in the number of patients that received ≥3 PRBC transfusions between the two groups with 15 patients (47.4%) in 25 units/kg group and 3 patients (27.3%) in 12.5 units/kg (P = .299). Additionally, no difference was observed in amount of additional hemostatic agents administered, hospital length of stay or mortality between the two groups. A higher rate of thromboembolic events was observed among patients receiving 25 units/kg vs 12.5 units/kg (22.6% vs 0%, P = .161). Reduced dosing of 4F-PCC from 25 units/kg to 12.5 units/kg following cardiac surgery resulted in no difference in clinical or effectiveness outcomes.

Title: Tofacitinib 20 vs 30 mg in acute severe ulcerative colitis: a double-blind randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Tofacitinib has emerged as a promising therapy for acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) due to its rapid onset of action. We compared the efficacy and safety of tofacitinib 20 mg/day vs 30 mg/day, both administered with intravenous corticosteroids (IVCS), in patients with ASUC.
METHODS: This was a double-blind, pilot, randomized controlled trial. Adult patients with ASUC were randomized to receive either tofacitinib 20 mg/day (Group 1) or 30 mg/day (Group 2) along with IVCS (hydrocortisone, 100 mg IV every 6 hours). The primary endpoint was clinical response by day 7. The secondary outcome was the cumulative probability of medical rescue therapy or post discharge escalation of therapy or colectomy within 90 days.
RESULTS: Seventy-two patients were randomized, with 36 allocated to each treatment group. At day 7, clinical response was achieved in 33/36 (91.7%) patients in Group 1 and 31/36 (86.1%) in Group 2(RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.90-1.25; P = .46). The absolute difference in response rates was 5.6% (95% CI -9.98% to 21.34%). Rescue therapy was required in 3 patients in Group 1 (all received infliximab) and 5 patients in Group 2 (2 underwent colectomy and 3 received infliximab). Event-free survival at 90 days, defined as the absence of rescue therapy, treatment escalation, or colectomy, was similar between groups (83.3% vs 80.2%; log-rank P = .74). Adverse events were predominantly mild, with no reported venous thromboembolism or major adverse cardiovascular events.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory pilot trial, no statistically significant differences were observed with tofacitinib 30 mg/day compared with 20 mg/day when administered with IVCS.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: Clinical Trials Registry-India: CTRI/2024/10/075098.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Clinical Relevance of Magnesium Supplementation In Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Abstract: Magnesium deficiency is common in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), affecting up to 48% of patients, yet remains underrecognized in routine clinical practice. A bidirectional relationship between hypomagnesemia and insulin resistance has been well characterized, and observational data consistently link higher magnesium intake to reduced risks of T2DM, hypertension, stroke, and heart failure. However, supplementation trials have yielded inconsistent results, limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up, heterogeneous formulations with differing bioavailability, and variable glycemic endpoints. Serum magnesium, the most widely used clinical measure, reflects less than 1% of total body stores and may fail to detect clinically significant depletion. No randomized trial has been powered for hard clinical outcomes such as diabetes prevention or cardiovascular events. Current American Diabetes Association guidelines recommend magnesium screening and supplementation only in high-risk groups with documented deficiency, with emphasis on dietary optimization as a first-line strategy. A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through December 2025, with priority given to meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, and clinical practice guidelines, particularly the ADA position statement and the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Magnesium Fact Sheet. This narrative review critically examines the evidence linking magnesium to glycemic control and cardiovascular risk in T2DM, highlights key methodological limitations, and identifies research priorities such as biomarker validation, formulation comparison trials, and adequately powered cardiovascular outcome studies needed to determine whether magnesium optimization should be incorporated into routine diabetes care.

Title: The Burden of Type 1 Peri-Operative Myocardial Infarction After Non-Cardiac Surgery: Insights From the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project From 2010-2023.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prevalence of perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI), the quality-of-care patients receive and their outcomes, and how this varies across different operations.
METHODS: We included adults from England with AMI between Jan 2010 and March 2023 from the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project registry, linked to Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). Cox-regression models compared risk of all-cause mortality at thirty-days and five-years, subgroup analyses compared operation type (orthopaedic, vascular, upper (UGI) and lower gastrointestinal (LGI) and urological).
RESULTS: We identified 2,821 episodes of type 1 PMI in 533,026 eligible patients (0.5%). Orthopaedics were the largest contributing speciality (45%). Risk of thirty-day mortality was significantly higher in PMI patients at thirty-days (adjusted Hazard Ratio):1.34 [95% CIs 1.21-1.49]) and five-years (1.36 [1.29-1.43]) (both P<0.001). For thirty-day mortality, risk was not significant in orthopaedics and urology but was for vascular (1.75 [1.40-2.18]), UGI (1.95 [1.43-2.66) and LGI surgery (1.94 [1.50-2.51]) (all P<0.001). For those who survived to hospital discharge, PMI patients had higher mortality risk at five-years (1.26 [1.19-1.34), especially high in the UGI (1.76 [1.44-2.13]), LGI (1.34 [1.13-1.59]) and urology groups (1.61 [1.34-1.93]) (all P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: PMI mortality is significantly higher than AMI all-comers, seen across all subspecialties up to five-years, with variation in the risk of mortality from PMI according to operation type. PMI may identify a high-risk vulnerable group of patients, whose increased mortality risk persists long term, even in those who survive to discharge.

Title: Diabetes, Long-term mortality, and LDL-C target attainment after an acute coronary syndrome: A population-based cohort study (2016-2024).
Abstract:
AIMS: To quantify the excess acute coronary syndrome (ACS) burden and post-ACS mortality associated with diabetes and assess LDL-C target attainment, focusing on sex differences.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 5,361 patients with the first ACS admission identified during the study period (2016-2024) in a Spanish healthcare department. Hospitalization trends were analyzed using population-based regression models. Long-term mortality was assessed by Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression. LDL-C target attainment was evaluated according to ESC/EAS recommendations.
RESULTS: Diabetes was present in 36.9 % of patients. ACS hospitalization rates declined by 8.3 % annually (95 % CI 6.1-10.4), with no diabetes-by-time interaction (p = 0.17). In-hospital case fatality was 6.3 % and did not differ by diabetes status. During a median 4.9-year follow-up, diabetes was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.22, 95 % CI 1.11-1.33), with a stronger association in women than men (interaction p = 0.009). Only 28.9 % achieved LDL-C < 55 mg/dL, with no temporal improvement; female sex independently predicted poor LDL-C control (adjusted OR 1.65, 95 % CI 1.38-1.97).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite declining ACS hospitalizations, DM remained associated with increased long-term mortality, particularly in women. LDL-C target attainment remained suboptimal, highlighting persistent gaps in secondary prevention.

Title: Topical Vancomycin for Prevention of Grade 2 or Higher Sternal Wound Infection After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical vancomycin paste over the sternal edges in preventing sternal wound infection (SWI).
METHODS: This single-center, prospective, single-blind controlled trial 1:1 randomized 360 adult patients undergoing elective full sternotomy cardiac surgery to receive either vancomycin paste or normal saline (NCT04500275). The primary endpoint was SWI within 90 postoperative days. The secondary endpoints included postoperative acute kidney injury, emergence of resistant pathogens and systemic vancomycin exposure.
RESULTS: The incidence of grade 2 or higher SWI within 90 days was significantly lower in the vancomycin group than in the placebo group (1 of 180, 0.6% vs. 7 of 180, 3.9%, p = .031). The subdistribution hazard ratio was 0.14 (p = .065). Deep SWI rate was 0.6% vs. 2.8% (p = .099). The incidence of acute kidney injury was comparable between the groups (31.7% vs. 28.9%, p = .251), even in patients with CKD stages ≥ 3. Systemic vancomycin concentrations were negligible and declined over time in non-dialysis patients. Levels above 10-20 mg/L persisted in some patients undergoing hemodialysis. Three cases of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus from various sources were observed in the vancomycin group of patients with CKD stage ≥ 3 or undergoing hemodialysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Topical vancomycin reduced grade 2 or higher SWI without increasing the risk of acute kidney injury. Systemic exposure was negligible, except in patients undergoing hemodialysis. While the emergence of VRE cannot be excluded, its incidence was negligible and does not outweigh the benefits of SWI reduction when using topical vancomycin.

Title: Current Generation Self-Expanding and Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Retrospective Multicenter Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evolving transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) technology warrants updated comparisons of the most commonly used current generation self-expanding (SE) versus balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THV).
METHODS: This 9-center retrospective analysis stratified patients undergoing TAVR from 2021-2024 into SE-THV and BE-THV cohorts balanced via propensity score matching. Primary outcomes were all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, stroke, and permanent pacemaker (PPM) need. Secondary outcomes were paravalvular leak (PVL) and acute kidney injury. All outcomes were assessed perioperatively and at 30 and 400 days. Analyses were repeated within LVEF , aortic valve area, and center-level strata.
RESULTS: The total cohort included 2,594 BE-THV and 1,058 SE-THV patients. Matching yielded 680 patients per cohort. After matching , SE-THV patients had higher risk for ischemic stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05) during index hospitalization, with no difference in mortality. At follow-up, the SE-THV cohort had higher risk of mild (p<0.05) and moderate (p<0.05) paravalvular leak, stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05). PPM after SE-THV was significantly lower in high-volume compared to low-volume centers. Kaplan-Meier survival did not differ. Among patients with LVEF ≥45%, SE-THV was associated with higher stroke risk (p<0.05); BE-THV patients with LVEF < 45% were associated with increased all-cause mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, SE-THV correlated with higher rates of ischemic stroke, PPM need, and PVL during index hospitalization and increased mild and moderate PVL upon follow-up. Mortality did not differ during index hospitalization or at follow-up. The normal LVEF SE-THV cohort was associated with higher stroke risk compared to all other groups.

Title: Cardiovascular phenotypes in women with Sjögren disease: hormonal, immune, and clinical perspectives.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sjögren disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder with a marked female predominance and an increasingly recognised, although incompletely characterised, cardiovascular (CV) burden. This review examines the biological, clinical, and gender-related determinants of CV involvement in women with SjD.
METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE covering the period from January 2010 to July 2026, supplemented by backward citation searching to identify relevant earlier studies. Original SjD-specific studies were prioritised, while systematic reviews, meta-analyses, consensus statements, and evidence from related autoimmune or cardiovascular populations were used to provide clinical and mechanistic context. Evidence was interpreted according to study design, population specificity, and recognised methodological limitations.
RESULTS: SjD-specific observational evidence supports an association with systemic immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, subclinical vascular injury, and selected cardiopulmonary manifestations. Sex-hormone signalling, menopausal changes, and X-linked immune mechanisms may contribute to female susceptibility, although their relationship with CV outcomes remains largely hypothetical. Evidence concerning coronary microvascular dysfunction, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, arrhythmias, autonomic dysfunction, and pulmonary hypertension is heterogeneous and frequently derived from small cohorts or indirect evidence. In women, fatigue, dyspnoea, pain, palpitations, and autonomic symptoms may overlap with systemic manifestations of SjD and complicate recognition of concomitant CV disease.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular care in women with SjD may benefit from combining established prevention and symptom-driven diagnostic pathways with attention to interstitial lung disease, systemic organ involvement, treatment exposure, and reproductive and hormonal history. The proposed assessment framework is intended to provide practical clinical orientation and to support individualised decision-making, rather than to define a standardised SjD-specific screening pathway. Prospective, sex-disaggregated studies are needed to clarify the prognostic relevance of these factors and to inform future recommendations regarding cardiovascular assessment and follow-up.

Title: Residual risk in coronary artery disease: Identification of cardio-reno-metabolic and psychosocial phenotypes in a Latin American cohort of the INTERASPIRE registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual cardiovascular risk remains substantial in patients with established coronary artery disease despite contemporary secondary prevention strategies. Conventional approaches focused on isolated risk factors may fail to capture the multidimensional heterogeneity of this population.
PURPOSE: To identify distinct clinical phenotypes using an unsupervised analytical approach and to explore their association with recurrent cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter observational study based on the INTERASPIRE registry, including 592 Latin American patients with prior acute coronary syndrome or coronary revascularization. Variables from a standardized interview were grouped into demographic, clinical, metabolic, and psychosocial domains. After variable selection, clustering was performed using Partitioning Around Medoids with Gower distance. Associations with 12-month cardiovascular events were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression models.
RESULTS: Three phenotypes were identified. Cluster 1 (42%) included younger patients with lower comorbidity burden and lower psychosocial vulnerability. Cluster 2 (27%) showed greater psychosocial burden and an adverse lipid profile, defining a higher-risk phenotype. Cluster 3 (31%) included older patients with multiple comorbidities and greater renal dysfunction. During 12-month follow-up, 7% experienced cardiovascular events. Event rates differed across clusters (3%, 10%, and 9%; log-rank p = 0.02). Compared with cluster 1, only cluster 2 showed increased risk (HR 2.66; 95% CI 1.11-6.39; p = 0.029).
CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised phenotyping identified three clinical profiles with distinct prognostic implications. Residual cardiovascular risk appears to reflect the interaction of lipid, renal, and psychosocial domains beyond traditional risk factors.

Title: Placental abruption as a marker of long-term maternal cardiovascular risk.
Journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology

Title: Evolutionary logic and biotechnological potential of alternative splicing in higher eukaryotes: Comparative insights from plants and animals.
Abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) generates transcript and protein isoforms, but its evolutionary significance cannot be inferred from isoform number alone. This review uses a comparative framework based on recent literature to separate splice-variant origin, functional consequence, and evolutionary retention in plants and animals. We synthesize evidence from long-read sequencing, single-cell isoform profiling, pangenomics, proteogenomics, and perturbation studies. Animal studies emphasize exon-level switches in neural, cardiac, immune, and germline programs, whereas plant studies highlight intron retention, exitron splicing, environmental responses, and polyploidy-associated regulation. These are tendencies shaped by biological and sampling differences, not exclusive properties of either kingdom. Three worked examples illustrate how reproducible regulation, conservation or population data, molecular consequences, and targeted perturbation support different levels of inference. Functional effects alone do not establish historical adaptation, and conservation alone does not identify the trait under selection. The framework helps prioritize isoforms for crop improvement, biomarkers, and RNA intervention. Clinical splice modulation and field-evaluated natural rice alleles demonstrate translational potential, while highlighting the distinction between validated outcomes and prospective engineering. Future studies should connect isoform-resolved measurements to causal perturbation and fitness or agronomic performance across relevant environments.

Title: Accelerated 3D Late Gadolinium Enhancement Pulse Sequence with Isotropic Spatial Resolution, Self-Navigation of Respiratory Motion, and Arrhythmia Rejection for Quantification of Left Atrial Fibrosis in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The left atrium (LA) is a thin structure (1.5-2.5mm). Conventional 3D late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) pulse sequences for imaging the LA typically have limited through-plane resolution (2.5-5mm) or prolonged scan times (10-15min), resulting in poor image quality and limited clinical translatability. We sought to develop and test whether a 3D LGE pulse sequence featuring 1.5mm³ isotropic spatial resolution and a predictable scan time of 600 heartbeats can produce diagnostically acceptable image quality at 1.5T for quantification of LA structural remodeling in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).
METHODS: A 3D LGE pulse sequence was developed using gradient-recalled echo (GRE) readout, stack-of-stars k-space sampling with variable density along the partition direction, retrospective arrhythmia rejection, and XD-GRASP reconstruction with self-navigation of respiratory motion. Thirty patients with AF (twenty imaged prior to first-time ablation, ten prior to repeat ablation) and twenty healthy controls were scanned using this pulse sequence. The upper limit of normal image intensity ratio (IIR) was derived from the control group; specifically, 2 standard deviations (SDs) above the mean. Suspected LA fibrosis was quantified by one rater. Two cardiothoracic radiologists independently graded the image quality across three categories (conspicuity, artifacts, noise) using a 5-point Likert scale per category, with a score of 3 considered clinically acceptable.
RESULTS: The proposed pulse sequence produced diagnostically acceptable image quality scores in all three categories for AF and control cohorts. Retrospective rejection of data acquired during ectopic heartbeats significantly (p<0.05) improved contrast-to-noise ratio (+3.7%) and sharpness (blur metric -3.2%) metrics, albeit at the expense of a significantly reduced signal-to-noise ratio (-4.4%). The upper limit of normal IIR was 1.43. Using this cutoff value to identify suspected LA fibrosis, compared with the control group (2.47 ± 2.24%), the first-time ablation group (7.45 ± 7.38%) was not significantly different (p = 0.14), whereas the repeat ablation group (14.94 ± 13.83%) was significantly different (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The proposed pulse sequence produces diagnostically acceptable image quality at 1.5T and provides evidence of LA structural remodeling in AF patients, including greater suspected LA fibrosis burden, relative to control subjects.

Title: Diffuse elevations of T1 and T2 are common in newly transplanted pediatric cardiac grafts without rejection and decrease over time.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric heart transplantation carries a high risk of subclinical myocardial injury and rejection. While cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) parametric map elevations detect subtle myocardial changes with rejection, the typical temporal evolution of T1 and T2 values and their correlation with diastolic function in new grafts remains poorly defined.
METHODS: This prospective study evaluated 14 pediatric heart transplant recipients without acute rejection who underwent 22 non-contrast 1.5T CMR with their routine catheterization. New grafts (≤6 months; n=7) were compared to age-, sex- and body surface area-matched controls with established, established grafts (≥12 months; n=15). Comprehensive T1 and T2 mapping was performed and systolic/diastolic function were quantified with left atrial (LA) strain, volumes, and ejection fraction. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models (LMM) and Hedge's g effect sizes.
RESULTS: Compared to established grafts, new grafts demonstrated significantly elevated Mean T1 (Δ 27 ms; p=0.005, g=1.25), Peak T1 (Δ 43 ms; p=0.02, g=1.03), and Mean T2 (Δ 2.6 ms; p=0.05, g=1.18). Longitudinal follow-up in three new grafts revealed temporal normalization of T1. Peak T2 (Δ2.5 ms; p=0.2, g=0.62) did not reach statistical significance. Functionally, new grafts exhibited trends of early diastolic impairment, including lower LA strain and higher indexed LA volumes. While these functional differences did not reach statistical significance, they demonstrated large, standardized effect sizes (g ≥ 0.8), suggesting directional trends that warrant larger investigation.
CONCLUSIONS: During the first 6 months post-transplant, pediatric grafts exhibit diffuse and focal T1 and T2 elevations accompanied by transient diastolic impairment. In this pilot study, these directional trends likely reflect expected ischemia-reperfusion injury, edema, and new graft remodelling rather than acute rejection. Utilizing graft-age-specific normative values is essential to avoid false-positive rejection diagnoses during early post-transplant CMR surveillance.

Title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
Abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA prior to DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs. 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated with Lower Postoperative MI, DVT, and VTE Rates.
Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly prescribed for glycemic control and weight management, but their association with postoperative thrombotic events after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study using de-identified data from the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including adults who underwent primary TKA between December 1, 2006, and June 1, 2025. Patients with prior myocardial infarction (MI), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), venous thromboembolism (VTE), or pulmonary embolism (PE) were excluded. Exposure was defined as a prescription for a GLP-1 RA within 1 year and 1 day before surgery. A 1:1 propensity score match was performed on demographics, relevant comorbidities, and medications, yielding 11,765 patients in each cohort. Outcomes were postoperative MI, DVT, VTE, and PE. Compared with matched controls, patients prescribed GLP-1 RAs had a significantly lower risk of MI (25/11,246 vs. 47/11,171; risk ratio [RR] 0.528; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.325-0.858). GLP-1 RAs use was also associated with a reduced risk of DVT (74/11,319 vs. 103/11,308; RR 0.718; 95% CI, 0.533-0.966) and VTE (133/11,040 vs. 172/11,027; RR 0.772; 95% CI, 0.617-0.967). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of PE between groups (49/11,352 vs. 58/11,382; RR 0.847; 95% CI, 0.580-1.238). Overall, preoperative GLP-1 RA use was associated with a significantly lower postoperative risk of MI, DVT, and VTE following TKA in this large, nationally representative cohort.

Title: Implementation of rapid pan-microbial metagenomics in paediatric intensive care: a single-centre, prospective, observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few clinical metagenomics studies have reported rapid results with associated clinical impact or described deployment of protocols beyond centres in which they were developed. We aimed to assess the feasibility and clinical impact of implementing a previously validated rapid pan-microbial respiratory metagenomic service in paediatric intensive care, reporting protocol modifications, feasibility, diagnostic performance, clinical impact, and staff perspectives.
METHODS: This single-centre, prospective, observational study was carried out at a general paediatric intensive care unit (ICU) and a cardiac paediatric ICU in Great Ormond Street Hospital (London, UK) between Nov 4, 2024, and Feb 28, 2025. Respiratory samples were obtained from patients selected by intensive care staff based on clinical suspicion of lower respiratory tract infection, with no exclusion criteria. Samples were analysed by a well-established published metagenomic workflow that simultaneously detects bacteria, fungi, and DNA and RNA viruses and provides same-day preliminary results and next-day final results; separate aliquots were sent for concurrent culture and PCR testing. Clinical impact (change in antimicrobials, diagnosis, or infection control) was evaluated through electronic health record review. Clinical staff were surveyed for their feedback via an anonymous online semistructured questionnaire.
FINDINGS: 177 samples from 122 patients (median age 3·4 months [IQR 1·2-36·0]; 54% male) were tested. 174 (98%) samples passed quality control. Sensitivity at 16-h sequencing was 89% (95% CI 80-95) for bacteria, 100% (70-100) for fungi, and 87% (76-93) for viruses, with specificities greater than or equal to 99% across all kingdoms. 42 (24%) of 174 samples analysed by metagenomics yielded 50 organisms that were not detected by routine diagnostics, all of which were confirmed by orthogonal PCR testing. Clinical impact was observed in 51 (29%) of 174 samples, comprising changes in antimicrobial therapy in 46 (26%) samples. Of these 46 samples, 15 (33%) resulted in cessation of antibiotics, ten (22%) in initiation of antibiotics, six (13%) in a change of antibiotic therapy, and 15 (33%) provided confidence to continue an empirical antibiotic choice. Of the 33 ICU staff members surveyed, 23 (72%) reported a positive view of metagenomics, none reported negative views, and 22 (67%) perceived additional benefits over routine testing.
INTERPRETATION: This clinical pilot of rapid respiratory metagenomics in paediatric intensive care showed high specificity and good sensitivity. Protocols developed for an adult population were adapted to a paediatric population, including adaptations for polymicrobial upper respiratory tract samples, which are more common in children. However, increased sensitivity and antimicrobial resistance prediction will be required for broader clinical implementation. Although changes in patient management were observed, particularly for antimicrobial stewardship, delineating the true contribution of metagenomic results offered by this study is difficult. Multicentre studies over multiple winter seasons, with control arms and predefined selection of patients and sample types, are needed to assess the impact on patient outcomes and cost-effectiveness.
FUNDING: NHS Respiratory Metagenomics Network (NHS England).

Title: Patient and Database Shift in Lightweight ECG Arrhythmia Classification: A Controlled Evaluation of Noise, Quantization, and Embedded Inference.
Abstract: Efficient microcontroller execution does not ensure reliable electrocardiogram classification across patients and databases. We conducted a controlled benchmark of three convolutional architectures under a corrected subject-disjoint MIT-BIH split, external INCART testing, Noise Stress Test Database artifacts, 16-bit floating-point (FP16) and full-integer 8-bit (INT8) conversion, and classifier-only invocation on an ESP32 without external RAM. Five fixed seeds were used. On the MIT-BIH test cohort (DS2), INT8 four-class macro-F1 was 0.474-0.498 and supraventricular (S) recall was 0.150-0.180. Mean S-class area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was below 0.5 in all six architecture-regime groups, although all corresponding record-cluster intervals included 0.5. Within-record ranking could remain high despite poor pooled ranking. On INCART, S-class ranking was stronger, with all six patient-cluster AUROC intervals above 0.5, but the representative mixed-noise depthwise-separable network (DS-CNN) achieved 0.797 recall with 0.074 precision. Including record 201, which shares a subject with test record 202, increased DS2 S-recall point estimates by 2.49-14.68 percentage points. In the primary architecture panel, FP16 and INT8 met the engineering tolerances in all 120 comparisons. DS-CNN required 9.49 ms per classifier invocation on the ESP32 using preprocessed, annotation-centered inputs. Acquisition, QRS detection, preprocessing, current, and energy were not measured. Patient-dependent S-score behavior and external false-positive predictions limited this panel more than numerical precision or microcontroller resources.

Title: Outcomes of preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump insertion in high-risk coronary artery bypass grafting: A decade of single-centre experience.
Abstract: BackgroundThe role of prophylactic preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the safety and outcomes of preoperative IABP insertion in high-risk CABG patients.MethodsA retrospective review of outcomes of patients who had preoperative IABP insertion undergoing isolated CABG at a single United Kingdom quaternary centre was conducted between January 2015 and June 2025. Indications for IABP insertion were divided into prophylactic (critical coronary anatomy) and non-prophylactic insertion (haemodynamic instability and persistent angina). Primary outcome was 30-day mortality, and secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, incidence of postoperative complications, specific complications related to IABP insertion and postoperative length of stay. Comparative analysis was performed between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed.Results610 patients underwent isolated CABG with preoperative IABP; 302 (49.5%) received prophylactic IABP and 308 (50.5%) had non-prophylactic insertion. There were 14 (2.3%) 30-day mortality and 20 (3.3%) 90-day mortality, with no significant difference in mortality between the two groups. Mean postoperative length of hospital stay was 11 ± 7 days; this was significantly longer in the non-prophylactic group (12 ± 8 vs 10 ± 7 days, p < 0.01). Postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in 42 patients (6.9%) and dialysis in 5 (0.8%), with no differences between the two groups. There were 25 (4.1%) IABP-related complications; 8 localised haematoma managed conservatively, 4 wound infections treated with intravenous antibiotics, 5 lower limb ischaemia (3 required surgical re-vascularisation), 2 fatal bowel ischaemia, 2 renal and splenic malperfusion, 2 localised femoral artery dissection and 2 retroperitoneal haematoma (1 required emergency laparotomy).ConclusionThis study supports the selective use of prophylactic IABP in patients undergoing high-risk CABG. In this selected cohort, preoperative IABP use was associated with low early mortality, favourable long-term survival and an acceptable complication profile.

Title: Large-scale plasma metabolic profiling identifies signatures and biomarkers associated with air pollution and arrhythmias: A prospective cohort study from UK Biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Air pollution is an established modifiable risk factor for cardiac arrhythmia, yet the metabolic mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate how air pollutants promote arrhythmias through metabolic pathway perturbations.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis of 449,068 UK Biobank participants without baseline arrhythmia. Exposures to PM2.5, PM10, NO2, and NOx were assessed using land use regression models. Plasma metabolomic profiling including 170 metabolites via 1H-NMR was performed at baseline. Elastic net regression, Cox proportional hazards models, and mediation analysis were employed to identify pollutant-associated metabolic signatures, quantify their mediating effects, and characterize pathway enrichment across different kinds of arrhythmias.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 16.31 years, a total of 47,381 arrhythmia cases were identified. All four pollutants were prospectively associated with increased arrhythmia risk (hazard ratios ranged from 1.015 to 1.257 per 10 μg/m3). The derived metabolomic signatures significantly mediated these associations between different air pollutants and arrhythmia (mediation proportions: PM2.5-related, 11.19%; PM10-related, 5.19%; NO2-related, 7.44%; NOx-related, 9.82%). Pathway enrichment analysis consistently identified lipid metabolism, ketone body metabolism, and amino acid metabolism as core affected pathways. Notably, compared to atrial fibrillation and supraventricular tachycardia, the ketone body metabolic pathway appeared to account for a larger proportion of the association with intraventricular block.
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that air pollution increases arrhythmia risk through distinct, subtype-specific metabolic perturbations, providing novel insights into the metabolic pathways linking environmental pollutants to different arrhythmia subtypes.

Title: Chest pain in the emergency room: value of the new HEAR score identifying patients with low risk of acute coronary syndrome without troponin testing.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest pain is a frequent reason for Emergency Department (ED) visits, although only a minority of patients ultimately present an Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS). Current diagnostic strategies rely heavily on troponin testing, but a new clinical tool requiring no blood sampling, the HEAR score, has recently been proposed. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of the HEAR score for identifying low-risk patients presenting with chest pain, using 45-day Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) as the primary outcome.
METHODS: All patients presenting with chest pain to the ED of Dijon University Hospital in 2019 were retrospectively analyzed in this single-center study. Patients were stratified as "low risk" (HEAR < 2) or "high risk" (HEAR ≥ 2). Outcomes assessed at 45-days included MACE (defined as a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and urgent coronary revascularization) and recurrence of ED consultation for chest pain.
RESULTS: Among 2177 patients presenting with chest pain, 1807 met inclusion criteria. Of these, 653 (36%) were classified as low risk (HEAR < 2). At 45-days, 22 (3%) low-risk patients reconsulted for chest pain compared with 64 (6%) in the high-risk group (p = 0.037). No MACE was identified among low-risk patients within the available follow-up data. The negative predictive value of a HEAR score < 2 was 100% (95% CI: 99.5%-100%), with an upper 95% confidence bound for the event rate of 0.46%.
CONCLUSION: A HEAR score < 2 identifies a substantial proportion of ED chest pain patients at very low risk of short-term adverse cardiovascular events. However, given the limitations of retrospective follow-up and potential under-ascertainment of events, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. The HEAR score may contribute to early clinical risk stratification rather than replace troponin-based strategies.

Title: Association of peripheral CD4⁺/CD8⁺ T-cell ratio with SYNTAX score and coronary stenosis severity in patients with coronary artery disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is characterized by chronic immune-inflammatory activation. The relationship between the peripheral CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratio and coronary stenosis severity remains unclear. We investigated its association with SYNTAX score and potential as a complementary marker.
METHODS: CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts were measured by flow cytometry in 297 patients with CAD and 181 controls. Coronary stenosis was assessed by angiography and SYNTAX score. Multivariable linear regression was used for SYNTAX score, and logistic regression for moderate-to-severe stenosis (SYNTAX > 23). Models were adjusted for age, sex, BMI, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, HbA1c, hs-CRP, creatinine, and medications. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR was applied. ROC analysis assessed incremental value beyond risk factors.
RESULTS: CD4+ counts and the CD4+/CD8+ ratio were higher, and CD8+ counts lower, in CAD patients, especially in acute coronary syndromes. In unadjusted analyses, SYNTAX score correlated positively with CD4+ count and the CD4+/CD8+ ratio and negatively with CD8+ count (weak to moderate). After adjustment, the CD4+/CD8+ ratio remained independently associated with SYNTAX score (β = 4.88, 95% CI 1.42-8.30, p = 0.006). For SYNTAX > 23, the ratio showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.598, 95% CI 0.526-0.670; sensitivity 0.587, specificity 0.552 at cutoff 1.90). Adding the ratio to conventional risk factors showed no substantial incremental value (ΔAUC = 0.010, DeLong p = 0.43, NRI = 0.082, IDI = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral T-cell imbalance is associated with greater angiographic coronary complexity in CAD. However, the CD4+/CD8+ ratio has limited discriminatory ability and should be considered a complementary candidate marker, not a standalone diagnostic or predictive tool. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required.

Title: Evaluating pre-rapid response team clinical escalations using a bidirectional messaging system in a tertiary hospital.
Journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-rapid response team (pre-RRT) systems are designed to facilitate early recognition and management of deteriorating hospitalised patients. In 2022, our institution implemented a novel role-based asynchronous messaging platform to support urgent clinical review (UCR) activations.
OBJECTIVES: To describes the frequency, timing, nature, and appropriateness of UCR activations and evaluates utilisation of the communication platform.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted including all UCR messages sent via a role-based communication system at a tertiary Australian hospital between January and June 2024. Message metadata were analysed to describe activity patterns and response times. A systematic sample of every fifth UCR message underwent detailed review to assess appropriateness and reasons for escalation.
RESULTS: During the six-month study period, 27 401 UCR messages were sent, representing a median of 182 (interquartile range: 164-201) activations per day. Activations demonstrated marked diurnal variation, peaking during nursing handover and routine observation periods. Median time to first written response was 9 min (interquartile range: 2-26). Detailed review of 5524 messages found that 99.6% were sent by nursing staff and 98.6% were directed to medical teams. Most reviewed messages (96.6%) were appropriate UCR-related communications, while only 3.4% were unrelated to the escalation process. Tachycardia (22.3%), hypotension (14.4%), and tachypnoea (12.2%) were the most common physiological triggers. Clinical concerns including uncontrolled pain, possible cardiac ischaemia, and bleeding were also frequent reasons for escalation.
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-RRT activations represent a substantial component of hospital clinical workload, with approximately 1000 UCR events occurring each week. A role-based asynchronous messaging platform enabled granular communication, an average medical response time of between 9 and 14 min, and was used appropriately in the vast majority of cases. These findings provide insights into the operational burden of pre-RRT systems and may inform future strategies to optimise escalation pathways, clinician workload, and patient safety.

Title: Circulating vitamin D metabolites are distinctly associated with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a prospective study.
Abstract: The epidemiological findings on specific vitamin D metabolites and health outcomes remain inconsistent and limited. We hypothesized that vitamin D metabolites may have distinct associations with all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. This study included 24,592 participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2007 to 2018. Baseline serum vitamin D metabolites, including 25(OH)D3, its epimer 3‑epi-25(OH)D3, and 25(OH)D2, were quantified using standardized liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Data on death and causes were obtained through the National Death Index records. Cox proportional-hazard models were used to estimate the hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). During a median follow-up of 6.4 years, 1397 all-cause deaths and 371 CVD deaths were documented. Serum 25(OH)D3 and total 25(OH)D exhibited L-shaped inverse associations with all-cause and CVD mortality, whereas 25(OH)D2 showed no association. When comparing extreme quartiles, the multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for 25(OH)D3 were 0.68 (95% CI: 0.56-0.83) for all-cause mortality and 0.71 (95% CI: 0.50-0.99) for CVD mortality. For 3‑epi-25(OH)D3, we observed a nonlinear inverse association with all-cause mortality that attenuated to null at around 10.7 nmol/L. Moreover, mediation analysis suggested that alkaline phosphatase and albumin collectively explained 20.0% and 20.4% of the associations of 25(OH)D3 and total 25(OH)D with CVD mortality, respectively. In a nationally representative population, serum 25(OH)D3 was inversely associated with all-cause and CVD mortality, while 3‑epi-25(OH)D3 and 25(OH)D2 showed distinct patterns of association with mortality. Our findings highlight the importance of distinguishing among vitamin D metabolites in mortality risk assessment.

Title: Emergency medicine pharmacotherapy literature of 2025.
Journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
Abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize pharmacotherapy-related emergency medicine (EM) literature indexed in 2025. Articles were selected using a modified Delphi approach. The table of contents from predetermined journals were reviewed and independently evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by paired authors. Pharmacotherapy-related publications deemed to be GRADE 1A and 1B were reviewed by the collective group for inclusion in the review. This article synthesizes and evaluates findings from 7 randomized controlled trials, 10 guidelines, clinical policies, position statements, or consensus recommendations, and 11 meta-analyses, providing critical insight into their potential clinical impact. Covered topics include guideline or policy updates on advanced cardiac life support, rapid sequence intubation, tranexamic acid in trauma, acute coronary syndromes, and hypertension. Randomized controlled trials covering sedative use in rapid sequence intubation, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and bacterial vaginosis, sodium bicarbonate for severe acidemia and acute kidney injury in the critically ill, and thrombolytic therapy beyond traditional time windows for ischemic stroke are also reviewed. Additional topics include nebulized and low-dose ketamine for analgesia, erector spinae plane block for renal colic, two-bag versus three-bag acetylcysteine regimens for acetaminophen overdose, QT prolongation in antipsychotic overdose, and naltrexone for opioid dependence.

Title: Peripheral perfusion index for differentiating cardiac and pulmonary dyspnea in the emergency department: A prospective observational study.
Journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dyspnea is a common reason for emergency department (ED) visits, often caused by cardiac or pulmonary conditions with overlapping clinical presentations. Rapid differentiation between these etiologies is crucial for timely management and prognosis. The peripheral perfusion index (PPI), derived from pulse oximetry, has emerged as a non-invasive biomarker of tissue perfusion. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of PPI in distinguishing cardiac from pulmonary causes of dyspnea and to assess its prognostic value for clinical outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study in the adult ED of Ankara Etlik City Hospital between March 1 and March 31, 2025. Adult patients presenting with dyspnea were consecutively enrolled, with predefined exclusion criteria applied. Demographic data, vital signs, laboratory parameters, and PPI values were collected within 30 min of presentation. Final diagnoses were established using clinical, laboratory, imaging findings, and specialist consultation. The primary outcome was the diagnostic accuracy of PPI in differentiating cardiac and pulmonary dyspnea. Secondary outcomes included ED disposition and 30-day mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 320 patients were included (median age: 73 years; 56.9% female). Pulmonary diseases accounted for 55.9% (n = 179), and cardiac diseases for 44.1% (n = 141). Median PPI was significantly lower in the cardiac group compared with the pulmonary group (1.8 [IQR 1.2-2.2] vs. 2.8 [IQR 2.0-4.3]; p < 0.001). PPI values were also lower in patients admitted to the ICU (1.5) and in 30-day non-survivors (1.5) compared with discharged patients (4.1; p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance for pulmonary disease prediction (AUC: 0.801; 95% CI: 0.749-0.844), with an optimal cutoff of >2.2 (sensitivity 71%, specificity 74%).
CONCLUSION: PPI is a simple, non-invasive, and rapidly obtainable parameter that may aid in differentiating cardiac from pulmonary causes of dyspnea in the ED. Lower PPI values were observed in patients with cardiac-origin dyspnea and were associated with ICU admission and 30-day mortality; however, the prognostic findings should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for residual confounding.

Title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, yet recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) challenged these findings.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings.
METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses. The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62).
CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

Title: Graph neural network for predicting reentrant drivers in atrial digital twins.
Journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Atrial Fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia and is associated with high risk of stroke and heart failure. While pulmonary vein isolation is a standard treatment, its efficacy is suboptimal for patients with persistent AF (PsAF), resulting in high recurrence rates. Increasing evidence indicates that fibrotic remodeling can create arrhythmogenic substrates outside the pulmonary veins, which may contribute to recurrence. Previous works have shown that PsAF Digital Twins (DT) can locate these arrhythmogenic regions and inform ablation targets for AF treatment, characterizing the full arrhythmogenic substrate through iterative simulations, including emergent reentries. While PsAF DTs are effective, their use in clinical practice is constrained by substantial computational demands.
METHODS: In this study, we developed a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to directly identify regions sustaining reentrant drivers (ablation targets) without the need of computationally expensive simulations. The GNN was trained on 31 high-resolution PsAF DTs. Afterwards, the GNN's predictions were prospectively validated on four new PsAF DTs, where the predictions served as virtual ablation targets and new simulations were performed to evaluate the GNN's predictions to eliminate reentrant drivers on new geometries and fibrotic distributions.
RESULTS: Across 8-fold cross validation, the GNN achieved an AUROC of 0.884 and an AUPRC of 0.174, both of which surpassed all other tested models. GNN's positive predictions with the greatest confidence were refined to regions with high fibrotic density and moderate fibrotic entropy. In the proof-of-concept prospective validation, GNN-guided ablation reduced emergent reentries by over 70% relative to the wide antral circumferential ablation pulmonary vein isolation (WACA PVI)-only control and reduced the mean number of additional simulation rounds required to reach non-inducibility by 66%.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the potential of a GNN to guide DT-based ablation for PsAF patients and to reduce the iterative simulation burden of DT workflows. These findings support the feasibility of GNN-guided substrate prioritization, with further validation supporting clinical integration.

Title: High- and low-nitrate vegetable intake produce similar effects on redox, inflammatory, and cardiometabolic markers in older adults: a randomized crossover trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare effects of high-nitrate (HN) and low-nitrate (LN) vegetable intake on redox, inflammatory, and cardiometabolic biomarkers in community-dwelling older adults.
METHODS: In this randomized, crossover trial, 39 older adults ≥60 years consumed 250 g/day of either HN or LN vegetables for 7 days, separated by a 7-day washout period. Assessments before and after each intervention included plasma and urinary NOx (nitrate and nitrite), blood pressure, lipid profile, triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase [SOD], catalase [CAT], glutathione peroxidase [GPx], glutathione S-transferase [GST]), serum total antioxidant capacity (sTAC), oxidative damage markers (malondialdehyde [MDA], protein carbonyls), cytokines (IL-6, IL-10; reduced subsamples, n = 18 and n = 35, respectively), and dietary/physical activity recalls. Treatment effects (HN vs. LN) were assessed using covariate-adjusted linear mixed-effects models (p < 0.05); effect size was calculated as Cohen's d (|d|).
RESULTS: The HN intervention provided a measured mean nitrate intake of 431.5 ± 163.6 mg/day and substantially increased plasma and urinary NOx concentrations compared to LN (p < 0.001). However, this did not translate into significant differences in any redox, inflammatory, or cardiometabolic markers (all p > 0.05). Effect sizes for between-intervention comparisons were consistently small (|d| ≤ 0.40), with the largest effects observed for GST (|d| = 0.40), TyG index (|d| = 0.32), and systolic blood pressure (|d| = 0.28).
CONCLUSIONS: No incremental contribution of nitrate-rich vegetable matrices to redox, inflammatory, or cardiometabolic markers was detected. The clinical relevance of nitrate-rich vegetables may be more apparent in populations with compromised vascular or metabolic function.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NUMBER: RBR-102bc3f2, website: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-102bc3f2. Date of registration: 26th September, 2022.

Title: Transplacental Flecainide and/or Digoxin for Fetal Tachyarrhythmias: Therapeutic Efficacy and Clinical Experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the efficacy and safety of transplacental flecainide and/or digoxin for fetal tachyarrhythmias when sotalol is unavailable.
METHOD: We evaluated transplacental flecainide, digoxin, or combination therapy in a retrospective and prospective cohort across two Thai tertiary centers. Outcomes were classified as complete cardioversion, partial response (rate control), or treatment failure.
RESULTS: Of 24 eligible pregnancies, 14 (58.3%) had supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), 8 (33.3%) had atrial flutter (AFL), and 2 (8.3%) had ventricular tachycardia (VT). Overall, clinical responses occurred in 91.7% (22/24) of fetuses. Flecainide monotherapy achieved 100% (9/9) complete cardioversion in SVT, compared with 50% (1/2) for digoxin. SVT combination therapy (n = 3) yielded 1 complete and 1 partial response. Among 7 flecainide-treated AFL cases, 5 (71.4%) achieved rate control and 2 (28.6%) achieved cardioversion; one digoxin-treated case fully converted. Flecainide resolved 1 of 2 VT cases (50%). Response rates were unaffected by hydrops, gestational age, or cardiac defects (p = 0.087-1.000). Maternal adverse events were mild and required no treatment discontinuation.
CONCLUSION: Transplacental flecainide demonstrates high efficacy in SVT and effective rate control with preserved cardiac function in AFL. Its favorable safety profile makes it a practical alternative for first-line therapy where sotalol is unavailable and flecainide monitoring is infeasible.

Title: Loncastuximab and Rituximab in Elderly Unfit/Frail Patients With Previously Untreated Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
Abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) therapy is typically treated with multi-agent chemotherapy with curative intent but is often challenging or poorly tolerated in patients who are elderly, frail, or have significant comorbidities. LOTIS-9 was a phase 2 trial of loncastuximab tesirine (loncastuximab tesirine-lpyl [Lonca]) plus rituximab (Lonca-R) in patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL who were unfit (cohort A) or frail with or without cardiac comorbidities (cohort B), the majority of whom typically would be ineligible for trials. Patients received Lonca (150 µg/kg during cycles 1-2, 75 µg/kg for subsequent cycles) and R (375 mg/m2) intravenously Q3W for 3-6 cycles, adapted based on response after cycle 3. The primary endpoint of cohort A was complete response (CR) rate; coprimary endpoints of cohort B were CR rate and proportion of patients who completed treatment per protocol. The median age was 84 years (range, 80-91) in cohort A (n=17) and 80 years (range, 67-92) in cohort B (n=24). The CR rates were 52.9% (A: 9/17) and 41.7% (B: 10/24), respectively. In cohort B, 8 (33.3%) patients completed treatment. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 31 (75.6%) patients, including 11 fatal events. Due to toxicity concerns in this medically fragile population, LOTIS-9 was voluntarily terminated prematurely though meaningful efficacy was demonstrated in patients who typically would be ineligible for clinical trials and/or standard of care therapies. These findings provide important insights for future trials. Additional investigation of targeted therapies in vulnerable unfit and frail patients with DLBCL is warranted. (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05144009).

Title: Organ damage profiles and associated factors in juvenile versus adult-onset SLE: a matched analysis from the Japanese ANSWER-SLE cohort.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To elucidate differences in organ damage in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) between juvenile-onset (<18 years) and adult-onset (≥18 years) using the Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics Damage Index (SDI).
METHODS: Among patients in the multicenter registry, ANSWER-SLE (2019-2023), total-SDI and organ domains of SDI were compared between juvenile- and adult-onset patients after 1:2 matching based on sex and current age. Factors associated with total SDI and organ domains of SDI were analyzed by regression models in the total population.
RESULTS: A total of 615 patients were included. Among them, 83 juvenile- and 166 adult-onset patients were matched. Juvenile-onset showed higher total-SDI (juvenile-onset vs. adult-onset, 2.17 vs. 1.16) and higher damage in the ocular, nervous system, renal, cardiovascular, and musculoskeletal domains than adult-onset. In the multivariable negative binomial regression analysis of the total cohort, younger age at onset (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.99, p=0.005) and older current age (IRR 1.03, p<0.001) were independently associated with higher total SDI scores. These associations persisted in the matched cohort (IRR 0.96 and IRR 1.03, respectively). In multivariable analyses of organ-specific damage adjusted for sex, current age, and age at onset, younger age at onset was associated with a higher SDI in the cataract, angina/coronary artery bypass, valvular disease, avascular necrosis, skin ulceration, and premature gonadal failure in the total cohort, and additionally with renal domain in the matched cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Juvenile-onset SLE is associated with organ damage compared to adult-onset SLE, with prominent ocular, neurological, renal, cardiovascular, and musculoskeletal systems.

Title: Relationship between Endothelial Activation and Stress Index and Coronary Artery Ectasia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is characterized by abnormal dilatation of the coronary arteries and is associated with endothelial dysfunction and systemic inflammation. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) has emerged as a novel biomarker reflecting endothelial activation and inflammatory stress.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between EASIX score and the presence of CAE.
METHODS: A total of 300 patients who underwent coronary angiography between July 2018 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The study was designed as a case-control study. Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence of CAE (150 CAE, 150 controls). The EASIX score was calculated using the following formula: EASIX = LDH × Creatinine / Platelet . Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine the predictive value of EASIX for CAE. Youden index statistical analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic power of ROC analysis and to calculate the optimal cut-off value. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Patients with CAE had significantly higher EASIX score compared with controls (1.46 ± 0.33 vs. 0.98 ± 0.74). In the ROC analysis, EASIX score had 72% sensitivity and 58% specificity when the cut-off value for EASIX≥ 0.74 (AUC=0.688, 95% CI:0.618-0.759, p<0.001). In Multivariable logistic regression analysis, the EASIX score was identified as an independent predictor of CAE (OR =2.12, 95% CI: 1.35-3.34, p=0.001).
CONCLUSION: The EASIX score was independently associated with the presence of CAE and demonstrated moderate discriminative ability.

Title: Lifestyle factors and clustered patterns of body shape change in Korean adults: A longitudinal observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major health problem driven by lifestyle habits and changes in body composition, particularly increased body fat mass and reduced skeletal muscle mass. Body mass index alone cannot fully characterize adiposity distribution or changes in muscle mass. Body-shape indicators such as waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio predict metabolic and cardiovascular disease risk; however, few studies have assessed longitudinal changes in these measures together with lifestyle factors. In this study, we aimed to identify clusters of body-shape change using 2-year follow-up data from Korean adults and to elucidate the body-composition and lifestyle factors underlying these changes.
METHODS: K-means cluster analysis was applied to 1,404 participants in the Korean Medicine Daejeon Citizen Cohort using 2-year changes in body mass index, waist circumference, hip circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, waist-to-height ratio, and body weight. Baseline body shape, body composition, and lifestyle indicators were compared across clusters, and multinomial logistic regression was used to identify variables associated with cluster membership.
RESULTS: Three clusters were identified: Stable (48.0%), Adiposity-Increasing (31.0%), and Adiposity-Decreasing (21.0%). At baseline, cluster membership was significantly associated with body fat mass. Over follow-up, changes in body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass showed strong associations with cluster assignment. In addition, clinically meaningful worsening in sleep quality (increase of ≥2.5 points in the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index) and reduced physical activity (decrease in activity as measured by the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire) were significantly associated with the Adiposity-Increasing cluster.
CONCLUSIONS: Changes in body composition, especially body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass, were closely associated with body-shape trajectories, while worsening sleep quality and declining physical activity were associated with the Adiposity-Increasing trajectory. These findings support an integrative approach that considers body shape, body composition, and modifiable lifestyle factors when characterizing adiposity-related trajectories and designing tailored lifestyle interventions.

Title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a complication of severe aortic stenosis. Its prevalence after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and prognostic significance are understudied, as are the post-TAVI trajectories of microvascular indices.
AIMS: The aims of this study were to determine the pooled prevalence of CMD, the influence of the diagnostic modality, the post-TAVI coronary flow reserve (CFR) and microvascular resistance changes, and the prognostic impact of baseline CMD on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from January 2010 to December 2025 for studies involving adults with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI in which CMD was assessed by wire-based thermodilution, angiography-derived indices, Doppler measurements, or stress cardiac magnetic resonance. The risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) pooled CMD prevalence (stratified by modality), CFR change (mean difference; before-after design), and prognostic hazard ratios (HRs). Change in microvascular resistance was synthesized narratively. The protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42025143775) and reported per the PRISMA 2020 guidance.
RESULTS: Eleven primary studies were analyzed, 10 of which (n = 1,212) contributed to the prevalence analyses. An additional study (n = 126) was included in the sensitivity analyses only. CMD prevalence was 46.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] [34.0, 59.9]; I2 = 72%) and 38.4% (95% CI [35.3, 41.7]; I2 = 0%) when assessed using wire-based thermodilution (k = 6, n = 324) and angiographic (k = 4, n = 888) indices, respectively. CFR increased post-TAVI by a pooled mean difference of +0.49 (95% CI [+0.27, + 0.71]; I2 = 72%; k = 5, n = 103 paired observations). Reductions in microvascular resistance were confined to pressure-to-velocity and reserve ratio indices, and absolute minimal microvascular resistance was unchanged (k = 4, n = 85). The HR for MACE was 3.22 (95% CI [0.98, 10.60]; I2 = 78%; k = 2, n = 585). Substantial heterogeneity reflected non-equivalent CMD definitions.
CONCLUSION: The prevalence of CMD pre-TAVI is influenced by the diagnostic method. CFR tends to improve after TAVI, likely due to reduced resting demand rather than structural repair. The CMD-MACE association should be viewed as hypothesis-generating due to limited studies, varied CMD definitions, and incompatible HR calculations. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized CMD definitions are required.

Title: Mechanical Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation - Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention during Cardiac Arrest: Feasibility and Outcomes.
Journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
Abstract: Cardiac arrest complicating acute coronary syndromes requires immediate coronary reperfusion; however, performing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) during active manual cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) presents significant technical challenges. The Lund University Cardiac Arrest System (LUCAS) provides automated mechanical chest compressions and enables uninterrupted CPR during coronary angiography and PCI. Existing evidence is primarily limited to case reports and small observational studies, mechanical CPR has emerged as a practical adjunct in catheterization laboratories where manual compressions are unsafe or logistically challenging. We report two cases from our center in which LUCAS-assisted PCI was performed during ongoing cardiac arrest in the setting of cardiogenic shock and acute coronary syndromes, alongside a structured narrative synthesis of contemporary literature addressing feasibility, procedural considerations, and clinical outcomes. Mechanical chest compressions allowed uninterrupted angiography and successful revascularization in both cases, with return of spontaneous circulation achieved in 1 patient. Despite procedural success, survival remained poor, reflecting severe global ischemia and metabolic derangement. LUCAS-assisted PCI is a technically feasible strategy that facilitates coronary reperfusion in carefully selected patients. Evidence of survival benefit remains limited and derives predominantly from observational studies and case reports rather than randomized controlled trials. The role of extracorporeal CPR as a complementary or alternative strategy warrants explicit consideration at appropriately resourced centers. Improved patient selection and integration into structured resuscitation pathways may enhance clinical outcomes.

Title: Differences in treatment and outcome of patients with ST- elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI in Germany.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI (NSTEMI) are very similar regarding pathophysiology and clinical treatments, especially NSTEMI comprises a much more heterogenic group of patients and underlying diseases. We therefore aimed to assess the treatments and outcomes of both entities in a large contemporary cohort.
METHODS: Patients with STEMI and NSTEMI between 01/01/2010-31/12/2018 were identified from the largest German health insurance (AOK, ≈ 26 million members). Patient demographics, their hospital course, adherence to guideline-directed drug therapy and overall survival were assessed.
RESULTS: In total 544,529 patients (mean age 74, IQR 62-82), one third of whom had a STEMI. Chronic kidney disease, peripheral arterial disease, and heart failure were more common in patients with NSTEMI. Patients with STEMI were more likely to get coronary angiograms and percutaneous coronary interventions. Although STEMI more frequently led to cardiogenic shock, the rate of serious cardiac events was lower. Mortality was higher for STEMI only within the first 30 days, whereas long-term survival rates were better. The combination of statins, angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin receptor blockers, beta blockers, and oral anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents was associated with higher overall survival in patients with STEMI (hazard ratio [HR] 0.21; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 0.20-0.23; p < 0.001) or NSTEMI (HR 0.40; 95%CI 0.38-0.42; p < 0.001). Nevertheless, the prescription rates decreased over time, particular in patients with NSTEMI.
CONCLUSION: Clear differences between STEMI and NSTEMI were observed regarding short- and long-term survival. Guideline-recommended therapy improved long-term survival, but decreased during the follow-up period.

Title: Premenopausal Depression and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease After Menopause: A Large Real-world Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: While depression has been linked to adverse cardiometabolic profiles in postmenopausal women, its temporal relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) when occurring before menopause remains unclear. This study examined whether depression diagnosed prior to menopause was associated with incident CVD after menopause.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Postmenopausal women were assigned to two cohorts: cohort 1 included women with depression diagnosed before menopause and without preexisting CVD, premature menopause, or conventional CVD risk factors (smoking, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, overweight/obesity, or family history of ischemic heart disease); cohort 2 included comparable women without premenopausal depression. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, including age at menopause, current age, and ethnicity. Risk differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals(CIs) were calculated to compare incident CVD (myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Time-to-event outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing, and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression.
