Title: Renal Dysfunction and Cardiorenal Syndrome in Acute Heart Failure: A Systematic Review of Residual Congestion and Decongestion Response.
Abstract: Renal dysfunction is common during hospitalization for acute heart failure and is traditionally considered a defining feature of cardiorenal syndrome type 1. However, the prognostic significance of worsening renal function may depend on the clinical context, particularly whether congestion persists or effective decongestion is achieved. This systematic review evaluated contemporary evidence regarding the relationships among renal dysfunction, residual congestion, decongestion response, and clinical outcomes in adults hospitalized with acute heart failure or cardiorenal syndrome type 1. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched for studies published between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, prespecified analyses of clinical trials, and post hoc analyses of trial-derived data that reported both renal and congestion-related outcomes. Five studies met the inclusion criteria. Residual congestion was consistently associated with worse clinical outcomes, whereas worsening renal function during effective decongestion did not uniformly predict adverse renal or cardiovascular events. Studies evaluating venous excess ultrasound (VExUS)-guided and bioimpedance-guided strategies suggested that objective congestion assessment may improve decongestion phenotyping, although the available evidence remains limited. Overall, the findings support a renal-congestion framework in which kidney function is interpreted alongside congestion burden, diuretic response, perfusion status, and the trajectory of renal recovery. This approach may better distinguish high-risk persistent congestion from transient renal changes occurring during successful decongestion. Future prospective studies should determine whether combined renal-congestion phenotypes improve risk stratification beyond creatinine-based definitions of cardiorenal syndrome alone.

Title: Effect of an artificial intelligence health education accurately linking system on self-management in young and middle-aged patients after percutaneous coronary intervention: a protocol.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is a common heart disease worldwide, and the morbidity and mortality rates among Chinese residents continue to rise. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can improve survival rates, but long-term management is required after the procedure. Traditional interventions have shortcomings such as dependence on medical institutions and the lack of personalized treatment plans. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Artificial Intelligence-based Health Education Precision Linkage System (AI-HEALS) in improving self-health management among young and middle-aged patients after PCI.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-center, randomized, single-blind, parallel-group controlled trial. Eligible patients aged 18-59 years from Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, will be randomly allocated at a 1:1 ratio to receive either standard care plus the AI-HEALS intervention (intervention group) or standard care alone (control group). The primary outcome is the change in self-management ability from baseline to the 3-month intervention endpoint, assessed using the Coronary Heart Disease Self-Management Behavior Scale (CSMS). Secondary outcomes include medication adherence, dietary behavior, exercise frequency, and psychological indicators. Assuming an effect size of d = 0.69, 80% statistical power, and a two-sided significance level of α = 0.05, with an anticipated 20% dropout rate, the required sample size was calculated as 86 participants (43 per group). Primary analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. Generalized linear mixed models will be used for repeated measures outcomes, and multiple imputation by chained equations will handle missing data. Quantitative findings will be integrated with qualitative data from structured interviews conducted among intervention group participants.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University (Approval No.[2024] 409-002). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and academic conferences.Clinical Trial Registration: http://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2500100519.

Title: Remote ischemic conditioning plus stenting for symptomatic carotid artery stenosis (RICSICAS): rationale and design.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) has emerged as a promising non-invasive strategy to protect the brain, with evidence suggesting its benefit in patients with carotid artery stenting (CAS). However, the long-term benefit and safety of chronic RIC in this population remain unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether chronic RIC reduces the incidence of major vascular events in high-risk patients with carotid artery stenosis who received CAS.
METHODS: RICSICAS is a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded endpoint evaluation (PROBE), single-center trial. We plan to enroll 450 high-risk patients with symptomatic carotid artery stenosis (Essen score ≥ 3) scheduled for CAS. Participants will be randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either standard medical therapy plus RIC or standard medical therapy alone. The RIC protocol involves bilateral upper-arm cuff inflation to 200 mmHg (5-min inflation/5-min deflation, 5 cycles) performed 1-2 times daily, starting 3 days before CAS and continuing for 12 months post-procedure, thus constituting a combined peri-procedural and chronic RIC strategy. The primary efficacy endpoint is the composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, TIA, and vascular death within 12 months. Safety endpoints include any RIC-related adverse event (e.g., limb pain, petechiae, peripheral nerve injury), and any serious adverse event.
SAMPLE SIZE: Assuming a 12-month event rate of 20% in the control group and a 40% relative risk reduction with RIC, with 80% power and a two-sided α of 0.05, 355 patients are required. Accounting for a 20% dropout rate/loss-to-follow-up, as well as the consumption of the interim analysis, the total sample size is set as 450.
DISCUSSION: This trial will provide high-level evidence on the role of long-term RIC as an adjunctive therapy for high-risk patients with symptomatic carotid artery stenosis undergoing CAS.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov, identifier: NCT07412249.

Title: How consistent is the determination of the anaerobic threshold among members of the same cardiac rehabilitation team?
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Consistency in the anaerobic threshold (AT) determination is essential for cardiac rehabilitation teams comprising multiple professionals who conduct cardiopulmonary exercise tests (CPETs) and interpret their results. The effect of years of experience on interpreting CPET results, including the AT, has been examined. However, consistency in the AT determination among members of the same institution with experience beyond the training period has not been reported.
METHODS: We evaluated consistency in the AT determination among four members at a cardiovascular hospital (three full-time physical therapists and one part-time consultant physician) with 4 to 30 years of experience with CPETs. Another full-time physical therapist acted as the controller and did not participate in the AT reading. This retrospective study used 260 blinded and randomized CPET data files from 130 patients (130 data pairs comprising inpatient and outpatient data). All observers determined the AT twice using the modified V-slope method.
RESULTS: The mean AT values showed significant interobserver differences (p<0.001) driven by a slightly but significantly lower value determined by the consultant physician. No significant differences in the values determined by the three full-time staff members were observed. Despite interobserver differences during inpatient and outpatient phases, the longitudinal change in the AT did not differ significantly (p=0.58). The intrarater reliability of four observers was good [intraclass correlation coefficient (1,1) = 0.87-0.94], with limits of agreement of 103.6 to 185.0 mL/min. The inter-rater reliability was also good [intraclass coefficient (2,1) = 0.87], with limits of agreement of observer pairs of 139.2 to 220.5 mL/min. Reliability was not associated with years of experience.
CONCLUSIONS: Good consistency in the AT determination is achievable in a clinical setting. Adherence to a single standardized method across the team likely facilitates this consistency and provides a reliable objective measure for monitoring exercise tolerance.

Title: Refractory Angina Pectoris: Medical and Interventional Treatment Options.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is among the more common cardiovascular diseases, affecting 4.7 million people in Germany alone. As many as 20% of patients with CHD still suffer from angina pectoris despite appropriate antianginal therapy and revascularization. Refractory angina pectoris reduces quality of life and increases mortality. In this review, we describe therapeutic strategies and the clinical evidence underlying them.
METHODS: This review is based on publications up to December 2025 retrieved through a selective search in Medline/PubMed for RCTs, before-and-after studies, and guidelines on the treatment of refractory angina pectoris.
RESULTS: The treatment of refractory angina pectoris begins with reducing risk factors, optimizing pharmacotherapy, and considering revascularization for functionally significant coronary stenosis. If these treatment options have been exhausted, the implantation of a sinus reducer may be considered, as recommended in the European guidelines (recommendation grade IIb). The evidence for this is derived from randomized trials and from multiple registry and observational studies. In the sham-controlled COSIRA trial, which involved 104 patients, an improvement in angina symptoms by at least two classes on the Canadian Cardiovascular Society (CCS) grading scale was observed in 35% of patients six months after implantation, compared with 15% in the control group. The multicenter ORBITA-COSMIC trial, which involved 51 patients, also yielded a reduction in daily angina pectoris compared with the control group (OR 1.40; 95% CI: [1.08; 1.83]). Potential complications include migration, embolization of the reducer, and coronary sinus perforation or dissection in 1-2% of patients. These events are only rarely clinically significant.
CONCLUSION: The sinus reducer may improve symptoms in selected patients, but the reported periprocedural complications and limited evidence to date on long-term outcomes should enter into the decision whether to provide this treatment to the individual patient.

Title: Sex-Based Differences in Chronic Heart Failure: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based disparities in patient enrollment and treatment effects in heart failure (HF) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been reported. We aim to systematically analyze sex-based enrollment and treatment effect differences in HF RCTs over time.
METHODS: RCTs enrolling patients with chronic HF were systematically searched on PubMed-MEDLINE. Eligible trials included pharmacological or device-based interventions with a hard primary endpoint (mortality and hospitalization) and reporting enrollment of women. Sex-specific treatment effects (HR or RR) were extracted. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, and pre-specified subgroup analyses were performed.
RESULTS: A total of 56 RCTs (39 drug, 17 device) were included. The pooled proportion of women enrollment was 27.0% (95%CI: 22.0% to 32.4%) in drug trials and 25.3% (95%CI: 21.0% to 29.9%) in device trials. Women were more underrepresented in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) than in HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) trials (21.0% vs 49.6%, p < 0.001). Among drug trials reporting sex-specific effects, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 0.94 (95%CI 0.89-1.01) and RR was 0.81 (95%CI 0.68-0.96), suggesting potentially greater benefit for women. No interaction was observed between HFrEF and HFpEF trials (HR: p = 0.44; RR: p = 0.95). The pooled interaction estimate on event counts was 0.90 (95%CI 0.84-0.96). For devices, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 1.05 (95%CI 0.90-1.22) and RR was 0.68 (95%CI 0.50-0.93).
CONCLUSION: Women remain underrepresented in HF RCTs. Sex-stratified analyses suggest a potentially greater relative benefit of drug intervention in women, which might inform future RCTs. Further studies are required to investigate the mechanisms of these differences.

Title: Diet Quality and Physical Activity at 3-4 Years Following a Hypertensive Pregnancy: A Blood Pressure Postpartum Cross-Sectional Sub-Study.
Journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), as well as being a leading global cause of maternal mortality, confer lifelong increased maternal cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Although lifestyle interventions may mitigate these risks, robust evidence remains scarce.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This cross-sectional sub-study of the three-armed, multicenter BP2 randomised controlled trial primarily assessed diet quality, physical activity, and their association with CVD risk markers in women 3-4 years after HDP, following different BP2 postpartum care/lifestyle intervention strategies implemented between six and 12 months post-HDP. Diet quality was evaluated using the Australian Recommended Food Score (ARFS) derived from the Australian Eating Survey. Duration of moderate-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) was estimated using the International Physical activity Questionnaire. Associations between key lifestyle outcomes and clinical cardiovascular markers were examined using linear regression models. Secondary lifestyle outcomes include estimated daily energy intake, food consumption, nutrients, estimated duration and engagement of specific physical activity types, and sedentary behaviour.
RESULTS: In 180 participants, the mean ARFS was 33.8 ± 10.5 (SD), with 61% scoring < 38 indicating suboptimal diet quality. Median MVPA was 515 (IQR 690) minutes/week with 87% meeting physical activity recommendations of at least 150 min/week. No significant differences were observed across BP2 lifestyle intervention strategies, HDP subtypes (chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia), or baseline body mass index (BMI) categories (< 30 vs. ≥ 30 kg/m2). Neither ARFS nor MVPA showed significant associations with blood pressure, BMI, or waist circumference.
CONCLUSIONS: Suboptimal diet was observed 3-4 years after HDP despite prior lifestyle interventions, highlighting the need for postpartum support and long-term lifestyle interventions to reduce CVD risks post-HDP.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Von Willebrand Factor Biomarkers in Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction: An Adjunct to Imaging and Hemodynamic Assessment.
Abstract: Imaging remains the foundation of prosthetic valve surveillance because it identifies valve morphology, lesion mechanism, and hemodynamic severity. However, acoustic shadowing, eccentric or multiple regurgitant jets, loading conditions, and reader variability can complicate assessment, particularly for paravalvular regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. High shear stress unfolds von Willebrand factor (VWF), promotes proteolysis of its high-molecular-weight multimers, and produces a measurable defect in primary hemostasis. Multimer analysis, closure time with adenosine diphosphate (CT-ADP), and the VWF activity-to-antigen ratio therefore provide a biologic signal of abnormal flow rather than an anatomic image. Prospective studies show that VWF abnormalities track residual paravalvular regurgitation during transcatheter aortic valve replacement, occur with dysfunctional prostheses, change after mitral paravalvular-leak repair, and are associated with bleeding. The evidence nevertheless remains observational; most diagnostic cohorts are small and single-center, thresholds lack independent validation, assays are vulnerable to hematologic and preanalytic confounding, and no completed randomized trial has shown that VWF-guided management improves outcomes. VWF testing is best viewed as an investigational adjunct when imaging and the clinical picture are discordant or when prosthetic dysfunction coexists with otherwise unexplained bleeding. It should not replace guideline-directed echocardiography or be used for routine surveillance outside research protocols.

Title: Meta-Analysis of Long-Term Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events of Different Biologics in Psoriatic Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease associated with systemic inflammation and an increased risk of cardiovascular events.
AREAS OF UNCERTAINTY: Although biologic therapies have transformed psoriasis treatment, the long-term impact of different biologic classes on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) remains unclear.
DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of PubMed was performed up to May 27, 2026. We included Comparative cohort studies of biologic therapies for psoriasis with follow-up durations of at least 52 weeks, as well as long-term open-label extension phases of randomized controlled trials that reported MACE outcomes. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies. Hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using the generic inverse variance method.
RESULTS: Four comparative cohort studies involving 57,331 patients were included in the quantitative synthesis. No significant difference in MACE risk was observed between interleukin (IL)-12/23 inhibitors and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) inhibitors (HR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.68-1.23), or between IL-12/23 inhibitors and IL-17 inhibitors (HR: 1.38, 95% CI: 0.73-2.62). Long-term open-label extension studies reported low MACE event rates (0%-1.33%) across biologic therapies.
CONCLUSIONS: Among biologic therapies with available long-term comparative data, no significant differences in MACE risk were observed between IL-12/23, TNF-α, and IL-17 inhibitors in patients with psoriasis. Further long-term, large-scale studies are warranted to better define the cardiovascular safety profiles of emerging biologic therapies.

Title: Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Aspirin Monotherapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With GRADE Evaluation and Trial Sequential Analysis.
Abstract: The optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following drug-eluting stent implantation remains uncertain. We evaluated extended DAPT versus aspirin monotherapy in patients who completed approximately 12 months of uneventful DAPT after percutaneous coronary intervention. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing these strategies. The primary outcome was myocardial infarction (MI); secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, stroke, and clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2-5). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model. Certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), and trial sequential analysis was performed for MI. Six trials involving 28,601 patients were included. Extended DAPT significantly reduced MI compared with aspirin monotherapy (RR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85; P = 0.001; I2 = 37%). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, or stroke. Clinically relevant bleeding was also not significantly different (RR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.66-2.15; P = 0.56), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 87%) and certainty was low. GRADE certainty was high for MI, cardiac death, and repeat revascularization; moderate for all-cause mortality; and low for stent thrombosis and bleeding. Trial sequential analysis for MI crossed the conventional significance boundary but not the trial sequential monitoring boundary or required information size. Extended DAPT may reduce MI, but individualized assessment of ischemic and bleeding risk remains important, and further adequately powered trials are warranted.

Title: Correction: Protocol for a randomized controlled trial comparing saturated and unsaturated fat sources of a ketogenic diet (KETO-IM) investigating cardiovascular, inflammatory and immune function outcomes in adults living with overweight and prediabetes or type 2 diabetes in Edmonton, Canada.

Rationale and design of a randomized controlled trial to evaluate thrombus modification efficacy of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in patients with ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction: The CAPTURE AMI study.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal myocardial perfusion remains impaired in up to half of patients after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), partly through the distal embolization of thrombus and plaque debris. Reduction of thrombus burden prior to PCI in STEMI has been associated with improved markers of perfusion. However, traditional manual syringe aspiration thrombectomy has demonstrated inconsistent efficacy of thrombus extraction in prior studies. Sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy may achieve more reliable coronary thrombus extraction, with promising early results in non-randomized analyses thus far.
OBJECTIVES: CAPTURE AMI (ClinicalTrials.gov; NCT07687576) will test whether sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy reduces pre-stent thrombus burden compared with standalone PCI in patients with highly thrombotic STEMI.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, single-center randomized controlled trial, 60 patients undergoing primary PCI with TIMI thrombus grade ≥ 4 will be randomized 1:1 to optical coherence tomography (OCT) guided PCI alone, or to sustained mechanical aspiration using the CAT-RX (Penumbra) Aspiration System followed by OCT-guided PCI. The primary endpoint is the absolute change in thrombus burden between two paired pre-PCI OCT runs, measured offline by blinded readers. Exploratory endpoints include pre-PCI thrombus volume, thrombus area and flow area, post-PCI in-stent thromboatheroma and flow volumes, final stent expansion and apposition on OCT, indices of coronary microvascular physiology and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events over 6-month follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: CAPTURE AMI will provide randomized, imaging- and physiology-based evidence on the thrombus-modifying efficacy of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in STEMI.

Title: Randomized trial of counter-pressure and position maneuvers to prevent vasovagal syncope after intravenous cannulation for cardiac CT: The CoPPMan-IVC trial.

Serratus Posterior Superior Intercostal Plane Block Versus Superficial Parasternal Intercostal Plane Block With Local Infiltration for Postoperative Analgesia in Open Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Postoperative pain after open cardiac surgery arises from both sternotomy and chest drains and is often inadequately controlled by anatomically limited techniques. This study compared the serratus posterior superior intercostal plane block (SPSIPB, C3-T10 spread) with superficial parasternal intercostal plane block (PSIPB) plus chest drain-site infiltration.
DESIGN: Prospective, randomized, controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment.
SETTING: Single-center tertiary referral cardiac surgery center.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults undergoing elective open cardiac surgery via median sternotomy; 80 assessed for eligibility, 76 randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Bilateral SPSIPB (n = 35) or bilateral PSIPB plus local anesthetic infiltration at mediastinal and pleural chest drain sites (n = 41), performed preoperatively under ultrasound guidance.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was cumulative 24-hour opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME); the registered secondary outcomes were Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores at rest and on coughing and the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) at 24 hours. All other comparisons were exploratory. Twelve patients were excluded after randomization (2 SPSIPB, 10 control), leaving 33 and 31 for analysis. Opioid consumption was significantly lower in the SPSIPB group (36.6 ± 17.5 v 56.7 ± 16.1 mg of MME; mean difference 20.1 mg of MME; 95% CI, 11.7-28.5; p < 0.001). NRS scores were comparable during the first postoperative hour but lower in the SPSIPB group from 2 hours onward during coughing and at 4, 8, and 24 hours at rest (all p ≤ 0.019). QoR-15 scores were higher in the SPSIPB group (119 [112-126] v 108 [105-111.5]; median difference 10 points; 95% CI, 6-15; p < 0.001), exceeding the minimal clinically important difference of 6 points. Adverse events, including postoperative nausea and vomiting, did not differ between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with PSIPB plus drain-site infiltration-an active comparator targeting both the sternal and drain regions-SPSIPB reduced opioid consumption and improved quality of recovery and may be a valuable component of multimodal analgesia within Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols.

Title: The effect of near-infrared spectroscopy guided intraoperative care on neurocognitive and functional outcomes after cardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse neurocognitive and functional outcomes are common after cardiac surgery. Cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitors regional cerebral oxygen saturation, allowing clinicians to detect and reverse cerebral desaturation. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs to evaluate whether intraoperative NIRS monitoring improves neurocognitive outcomes after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, CINAHL, Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science for RCTs comparing NIRS-guided intraoperative management with usual care in adults undergoing on-pump cardiac surgery, assessing the outcomes of postoperative cognitive decline, delirium, stroke, mortality, and functional recovery. We pooled data using random-effects meta-analysis and assessed certainty of evidence using GRADE methodology.
RESULTS: We included 17 RCTs (N=2288). NIRS-guided management probably reduces early postoperative cognitive decline (risk ratio [RR] 0.65, 95% CI 0.42-0.99; I2=65%, moderate certainty), may have little or no effect on stroke (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.42-1.91; low certainty) or mortality (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.47-1.52; low certainty), and may have no effect on delirium (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56-1.09; I2=32%, low certainty). Findings were primarily derived from small, single-centre trials with heterogenous NIRS thresholds and intervention algorithms. Few studies evaluated outcomes beyond 30 days, and none evaluated validated measures of quality of life or function.
CONCLUSIONS: Although NIRS-guided intraoperative care shows promise for reducing early postoperative cognitive decline after cardiac surgery, evidence of benefit for other neurocognitive or clinical outcomes remains limited. Large multicentre studies are needed to confirm its utility, refine intervention thresholds, and determine its impact on long-term cognition, function, and quality of life. Systematic review protocol. PROSPERO (CRD42022336468).

Title: Ulinastatin Protects Cognition in Cardiac Surgical Patients.
Journal: Annals of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery : official journal of the Association of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons of Asia
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the incidence of postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) in patients undergoing cardiac valve surgery and the potential protective effects of ulinastatin on POCD.
METHODS: This was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind clinical trial. A total of 300 patients undergoing cardiac valve surgery were enrolled across the 3 hospitals and randomized to the control or ulinastatin treatment groups. The patients' cognition was evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). POCD was defined as a lower cognitive score after surgery than the baseline score. Serum levels of proinflammatory cytokines were measured by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.
RESULTS: The incidence of POCD in the control group was significantly higher than those in the ulinastatin group (42/150 vs. 24/150, p <0.05). The MMSE score in the control group was significantly lower after the operation [D0 vs. D3: 27.72 (1.88) vs. 27.09 (2.61), p <0.05], but did not change in the ulinastatin group [D0 vs. D3: 27.63 (2.29) vs. 27.31 (2.47), p >0.05]. In the ulinastatin group, plasma levels of matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9) and S100 calcium-binding protein B (S100β) were significantly lower than those in the control group after the operation.
CONCLUSIONS: The present study confirms that a transient proinflammatory state impairs cognition in patients undergoing cardiac surgery and indicates that perioperative administration of ulinastatin protects cognition.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Continuous wound infiltration with local anesthetics in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Chinese medical sciences journal = Chung-kuo i hsueh k'o hsueh tsa chih
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative analgesia is critical to recovery after cardiac surgery. Continuous wound infiltration (CWI) with local anesthetics (LAs) has been proposed as an opioid-sparing adjunct, but its efficacy beyond pain control and its safety profile remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing CWI with control in adult cardiac surgery. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to August 30, 2025, and updated on April 2, 2026. Primary outcomes were postoperative Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain scores and cumulative morphine consumption. Secondary outcomes included mechanical ventilation duration, length of stay, mortality, complications, patient satisfaction, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE).
RESULTS: Twelve RCTs involving 2,117 patients were included. CWI significantly reduced VAS during mobilization at 24 h (MD=-0.93, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -1.53--0.33, P = 0.002) and 48 h (MD=-0.80, 95% CI: -1.17--0.44, P < 0.001), and decreased 48-hour morphine consumption (MD=-8.10 mg, 95% CI: -13.41--2.79, P = 0.003). No significant effects were observed on VAS at rest, mechanical ventilation duration, ICU or hospital length of stay, mortality, or major cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, gastrointestinal complications, or postoperative infections. Patient satisfaction was higher with CWI. Technical complications were uncommon, and no clinically significant LA toxicity was reported.
CONCLUSIONS: In adult cardiac surgery, CWI with LAs modestly improves analgesia during mobilization and reduces opioid requirements without clear improvement in major clinical outcomes or length of stay. CWI appears safe and feasible and may serve as an adjunct in multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia strategies. Further adequately powered trials are warranted to define its comparative effectiveness within contemporary enhanced recovery after surgery pathways.

Title: Outcomes of Open vs Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting.
METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into two groups based on the intervention: EVAR vs OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed.
RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.25, 95%CI: 0.18-0.34, p<0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95%CI: 0.23-0.42, p<0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95%CI: 0.19-0.31, p<0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the two treatment modalities.

Title: Effects of a 12-week yogic breathing intervention on metabolic syndrome severity and cardiovascular risk factors: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the effects of Yogic breathing (Sudarshan Kriya Yoga [SKY]) on conventional and atypical cardiovascular risk factors in adults with metabolic syndrome (MetS).
METHODS: In this 12-week, two-arm randomized controlled trial, 72 adults (30-60 years) with MetS were randomized (1:1) to SKY plus standard care or waitlisted standard care control group. Conventional and atypical cardiovascular risk factors, spanning behavioral, biological, inflammatory, oxidative, and autonomic markers, were assessed at baseline and 3 months. Between-group effects were evaluated by ANCOVA (adjusted for baseline values and medication use) using per-protocol (PP) and intention-to-treat (ITT; last observation carried forward) analyses.
RESULTS: 64 participants completed follow-up (SKY, n = 34; control, n = 30). Improvements consistent across PP and ITT occurred in waist circumference (p = 0.025/0.035), MetS severity score (MetSSS) (p = 0.020/0.014), and heart rate variability (HRV) low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) power (p = 0.035/0.010). Self-regulation of eating behavior, systolic blood pressure (SBP), and LF/HF ratio were significant only under ITT (p = 0.0498, 0.035, 0.041), not PP (p = 0.146, 0.056, 0.118). No significant between-group differences were observed for other outcomes. Within SKY, changes in HF power and superoxide dismutase (SOD) correlated inversely with changes in MetSSS (r = -0.36, p = 0.039; r = -0.55, p = 0.001). No adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSION: 12-week of SKY improved waist circumference, MetS severity, and selected HRV measures in MetS adults. These findings were robust across analyses, while other outcomes were non-significant or inconsistent. Exploratory associations between HRV, SOD, and MetSSS warrant testing in larger, longer-duration trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Prospectively registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2023/08/056540) on 16-Aug-2023.

Title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
Abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) non-thoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with non-thoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with < 2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

Title: Association of beta-blocker therapy with outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction stratified by GRACE risk score: A nationwide registry analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between beta-blocker use following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and clinical outcomes remain uncertain in the contemporary era of near-universal early revascularization and drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation, particularly for patients with preserved left ventricular function. We sought to determine whether associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied across Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) risk strata.
METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of 11,866 STEMI survivors from two prospective nationwide Korean registries who underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with second-generation DES. Patients were categorized by beta-blocker prescription at discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at one year; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Propensity-score matching and inverse-probability treatment weighting were employed to mitigate confounding. Variation in associations was examined across the continuous GRACE risk spectrum, categorized into low-risk (GRACE <85), intermediate-risk (GRACE 85-179), and high-risk (GRACE ≥180) strata.
RESULTS: Beta-blockers were prescribed to 83.8% of the cohort. After propensity matching, beta-blocker use was associated with lower one-year all-cause mortality (2.7% vs. 4.2%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44-0.91) and MACE (6.0% vs. 8.3%; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.55-0.92). These associations attenuated by three years. The GRACE 2.0 score exhibited robust discrimination for mortality (AUC = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.76-0.82). Continuous interaction analyses showed small model-estimated absolute risk differences in low-risk patients (GRACE <85), whereas the largest model-estimated absolute risk difference was observed in intermediate-risk individuals (GRACE 85-179).
CONCLUSIONS: Among STEMI survivors treated with contemporary PCI, associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied according to baseline GRACE risk. No statistically significant association was observed in low-risk individuals (GRACE <85), whereas the association with lower mortality was most evident in the intermediate-risk group (GRACE 85-179). These hypothesis-generating findings warrant evaluation in randomized trials before being used to guide treatment decisions.

Title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency.
Journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/- mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II-treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/- mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility-HFpEF interactions.

Title: Leadless Pacemakers After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Time-to-Event Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent pacemaker implantation is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Leadless pacemakers (LPs) may reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but their clinical outcomes after TAVR remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of LPs compared with transvenous pacemakers (TVPs).
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized and observational studies were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled proportions, risk ratios (RRs), and mean differences (MDs). Reconstructed Kaplan-Meier data were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Ten studies involving 10,809 patients (1030 LP and 9779 TVP recipients) were included. The pooled procedural success rate of LP implantation was 98% (95% CI 95%-99%). Implantation success was comparable between LP and TVP (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a shorter hospital stay with LP (MD -1.37 days, 95% CI -2.33 to -0.41) and a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.96). Overall survival did not differ between groups (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.44-1.23), although reconstructed survival curves showed late separation favoring LP. Device-related and vascular complications were comparable between LP and TVP.
CONCLUSIONS: LP implantation after TAVR demonstrates excellent procedural success and clinical outcomes comparable to TVPs. LPs may reduce hospital stay and heart failure hospitalization, supporting their use as an alternative pacing strategy in appropriately selected patients.

Title: Safety and Efficacy of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Female Patients: A Secondary Analysis of the ANH Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Female patients undergoing cardiac surgery have a higher transfusion burden, yet they remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. Although the ANH trial showed no significant reduction in the proportion of patients receiving allogeneic blood transfusions with acute normovolemic hemodilution, evidence regarding its efficacy and safety specifically in female patients remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) compared with usual care in female patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a post hoc secondary analysis of the multicenter, randomized ANH trial, which was conducted at 32 centers in 11 countries from April 2019 to December 2024. Of 2010 patients in the original ANH trial, 405 were women and were included in this analysis; 219 had been randomized to receive ANH and 186 to usual care. This secondary analysis was conducted from August 2025 to January 2026.
INTERVENTION: Withdrawal of at least 650 mL whole blood with crystalloids replacement and reinfusion after cardiopulmonary bypass.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the occurrence of at least 1 allogeneic packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion during the index hospitalization. Safety outcomes included intraoperative hypotension, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, mortality, and other perioperative complications.
RESULTS: The median (IQR) age of the participants was 62 (54-69) years. The occurrence of allogeneic pRBC transfusion was similar in the ANH and usual care groups (38.8% vs 44.6%, respectively; relative risk [RR], 0.87; 95% CI, 0.69-1.10; P = .24). Intraoperative hypotension occurred more frequently with ANH (16.0% vs 4.8% in usual care; RR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.62-6.74; P = .02). Patients receiving ANH also had longer ICU stays (mean difference, 21.13 hours; 95% CI, 1.89-40.38; P = .03) and hospital stays (mean difference, 1.92 days; 95% CI, 0.14-3.70; P = .04). No significant differences were observed in mortality or other postoperative complications.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this post hoc secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial, ANH was not associated with a reduction in allogeneic pRBC transfusion among women undergoing cardiac surgery and was associated with more frequent intraoperative hypotension and longer ICU and hospital stay. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered studies specifically designed to evaluate female patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03913481.

Title: The impact of intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative sepsis and/or systemic inflammatory response syndrome caused by infective endocarditis (IE) can lead to significant postoperative mortality. Intraoperative hemoadsorption therapy has shown promising results in the treatment of sepsis and dysregulated inflammatory response during cardiac surgery. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of intraoperative hemoadsorption in high-risk patients with IE undergoing cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A total of 176 high-risk patients with IE were enrolled from 10/2020 to 10/2024. Patients with intraoperative hemoadsorption (HA group, n = 93) were compared to patients without hemoadsorption (control, n = 83). The primary endpoint was a composite of 30-day mortality, incidence of vasoplegic syndrome within the first 24 h and 7 days postoperatively, and intensive care (ICU) stay, analyzed using an unmatched hierarchical win-ratio method.
RESULTS: There were no differences in baseline characteristics between the groups. The mean hemoadsorption time was 106 ± 61 min in the HA group. Vasoplegic syndrome was more frequent in the control group (49.4% vs. 24.7%, p < 0.001). Importantly, 30-day mortality was also significantly lower with intraoperative hemoadsorption (7.5% vs. 20.5%, p = 0.003). The mean ICU stay was shorter in the HA group (7.8 ± 4.6 vs. 11.5 ± 4.2 days, p < 0.001). The analysis met the primary endpoint in favor of patients receiving intraoperative hemoadsorption (win ratio 3.83; 95% CI 2.55, 5.74; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk cardiac surgery patients with IE, the intraoperative use of hemoadsorption was associated with a significantly lower incidence of postoperative vasoplegic syndrome and lower overall 30-day mortality. These findings should be interpreted in the context of the study's methodological limitations and confirmed in future randomized controlled trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB00012919) of the French Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery (CERCSFCTCV20251021).

Title: Minoxidil and Prostaglandin Analogs for Chemotherapy-Induced Alopecia: A Scoping Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy-induced alopecia (CIA) is common, distressing, and markedly impairs patients' quality of life. Although scalp cooling is the only approved preventive strategy, its effectiveness and accessibility remain limited. Therefore, alternative pharmacologic approaches, such as minoxidil and prostaglandin analogs, have been explored.
METHODS: This scoping review aimed to explore the available evidence on minoxidil's efficacy and safety and the potential role of prostaglandin analogs in alopecia. PubMed, Cochrane Library, Medical Online, and Ichushi-Web were comprehensively searched from inception to February 2026. Studies evaluating minoxidil in CIA and prostaglandin analogs in any alopecia type were included. Case reports, case series, and non-human studies were excluded.
RESULTS: Seven studies were included. Five studies evaluated minoxidil in CIA, including two randomized controlled trials and three retrospective studies on prophylactic and therapeutic use, respectively. Prophylactic topical minoxidil did not markedly prevent CIA but was associated with earlier hair regrowth. In contrast, therapeutic use-particularly of oral minoxidil-improved hair density and treatment response. No serious adverse events were reported, although cardiovascular effects remain a concern with oral formulations. Two randomized controlled trials evaluated prostaglandin analogs in non-chemotherapy-related alopecia and showed markedly improved hair density and regrowth. However, no study directly assessed their efficacy in CIA.
CONCLUSIONS: Minoxidil may be beneficial for hair regrowth in CIA but shows limited preventive efficacy. Prostaglandin analogs are promising but untested in this setting. Future studies should evaluate their role, particularly in combination with minoxidil, to address the current evidence gap and improve outcomes for patients with CIA.

Title: Efficacy of a Meta-Analysis-Recommended Immersion Protocol vs. Field-Practical Cold-Water Immersion Protocol for Performance Recovery: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
Journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
Abstract: Kaji, R, Takeuchi, K, Okubo, S, and Yoshida, N. Efficacy of a meta-analysis-recommended immersion protocol vs. field-practical cold-water immersion protocol for performance recovery: A randomized crossover trial. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-We examined the effects of 2 cold-water immersion (CWI) protocols-15° C for 11 minutes and 10° C for 2.5 minutes-on performance recovery following exercise-induced fatigue. Fifteen male collegiate athletes completed 3 randomized crossover conditions with a 2-week washout: 15° C-11 minutes (evidence-based method), 10° C-2.5 minutes (field-practical method), and a seated-rest control. Outcomes included 20-m sprint time (T20), countermovement jump (CMJ), and Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 2 (YYIR2). The 20-m sprint time and CMJ were assessed before exercise (PreEx), immediately after exercise, immediately after the intervention, and at 1, 24, 48, and 72 hours postintervention, whereas YYIR2 was assessed at PreEx and at 72 hours postintervention. Physiological measures (tympanic temperature, skin temperatures, and heart rate) and perceptual measures (subjective fatigue and muscle soreness) were recorded. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. The 10° C-2.5-minute protocol maintained T20 performance during the acute phase, whereas the 15° C-11-minute protocol facilitated later recovery. Countermovement jump performance transiently declined under both CWI conditions; however, a significant improvement at 72 hours occurred only with the 10° C-2.5-minute protocol. Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 2 performance did not differ between conditions. Thermal and cardiovascular responses varied by protocol and reflected recovery patterns. Subjective fatigue improved in both CWI conditions, whereas muscle soreness showed minimal differences. In conclusion, both evidence-based and field-practical CWI protocols enhanced recovery; however, they demonstrated distinct temporal profiles. The 10° C-2.5-minute protocol supported immediate restoration, whereas the 15° C-11-minute protocol promoted delayed recovery. For practical applications, protocol selection should align with sport-specific demands, recovery time, and performance objectives.

Title: Clinical application of volatile sedation in adult intensive care units: pharmacological mechanisms, delivery systems, and safety.
Abstract: Sedation is essential in critically ill mechanically ventilated patients, yet conventional intravenous agents carry risks of accumulation, organ-dependent clearance, and adverse effects. Volatile anesthetics offer several pharmacokinetic advantages, but their adoption in the intensive care unit has historically been limited by technical constraints. This review offers an updated, clinically focused overview of volatile- based sedation in adult intensive care units, covering pharmacological mechanisms, delivery systems, clinical outcomes, safety, and practical application. This review was conducted through systematic searching of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2016 and December 2025. Sevoflurane and isoflurane achieve sedation primarily via γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor modulation and offer organ-independent clearance, rapid onset/offset, and real-time end-tidal monitoring. Modern delivery systems, including reflection devices (Sedaconda-ACD) and automated platforms (MIRUS), have improved intensive care unit feasibility. Clinical evidence suggests volatile sedation may reduce awakening times and duration of mechanical ventilation compared with intravenous agents; however, results across randomized trials and meta-analyses are heterogeneous. Potential benefits have been reported in acute respiratory distress syndrome, post-cardiac arrest care, neurocritical illness, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and refractory agitation, but robust evidence is lacking across all settings. Limitations include hemodynamic effects, increased circuit dead space, renal safety concerns with sevoflurane, infrastructure requirements, occupational exposure, environmental impact, and cost. Volatile sedation is a feasible and pharmacologically rational option for selected mechanically ventilated intensive care unit patients, particularly those requiring prolonged sedation or with organ dysfunction limiting conventional agents. Current evidence does not support universal superiority over intravenous sedation. Inhaled anesthetics should be incorporated into individualized, multimodal sedation strategies within structured institutional frameworks. Large multicenter trials are needed to clarify effects on mortality, long-term neurological outcomes, and quality of life.

Title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention.
RESULTS: Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06462313.

Title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care.
OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH).
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization.
RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious.
CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).
Publication Types: Clinical Trial, Phase II; Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Therapeutic Potential of Flavonoids and Their Metabolites in Hyperlipidaemia: Molecular Mechanisms, Bioavailability and Clinical Perspectives.
Abstract: Hyperlipidaemia is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and remains a global health concern. Although conventional lipid-lowering drugs are effective, their long-term use is often associated with adverse effects, prompting interest in safer dietary alternatives. Flavonoids, such as quercetin, naringenin, and catechins, have gained attention for their hypolipidemic and cardioprotective properties. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on the therapeutic potential of quercetin, catechins, naringenin, and their bioactive metabolites in the management of hyperlipidaemia. The literature was identified through comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and March 2026 using combinations of the keywords flavonoids, quercetin, catechins, naringenin, metabolites, hyperlipidaemia, dyslipidaemia, lipid metabolism, cardiovascular disease, and gut microbiota. Original research articles, clinical studies, experimental investigations, and high-quality review articles published in English were considered, while duplicate, non-English, and unrelated reports were excluded from the study. Evidence indicates that flavonoids and their metabolites modulate multiple pathways involved in lipid homeostasis, including the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, activation of AMPK and PPARα, suppression of SREBP-1c, enhancement of LDL receptor expression, regulation of gut microbiota, and attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammation. Despite encouraging preclinical and clinical findings, limited bioavailability, extensive metabolism, inter-individual variability, and insufficient long-term clinical evidence remain important challenges. Overall, flavonoids and their metabolites represent promising adjunctive dietary strategies for improving lipid metabolism and reducing cardiovascular risk. However, welldesigned randomized clinical trials and advanced delivery systems are needed to establish their therapeutic efficacy and clinical applicability.

Title: Maintaining Quality of Genetic Counseling Services While Maximizing Efficiency: Protocol for the GC-PRO Intervention Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial.
Abstract: The rapid integration of genomic medicine into clinical care has created an unprecedented demand for genetic counseling (GC) services. Attempts to streamline care have involved integration of GC assistants, group counseling sessions, and development of educational technology supplements; meanwhile, improving the efficiency of the core clinical interaction itself remains understudied. This study will evaluate the GC-PRO Intervention, a targeted communication training for genetic counselors designed to optimize visit time by aligning counseling with patient-centered needs and removing processes that do not contribute to positive patient experiences. Using a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial design across clinical specialties (e.g., prenatal, cancer, cardiology, and general genetics) at two academic health centers, we will recruit approximately 20 genetic counselors and 994 patients. To ensure the intervention and study design are culturally responsive, we are utilizing a community-based participatory research approach with four multicultural community advisory boards. The intervention training focuses on three evidence-based communication skills: Tailoring (assessing and integrating patient needs and values), Streamlining (reducing time spent gathering patient medical and family history information), and Main Messaging (reducing lecturing through increasing conversational exchanges). The primary outcome is visit time, and secondary outcomes include patient-reported measures of empowerment, activation, trust, working alliance, patient-centered communication, and overall satisfaction. Data will be analyzed using linear and generalized mixed-effects models to compare the intervention to standard of care, accounting for calendar time, counselor nesting, and pre-specified patient characteristics to improve precision. We hypothesize that this intervention will significantly reduce average visit time while maintaining or improving session quality, as measured against pre-specified non-inferiority thresholds. With 80% power to detect a 5-min difference in session length, this study aims to provide a scalable framework for efficient GC services without sacrificing the counselor-patient relationship or patient-centered outcomes.

Title: Efficacy of Home-Based Telerehabilitation Versus Center-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation on Cardiopulmonary Function and Exercise Capacity in Patients After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL.
Journal: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The objective is to compare the effects of a home-based telerehabilitation (HBTCR) program, traditional center-based cardiac rehabilitation (CBCR), and usual care on cardiopulmonary function and exercise capacity in patients after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 111 patients, 4 to 8 weeks after CABG surgery, were assigned to 12 weeks of HBTCR (n = 37), CBCR (n = 37), or to a control group (n = 37). The HBTCR group utilized wearable sensors and a mobile app for remote monitoring and coaching. The CBCR group underwent supervised on-site sessions. Primary outcomes were changes in peak oxygen uptake () and 6-minute walk distance. Secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction, psychological status, and quality of life.
RESULTS: Among 101 completers, both HBTCR and CBCR groups showed significant improvements in (HBTCR: +5.1; CBCR: +4.8 mL/kg/min) and 6-minute walk distance (HBTCR: +85.2 m; CBCR: +81.5 m) versus control (P < .001), with no difference between interventions. Significant improvements in left ventricular ejection fraction, psychological scores, and quality of life were also observed in both intervention groups compared with control (P < .05). Adherence was high (HBTCR: 92.1%; CBCR: 85.3%) with no major adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that an HBTCR program has similar efficacy as CBCR in improving cardiopulmonary function, exercise capacity, and patient-centered outcomes after CABG. An HBTCR program represents a viable, accessible alternative model for delivering comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation and secondary prevention.

Title: Effects of different exercise types on visceral adipose tissue and glycemic parameters in adults with stage 1 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, particularly at stage 1, is increasingly prevalent worldwide. Although exercise interventions are recognized as effective in reducing visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and improving glucose metabolism, their effects in adults with stage 1 CKM syndrome remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically analyze the effects of different exercise types on VAT, fasting blood glucose (FBG), and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) in adults with stage 1 CKM syndrome.
METHODS: We searched six bibliographic databases-China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), WanFang Database, VIP Database, Web of Science, Embase, and PubMed-from inception to 15 April 2026, using the PICOS framework. A frequentist random-effects Network Meta-Analyses was conducted using STATA 18.0 software to evaluate the effects of interventions on VAT, FBG and HbA1c. The effectiveness of various exercise intervention types was ranked by calculating the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), and the risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB 2.0) tool. This study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261304633).
RESULTS: Thirty-seven randomized controlled trials involving 3483 participants were included. Compared with the control group, aerobic training significantly decreased VAT [standardized mean difference = -0.44, 95% confidence interval (CI): (-0.62, -0.26)], while mind-body exercise (MBE) significantly improved FBG [mean difference (MD) = -1.16 mmol/L, 95% CI: (-1.57, -0.75)] and HbA1c [MD = -0.35%, 95% CI: (-0.62, -0.07)]. Subgroup analysis revealed that high-intensity interval training with an intervention duration of ≤ 12 weeks (SUCRA = 67%) and aerobic training with a duration of >12 weeks (SUCRA = 94.9%) had the highest probability of being the most effective intervention for reducing VAT in included studies. In addition, mind-body exercise ranked highest for FBG improvement, though with limited certainty.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide evidence that different exercise types exert distinct benefits on metabolic health in adults with stage 1 CKM syndrome. In particular, aerobic training may be more effective than other exercise types in reducing VAT, while MBE may contribute to more benefits in improving FBG and HbA1c.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261304633, Identifier CRD420261304633.

Title: Mechanical circulatory support devices in heart failure: a narrative review of current evidence, clinical applications, complications, and future directions.
Abstract: Mechanical circulatory support devices (MCSDs) have evolved from rescue therapy for refractory cardiogenic shock (CS) to an essential component of advanced heart failure management, spanning temporary support, bridge strategies, durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), and total artificial heart (TAH). This structured narrative review summarizes the historical evolution, current indications, device classification, major short-term and long-term platforms, adverse events, and future directions of MCSDs. Literature was selected in a structured narrative manner with emphasis on contemporary guidelines, randomized or comparative studies, major registries, and representative Chinese experience. Available evidence shows that MCSDs can improve hemodynamics and, in selected populations, survival and quality of life; however, these benefits must be balanced against bleeding, stroke, infection, right heart failure, device malfunction, cost, and major ethical and access constraints. Current practice thus necessitates careful patient selection, stage-based therapeutic escalation, and rigorous evaluation of mixed evidence pertaining to temporary MCSDs, LVAD and TAH, instead of merely describing individual devices.

Title: Reading discordant bedside indices in sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: an evidence-mapping framework for diagnosis and trial design.
Abstract: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) affects 20%-30% of patients with septic shock and independently predicts mortality, yet it lacks a consensus definition or validated reference standard. Bedside diagnostic indices-left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain, E/e', troponin level, and cardiac index-are frequently discordant, and no principled framework exists for interpreting this discordance. In parallel, every major pharmacological intervention targeting SICM, including levosimendan, corticosteroids, and beta-blockers, has failed to demonstrate consistent mortality benefit across randomised trials. Herein, we propose that both impasses may share a single root cause: a construct validity failure in which bedside indices used for diagnosis and trial enrolment do not reliably identify the specific pathophysiological processes that they are assumed to represent. We present a structured evidence-mapping framework that organises six bedside diagnostic methods against seven pathophysiological trait dimensions of SICM, grading the evidence for each combination against explicit criteria and identifying structural blind spots. The framework explains why index discordance is a diagnostic signal rather than a measurement error, identifies two dimensions-metabolic dysfunction and cardiac-specific inflammatory signalling-that are structurally invisible to all current bedside diagnostics and whose invisibility offers a testable explanation for repeated trial failures, and translates these insights into a three-step bedside reasoning framework. When LVEF is depressed but longitudinal function is preserved, the framework directs assessment towards ventriculo-arterial uncoupling rather than inotrope escalation; when right ventricular dysfunction predominates, it directs assessment towards reverse resuscitation. The framework reframes index discordance from a source of diagnostic paralysis into a source of clinical precision and defines the enrolment biomarker agenda required to make future SICM trials mechanistically interpretable.

Title: Trajectory-based associations between a structured acupressure protocol, blood pressure variability, and autonomic balance in patients with primary hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a major global public health problem, with suboptimal rates of blood pressure control despite widespread pharmacological treatment. Beyond mean blood pressure levels, blood pressure variability (BPV) and autonomic nervous system imbalance, reflected by heart rate variability (HRV), have emerged as important predictors of cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to examine trajectory-based associations between a structured acupressure intervention, blood pressure variability, and autonomic balance in patients with primary hypertension.
METHODS: Participants received either structured acupressure (12 sessions over 4 weeks) plus usual care or usual care alone. Blood pressure variability was assessed using 24-hour ambulatory monitoring. Autonomic balance was measured via heart rate variability indices. Linear mixed-effects models estimated longitudinal trajectories. Mediation was tested using structural equation modelling.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, the intervention group showed greater reductions in systolic blood pressure variability (β = -1.92, 95% CI -2.78 to -1.06, p < .001). High-frequency heart rate variability increased (β = 84.60, 95% CI 47.60 to 121.60, p < .001), and the low/high-frequency ratio decreased (β = -0.42, 95% CI -0.60 to -0.24, p < .001). Exploratory mediation analysis identified a significant indirect association, suggesting that changes in autonomic balance may partially account for the observed relationship.
CONCLUSION: Structured acupressure was associated with favorable longitudinal changes in blood pressure variability and autonomic function compared with usual care. Mediation analysis suggested that changes in autonomic balance may partially account for the observed association; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the quasi-experimental design does not allow causal inference. Randomized sham-controlled studies are required to confirm these findings.

Title: Cannabinoids in oncology: pharmacology, clinical applications, and translational perspectives.
Abstract: Cannabis and cannabinoid products are increasingly used by patients with cancer for symptom management and supportive care. Although cannabis is widely used to alleviate cancer- and treatment-related symptoms, many patients also believe that it possesses direct anticancer activity. This review provides a comprehensive pharmacologic and clinical assessment of cannabinoids in oncology, integrating the endocannabinoid system, cannabinoid receptor signaling, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic applications, adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, and emerging antitumor research. The strongest clinical evidence supports selected cannabinoid preparations for refractory chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, whereas evidence for cancer-related pain, appetite stimulation, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and opioid-sparing effects remains limited or inconsistent. Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) differ substantially in receptor pharmacology, psychoactive effects, metabolism, and toxicity, with important implications for product selection, dosing, and interactions with anticancer and supportive-care medications. Preclinical studies demonstrate antiproliferative, proapoptotic, antiangiogenic, and immunomodulatory effects across multiple tumor models; however, cannabinoid signaling is highly context dependent and may also promote tumor progression in selected settings. Human evidence for direct anticancer activity remains sparse, consisting predominantly of small early-phase studies and observational data, with no established improvement in tumor response, progression-free survival, or overall survival. Particular caution is warranted regarding neuropsychiatric and cardiovascular toxicity, pharmacokinetic drug interactions, and the potential influence of cannabis on immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes. Overall, cannabinoids have defined but limited roles in supportive oncology, while their direct antitumor potential remains investigational. Future studies should prioritize standardized formulations, pharmacologically informed dosing, rigorous randomized designs, clinically meaningful endpoints, and biomarker-based approaches to define therapeutic benefit and risk.

Title: Cardiovascular outcomes of oral incretin-based drugs in type 2 diabetes: a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 67,679 patients.
Abstract:
