BACKGROUND: While injectable GLP-1 receptor agonists like semaglutide have demonstrated clear cardiovascular benefits in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), the role of oral incretin-based therapies, including oral semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors-remains less well defined. Comprehensive evaluation of their cardiovascular efficacy is warranted.
RESEARCH QUESTION: What are the cardiovascular outcomes associated with oral incretin-based therapies, specifically oral semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors, in patients with T2DM compared to placebo or standard care.
METHODS: We searched electronic databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Meta-analysis was conducted in R version 4.4.3 using the "meta" and "metasens" packages. Statistical analysis was performed using R software and RStudio (version 4.4.2). We calculated pooled estimates using risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 9 studies comprising 67,679 patients were included, of which two evaluated oral semaglutide and the remaining seven assessed DPP-4 inhibitors. There was no significant reduction in all-cause mortality (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90-1.04, p = 0.35) or cardiovascular death (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91-1.05, p = 0.48). Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) showed a non-significant reduction overall (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-1.00, p = 0.06), with oral semaglutide demonstrating a significant benefit (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.95, p = 0.003). Non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI) (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.88-1.09) and non-fatal stroke (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.83-1.03) were not significantly affected. Hospitalizations due to heart failure (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.84-1.13) and unstable angina (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15) remained unchanged. Coronary revascularization was slightly reduced with oral semaglutide (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.91). Adverse events leading to discontinuation were higher with oral semaglutide (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.15-1.98), while serious adverse events were significantly reduced (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99, p = 0.003). Sensitivity analyses were conducted due to significant heterogeneity in key outcomes. While omitting certain studies reduced heterogeneity, the overall results remained consistent.
CONCLUSION: Oral incretin-based therapies were not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, or MACE overall, though oral semaglutide showed a significant MACE benefit and reduced coronary revascularization on subgroup analysis. Non-fatal MI, fatal or non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, fatal or non-fatal stroke and hospitalization due to heart failure or unstable angina were unaffected, and oral semaglutide carried a higher risk of treatment discontinuation. These findings suggest no clear class-wide cardiovascular benefit of oral incretins, with signals specific to oral semaglutide warranting confirmation in dedicated trials.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251113835.

Title: Vietnamese expert consensus on the diagnosis and multidisciplinary management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved rapidly from a surgery-centered approach toward biomarker-informed, multimodality care integrating staging, pathology, surgery, perioperative systemic treatment, and postoperative surveillance. In Vietnam, implementation remains heterogeneous across institutions, particularly in access to fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT), invasive mediastinal staging, molecular testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. This project aimed to develop a Vietnamese multidisciplinary expert consensus to contextualize contemporary international evidence for clinical practice in Vietnam.
METHODS: A structured, modified Delphi-informed consensus process was conducted in Vietnam between August 2025 and January 2026. The workflow comprised seven stages: scoping; a baseline practice survey; initial draft development; expert review of parts 1 and 2; post-meeting written feedback, revision, electronic recirculation, and formal voting for these sections; a multidisciplinary consensus meeting and formal voting for parts 3 and 4; and editorial harmonization and consolidation. The panel included specialists in thoracic surgery, medical oncology, respiratory medicine, pathology, nuclear medicine, radiation oncology, and related disciplines. Classes of recommendation were adapted from the European Society of Cardiology framework. All statements submitted to formal consensus voting were formally rated, with consensus predefined as at least 75% agreement.
RESULTS: The final document comprised 35 consensus statements across four domains: preoperative diagnosis and staging (n=7), surgery and postoperative surveillance (n=8), neoadjuvant and perioperative treatment (n=12), and adjuvant treatment (n=8). Across the meeting rosters, 32 unique experts were identified, with strong representation from thoracic surgery and medical oncology. The baseline survey and expert discussions highlighted implementation gaps in FDG-PET/CT, invasive mediastinal staging, biomarker testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. All 35 consensus statements met the predefined threshold, with agreement ranging from 82% to 100%.
CONCLUSIONS: These consensus statements provide a multidisciplinary, evidence-informed framework for the diagnosis and management of resectable NSCLC across the perioperative pathway. By contextualizing international evidence within Vietnamese clinical practice, the document may help improve consistency of care, support biomarker-guided and multimodality treatment, and strengthen multidisciplinary decision-making across institutions.

Title: Minimally Invasive Hematoma Evacuation for Acute Spontaneous Supratentorial Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a severe form of stroke associated with high morbidity and mortality. While surgical evacuation aims to reduce hematoma burden and improve outcomes, its clinical benefit over medical management remains uncertain. Previous systematic reviews have evaluated a broad range of surgical interventions for ICH; however, evidence specific to MIS remains less clearly defined. Therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the efficacy and safety of minimally invasive hematoma evacuation in patients with acute spontaneous supratentorial ICH.
METHODS: This meta-analysis was performed in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and Cochrane recommendations. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted from inception to February 2026. We included randomized controlled trials that compared minimally invasive hematoma evacuation with medical or conventional surgical management. Risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD) were pooled using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: A total of 12 RCTs involving over 2302 patients were included. Minimally invasive hematoma evacuation significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.97; p = 0.02) and 6-month mortality (RR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.64-0.96; p = 0.02). No significant differences were observed in 7-day or 30-day mortality, although a trend favoring the intervention was noted. Functional outcomes, including mRS 0-1 and mRS 0-3, did not improve significantly. Among secondary outcomes, minimally invasive approaches were associated with greater hematoma volume reduction (MD = 62.47; p = 0.04) but also a higher risk of rebleeding (RR = 2.37; p = 0.002) and cardiac events (RR = 5.08; p = 0.009). No significant differences were found in ischemic stroke, renal failure, gastrointestinal bleeding, seizures, urinary tract infections, or length of hospital and ICU stay.
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive hematoma evacuation significantly decreases mortality in patients with spontaneous ICH, especially with endoscopic techniques; however, it does not markedly enhance functional outcomes and may elevate the risk of complications such as rebleeding and cardiac events. These results underscore the necessity for meticulous patient selection and additional high-caliber trials to enhance treatment strategies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Pharmacotherapy for MASLD/MASH: approved therapies, drug repurposing, and emerging mechanism-based candidates.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASLD/MASH) pharmacotherapy is changing rapidly after the approval of resmetirom and semaglutide for selected adults with noncirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis; management must also address obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular risk, and kidney disease.
AREAS COVERED: This structured narrative review evaluates approved, comorbidity-directed, repurposed, and emerging therapies according to mechanism, regulatory status, endpoint strength, safety, interactions, and implementation. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched without a lower date limit through September 2026 and supplemented by U.S. and European regulatory documents, society guidance, randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and selected mechanistic studies. Therapies include thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonism, incretin and glucagon-containing agonists, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor pathways, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition, de novo lipogenesis/fatty acid synthase inhibition, fibroblast growth factor 21 analogues, lipid/remnant pharmacology, farnesoid X receptor signaling, antioxidants, and lower-evidence repurposing candidates.
EXPERT OPINION: Resmetirom and semaglutide anchor approved MASH-directed treatment in eligible F2-F3 disease, while comorbidity-directed therapy should be individualized by liver stage and cardiometabolic priorities. Tirzepatide, FGF21 analogues, denifanstat, and rational combinations may broaden treatment, but cross-trial comparisons and surrogate endpoints require cautious interpretation.

Title: Dual-track Parallel and Integrated Innovation: Recent Advancements of Clinical Decision Support Systems in Cardiovascular Diseases from the Perspective of Integrative Chinese and Western Medicine.
Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading causes of death worldwide, have a growing disease burden, and present multiple challenges for precision management. Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) are tools that leverage information technology to assist clinicians in diagnosis and treatment decisions and provide references for clinical decision-making by offering personalized suggestions, prompts, or reminders. By integrating multisource data, evidence-based guidelines, and artificial intelligence algorithms, CDSS can support diagnosis, prescribing, and comorbidity management. Studies in hypertension have reported improvements in prescribing and blood pressure, while effects on major cardiovascular events and mortality require further evaluation. Notably, with the continuous development of informatization and digitalization of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), traditional Chinese medicine clinical decision support systems (TCM-CDSS), as an innovative achievement integrating traditional medicine with modern information technology, have shown promise in supporting the prevention and treatment of CVDs. TCM-CDSS achieves an intelligent diagnosis and treatment closed loop from "syndrome differentiation" to "formula recommendation" by integrating TCM theory of "principles, methods, formulas, and medicinals," renowned TCM experts' clinical experience, TCM knowledge graphs, and intelligent syndrome differentiation algorithms, providing a new paradigm for individualized diagnosis and treatment of CVDs such as hypertension and coronary heart disease (CHD). However, reviews addressing the integration of Chinese and Western medicine in cardiovascular CDSS remain limited. To address this knowledge gap, this review adopts a conceptual framework of "dual-track parallel and integrated innovation" to systematically elaborate on the current application status of CDSS across major CVDs. We critically stratified current clinical evidence tiers, highlighting the widespread reliance on retrospective studies and the urgent need for large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Furthermore, we propose that the future paradigm lies in mechanism-data, dual-driven hybrid architectures that quantitatively anchor Western physiological indicators to TCM macrosyndromes. Finally, we provide targeted solutions for the core technical bottlenecks, including Electronic Health Record workflow integration, cross-system comorbidity management, and grassroots application feasibility. These results provide an important reference for the precise treatment of CVDs and a basis for developing new paradigms for CVD prevention and treatment.

Title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.
EXPERT OPINION: Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

Title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.
Abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a heterogeneous syndrome associated with persistently high mortality despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support. One recent randomized controlled trial suggested a mortality benefit of a percutaneous microaxial flow pump in a cohort of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by CS, whereas routine veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in populations with acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS has not improved survival and is associated with higher complication rates. These findings underscore the importance of phenotype-driven patient selection, incorporating the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) and Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) classifications to guide device selection, timing, escalation, and de-escalation. This clinical consensus statement from the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) updates the 2020 expert consensus document and provides updated practical guidance based on the recent evidence on the use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS. Emphasis is placed on patient/device selection according to recent evidence, multidisciplinary shock teams, regionalized hub-and-spoke systems, structured protocols for escalation and futility, and the integration of contemporary trial data and best practices to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.

Title: Perioperative Outcomes of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Cardiac Surgery: Evidence From Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) is a blood conservation strategy used in cardiac surgery, but its efficacy in reducing allogeneic blood transfusion remains debated. This systematic review and meta-analysis updates the existing evidence by incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to provide a contemporary assessment of ANH's impact on perioperative transfusion outcomes. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane Central up to August 2025 for RCTs comparing ANH to standard care in adult cardiac surgery. Primary outcomes were the number of allogeneic red blood cell units transfused, the rate of allogeneic blood transfusion, and estimated total blood loss. Data were pooled using random-effects models, and subgroup analyses were performed by type of surgery. Thirty-one RCTs involving 4426 patients (ANH = 2242, control = 2184) were included. ANH significantly reduced the rate of allogeneic blood transfusion (risk ratio 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66-0.87; P < 0.0001), the number of allogeneic red blood cell units transfused (standardized mean difference -0.42, 95% CI -0.64 to -0.20; P = 0.0001), and estimated total blood loss (standardized mean difference -0.42, 95% CI -0.63 to -0.21; P < 0.0001). Substantial heterogeneity was observed. Subgroup analysis demonstrated that benefits were most consistent in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting. In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, particularly coronary artery bypass grafting, ANH reduces exposure to allogeneic blood transfusion and decreases perioperative blood loss. Despite significant heterogeneity across studies, these findings support the inclusion of ANH within multimodal blood management protocols. Further large, high-quality RCTs with standardized protocols are warranted to confirm its role in modern practice.

Title: What is the significance of intra-operative oliguria with regard to post-operative acute kidney injury? A physiology-informed framework for intra-operative oliguria management.
Journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-operative oliguria is frequently interpreted as a surrogate for hypovolaemia or impaired renal perfusion, often prompting reflexive and potentially harmful fluid administration. However, urine output during anaesthesia is influenced by a complex interplay of neurohormonal activation, surgical stress, and positive pressure ventilation, which can decouple diuresis from actual renal blood flow. This perspective articles critically appraises the evidence linking intra-operative oliguria to acute kidney injury (AKI) and explores the physiological pitfalls of interpreting urine output as an isolated haemodynamic target.
RESULTS: Recent high-level evidence confirms a significant correlation between intra-operative oliguria and post-operative AKI, yet also highlights substantial heterogeneity in the thresholds and durations used across clinical practice. To address this, we propose a conceptual, physiology-informed framework that categorises reduced urine output into four distinct clinical phenotypes: adaptive (a physiologic neurohormonal response to stress), haemodynamic (potentially reversible hypoperfusion), high-risk/complex (occurring in major surgery or vulnerable patients), and injury-associated (established renal damage). In one highly selected high-risk population, a single randomised trial reported that targeting supranormal, urine-guided hydration was associated with a lower incidence of AKI. These findings are hypothesis-generating only and should not be generalised, but they raise the possibility that oliguria in narrowly defined contexts may represent a potentially modifiable signal warranting further prospective study rather than passive observation. Bedside adjuncts, such as ultrasound assessment of cardiac output or venous congestion, may assist in differentiating these phenotypes, although their intra-operative validation remains limited. This framework is intended as a hypothesis-generating conceptual aid to clinical reasoning, not as a validated clinical algorithm or practice recommendation.
CONCLUSION: Interpreting intra-operative oliguria requires a fundamental shift from binary thresholds to context-dependent phenotyping. Effective management must prioritise individualised assessment-integrating surgical risk, baseline patient vulnerability, and dynamic monitoring-rather than responding to isolated urine output triggers.

Title: Acute cardiovascular, autonomic and endocrine responses to a one-hour competitive esports session: a randomized controlled crossover study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Competitive esports involve prolonged sedentary behavior combined with high cognitive and emotional demands, potentially influencing acute physiological responses. However, evidence regarding acute cardiovascular, autonomic, and endocrine responses to competitive gaming remains inconsistent and methodologically heterogeneous.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled crossover study, sixteen healthy male EA Sports FC players completed a one-hour competitive gaming session and a control condition (documentary viewing). Heart rate (HR), root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) and standard deviation of NN-intervals (SDNN) for heart rate variability (HRV) were recorded continuously. Peripheral and central blood pressure, pulse wave velocity (PWV) and salivary cortisol were assessed at baseline, post-session, and after 15 min of rest. Linear mixed-effects models examined the effects of condition, time, and their interaction while accounting for period and sequence effects.
RESULTS: RMSSD (p = 0.005, ηₚ² = 0.13) and SDNN (p = 0.040, ηₚ² = 0.08) showed a significant Condition x Time interaction, with an increase in the control condition, whereas no significant temporal changes were observed during gaming. No significant Condition x Time interactions were observed for HR, PWV, peripheral and central blood pressure. Salivary cortisol decreased over time in both conditions (p < 0.001, ηₚ² = 0.33) without condition-specific effects (p = 0.765).
CONCLUSION: In this laboratory setting, no significant condition specific temporal changes in acute hemodynamic or cortisol responses were detected during competitive gaming compared with passive documentary viewing. The observed differences in cardiac autonomic regulation were primarily driven by an increase in HRV during the control condition, whereas no significant temporal changes in HRV were observed during gaming.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was preregistered in the German Clinical Trials Registry on 05 June 2024 (ID: DRKS00034399).

Title: Early versus deferred intravenous calcium in patients with sepsis and ionized hypocalcemia: a target-trial emulation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravenous calcium is frequently administered during sepsis, yet whether early treatment improves 24-h hemodynamic recovery remains uncertain. We compared 24-h hemodynamic recovery between calcium initiation within 2 h of a non-emergency low-ionized calcium (iCa) result and no calcium initiation during the first 6 h after the result.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective target-trial emulation of 2016-2025 high-resolution electronic health records from Zigong Fourth People's Hospital. Adults with sepsis, final or corrected iCa of 0.90-1.10 mmol/L, and no emergency indication were eligible at result availability. Strategies were executed calcium within 2 h versus no calcium through 6 h; care after 6 h was unrestricted. Clone-censor weighting and overlap tilting addressed grace periods, measured time-varying confounding, and clinical equipoise. The primary outcome was being alive and vasopressor-free at 24 h. Estimates and two-sided 95% percentile intervals came from 2,000 patient-level bootstrap samples with model refitting.
RESULTS: Of 5,993 patients, 1,538 initiated calcium within 2 h, 147 initiated at 2-6 h, and 4,308 received none through 6 h; none of the latter initiated calcium during 6-24 h. The standardized probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery was 69.9% with early calcium and 61.1% with deferral, corresponding to a risk difference of + 8.69 percentage points (95% percentile interval, + 4.66 to + 12.84) and a risk ratio of 1.142 (1.074-1.214). The estimated association varied with baseline norepinephrine-equivalent dose (Holm-adjusted P = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶), whereas the iCa interaction did not remain statistically supported after adjustment (P = 0.097). Early calcium was associated with a 1.29-percentage-point higher observed risk of hypercalcemia (95% percentile interval, + 0.64 to + 2.05). Intervals for severe arrhythmia, new renal replacement therapy, and hospital mortality included the null.
CONCLUSIONS: Early intravenous calcium was associated with a higher probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery than the deferred strategy, whose observed pathway involved no calcium through 24 h. Estimated effects were larger at higher vasopressor doses. Early calcium was associated with a modestly higher observed risk of hypercalcemia. These findings support randomized evaluation in vasopressor-treated patients. Baseline iCa modification remains exploratory.

Title: Central and peripheral vascular recovery following resistance exercise with and without blood flow restriction across age groups: a parallel group crossover randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity resistance training (HIRT) benefits musculoskeletal and vascular health but may be poorly tolerated by older adults. Low-intensity resistance training (LIRT) is an alternative, yet evidence on arterial stiffness is mixed, and it often fails to improve vascular health due to insufficient stimulus. Blood flow restriction (BFR) enhances hemodynamic stimulus, but its acute cardiovascular effects in older adults remain unclear.
PURPOSE: To compare central and peripheral vascular responses following acute LIRT with BFR versus HIRT across age groups.
METHODS: In a randomized crossover design, 19 young (22±3 years) and 19 older (70±9 years) adults completed three sessions: HIRT (3 × 10 reps at 75%1RM), LIRT+BFR (4 × 20 reps at 30%1RM with continuous cuff occlusion), and no exercise. Central and peripheral vascular function were assessed via oscillometric pulse wave analysis at rest, 5-min (RECOV1), and 30-min (RECOV2) post-exercise.
RESULTS: In older adults, neither HIRT nor LIRT+BFR altered total peripheral resistance (TPR), aortic reservoir function, or subendocardial viability ratio (SEVR) throughout post-exercise, with no differences observed between conditions. Conversely, young adults exhibited reductions at RECOV1 following HIRT in TPR (Δ = -  0.176 PRU), reservoir function (Δ = -  11.9%), and SEVR (Δ = -  47.1%), persisting at RECOV2 (all p < 0.05). LIRT+BFR elicited minor changes. Most variables normalized within 30 min for both groups.
CONCLUSION: In older adults, LIRT+BFR elicits post acute central vascular responses comparable to HIRT, with stable coronary perfusion and rapid recovery supporting the short-term tolerability of both modalities. LIRT+BFR thus represents a viable alternative to HIRT for older population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT06596304).

Title: Need for population-specific lipid guidelines for South Asians: Focus on the Indian population and its distinct cardiometabolic risk profile.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: South Asian individuals bear a disproportionately high burden of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), characterized by earlier onset, greater severity, and higher mortality compared with Western populations. This is despite lower average low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and is driven by a distinctive cardiometabolic phenotype, including adverse lifestyle factors, high prevalence of insulin resistance and diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, increased small dense LDL particles, elevated lipoprotein(a), and low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels.
OBJECTIVE: To review the cardiometabolic risk profile of South Asians and the rationale for population-specific lipid management strategies, with a focus on contemporary evidence and recommendations from the Lipid Association of India (LAI).
METHODS: The relevant evidence was identified from published prospective cohort studies, randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, and international and Indian guidelines with emphasis on studies evaluating South Asian/ Indian populations. The literature was evaluated with specific attention to differences in ASCVD burden, age at disease onset, cardiometabolic risk factors, lipid and lipoprotein profiles, and treatment responses between South Asian/Indian and Western populations. Evidence supporting intensive LDL-C lowering and combination lipid-lowering therapy was reviewed.
RESULTS: South Asians demonstrate a high prevalence of atherogenic dyslipidemia characterized by hypertriglyceridemia, low HDL-C, elevated non-HDL-C, and increased apolipoprotein B (apo B) containing particles, often with relatively modest LDL-C levels. Western risk prediction models and lipid thresholds may therefore underestimate ASCVD risk in this population. LAI guidelines recommend lower LDL-C targets than Western counterparts, refined ASCVD risk stratification including extreme-risk group categories, and the use of non-HDL-C and apo B as complementary therapeutic targets. Combination lipid-lowering therapy with statins, ezetimibe, bempedoic acid, and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors is often required to achieve recommended goals and address residual lipid-related risk.
CONCLUSION: Given the distinctive cardiometabolic profile and high ASCVD burden, population-specific lipid guidelines are essential. Intensive LDL-C and non-HDL-C lowering, comprehensive risk stratification, and early combination therapy, alongside sustained lifestyle modification and optimal management of comorbidities, are key strategies to mitigate the growing epidemic of ASCVD in South Asian populations.

Title: Effectiveness and safety of coenzyme Q10 in people with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVES: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) supplementation has previously shown efficacy in improving symptoms and outcomes for people with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. This review aims to assess whether CoQ10 may also be effective and safe for those with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
DATA SOURCES: We searched databases including Embase, MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science, CINAHL, AMED, ClinicalTrials.gov and the ISRCTN registry on 25 June 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults (≥18 years) with HFpEF, defined as an ejection fraction of ≥50%. Eligible studies compared any CoQ10 regimen with placebo or standard care.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB2 and the certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). We conducted random-effects pairwise meta-analysis where possible, using the RevMan V.5.4 software. Synthesis without meta-analysis was conducted for other outcomes.
RESULTS: Three RCTs (264 participants) with a treatment duration of 8–24 weeks were included. The effect of CoQ10 on mortality in individuals with HFpEF was very uncertain (2/101 participants receiving CoQ10 vs 0/105 participants receiving placebo). No cardiovascular deaths occurred in either group (206 participants, very low certainty evidence). The effect of CoQ10 on hospitalisation due to heart failure was very uncertain (1/19 participants receiving CoQ10 vs 0/20 participants receiving placebo). Evidence on quality of life was mixed and also considered very uncertain, with one study indicating benefit from CoQ10 (mean difference (MD) 22.41 points on the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire, 95% CI 12.18 to 32.64, 73 participants) and another indicating no benefit (MD −8.52 points, 95% CI −19.20 to 2.16, 66 participants).
CONCLUSION: Current evidence is insufficient to determine whether CoQ10 improves outcomes in HFpEF. Larger, high-quality and adequately powered RCTs using consistent diagnostic criteria are needed before CoQ10 can be recommended in clinical practice.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251027238.

Title: Antithrombotic therapy regimens after transcatheter valve-in-valve and valve-in-ring procedures: a scoping review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the existing literature on antithrombotic strategies employed after transcatheter valve-in-valve (ViV) and valve-in-ring (ViR) procedures across all valve groups and to provide recommendations for areas of further research.
DESIGN: We conducted a scoping review reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines.
DATA SOURCES: We systematically searched CENTRAL, EMBASE and MEDLINE from database inception until 19 January 2026. Reference lists of included studies were also manually screened.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised-controlled trials, cohort or case-control studies reporting efficacy and/or safety outcomes of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing transcatheter ViV or ViR procedures involving aortic, mitral, tricuspid and/or pulmonary valves were included.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Records were screened for eligibility and data were extracted using a structured charting form. Results were synthesised descriptively and grouped according to valve type.
RESULTS: Of 444 studies screened, 41 were included (10 aortic ViV, 27 mitral ViV/ViR, 1 pulmonary ViV, 1 tricuspid ViV and 2 aortic and mitral ViV). Median sample size was 32 (IQR 14–91; range 5–4243). Ten studies reported a uniform antithrombotic strategy; 30 reported variable strategies, and 1 reported only a protocol-recommended strategy without observed use or adherence. Anticoagulation, with or without antiplatelet therapy, was commonly reported following mitral ViV/ViR, while regimens reported following aortic ViV were highly variable but antiplatelet therapy predominated slightly over anticoagulant therapy. Thrombotic and bleeding outcomes were reported in a highly heterogenous manner.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence guiding antithrombotic therapy after ViV is heterogeneous and largely observational, underscoring the need for high-quality studies to inform optimal management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: This scoping review is registered on the Open Science Framework and can be accessed at: https://osf.io/exvc2/overview?view_only=aeb99d7b79734510826a8ce408e70b03.

Title: Evidence on Valve Selection for Small Aortic Annuli in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients with small aortic annuli presents unique challenges related to prosthesis-patient mismatch, residual gradients, conduction disturbances, and lifetime valve management. Recent observational data have suggested potential differences in mid-term survival between self-expanding valve and balloon-expandable valve platforms; however, these findings have not been consistently supported by other observational studies or long-term randomized evidence. Importantly, both severe prosthesis-patient mismatch and permanent pacemaker implantation may carry prognostic implications, underscoring the competing risks involved in valve selection. In conclusion, current evidence does not establish the clinical superiority of one transcatheter valve platform over another, supporting an individualized approach to valve selection.

Title: From animal behavior to human perioperative neurocognitive disorders: Translational boundaries of the gut-brain axis.
Abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), including postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder, are common after surgery in older adults, and the gut-brain axis has been proposed as a contributing pathway. Most mechanistic support rests on rodent behavioral assays, yet these endpoints and human clinical diagnoses are routinely treated as interchangeable. This critical narrative review examines that translational boundary. PND is used here as a clinically consequential test case for a broader behavioral-neuroscience problem: how animal behavioral phenotypes, microbiome-associated signals, and intervention effects should be translated into human diagnostic constructs. A structured search identified and appraised the principal evidence rather than an exhaustive synthesis; no formal risk-of-bias or certainty-of-evidence assessment was performed. Evidence was separated into human perioperative studies reporting a neurocognitive outcome with either a measured gut-brain exposure or a gut-directed intervention; those reporting gut-brain change without a cognitive outcome; perioperative preclinical evidence; and indirect non-perioperative evidence. The retrieved human perioperative evidence spans observational cohorts across gastric, orthopedic, spinal and cardiac surgery, multi-omic and metabolomic cohorts, and randomized perioperative probiotic trials reporting lower rates of study-defined cognitive outcomes. It nonetheless remains heterogeneous and largely single-center, with modest event numbers, inconsistent sampling and assessment, and limited external validation. Mechanistic support still comes mainly from perioperative rodent models using water maze, fear-conditioning, recognition-memory, and delirium-like readouts, which measure narrow, species-specific capacities and are not diagnostic equivalents of POD, DNR, or postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Microbiome-mediated causation is unproven, and cross-species endpoint alignment remains a central route to improved translation.

Title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes After Physiology-Guided vs Angiography-Guided Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: From the FARGO Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) may reduce unnecessary grafts and improve outcomes. However, in the FARGO (Fractional Flow Reserve vs Angiography Randomization for Graft Optimization) trial, FFR was reduced significantly after 6 months in deferred lesions.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes after FFR-guided CABG compared to angiography-guided CABG.
METHODS: In this multicenter randomized clinical trial, 100 patients were randomized to FFR-guided (n = 50) or angiography-guided CABG (n = 50). Patients underwent a 6-month follow-up coronary angiography with FFR in deferred lesions. In this extended long-term follow-up revascularization, myocardial infarction, stroke, death, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), a composite of the individual endpoints, were assessed.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 8.8 years (IQR: 8.3, 9.3), patients in the FFR-guided group had significantly more MACCE compared to the angiography-guided group, (26 [52%] vs 16 [32%], log-rank test P = 0.03). This difference was driven by significantly more long-term revascularization, FFR-guided CABG 32% vs angiography-guided 12%, log-rank test P = 0.01. The revascularization rate was significantly higher from 0 to 1 year (12 [24%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.01), whereas beyond 1 year, rates were similar (4 [8%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.47). Most patients had stable symptoms, and revascularization was symptom-driven. Myocardial infarction (6 [12%] vs 3 [6%]), death (10 [20%] vs 7 [14%]), and stroke (6 [12%] vs 6 [12%]) did not differ significantly between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: FFR-guided CABG was associated with a significantly higher rate of MACCE after CABG, driven by more revascularization within the first year.

Title: A prospective exploratory study on the effects of Baduanjin exercise on cardiopulmonary and functional capacity in adults with severe burns.
Journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To preliminarily explore the effects of Baduanjin exercise on cardiac function, pulmonary function, and functional capacity in adults with severe burns.
METHODS: In this prospective, exploratory, non-randomized, controlled study, 32 adults with severe burns were assigned into a control group (standard burn rehabilitation, n = 16) or an exercise group (additional Baduanjin exercise, n = 16) based on preference. During the study, one patient in the control group withdrew due to the placement of a tissue expander; in the exercise group, one patient withdrew due to the placement of a tissue expander, and another was lost to follow-up. Finally, 15 patients were included in the control group and 14 in the exercise group. At rest, heart rate (HR), stroke volume (SV), respiratory rate (RR) and vital capacity (VC), as well as 6 min walk distance (6MWD) and upper limb function were measured before and after the intervention. Adherence and actual training frequency were recorded using rehabilitation diaries.
RESULTS: No significant differences in baseline characteristics or pre-intervention indicators were found (all p > 0.05).After intervention, the exercise group showed significantly higher SV, VC, and 6MWD, and lower RR and Quick DASH scores than the control group (all p < 0.05), with no significant group difference in HR (p = 0.907). Multiple linear regression confirmed significant effects of Baduanjin on all outcomes (all p < 0.05). Adherence was comparable between groups (92.85% vs. 73.33%, p = 0.330), but actual training frequency was higher in the exercise group (34.64 ± 4.56 vs. 30.67 ± 5.71, p = 0.049).
CONCLUSION: The findings of this study preliminarily suggest that Baduanjin exercise combining with standard burn rehabilitation may have positive effects on improving cardiopulmonary function and functional capacity in adults with severe burns. However, these conclusions require validation in future randomized controlled trials.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear.
METHODS: This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint.
RESULTS: Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group.
CONCLUSIONS: In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

Title: Effects of Active Video Games on Cardiometabolic Health in Children and Adolescents: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic risk factors emerging during childhood and adolescence may persist into adulthood and increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. Although physical activity improves cardiometabolic health, maintaining regular participation remains challenging. Active video games (AVG), which combine physical activity with video game enjoyment, may provide an engaging approach to promote physical activity participation.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effects of AVG on cardiometabolic health in children and adolescents and to explore potential moderators of these effects.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from database inception to July 2026. Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating AVG in children and adolescents aged 4-18 years were included, with comparisons against no intervention, sedentary video games, or regular physical activity. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to estimate pooled effects. Subgroup analyses explored potential moderators. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool (RoB 2; Cochrane), sensitivity analyses examined robustness, and small-study effects were evaluated when feasible. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation).
RESULTS: A total of 14 RCTs involving 942 children and adolescents were included. AVG were associated with a small but significant reduction in BMI (Hedges g=-0.23, 95% CI -0.35 to -0.10; 95% prediction interval [PI] -0.43 to -0.01; P=.002). SBP (Hedges g=-0.18, 95% CI -0.36 to -0.001; 95% PI -0.43 to 0.07; P=.0497) showed a small statistically significant reduction, although the 95% PI crossed the null. No significant effects were observed for diastolic blood pressure (DBP) (Hedges g=-0.11, 95% CI -0.86 to 0.63; 95% PI -2.09 to 1.75; P=.59), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL) (Hedges g=0.05; 95% CI -0.21 to 0.31; 95% PI -0.54 to 0.57; P=.65), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL) (Hedges g=-0.26, 95% CI -0.64 to 0.13; 95% PI -1.18 to 0.69; P=.15), total cholesterol (TC) (Hedges g=-0.96, 95% CI -3.79 to 1.88; 95% PI -5.71 to 3.86; P=.37), triglycerides (Hedges g=-0.20, 95% CI -0.70 to 0.31; 95% PI -1.41 to 0.99; P=.38), heart rate (HR) (Hedges g=-0.14, 95% CI -1.74 to 1.46; 95% PI -4.23 to 5.38; P=.47), or glucose (Hedges g=-0.17, 95% CI -0.37 to 0.02; 95% PI -0.42 to 0.07; P=.07) following AVG. No significant BMI subgroup differences were observed by gender, intervention type, or nutritional status.
CONCLUSIONS: This review extends previous evidence by providing an updated RCT-only evaluation of a broader pediatric population and a wider range of cardiometabolic outcomes. AVG were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure (SBP), although evidence for other cardiometabolic outcomes remains uncertain. By clarifying both potential benefits and remaining evidence gaps, this review provides a broader basis for future research and intervention development. AVG may serve as an engaging adjunct to support physical activity participation among children and adolescents.

Title: Risk Visualization With Petal-X and Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Support Person-Centered Care and Lifestyle Change in Cardiovascular Prevention: Qualitative Descriptive Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. In primary prevention, effective communication of individual risk and support for behavior change are crucial. Interactive risk visualizations can enhance understanding and engagement, while continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) offers immediate feedback on the physiological effects of daily choices.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore how patients at increased CVD risk and family medicine nurses perceive CVD risk visualization (Petal-X) and the integration of real-time glucose monitoring, with a focus on perceived person-centered care (PCC), motivation, and lifestyle change. This manuscript reports the qualitative phase of a larger sequential mixed methods study; the quantitative randomized controlled trial is reported separately.
METHODS: Using total population (census) sampling within a closed, predefined trial cohort, we invited every eligible patient who had completed the intervention arm of a parallel randomized controlled trial and every eligible registered nurse providing preventive consultations at the same single community health center in central Slovenia who had been familiarized with the intervention and with the Petal-X dashboard; 6 patients at increased CVD risk who had used the Petal-X dashboard in combination with CGM, and 6 nurses familiar with the intervention, took part, and interviews were conducted between September and December 2024. Data were collected through individual, face-to-face semistructured interviews that explored perceptions of the visualization, real-time glucose monitoring, and lifestyle change. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed by inductive qualitative content analysis within a qualitative descriptive design; coding continued until code saturation and data adequacy were judged to have been reached.
RESULTS: The analysis produced 11 subcategories, which were grouped into 4 categories, with an overarching theme running across them: visualization and digital tools as support for PCC to enhance motivation and lifestyle change in individuals at risk of CVD. Patients and nurses reported that personalized visual displays improved understanding of risk factors, facilitated dialogue and shared decision-making, and increased patients' sense of involvement, responsibility, and control, although the 2 groups differed in emphasis: patients foregrounded personal meaning and self-regulation, whereas nurses foregrounded communication and fit with the consultation workflow. CGM was perceived as particularly motivating by linking behavior (food, activity, and stress) to real-time glucose changes, encouraging dietary and activity adjustments that some participants maintained after the intervention. Key barriers included variable digital literacy (especially among older users), fear or mistrust of technology, the attentional burden of continuous monitoring, potential information overload, workflow integration needs, and affordability or accessibility of CGM.
CONCLUSIONS: Interactive CVD risk visualization Petal-X, especially when complemented by CGM, was perceived as a meaningful support for PCC and a driver of motivation and lifestyle change in primary prevention. Implementation should address training, usability, integration into routine workflows, and equity of access.

Title: Effects of tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist) on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity in heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, has demonstrated clinical benefits in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity. However, its effects on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity have not been comprehensively synthesized. We hypothesized that tirzepatide produces significant reductions in cardiorenal biomarkers and improvements in functional capacity compared to placebo or standard of care.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42026137255) searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 17, 2026, without restrictions. Randomized controlled trials and prospective observational studies reporting NT-proBNP, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS), 6-minute walk test (6 MWT), or renal outcomes with tirzepatide vs placebo or standard of care were included. Data were pooled using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment.
RESULTS: Seven studies (5 RCTs, 2 observational; 5406 participants) were included. Tirzepatide significantly reduced hsCRP by 34.3% (95% CI: -38.4% to -30.1%; P < .0001; I2 = 0.0%; 6 studies) and NT-proBNP by 17.6% (95% CI: -26.7% to -8.5%; P = .0001; I2 = 58.1%; 3 studies). In the SUMMIT trial, KCCQ-CSS improved by 5.1 points (P < .001) and 6 MWT by 15.8 m (P = .004). Single-trial data demonstrated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) preservation (+2.90 mL/min/1.73 m2/year; 95% CI: 0.94 to 4.86) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio reduction (-25.0%; 95% CI: -36.0% to -13.0%).
CONCLUSION: Tirzepatide produces consistent anti-inflammatory effects and significant natriuretic peptide reductions, supported by moderate Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation certainty. Evidence for functional and renal outcomes remains limited to single-trial analyses and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending larger dedicated heart failure trials.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD42026137255.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Enlicitide in Hypercholesterolemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high-risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL-C targets. Enlicitide (MK-0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9-directed therapies.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of enlicitide in adults with hypercholesterolemia and assess its dose-dependent effects on lipid parameters.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through March 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation was performed. The primary outcome was the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline. Secondary outcomes included non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), lipoprotein(a), triglycerides, and safety outcomes. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2.0 and GRADE.
RESULTS: Three placebo-controlled RCTs involving 3593 participants were included. Enlicitide significantly reduced LDL-C compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], -56.19%; 95% CI, -64.14 to -48.25; p < 0.0001), with moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 56.9%). Significant reductions were also observed in non-HDL-C (MD, -51.36%), ApoB (MD, -47.09%), lipoprotein(a) (MD, -20.10%), and triglycerides (MD, -13.12%). A numerical dose-response gradient was observed, although subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and treatment discontinuation were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSION: Enlicitide produced substantial reductions in LDL-C and other atherogenic lipid parameters without an apparent increase in adverse events. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials, moderate heterogeneity, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Dose-response, duration-related lipoprotein(a), and triglyceride findings were exploratory and substantially driven by single trials. Long-term cardiovascular outcomes trials are needed to establish clinical benefit.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Haemodiafiltration, haemofiltration and haemodialysis for adults with kidney failure.
Journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
Abstract:
RATIONALE: Convective extracorporeal dialysis modalities, haemofiltration (HF), haemodiafiltration (HDF), and acetate-free biofiltration (AFB), remove excess body fluid across the dialysis membrane through an interplay of positive and negative pressures and accumulated middle- and larger-sized solutes more efficiently than haemodialysis (HD). This increased removal of larger solutes, combined with the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid in convective dialysis, is hypothesised to reduce the frequency and severity of symptoms during HD and improve long-term clinical outcomes. This is an update of a review first published in 2006 and updated in 2015.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the benefits and harms of convective (HF, HDF, or AFB) versus diffusive (HD) dialysis modalities, or expanded HD (HDx), in preventing all-cause and cardiovascular death, cardiovascular morbidity, fatigue, and vascular access problems in adults with kidney failure.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and two trial registers up to 3 April 2025. Additionally, handsearching of journals and conference abstract books was performed, and the references of the included studies were reviewed.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing convective therapy (HF, HDF, AFB) with another convective therapy or with diffusive therapy (HD or HDx) for treating adults with kidney failure.
OUTCOMES: Critical and important outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular death, nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, problems with vascular access, hospitalisation, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL).
RISK OF BIAS: Two authors independently assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We summarised treatment effects using the random-effects model and reported risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous data with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the confidence of the evidence using the GRADE approach.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We identified 62 eligible studies (6897 participants). In total, 54 studies (6525 participants) compared HF, HDF or AFB with HD (both high-flux and low-flux); two studies (24 participants) compared AFB with HDF; three studies (62 participants) compared HDF with HF; and four studies (163 participants) compared HDx with HDF/HD.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Convective dialysis, compared with diffusive therapy, likely reduces the risk of death (any cause) (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.96; I² = 0%; 15 studies, 5463 participantss; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness) and cardiovascular death (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92; I² = 0%; 9 studies, 4761 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Cardiovascular morbidity was likely not different between convective and diffusive dialysis (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.22; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 2074 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Little to no differences were found between convective and diffusive dialysis on fatigue (MD -0.95, 95% CI -2.50 to 0.60; 1 study, 543 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), problems with vascular access (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.50; 1 study, 124 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), hospitalisation (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.37; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 600 participants; low-certainty evidence due to indirectness and imprecision), or physical quality of life (MD 0.66, 95% CI -1.08 to 2.40; 1 study, 538 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision). Direct comparisons between different convective modalities were limited and underpowered to detect meaningful differences.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Convective dialysis likely reduces all-cause and cardiovascular death. Effects on nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, vascular access failure, and hospitalisation are inconclusive. Future RCTs should prioritise methodological rigour and could focus on unresolved questions, including the impact of convective therapies on patient-centred outcomes such as symptom burden, HRQoL, functional status, and intradialytic tolerance, as well as investigating barriers to uptake, evaluating health system readiness, assessing cost-effectiveness, and identifying strategies to promote equitable access.
FUNDING: No specific funding.
REGISTRATION: Previous versions available via DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD006258 and DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD006258.pub2.

Title: Combined ischaemia and vulnerable plaque percutaneous coronary intervention to reduce cardiovascular events: design and rationale of the COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract: Fractional flow reserve (FFR) assessment represents the most widely used revascularisation strategy of the last two decades. However, many FFR (+) lesions, particularly those in the grey zone, can be safely treated medically, while other lesions carrying vulnerable plaque (VP) features can cause future events despite the absence of ischaemia. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) can identify lesions with VP morphology. The objective of this study is to determine whether a combined revascularisation strategy - targeting only severely ischaemic lesions (FFR ≤0.75) and extending treatment to OCT-assessed VP, even in the absence of ischaemia (FFR>0.80) - could reduce future adverse events compared with the current revascularisation practice based exclusively on the presence of ischaemia (FFR ≤0.80). The COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial is a global, prospective, randomised, single-blinded, sham-controlled, superiority trial. A total of 1,223 all-comer patients with multivessel disease (≥2 lesions with a diameter of stenosis ≥50%) will be randomised 1:1 to revascularisation if the FFR is ≤0.75 or a VP is present (experimental arm) versus FFR ≤0.80 in the comparative arm. The primary endpoint is a composite of cardiac death, any myocardial infarction, or any clinically driven revascularisation within 24 months. The trial has already completed enrolment in 50 centres worldwide. COMBINE-INTERVENE is the first trial evaluating the impact of a revascularisation strategy that targets lesions that are either severely ischaemic or carry an OCT-assessed VP versus revascularisation based on ischaemia alone. The trial is powered for superiority. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05333068).

Title: Guideline directed medical therapy and decongestion in patients with acute heart failure.
Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

Title: The Impact of Local Heat Therapy on Comfort and Physiological Parameters in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome leads to disturbances in physiological parameters and reduces patient comfort due to the nature of the disease and its associated complications. This study examined the effect of local heat therapy on the comfort and physiological parameters of patients with acute coronary syndrome.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This clinical trial utilized a block randomization method to allocate 80 patients with acute coronary syndrome into two groups of 40 participants each. In the intervention group, a heat pack warmed in water to 75 °C was wrapped in a special towel and applied to the posterior thoracic region (T4-T11 vertebrae). During the intervention, the patient lay in the supine position on the heat pack. Each heat therapy session lasted 23 minutes. In the control group, a similar heat pack was used at a temperature of 37°C. Heat therapy was performed every 12 hours for 2 days (a total of four sessions). The Kolkaba Comfort Questionnaire and physiological parameters were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Data analysis was performed with statistical significance established at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Before the intervention, no significant differences were found between the groups. However, at the end of the intervention, heat therapy in patients with acute coronary syndrome significantly increased comfort, regulation of physiological parameters was observed, and enhanced oxygen saturation (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Heat therapy can be used as a safe and complementary intervention alongside modern medicine to enhance comfort and regulate physiological parameters in patients with acute coronary syndrome.

Title: Aloe Vera Gel Compared to Cold/Warm Compresses for Reducing Ecchymosis at the Saphenous Vein Graft Harvest Site: Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
Journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The saphenous vein harvest site in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery is highly susceptible to edema and local complications such as ecchymosis. This study aimed to compare the efficacy of aloe vera gel with that of cold and warm compresses in reducing ecchymosis at the lower leg harvest site in patients undergoing CABG surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This two-group randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted on 60 patients scheduled for CABG surgery. Eligible participants were selected through convenience sampling and randomly assigned to either Group A (aloe vera gel) or Group B (cold and warm compresses). For each participant, one leg was randomly assigned as the intervention site and the other as the control. Data collection tools included a demographic and surgical information form and an ecchymosis assessment chart. The intervention lasted for 6 days. Control legs received routine postoperative dressing. Photographs were taken on postoperative days, and the ecchymosis area was measured using ImageJ software.
RESULTS: Before the intervention, there was no significant difference in the mean ecchymosis area between the two groups (p > 0.05). The mean ecchymosis area in the treated leg decreased significantly compared to the control leg in both groups on days 5, 7, 10, and 30 (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Aloe vera gel was significantly more effective than cold and warm compresses in reducing ecchymosis at the saphenous vein graft (SVG) harvest site. Aloe vera gel can be considered an effective adjunctive treatment to minimize ecchymosis in patients following CABG surgery.

Title: Vibroacoustic lung therapy and early postoperative oxygenation after cardiac surgery: a multicentre prospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative respiratory dysfunction remains a clinically significant problem after cardiac surgery. However, clinical evidence on vibroacoustic pulmonary therapy in adult cardiac surgery patients remains limited. The study aimed to compare early postoperative oxygenation following vibroacoustic pulmonary therapy using VibroLUNG with routine manual chest physiotherapy after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, observational, non-randomized comparative study included adult patients aged 18-80 years who underwent elective cardiac surgery and developed postoperative respiratory dysfunction meeting the study eligibility criteria. Group allocation reflected routine clinical practice and device availability at the participating centers. Patients received either vibroacoustic pulmonary therapy using VibroLUNG or routine manual percussion chest physiotherapy. The principal respiratory outcome analysed in this manuscript was the P/F ratio at the early postoperative assessment. Key secondary outcomes included FiO₂ requirement, SpO₂, PaO₂, PaCO₂, acid-base status parameters, clinical scales, radiographic findings, length of stay, and recorded safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 354 screened patients, 317 were included in the analysis: 156 in the VibroLUNG group and 161 in the control group. Baseline anthropometric characteristics were comparable; however, the distribution by center/region differed substantially between the groups. At the early postoperative assessment, the VibroLUNG group had a lower administered FiO₂ [35.0% [30.0-41.0] vs. 41.5% [40.0-50.0], p < 0.001]. In the principal centre-adjusted analysis, the P/F ratio was higher in the VibroLUNG group by 23.8 units (95% CI 8.1-39.5; p=0.003). Before extubation, FiO₂ remained lower in the VibroLUNG group [30.0% [30.0-35.0] vs. 35.0% [30.0-50.0], p < 0.001], whereas the unadjusted difference in the P/F ratio was not statistically significant. No device-related adverse events, device deficiencies, or deaths during study participation were recorded.
CONCLUSION: VibroLUNG use was associated with a higher early postoperative P/F ratio and lower administered FiO₂. No adverse events, device deficiencies, or deaths were recorded during the study observation period. Causal inference is limited by the non-randomized design and centre-level differences.

Title: Comparison of the approaches to combine Renal Replacement Therapy with Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation - a Scoping Review.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used for cardiac and respiratory failure and is associated with high rates of acute kidney injury (AKI) and fluid overload requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT). ECMO and RRT can be run independently in parallel, or RRT hemofilter or device can be integrated into the ECMO circuit. Several parallel and integrated ECMO-RRT configurations have been described, but the optimal approach remains uncertain.This scoping review mapped the available literature comparing at least two ECMO-RRT configurations, summarized reported outcomes, and identified knowledge gaps.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov without restrictions, with the final search conducted on February 9, 2026. Eligible studies compared at least 2 ECMO-RRT configurations linked to reported outcomes. Data on study characteristics, configurations, outcomes, and anticoagulation were extracted and synthesized.
RESULTS: Of 6,806 records, 20 studies were included: 12 were clinical including 1 randomized controlled trial, 3 in vitro, 1 in silico, and 4 surveys. More than 8 ECMO-RRT connection schemes have been described by clinical studies since 2013. No consistent differences in efficiency or clinical outcomes were observed between the configurations compared. Integrated methods were associated with longer or comparable hemofilter lifespan. Surveys confirmed heterogeneous medical practices, and 2 safety concerns (unstoppable pressure alarms and air embolism) were reported.
CONCLUSION: Evidence on ECMO-RRT configurations is limited and heterogeneous. Future systematic and rigorous comparison of all the configurations through preclinical and clinical studies is needed to harmonize medical practices and inform the development of guidelines.

Title: Physical activity and improvement of physiological parameters by training.
Journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
Abstract: Living a better life greatly depends on maintaining healthy physiological parameters, including cardiovascular fitness, a well-balanced neuro-immuno-endocrine axis, and cognitive function-all of which contribute to focus, sharp memory, and self-esteem while mitigating age-related cognitive decline. Physical activity (high, moderate and resistance training, RT) is one of the most important lifestyle choices for reducing disease risk and improving overall health, particularly aerobic training, which increases maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max), a marker of cardiorespiratory fitness. Here, we focus on how exercise influences physiology that may contribute to improvements in health-related quality of life (QoL). Specifically, we discuss based on evidence from randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and experimental animal models the neurobiological, endocrine, immune, metabolic, and cardiovascular adaptations induced by exercise, including changes in neurochemical signaling, trophic mediators, hormones, cytokines, and cardiorespiratory fitness. Specific nutrients as supplements (creatine, omega-3 fatty acids and some amino acids) and dietary patterns (mediterranean, ketogenic, intermittent fasting) are also discussed. It is never too late to start moving-regular physical activity has been shown to counteract several deleterious effects of a sedentary lifestyle by reducing systemic inflammation, attenuating age-related brain changes, and lowering the risk of neurodegenerative diseases.

Title: Peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonists for recovery of bowel function after radical cystectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative ileus (POI) is common after radical cystectomy (RC) and contributes to prolonged hospital stay, increased healthcare costs, and reduced patient quality of life. Peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonists (PAMORAs), including alvimopan, naloxegol, and methylnaltrexone, have been investigated as strategies to reduce POI while preserving opioid-mediated analgesia. Previous systematic reviews have shown benefit of PAMORAs, particularly alvimopan, in abdominal procedures such as bowel resection and hysterectomy, but evidence specific to RC remains heterogeneous and limited. We aimed to evaluate whether incorporation of PAMORAs (alvimopan, naloxegol, or methylnaltrexone) into enhanced recovery pathways reduces POI compared with enhanced recovery pathways alone in patients undergoing RC.
METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) was conducted to identify studies evaluating PAMORAs for prevention of POI following RC. Search terms included alvimopan, naloxegol, methylnaltrexone, and RC. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized trials, and observational studies comparing PAMORAs with placebo or standard care. Two independent reviewers extracted data using Covidence software. Outcomes included time to gastrointestinal recovery, time to first flatus, time to first bowel movement, length of stay (LOS), POI incidence, adverse events (including cardiovascular events), and costs. Results were summarized in a Summary of Findings table.
RESULTS: Across included studies, PAMORAs were associated with improved postoperative gastrointestinal recovery, although certainty of evidence varied. PAMORAs shortened time to first flatus by approximately 1 day [mean difference (MD) =-0.97 days; 95% confidence interval (CI): -1.07 to -0.87] across six observational studies with no detectable heterogeneity (I2=0%), but certainty of evidence was very low due to non-randomized designs and risk of bias. Time to first bowel movement was reduced by approximately 1.3 days (MD =-1.30 days; 95% CI: -1.81 to -0.79) across nine studies, although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2=84%).
CONCLUSIONS: PAMORAs appear to improve postoperative gastrointestinal recovery following RC. However, overall certainty of evidence remains low due to reliance on non-randomized studies and heterogeneity. Alvimopan has the strongest supporting evidence, while data for naloxegol and methylnaltrexone remain limited.

Title: Digital and algorithmic strategies for guideline-directed medical therapy initiation and up-titration in adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) reduces morbidity and mortality in heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet underuse and suboptimal up-titration remain common. Digital and algorithmic strategies are increasingly being used to address these gaps, but their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain.
METHODS: This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidance and was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251268580). PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through 26 December 2025. Randomized and comparative studies enrolling adults with HFrEF were eligible if they evaluated digital, algorithm-based, or telemonitoring strategies designed to facilitate GDMT initiation, titration, or optimization versus usual care.
RESULTS: Six randomized comparative trials involving 3706 participants were included. Interventions comprised provider-facing electronic health record alerts and digitally enabled remote titration or telemonitoring pathways. Five of the six trials showed improvements in medication-optimization outcomes; the single neutral trial was a provider-facing alert intervention that showed no difference in GDMT prescribing at hospital discharge. Remote pathway-based strategies demonstrated the largest effects, including higher titration completion (82.1% vs 53.8% at 6 months; an absolute difference of approximately 28 percentage points) and greater improvements in therapy scores. Alert-based interventions showed mixed findings, including no difference in overall GDMT class prescribing at discharge in one inpatient trial (34% vs 34%). Meta-analysis was not performed because of substantial heterogeneity in interventions, outcomes, and reporting formats.
